name: Acadia National Park
line: Granite coast, carriage roads and Cadillac sunrise

jewels.name: Cadillac Mountain summit and first sunrise
jewels.booking_route: none needed on foot; vehicles need the Cadillac Summit Road reservation
jewels.blurb: 1,530 ft summit; from October 7 to March 6 the first place in the country to see the sun rise; reachable on foot by the North Ridge (4.4 mi round trip) or South Ridge (7.1 mi round trip) trails

jewels.name: Park Loop Road
jewels.booking_route: park entrance pass ($35 private vehicle, 7 days)
jewels.blurb: the 27-mile scenic drive around the east side of Mount Desert Island, built 1921-1958, reaching Sieur de Monts, Sand Beach, Otter Point, Jordan Pond and Cadillac Mountain

jewels.name: The Rockefeller carriage roads
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: 45 miles of broken-stone carriage roads built 1913-1940, open to walkers, cyclists, riders and skiers; Class 1 e-bikes permitted, Class 2 and 3 prohibited

jewels.name: Jordan Pond and the Jordan Pond Loop
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: an inland lake bound by Penobscot and Pemetic mountains and The Bubbles, with day hikes from level to strenuous starting at the boat launch, carriage road sign 15 or The Bubbles lot

jewels.name: Thunder Hole and Ocean Path
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: a narrow inlet where wave spray can top 40 feet, best one to two hours before high tide, on the 2.2-mile Ocean Path from Sand Beach toward Otter Point

jewels.name: Cadillac Summit Road vehicle reservation
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov only - "not available for purchase at the park"
jewels.blurb: required Wed May 20 through Sun Oct 25, 2026, $6, "sold online in advance at Recreation.gov"; 30 percent released 90 days ahead, 70 percent at 10 am ET two days ahead; not required on foot, bike or by taxi

jewels.name: Jordan Pond House popovers
jewels.blurb: tea and popovers on the lawn since 1893, operated by Dawnland LLC; most tables are held for walk-ins and the peak-season wait averages about 40 minutes

jewels.name: The Beehive Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: one of Acadia's rung and ladder trails up a 450-foot cliff above Sand Beach; the NPS calls it not recommended for small children, closed to dogs, and very dangerous in inclement weather

jewels.name: The Precipice Trail and the peregrine closure
jewels.booking_route: none needed; closed seasonally for nesting falcons
jewels.blurb: the iron-rung climb of Champlain Mountain's east face, closed for several months every year to protect nesting peregrine falcons; entry to a closed area is a federal violation

jewels.name: Schoodic Peninsula and Winter Harbor
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: the only mainland part of the park, about an hour's drive from Hulls Cove, managed as a minimally developed, low-visitation area with a 6-mile one-way loop road

jewels.name: Bar Harbor
jewels.blurb: the Chamber of Commerce's "gateway to Acadia National Park", with seafood, locally owned shops and lodging from boutique hotels and B&Bs to woodland camping

jewels.name: Island Explorer shuttle
jewels.blurb: "fare-free" buses "linking hotels, inns, and campgrounds with destinations in Acadia National Park and neighboring village centers", run by Downeast Transportation; spring routes from May 20, others June 23 to October 12, 2026

jewels.name: Under Canvas Acadia, Surry
jewels.booking_route: undercanvas.com own booking; advisor bookings against our CLIA number
jewels.blurb: safari-inspired canvas tents on 100 waterfront acres with "1,200 feet of shoreline right at camp", king beds, ensuite bathrooms and wood-burning stoves; dogs welcome for a nightly fee; season May 7 to October 22, 2026

jewels.name: Blackwoods Campground (NPS)
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov only; not at the campground office
jewels.blurb: in-park campground on the east side of Mount Desert Island near the Park Loop Road; reserve on Recreation.gov, 90% of sites released six months ahead and 10% at 14 days

jewels.name: Seawall Campground (NPS)
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov only; not at the campground office
jewels.blurb: in-park campground on the west side of Mount Desert Island; Recreation.gov only, same six-month and 14-day release pattern as Blackwoods

jewels.name: Schoodic Woods Campground (NPS)
jewels.blurb: the park's mainland campground on the Schoodic Peninsula; the NPS calls it the most approachable for visitors with mobility challenges, with all campground roads paved

jewels.name: Bar Harbor Whale Watch Co.
jewels.blurb: whale watch, Acadia-by-sea nature, lobster-and-seal and lighthouse cruises from 1 West Street, Bar Harbor; whale watches from $84

jewels.name: Acadia by Carriage at Wildwood Stables
jewels.blurb: horse-drawn tours on the carriage roads, May 23 to October 18, 2026: Day Mountain (1 hr) and Rockefeller's Bridges (2 hr, three stone bridges and the Jordan Pond Gatehouse)

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Resort Bar Harbor Regency
jewels.blurb: 123 Eden Street, Bar Harbor: a 280-room Holiday Inn Resort over Frenchman Bay with a marina, lobster pond, outdoor pool, Kids Club and KidSuites, per the IHG franchise opening release (May 21, 2014; read 2026-10-03, not re-confirmed on IHG's page, which refused the fetch with HTTP 403). Stewman's runs its second lobster pound at the Regency.

jewels.name: Hampton Inn Bar Harbor
jewels.booking_route: hilton.com (brand booking; not fetched - HTTP 403); phone (207) 288-3210
jewels.blurb: 12 Norman Road, Bar Harbor, listed by Visit Maine as "Bright and modern" with "stunning views of the ocean and mountains", pools, fitness center and complimentary breakfast; seasonal hours. Hilton's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403).

jewels.name: Terramor Outdoor Resort, Bar Harbor
jewels.booking_route: Terramor's own site (did not resolve when fetched 2026-10-03)
jewels.blurb: a KOA-owned glamping resort at the gateway to Acadia, opened in 2020 on a former campground; the first SITES-certified glamping resort, donating $1 per online booking to Friends of Acadia

jewels.name: Isle au Haut by mailboat from Stonington
jewels.booking_route: Isle au Haut Boat Services, Stonington (schedule not read)
jewels.blurb: year-round mailboat to the island with seasonal service to the park's Duck Harbor landing; Duck Harbor campground is reached by mailboat only and has no potable water

jewels.name: Duck Harbor Campground (NPS), Isle au Haut
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov; all sites released 10 am April 1
jewels.blurb: reached by mailboat only, no potable water; all Duck Harbor reservations release on April 1 each year on Recreation.gov

jewels.name: Acadia Outfitters / Acadia Bike & Coastal Kayaking Tours
jewels.blurb: 106 Cottage Street, Bar Harbor: bike, e-bike, sea kayak and paddleboard rentals and guided sea kayak tours, operating since 1980; open May 15 to October 15

jewels.name: Downeast Windjammer: schooner Margaret Todd
jewels.blurb: four-masted schooner sails of about 1.5 to 2 hours on Frenchman Bay from 1 Newport Drive, Bar Harbor (afternoon $49, sunset $58); the same company runs ferries to the Cranberry Isles and to Winter Harbor for Schoodic

jewels.name: Lulu Lobster Boat Ride
jewels.blurb: two-hour trip on a traditional Downeast lobster boat from 55 West Street, Bar Harbor, with a trap-hauling demonstration, seals and Egg Rock Light; May 7 to October 17, 2026, ages 6 and up, from $46

jewels.name: Oli's Trolley Acadia tours
jewels.blurb: narrated 2.5-hour trolley tour from 55 West Street, Bar Harbor, covering the full 27-mile Park Loop Road with photo stops at Cadillac Mountain, Jordan Pond and Thunder Hole; May through October

jewels.name: Atlantic Climbing School
jewels.blurb: AMGA-accredited guide service at 67 Main Street, Bar Harbor, since 1994, running climbing courses at Otter Cliffs and South Wall plus guided hiking in Acadia

jewels.name: Maine State Sea Kayak, Southwest Harbor
jewels.blurb: guided sea kayak tours around Mount Desert Island, including youth and oyster-farm tours, with fat-tire e-bike rentals; based at 254 Main Street, Southwest Harbor

jewels.name: Bar Harbor / Oceanside KOA Holiday
jewels.blurb: oceanfront campground at 136 County Road, Bar Harbor, with RV and tent sites, camping and deluxe cabins and Airstream trailers, bike rentals and a dog park

jewels.name: Narrows Too RV Resort, Trenton
jewels.booking_route: Thousand Trails membership / nightly via rvonthego.com
jewels.blurb: Thousand Trails waterfront RV resort at 1150 Bar Harbor Road with 531 sites and rental lodging, heated pool and ocean views; season May 1 to October 26

jewels.name: Mt Desert Narrows Camping Resort, Bar Harbor
jewels.booking_route: Thousand Trails membership / nightly via rvonthego.com
jewels.blurb: 258 RV, tent and rental sites at 1219 State Hwy 3 on the Atlantic, with heated pool and playground; season May 15 to October 13

jewels.name: Bar Harbor Campground
jewels.blurb: full-hookup and water-electric RV sites plus tent sites on a bluff at 409 State Hwy 3, about 2 miles from the park, with ocean-view sites and a heated pool; mid-May to mid-October

jewels.name: Mount Desert Campground
jewels.blurb: wooded and waterfront tent sites, many on platforms, on Somes Sound; trailers and RVs limited to 20 feet

jewels.name: Hadley's Point Campground
jewels.blurb: tent, RV (water and electric) and cabin sites at the northernmost point of Mount Desert Island near a public saltwater beach

jewels.name: Hampton Inn Ellsworth
jewels.blurb: 4 Downeast Highway, Ellsworth, built 2010 near Routes 1 and 3 "which leads south to Bar Harbor/Acadia National Park and Schoodic Point"; Bar Harbor about 30 minutes by car; indoor pool, fitness center, free breakfast and parking. Operated by Witham Family Hotels.

jewels.name: Acadia Wilderness Lodge, West Tremont
jewels.blurb: a yurt village and forest glamping tents on the quiet west side of Mount Desert Island, with king beds, soaking tubs and private grills; Bass Harbor Head Lighthouse about 10 minutes away

jewels.name: Evergreen Yurts, Bar Harbor
jewels.blurb: 24-foot yurts with full bathroom, kitchen, queen bed and heat pump beside Northeast Creek off Route 3, about 5 miles from Hulls Cove Visitor Center; open May through October

jewels.name: Acadia Yurts and Wellness Center, Southwest Harbor
jewels.blurb: yurt and tiny-house rentals at 200 Seal Cove Road on Mount Desert Island, with yoga, a flotation tank, massage and an infrared sauna by appointment; open year-round

jewels.name: Ferncrest Acadia, Sargentville
jewels.blurb: geodesic domes (Classic and Family) and camp cabins on the Blue Hill Peninsula, about an hour from the park, positioned as the quieter side of the Acadia region

jewels.name: Beal's Lobster Pier, Southwest Harbor
jewels.blurb: working lobster pier at 182 Clark Point Road operating since 1932, where boats unload while you eat lobster rolls (original, spicy, lemon, garlic), chowder and whoopie pies; pier closed October to May, nationwide shipping year-round

jewels.name: Thurston's Lobster Pound, Bernard
jewels.blurb: waterfront lobster pound at 9 Thurston Road serving lobster fresh from the boat; Memorial Day weekend to mid-October, Tuesday to Saturday

jewels.name: Stewman's Lobster Pound, Bar Harbor
jewels.blurb: two oceanfront lobster pounds, downtown Bar Harbor and at the Bar Harbor Regency; the chamber's Lobster Roll Tour lists the downtown pound at 35 West Street for an 'authentic downeast lobster bake'

jewels.name: Havana, Bar Harbor
jewels.booking_route: phone (207) 288-2822 (not confirmed until they call back)
jewels.blurb: American fine dining with Latin influences at 318 Main Street, menus changing weekly or daily; the restaurant cites a Wine Spectator Award of Excellence and a James Beard nomination; open daily 4-10pm

jewels.name: Abbe Museum, Bar Harbor
jewels.blurb: Wabanaki arts and cultures museum at 26 Mt Desert Street, which began as a small trailside museum inside Acadia National Park

jewels.name: Islesford Dock Restaurant & Gallery, Little Cranberry Island
jewels.blurb: seasonal restaurant at 1 Main Street, Islesford, reached by the Beal & Bunker ferry from Northeast Harbor or Cranberry Cove Ferry from Southwest Harbor; site shows closed for the season, reopening in spring

jewels.name: Dahlia's at The Asticou, Northeast Harbor
jewels.booking_route: rooms via Opal Collection reservations; dining booking not observed; phone 207.276.8600
jewels.blurb: seasonal local-seafood-and-produce restaurant in an 1883 rusticator-era shingle-style hotel at 15 Peabody Drive, with the Moss Bar and poolside Cabana Bar

jewels.name: Peekytoe Provisions, Bar Harbor
jewels.blurb: year-round fresh-never-frozen seafood and provisions shop with a full bar at 244 Main Street: oysters, local shellfish, tinned conservas, cheese and charcuterie, plus seacuterie boards and rental provisioning; daily 11am-9pm

jewels.name: The Chart Room Restaurant, Bar Harbor
jewels.blurb: per the Bar Harbor Chamber of Commerce listing, fresh-caught seafood at 565 Eden Street, operating since 1990

jewels.name: Mount Desert Island Ice Cream, Bar Harbor
jewels.blurb: small-batch ice cream made no more than 5 gallons at a time with beans scraped and lemons squeezed by hand; Bar Harbor shop and kitchen, with sister shops in Portland, Washington DC and Japan

jewels.name: Bar Harbor Lobster Roll Tour
jewels.blurb: per the Bar Harbor Chamber of Commerce, a self-guided lobster roll trail of 28 listed stops across Bar Harbor and Southwest Harbor, tracked in the Visit Bar Harbor app

jewels.name: Atlantic Brewing Company and Mainely Meat Barbeque, Bar Harbor
jewels.booking_route: tours booked via own site; phone 207.288.2337
jewels.blurb: brewery at 15 Knox Road, Town Hill, with a tasting room open daily 11am-7pm, brewery tours Friday at 3 and weekends at 12 and 3, and Mainely Meat Barbeque on site; a Midtown taproom at 52 Cottage Street

jewels.name: Bar Harbor Winery
jewels.blurb: Maine craft-wine tasting room at 854 State Highway 3 pouring flights of three on a board, with a shop of local artisan goods; Monday to Saturday noon-6pm

jewels.name: Acadia hiking kit: sturdy shoes, rain jacket and warm layers
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to rei.com (AvantLink); in person at Cadillac Mountain Sports, Bar Harbor
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Wear sturdy hiking shoes and dress for variable weather"; bring "Adequate clothing (rain jacket and warm layers). Weather can be unpredictable and change quickly." "Carry water; at least 20 oz (.6 L) and more on warm days".

jewels.name: Tick protection: repellent and long pants
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Ticks are prevalent in Acadia and are mostly active late spring to early fall." "Wear light-colored clothing so ticks are easier to spot", "Wear pants tucked into socks", "Spray your shoes and clothing with repellent".

jewels.name: Headlamp and topographic map, not the phone
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to blackdiamondequipment.com (AvantLink); trail maps also sold at the park
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Do not rely on your phone for maps or flashlights. Limited cell service, GPS, and flashlight use drain batteries quickly." "Consult a topographic map before hiking. Do not rely on the park handout map."

jewels.name: Water treatment for Duck Harbor on Isle au Haut
jewels.blurb: NPS: "There is no potable water source at Duck Harbor Campground. Plan ahead to treat the water or bring enough potable water for the duration of your stay."

jewels.name: Cadillac Mountain Sports
jewels.booking_route: walk-in retail, Bar Harbor and Ellsworth
jewels.blurb: "Maine's Performance Outfitter" with stores at 26 Cottage St., Bar Harbor, and in Ellsworth, plus Cadillac's The North Face at 39 Cottage St.: "our staff is here to help you select the best gear and apparel for outdoor adventures."

faq.q: Do you need reservations for Acadia National Park?
faq.a: Only for Cadillac Summit Road by vehicle. The NPS states: "Vehicle reservations are required for Cadillac Summit Road from Wed May 20 through Sun Oct 25, 2026." They cost $6 and are "sold online in advance at Recreation.gov. They are not available for purchase at the park." "Vehicle reservations are not required for any other areas of the park, or for visitors who enter the area by foot, bike, or taxi."

faq.q: How much is an Acadia National Park pass?
faq.a: Per the NPS: private vehicle $35, motorcycle $30 and per person $20 (on foot or bicycle), each valid 7 days; the Acadia annual pass is $70. Non-US residents pay a "$100 per person fee" in addition to the entrance pass, and the Cadillac Summit Road reservation is $6.

faq.q: Can you visit Acadia National Park without a car?
faq.a: Yes, by the Island Explorer: "The fare-free Island Explorer features bus routes linking hotels, inns, and campgrounds with destinations in Acadia National Park and neighboring village centers." "Spring service on the Gateway Center, Loop Road, and Schoodic routes begins May 20, 2026. Other Island Explorer buses operate from June 23 through October 12, 2026."

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Acadia National Park for fall foliage?
faq.a: The NPS says "The peak generally comes in mid-October" and points visitors to Maine's fall foliage website, updated every Wednesday in season. Fall weather is "Variable weather; 30-70 F (-1-21 C)".

faq.q: Can you camp in Acadia National Park?
faq.a: Yes, at Blackwoods, Seawall, Schoodic Woods and Duck Harbor. "All campsite reservations must be made in advance at Recreation.gov"; for the first three, "90 percent of campsites are released six months in advance on the first of each month at 10 am" and the rest 14 days ahead. "There is no backcountry camping, 'out-of-bounds' camping, overnight parking, or winter camping allowed anywhere in Acadia."

faq.q: Is Acadia National Park dog friendly?
faq.a: The NPS states: "There are 100 miles (161 km) of hiking trails and 45 miles (72 km) of carriage roads in the park where pets are permitted." Pets "must be kept on a leash no longer than 6 feet (2 m) at all times", and six trails, including the Precipice and Beehive, are closed to pets.

faq.q: Is Acadia National Park open in winter?
faq.a: Parts of it. The NPS operating table closes the Park Loop Road and paved roads from Dec 1 to Apr 15 and unpaved roads from Nov 15 to May 15, while the Schoodic Loop and Point Road are listed "Year-round" and the carriage roads "Year-round, seasonal closures".

name: Hammonasset Beach State Park
line: Connecticut's largest shoreline park and its clam shacks

jewels.name: Hammonasset Beach (two-mile swimming beach)
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free for Connecticut-registered vehicles; out-of-state parking paid at the gate
jewels.blurb: "a two-mile sandy stretch of beach" on Long Island Sound at "Connecticut's largest shoreline park"; "Cool off with a dip in the refreshing saltwater or don your scuba gear and explore what's below anywhere along the park's two-mile stretch of shoreline"; open daily 8:00 a.m. to sunset

jewels.name: Hammonasset Beach State Park Campground
jewels.blurb: "558 grassy open campsites (including eight rustic cabins)"; water and electric $35 resident / $45 non-resident, basic $20 / $30, rustic cabin $70 / $80 with a 7-night Sunday-to-Sunday minimum, plus a $9 processing fee; bathhouses with hot showers, camp store, playground, amphitheater; "Pets are not allowed at this campground" in season

jewels.name: Meigs Point Nature Center
jewels.booking_route: walk-in, free; group programmes and birthday parties by phone 203-245-8743
jewels.blurb: "a state-of-the-art environmental education center" with "4,000 square feet of hands-on learning experiences, including a saltwater touch tank; live turtles, snakes, amphibians, crabs, and fish"; "Nature Center Admission: Free"; Tuesday-Sunday 10am-5pm April-October, 10am-4pm November-March

jewels.name: Hammonasset Beach State Park Walk and the boardwalk
jewels.blurb: "3.4-mile paved multi-use trail... Level of difficulty: Easy... This heavily trafficked out-and-back trail hugs the coastline, offering shoreline vistas from the nature center all the way to the western section of the beach"

jewels.name: Surfcasting from the Meigs Point and West Beach jetties
jewels.booking_route: none needed - Connecticut fishing licence rules apply (portal.ct.gov/DEEP/Fishing/CT-Fishing)
jewels.blurb: "Surf cast from the stone breakwater. Cast a line from the serenity of your canoe. Catch dinner while catching the sunrise." Daytime fishing at Meigs Point Jetty and West Beach Jetty (May-October); night fishing along the entire beach in peak season only; blackfish, striped bass and fluke

jewels.name: Willard's Island Nature Trail
jewels.blurb: "1.1-mile paved trail... Level of difficulty: Easy... Head inland and away from the beach for some solitude and a closer look at the park's expansive salt marshes."

jewels.name: Meigs Point Trail
jewels.blurb: "1.4-mile trail... Level of difficulty: Easy... This out-and-back trail takes along the rocky, sandy shoreline takes you out and around Meigs Point."

jewels.name: The BURT bike trail
jewels.blurb: "Ride through the park on Hammonasset's three-mile BURT trail from West Beach all the way to Meigs Point."

jewels.name: Meigs Point jetty kayak and boat launch
jewels.blurb: "Follow signs to Meigs Point and the fishermen's parking area. Look for the launch on the east side of the Meigs Point jetty." Life jackets are mandatory October 1 through May 31, and children under 12 must wear them year-round

jewels.name: Hammonasset picnic shelters
jewels.blurb: "Rent one of our four picnic shelters: (3) 20 x 60-ft., (1) 20 x 33-ft. Each shelter has space for 65 people, 12 picnic tables and 2 charcoal pedestal grills." Rental fee $220 plus $9 processing fee

jewels.name: Meigs Point events: Beach Cleanup (Oct 3, 2026) and Astronomy Night (Nov 6, 2026)
jewels.blurb: the nature center lists a Beach Cleanup "Saturday, October 3rd 10am - 12pm" and an Astronomy Night "Friday, November 6th", alongside "40 educational programs" for groups

jewels.name: Lenny & Joe's Fish Tale Restaurant, Madison
jewels.booking_route: phone (203) 245-7289 (own site ljfishtale.com returned 403 this session)
jewels.blurb: "Started as a 'roadside clam stand' in 1979 and today continues the tradition of serving the highest quality seafood available to diners who come from all over New England"; seafood "broiled, baked, fried, sauteed, charbroiled, steamed" at 1301 Boston Post Rd., Madison; Sunday-Thursday 11:30 a.m.-8:30 p.m., Friday and Saturday to 9 p.m.; a second location in Westbrook

jewels.name: The Place Restaurant, Guilford
jewels.booking_route: not observed - no reservation policy on own site; phone 203-453-9276
jewels.blurb: "a truly unusual outdoor seafood restaurant in Guilford, CT where visitors dine outdoors while a crackling wood fire roasts savory clams, smoky lobsters, sweet corn and much more"; tree-stump seats at red tables; 901 Boston Post Rd; open May through late October, weather permitting; cash and ATM, no credit cards

jewels.name: Guilford Lobster Pound
jewels.blurb: "Hot, buttery lobster rolls served dockside." Bart Mansi has run it since 1991, catching lobster from his 42-foot boat; Hot Buttered Lobster Roll $27 with 4 oz of meat; 505A Whitfield St., Guilford; Monday-Thursday 12-6pm, Friday-Sunday 12-7pm, weather dependent; BYOB, cash only

jewels.name: Lobster Landing, Clinton
jewels.booking_route: online ordering on own site; phone 860.669.2005
jewels.blurb: waterfront lobster shack at 152 Commerce St, Clinton, claiming "The Best Lobster Roll in New England"; lobster rolls at market rate from $31.50; open daily from 11AM; BYOB; a Senior Menu every Wednesday for age 60+

jewels.name: Chamard Vineyards, Clinton
jewels.blurb: farm, winery and bistro at 115 Cow Hill Road, Clinton, with "acclaimed cuisine, thoughtfully paired with our wines"; wine tastings; Wednesday-Saturday 12-9pm, Sunday 11am-5pm; a sister waterfront cafe, Pas Place, serves Chamard wines

jewels.name: Bishop's Orchards, Guilford
jewels.booking_route: walk-in; pick-your-own pricing and availability by phone 203-458-PICK
jewels.blurb: "A 150+ year local tradition rooted in fresh, local food & memorable experiences"; year-round farm market at 1355 Boston Post Road, pick-your-own (berries and peaches in summer, apples and pears in fall), "Bishop's fruit wines and hard ciders" with daily tastings, a creamery 11am-9pm, and a Fall Festival open through 11/1

jewels.name: Madison Beach Hotel, Curio Collection by Hilton
jewels.blurb: "Indulge in AAA Four Diamond elegance at Connecticut's premier luxury beachfront resort" at 94 W. Wharf Rd., Madison; "33 of the 34 guest rooms feature furnished balconies overlooking the Long Island Sound"; joined Hilton's Curio Collection in 2015

jewels.name: Water's Edge Resort and Spa, Westbrook
jewels.blurb: "Connecticut's Largest Beachfront Resort" at 1525 Boston Post Road, Westbrook, with "a private white sand beach, restaurants, entertainment, a premium spa"; ocean-view rooms, suites, villas by the sea and weekly house rentals; Dattilo, Seaview Bistro, Sunset Bar & Grill, Julia's Beach Bar and Cappuccio Caffe

jewels.name: Riverdale Farm Campsites, Clinton
jewels.blurb: "Part of a 100-acre colonial farm, Riverdale Farm Campsites is nestled between a winding country road and the meandering Hammonasset River"; wooded, waterfront and meadow sites, full hookups and 50-amp service, cabins, a pool (new in 2025), spring-fed pond swimming; 111 River Road, Clinton

jewels.name: Hartwoods, North Guilford (Hipcamp)
jewels.blurb: a one-site wooded tent and RV pitch with 30-amp electricity and water hookup, listed by Hipcamp as 9.7 mi from Hammonasset Beach and rated 97% from 102 reviews; re-typed 2026-10-03 from glamping to campground - the Hipcamp listing reads 'Tent, RV'

jewels.name: Shoreline cottages near Hammonasset (Airbnb)
jewels.blurb: Airbnb's Hammonasset page lists shoreline rentals in Madison, Guilford, Westbrook and Clinton, among them a Madison carriage house "Just 1 mile and your feet are on 2 miles of white sandy beach" and a Clinton cottage a "stone's throw from Hammonasset State Park"

jewels.name: Indian River Marina & Kayak, Clinton
jewels.booking_route: own website reservations; Docklyne online booking; phone (860) 664-3704
jewels.blurb: "about one-quarter mile up the Indian River from the Clinton Harbor where three rivers – the Hammonasset, Indian, and Hammock – converge on their way to Long Island Sound"; kayak, canoe and paddleboard rentals launching on the Indian River, with delivery and drop-offs to nearby waters; 58 Commerce Street, Clinton

jewels.name: Thimble Islands Cruise (Sea Mist), Stony Creek, Branford
jewels.blurb: Sea Mist, a 44-foot boat, runs a "45 minute narrated cruise" from the Stony Creek Dock through the Thimble Islands; the 40-foot catamaran Island Time runs a one-hour Branford River and shoreline cruise

jewels.name: Guilford Town Green
jewels.blurb: the Connecticut Office of Tourism: "Guilford, settled in 1639, is a charming town steeped in history and brimming with modern attractions. Known for its award-winning Town Green, it offers unique shopping, dining, galleries, and family-friendly events."

jewels.name: Downtown Madison and R.J. Julia Booksellers
jewels.booking_route: none needed - public downtown; shops walk-in
jewels.blurb: Madison's "pedestrian-friendly downtown" with bookstores, galleries, cinema, tea emporiums, cafes and boutiques; the state tourism office calls R.J. Julia Booksellers "famous independently and woman-owned"

jewels.name: Ashley's Ice Cream
jewels.booking_route: walk-in (own site ashleysicecream.com did not load this session)
jewels.blurb: the Connecticut Office of Tourism names "Ashley's Ice Cream for fresh ice cream consistently voted some of the best in the state" among the coastal towns' stops

jewels.name: Aces High RV Park, East Lyme
jewels.booking_route: Camping.com booking portal linked from the park's site, or phone 860-739-8858

faq.q: How much does it cost to get into Hammonasset Beach?
faq.a: Connecticut residents park free. Out-of-state vehicles pay $22 on weekends and holidays, $15 on weekdays and $7 after 4:00 pm; an out-of-state season pass is $112.

faq.q: What are Hammonasset Beach State Park's hours?
faq.a: Open daily 8:00 a.m. to sunset, and open 24 hours for camping and fishing from Memorial Day to Columbus Day. The 2026 season runs May 22 to October 12 (noon).

faq.q: How much is camping at Hammonasset Beach State Park?
faq.a: Water and electric sites are $35 for residents and $45 for non-residents; basic sites $20 and $30; rustic cabins $70 and $80 with a 7-night Sunday-to-Sunday minimum. A $9 processing fee applies. Book on ReserveAmerica or at 1-877-668-CAMP (2267).

faq.q: What time is check-in at Hammonasset Beach State Park?
faq.a: "Check in time for campsites is 1:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m." Arrivals after 10 p.m. use a temporary stopover area until morning. Cabins check in from 2:00 p.m. on Sundays and check out at 11:00 a.m. on departure day.

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Hammonasset Beach State Park?
faq.a: On a leash in the picnic areas year-round, and on the beach only from September 30 to April 1. The campground does not allow pets in season.

faq.q: Can you drink alcohol at Hammonasset Beach State Park?
faq.a: Not on the beach or boardwalk. Connecticut State Parks: "Alcoholic beverages are permitted in many state parks and forests, but not on beaches or boardwalks."

faq.q: Can you swim at Hammonasset Beach State Park?
faq.a: Yes, anywhere along the two-mile shoreline. State parks say "Lifeguards are staffed at some of these areas during the peak summer season. Lifeguard coverage on any specific day is dependent on seasonality, time of day, and staffing levels." Beach rules include no alcohol, glass, pets, flotation devices or snorkels in swimming areas.

faq.q: What is the water quality at Hammonasset Beach State Park?
faq.a: Connecticut State Parks publishes a Swimming Areas Water Quality Report, "updated weekly from Memorial Day through Labor Day", at ctparks.com/water-quality-report.

faq.q: Can you fish at Hammonasset Beach State Park?
faq.a: Yes. Daytime fishing is allowed at the Meigs Point and West Beach jetties (May-October), and night fishing along the entire beach in peak season only. The park names surf casting for blackfish, striped bass and fluke.

faq.q: What town is Hammonasset Beach State Park in?
faq.a: Madison, Connecticut - 1288 Boston Post Rd., Madison, CT 06443.

faq.q: Is Jones Beach State Park free?

faq.q: Are dogs allowed at Jones Beach State Park?

faq.q: Can you swim at Jones Beach State Park?

faq.q: How many acres is Jones Beach State Park?

faq.q: When did Jones Beach State Park open?

faq.q: What time does Jones Beach State Park open?

faq.q: How much does it cost to get into Letchworth State Park?
faq.a: NYS Parks lists the vehicle entrance fee as "$10 per vehicle (car, truck, van, motorcycle, etc)" and "All Buses $35", with "Pool & Museum included!" The $80 Empire Pass gives unlimited day-use entry at most State Parks facilities.

faq.q: When does Letchworth State Park stop charging?
faq.a: For 2026 the park lists the vehicle fee as collected "5/8/26 - 10/18/26: 9 am - 5 pm, daily."

faq.q: Which entrance is best for Letchworth State Park?
faq.a: It depends on what you want to see. The park lists the Portageville Entrance (South) for "Access to the Glen Iris Inn, Museum, Middle and Upper Falls Area, and the Genesee Arch Bridge"; the Castile Entrance (South) for the Archery Field Overlook, the Lower Falls Area, A and B Cabins and the Humphrey Nature Center; the Mt Morris Entrance (North) for the G.W. Harvey Swimming Pool and Highbanks Recreation Area; and the Perry Entrance (West) for "Direct access to Highbanks Camping Area".

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Letchworth State Park?
faq.a: Yes, with limits. "A maximum of two pets are allowed in camping loops 100, 200, 700 and 800, Cabin Area C and day use areas unless prohibited by sign or directive." Pets must be "crated or on a leash not more than 6-feet in length", proof of rabies inoculation is required at check-in, and pets are not permitted in playgrounds, buildings, boardwalks or pools (service animals excepted).

faq.q: Can you swim at Letchworth State Park?
faq.a: Only in the pool. "Swimming is only permitted at the Harvey Swimming Pool on the North end of the park"; "Entry to the pool is free. Regular vehicle admission fees to enter the park still apply. Swimming in the Genesee River is prohibited." NYS Parks lists the 2026 pool season as "Projected opening 6/27 - Labor Day", 11:00 am-6:45 pm.

faq.q: When is peak foliage at Letchworth State Park?
faq.a: The county tourism office names "Peak Leaf Season – Columbus Day weekend and the following weekends", when "traffic is very slow and congested" and park management "may close portions of the park due to congestion/overcrowding."

faq.q: Is Letchworth State Park open in the winter?
faq.a: Yes. "The park is open 6am-11pm. However, there are various seasonal winter closures to be aware of." There is a tubing hill near Trailside Lodge (bring your own inflatable tube), snowmobiling on designated trails, and cross-country skiing and snowshoeing "as conditions allow."

faq.q: Can you fly a drone in Letchworth State Park?
faq.a: Only with a permit. "Drones can be used by permit only in certain areas of the park. Fees and insurance requirements apply." Call the park visitor center at (585) 493-3600.

faq.q: Can you get married at Letchworth State Park?
faq.a: Yes. "Getting married at the park is free; however, it is asked that bridal parties call the visitor's center at (585) 493.3600 to ensure area availability for the event. Regular vehicle admission fees apply and additional permits may be required." The Glen Iris Inn also hosts weddings overlooking Middle Falls.

faq.q: How far is Letchworth State Park from Niagara Falls?
faq.a: Adventure Bound Four Winds, a campground in Portageville next to the park, states that from its site "Rochester, New York ... is 45 minutes north. Buffalo is 60 minutes north. Niagara Falls is 75 minutes away." These are the campground's own drive times, not a park or transport-authority figure.

line: Nineteen waterfalls above Seneca Lake wine country

jewels.name: Watkins Glen International

Its 2026 NASCAR weekend: "Friday, May 8 - NASCAR CRAFTSMAN Truck Series Race", "Saturday, May 9 - NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series Mission 200 at The Glen", "Sunday, May 10 - NASCAR Cup Series Go Bowling at The Glen". "Fans can purchase tickets... at www.theglen.com."

jewels.blurb: NY State Parks: the North and South Rim trails are open year-round, sunrise to sunset, with no gorge or waterfall access November to May. Pets are allowed in day use areas "(except the Gorge Trail)", a maximum of two, on a leash no longer than 6 feet.

jewels.blurb: From Seneca Harbor Station, 1 N. Franklin St: the Seneca Spirit's "50-minute narrated excursion" past Hector Falls and the east shore cliffs and a "1.5-hour twilight journey"; the Seneca Legacy's dinner cruises with a "multi-course meal featuring the best of the Finger Lakes", music evenings and lunch cruises; "From spring through fall"; charters for "up to 200 dining guests or 250 passengers".

jewels.name: Watkins Glen Harbor Hotel
jewels.blurb: "A premier four-season resort" "at the southern tip of Seneca Lake", with lake-view deluxe rooms and suites, many with private balconies; Blue Pointe Grille and Coldwater Bar; the park offers "unforgettable outdoor experiences just moments from the hotel" in the hotel's words.

jewels.name: Glenora Wine Cellars and the Inn at Glenora
jewels.blurb: "The first winery on Seneca Lake, located just 10 minutes from Watkins Glen", "Since 1977"; a 30-room Inn, Veraisons Restaurant with a covered terrace, daily tastings and "behind-the-scenes cellar tours". An October offer read today: Sunday-Thursday stays from $153.30 per night with code FALL.

Reserved educational tastings on Tock or walk-ins for wines by the glass; guided Harvest Tours October 9 and 16, 2026, 3:00-4:15 pm.

jewels.blurb: Tent and trailer sites $18-$30 per night; rustic cabins $58 per night with a 3-night minimum; an out-of-state camping fee is added. The 2026 season opened May 8; reservations through ReserveAmerica or 1-800-456-2267.

Groups of 10+ use the park's form or email the regional educators.

jewels.name: Schooner True Love

jewels.name: Seneca Lodge

jewels.name: Montour Falls, the Valley of Tumbling Waters
jewels.blurb: The neighbouring village: "As the southern gateway to the Finger Lakes Region Montour Falls is noted for its natural as well as its historical beauty. Surrounded by hills rising 1,000 feet, it is the focal point for seven natural glens which radiate from its borders, with more than a score of beautiful waterfalls".

jewels.name: Naturluxe & Stars

Tasting room Mon-Sat 10am-6pm, Sun 11am-6pm; vineyard tours every hour on the hour until 4pm, year-round, tickets in the tasting room; Fox Run Cafe daily 11am-5pm; the Vineyard House for overnight stays.

jewels.name: Lakeside Resort and 3812 Bistro

The rei.com store page returned HTTP 403 today, so the address and hours were not read.

faq.q: Is Watkins Glen State Park free?
faq.a: No. The state charges a vehicle entry fee of "$10 per vehicle", which includes pool access.

faq.q: How long is the Watkins Glen State Park trail?
faq.a: NY State Parks describes "The Gorge Trail with 19 waterfalls in a 1-mile stretch"; within two miles the glen descends 400 feet past 200-foot cliffs.

faq.q: How long does it take to walk Watkins Glen State Park?
faq.a: The Gorge Trail takes "About 1.5 to 2 hours one way, depending on stops", says the county visitor bureau, which suggests starting at the main entrance and returning by the South Rim Trail.

faq.q: Is Watkins Glen State Park open in November?
faq.a: The park is "Open year round dawn to dusk", but "The Gorge Trail with 19 waterfalls in a 1-mile stretch will close for the season on October 25, 2026" and re-opens in mid to late May. The North and South Rim trails stay open year-round, with no gorge or waterfall access November to May.

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Watkins Glen State Park?
faq.a: Yes, but not on the gorge: "Pets are not allowed on the Gorge Trail. A maximum of two pets are allowed in campsites and day use areas (except the Gorge Trail)". Pets must be supervised, on a leash no longer than 6 feet, with proof of rabies vaccination.

faq.q: Can you camp at Watkins Glen State Park?
faq.a: Yes. Tent and trailer sites are $18-$30 per night and rustic cabins $58 per night with a 3-night minimum, plus an out-of-state fee; the 2026 season opened May 8, and reservations are through ReserveAmerica or 1-800-456-2267.

faq.q: Can you swim at Watkins Glen State Park?
faq.a: In the park's pool. Its 2026 season ran June 27 to September 7, weekdays 12:00 p.m. to 5:45 p.m. and weekends 11:30 a.m. to 6:45 p.m., and entry is included in the $10 vehicle fee. The state's page names no swimming in the gorge.

faq.q: What time is Watkins Glen State Park open?
faq.a: "Open year round dawn to dusk."

faq.q: What is the best time of day to visit Watkins Glen State Park?
faq.a: "Arrive early in the morning to avoid crowds, especially on weekends and peak summer months," advises the county visitor bureau.

faq.q: Where do you enter Watkins Glen State Park?
faq.a: There are three entrances, linked by the park shuttle when it runs: "Main- 1009 N. Franklin St, Watkins Glen, NY 14891 South- 3530 Route 419, Watkins Glen, NY 14891 Upper- 3310 Route 409, Watkins Glen, NY 14891". The shuttle is $6 per person one way.

faq.q: Do I need a ticket for Shenandoah National Park?
faq.a: An entrance pass covers the park. Old Rag Mountain also needs its own day-use ticket from March 1 to November 30, including the Saddle, Ridge and Ridge Access trails: $2.00 per person of any age, sold only through Recreation.gov or 877-444-6777, separate from the entrance pass; 800 a day, 400 released 30 days ahead and 400 released 5 days ahead, at 10:00 a.m.

faq.q: How much does it cost to get into Shenandoah National Park?
faq.a: "Private Vehicle $30.00" for seven consecutive days, "Motorcycle $25.00", "Per Person $15.00" for walk-up or bicycling visitors 16 and older (children under 16 free), and "Annual Entrance - Park $55.00". Since July 1, 2025 the park "accepts only mobile or electronic payments for entrance and campground fees."

faq.q: When is Shenandoah National Park free?
faq.a: The park lists eight fee-free entrance days in 2026: February 16, May 25, June 14, July 3-5, August 25, September 17, October 27 (Theodore Roosevelt's birthday) and November 11 (Veterans Day).

faq.q: Can you drive through Shenandoah National Park?
faq.a: Yes, on Skyline Drive, which "runs 105 miles north and south along the crest of the Blue Ridge Mountains", with a 35 mph limit in most places and four entrances. The NPS says "most people need at least 3-4 hours to simply drive through" the park.

faq.q: When is peak foliage in Shenandoah National Park?
faq.a: The NPS: "generally, fall colors seem to be at their most brilliant stage around the 2nd or 3rd week of October."

faq.q: Can you camp in Shenandoah National Park?
faq.a: Yes. Campgrounds are booked through Recreation.gov: Big Meadows is reservation only; Mathews Arm and Loft Mountain have both reservable and first-come sites; Lewis Mountain is first-come, first-served with self-registration and "Sites can not be reserved". Backcountry camping needs a permit bought through Recreation.gov.

faq.q: Is Shenandoah National Park part of the Appalachian Trail?
faq.a: Yes. The park has "over 500 miles of hiking trails, including 101 miles of the Appalachian Trail".

faq.q: Where can I stay in Shenandoah National Park?
faq.a: "All lodging facilities in Shenandoah National Park are operated by Delaware North, the Park concessionaire": Skyland (mile 41.7), Big Meadows Lodge (mile 51) and Lewis Mountain Cabins (mile 57.5), booked at goshenandoah.com or 877-847-1919. The Potomac Appalachian Trail Club maintains six primitive cabins in the park.

faq.q: Is Shenandoah National Park open?
faq.a: The NPS: "Shenandoah National Park is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week". Portions of Skyline Drive are periodically closed in inclement weather, and lodges, waysides and campgrounds are seasonal.

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Shenandoah National Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Pets are allowed, if leashed, on most trails" and in campgrounds, on "a physical leash no longer than 6 feet at all times." Closed to pets are trails including Fox Hollow, Stony Man, Limberlost, the Old Rag Ridge and Saddle trails, Dark Hollow Falls, Bearfence Mountain and Frazier Discovery - "fewer than 20 miles of the 500+ miles of trails".

name: Liberty State Park
line: Statue of Liberty views and the Ellis Island ferry

jewels.name: Statue City Cruises ferry to the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island
jewels.booking_route: own website booking (statuecitycruises.com), ticket windows in the CRRNJ Terminal, or 1-877-LADYTIX (1-877-523-9849)
jewels.blurb: "Statue City Cruises is the ONLY ferry service authorized by the National Park Service to sell tickets for, and provide transportation to Liberty and Ellis Islands"; the New Jersey departure is "the historic railroad terminal in Liberty State Park". NPS-listed fares: adult (13+) $26.00, senior (62+) $23.00, child (4-12) $17.00, under 4 free; pedestal or crown access adds $0.30.

jewels.name: Central Railroad of New Jersey (CRRNJ) Terminal
jewels.booking_route: none needed to enter ("Entrance Fee None"); history programmes by pre-registration with the Nature Center, 201-915-3400 x503
jewels.blurb: "Built in 1889, the Central Railroad of New Jersey (CRRNJ) Terminal stands as the cornerstone of Liberty State Park. It is listed on the State and National Registers of Historic Places." It welcomed "new immigrants from Ellis Island"; train service ceased in 1967 and the terminal "now serves as a gateway for visitors to the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island." History programmes (Historic Trilogy, Explosion at Black Tom, Trail of the Blue Comet) run monthly with pre-registration.

jewels.name: Statue of Liberty National Monument
jewels.booking_route: reached only by the Statue City Cruises ferry; crown and pedestal by reservation with the ferry ticket
jewels.blurb: "A gift of friendship from the people of France to the United States", dedicated October 28, 1886. The Statue of Liberty Museum on Liberty Island holds "artifacts and exhibits, including the original torch"; crown and pedestal access need reservations. "The National Park Service does not charge an entrance fee to visit the museums on Liberty Island and Ellis Island" - the cost is the ferry.

jewels.name: Empty Sky, 9/11 Memorial
jewels.booking_route: none needed - inside the park; NJDEP lists "Entrance Fee: None"
jewels.blurb: "The official State of New Jersey Memorial that honors the memory of the 750 people that lived in or had ties to New Jersey that lost their lives" on September 11, 2001. Twin stainless steel walls "210 feet long, the width of each side of the World Trade Center Towers", 30 feet high; designed by Jessica Jamroz and Frederic Schwartz, dedicated September 11, 2011.

jewels.name: Ellis Island National Museum of Immigration
jewels.booking_route: reached by the Statue City Cruises ferry from Liberty State Park or The Battery
jewels.blurb: "A memorial to all who pursued the American dream and have made this nation their adopted home"; over 12 million immigrants were processed here during 1892-1924. The Registry Room (the Great Hall) is where "millions of immigrants were inspected" and "required to pass both a medical and legal inspection".

jewels.name: Liberty Science Center
jewels.booking_route: own website booking (lsc.org; best rates at least one day in advance); groups of 10+ on 201-253-1310 or groups@lsc.org
jewels.blurb: At 222 Jersey City Boulevard, home of the Jennifer Chalsty Planetarium and exhibits including Energy Quest, Our Hudson Home, Bees to Bots and Microbes Rule!; parking $7.00 for cars, 750 spaces with overflow at the nearby Light Rail lot; NJ Transit riders save $5 per person (up to 4 passes). Closed October 5-7, 2026. NJDEP calls its planetarium "the largest planetarium in the western hemisphere".

jewels.name: Hudson River Waterfront Walkway (Liberty State Park promenade)
jewels.blurb: "A two-mile promenade, Hudson River Waterfront Walkway links two picnic and playground areas, the Nature Center and the CRRNJ Terminal while presenting visitors with a sweeping view of the Hudson River."

jewels.name: Liberty Landing Ferry to Brookfield Place, Manhattan
jewels.booking_route: pay onboard (per NJDEP); 10-trip booklet $80 and monthly pass $320 per the operator
jewels.blurb: Runs between Liberty Landing Marina, Warren Street (Jersey City) and Brookfield Place Terminal, New York; one-way adult $10.00, children 7-12 $5.00, 6 and under free, seniors $6.00; weekdays 6:30am-7:30pm, weekends 9:30am-7:30pm, hourly. The boat docks at the marina behind Liberty House Restaurant, where parking is available. NJDEP: "Fares are collected onboard."

jewels.name: Richard J. Sullivan Natural Area
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free public natural area
jewels.blurb: A 36-acre state Natural Area "consisting mainly of salt marsh, one of the few remaining tidal marshes of the Hudson River Estuary"; its berry-bearing shrubs and trees "make the area a haven for many different species of birds", with self-guided nature paths.

jewels.name: The Nature Center at Liberty State Park
jewels.booking_route: none needed to visit; programmes by email or phone with the Nature Center
jewels.blurb: "An environmental and historical education facility located on Freedom Way. Open year-round the center features exhibits focusing on the natural history and ecology of the Hudson River Estuary", open seven days a week, 8 a.m.-4 p.m.; contact LSPNatureCenter@dep.nj.gov or 201-915-3400 Option 4.

jewels.name: Liberty Landing Marina
jewels.booking_route: online transient booking via Molo (book.getmolo.com/libertylandingmarina/search) or (201) 985-8000
jewels.blurb: At 80 Audrey Zapp Dr, operated by Suntex; contract and transient slips, a fuel dock, a marine service centre and store, and a Certified Clean Marina designation. NJDEP: "250 slips, transient dockage, dry dock storage, a 24-hour fueling facility".

jewels.name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum, Lower Manhattan
jewels.booking_route: own website booking for the Museum (advance tickets); groups via reservations@911memorial.org or (212) 312-8800
jewels.blurb: At 180 Greenwich Street; honours nearly 3,000 people killed on September 11, 2001 and in the February 26, 1993 bombing. The Memorial is "free and open to the public seven days a week", daily 8 a.m.-8 p.m.; the Museum opens Wednesday-Monday 9 a.m.-7 p.m. (last entry 5:30 p.m.) with advance tickets. Reached from the park by the Liberty Landing Ferry to Brookfield Place.

jewels.name: Sea the City jet ski tours, Liberty Landing Marina
jewels.blurb: Departs Liberty Landing Marina, 84 Audrey Zapp Dr: "Sea The Highlights: 1-Hour Jet Ski Tour" from $185 and "Sea It All: 2-2.5 Hour Jet Ski Tour" from $335; "No Experience Necessary", ages 10+ with parent or guardian, maximum 9 guests per tour; also a hot tub boat tour.

jewels.name: Liberty State Park picnic areas and pavilions
jewels.booking_route: pavilions and group areas by application to libertystatepark@dep.nj.gov or 201-915-3400 Option 2; small groups first-come
jewels.blurb: Groups of 20 or fewer need no permit and may bring their own charcoal grill; seven Open-Air Group Picnic Areas (20-50 people) by free permit; Pavilion A (up to 120) $200 NJ resident / $250 non-resident and Pavilion B (up to 80) $150 / $200. "No propane grills, wood fires, generators"; no alcohol; "Wedding receptions/ceremonies are not permitted in the park."

jewels.name: Fishing and crabbing on Upper New York Bay
jewels.booking_route: none needed at the park; NJ Saltwater Recreational Registry Program applies
jewels.blurb: "The Upper New York Bay and Hudson River offer excellent opportunities for fishing. Common species include bluefish, shad, striped bass and blue claw crabs." Permitted under NJ Fish and Wildlife laws; "Consumption advisories may exist for certain species."

jewels.name: Boat launch and car-top kayak launch
jewels.booking_route: permits at the park office or the Parking Lot 2 ticket machine; car-top launch free
jewels.blurb: The trailered-boat launch in Parking Lot 2 runs 6 a.m.-10 p.m. year-round with mandatory permits (max trailer 23 ft); daily launch $20 NJ resident / $25 non-resident, seasonal $170 / $200. Kayaks and canoes launch from the East Jetty by Parking Lot 4 with "No permit required, no fee".

jewels.name: Maddy Rose, Liberty Landing
jewels.blurb: "Where bold flavors meet unbeatable waterfront city views": steaks, seafood and Mediterranean-inspired coastal cuisine with a Wine Spectator award-winning wine list, at 76 Audrey Zapp Dr; lunch Wed-Fri 12-3pm and Sat-Sun 11am-3pm, dinner Wed-Sun.

jewels.name: The Feathered Fox, Liberty Landing
jewels.booking_route: online reservation form on own website; phone (201) 419-6791
jewels.blurb: "Executive Chef Chris Siversen and the team behind Jersey City's Maritime Parc" reinvent the steakhouse "with stops that include inventive sushi and an exquisite raw bar", at 84 Audrey Zapp Drive.

jewels.name: Razza Pizza Artigianale, Jersey City
jewels.blurb: Wood-burning-oven pizza, small plates, beer, wine and seasonal cocktails at 275-277 Grove Street; NJ Monthly: "This stylish 40-seat restaurant serves one of the best wood-fired pizzas we've ever had." Mon-Thu 5-10pm, Fri-Sat 3-10pm, Sun 3-9pm.

jewels.name: Liberty House Restaurant
jewels.blurb: A park tenant at 76 Audrey Zapp Drive, named by NJDEP as one of the designated places where weddings and receptions may be held in the park; the marina describes it as offering "one of the region's most iconic settings for weddings, celebrations, corporate gatherings, and private events."

jewels.name: Maritime Parc
jewels.booking_route: phone (201) 413-0050, info@maritimeparc.com or online enquiry form
jewels.blurb: At 84 Audrey Zapp Drive in the park: a waterfront venue with a "280-degree wraparound terrace" overlooking the New York skyline and the Hudson River, with menus built on seasonal ingredients; NJDEP names "The Restaurant at Maritime Parc" as a park wedding tenant.

jewels.name: Nathan's Famous Hot Dogs, Liberty Landing
jewels.blurb: "Serving up World Famous Hot Dogs, Fresh Angus Burgers, Hand-dipped Chicken and more" on the far side of Liberty House; Thursday and Sunday 12-6pm, Friday and Saturday 12-7pm, May-October, weather dependent.

jewels.name: Liberty Harbor RV Park, Jersey City
jewels.blurb: An urban RV park at 11 Marin Blvd with "Water + 30A/50A electric" at each site and on-site dump stations (no individual sewer); "Nightly rates start at $170" with a 50% non-refundable deposit; "2 PATH stops to World Trade Center from Grove Street".

jewels.name: Hyatt Regency Jersey City on the Hudson
jewels.blurb: Listed by Hudson County tourism under Jersey City ("6 miles from NYC"), which singles out "the Hyatt Regency's waterfront vistas in Jersey City". The brand's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403).

jewels.name: Hyatt House Jersey City
jewels.blurb: Listed by Hudson County tourism under Jersey City, which names "the luxe Hyatt House's sweeping Lower Manhattan views". The brand's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403).

jewels.name: The Westin Jersey City Newport
jewels.blurb: Listed by Hudson County tourism among Jersey City hotels ("6 miles from NYC"). Marriott's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Canopy by Hilton Jersey City Arts District
jewels.blurb: Listed by Hudson County tourism among Jersey City hotels ("6 miles from NYC"). Hilton's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Collective Governors Island
jewels.blurb: Glamping on Governors Island in New York Harbor - Voyager and Urban Cowboy tents, Basecamp Cabins (including ADA units) and suites - with "dreamlike views of the Statue of Liberty"; "Open seasonally from May to November", an 8-minute ferry from Battery Maritime Terminal in Manhattan.

jewels.name: Sandy Hook Campground (Gateway National Recreation Area)
jewels.blurb: Tent camping only ("RVs cannot be accommodated"), May-September 2026: standard sites up to 6 people $30/night ($15 with Senior/Access Pass), larger sites up to 10 people $50, group sites $150; maximum 14 consecutive nights; "Alcohol, pets, and charcoal grills are NOT allowed at tent camping sites."

jewels.name: Picnic kit for Liberty State Park lawns: blankets, camp chairs, a sunshade and a charcoal grill
jewels.booking_route: affiliate link to the retailer (AvantLink); bought before the trip
jewels.blurb: NJ State Parks: "Groups of 20 people or less may also picnic on the grass, using their own blankets and camping chairs. A maximum of one Sunshade or canopy, no bigger than 10′ x 10′ is allowed per group. Small groups may bring their own charcoal grill"; "All spent coal must be disposed of in the designated 'Hot Coal' dumping bins."

jewels.name: Tick protection for the park's trails and natural area
jewels.booking_route: affiliate link to the retailer (AvantLink); bought before the trip
jewels.blurb: NJ State Parks rules for Liberty State Park, Tick Protection: "Use insect repellent, wear light-colored clothing, tuck pants into socks, stay on trails, check yourself when you get home, shower and wash clothes immediately."

jewels.name: Fishing and crabbing kit for Upper New York Bay
jewels.booking_route: affiliate link to the retailer (AvantLink); bought before the trip
jewels.blurb: NJ State Parks: "The Upper New York Bay and Hudson River offer excellent opportunities for fishing. Common species include bluefish, shad, striped bass and blue claw crabs. Fishing and crabbing are permitted in accordance with NJ Fish and Wildlife laws." "Please dispose of all stray fishing line properly."

jewels.name: Paddling kit for the car-top kayak launch
jewels.booking_route: affiliate link to the retailer (AvantLink); bought before the trip
jewels.blurb: NJ State Parks: "Car-top Boats (Kayaks, Canoes) No permit required, no fee. Car-top boats can be launched from the car-top boat launch located at the East Jetty by Parking Lot 4. Hours of operations are 6 a.m. to 10 p.m."

faq.q: Is there a ferry from Liberty State Park to the Statue of Liberty?
faq.a: Yes. NJDEP: "Ferry service from Liberty State Park to the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island is available throughout the year. For rates, ferry schedules, and to purchase tickets online please visit Statue City Cruises' website or call 1-877-LADY-TIX or 877-523-9849. Tickets may also be purchased at the ticket window inside the CRRNJ Terminal Building."

faq.q: How do I get to Ellis Island from Liberty State Park?
faq.a: By the Statue City Cruises ferry from the historic railroad terminal in the park. The NPS states that "Statue City Cruises is the ONLY ferry service authorized by the National Park Service to sell tickets for, and provide transportation to Liberty and Ellis Islands", and warns against buying from third-party vendors offering higher prices or non-landing boats.

faq.q: How do I get to Liberty State Park from NYC by ferry?
faq.a: The Liberty Landing Ferry runs between Brookfield Place Terminal in New York, Warren Street in Jersey City and Liberty Landing Marina in the park, weekdays 6:30am-7:30pm and weekends 9:30am-7:30pm. One-way fares: adult $10.00, children 7-12 $5.00, seniors $6.00, 6 and under free. The boat docks at the marina behind Liberty House Restaurant.

faq.q: Is Liberty State Park free?
faq.a: There is no entrance fee: NJDEP lists "Entrance Fee: None". Fees apply to the picnic pavilions, the trailered-boat launch and the ferries, not to entering the park.

faq.q: When does Liberty State Park close?
faq.a: NJDEP lists the gate hours as 6am-10pm, with the Park Office open 8am-4pm daily.

faq.q: Can you fish at Liberty State Park?
faq.a: Yes. "Fishing and crabbing are permitted in accordance with NJ Fish and Wildlife laws." Common species include "bluefish, shad, striped bass and blue claw crabs", and "Consumption advisories may exist for certain species."

faq.q: Can you grill at Liberty State Park?
faq.a: Charcoal only. "Small groups may bring their own charcoal grill, whether picnicking at our tables, or on the grass. All spent coal must be disposed of in the designated 'Hot Coal' dumping bins." The picnic rules also state: "No propane grills, wood fires, generators or access to electrical outlets."

faq.q: Is Liberty State Park dog friendly?
faq.a: Pets are allowed on a leash: "Pets must always be on a leash no longer than six feet in length and under the control of the owner. Please clean up after your pets."

faq.q: Is Liberty State Park a national park?
faq.a: No. It is a New Jersey state park, published by the Department of Environmental Protection under State Parks, Forests & Historic Sites, with its office in the CRRNJ Terminal Building, 1 Audrey Zapp Drive, Jersey City. The Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island, reached by ferry from the park, are National Park Service sites.

faq.q: Can you smoke in Liberty State Park?
faq.a: No. "State law prohibits the smoking of tobacco and use of electronic smoking (vaping) devices in all state parks, forests, historic sites, recreation areas, golf courses and marinas."

seo.meta_title: Liberty State Park, NJ: Statue of Liberty Ferry, CRRNJ Terminal & Jersey City | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: No entrance fee, the only New Jersey ferry to the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island, the CRRNJ Terminal, Empty Sky memorial and Liberty Science Center.
