name: Congaree National Park
line: Old-growth floodplain forest and synchronous fireflies

jewels.name: Boardwalk Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free park trail; entrance to the park is free
jewels.blurb: 2.6 miles round trip, rated EASY: "The boardwalk begins on a bluff at the Harry Hampton Visitor Center with an elevated section that leads down into the old-growth bottomland hardwood forest"; bald cypress and tupelo in the lowest elevations; "The boardwalk has benches along the way and is wheelchair and stroller accessible."

jewels.name: Synchronous Firefly Viewing Event
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov lottery (recreation.gov/ticket/facility/300008), one entry per household
jewels.blurb: "there are only three species of synchronous fireflies that can be found in North America"; the 2026 event ran May 13-20, entry by Recreation.gov lottery only - $1 non-refundable application, $24 more if awarded ($25 total), 145 passes per night, one passenger vehicle of up to 8 people per pass; viewing "best just after dark, usually between 9:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m."

jewels.name: Cedar Creek Canoe Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free, bring-your-own boat from Bannister Bridge or South Cedar Creek landings
jewels.blurb: "The marked Cedar Creek Canoe Trail winds approximately 15 miles through the Congaree Wilderness, starting at Bannister's Bridge and going all the way to the Congaree River"; through "some of the tallest trees in eastern North America". Bring your own boat - "the park does not rent out kayaks or canoes".

jewels.name: Harry Hampton Visitor Center
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free, 100 National Park Road, Hopkins, SC 29061, 803 776-4396
jewels.blurb: Open 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. daily, closed New Year's Day, Washington's Birthday, Columbus Day, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day; "The majority of trails begin from the Harry Hampton Visitor Center"; free self-guided Boardwalk brochure, park store, loaner wheelchairs.

jewels.name: Champion trees of the old-growth forest
jewels.booking_route: none needed - seen from the Boardwalk and park trails
jewels.blurb: "The average canopy height of the forest here is over 100 feet tall, and it contains the highest concentration of champion-sized trees anywhere in North America. The tallest tree in the park is the National Champion loblolly pine, which when last measured, is 170 feet tall and has a circumference of over 15 feet."

jewels.name: Weston Lake Trail (#3)
jewels.blurb: 4.5 miles round trip, MODERATE: "great views of Cedar Creek where otters and wading birds are regularly observed"; the eastern portion follows a cypress-tupelo slough "where many cypress knees can be seen sticking up out of the water."

jewels.name: Longleaf Campground
jewels.blurb: "10 individual and 4 group camping sites" at $15 and $25 a night; "Each site has a fire ring and a picnic table"; two vault toilets, no running water on site; tents and hammocks only, sleeping in vehicles prohibited; Senior and Access Pass holders receive 50% off. One accessible site (Site 1).

jewels.name: Kingsnake Trail (#6)
jewels.blurb: 12 miles, DIFFICULT: "a favorite trail for birders because of the diverse vegetation and proximity to Cedar Creek"; current condition "MAY BE DIFFICULT TO FOLLOW IN SOME AREAS; USE CAUTION".

jewels.name: Oakridge Trail (#4)
jewels.blurb: 7.1 miles round trip, DIFFICULT: "Passing through a rich stretch of old-growth forest, this trail traverses a subtle ridge where a variety of large oak trees grow"; low-lying sloughs make it "great for viewing wildlife like deer and wild turkey."

jewels.name: Boggy Gut Trail (#5)
jewels.blurb: 11.1 miles round trip, DIFFICULT: "This trail leads to the Congaree River"; "Approximately ten times a year the river overflows its banks and pulses water through the bottomland forest. When the river is low, a large sandbar may be visible." Current condition notes "NUMEROUS TREES DOWN DUE TO RECENT STORMS".

jewels.name: Bates Ferry Trail (#7)
jewels.blurb: 2.2 miles round trip, EASY, from Route 601 in the eastern section: follows "a 1920's ferry road south to the Congaree", a remnant of the colonial-era ferries "which once crossed near here"; the river bank "is steep and could potentially be slippery." RVs cannot use its parking lot.

jewels.name: Fork Swamp Trail (#9)
jewels.blurb: 0.6 miles, MODERATE: "runs alongside the southern channel of Bates Old River, an oxbow lake created by a hurricane in 1852."

jewels.name: Firefly Trail (#10)
jewels.booking_route: none needed outside the firefly event; event nights need a Recreation.gov pass
jewels.blurb: 1.8 miles round trip, EASY: "Visitors are treated to a magical light show produced by synchronous fireflies along this trail in late spring"; one of the four trails the NPS lists as not subject to periodic flooding.

jewels.name: Bluff Trail (#1)
jewels.blurb: 1.8 miles round trip, EASY: an upland loop north of the Visitor Center through "a young forest of loblolly and longleaf pines. Evidence of prescribed burns can be found along this trail."

jewels.name: Sims Trail (#2)
jewels.blurb: 3.2 miles round trip, EASY: follows an old gravel road from the Bluff Trail to Cedar Creek, crossing the boardwalk twice; the clearing at the Weston Lake junction "was the site of a hunt club where Harry Hampton was once a member."

jewels.name: Bluff Campground
jewels.blurb: "6 individual campsites" at $10 a night, "Each site has a fire ring and picnic table"; no restroom or water; about a 1-mile hike from the parking area.

jewels.name: Backcountry camping in the Congaree Wilderness
jewels.booking_route: free permit requested by email to the park, 72+ hours ahead
jewels.blurb: "Camping in the backcountry is FREE and requires a permit", requested by email at least 72 hours ahead; campers "may select any suitable place, as long as they remain 100 feet away from Cedar Creek"; 6 campers and 3 structures per site; "Open fires are not permitted in the backcountry". No permits are issued during the firefly event.

jewels.name: Fishing in Congaree National Park
jewels.booking_route: none needed in the park - a South Carolina fishing license is required (SCDNR)
jewels.blurb: "Fishing is allowed within Congaree National Park with a valid South Carolina fishing license"; permitted in all areas but not "from or within 25 feet of any man-made structure"; motorized boats prohibited; no minnows, amphibians or fish eggs as bait; state fish-consumption advisories apply on the Congaree River.

jewels.name: Congaree River Blue Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - a public river trail; self-guided or with a Columbia outfitter
jewels.blurb: American Rivers: the trail runs the Congaree River's 50 miles from near Columbia to Congaree National Park, where visitors can "paddle 20 miles of the Blue Trail"; it was "the first Blue Trail established by American Rivers and our partners in 2007." The NPS calls it "the 50-mile designated recreational paddle trail".

jewels.name: Carolina Outdoor Adventures
jewels.blurb: Started in 2015 by owner/operator Billy Easterbrooks; calls itself "one of a few companies permitted to operate in Congaree National Park"; a Congaree National Park feature kayak trip plus seasonal "Park after dark/Full Moon Paddles". The NPS lists it for guided ~3-hour kayak tours daily at 9:30 am, meeting at South Cedar Creek Landing. Irmo, SC; 803-381-2293.

jewels.name: J.K. Adventure Guides
jewels.blurb: "Let us help you explore our rivers in Columbia, SC or Congaree National Park by Kayaking or Canoeing"; trips listed for Congaree National Park, the Congaree, Saluda and Broad rivers and a Spider Lily trip. The NPS lists it for guided ~3-hour canoe and kayak tours at 9 am and 1 pm most days from South Cedar Creek Landing. (803) 397-0000.

jewels.name: Palmetto Outdoor
jewels.blurb: "a tubing and canoe outfitter located in the heart of West Columbia's River District", offering a year-round "guided Congaree National Park Canoe tour". The NPS lists it for guided ~3-hour canoe tours at 11 am most days from South Cedar Creek Landing.

jewels.name: River Runner Outdoor Center
jewels.booking_route: pickup at store in Columbia (contact not read - own site down)
jewels.blurb: Listed by the NPS among outfitters for Cedar Creek: "Mon-Sat 10am-6pm, Canoe and kayak rentals, pickup at store" - the park itself does not rent boats. Its own website did not resolve when fetched.

jewels.name: Harriet Barber House
jewels.booking_route: tours via the site's DONATIONS/TOURS page (hours and terms not read)
jewels.blurb: In Hopkins, named by the NPS as part of the Reconstruction Era National Historic Network. Its own history: "In 1872 Samuel Barber, a former slave, purchased lot number 35, which contained forty-two and one-half acres of the Hopkins Tract, one of six tracts in Lower Richland County purchased by the South Carolina Land Commission for redistribution"; Harriet Barber made the final payment and received title in 1879.

jewels.name: Poinsett State Park
jewels.blurb: Wedgefield: "1000 acres of diverse landscape" called the "mountains of the midlands"; 10-acre Levi Mill Lake with paddleboard, kayak, canoe and jon boat rentals; "25.6 miles of trails"; "50 campsites are available with 24 including power and 26 without power" plus "5 Rustic CCC Cabins"; admission "$3 adults"; hours "9am-dark, year round".

jewels.name: Sesquicentennial State Park
jewels.blurb: 9564 Two Notch Rd, Columbia: "1419 acres of parkland" with a 30-acre lake for paddling and fishing, "12 miles of hiking and biking trails", "78 standard campsites with electric and water for RVs or tents, 9 of which are full service"; admission "$6 adults"; open "8 a.m. - Sunset, daily". Named by the NPS on its nearby-attractions page.

jewels.name: Hotel Trundle
jewels.blurb: 1224 Taylor Street, Columbia's Main Street District: three restored historic buildings - the Rose Talbert Building (1914), Powell Furniture Building (1920) and Western Auto (1940); (803) 722-5000. The NPS places Columbia's lodging "approximately 20 minutes from the park" (nps.gov/cong eating & sleeping).

jewels.name: Cozy RV Retreat with Fire Pit and Outdoor Deck
jewels.blurb: A Hopkins caravan for four on 2.5 wooded acres, "20 minutes from downtown Columbia and 5 minutes from Congaree national park"; one queen bedroom, fire pit, deck, Wi-Fi, pets allowed; check-in 3:00-4:00 PM. Listed as "New" with no reviews.

jewels.name: Sweetwater Lake Campground
jewels.blurb: St. Matthews: glamping tents with "queen size bed, crisp, clean linen, two hammocks, grill, fire pit and firewood", plus RV and tent sites, a bathhouse with showers and a private 40-acre spring-fed lake; "Only one mile off of I26 exit 139"; 2-night minimum for glamping tents.

jewels.name: Camp at The Farm - Outside Inn
jewels.blurb: Santee: a working farm of 63+ acres with 25 full-hook-up RV sites (28-75 ft), 2 glamping units (a canvas tent and a renovated vintage RV), "nearly 2 miles of wooded walking trails", bathhouse, laundry, and Highland cattle, goats, pigs and donkeys with scheduled farm tours.

jewels.name: Big Rig Friendly RV Resort
jewels.blurb: West Columbia: 10 RV sites with full hookups - "20/30/50 Amp power service" plus sewer and water - complimentary Wi-Fi, campfires permitted, pets welcome. Hipcamp lists it 21 miles from Gadsden.

jewels.name: Motor Supply Co. Bistro
jewels.blurb: 920 Gervais St., Columbia: farm-to-table since 1989 with sustainably sourced meats, house-made sauces and desserts and South Carolina seafood; "Recommended in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide"; brunch Fri-Sun, dinner nightly.

jewels.name: The War Mouth
jewels.booking_route: walk-in; call ahead for groups of 6+ (803-569-6144)
jewels.blurb: 1209 Franklin Street, Columbia: "whole-hog BBQ slowly cooked over hardwood embers, alongside dishes created from locally sourced produce"; Mon 11:30 AM-9 PM, Tue-Sat 11:30 AM-10 PM, closed Sundays.

jewels.name: Mr. Friendly's New Southern Cafe
jewels.blurb: 2001-A Greene St, Historic Five Points, Columbia: "Since 1995, we have been serving New Southern Cuisine in a sophisticated, yet casual environment"; lunch weekdays, dinner Mon-Sat.

jewels.name: Bourbon
jewels.blurb: 1214 Main Street, Columbia: "Cajun-Creole classics like gumbo, jambalaya, and étouffée" and over 600 whiskeys; "Bourbon is walk-in only".

jewels.name: Lula Drake Wine Parlour
jewels.booking_route: phone 803.606.1968 (no reservation method on the page)
jewels.blurb: 1635 Main Street, Columbia: a wine parlour open Tue-Thu 5-10 pm and Fri-Sat 5-11 pm; 803.606.1968.

jewels.name: Soda City Market
jewels.booking_route: none needed - an open street market
jewels.blurb: "Columbia's weekly Main Street event inspired by traditional European street markets": every Saturday 9 a.m.-1 p.m. year-round on the 1300-1700 blocks of Main Street, about 200 vendors a week, each required to make or grow their own products.

jewels.name: Riverbanks Zoo & Garden
jewels.blurb: 500 Wildlife Parkway, Columbia: about 3,000 animals and 5,700 plant varieties; open 9:00am-5:00pm on the day read; the Saluda Skyride closed October 5-9 for staff training.

jewels.name: South Carolina State Museum
jewels.blurb: 301 Gervais Street, Columbia: "The largest and most comprehensive museum in the state", four floors of history, art, natural history and science; a 55ft digital-dome planetarium and a public observatory with a 1926 telescope; closed Mondays; $1 general admission on the first Sunday of each month.

jewels.name: Friends of Congaree Swamp
jewels.booking_route: none needed - membership and information via the website
jewels.blurb: "Advocates for Congaree National Park and its unique environment" - stewards of the park, "an International Biosphere Reserve, and a Globally Important Bird Area"; hosts research symposiums and publishes trail guides to the Boardwalk Loop, Bluff Trail and Cedar Creek. PO Box 7746, Columbia; 803-331-3366.

jewels.name: Congaree Riverkeeper
jewels.booking_route: none needed - information and volunteering via the website
jewels.blurb: "The river watchdog of the South Carolina Midlands, looking out for the Broad, Lower Saluda, and Congaree Rivers" - river cleanups, water-quality monitoring and policy advocacy. 803.760.3357.

jewels.name: The COMET Bus Route 47
jewels.booking_route: fares and schedules at catchthecometsc.gov (not read)
jewels.blurb: "The COMET offers regularly scheduled bus service to and from the park via Bus Route 47. The bus stop is located outside of the Harry Hampton Visitor Center near the middle parking lot"; the NPS warns ride-share services "may not provide pick up service from Congaree National Park."

jewels.name: Courtyard by Marriott Cayce
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "1125 Fort Congaree Trail, Cayce, SC 29033", "19 miles from Congaree National Park". Marriott's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: SpringHill Suites by Marriott Fort Jackson Columbia
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "170 East Exchange Blvd, I-77, Exit 9A, Columbia, SC 29209", "17 miles from Congaree National Park". Marriott's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Home2 Suites by Hilton Southeast Fort Jackson Columbia
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "7340 Garners Ferry Road, I-77, Exit 9A, Columbia, SC 29209", "16 miles from Congaree National Park". Hilton's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Cedar Creek paddling kit (PFD, whistle, map and compass)
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to rei.com (AvantLink); the boat itself rents from the Columbia outfitters the NPS names
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Before beginning your trip, make sure that you have the proper equipment. Besides a canoe or kayak, you should have a personal flotation device (PFD), whistle, weather appropriate clothing, water, food, sunscreen and insect repellent." "No matter the length of your trip, it is highly advisable to always carry a map and compass with you." Water levels "can fluctuate as much as 10 feet"; flood stage is set at 8 feet.

jewels.name: Bug spray and sunscreen for the floodplain
jewels.blurb: NPS lists "sunscreen and insect repellent" in the paddler's kit, and beyond the Ten Essentials: "You may need additional items depending on current conditions and the activity in which you participate (e.g. life jacket/PFD, bug spray, personal locator beacon)." Downed trees hide "spiders, wasps and other stinging insects, and snakes".

jewels.name: Backpacking stove for backcountry camping
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Open fires are not permitted in the backcountry. Campers are permitted the use of a backpacking stove for cooking." There are no designated backcountry sites, and "It is advisable to check the river forecast prior to your visit to ensure that a rise in water levels is not forecast."

jewels.name: Personal locator beacon where the cell signal drops
jewels.blurb: NPS names a "personal locator beacon" among the extras beyond the Ten Essentials, and warns: "Cell service can be unreliable in the park, so you may have to find a place where there is reception, or send someone with a cell phone to make the call."

faq.q: Is Congaree National Park free?
faq.a: Yes. The NPS states: "Entrance to Congaree National Park is free. There is no fee to enter the park." Camping, the picnic shelter and the firefly event carry their own fees.

faq.q: Can you camp in Congaree National Park?
faq.a: Yes, in tents or hammocks. Longleaf Campground has "10 individual and 4 group camping sites" ($15 and $25 a night) and Bluff Campground has "6 individual campsites" ($10), both reserved "through Recreation.gov or by calling 1-877-444-6777". Backcountry camping needs a free permit requested at least 72 hours ahead. RVs and sleeping in vehicles are not allowed.

faq.q: Can you kayak in Congaree National Park?
faq.a: Yes. "The marked Cedar Creek Canoe Trail winds approximately 15 miles through the Congaree Wilderness, starting at Bannister's Bridge and going all the way to the Congaree River." You bring your own boat or go with one of the outfitters the NPS lists.

faq.q: Can you rent kayaks at Congaree National Park?
faq.a: Not from the park: "No, the park does not rent canoes or kayaks. Canoes or kayaks can be rented through outfitters in the city of Columbia."

faq.q: When is firefly season in Congaree National Park?
faq.a: "Every year, Congaree National Park hosts synchronous fireflies for approximately two weeks between mid-May and mid-June." The 2026 viewing event ran May 13-20, with entry by a Recreation.gov lottery that opened April 7 and closed April 14.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Congaree National Park?
faq.a: The NPS says the park "is best experienced in the spring and fall when temperatures are at their most comfortable and insects are generally not a problem." Fall colors peak "between the end of October and early November", and autumn water levels are "ideal" for paddling Cedar Creek.

faq.q: Is Congaree National Park dog friendly?
faq.a: Yes: "Pets are allowed on all trails, including the boardwalk, as well as in the campgrounds." They must be on a leash no longer than 6 feet and never left unattended. No pets are allowed during the firefly event; service animals are welcome.

faq.q: Can you fish in Congaree National Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Fishing is allowed within Congaree National Park with a valid South Carolina fishing license." It is not allowed "from or within 25 feet of any man-made structure, including bridges, boardwalk, and overlooks", and boats with inboard or outboard motors are prohibited.

faq.q: What is the closest airport to Congaree National Park?
faq.a: "The nearest major airport to Congaree National Park is Columbia Metropolitan Airport which is located approximately 30 minutes from the park." Charlotte Douglas and Charleston International are each about 2 hours away, per the NPS.

faq.q: Is Congaree National Park a swamp?
faq.a: The NPS describes it as a floodplain: "A floodplain, also known as a bottomland, is a low-lying area along a stream or river that will periodically be covered by water throughout the year. A swamp is an area that has significant areas of water flowing over it throughout the entire year... a floodplain will not always be a swamp."

seo.meta_title: Congaree National Park: Boardwalk, Cedar Creek & Fireflies | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: Free entry, a 2.6-mile accessible boardwalk, 15 miles of Cedar Creek canoe trail, May's synchronous fireflies by lottery, and where to camp and stay nearby.

name: Everglades National Park
line: Sawgrass, mangroves and the Anhinga Trail

jewels.name: Anhinga Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - covered by the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: "A self-guiding pavement and boardwalk trail winding through and over sawgrass marsh and freshwater slough"; 0.8 miles (1,200 meters) round trip, wheelchair accessible; visitors may encounter "alligators, fish, turtles, anhingas, and many other birds, especially during the winter". At the Royal Palm area; pets not allowed.

jewels.name: Shark Valley Tram Tour
jewels.booking_route: own website (sharkvalleytramtours.com, "Click to Book a Tram or Bike Tour") or 305-221-8455
jewels.blurb: "Guided two-hour tram tours are offered along a fifteen-mile loop trail"; Adults $31, Seniors $24, Children (3-12) $16 per the NPS listing. The operator, Shark Valley Tram Tours, describes "Park-trained naturalists" and a stop at the halfway observation tower; open 8:30am - 6:00pm daily; 305-221-8455.

jewels.name: Flamingo Lodge
jewels.booking_route: flamingoeverglades.com/flamingo-lodge-restaurant/ or 855-708-2207 (own site refused the fetch, HTTP 403)
jewels.blurb: Opened October 27, 2023, built and run by "Everglades Guest Services, LLC, an authorized concessioner of the NPS": 24 rooms - "eight two-bedroom suites that can accommodate up to six guests", "twelve one-bedroom suites suitable for up to four guests" and "four studios designed for two guests" - with four ADA accessible rooms. The NPS release stated nightly rates from $159 (June-October) and $259 (November-May), plus tax.

jewels.name: Flamingo Boat Tours
jewels.blurb: Two 90-minute options from Flamingo Marina - the Backcountry Whitewater Bay tour and the Florida Bay tour; Adults $40, Children $20, per the NPS listing. Pets not permitted.

jewels.name: Shark Valley loop and observation tower
jewels.booking_route: none needed to walk or ride your own bike; rentals from Shark Valley Tram Tours on site
jewels.blurb: "Shark Valley Visitor Center provides the gateway to a panoramic 15-mile loop trail and observation tower"; the tower is "located halfway along the loop" and "offers panoramic views of the Everglades." Bicycle rentals on site ($25 per bike per the NPS listing). "During peak visitor season...parking is extremely limited and usually fills by 10 am."

jewels.name: Ten Thousand Islands Boat Tour
jewels.booking_route: operator website (evergladesnationalparkboattoursgulfcoast.com, which redirected to evergladers.com when fetched; no booking details read)
jewels.blurb: From the Gulf Coast: Everglades National Park Adventures runs the Ten Thousand Islands boat tour on a 49-passenger pontoon; tours "depart daily" from 929 Dupont Street in Everglades City, about two miles north of the visitor center. The NPS lists it at 90 minutes.

jewels.name: Flamingo Campground
jewels.blurb: "one of two drive-in campgrounds accessible from the Homestead entrance of the park. It offers solar-heated showers, two dump stations, picnic tables, grills, and an amphitheater"; 274 sites, 41 with electric hookups, 40 walk-to sites, 3 group sites; RV with electric $50 Mon-Thu / $60 Fri-Sun, tent or non-electric $33 / $38.50; maximum RV length 35 feet; open year-round.

jewels.name: Flamingo glamping tents and houseboats
jewels.blurb: The NPS lists overnight stays at Flamingo "in fully equipped houseboats, in a winter or summer glamping tent, or on the campgrounds"; the concessioner, Everglades Guest Services, operates "campsites, eco-tents and houseboats".

jewels.name: Everglades Wilderness Waterway
jewels.booking_route: wilderness campsites reserved on Recreation.gov (90 days ahead)
jewels.blurb: "The 99-mile Wilderness Waterway attracts interest because it connects Flamingo and Everglades City"; "Most paddlers allow at least eight days to complete the trip"; "recommended for experienced paddlers only", with a vehicle shuttle arranged in advance for one-way trips.

jewels.name: Wilderness camping and chickees
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov; the NPS Gulf Coast page states a $21 administrative fee plus nightly per-person charges
jewels.blurb: "ground sites, beach sites, and elevated camping platforms ('chickees')" reached by canoe, kayak, motorboat or on foot; "A wilderness camping permit is required for all wilderness campsites"; since January 2, 2023 "all Marjory Stoneman Douglas Wilderness campsites will only be available for advanced reservations on Recreation.gov", opening 90 days ahead.

jewels.name: Gumbo Limbo Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - covered by the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: "The Gumbo-Limbo trail is a self-guided, paved trail meandering through a shaded, jungle-like hardwood hammock"; 0.4 miles (600 meters) round trip, wheelchair accessible, with accessible restrooms, a bottle-filling station and benches.

jewels.name: Long Pine Key Campground
jewels.blurb: 108 sites for tents or RVs with no electrical hookups, plus a group site; $33 Mon-Thu and $38.50 Fri-Sun, group site $60; maximum RV length 35 feet; "open seasonally November - April (closed May to October)"; "one of two frontcountry camping options run by the 'Flamingo Adventures' concession."

jewels.name: Ernest F. Coe Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: "the visitor center closest to Homestead for Everglades National Park. It is open 365 days a year and offers educational displays, orientation films, and informational brochures"; 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM daily, off Palm Drive (State Road 9336) from Florida City.

jewels.name: Guy Bradley Visitor Center, Flamingo
jewels.blurb: "provides access to the southernmost region of Everglades National Park" with rangers, displays, a gift shop and backcountry permits; "roughly 38 miles (1 hour) south of the park main entrance"; 8 am to 5 pm daily November 16 - April 30, closed Wednesday and Thursday in summer.

jewels.name: Marjory Stoneman Douglas Visitor Center (Gulf Coast)
jewels.booking_route: none needed - rangers on site or (786) 758-0635
jewels.blurb: "open daily from 9am to 5pm. The site features a kayak launch, wildlife watching, and a picnic area"; reached from I-75 exit 80, 20 miles south on State Road 29 to Everglades City. Park passes cannot be bought here - only at Shark Valley or Homestead.

jewels.name: Eco Pond
jewels.booking_route: none needed - covered by the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: "Located on the road to the Flamingo Campground, Eco Pond has a ½ mile loop trail." The NPS lists birding at Flamingo among its featured activities.

jewels.name: Bobcat Boardwalk Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - covered by the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: At Shark Valley: "A short accessible .2 miles trail that winds through a willowhead."

jewels.name: Coot Bay Pond
jewels.booking_route: none needed - bring your own boat or rent at Flamingo Marina
jewels.blurb: "This small pond opens up to Coot Bay, and is great for paddling and wildlife viewing."

jewels.name: Flamingo Marina
jewels.booking_route: Everglades Guest Services (flamingoeverglades.com, 855-708-2207) for slips and rentals
jewels.blurb: "The Flamingo Marina, open year-round, can accommodate boats with electric and water hookups"; the Flamingo Fish Cleaning Station "is located adjacent to public boat ramps and the marina store". The NPS lists "bicycle and boat rentals" at Flamingo.

jewels.name: Fishing in Everglades National Park
jewels.booking_route: none needed in the park - a Florida fishing licence is required
jewels.blurb: "A Florida fishing license is required, unless you are under 16 years of age or you are a Florida resident over the age of 65"; freshwater rules apply north of Nine Mile Pond and saltwater rules south of it.

jewels.name: Flamingo Restaurant
jewels.booking_route: walk-in at Flamingo (no reservation method read)
jewels.blurb: "The Flamingo Restaurant, adjacent to the Flamingo Lodge, is open daily for breakfast, lunch, and dinner"; the NPS release describes "traditional South Florida fare while enjoying views of nearby Florida Bay" and a full-service bar.

jewels.name: Coopertown Airboats
jewels.blurb: One of "three authorized airboat businesses inside Everglades National Park" on the Tamiami Trail, per the NPS. Its own page: airboat rides covering "approximately 5 miles of this unique environment", standard and private tours, gift shop; 22700 Southwest 8th Street, Miami, FL 33194; (305) 226-6048.

jewels.name: Everglades Alligator Farm
jewels.booking_route: FareHarbor (fareharbor.com/embeds/book/everglades) from the own website, or phone
jewels.blurb: "Airboat Rides & Alligator Shows" - airboat rides with 360° spins, 2,000+ alligators, animal encounters; family-owned since 1992; 40351 SW 192nd Ave, Homestead, FL 33034; daily 9:00 AM - 5:30 PM; +1 (305) 247-2628.

jewels.name: Everglades Adventures Kayak & Eco Tours
jewels.blurb: 605 Buckner Ave N, Everglades City: guided kayak tours "with the guidance and knowledge of a trained naturalist" (from $89), guided bike tours (from $79), kayak and canoe rentals (from $29), Wilderness Waterway trips of 5-10 days (from $725) and kayak-camping combos with meals and gear; daily 8:00 am - 9:00 pm; 239-294-8487.

jewels.name: Ivey House
jewels.blurb: 605 Buckner Ave N, Everglades City: "Enjoy peaceful accommodations by night and exciting adventures by day!" - king or queen rooms beside "a screened-in courtyard and pool"; arranges airboat tours, seasonal kayak tours "that leave right from the hotel" and fishing charters; 239-695-3299.

jewels.name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Homestead Florida City
jewels.blurb: Marriott's Fairfield Inn & Suites at "60 SW 352nd St., Florida City, FL 33034" - Florida City is where Palm Drive (State Road 9336) leads to the park's main entrance, per the NPS. Marriott's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: TownePlace Suites by Marriott Miami Homestead
jewels.blurb: "935 Northeast 30th St., Homestead, FL 33033 ~9.10 miles northeast" of Florida City, as the listing states. Marriott's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Hampton Inn & Suites Homestead Miami South
jewels.blurb: Hilton's Hampton Inn & Suites at "2855 NE 9th St., Homestead, FL 33033 ~9.02 miles northeast" of Florida City, as the listing states. Hilton's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Florida City
jewels.blurb: IHG's Holiday Inn Express & Suites at "35200 South Dixie Highway, Florida City, FL 33034", as the listing states. IHG's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Baker's Cay Resort Key Largo, Curio Collection by Hilton
jewels.blurb: Hilton's Curio Collection resort at "97000 Overseas Highway, Key Largo, FL", listed among hotels near Florida City - the top-tier brand option within reach of the Homestead entrance. Hilton's own page was not fetched (hilton.com returned HTTP 403 for the Homestead property), so nothing else about it is stated here.

jewels.name: Everglades Isle
jewels.blurb: "A luxury motorcoach resort and marina nestled in beautiful Everglades City on Florida's Gulf Coast": 59 motorcoach lots, 2 luxury villas and 74 boat slips; pool, spa, fitness center, clubhouse, pickleball and a full-service bar; "All motorcoaches must be Class A or Super C, 36'+ in length, and twelve years old or newer." 803 N Collier Ave; (239) 695-2600.

jewels.name: Chokoloskee Island Resort
jewels.blurb: 1150 Hamilton Lane, Chokoloskee: a waterfront "All Age RV Park" with 40+ RV sites with water and power, trailer and cottage rentals, a "Marina" and "Boat Launch Ramp", docks, a tiki gathering spot and boat and kayak rentals; front desk 239-695-2414.

jewels.name: Miami Everglades RV Resort
jewels.blurb: 20675 SW 162nd Ave, Miami: "Everglades National Park is less than 10 miles away"; clubhouse, pool ("currently closed until further notice"), shuffleboard, mini golf, dog park, rental campers; "Open Year Round"; 305-233-5300.

jewels.name: Larry & Penny Thompson Park Campground
jewels.blurb: Miami-Dade County park: "The campground consists of 240 separate campsites for recreational vehicles, each with electrical, sewer and water hookups"; tent sites "Daily rate: $25 + tax", check-in 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.

jewels.name: Trail Lakes Campground
jewels.booking_route: own website ("click here to go camping") or 1-800-504-6554
jewels.blurb: 40904 Tamiami Trail, Ochopee, in Big Cypress National Preserve: "chickee huts" for glamping - "Native American built chickee cottages" - plus air-conditioned rustic cabins, RV sites to 50 feet with 30/50 amp and water, primitive tent camping, and swamp buggy and airboat tours; 1-800-504-6554. The Dyrt lists it "7mi from Everglades City".

jewels.name: Robert Is Here
jewels.blurb: "The World's Best Fruit Stand", "Since 1959": exotic and tropical fruit, "out-of-this-world milkshakes" made with hand-cut fruit, a petting zoo and picnic areas; 19200 SW 344th St, Homestead - on the road to the park entrance; "Open everyday from 9am-6pm", closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day; (305) 246-1592.

jewels.name: Schnebly Redland's Winery
jewels.blurb: "the southernmost winery in the United States", making "exotic tropical fruit wines", with Miami Brewing Company and a farm-to-table restaurant; 30205 SW 217th Ave, Homestead; wine tasting $25, tour $16, tour and tasting $41; (305) 242-1224.

jewels.name: Shiver's BBQ
jewels.blurb: "authentic hickory smoked barbecue" in Homestead since 1950; 28001 South Dixie Highway, Homestead, FL 33033; (305) 248-2272.

jewels.name: Triad Seafood Market & Cafe
jewels.blurb: Restaurant and seafood market at 401 W School Dr, Everglades City: "All-You-Can-Eat Stone Crab Season Begins October 15"; seasonal from October through spring - "Please call ahead for current hours and to confirm stone crab availability"; 239-695-2662.

jewels.name: HavAnnA Cafe of the Everglades
jewels.blurb: A "casual family owned-restaurant that many visitors to Chokoloskee make a special point of enjoying for breakfast, lunch, or early dinner" - seafood with Latin influences, blackened grouper, stone crab and Cuban sandwiches; 191 Smallwood Drive, Chokoloskee; "open Wednesday-Sunday from 7am to 4pm"; 239-695-2214. Its own site (havanacafeoftheeverglades.com) returned 404.

faq.q: How much is Everglades National Park?
faq.a: The NPS fees page lists "Private Vehicle: $35.00" ("Good for 7 consecutive days"), "Motorcycle: $30.00", "Per Person: $20.00" and "Annual Entrance - Park: $70.00". Only "Digital passes or credit/debit cards" are accepted, at the Homestead and Shark Valley entrance stations or online.

faq.q: Can you camp in Everglades National Park?
faq.a: Yes. Flamingo Campground (274 sites, 41 with electric hookups, open year-round) and Long Pine Key Campground (108 sites, "open seasonally November - April") are booked through Everglades Guest Services at 1-855-708-2207. Wilderness ground sites, beach sites and chickees need a permit, and "all Marjory Stoneman Douglas Wilderness campsites will only be available for advanced reservations on Recreation.gov."

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Everglades National Park?
faq.a: The NPS describes the dry season, "from about December to mid-May, with temperatures ranging from the low 50s to upper 70s... and low humidity", against a wet season "from about mid-May to November" with temperatures "into the low 90s". December through April is peak visitation because "the warm winters...attract the largest variety of wading birds."

faq.q: Can you drive through Everglades National Park?
faq.a: Not end to end. The park has three entrances - the main Homestead entrance, Shark Valley on U.S. 41 and the Gulf Coast in Everglades City - and "these entrances do not interconnect within the park." From Homestead, the main park road leads to Royal Palm and Flamingo.

faq.q: Are there airboat tours in Everglades National Park?
faq.a: Yes: "There are three authorized airboat businesses inside Everglades National Park. All three are located along the Tamiami Trail (Coopertown, Everglades Safari Park, and Gator Park)."

faq.q: Can you swim in Everglades National Park?
faq.a: Largely no: "Swimming/Snorkeling is prohibited in all canals, ponds, freshwater lakes, marked channels, and boat basins inside the park."

faq.q: Can you fish in Everglades National Park?
faq.a: Yes, with a licence: "A Florida fishing license is required, unless you are under 16 years of age or you are a Florida resident over the age of 65." Freshwater rules apply north of Nine Mile Pond and saltwater rules south of it.

faq.q: Where can you stay in Everglades National Park?
faq.a: Only at Flamingo: the NPS lists stays "in Flamingo Lodge, in fully equipped houseboats, in a winter or summer glamping tent, or on the campgrounds", plus Long Pine Key campground near the Homestead entrance and "numerous backcountry sites for wilderness camping". Outside the park, the NPS points to Homestead, Florida City, Miami, Everglades City and Chokoloskee.

faq.q: When was Everglades National Park established?
faq.a: "Established in 1947 as the first national park created for its biodiversity, Everglades National Park protects 1.5 million acres of wetland, forest, and marine habitats".

faq.q: Is Everglades National Park open?
faq.a: "Everglades National Park is open 7 days a week, 24 hours a day." Staffed entrance hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. daily, and the Ernest F. Coe, Shark Valley and Gulf Coast visitor centers open 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM.

seo.meta_title: Everglades National Park: Anhinga Trail, Shark Valley & Flamingo | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: Three entrances that do not connect, the Anhinga Trail, Shark Valley's 15-mile loop, Flamingo Lodge and campgrounds, airboats and where to stay nearby.

name: Biscayne National Park
line: Coral reefs, island keys and shipwrecks off Miami

jewels.name: Biscayne National Park Institute boat, snorkel and paddle tours
jewels.booking_route: FareHarbor on the Institute's own site, 786-335-3644, or the park store
jewels.blurb: "a non-profit where your purchase directly benefits the park"; trips include the "Boca Chita Key Heritage Cruise from Coconut Grove", "Snorkel Experience", "Jones Lagoon Eco-Paddle", "Kayak the Seagrasses of Stiltsville" and "Sail, Paddle and Snorkel", from the Dante Fascell Visitor Center, Dinner Key Marina and the Deering Estate; most standard trips $65-$219. The NPS: "Advance reservations are advised", 786-335-3644.

jewels.name: Boca Chita Key
jewels.booking_route: first-come, first-served; $25 day-use docking Fri-Mon and federal holidays, $60 a night camping and docking
jewels.blurb: "the park's most popular island": "beautiful waterfront views, a grassy camping area, picnic tables and grills. Toilets are available, but there are no showers, sinks or drinking water." Harbor entrance about four feet at low tide; pets prohibited, "including on boats docked in the harbor".

jewels.name: Maritime Heritage Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free; reached by private boat or an Institute snorkel/dive trip
jewels.blurb: "Six wrecks, spanning nearly a century and a wide variety of sizes and vessel types" - Arratoon Apcar (1878), Erl King (1891), Alicia (1905), Lugano (1913), Mandalay (1966) and an unidentified 19th-century wooden sailing vessel - plus the Fowey Rocks Lighthouse; "Access to the sites on the trail is by boat only." Three wrecks suit scuba.

jewels.name: Dante Fascell Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: "9700 SW 328th Street, Sir Lancelot Jones Way, Homestead, FL 33033", at the end of SW 328th Street; "open 7 days a week from 9 AM-5 PM". Only selected America the Beautiful passes are sold here - "4th grade, Access, and U.S. military passes". Pets are not allowed inside.

jewels.name: Elliott Key
jewels.booking_route: first-come, first-served; $25 day-use docking Fri-Mon and federal holidays, $60 a night camping and docking
jewels.blurb: "The largest island in the park", once "a thriving community of pioneers engaged in pineapple farming, sponging, wrecking"; campground with restrooms, "cold water showers", drinking water, tables and grills; "There are 33 boat slips in the marina", about 2½ feet deep at low tide. Leashed pets allowed in developed areas.

jewels.name: Mandalay shipwreck
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free; by private boat or an Institute snorkel trip
jewels.blurb: The 1966 wreck on the Maritime Heritage Trail that the NPS names as particularly accessible to snorkellers; "Access to the sites on the trail is by boat only."

jewels.name: Stiltsville
jewels.booking_route: seen from the water; entry to the structures by Stiltsville Trust permit only
jewels.blurb: "Seeming to float above Biscayne Bay's shallow seagrass beds, Stiltsville has a colorful history that dates back to the 1930s"; 27 structures in 1960, "only seven buildings standing" after Hurricane Andrew in 1992. "Public access to the structures themselves is by permit only" (Stiltsville Trust).

jewels.name: Fowey Rocks Lighthouse
jewels.booking_route: none needed - by boat; the lighthouse itself is closed to the public
jewels.blurb: "The newest addition to the trail is the Fowey Rocks Lighthouse", built 1878; "not open to the public", but "snorkeling is great around the base."

jewels.name: Jones Lagoon
jewels.blurb: Named by the NPS among the concession tours - "exploring the seldom seen wonders of Jones Lagoon" - and run by the Institute as the "Jones Lagoon Eco-Paddle". "Trips may be booked by using the link below, by calling 786-335-3644 or by stopping at the park store."

jewels.name: Spite Highway, Elliott Key
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free trail; island reached by private boat
jewels.blurb: A trail "approximately six miles down the center of the island" through maritime forest; Elliott Key also has "a mile-long loop trail" that "starts near the campground".

jewels.name: Convoy Point grounds and canoe/kayak launch
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free; bring your own paddle craft
jewels.blurb: The mainland grounds beside the visitor center and the canoe/kayak launch are "open 7 days a week from 7 AM-5:30 PM"; leashed pets are allowed on "The grounds at Convoy Point".

jewels.name: Fishing and lobstering in Biscayne National Park
jewels.booking_route: none needed in the park - a Florida fishing licence (state) is required
jewels.blurb: "With limited exceptions, a valid Florida fishing license is required to fish in the park. Children under 16 years of age do not require a license." "The taking of lobster is prohibited in the Biscayne Bay/Card Sound Lobster Sanctuary", and in five Coral Reef Protection Areas marked with yellow buoys; lionfish may be speared without a licence using lionfish-specific devices.

jewels.name: Adams Key
jewels.blurb: A day-use island "Open 9 AM until official sunset daily", reached across the navigable waters, which are "Open 24 hours a day".

jewels.name: Manatee watching
jewels.booking_route: none needed - ask a ranger at the Dante Fascell Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: Asked whether manatees can be seen: "yes, ask a park ranger about recent sightings. Manatees are more common during the colder months."

jewels.name: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park
jewels.booking_route: Peek online booking from the concession site, or (305) 451-6300
jewels.blurb: Key Largo, MM 102.5: "The first undersea park in the United States", about 70 nautical square miles; a 65-foot glass-bottom catamaran for up to 130 passengers, 2.5-hour snorkel tours with about 1.5 hours in the water, scuba trips, and kayak/canoe rentals on "50 miles of natural mangrove wilderness trails". (305) 451-6300. The state-park page refused the fetch (HTTP 403); this is the concession's own site.

jewels.name: Rainbow Reef Dive Center
jewels.blurb: Key Largo: "Dive & snorkel trips, gear rental sales and service, all levels of dive training, hotel accommodations, and dive/hotel packages"; reef, wreck, drift and night dives at 18-120 feet; a PADI 5 Star Instructor/Career Development Center. 1-800-457-4354 / 305-451-7171.

jewels.name: Homestead Bayfront Park
jewels.booking_route: pay at the gate; marina services through the park office
jewels.blurb: Miami-Dade County park "adjacent to Biscayne National Park": the "Atoll Pool" swim area ("Sunrise to sunset, seven days a week"), a beach, the Herbert Hoover Marina with "boat-launching ramps" and fuel, and La Playa Grill Seafood Bar. Vehicle entry "$5 weekdays; $7 weekends and holidays"; boat ramps open "six a.m. to ten p.m."

jewels.name: Larry & Penny Thompson Park campground
jewels.booking_route: phone the park, (305) 232-1049; tent sites first-come, first-served
jewels.blurb: 12451 SW 184th St., Miami, beside Zoo Miami: a 270-acre county park with "240 campsites for recreational vehicles as well as an individual tent area", "four large restroom and laundry facilities with hot showers, water and electrical hook-ups for all RVs and complimentary WiFi", and a freshwater swimming lake. Tent sites first-come, first-served. (305) 232-1049. Sourced to Greater Miami's tourism board.

jewels.name: Goldcoaster RV Resort
jewels.blurb: 34850 S.W. 187th Ave., Homestead: "Surrounded by Everglades National Park and Biscayne National Park"; pool, hot tub/sauna, arcade, playground, pavilion, shuffleboard, laundry and internet; "100% pet-friendly", a "resort-style gated community" where about 90% of trailers are permanently stationed.

jewels.name: Gate to the Keys
jewels.blurb: Homestead: three RV-only sites (Rabbit, Rooster, Peacock) with electric and water hookups among "Banana, Lychee, Mangos, avocado" trees; campfires allowed, pets welcome; about 2 miles from Robert Is Here; "Within a 30-minute drive from the Everglades Ernest F. Coe Visitor Center" (listing's own wording). Hipcamp listing, not the host's own site.

jewels.name: Sun Outdoors Key Largo
jewels.blurb: 97680 Overseas Hwy, MM 97.5, Key Largo: 24 full-hookup RV sites plus 20 motel rooms, efficiencies and cottages; boat launch, docks, private beach, "free kayaks", tiki area and BBQ. Hipcamp lists it 27 miles from Homestead. Hipcamp listing, not the operator's own site.

jewels.name: Tropical Farm Stay Retreat - Cozy Tiny Barn
jewels.blurb: Homestead, on "a peaceful fruit farm in the heart of the Redlands": a converted horse barn tiny home for 4 with "full private bathroom with a walk-in shower", kitchen, Wi-Fi and fenced patio, among tropical fruit trees, chickens and a mini horse; "Within a 30-minute drive from the Dante Fascell Visitor Center" (listing's own wording). Listed on Hipcamp's Homestead glamping page.

jewels.name: Baker's Cay Resort Key Largo, Curio Collection by Hilton
jewels.blurb: 97000 Overseas Highway, Key Largo: 15 acres of a former pineapple plantation overlooking Florida Bay; five dining venues (Calusa, Dry Rocks, The Pool Bar, Tiki Bar, Dock to Dish), Scupper's watersports rentals, pools, and day resort passes for non-guests. +1-305-852-5553.

jewels.name: Courtyard by Marriott Miami Homestead
jewels.blurb: 2905 NE 9th Street, Homestead: outdoor pool, free Wi-Fi and The Bistro on site; 10 minutes from Homestead-Miami Speedway. Sourced to Priceline's Homestead hotel listing; marriott.com was not fetched (brand sites returned HTTP 403 in this session).

jewels.name: TownePlace Suites by Marriott Miami Homestead
jewels.blurb: 935 NE 30th Terrace, Homestead: studios and suites with "complimentary buffet breakfast" and an outdoor pool. Sourced to Priceline's Homestead hotel listing.

jewels.name: Hampton Inn & Suites by Hilton Homestead Miami South
jewels.blurb: 2855 NE 9th Street, Homestead: "daily continental breakfast and coffee" and a heated outdoor pool; 11 miles from the Everglades per the listing. Sourced to Priceline's Homestead hotel listing; hilton.com returned HTTP 403.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Florida City
jewels.blurb: 35200 S. Dixie Hwy., Florida City: outdoor pool and "hot breakfast buffet", 2.5 miles from downtown Homestead per the listing. Sourced to Priceline's Homestead hotel listing; the hotel's own site did not connect.

jewels.name: Robert Is Here
jewels.blurb: 19200 SW 344th St, Homestead: "The World's Best Fruit Stand" since 1959 - fresh produce, handmade milkshakes and smoothies, a petting zoo and picnic areas; open daily 9am-6pm (closed Thanksgiving and Christmas). (305) 246-1592.

jewels.name: Black Point Ocean Grill
jewels.booking_route: phone 305-258-3918 (no reservation method on the page)
jewels.blurb: 24775 S.W. 87th Avenue, Cutler Bay, at Black Point Marina: "fresh seafood, produce, hand cut steaks, salads and sandwiches" on the water; open daily from 11am, to midnight Friday and Saturday. 305-258-3918.

jewels.name: Schnebly Redland's Winery & Brewery
jewels.booking_route: OpenTable for the restaurant; tastings and tours on the own site
jewels.blurb: 30205 SW 217th Ave, Homestead: "The southernmost winery in the United States", tropical fruit wines, an on-site brewery and a thatched tiki restaurant; wine tasting $25, winery tour $16, combo $41. (305) 242-1224.

jewels.name: Shiver's BBQ
jewels.blurb: 28001 S Dixie Hwy, Homestead: "Since 1950" - "slow smoked ribs, brisket, pulled pork and Southern sides", hickory-smoked. (305) 248-2272.

jewels.name: The Fish House Restaurant and Seafood Market
jewels.blurb: 102401 Overseas Highway, Key Largo: "the finest seafood available" with daily catches and an on-site seafood market that will "cook your catch"; "No reservations needed, just come on in". 305.451.4665.

jewels.name: Key Largo Conch House
jewels.blurb: 100211 Overseas Hwy, Key Largo: "Fresh Local Seafood and Produce" and "homemade desserts" at breakfast, lunch and dinner; breakfast 8-11 am weekdays, dinner from 4 pm daily. 305-453-4844.

jewels.name: Coral Castle Museum
jewels.booking_route: tickets at the gate or on the own site (admission not read)
jewels.blurb: 28655 S. Dixie Highway, Homestead: an "architectural marvel constructed single-handedly by Edward Leedskalnin from 1923 to 1951" from limestone blocks; open daily 9AM-8PM, last tour 7:00PM. (305) 248-6345.

jewels.name: Reef-safe sun protection for Biscayne's reefs and wrecks
jewels.booking_route: affiliate link to the retailer (AvantLink); bought before the trip
jewels.blurb: NPS, Biscayne safety page: "You can help protect yourself AND the resources of Biscayne National Park by using 'Reef-Safe Sun Protection'." Pack a reef-safe sunscreen before the boat, snorkel or paddle day.

jewels.name: UV-blocking water clothing, polarized glasses and hats
jewels.booking_route: affiliate link to amazon.com (Amazon Associates); bought before the trip
jewels.blurb: NPS, Biscayne safety page, alongside reef-safe sun protection: "or UV blocking clothing designed for the water. Things like polarized glasses and hats can also be helpful."

jewels.name: Drinking water and insect protection for Boca Chita and Elliott Key camping
jewels.booking_route: affiliate link to the retailer (AvantLink); bought before the trip
jewels.blurb: NPS camping page: "Drinking water is available, but bring water as a precaution if the system goes down." "Insects – May be prevalent year round. Expect heavy populations of insects during the warmer months." Elliott Key: "Mosquitoes and no-see-ums (biting midges) are prevalent year round."

faq.q: Is Biscayne National Park free?
faq.a: Entry is free: "The park has no entrance fees." Docking is charged - "$25.00 Friday - Monday and Federal Holidays" for day use, and "$60.00 per night" for overnight camping and docking.

faq.q: Do you need a boat to get to Biscayne National Park?
faq.a: For most of it, yes: "the park is 95% water", and "the coral reefs are over ten miles from the mainland by boat, so please consider one of the snorkel tours." The Dante Fascell Visitor Center and Convoy Point grounds are reached by car.

faq.q: How do I get to Biscayne National Park?
faq.a: The visitor center is at "9700 SW 328th Street, Sir Lancelot Jones Way, Homestead, FL 33033". From the Florida Turnpike take Exit 6 (Speedway Boulevard), turn left to SW 328th Street and go four miles to the park entrance; from US 1 northbound turn right on SW 344th Street (Palm Drive), then right on SW 328th Street and "Continue for four miles to the end of the road."

faq.q: Can you camp at Biscayne National Park?
faq.a: Yes, on Elliott Key and Boca Chita Key, but "The only access to these islands is by boat" and "No reservations may be made in advance for these campgrounds; they are available on a first-come, first-served basis." Overnight camping and docking is $60 a night.

faq.q: What tours are there in Biscayne National Park?
faq.a: The Biscayne National Park Institute runs "eco-adventures including snorkeling at a shipwreck on the Maritime Heritage Trail and colorful coral reefs full of life, cruises to Boca Chita Key and lighthouse, sailing on beautiful Biscayne Bay, exploring the seldom seen wonders of Jones Lagoon". Book online, on 786-335-3644 or at the park store; "Advance reservations are advised."

faq.q: Can you fish in Biscayne National Park?
faq.a: Yes: "With limited exceptions, a valid Florida fishing license is required to fish in the park. Children under 16 years of age do not require a license." Fishing is prohibited in the harbors, docks and picnic areas at Boca Chita Key, Elliott Key and Convoy Point.

faq.q: Can you catch lobster in Biscayne National Park?
faq.a: Only outside the protected areas: "The taking of lobster is prohibited in the Biscayne Bay/Card Sound Lobster Sanctuary including all natural, artificial and tidal creeks between the islands and along the mainland", and in five Coral Reef Protection Areas marked with yellow buoys. The NPS points to its lobstering page for full rules.

faq.q: Is Biscayne National Park dog friendly?
faq.a: In part. Pets are allowed on "The grounds at Convoy Point" and "Elliott Key", but not on "Boca Chita Key, including on boats docked in the harbor" or in "The Dante Fascell Visitor Center". "Pets must be kept on a leash no longer than 6 feet and under your control at all times."

faq.q: Where can you see manatees in Biscayne National Park?
faq.a: The NPS says: "yes, ask a park ranger about recent sightings. Manatees are more common during the colder months."

faq.q: When is Biscayne National Park open?
faq.a: The Dante Fascell Visitor Center "is open 7 days a week from 9 AM-5 PM"; the Convoy Point grounds and canoe/kayak launch are "open 7 days a week from 7 AM-5:30 PM"; the navigable waters are "Open 24 hours a day"; Adams Key is "Open 9 AM until official sunset daily".

seo.meta_description: Free entry, a 95% water park off Miami: boat-in camping on Boca Chita and Elliott Key, six wrecks on the Maritime Heritage Trail, and tours from Homestead.

name: Dry Tortugas National Park
line: Fort Jefferson, coral reefs and sooty terns

jewels.name: Fort Jefferson
jewels.booking_route: none needed inside the park - entry with the $15 park entrance fee (included in ferry tickets)
jewels.blurb: "Fort Jefferson, the largest all-masonry fort in the United States, was built between 1846 and 1875 to protect the nation's gateway to the Gulf of America"; "Distinguishing features include decorative brickwork and 2,000 arches." Never finished nor fully armed; a Civil War prison whose "most famous prisoner was Dr. Samuel Mudd, the physician who set the broken leg of John Wilkes Booth." Open sunrise to sunset.

jewels.name: Garden Key swim beaches and snorkeling
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free with park entry; the ferry and seaplane lend snorkel gear
jewels.blurb: "The swim areas on Garden Key are accessible via North, South, and East Beach. These beaches offer gradual slope and easy entry and are ideal for beginner swimmers and snorkelers." The park sits "at the southwest corner of the Florida Keys reef system, the third largest in the world". "No lifeguard on duty."

jewels.name: Yankee Freedom ferry
jewels.blurb: "Yankee Freedom III, LLC is authorized by the NPS and the Department of the Interior to serve the public at Dry Tortugas National Park"; "the Official Dry Tortugas National Park Ferry", a high-speed catamaran from 100 Grinnell Street, Key West. Day itinerary: depart 8:00 am, arrive Fort Jefferson 10:15 am, return 5:15 pm; breakfast and lunch, snorkel gear, a narrated fort tour and the park entrance fee included. Read from a Wayback snapshot of 2026-08-18 - the live site returned HTTP 403.

jewels.name: Key West Seaplane Adventures
jewels.booking_route: own website ("This is the only direct booking website") or 305-293-9300
jewels.blurb: "We are the only Seaplane Service permitted in Dry Tortugas National Park." Half-day trip "just under 4 hours long, providing at least 2 1/2 hours of island time", full day at least 6 1/2 hours; "Travel time is approximately 40 minutes each way". Adult fares read: $527 half day, $910 full day, plus the $15 NPS entrance fee. 3471 South Roosevelt Blvd., Key West; 305-293-9300.

jewels.name: Garden Key Campground
jewels.booking_route: first come, first served on arrival; fees paid via Recreation.gov Scan & Pay; group site by emailed application
jewels.blurb: Primitive campground a short walk from the dock: eight regular sites for up to six people (first come, first served, "All campers, once they arrive, will be guaranteed a place to camp") plus a group site for 10-20 by reservation; $15 a night per site, $30 for the group site. Composting toilets, no showers, no water; ferry campers limited to 60 lbs of gear and no gas canisters.

jewels.name: Loggerhead Key and Little Africa
jewels.booking_route: none needed - private boat, kayak or a permitted charter; no public transport to the island
jewels.blurb: "The largest island in the Dry Tortugas, Loggerhead Key is a site of shipwrecks, a significant lighthouse installation, and where the historic Carnegie Laboratory for Marine Ecology once stood." Three miles from Garden Key, day use only, reached by private vessel or kayak; its northwest swim area holds "a remarkable coral formation aptly named Little Africa."

jewels.name: Bush Key sooty tern colony
jewels.booking_route: none needed - on foot by land bridge when present, otherwise by kayak or canoe
jewels.blurb: 16 acres; "Bush Key closes every year around February to September, when up to 80,000 sooty terns and 4,500 brown noddies make nests and raise their young on the island. This is the only significant breeding colonies of sooty terns and brown noddies in the United States." When open, a 1-mile round-trip shoreline trail, sunrise to sunset.

jewels.name: Birding and sea turtles
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free with park entry; NPS-permitted birding tours listed separately
jewels.blurb: "Nearly 300 hundred species of birds have been spotted in the Dry Tortugas. Some species, like the magnificent frigatebird and sooty tern, nesting nowhere else in the continental United States"; green and loggerhead turtles nest here, one of "5 different sea turtles commonly found in the park". "Spring migration is the preferred season."

jewels.name: Windjammer Wreck (Avanti)
jewels.booking_route: none needed - private boat on a day-use mooring buoy, or an NPS-permitted dive charter
jewels.blurb: On Loggerhead Reef, "identified as the Norwegian Avanti, which sank January 22, 1907 while en route to Montevideo, Uruguay from Pensacola"; an iron-hulled three-masted ship of 1875, 261.4 feet long. Two wreckage fields, each "roughly 110 feet in length". The Loggerhead Key page places it "a mile southwest of Loggerhead Key".

jewels.name: Paddling from Garden Key
jewels.booking_route: none needed - bring your own kayak on the ferry by advance arrangement
jewels.blurb: "Bush and Long Key are the closest to Garden Key and home to thousands of nesting birds in the spring. A trip around these two islands generally takes a few hours." Loggerhead Key "can take several hours to paddle round trip" and "involves crossing deep, open water with very strong currents." PFD, signalling device and portable VHF radio required; launch from the dinghy beach.

jewels.name: Fishing in Dry Tortugas National Park
jewels.booking_route: none needed in the park - a Florida saltwater licence is required (FWC)
jewels.blurb: "A Florida Saltwater fishing license is required, unless you are under the age of 16 or a Florida resident over the age of 65." Circle hooks only; fishing prohibited in the Research Natural Area (46% of the park); "Neither spearfishing nor lobstering is allowed in the Park." Shore spots include the main dock when the Yankee Freedom is not present and the seaplane beach when the seaplane is away.

jewels.name: Night sky over Garden Key
jewels.booking_route: none needed - campers and overnight boaters only
jewels.blurb: "With minimal light pollution, Garden Key offers incredible views of the Milky Way and star-filled skies." The NPS camping page lists "amazing star gazing" among the reasons to stay overnight.

jewels.name: Garden Key Visitor Center
jewels.booking_route: none needed - inside Fort Jefferson's island
jewels.blurb: "Garden Key Visitor Center is open every day from 8:30 AM - 4:30 PM." Garden Key is "home to park headquarters, visitor center, campgrounds and great swimming and snorkeling areas", about 14 acres.

jewels.name: Private boating and overnight anchoring
jewels.booking_route: digital entrance pass on Recreation.gov; boat permit filed at Garden Key
jewels.blurb: "Overnight anchoring is only allowed in sandy bottom within 1 nautical mile of the Garden Key lighthouse. There is no anchoring allowed anywhere within the Research Natural Area (RNA)"; RNA mooring buoys are day use only, maximum 2 hours. Private boaters buy a digital entrance pass in advance on Recreation.gov; "Cash is not accepted." After Hurricane Ian, "space for personal vessels is extremely limited" at Garden Key.

jewels.name: Laid Back Key West
jewels.booking_route: own website enquiry; (303) 900-7200 per the NPS permitted-guide list
jewels.blurb: Listed by the NPS as a permitted guide for diving/snorkeling and guided fishing. Its own page offers a "Private Dry Tortugas Charter from Key West" and a "Small-Group Dry Tortugas Day Trip from Key West" ("Fort Jefferson · Snorkeling · Fishing · 70 Miles Offshore"). Hurricane Hole Marina, 5130 Overseas Hwy, Key West.

jewels.name: Restless Native Charters
jewels.blurb: The only sailboat-tour operator on the NPS's permitted-guide list for Dry Tortugas ((858) 775-1709). Its own site carries private captained charters with Captains Brad and Maddie, booked through FareHarbor.

jewels.name: Key West Boat Charters
jewels.blurb: On the NPS motorized-tours permit list ((305) 304-0988). "Key West Boat Charters is more than a brokerage service"; a Dry Tortugas yacht trip to "Explore a 19th Century Fort, known as Fort Jefferson, the largest brick building in the western hemisphere", and "The 90-foot luxury yacht, Mia".

jewels.name: Dream Catcher Charters (Capt. Steven Lamp)
jewels.blurb: Listed by the NPS under eco tours, guided fishing and motorized tours ((305) 292-7212). "Key West fishing guide since 1994"; flats, reef, backcountry, deep-sea and Dry Tortugas fishing; "4, 6 and 8 hour trips daily year round".

jewels.name: Boyd's Key West Campground
jewels.booking_route: own website (booking engine not identified on the page read)
jewels.blurb: "Southernmost Hospitality Since 1963", on waterfront Stock Island "just 4 miles from Duval Street": full hook-up RV sites (30/50 amp, water, sewer, cable), "Scenic tent sites with picnic tables, grills", tiny homes for two, RV rentals, heated pool, kayak and paddleboard rentals, pets welcome. 6401 Maloney Avenue.

jewels.name: Leo's Key West Campground
jewels.booking_route: RMS Cloud booking engine and bookeddirectly.com (own website links)
jewels.blurb: "Closest campground to Key West": "Back-in, full hookup gravel sites that accommodate self-contained RV's up to 42 feet", larger premium sites with optional waterfront views, a camper or 1-bedroom apartment for no-RV stays, laundry, Wi-Fi, tiki huts, dog park and launch for kayaks and small dinghies. 5264 Suncrest Rd.

jewels.name: Sugarloaf Key / Key West KOA Resort
jewels.blurb: "Located at Mile Marker 20 on US-1 in the Florida Keys": RV sites with KOA Patios, Deluxe Cabins "with full baths and linens", tent sites, a year-round pool and the on-site Sugarloaf Key Hotel; "Both our campground and the hotel are approximately a 30 minute drive from the main Key West area."

jewels.name: Sugarloaf Key RV Resort & Cottages
jewels.blurb: 311 Johnson Road, Summerland Key: listed on Campspot as "Waterfront, Fishing, Pool", pets allowed, booked instantly on Campspot; the listing links it to Sun Outdoors Sugarloaf Key.

jewels.name: Little Palm By The Sea
jewels.blurb: A waterfront RV site on Kemp Channel in Venture Out, Cudjoe Key, "25 miles to Key West", with picnic table, boat slip and swim ladder; the gated community has a marina, heated pool and spa and an ocean swimming area. Hipcamp lists it "Within a 60-minute drive from the Dry Tortugas Key West Eco Discovery Center."

jewels.name: Casa Marina Key West, Curio Collection by Hilton
jewels.blurb: "1920's History in Key West with a New Contemporary Style"; renovated, "all 311 guestrooms, including 63 suites"; the "Largest Private Beach in Key West", Spa al Mare and the beachfront restaurant Dorada.

jewels.name: The Reach Key West, Curio Collection by Hilton
jewels.booking_route: own website / hilton.com (brand booking; the hilton.com page returned HTTP 403)
jewels.blurb: Every room "feature[s] their own balcony"; the signature restaurant Four Marlins; "Lounge by the oceanfront pool or feel the sand between your toes on the island's only natural sand beach." Snorkeling, diving and fishing arranged from the resort.

jewels.name: La Concha Key West, Autograph Collection
jewels.booking_route: own website / marriott.com (brand booking; the marriott.com page returned HTTP 403)
jewels.blurb: On Duval Street, a near-centennial landmark "where Hemingway and Capone once roamed"; after a comprehensive renovation it "returns with renewed purpose– blending heritage, design, and modern luxury under Marriott's Autograph Collection." Rooms from Double Queens to the Hemingway Suite and the Grand Dame Villas.

jewels.name: Blue Heaven
jewels.blurb: 729 Thomas Street, "just two blocks from Duval"; opened September 19, 1992 when "Suanne the artist and Richard the writer cooked and served black beans, rice and fish to their first lunch customers on painted picnic tables under the Spanish Lime tree"; "featured in the MICHELIN Guide". Breakfast and lunch first come, first served; limited dinner reservations.

jewels.name: Louie's Backyard
jewels.blurb: 700 Waddell Avenue: "Island fare with a twist", "Where upscale dining meets the Atlantic Ocean", with an upstairs café and the waterside Afterdeck Bar. The page read states "We will be closed for vacation from September 8th until October 15th."

jewels.name: Hogfish Bar & Grill
jewels.blurb: 6810 Front Street inside Safe Harbor Marina, Stock Island: "a dockside seafood restaurant and bar" with "fresh local seafood straight off the boats, and a working-waterfront view. Come by boat or by car"; Key West pink shrimp and fried hogfish; live music on the deck most weekends.

jewels.name: El Siboney Restaurant
jewels.booking_route: walk-in; call ahead for the paella
jewels.blurb: 900 Catherine Street: "Authentic Cuban Cuisine" in a family-oriented restaurant; "One of our signature offerings is the renowned Paella Valenciana" - call at least one hour ahead to reserve it.

jewels.name: Santiago's Bodega
jewels.blurb: 207 Petronia Street: "Fine Wines – Sangria – Tapas – Dessert" in a dining room of "mismatched chairs, custom art and reclaimed wood"; 305-296-7691.

jewels.name: Kermit's Key Lime Shop
jewels.blurb: The Key West key lime shop: pies, pie bars and "everything key lime flavored", including gluten-free key lime pie, with online ordering for shipped desserts.

jewels.name: Florida Keys Eco-Discovery Center
jewels.booking_route: none needed - walk in; groups email the centre a week ahead
jewels.blurb: Run by Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary (NOAA) and listed by the NPS among Dry Tortugas visitor facilities: 6,000 square feet of exhibits on "the only coral barrier reef in the continental United States", a replica of the Aquarius undersea lab and a maritime-history exhibit; open Wednesday-Saturday, 9AM - 4PM.

jewels.name: The Hemingway Home & Museum
jewels.blurb: 907 Whitehead Street: the museum is open every day, 9:00am-5:00pm for walk-in visits; "Ernest Hemingway was given a white six-toed cat by a ship's captain and some of the cats who live on the museum grounds are descendants of that original cat, named Snow White."

jewels.name: Key West Lighthouse & Keeper's Quarters
jewels.booking_route: own website tickets (Key West Art & Historical Society)
jewels.blurb: 938 Whitehead Street, across from the Hemingway Home: "The current lighthouse opened in 1848 with a woman as its keeper"; later fitted with a Third Order Fresnel Lens. Open Monday to Sunday 10:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. (last admission 4:30 p.m.); fully ADA accessible except the tower.

jewels.name: Garden Key camping kit: tent, pad and strong stakes
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Campers must bring all supplies, including a tent, fresh water, fuel, ice, and food." Bring a "Tent (required), sleeping bag and pad, and strong stakes for the frequent high winds." "There are no rentals or supplies for sale once you arrive."

jewels.name: Snorkel gear that fits
jewels.blurb: NPS camping list: "snorkel gear, binoculars, sunglasses and sunscreen". "Before snorkeling, make sure that all equipment fits properly." "An approved dive flag must be displayed at all times when snorkeling outside of the designated snorkel area." Day-trippers on the ferry get loaner snorkel gear with the ticket.

jewels.name: Reef-friendly mineral sunscreen
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Make sure you bring anything that you may need, such as protective clothing, sunscreen, or medication ... You will not be able to purchase these items in the park." The park lies on "the Florida Keys reef system, the third largest in the world". NOAA (https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/news/sunscreen-corals.html, read 2026-10-03): "specific (chemical) UV filters found in chemical sunscreen can harm aquatic life, including corals"; "Mineral sunscreen, which does not use (chemical) UV filters, is considered a better option."

jewels.name: Sun shirt, long pants and wide-brimmed hat
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Be sure to arrive prepared with sun protection including breathable clothing, sunscreen, and a hat." Campers bring a "lightweight long-sleeve shirt and pants for sun and bug protection, wide-brimmed hat." NOAA adds: "use Ultraviolet Protection Factor (UPF) sunwear".

jewels.name: Kayaker's required kit: PFD, signal device, VHF radio
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Required equipment for any kayak use includes a PFD (Personal Floatation Device), a signaling device (typically a whistle and/or hand-held mirror) and a portable VHF radio. These items should be brought from the mainland by the kayaker, there are no services at the park."

faq.q: How far is Dry Tortugas National Park from Key West?
faq.a: "Dry Tortugas National Park is a remote island park located about 70 miles (113 km) west of Key West, Florida. There are no roads to the park. Visitors can only reach Dry Tortugas by boat or seaplane."

faq.q: Can you drive to Dry Tortugas National Park?
faq.a: No. "Cars cannot access Dry Tortugas National Park. There are no bridges or roads connecting the park to the Florida Keys." "Visitors must travel by ferry, seaplane, private boat, or permitted charter."

faq.q: Can you fly to Dry Tortugas National Park?
faq.a: Yes, by seaplane from Key West. Key West Seaplane Adventures states: "We are the only Seaplane Service permitted in Dry Tortugas National Park." "Travel time is approximately 40 minutes each way"; the half-day trip gives "at least 2 1/2 hours of island time" and the full day "at least 6 1/2 hours".

faq.q: How much is Dry Tortugas National Park?
faq.a: "The entrance fee for Dry Tortugas National Park is $15.00 per person and is good for 7 consecutive days. Any person 15 years old and under is exempt from paying an entrance fee." "Ferry tickets include the cost of entrance to the park, but NOT camping fees." The park does not accept cash.

faq.q: Can you camp at Dry Tortugas National Park?
faq.a: Yes, on Garden Key only. "Reservations are not accepted for the 6-person sites. All campers, once they arrive, will be guaranteed a place to camp." Sites are $15 a night; groups of 10-20 must reserve. "Campers must bring all supplies, including a tent, fresh water, fuel, ice, and food", and the ferry "is limited to 10 camping passengers per day."

faq.q: Where should you stay when visiting Dry Tortugas National Park?
faq.a: Inside the park the only options are the Garden Key primitive campsites and, for private boaters, "overnight on their vessels while anchored in designated areas." "There are no restaurants, hotels, fuel stations, marine supplies, fishing supplies, or other gear available for rent or purchase on the island." Hotels and RV parks are in Key West, where the ferry and seaplane depart.

faq.q: Can you snorkel in Dry Tortugas National Park?
faq.a: Yes. "The swim areas on Garden Key are accessible via North, South, and East Beach. These beaches offer gradual slope and easy entry and are ideal for beginner swimmers and snorkelers." Off Loggerhead Key's swim beach lies "a remarkable coral formation aptly named Little Africa." "No lifeguard on duty."

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Dry Tortugas National Park?
faq.a: "Park visitation is typically highest during February through April, the months that generally offer the most pleasant and comfortable weather conditions." Winter seas "are generally rougher" because it is windier; the summer wet season runs "from about mid-May to November", and hurricane season runs June 1 to November 30. For birds, "Spring migration is the preferred season."

faq.q: Is Dry Tortugas National Park dog friendly?
faq.a: Only partly: "Pets are permitted on Garden Key but not inside Fort Jefferson. Pets are not permitted on any other key in the park." They must be leashed, and "The commercial ferry and the seaplane do not allow pets onboard" - pets come only by private boat or with a permitted tour guide.

faq.q: When was Dry Tortugas National Park established?
faq.a: Fort Jefferson National Monument was designated on January 4, 1935; "The monument was expanded in 1983 and re-designated as Dry Tortugas National Park on October 26, 1992 by an act of Congress."
