name: Blue Spring State Park
line: Winter manatee refuge and spring run

jewels.name: Manatee viewing from the Spring Run boardwalk
jewels.booking_route: park entry only - day-use reservation at reserve.floridastateparks.org ($6 per vehicle)
jewels.blurb: "From mid-November to March, hundreds of manatees congregate in the spring run to seek shelter from the cold"; seen "from the boardwalk, which stretches 1/3 of a mile from the St. Johns River to the headspring" - "socializing and mothers nursing their small calves". Numbers grew "from about 36 animals when research began in the 1970s to over 700 animals in 2023."

jewels.name: Swimming in the Blue Spring Run
jewels.blurb: "Blue Spring offers swimming in a crystal-clear spring run" in 72-degree water, open "annually from April 1 to November 14"; "Swimming or diving with the manatees is not permitted"; food, coolers, glass, pets and inflatables over 72 inches are among the items prohibited on the water.

jewels.name: St. Johns River Nature Cruise
jewels.blurb: A 2-hour narrated cruise "setting sail from the docks at Blue Spring State Park"; wildlife "including majestic wading birds, gentle manatees, vibrant aquatic plant life, enchanting cypress forests, and the occasional glimpse of awe-inspiring alligators". Florida State Parks lists departures "daily at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m." and a Platinum Level certification from the Florida Society for Ethical Ecotourism.

jewels.name: Thursby House
jewels.booking_route: none needed - included in park admission
jewels.blurb: "The Thursby House was built by Louis Thursby in 1872 and became a hub of activity on the St. Johns River, hosting steamboat passengers"; Thursby, a "Gold Rush prospector turned orange-grower", bought Blue Spring in 1856, and "Mrs. Thursby was Orange City's first postmistress." Interpretive exhibits inside; the first floor is accessible.

jewels.name: Blue Spring State Park Campground
jewels.booking_route: Florida State Parks reservations website or 800-326-3521
jewels.blurb: "51 campsites (recreational vehicles up to 40 feet long) located in the sand pine scrub and within walking distance of the spring. Each site is equipped with a picnic table, water, electricity and a grill." Dump station; accessible sites; pets welcome under the park pet policy. $24 a night plus tax, a $6.70 reservation fee and a $7 nightly RV utility fee.

jewels.name: Blue Spring cabins
jewels.booking_route: Florida State Parks reservations website or 800-326-3521, up to 11 months ahead
jewels.blurb: "Six two-bedroom cabins are located in a shady oak hammock near Blue Spring"; up to six people (three beds), electric fireplace (November-March), central heating and cooling, full kitchen, screened porch; "televisions and phones are not provided"; two-night minimum; pets not permitted; Cabin 2 accessible. $95 a night plus tax and fees.

jewels.name: Scuba diving in Blue Spring
jewels.booking_route: none needed for certified divers - park entry only
jewels.blurb: "Scuba diving is a popular activity in the spring"; "Capacity is limited to 32 scuba diving individuals at one time"; open water divers are "prohibited from carrying lights and diving below 60 feet"; dives "completed one hour before sunset"; keep "a minimum distance of 50 feet between you and manatees at all times."

jewels.name: Tubing the spring run
jewels.booking_route: walk-in at the park rental station
jewels.blurb: "You can enter the water at the upper entry, swim to the spring boil and float back down to the main swim dock. The float run lasts about an eighth of a mile." Rentals from Blue Spring Adventures: "Single tubes start at $7 for the first hour"; "Tubing is walk-in only" and summer only.

jewels.name: Pine Island Trail
jewels.blurb: "Pine Island Trail is 3.6 miles in length (one way) and takes you through numerous plant communities from the desert-like scrub to the blackwater stream known as the St. Johns River." The park's photo gallery carries a "Black Bear on the Pine Island Trail".

jewels.name: Sand Pine Scrub Trail and the Florida scrub-jay
jewels.blurb: "Sand Pine Scrub Trail is a 0.25 loop located between the Blue Spring main office and the campground. Look for the endemic Florida scrub-jay on this trail." "Feeding Florida scrub-jays is against the law."

jewels.name: Paddling Blue Spring Run and the St. Johns River
jewels.booking_route: none needed with your own boat; "there is no launching fee" (Blue Spring Adventures FAQ)
jewels.blurb: "You are invited to canoe beautiful Blue Spring Run and the St. Johns River"; personal boats launch "at the canoe kayak rental beach located in the lower day use area"; "Paddling is not allowed in the swimming area between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m."; the run closes to boating in manatee season.

jewels.name: St. Johns River fishing dock
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park entry; FWC licence where required
jewels.blurb: "Visitors can fish from the accessible fishing dock on the St. Johns River. Fishing is not permitted in the Blue Spring Run"; "A fishing license may be required" under Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission rules.

jewels.name: Manatee Gift Shop, canteen and camp store
jewels.blurb: "The Manatee Gift Shop, food service, camp store and water activities rental station are located near the public swimming area"; Blue Spring Adventures lists retail and canteen hours "Daily 9am - 4pm".

jewels.name: Picnic pavilions and playground
jewels.booking_route: none needed - first come, first served
jewels.blurb: "Three accessible picnic pavilions are offered that have stand-up grills. There is also a large accessible barbecue grill by the pavilions near the river"; "All pavilions are first come, first served"; "A playground is located in the lower day-use area."

jewels.name: Blue Spring Adventures rentals and kayak tour
jewels.blurb: The park concessionaire: "We offer kayaks and canoes for self-guided hourly rentals", e-bike rentals, a guided kayak tour, and a "narrated 2 hour boat charter for up to 50 guests". "Kayaks and canoes must be reserved in advance. No same day bookings available. Kayaking in the spring is prohibited." 833-953-2583.

jewels.name: Florida Dive Company - Blue Spring tours
jewels.booking_route: FareHarbor, online only ("we do not accept over the phone payments or bookings")
jewels.blurb: Group Snorkel Tour "$65 per person" (45-60 minutes, ages 10+), Try Scuba "From $150 per person", Group Scuba Tour "$85 per person" (Open Water certification); season "April 1 to November 14"; Wednesday-Sunday, 6:30 AM-1 PM; meets in the upper day-use area. 386.663.8030.

jewels.name: Hontoon Island Adventures
jewels.blurb: "Just a short, free ferry ride from the mainland" at Hontoon Landing: kayak, canoe, bike, pontoon and jon boat rentals, "rustic cabins or primitive campsites", moorage slips "with electric and water", and the option to "cruise to nearby Blue Spring by kayak." Concession for Hontoon Island State Park.

jewels.name: Courtyard by Marriott DeLand Historic Downtown
jewels.blurb: "Ideally located within walking distance of Stetson University and the shops and restaurants of Main Street DeLand"; the hotel itself names "nearby attractions like Blue Spring State Park"; outdoor pool, gym, The Bistro; pets welcome ($50 one-time fee). +1 386-943-9500. Read from Marriott's page as archived 2025-12-07 (the live page returned HTTP 403).

jewels.name: Hampton Inn Debary-Deltona
jewels.booking_route: hilton.com (brand booking; not fetched - HTTP 403) or Booking.com
jewels.blurb: Booking.com: "located in DeBary, 10 miles from Blue Springs State Park"; "This 3-star hotel offers a 24-hour front desk and free WiFi." Hilton's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403).

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Deland South by IHG
jewels.booking_route: ihg.com (brand booking; not fetched - HTTP 403) or Booking.com
jewels.blurb: Booking.com: "located in De Land, within 5.7 miles of Blue Springs State Park and 2.8 miles of Spec Martin Stadium." IHG's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403).

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Orange City - Deltona by IHG
jewels.booking_route: ihg.com (brand booking; not fetched - HTTP 403) or Booking.com
jewels.blurb: Booking.com: "Located in central Orange City, this hotel is adjacent to Deltona Memorial Gardens. Features include a outdoor swimming pool, free full breakfast". IHG's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403).

jewels.name: Hontoon Landing Resort & Marina
jewels.blurb: Booking.com: "Located in De Land, 14 miles from Blue Springs State Park, Hontoon Landing Resort & Marina has accommodations with an outdoor swimming pool, free private parking and a terrace." The departure point for the free Hontoon Island ferry (Hontoon Island Adventures). Its own site did not resolve.

jewels.name: Orange City RV Resort
jewels.blurb: Campspot: 4 miles straight-line from the park; "The pull-thru RV sites are perfect for bigger rigs and include full hookup, cable, and Wi-Fi. Don't have an RV? Rent one of the comfortable, onsite RV units"; pool, hot tub, bocce, kiddie pool; "A short, 45-minute drive to Orlando's many attractions". Starting at $42.00.

jewels.name: Paradise Lakes - Deltona
jewels.blurb: Campspot: 8 miles straight-line; "Ideally situated in Deltona, the campground provides easy access to the thrills of Universal Orlando Resort" and Daytona; relaxation "on-site by the peaceful lake", cornhole and horseshoes; "New to Campspot!", starting at $60.00, no ratings yet.

jewels.name: Luna Sands Resort
jewels.blurb: 1440 E Minnesota Ave, Orange City: "With over 120 sites, plus 6 additional overflow sites"; back-in and pull-through 30/50 amp RV sites with sewer, 20 amp water-and-electric sites, campsites and cabins; pool, clubhouse, tiki bar, general store, "themed weekend events from November through April". (386) 775-3996.

jewels.name: Daytona's Endless Summer Campground
jewels.blurb: Campspot: 24 miles straight-line, 3520 S. Nova Road, Port Orange: "full-hookup 30/50 AMP RV sites—including select big-rig pull-throughs up to 75 feet—alongside classic cabins, deluxe cabins with private bathrooms, and spacious two-bedroom lodges"; a "43,000-gallon year-round pool". Starting at $54.00.

jewels.name: St. John's River Campground, Astor
jewels.blurb: "Enjoy camping in one of our shady camp sites located just 1/4 mile from the beautiful St. Johns River"; "Full hook-ups for RV's", cabin rentals, recreation room, laundromat and showers; daily, weekly or monthly rates; "Call 1-352-636-3139 today to reserve your camp site".

jewels.name: Beautiful Bell Tent Nestled Amidst Trees, Seville
jewels.blurb: Glamping Hub bell tent for "2 guests • 1 bedroom • 1 bed • 1 bathroom" with a queen bed, heating, Wi-Fi, electricity, water and lake access; pets allowed; check-in "From 03:00 PM". "This is a new property on Glamping Hub, there are no reviews yet." Surfaced on Glamping Hub's DeLand search page.

jewels.name: De Leon Springs State Park
jewels.booking_route: Florida State Parks entry (fee not read in this build)
jewels.blurb: Named by Florida State Parks among places near Blue Spring: "a recreational swimming area and a fascinating history" at 601 Ponce De Leon Blvd., De Leon Springs. Glamping Hub's DeLand page adds "you can take a dip 25 feet down to the mouth of the springs."

jewels.name: Downtown DeLand Main Street
jewels.blurb: MainStreet DeLand: "Independent restaurants, cafes, bakeries, and coffee shops abound. Gourmet, scratch-made, locally sourced" - Greek, Cuban, Mexican, Thai and Italian. Glamping Hub's DeLand page: "founded in 1876 and is home to Stetson University, Florida's oldest college."

jewels.name: Cress Restaurant
jewels.booking_route: online reservations from the own website; call for 12 or more
jewels.blurb: 103 W. Indiana Ave, DeLand: "We are a 2026 DiRoNA Award Recipient"; lamb, duck and game meats; the wine list "has be[en] recognized with Wine Spectator's Award of Excellence 4 years running 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025". (386) 734-3740 (MainStreet DeLand listing).

jewels.name: De La Vega Restaurante y Galleria
jewels.booking_route: phone (386) 734-4444 (no booking method read on the page)
jewels.blurb: 128 N. Woodland Blvd., DeLand, (386) 734-4444 (MainStreet DeLand listing); its own site calls it "Latin Fusion Wine Tapas Sangria – Downtown DeLand FL".

jewels.name: Persimmon Hollow Brewing Co.
jewels.blurb: Downtown DeLand taproom of a local brewery, with a Mug Club and "Find Our Beer Near You" listings; tagline "drink sensibly, but get weird." Taproom hours and address were not printed in the page text read.

jewels.name: Forno Bello Wood Fired Pizza & Italian Cuisine
jewels.blurb: 138 S. Woodland Blvd, DeLand, 386-279-0078 - listed by MainStreet DeLand among downtown restaurants. Its own site (fornobellodeland.com) returned no readable text.

jewels.name: Trilogy Coffee Roasting Co.
jewels.blurb: "We are Trilogy Coffee Roasting Co. located in historic Downtown DeLand, Florida"; roasting since at least 2014 ("serving our wholesale customers since 2014"); 136 W. Georgia Avenue, (386) 624-6057 (MainStreet DeLand listing).

jewels.name: Boston Coffeehouse
jewels.blurb: "Celebrating 30 years of being part of the communities we serve. With five locations and awards for Best Coffeehouse, Best Lunch, and Best Drinks"; sandwiches and specialty coffee. DeLand location 109 East New York Avenue, 386-738-2326 (MainStreet DeLand listing).

jewels.name: Pat and Toni's Sweet Things
jewels.blurb: "Handmade Chocolates, Fudge, Candy, and Frozen Treats" - a chocolate shop in DeLand that also ships handmade chocolates across the U.S.; 124 N. Woodland Blvd., 386-734-0066 (MainStreet DeLand listing).

jewels.name: Cafe DaVinci DeLand
jewels.booking_route: walk-in (show listings on the own website)
jewels.blurb: "DeLand's Best Original Live Music Venue" - "Drink Local, Dance Local", with upcoming shows and specials listed on its own site.

faq.q: Can you swim at Blue Spring State Park?
faq.a: Yes, in season: "Swimming in the spring run is open annually from April 1 to November 14. Reopening may be slightly delayed if a significant number of manatees remain in the spring." From November 15 to March 31, "swimming and all other water activities in the spring run are prohibited to protect the manatees."

faq.q: When is manatee season at Blue Spring State Park?
faq.a: "Manatee season runs from November 15 to March 31, when manatees rely on the spring's constant 72 °F water for survival." Florida State Parks adds that the closure dates "may begin sooner and end later depending on manatee presence."

faq.q: Can you swim with manatees at Blue Spring State Park?
faq.a: No. "Swimming or diving with the manatees is not permitted." Divers must "Keep a minimum distance of 50 feet between you and manatees at all times." Manatees are viewed from the boardwalk, which "stretches 1/3 of a mile from the St. Johns River to the headspring."

faq.q: What is the entrance fee at Blue Spring State Park?
faq.a: "$6 per vehicle (two to eight people). $4 single-occupant vehicle. $2 pedestrians, bicyclists, extra passengers, passengers in vehicle with holder of Annual Individual Entrance Pass."

faq.q: Do you need reservations for Blue Spring State Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Beginning July 15, 2026, all visitors to Blue Spring State Park, including Florida State Parks annual passholders, pedestrians and cyclists, must have a reservation to enter the park." "Reservations can be made up to 60 days in advance. Same-day reservations may be made until the reservation limit has been met." A camping or concession booking also admits you.

faq.q: Can you camp at Blue Spring State Park?
faq.a: Yes. "The campground has 51 campsites (recreational vehicles up to 40 feet long) located in the sand pine scrub and within walking distance of the spring. Each site is equipped with a picnic table, water, electricity and a grill." There are also six two-bedroom cabins. Reserve through the Florida State Parks reservations website or 800-326-3521.

faq.q: Is Blue Spring State Park dog friendly?
faq.a: Partly. The park concessionaire's FAQ: "Pets are permitted in the park only in designated areas, but must be leashed. Pets are not allowed in the water. Pets are not permitted onboard tour boats." Florida State Parks welcomes pets in the camping area under its pet policy, but "Pets are not permitted in cabins."

faq.q: Does Blue Spring State Park have alligators?
faq.a: On the St. Johns River, yes: the park's nature cruise operator lists "majestic wading birds, gentle manatees, vibrant aquatic plant life, enchanting cypress forests, and the occasional glimpse of awe-inspiring alligators", and notes that "sightings vary from day to day."

faq.q: How far is Blue Spring State Park from Orlando?
faq.a: The park's cruise operator says it is "Located just 45 minutes away from both Orlando and Daytona."

faq.q: When does Blue Spring State Park open?
faq.a: "The park is open from 8 a.m. until sundown, 365 days a year." Campers arriving after sunset should call 386-775-3663 on the day of arrival for the gate combination.

name: Honeymoon Island State Park
line: Gulf barrier-island beaches and virgin slash pines

jewels.name: Honeymoon Island beaches
jewels.booking_route: none needed - included in park admission ($8 per vehicle)
jewels.blurb: "With approximately four miles of shoreline": "areas designated for swimming on the main beach, a pet beach on the south end, and great shelling and walking on the north end, which turns into a sand spit"; rinse showers by the boardwalks; warning flags posted, and "Lifeguards are not provided."

jewels.name: Caladesi Island Ferry
jewels.booking_route: walk-up ticket office at Honeymoon Island State Park only - "Tickets are not available for purchase online"
jewels.blurb: Two ferry boats from the Honeymoon Island docks to Caladesi Island, "3 Miles of pristine beaches accessible only by boat"; hourly from 10am all year, half-hourly mid-February to Labor Day and weekends; round trip "Adults $20", "Children (6-12) $10", "5 and Under Free"; "Tickets are not available for purchase online!" - bought at the ticket office in Honeymoon Island State Park. 727-734-5263.

jewels.name: Osprey Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - included in park admission
jewels.blurb: "Observe one of the few remaining South Florida virgin slash pine stands along the Osprey Trail, which provides visitors with 2.5 miles of walking"; some of the trees "are almost 200 years old", with bald eagles, osprey and great horned owls nesting in winter and spring and a large gopher tortoise population. Leashed dogs allowed.

jewels.name: Rotary Centennial Nature Center
jewels.booking_route: none needed - included in park admission
jewels.blurb: "a great place to learn about the history of Honeymoon and Caladesi Islands as well as find information on the plants and animals that can be found on the islands"; "open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Wednesday through Sunday"; its elevated observation deck "at low tide provides many opportunities to see wading birds around the seagrass beds in the St. Joseph Sound."

jewels.name: Pet Beach
jewels.booking_route: none needed - included in park admission
jewels.blurb: "Dogs are allowed in designated areas such as the pet beach on the southern tip of the island and on the nature trail. Pets must be on a 6-foot hand-held leash at all times in these areas." Owners must pick up after their pets.

jewels.name: North-end sand spit and shelling
jewels.booking_route: none needed - included in park admission
jewels.blurb: "great shelling and walking on the north end, which turns into a sand spit." Since April 9, 2024, "Erosion and sand migration have separated the northernmost mile" of the sandspit, "forming a temporary cut"; the park says "do not venture into or through the water."

jewels.name: Pelican Cove paddling
jewels.booking_route: bring your own kayak, or rent at the park concession (Florida Beach Services)
jewels.blurb: "Kayaks can be rented through the concession or, if you have your own, explore Pelican Cove, which lies between the sand spit and nature trail."

jewels.name: Cafe Honeymoon and the park concession
jewels.blurb: "Florida Beach Services offers casual beach fare, has a small gift shop and is located steps away from the ferry dock"; the concession "offers food, beverages, beach supplies and souvenirs. Kayaks, umbrellas and beach chairs are available for rent." Alcohol is prohibited in the park "except at the restaurant in the park where alcohol is sold." Cafe Honeymoon 727-736-2132.

jewels.name: Beach weddings at the Honeymoon Pavilion
jewels.booking_route: enquiry by phone (727) 260-5503 or the site's contact page; deposits handled by the venue
jewels.blurb: The in-park events team: "Having hosted hundreds of weddings on the beaches of Tampa Bay, our experienced event team can customize your Wedding Package for Honeymoon Island"; "Wedding Ceremonies and Private Beachfront Receptions", plus corporate meetings and private parties at the Pavilion. (727) 260-5503.

jewels.name: Picnic area and Limitless playground
jewels.booking_route: none needed - first-come, first-served, included in park admission
jewels.blurb: "A picnic area is located on the northern end of the island. There are picnic tables, two covered pavilions, restrooms and barbecue grills"; the pavilions are "non-reservable" and first-come, first-served; "There is a Limitless playground located in the picnic area on the north end of the island."

jewels.name: Surf and pass fishing
jewels.booking_route: none needed in the park - Florida fishing licence rules apply (FWC)
jewels.blurb: "Surf and pass fishing can yield catches of flounder, snook, trout, redfish, snapper, whiting, sheepshead, pompano, Spanish mackerel, cobia, ladyfish and tarpon"; all fishing must follow state rules and "A fishing license may be required."

jewels.name: Surfing by bathhouse 3
jewels.booking_route: none needed - included in park admission
jewels.blurb: "Surfing is allowed in the park, and it's usually pretty good on the north end by bathhouse 3."

jewels.name: Wheel Fun Rentals bicycles and surreys
jewels.booking_route: rent on site (operator page not reached - HTTP 404)
jewels.blurb: Florida State Parks: "Spend the day exploring beautiful Honeymoon Island with Wheel Fun Rentals... multi-passenger Surreys and beach cruisers. Ride to your heart's content on paved trails throughout the island." Florida law requires helmets for cyclists 16 and under. The operator's own location page returned 404 when fetched.

jewels.name: Caladesi Island State Park
jewels.booking_route: reached by the Caladesi Island Ferry from Honeymoon Island, by kayak, or by private boat
jewels.blurb: "One of the few untouched islands along the Gulf Coast, Caladesi Island State Park is accessible only by boat"; nature trails to the historic Scharrer Homestead; "over 3 miles of paddling through the majestic mangrove tunnels"; shelling for "conchs, whelks and olives" (live shelling prohibited); the park calls itself "America's Best Beach in 2008".

jewels.name: Caladesi Island marina boat camping
jewels.booking_route: Florida State Parks reservations website or 800-326-3521; first-come, first-served at the marina
jewels.blurb: "Caladesi Island State Park has a marina with floating docks with 50 amp electric service and water hookups"; overnight docking in the "108-slip bayside marina" with registration before sundown; "Fees are $24 per night, plus tax, plus a nonrefundable $6.70 reservation fee or $1 per foot, plus tax"; three sites ADA accessible.

jewels.name: Sail Honeymoon Kayak & SUP Rentals
jewels.blurb: On the Dunedin Causeway: kayak and stand-up paddleboard rentals, "NO RESERVATIONS NECESSARY"; "shallow and protected waters... kayak trails, 12 spoil islands, 6 miles of inland waterways, 2 state park islands"; Caladesi Island is "Only a 15 minute paddle from our location". Closes in bad weather. (727) 734-0392.

jewels.name: Fenway Hotel, Autograph Collection
jewels.booking_route: own website booking engine or (844) 569-9879 (marriott.com page returned HTTP 403)
jewels.blurb: 453 Edgewater Dr., Dunedin; an Autograph Collection hotel with HEW Parlor & Chophouse and the Hi-Fi Rooftop Bar, "Originally home to WGHB in 1925"; reservations (844) 569-9879.

jewels.name: Hampton Inn Dunedin
jewels.blurb: A Hilton-brand hotel "Opened in 2019", described as "the only one on the Dunedin Causeway", with free breakfast, pet-friendly rooms and included parking; guests can walk the causeway, "rent kayaks to visit Caladesi Island" and "enjoy the beaches at Honeymoon Island." Source is a Florida travel guide, because hilton.com returned HTTP 403.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Clearwater North-Dunedin
jewels.blurb: An IHG hotel "on a prime corner in downtown Dunedin, at the corner of Broadway and Skinner and backing to the popular Pinellas Trail"; parking and breakfast included; "Main Street is less than a half mile away." Source is a Florida travel guide, because ihg.com returned HTTP 403.

jewels.name: Clearwater / Lake Tarpon KOA Holiday
jewels.blurb: 37061 US Hwy 19 N, Palm Harbor: "a resort-style RV park and campground" "Set between Clearwater and Tarpon Springs", "the closest KOA to Tampa"; RV sites with a KOA Patio, Deluxe Cabins with full baths and Premium Tent Sites; pool, dog park, and "a free breakfast buffet served every morning"; "Full Hookup RV Sites Starting at $69!" (727) 937-8412.

jewels.name: Sun Retreats Dunedin
jewels.blurb: "formerly known as Dunedin RV Resort", "Nestled in a tree grove near Clearwater beaches": "more than 230 spacious RV sites", heated outdoor pool, shuffleboard, pet walk and fitness centre, plus the on-site Blue Moon Inn with kitchenette rooms. Hipcamp lists it "2.1mi from Palm Harbor".

jewels.name: Fort De Soto Park campground
jewels.booking_route: Pinellas County camping reservations (camping information page)
jewels.blurb: Pinellas County's largest park: "1,136 acres made up of five interconnected islands" with a "236-site family camping area with facilities", "almost three miles of beautiful white sandy beach", a dog beach, the historic fort, and "seven miles of paved trail connecting North Beach, East Beach, the boat ramp and the camping area." 3500 Pinellas Bayway South, Tierra Verde.

jewels.name: The Olive Grove
jewels.blurb: "Aframe Cabin Tent nestled in a 4 acre olive orchard" on a working farm that mills its own extra virgin olive oil; queen bed, Wi-Fi, heat and AC, TV, fire pit, separate kitchenette and hot-water bathrooms; "No pets please". Hipcamp lists it "37mi from Palm Harbor", 12 sites.

jewels.name: The Funky Flamingo
jewels.blurb: Weeki Wachee, "on the Mud Spring between the Gulf Of Mexico and Weeki Wachee River": a camper on an Old Florida waterfront with "500 feet of waterfront"; "Kayaks are provided", vintage 1960s small-boat rentals, a grill, outdoor sink and restroom. Hipcamp lists it "33mi from Palm Harbor", 1 site.

jewels.name: Frenchy's Outpost Bar & Grill
jewels.blurb: 466 Causeway Blvd, Dunedin: "an open-air Key West Style restaurant situated near the causeway to beautiful Honeymoon Island", with a large tiki bar; the newest of the Frenchy's family, "Local favorite since 1981". (727) 625-3619.

jewels.name: Madison Avenue Pizza
jewels.booking_route: walk-in or online ordering; large-party reservations via the site
jewels.blurb: 2660 Bayshore Boulevard, Dunedin, "at the intersection of Alternate 19 and Curlew, right by Honeymoon Island": brick-oven pizza "homemade from scratch", calzones, strombolis and wings; dine in or carry out; closed Tuesdays.

jewels.name: Dunedin Brewery
jewels.blurb: 937 Douglas Avenue, Dunedin: "FL's Oldest Microbrewery", "Brewing since 1996" - "the oldest distributing microbrewery still in operation" in Florida, with pub food and live music on two stages every weekend; kitchen open daily from 11am. 727-736-0606.

jewels.name: The Living Room
jewels.blurb: 487 Main Street, Dunedin: "Eclectic Fine Dining in Tampa Bay", with music and reservations; a sister room in Wesley Chapel; the site states a 15% service charge.

jewels.name: HEW Parlor & Chophouse
jewels.blurb: At the Fenway Hotel, 453 Edgewater Dr., Dunedin: "The namesake of Herman Everett Wendell. Classic, chef-driven, show stopping"; with the Hi-Fi Rooftop Bar upstairs, "Originally home to WGHB in 1925".

jewels.name: Hellas Restaurant & Bakery
jewels.booking_route: reservations and to-go ordering via the site, or (727) 943-2400
jewels.blurb: 785 Dodecanese Blvd, Tarpon Springs: "our family has been serving authentic Greek food and pastries for over 50 years", "in the heart of the historic Sponge Docks"; restaurant plus European-style bakery. (727) 943-2400.

jewels.name: St. Nicholas Boat Line
jewels.booking_route: walk-up ticket booth on Dodecanese Boulevard, no reservations
jewels.blurb: From the Tarpon Springs Sponge Docks: "a sponge diving demonstration cruise on the Anclote River" where a diver suits up "in over 170 pounds of traditional diving equipment" and harvests a live sponge; "Family-owned since 1924 and pet-friendly", "one of the oldest continuously operating attractions in the State of Florida"; "No reservations needed".

jewels.name: Dunedin
jewels.blurb: The gateway town: Florida State Parks places Honeymoon Island "Just two miles west of Dunedin". Visit Dunedin lists ferries, trolleys and tiki rides under getting around, and bed & breakfasts, boutique hotels and inns among its places to stay.

faq.q: What is the entrance fee for Honeymoon Island State Park?
faq.a: Florida State Parks lists "$8 per vehicle (limit eight people)", "$4 single-occupant vehicle", "$2 pedestrians, bicyclists, extra passengers", and a "$4 per vehicle: Sunset fee, starting one hour prior to park closing".

faq.q: What are Honeymoon Island State Park's hours?
faq.a: "8 a.m. to sunset, 365 days a year." The Rotary Centennial Nature Center inside the park is "open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Wednesday through Sunday."

faq.q: Is Honeymoon Island State Park dog friendly?
faq.a: In designated areas: "Dogs are allowed in designated areas such as the pet beach on the southern tip of the island and on the nature trail. Pets must be on a 6-foot hand-held leash at all times in these areas." Service animals are allowed in all areas.

faq.q: How does the Honeymoon Island State Park ferry to Caladesi Island work?
faq.a: "There are two ferry boats that depart from Honeymoon Island Docks." The ferry "departs hourly all year, beginning at 10am, with half hour departures Mid-February thru Labor Day and weekends", with a "Maximum stay of up to 4 hours". It runs "every day except Thanksgiving and Christmas weather permitting."

faq.q: How much does the Caladesi Island State Park ferry cost?
faq.a: Round trip: "Adults $20", "Children (6-12) $10", "5 and Under Free", with a military discount for active-duty and retired personnel. "Tickets for the ferry must be purchased at Caladesi Ferry Ticket Office at Honeymoon Island State Park. Tickets are not available for purchase online!"

faq.q: What trails are at Honeymoon Island State Park?
faq.a: "Observe one of the few remaining South Florida virgin slash pine stands along the Osprey Trail, which provides visitors with 2.5 miles of walking." Walkers and runners also use "the park drive, the Osprey Trail and four miles of beach", and Wheel Fun Rentals bikes ride "paved trails throughout the island."

faq.q: Can you swim at Honeymoon Island State Park?
faq.a: Yes, in "areas designated for swimming on the main beach". Watch the warning flags - "Double red flags mean absolutely no swimming because of high winds and undertow currents" - and note "Lifeguards are not provided." At the north-end cut, the park says "do not venture into or through the water."

faq.q: Can you fish at Honeymoon Island State Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Surf and pass fishing can yield catches of flounder, snook, trout, redfish, snapper, whiting, sheepshead, pompano, Spanish mackerel, cobia, ladyfish and tarpon." Fishing must follow state rules on size, number, method and season, and "A fishing license may be required."

faq.q: Is Honeymoon Island a state park?
faq.a: Yes. "In 1974, the state of Florida purchased 113 acres of the island. Over the next six years, Florida purchased the remaining parcels of land on the island, and on Dec. 7, 1981, Honeymoon Island State Recreation Area was created." It is now run by Florida State Parks as Honeymoon Island State Park.

faq.q: Can you kayak to Caladesi Island State Park?
faq.a: Yes. Sail Honeymoon on the Dunedin Causeway rents kayaks and SUPs with "NO RESERVATIONS NECESSARY" and says Caladesi Island is "Only a 15 minute paddle from our location". On the island, Florida State Parks lists "over 3 miles of paddling through the majestic mangrove tunnels".

name: Great Smoky Mountains National Park

jewels.name: Cades Cove Loop Road

jewels.name: Kuwohi Observation Tower (formerly Clingmans Dome)

jewels.name: Kuwohi Road, 2026 season

jewels.name: Alum Cave Trail to Arch Rock and Alum Cave Bluffs

jewels.name: Roaring Fork Motor Nature Trail

faq.q: Is Great Smoky Mountains National Park free?
faq.a: Entry is free: "Great Smoky Mountains National Park does not charge an entrance fee." But "Parking tags are required for all vehicles parking for longer than 15 minutes": Daily $5, Weekly $15, Annual $40 in 2026, sold on recreation.gov and at automated machines. Vehicles with state-issued disability placards or plates are exempt.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Great Smoky Mountains National Park for fall colors?
faq.a: "Typically, the last three weeks of October are the best time of year to view fall colors."

faq.q: How busy is Great Smoky Mountains National Park?
faq.a: The NPS says it draws "around 12 million visitors a year," making it "the most visited national park in the country." "The park typically experiences peak visitation between 9 AM and 2 PM"; in busy seasons it advises entering "no later than 8 AM" or "around 3 PM."

faq.q: Can you camp in Great Smoky Mountains National Park?
faq.a: Yes, at 10 developed frontcountry campgrounds. "Advance reservations are required" through Recreation.gov or 877-444-6777. Cades Cove and Smokemont are open year-round and the rest seasonally; stays are limited to 14 consecutive days and six people per site.

faq.q: Can you stay in the Smoky Mountains National Park?
faq.a: Beyond the campgrounds, LeConte Lodge on Mount LeConte calls itself "the highest guest lodge in the eastern United States", at about 6,400 feet. It is reachable only on foot, by trails of 5 to 9.1 miles, and opens from late March to mid-November. Reservations are made directly with the lodge.

faq.q: Is Great Smoky Mountains National Park dog friendly?
faq.a: Only in some places. Pets are allowed "In frontcountry campgrounds", "In picnic areas", "Along roadways" and "On two dog-friendly trails—the Gatlinburg Trail and the Oconaluftee River Trail", and "must be kept on a leash no longer than 6 feet at all times." Other trails are off-limits to pets.

faq.q: Can you fish in Great Smoky Mountains National Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Fishing is permitted year-round in open waters from 30 minutes before official sunrise to 30 minutes after official sunset." Anglers 16 and older need "a valid fishing license or permit from either Tennessee or North Carolina", and "Only artificial flies or lures with a single hook may be used."

faq.q: What is the closest airport to Great Smoky Mountains National Park?
faq.a: On the Tennessee side, "McGhee-Tyson Airport (TYS) located just south of Knoxville in Alcoa... approximately 45 miles west of the Gatlinburg entrance." On the North Carolina side, "Asheville Regional Airport is located approximately 60 miles east of the Cherokee entrance to the park."

faq.q: When was Great Smoky Mountains National Park established?
faq.a: "Great Smoky Mountains National Park was founded in 1934."

seo.meta_title: Great Smoky Mountains: Cades Cove, Kuwohi & Elk | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: No entrance fee, a $5 parking tag, October colour, the elk rut and the firefly lottery, plus the gateway towns and stays around America's most visited park.

hero.query: Great Smoky Mountains National Park, Cades Cove

name: New River Gorge National Park and Preserve
line: Steel-arch gorge, whitewater and sandstone climbs

jewels.name: New River Gorge Bridge
jewels.blurb: 876 feet high, 3,030 feet long with a 1,700-foot arch, completed October 22, 1977; "the longest steel span in the western hemisphere" and it "turned a 40-minute drive into less than a minute"

jewels.name: Bridge Day 2026 (October 17)
jewels.blurb: "West Virginia's largest single-day festival and one of the largest extreme sports events in the world" - BASE jumping, rappelling and high line, and the one day the public walks across the bridge

jewels.name: Bridge Walk
jewels.booking_route: online "BOOK NOW"; engine not named on the page
jewels.blurb: a harnessed walk on the catwalk "25 feet beneath the New River Gorge Bridge", the full 3,030 feet; from $79, ages 8+ and 48 inches tall, year-round; Bridge Day walk $125; the NPS names it "the only company that take visitors on the bridge"

jewels.name: Canyon Rim Visitor Center and bridge boardwalk
jewels.blurb: "A short boardwalk descends into the gorge to two observation decks" facing the arch, with "a fully accessible ramp" to the upper deck and a two-mile view south from the back deck

jewels.name: Grandview
jewels.blurb: Main Overlook 1,400 feet above the river with seven miles of gorge in view; Catawba rhododendron in mid-May, great rhododendron in July; area open year-round, visitor centre normally June to August

jewels.name: Rock climbing on the Lower New
jewels.blurb: "over 1,400 established rock climbs" on hard sandstone cliffs 30 to 120 feet tall, mostly 5.9 and harder; best late April to mid-June and mid-September to late October; NPS: "Many of the climbing locations are located miles from roads, and rescue is difficult."

jewels.name: Whitewater on the New and the Gauley
jewels.blurb: the New runs "from mild pools and riffles on the upper parts to big whitewater rapids in the lower section", season April to October; the Gauley's "steep and technical rapids" peak early September to mid-October; seven licensed outfitters

jewels.name: Sandstone Falls
jewels.blurb: falls spanning 1,500 feet across the New River, dropping 10-25 feet around islands, reached by boardwalk and bridges with a half-mile island loop; NPS: "The river around Sandstone Falls has been the site of several drownings - always wear a lifejacket when in or near the water."

jewels.name: Fayette Station Road
jewels.blurb: "an 8-mile, one-way road" of hairpins to the river and under the bridge, built about 1911-1912; "vehicles over 12 feet in height cannot complete the tour"; audio tour on the NPS App

jewels.name: Thurmond
jewels.blurb: a C&O railroad boomtown whose freight revenue once beat Cincinnati and Richmond combined; self-guided walking tour of the historic district and a depot visitor centre open daily Memorial Day to Labor Day

jewels.name: Endless Wall, Long Point and Grandview Rim trails
jewels.blurb: the NPS's overlook trails: Endless Wall 2.2-2.6 miles, Long Point 3.2 miles (rock outcrop view of the bridge), Grandview Rim 3.2 miles; "parking lots for popular trails may fill up quickly"

jewels.name: Park campgrounds (first-come, free)
jewels.blurb: Stone Cliff Beach, Army Camp, Grandview Sandbar, Glade Creek, War Ridge/Backus Mountain, Brooklyn, Thayer and Meadow Creek: "no camping fees at park campgrounds" and "Reservations are not available; all sites are first-come, first-serve"

jewels.name: ACE Adventure Resort, Oak Hill
jewels.booking_route: own "Book Now" engine (not named); group rates and packages; 1-800-787-3982
jewels.blurb: a 1,500-acre resort bordering the park: Lower New, Upper New and fall Gauley rafting, a 5-acre spring-fed waterpark, zip lines and aerial park, climbing, deluxe cabins, cabin tents, bunkhouses, RV and tent sites, and the Lost Paddle Bar & Grill

jewels.name: Adventures on the Gorge, Lansing
jewels.booking_route: own integrated "Book Now" widget (engine not named); group packages; 844-823-2684
jewels.blurb: on the gorge rim: Upper New, Lower New and Gauley rafting, jet boats, the Treetops Zipline Canopy Tour and TimberTrek, guided climbing, horseback riding, and lodging from deluxe cabins to glamping tents and RV sites; dining at Smokey's and Chetty's Pub

jewels.name: River Expeditions, Oak Hill
jewels.booking_route: online booking on its own site (engine not named); 800-463-9873
jewels.blurb: half-day to multi-day rafting on the New and the Gauley, The Ridges zipline, and cabins, bungalows, safari tents, RV and tent sites with "the 4th consecutive night is free"

jewels.name: Cantrell Ultimate Rafting, Fayetteville
jewels.blurb: billed as "West Virginia's only remaining family-owned and operated rafting company": Upper and Lower New, Upper and Lower Gauley and Bridge Day specials, with tent camping, cabins and Our House Pub & Grill at base camp

jewels.name: West Virginia Adventures, Hico
jewels.blurb: a family-owned outfitter running the New and the Gauley; the Lower New trip is listed at $119+, Class III/IV, 6 hours; group programmes for scouts, schools, corporate teams and family reunions

jewels.name: New & Gauley River Adventures, Lansing
jewels.blurb: "Small company, big adventures with no resort fees" - family-owned 30+ years, Upper and Lower New and Upper and Lower Gauley trips, cabins, Breeze Hill and Meadow River campgrounds, Undercut Pub & Grill

jewels.name: Hilltop Sunrise, Oak Hill
jewels.blurb: a two-acre site with a bunkie-style cabin for two (queen bed, private outdoor shower, solar), an electric tent platform and a full-hookup RV site; "Just 15 minutes to whitewater rafting, rock climbing ... New River Gorge Bridge"; April to October

jewels.name: New River Cabins and Tiny Houses, Hico
jewels.blurb: four 206-square-foot tiny houses with loft (no children under 10, closed October 22 to May 1) and seven cabins for 4-8, with fire rings and free laundry

jewels.name: The Hill - New River Gorge, Fayette County
jewels.booking_route: Airbnb (each tent links to an Airbnb listing)
jewels.blurb: three furnished bell tents (Wildwood Flower, Blackberry Blossom, Red Daisy) on 16 acres of family land, each with electricity, air conditioning, mini-fridge, coffee cart, private deck with smokeless firepit and hammock; shared shower house and creek access

jewels.name: American Alpine Club New River Gorge Campground, Lansing
jewels.blurb: the climbers' campground, "walking distance of popular climbing crags and hiking trails": 40 platform tent sites ($25 member/$35 non-member), 7 vehicle sites and communal spots, free showers; 2026 season March 27 to November 29; no RVs, trailers or vehicles over 20 feet

jewels.name: New River Mountain Guides, Fayetteville
jewels.booking_route: online booking engine on its own site (not named); 304-760-9791
jewels.blurb: "the only local climbing guide service Accredited by the American Mountain Guide Association", over three decades in the gorge: rappelling, half- and full-day climbs, family trips, lead, crack and multi-pitch courses; 101 E Wiseman Ave

jewels.name: Appalachian Mountain Guides, Fayetteville
jewels.booking_route: not observed (calendar on site; engine not named)
jewels.blurb: "an owner-operated climbing school, based near the rim of the New River Gorge National Park" - half- and full-day climbing in the park and lake climbing at Summersville Lake; "Accepting bookings for 2026 on all Trips and Courses"

jewels.name: Arrowhead Bike Farm, Fayetteville
jewels.booking_route: online reservation on its own site (engine not named)
jewels.blurb: bike shop with Trek mountain bike rentals and instruction, a year-round campground with direct access to the park's Arrowhead trails, resident goats, and The Handle Bar + Kitchen with local and national craft beer; 8263 Gatewood Rd

jewels.name: Secret Sandwich Society, Fayetteville
jewels.blurb: sandwiches on "premium beef, pork, deli meats and all natural chicken breast" with a seasonal cocktail programme, at 103 Keller Avenue; open daily from 11 am

jewels.name: Bridge Brew Works, Fayetteville
jewels.blurb: "We're small. Very small, and we like it. You will too." - an independent craft brewery and tasting room with flights and growlers and a food truck on site; Tuesday to Sunday 1-9 pm, March to December

jewels.name: The Freefolk Brewery, Hico
jewels.blurb: craft brewery and "HOME OF AMPLE PIZZA!" with wood-fired pies, at 25385 Midland Trail; open from 4 pm weekdays, 1 pm Saturday

jewels.name: Glen Ferris Inn, Glen Ferris
jewels.blurb: an inn serving guests since 1839 (once Stockton Tavern) overlooking the Kanawha River and Kanawha Falls, with historic suites and a riverside restaurant serving breakfast, lunch and dinner

jewels.name: Sandstone Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: the park's southern gateway at I-64 Exit 139: a 9,800-square-foot green-design building with interactive exhibits on the New River watershed, a 12-minute film, and a native garden "registered as a monarch waystation"

jewels.name: Kaymoor mine site
jewels.blurb: a Low Moor Iron Company coal operation opened in 1899 that shipped 28,074 long tons in 1900; the 2.0-mile Kaymoor Miners Trail leads to the ruins

jewels.name: Nuttallburg
jewels.blurb: "one of the most intact examples of a coal mining complex in West Virginia", leased by Henry Ford's Fordson Coal Company in the 1920s, with its tipple over the old rail line; reached by 4.1 miles of narrow Keeneys Creek Road ("Large vehicles and trailers are not recommended") or the 0.75-mile Headhouse Trail

jewels.name: Babcock State Park and the Glade Creek Grist Mill, Clifftop
jewels.blurb: 4,127 acres "known for the Glade Creek Grist Mill, a fully functional replica of the original Cooper's Mill"; cabins year-round and a campground spring through fall

jewels.name: Hawks Nest State Park, Ansted
jewels.blurb: a 270-acre state park in whitewater country with a lodge (breakfast included, per a guest review on the page), a nature museum, jetboat rides and hiking trails

jewels.name: High Ground Crossing RV Park, Victor
jewels.blurb: 28 pull-through, back-in and tent sites with 50/30-amp full hookups, free Wi-Fi, pet-friendly, open year-round, in the "heart of the New River Gorge" near Ansted and Fayetteville

jewels.name: Pies & Pints, Fayetteville
jewels.blurb: "the original cornerstone location" of the Pies & Pints chain at 219 West Maple Avenue: pizza and craft beer, daily from 11 am, weekday happy hour 3-6 pm

jewels.name: Tamarack Marketplace, Beckley
jewels.blurb: "the Best of West Virginia" - work by over 500 juried West Virginia artists, glass-blowing classes and a restaurant of "Appalachian inspired cuisine", open daily 9 am to 7 pm off I-64 Exit 45

jewels.name: Kirkwood Winery, Summersville
jewels.blurb: a winery three miles north of Summersville making over 10,000 gallons a year - fruit wines, Ramp wine, Concord Stomp and classic varietals - with tastings daily 9-5, the Isaiah Morgan Distillery nearby, and the 35th Wine and Music Fest on September 18-19, 2026

jewels.name: Riverfront Glamping on the New River, Layland
jewels.booking_route: Airbnb (CVB link redirects to an Airbnb listing)
jewels.blurb: riverfront glamping in Layland listed by the New River Gorge CVB among the area's camping and RV options; its CVB link opens an Airbnb listing, which was not read this session

jewels.name: Courtyard by Marriott Beckley
jewels.blurb: listed on the Beckley Area Lodging sheet as "Courtyard by Marriott (Exit 44) 124 Hylton Lane Beckley, WV 25801 (304) 252-9800" (federal MSHA academy sheet, created July 2022); "Exit 44 is off I-77". Marriott's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403)

jewels.name: Hampton Inn Beckley
jewels.blurb: listed on the Beckley Area Lodging sheet as "Hampton Inn (Exit 44) 110 Harper Park Drive Beckley, WV 25801 (304) 252-2121" (federal MSHA academy sheet, created July 2022). Hilton's own page was not fetched (brand sites return 403)

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express Beckley
jewels.blurb: listed on the Beckley Area Lodging sheet as "Holiday Inn Express (Exit 44) 114 Dry Hill Road Beckley, WV 25801 304-255-2200" (federal MSHA academy sheet, created July 2022). IHG's own page was not fetched (brand sites return 403)

jewels.name: The Resort at Glade Springs, Daniels
jewels.blurb: "Nestled in the Appalachian Mountains near New River Gorge National Park": 4,100 acres at 255 Resort Dr. with championship golf, a full-service spa, and "cozy guest rooms to spacious suites and luxury vacation rentals"; 844-668-5760

jewels.name: Quality Inn New River Gorge, Fayetteville
jewels.blurb: listed by the New River Gorge CVB among the area's hotels and motels, in Fayetteville; the CVB's dining page names Elliott's Whitewater Bar & Grill at this Choice Hotels property

jewels.name: Comfort Inn, Oak Hill
jewels.blurb: listed by the New River Gorge CVB among the area's hotels and motels, in Oak Hill (a Choice Hotels brand); nothing else about the property was read

jewels.name: Firecreek BBQ & Steaks, Fayetteville
jewels.blurb: steaks and BBQ "smoked and seasoned to perfection" at 310 Keller Avenue; Tue-Thu 4-8 pm, Fri 4-9 pm, Sat 12-9 pm, Sun 12-8 pm; (304) 900-5505

jewels.name: Rain gear and hiking shoes for the gorge trails
jewels.booking_route: affiliate link to the retailer (AvantLink); bought before the trip
jewels.blurb: The NPS hiking-safety page: "Wear appropriate clothes and shoes for hiking." "Carry rain gear; sudden thunderstorms can occur at any time."

jewels.name: Water and trail snacks for longer hikes
jewels.booking_route: affiliate link to the retailer (AvantLink); bought before the trip
jewels.blurb: The NPS: "Bring water and drink regularly; bring snacks or lunch for longer hikes." Also: "During spring and summer, check for ticks."

jewels.name: Water Stone Outdoors, Fayetteville
jewels.blurb: "Water Stone Outdoors has been selling outdoor gear and apparel in Fayetteville, WV since 1994": climbing gear, camping gear, apparel and books, plus rentals and consignment; 101 East Wiseman Avenue, Fayetteville, WV 25840, 304-574-2425

faq.q: Is New River Gorge National Park free?
faq.a: Yes. The NPS states: "New River Gorge National Park and Preserve does not charge an entrance fee."

faq.q: Can you camp at New River Gorge National Park?
faq.a: Yes. The NPS lists park campgrounds including Stone Cliff Beach, Army Camp, Grandview Sandbar and Glade Creek, with "no camping fees at park campgrounds"; "Reservations are not available; all sites are first-come, first-serve."

faq.q: Can you walk on the New River Gorge Bridge?
faq.a: Yes, with Bridge Walk: a harnessed walk on the catwalk "25 feet beneath the New River Gorge Bridge", year-round from $79, for ages 8 and up and at least 48 inches tall. The NPS names it "the only company that take visitors on the bridge".

faq.q: What is the best time to visit New River Gorge National Park?
faq.a: It depends on the activity. The NPS gives climbing as best "late April to mid-June" and "mid-September to late October"; the Gauley's "main season is early-September through mid-October" and New River rafting runs "April through October".

faq.q: Is New River Gorge National Park dog friendly?
faq.a: Yes: "Pets are allowed on all trails at New River Gorge National Park and Preserve." They "must always be on a physical leash no longer than 6 feet", and "Pets are not allowed in any park buildings or visitor centers" or at ranger-led programs.

faq.q: Can you fish in New River Gorge National Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Fishing is one of the most popular activities on the New River." "All persons fishing in the park are required to have a West Virginia fishing license." The NPS names bass, walleye, muskellunge, crappie, bluegill, carp and catfish.

faq.q: What is the closest airport to New River Gorge National Park?
faq.a: "Charleston WV, approximately 70 miles northwest of the park, is the closest major airport. Some flights are also available nearby at Beckley WV." Highway access is "from Route 19, between Beckley and Hico, and from I-64, between Mossy and Sandstone."

faq.q: Are there hotels in New River Gorge National Park?
faq.a: No: "The park does not have any lodging facilities, but motels, cabins, and bed & breakfasts are available in surrounding towns." The NPS adds that "Hawks Nest and Pipestem Resort State Parks have lodges".

faq.q: Where can you eat near New River Gorge National Park?
faq.a: Not inside the park. The NPS says: "Restaurants and grocery stores can be found in Beckley, Fayetteville, Sandstone, Glen Jean, Oak Hill, Mount Hope, Beaver, Hinton, and other towns around the park."

seo.meta_title: New River Gorge National Park: Bridge, Bridge Day, Rafting & Climbing | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: A free West Virginia national park: the 876-foot bridge, Bridge Day, Lower New and Gauley rafting, 1,400+ climbs, free camping and glamping near Fayetteville.

hero.query: New River Gorge Bridge, West Virginia

name: Mammoth Cave National Park
line: The world's longest known cave system

jewels.name: Historic Tour
jewels.blurb: "This classic Mammoth Cave Tour visits many of the historic areas that originally made Mammoth Cave famous. Going through tunnels that humans have used for thousands of years"; 2 hours, 2 miles, 540 stairs; adult $24, youth $18, child $6. "there are no alternative routes."

jewels.name: Domes and Dripstones Tour
jewels.blurb: "This tour begins in a sinkhole, passes through huge domes, amazing breakdown, and ends in the dripstone section known as Frozen Niagara"; 2 hours, 0.75 miles, 638 stairs; adult $30, youth $25, child $8.

jewels.name: Frozen Niagara Tour
jewels.blurb: "The naturally decorated Frozen Niagara section remains one of the most famous at Mammoth Cave"; "ideal for anyone with difficulty walking long distances or negotiating stairs"; 1.25 hours, 0.25 miles, 64 stairs; adult $26, youth $22, child $7.

jewels.name: Accessible Tour
jewels.blurb: "Utilizing the Elevator Entrance, this tour emerges near the famous Snowball Room" and continues through historic Cleaveland Avenue; 2 hours, 0.5 miles, no stairs, 12 tickets per tour time; adult $27, youth $21, child $7.

jewels.name: Wild Cave Tour
jewels.blurb: "The most extreme tour offered at Mammoth Cave, this crawling tour is an all-day adventure underground"; 6 hours, 5 miles, about 500 stairs, age 16+, chest and hip no more than 42 inches; coveralls, helmets, knee pads and head lamps "are provided by the park"; $79.

jewels.name: Violet City Lantern Tour
jewels.blurb: "A truly historic way to experience Mammoth Cave, this tour travels exclusively by lantern light"; 3 hours, 3 miles; "the use of flashlights is prohibited"; age 6+; adult $32, youth $27.

jewels.name: Grand Avenue Tour
jewels.blurb: "At 4 hours long, this lengthy tour explores the geologic diversity of what Mammoth Cave has to offer. Going through slot canyons, tubular passageways, tall canyons, and tunnels sparkled with gypsum"; age 6+; adult $42, youth $34.

jewels.name: Heritage Trail to Sunset Point
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free park trail; entrance to the park is free
jewels.blurb: A 0.6-mile out-and-back to "a park-favorite panorama of the Green River Valley"; "The first .5 miles of the trail is a raised, wooden walkway" with railings and benches; "appropriate for all visitors and all ranges of mobility"; free.

jewels.name: Green River paddle, Dennison Ferry to Green River Ferry
jewels.booking_route: none needed with your own boat; rentals from the two NPS-listed liveries
jewels.blurb: 7.6 miles, about 2.5 to 4 hours: "scenic flat waters with gravel bars, islands, and back channels"; "Riverside caves are accessible by paddle craft at lower water levels". The Green "is home to more than 150 fish species, more than 70 species of mussel". River use is prohibited at or above 20 feet on the park gauge.

jewels.name: Green River Ferry
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free; status on the ferry hotline
jewels.blurb: "first developed in 1934 and is the last remaining active river ferry in the park"; shuttles vehicles, hikers and bikers "364 days a year"; free; vehicles up to 12 tons and no more than 16 feet long; hotline (270) 758-2166.

jewels.name: Cedar Sink Trail
jewels.blurb: "an enormous sinkhole called Cedar Sink. It hosts a stunning variety of spring and summer wildflowers"; a 1-mile loop of 45-60 minutes with "A total of 295 stairs"; about 10 minutes from the visitor center; free.

jewels.name: Echo River Spring Trail
jewels.blurb: From the Green River Ferry parking area: "a one-mile wheelchair accessible loop path through the forest. This hike is a great destination for avid bird watchers"; picnic tables at the trailhead, benches and viewpoints along the way.

jewels.name: Mammoth Cave Railroad Bike and Hike Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free trail; e-bike rental in Cave City
jewels.blurb: 9 miles on the line of the railroad that "brought early tourists to Mammoth Cave" from 1886 until "its final run on August 1, 1931"; reached from Park City, points on Mammoth Cave Parkway and the visitor center; helmets recommended.

jewels.name: North side backcountry trails
jewels.booking_route: none needed for day use; reached by the Green River Ferry or via Brownsville
jewels.blurb: "Mammoth Cave National Park's backcountry boasts 37 square miles of forest and more than 60 miles of trails"; open to hikers, horses and, on Big Hollow, mountain bikes - "over 10 miles of single track" from Maple Springs.

jewels.name: The Lodge at Mammoth Cave
jewels.blurb: "located directly next to the visitor center": Sunset Terrace rooms (2 queens, up to 5), Heritage Trail rooms, Historic Cottages (1-2 people, no TV or Wi-Fi), seasonal pet-friendly Woodland Cottages ($30 a night per pet) and Family Cabins "Just opened in August 2025" with full kitchens; 2811 Entrance Rd.

jewels.name: Mammoth Cave Campground
jewels.blurb: "Tent campsites, group campsites, RV campsites, and accessible campsites just a short walk from the visitor center"; 111 sites, open March 1 - November 30, $25 a night ($12.50 Senior/Access), group $40; RVs up to 38 ft; no hookups.

jewels.name: Houchin Ferry Campground
jewels.blurb: "Every campsite has a river view"; 12 tent-only sites, open year round, $20 a night ($10 Senior/Access), "No RV or Trailers"; 15 miles from the visitor center and 1.5 miles from Brownsville.

jewels.name: Maple Springs Group Campground
jewels.blurb: "Group campsites, horseback group campsites, and RV campsites just a 10 minute drive from the visitor center" across the Green River Ferry; 7 sites with hookups (no sewer), $50 a night, March 1 - November 30; sites 1-4 "are designed to accommodate horses".

jewels.name: Backcountry and riverside camping
jewels.blurb: Thirteen designated backcountry sites "accessible only by hiking or horseback", one party of up to eight; riverside and island camping on the Green and Nolin "only accessible by boat"; $10 permit per trip; river levels must stay below 20 feet.

jewels.name: Green River Grill & Bar
jewels.blurb: In the Lodge: "Kentucky favorites prepared with local and regional farm-fresh foods", "a 3-star certified Green Restaurant"; open daily, lunch 11:00 am-3:30 pm, dinner 5:00-8:00 pm, kids menu; (270) 451-2288.

jewels.name: The Lantern Café
jewels.blurb: In the Lodge, across the foot bridge from the visitor center: "grab and go food needs and ice cream", 10:00 am-6:00 pm; also a 3-star certified Green Restaurant.

jewels.name: Caver's Camp Store
jewels.blurb: On Mammoth Cave Parkway beside the campground: "general supplies, snacks, groceries, souvenirs, quick food service as well as showers and a self-service laundry"; the only legal firewood source, since "transport of firewood into the park is prohibited"; Sun-Thu 9-5, Fri-Sat 8-7.

jewels.name: Ranger-led stargazing
jewels.booking_route: none needed - check the park calendar
jewels.blurb: "Ranger-led stargazing programs are offered throughout the year to provide an opportunity to experience unfettered views of the starry night"; attendees view planets "through telescopes provided by the park"; dates on the park calendar.

jewels.name: Fishing the Green and Nolin rivers
jewels.booking_route: none needed - no licence inside the park
jewels.blurb: "No fishing license or permit is required within the boundary of Mammoth Cave National Park"; Kentucky size and possession limits apply; the rivers hold "muskellunge, bluegill, catfish, bass, perch, crappie, and other game fish".

jewels.name: Mammoth Cave Historic Train
jewels.blurb: "Hercules" and Coach #2: a Baldwin "dummy" locomotive and combine coach "among the last of their kind used in the United States"; the 9-mile line from Glasgow Junction (Park City) opened "November 8th of 1886" and ran 45 years. National Register of Historic Places.

jewels.name: Cave-tour kit: light jacket and sturdy shoes
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI.com via AvantLink)
jewels.blurb: The NPS kit list for every tour: "Cave temperatures are cool, averaging around 54°F. It's a good idea to bring a light jacket"; "Wear sturdy shoes and watch your step on the rugged pathways." Not allowed: "Child backpack carriers", strollers, tripods and large trekking backpacks.

jewels.name: Crawling-tour boots: lace-up, ankle-high, slip-resistant
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI.com via AvantLink)
jewels.blurb: For the Introduction to Caving and Wild Cave tours: "Participants must provide their own lace-up hiking boots that cover the ankle and are equipped with slip-resistant tread. Athletic shoes or slick-soled footwear do not meet these requirements" - "no exceptions"; bring a spare pair of shoes for boot cleaning.

jewels.name: Tick kit: permethrin, gaiters, long sleeves
jewels.blurb: "Ticks can be prevalent throughout the park"; the NPS says wear "light-colored clothing, long sleeves, and long pants, with pant legs tucked into socks", "Consider wearing gaiters", and "0.5% Permethrin insecticide applied to clothing is effective in reducing tick bites"; picaridin "will not ruin synthetic fabrics".

jewels.name: US Coast Guard-approved life jacket
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI.com via AvantLink); liveries supply boats
jewels.blurb: "Always wear a life jacket": PFDs are "required to be worn by children ages 12 and under at all times while on rivers inside of Mammoth Cave National Parks"; "Federal and state law requires a Type I, II, or III PFD for each person onboard"; tubes and pool rafts are prohibited on the rivers.

jewels.name: Green River Canoeing and Kayaking
jewels.blurb: Listed by the NPS as a livery operating under a commercial use authorization; "the oldest licensed outfitter in Mammoth Cave National Park", founded by Joel and Barbara Davis with four canoes, now "more than 100 canoes and kayaks"; trips "ranging from three hours to two nights or more"; open April-October; 23839 Louisville Rd, Park City; (270) 773-5712.

jewels.name: Adventures of Mammoth Cave
jewels.blurb: Cave City; the NPS lists it as "Mammoth Cave Canoe and Kayak". "the first and original Canopy-styled tour in the state" - a five-line zipline canopy tour from $64, canoe and kayak rental from $65, mountain e-bike rental from $45 for the 9-mile railroad trail, horseback rides from $45 (ages 5+); (270) 773-6087.

jewels.name: Double J Stables and Horsemen's Campground
jewels.blurb: Named by the NPS as the authorized guided-riding operator; "located off the Northeastern corner of Mammoth Cave National Park" with direct trail access - "You do not need to cross or ride on any public roads"; small guided groups, riders "as young as 6"; campground with water/electric and rustic sites, "We welcome campers without horses"; reservations required, 270-286-0310.

jewels.name: Cave Country RV Campground
jewels.blurb: 216 Gaunce Drive, Cave City: "All sites are pull-throughs & full-hookup with 50amp"; pickleball courts, seasonal pool, laundry, fire pits, fitness centre, dog park and walking trail; check-in 1:00 pm Central; (270) 773-4678.

jewels.name: Singing Hills RV Park and Campground
jewels.blurb: "open year round and is only two miles from Mammoth Cave National Park"; owned since 2007 by Eldon and Beth Brown, who live on site; catch-and-release pond; "word of mouth advertising has us full nearly every night during tourist season"; reservations on the honor system by phone.

faq.q: Is Mammoth Cave National Park free?
faq.a: Entry is: "There is no fee to enter Mammoth Cave National Park. However, there are fees associated with cave tours, camping, and shelter rentals." Tours run from $15 (Mammoth Passage, adult) to $79 (Wild Cave).

faq.q: Do you need reservations for Mammoth Cave National Park?
faq.a: Not to enter, but to go into the cave: "Tickets are required to enter Mammoth Cave. Reservations are strongly recommended. Reservations are the only way to ensure a spot is available for your party." Book on Recreation.gov or at 877-444-6777; "Availability of walk-up tickets is not guaranteed."

faq.q: What should I wear to Mammoth Cave?
faq.a: The NPS says cave temperatures "usually hover around 54°F (12.2°C), year-round. A light jacket or sweater is recommended, as are good shoes for walking." The crawling tours require "lace-up hiking boots that cover the ankle" with slip-resistant tread.

faq.q: Can you camp at Mammoth Cave National Park?
faq.a: Yes. "Mammoth Cave National Park has three frontcountry campgrounds" - Mammoth Cave, Maple Springs and Houchin Ferry - plus backcountry and riverside sites. "All camping in the park requires a permit and most sites are available by reservation" on Recreation.gov.

faq.q: Can you kayak in Mammoth Cave National Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Over 30 miles of the Green and Nolin Rivers trace through the Mammoth Cave National Park". The popular Dennison Ferry to Green River Ferry trip is 7.6 miles, 2.5 to 4 hours. Children 12 and under must wear a life jacket, and river use is prohibited at or above 20 feet on the park gauge.

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Mammoth Cave National Park?
faq.a: On the surface, yes: "Leashed pets are allowed on all surface trails in the park" on a leash up to 6 feet, but "Pets are not permitted in caves or park buildings." The Lodge runs a self-service day kennel; dogs need proof of rabies, DHLP, Bordetella and parvo vaccination.

faq.q: What is the closest airport to Mammoth Cave National Park?
faq.a: "The closest full-service international airports to the park are Louisville International Airport (80 minutes) and Nashville International Airport (90 minutes)." The directions page puts Louisville 89 miles and Nashville 99 miles from park headquarters, with car rentals at both.

faq.q: How does the Green River Ferry at Mammoth Cave work?
faq.a: "The Green River Ferry operates year-round with the exception of December 25" and "is free to use". Hours are "6 a.m. to 6 p.m. CST"; vehicles must not exceed 12 tons or 16 feet, and service depends on river levels - call the hotline at (270) 758-2166.

faq.q: What time zone is Mammoth Cave National Park in?
faq.a: "Mammoth Cave is on Central Time (GMT-5). Visitors coming from the north will cross the boundary from the Eastern Time zone (GMT-4) at the northern Hart County line."

faq.q: Is Mammoth Cave National Park wheelchair accessible?
faq.a: Partly. "The Accessible Tour was expressly created for visitors with mobility devices such as motorized wheelchairs or walkers. There are no stairs on this tour". The visitor center "is fully accessible", and "The Heritage Trail, Echo River Spring Trail, Sand Cave Trail, and the Sloan's Crossing Pond Trail are all wheelchair accessible."

faq.q: Is Cuyahoga Valley National Park free?
faq.a: Yes. The NPS states: "No, Cuyahoga Valley is a fee-free park that does not require a reservation for entry."

faq.q: Do you need a pass for Cuyahoga Valley National Park?
faq.a: No. "An entrance pass is not required to access Cuyahoga Valley National Park." Two picnic shelters need reservations with fees.

faq.q: Can you camp in Cuyahoga Valley National Park?
faq.a: No. The NPS: "No, Cuyahoga Valley National Park does not offer camping but you can discover camping nearby." Campgrounds outside the park range from Heritage Farms in Peninsula to state parks within 50 miles.

faq.q: Where can you stay in Cuyahoga Valley National Park?
faq.a: The NPS names two lodging properties in the park: "These are Stanford House and the Inn at Brandywine Falls", and says nearby communities offer more.

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Cuyahoga Valley National Park?
faq.a: Yes, on a leash: "Dogs can go on most of the trails in the park, but they must remain on a leash." Dogs are prohibited on the mountain bike trails.

faq.q: Can you fish in Cuyahoga Valley National Park?
faq.a: Yes, with a state licence: the NPS says that if you have a valid Ohio fishing license then you can fish in the park.

faq.q: Is there a train in Cuyahoga Valley National Park?
faq.a: Yes. The Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad runs through the park, and in season the NPS says you can "bike or hike the Towpath Trail or paddle the river in one direction, and ride the train back". The 2026 Explorer program ran June 1 to September 7.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Cuyahoga Valley National Park?
faq.a: For fall colour, the NPS says "Peak color is usually during the third week of October" - Oak Hill early in the month, Brandywine Falls mid-month and the Ledges late - and advises weekdays or morning and late afternoon to avoid crowded lots.

faq.q: Is Cuyahoga Valley National Park closed?
faq.a: The park is open, with dated closures: the Towpath from Boston Trailhead to Lock 29 in Peninsula, "Tentative closure dates: August 24–November 20, 2026 and March 29–April 21, 2027"; a "River-wide closure near river mile 17 due to bridge construction"; part of Oak Hill Road; and Dickerson Run Trail, "closed until further notice."

faq.q: What should you wear to Cuyahoga Valley National Park?
faq.a: The NPS says: "Wear or bring sturdy hiking shoes when going on a trail"; "During wet conditions, wear waterproof boots with a heavy tread"; and "Wear light-colored clothing to easily find ticks." It also says to bring water, bug spray and sunscreen.

jewels.name: Indiana Dunes State Park (Indiana DNR)

faq.q: What is the difference between Indiana Dunes National Park and the state park?
faq.a: They are two parks run by two agencies. The state park is run by the Indiana DNR and charges its own gate fee ($7 Indiana vehicles, $20 out-of-state per day); the NPS states national park passes do not apply at the state park.

faq.q: What does it cost to enter Indiana Dunes National Park?
faq.a: A 7-day pass is $25 per private vehicle, $20 per motorcycle or $15 per person 16 and older; the park's annual pass is $45. The America the Beautiful pass is $80 for residents and $250 for non-residents.

faq.q: How do I get to Indiana Dunes National Park from Chicago?
faq.a: By train or car. The NPS states "The Chicago and South Shore Train has stops within the park"; the South Shore Line runs from Millennium Station in downtown Chicago, with Dune Park, Beverly Shores and Michigan City 11th St among its stations.

faq.q: Can you camp at Indiana Dunes National Park?
faq.a: Yes, at Dunewood Campground in Beverly Shores: 67 sites (54 drive-in RV or tent, 13 tent-only), showers and a dump station, no electric or water hookups, open April 1 through November 1 at $25 a night, reserved on recreation.gov six months ahead.

faq.q: Can you rent a boat at Indiana Dunes National Park?
faq.a: Not in the park. The NPS states "No marinas, boat rentals, or launches operate within the park itself" and points to commercial facilities in Porter, Lake and LaPorte counties; hand-carried non-motorized boats may launch from park beaches except West Beach's lifeguarded area in peak season.

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Indiana Dunes National Park?
faq.a: Yes, on a leash: "Pets must be restrained on a leash no longer than 6 feet (2 meters)." They are allowed on beaches year-round except the West Beach lifeguarded area from Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day weekend, and "Pets are not allowed on the Pinhook Bog Trail". Service animals may go everywhere.

faq.q: What should I bring to Indiana Dunes?
faq.a: The NPS recommends "UVA/UVB sunscreen, a hat, lightweight and light-colored clothing, and sunglasses", plenty of water, long sleeves and tucked-in pants with insect repellent against ticks and mosquitoes, and in winter "layers of loose-fitting clothes (including headwear)".

faq.q: Can you swim at Indiana Dunes National Park?
faq.a: Yes. West Beach has lifeguards from the Friday of Memorial Day weekend through the Monday of Labor Day weekend, 10 am to 6 pm, and eight named beaches carry restrooms and potable water.

faq.q: What is the weather like at Indiana Dunes National Park?
faq.a: The NPS: "Summers are warm and humid with high temperatures generally in the mid-80ºF's (30ºC) and low temperatures in the mid-60ºF's (18ºC)"; "Highs in winter are usually in the low to mid 30sºF (0ºC) with low temperatures in the low 20sºF (-5ºC)". Lake Michigan weather "can change quickly."
