hero.query: Indiana Dunes National Park, Indiana

name: Voyageurs National Park
line: Boat-in lake country and Kettle Falls

jewels.name: Kettle Falls Hotel
jewels.blurb: The park's only lodging, run by "Official Concessioners of Voyageurs National Park": hotel rooms (Double $110, Single $90 a night) and villas with a 3-night minimum (Non-Kitchen $210, Kitchen $260, Suite sleeping up to 8 $390); rents boats, canoes ($25/day) and kayaks ($35/day); shuttle "$ 50.00/person round trip". "Tough place to get to..... But well worth it once you get there!"

jewels.name: Kettle Falls Cruise and Tour (ranger-led)
jewels.blurb: From the Rainy Lake Visitor Center on the Voyageur, the "Kettle Falls Cruise (6.5 hrs)" is a "Hotel visit with 2-hour ground tour plus dam exploration"; from Kabetogama/Namakan on the Ne-Zho-Dain, the "Kettle Falls Tour (5.5 hrs)" with a 2-hour land tour. Season mid-June through the end of September; tickets from April 15 at 9am.

jewels.name: Ellsworth Rock Gardens
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free day-use site reached by boat; a 2.5-hour ranger tour runs on the Ne-Zho-Dain (Recreation.gov)
jewels.blurb: "Showplace of Lake Kabetogama" since the 1940s: Chicago carpenter Jack Ellsworth built "62 terraced flower beds" with "more than 13,000 lilies" and "over 200 abstract rock sculptures that have been compared to the work of modern sculptors like Noguchi and Brancusi"; "the most popular day use destination in Voyageurs National Park." 5 miles by boat from the Kabetogama Lake Visitor Center (nps.gov getting around).

jewels.name: Houseboating in Voyageurs (NPS permit)
jewels.blurb: "Houseboats are required to have a permit for overnight use"; "There is a $15 nightly fee in additional to a $10 reservation service fee per transaction"; designated sites carry fire rings and mooring posts, undesignated sites must be "at least 200 yards from developed areas", two houseboats per site. "All houseboat rentals are commercially operated by companies located just outside the park's boundaries."

jewels.name: Frontcountry boat-in campsites
jewels.blurb: "137 sites are located on the park's large lakes and are directly accessible from any park boat launch"; "all camping types require a reservation/permit" and "All tent campsites within Voyageurs National Park require a reservation fee and nightly amenity fees". Bear-proof food lockers at campsites hold two 48-quart coolers.

jewels.name: Grand Tour on the Voyageur (ranger-led)
jewels.blurb: From the Rainy Lake Visitor Center: "Grand Tour (2.5 hrs)" - "Wildlife and scenery focused, cultural/historic narratives included"; and "Life on the Lake Tour (2.5 hrs)" to gold-mine and fish-camp sites with a ranger-led hike. NPS vessels are accessible.

jewels.name: North Canoe Voyage
jewels.blurb: A special interpretive programme of "1 hour on land and 1/2 hour on the water" (1.5 hours in all) in a voyageur-style North canoe; minimum age 8; from the Rainy Lake and Ash River visitor centers.

jewels.name: Kettle Falls Dam and historic crossing
jewels.booking_route: none needed - reached by private boat, water taxi or ranger tour
jewels.blurb: "Many centuries ago, Kettle Falls was a main artery of the travel route along the wilderness border region. Native peoples gathered, hunted, and speared sturgeon at the falls, voyageurs paddled and portaged through the area"; the dams were begun around 1910, and the hotel built by timber cruiser Ed Rose has hosted travellers "since 1913" - bought in 1918 "for $1,000 and four barrels of whiskey." 13 miles by boat from the Ash River Visitor Center.

jewels.name: Kettle Falls Hotel dining room
jewels.blurb: "The only location to purchase food within Voyageurs National Park is at the Kettle Falls Hotel"; "The Kettle Falls Hotel has a restaurant that offers full sit-down meals for breakfast, lunch, and dinner" - about 15 miles from the nearest road and only reachable by watercraft.

jewels.name: Rainy Lake and Kabetogama ice roads
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free; check the weekly Winter Ice and Trail Conditions Report
jewels.blurb: Winter roads on the frozen lakes: the "Rainy Lake Ice Road begins at the visitor center boat launch" and the "Kabetogama Lake Ice Road connects the Ash River and Kabetogama Lake Visitor Centers"; "open to cars and trucks of less than 7,000 lbs. gross vehicle weight. Snowmobiles are not permitted on the ice road"; 30 mph limit; "conditions vary yearly".

jewels.name: Groomed snowmobile trails
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free trails; snowmobile rentals from CUA holders
jewels.blurb: "110 miles of staked and groomed trails for snowmobiling" on frozen lakes and designated safety portages only; land areas are off-limits except for safety portages and "hill climbing is prohibited."

jewels.name: Snowshoe and ski rental, Rainy Lake Visitor Center
jewels.booking_route: walk-up at the Rainy Lake Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: "From January through March, the Rainy Lake Visitor Center offers rentals Friday-Monday, 10am-4pm": "$10 per pair for adults / $5 for children 16 & under" - traditional wooden snowshoes and cross-country skis with boots and poles.

jewels.name: Bear-resistant food storage (NPS kit)
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (BearVault via AvantLink; REI.com via AvantLink)
jewels.blurb: About 150 black bears live in the park. The NPS: "Secure food and other scented items at all times by using bear lockers or bear-resistant cans"; food must be stored "in a park bear-proof food locker, in a certified bear-proof cooler or canister according to manufacturer's instructions, hung from a backcounbtry bear pole, or hung fourteen feet from the ground". The kit this asks for is a certified bear canister or bear-proof cooler.

jewels.name: EPA-approved bear pepper spray (NPS kit)
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (Counter Assault via AvantLink)
jewels.blurb: "Bear pepper spray can be used defensively to stop an aggressive bear in Voyageurs. Human pepper spray and bear pepper spray are not the same. Make sure you select an EPA approved product that is specifically designed to stop bears. It has no repellent properties, so do not apply it to your equipment."

jewels.name: Boat safety kit: PFDs, whistle, GPS, first aid (NPS kit)
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates)
jewels.blurb: The NPS boating checklist: "one wearable U.S. Coast Guard approved personal flotation device (PFD) on board and accessible for each person in the watercraft" (state law, canoes and kayaks included); "a whistle or horn capable of producing a continuous sound for two seconds"; "handy to have a handheld GPS device"; "Flashlight and first aid kit: In-case of emergency have the essentials on board."

jewels.name: Water treatment for lake water (NPS kit)
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates)
jewels.blurb: "Thinking of Drinking the Water? Always treat lake water before using it for drinking or cooking." The kit this asks for is a filter, purifier or treatment tablets.

jewels.name: Dark Sky Park and northern lights viewing
jewels.blurb: A designated Dark Sky Park; the two designated viewing areas are "The Meadwood Road Day Use Area" on the Ash River Visitor Center road and "the upper parking lot at the Rainy Lake Visitor Center". The aurora "can appear any time of year. However, Voyageurs winters provide longer periods of darkness, which can increase your chances".

jewels.name: Fishing the park's 30 named lakes
jewels.booking_route: none needed in the park - a Minnesota fishing licence is required (Minnesota DNR)
jewels.blurb: "Fish abound in the 30 named lakes, which consist of four large lakes and 26 smaller interior lakes"; "Fifty-four fish species", including Walleye, Sauger, Northern Pike and Smallmouth Bass. "Visitors fishing within Voyagers National Park must obtain a State of Minnesota Fishing license."

jewels.name: Backcountry camping and interior-lake canoes
jewels.blurb: Backcountry sites "require travel by water to a remote trailhead, but then visitors must hike"; "The park rents canoes and kayaks on its other interior lakes (e.g., Locator Lake, Little Shoepack Lake) through its backcountry camping program."

jewels.name: Kab-Ash Trail primitive campsites
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov permit ("all camping types require a reservation/permit")
jewels.blurb: "All campsites in Voyageurs are only accessible by watercraft, with the exception of two hike-in primitive campsites along the Kab-Ash Trail" - camping "that incorporates hiking and backpacking without needing a boat". Pets are not allowed at the Kab-Ash primitive sites (NPS pets page).

jewels.name: Rainy Lake Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: Summer "9 a.m. - 5 p.m., 7-days a week"; "October 1-31, 2026: 10 a.m.-4 p.m."; home port of the Voyageur tour boat, start of the Rainy Lake ice road, winter rentals, the accessible first 1/4 mile of the Oberholtzer Trail, and a designated dark-sky viewing lot.

jewels.name: Ash River Visitor Center (historic Meadwood Lodge)
jewels.blurb: "Historic Meadwood Lodge now serves as Ash River Visitor Center"; summer "9 a.m. - 5 p.m., 7-days a week", last day of the 2026 season "September 27, 2026", reopening "May 29, 2027". 13 miles by boat to Kettle Falls (nps.gov getting around).

jewels.name: Rainy Lake Houseboats
jewels.blurb: International Falls (2031 County Road 102): "9 Houseboat Styles" on Rainy Lake "in Voyageurs National Park - the only inland water-based park in the National Park System", with fishing for walleye, smallmouth bass, northern pike, crappie and musky; also runs VNP tours and fishing guides. 1-800-554-9188.

jewels.name: Voyagaire Lodge & Houseboats, Crane Lake
jewels.blurb: "Largest Fleet of Houseboat Rentals in Minnesota" - "With 34 houseboats available"; an "Assistant Captain" can guide first-timers from the dock; plus lodge rooms, dining, boat, UTV and snowmobile rentals and a fishing guide service. "The Gateway to Voyageurs National Park - Crane Lake, Minnesota."

jewels.name: Northernaire Houseboats
jewels.blurb: 2690 County Road 94, International Falls: "11 different types of houseboats" from the 2-person Explorer to the 12-person Aurora ("Luxury"); season "from May to September, weather permitting"; Rainy Lake "is the largest lake in Voyageurs National Park spanning 73 miles in one direction."

jewels.name: Voyageurs Outfitters
jewels.blurb: A CUA holder listed by the NPS for Rainy Lake and Kabetogama boat rentals: the full-day Kettle Falls boat tour ("From $ 274.19", 6 hours, 6 passengers) and a two-hour Grand Boat Tour; kayak rental "Paddle and PFD included", canoe packages with "a 16' NovaCraft fiberglass canoe" and two PFDs, SUPs, fishing boats, pontoons, snowshoe rental and water taxis.

jewels.name: Rainy Lake Aquatics
jewels.blurb: Ranier: "Canoe, Kayak & Paddleboard Rentals" by the day or for multiple days, with "youth rentals", "angler equipment", tandem kayaks and 2- and 3-seat canoes "to paddle to one of the many amazing camp sites"; water taxi for renters with Rainy Lake Charters. Listed by the NPS as a Rainy Lake rental CUA holder.

jewels.name: Wilderness Inquiry - Voyageurs Family Canoe
jewels.blurb: Five days from the Ash River Visitor Center, "Price $ 765 (Adult)", up to 15 people; "youth travel at 25% less than adults"; includes guides, campfire meals, "Equipment for all outdoor activities", shared tents and park permits and fees. Day 1 paddles into Kabetogama Lake to camp on Bald Rock. A CUA holder on the NPS guided-trips list.

jewels.name: Ash Riviera Resort
jewels.blurb: 10351 Ash River Trail, Orr: "gateway to the Voyageurs National Park"; "a few rustic, fully equipped cabins with private decks" and "RV sites with full hook-ups, bathroom facilities and laundry on-site"; rental boats for "a relaxing cruise around the islands or to Kettle Falls". Listed by the NPS for Kabetogama/Ash River boat rentals.

jewels.name: Rainy Lake RV Campground
jewels.blurb: 2967 MN 11E, International Falls: "a private 32 acre compound on the shores of Rainy Lake" with "40x50 full hookup sites that include sewer, 20/30/50 amp electricity, water, a dock slip, fish cleaning facility"; nightly, weekly, monthly and seasonal stays; private beach next to Bohman's Boat Landing. 218-288-1130.

jewels.name: Voyageurs RV Campground by Venserra
jewels.blurb: International Falls: "spacious RV sites equipped with both 30- and 50-amp electrical service, as well as water and sewer hookups" - three full-hookup sites for rigs of 30-45 feet, pull-throughs, restrooms, pet-friendly; "Within a 30-minute drive from the Rainy Lake Visitor Center". Reviews on the listing report bathrooms and showers needing attention.

jewels.name: City Beach Campground, International Falls
jewels.booking_route: City of International Falls (terms on the city page; booking method not read)
jewels.blurb: 3405 County Road 46, "3 miles east of International Falls": "650 feet of sand beach on Rainy Lake", a covered picnic pavilion, grills, dressing and bathroom facilities, a floating swim platform and "Camp Sites - tents only". Named by the NPS as the city's public campground for visitors without a boat.

jewels.name: Woodenfrog and Ash River state forest campgrounds
jewels.blurb: "In the Kabetogama and Ash River area, the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources (DNR) offers two nearby facilities: Woodenfrog State Forest Campground (Kabetogama) Ash River State Forest Campground (Ash River)" - the NPS's answer for car and tent campers without a watercraft. The DNR facility pages refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so site counts and fees are not stated here.

jewels.name: 16 Squared Cabin, Nett Lake
jewels.blurb: Host Amanda N. describes a "Glamp" on 160 acres of pine forest, fields and a pond with miles of trails: a cabin for 5 with two sets of bunkbeds, wood-burning stove, firewood, outhouse, picnic table, porch grill, potable water in jugs; no electricity, Wi-Fi or running water; pets on leash. 98% recommend (116 ratings).

jewels.name: Cantilever Distillery and Hotel, Ranier
jewels.blurb: "Just steps away from Rainy Lake and minutes from Voyageurs National Park": "31 hotel rooms" with claw-foot tubs, a rooftop sauna and hot tub, and a cocktail room pouring its own Minnesota-grain bourbon, gin and vodka. "We are excited to announce our partnership with Wyndham Hotels® as the newest boutique hotel in the Trademark Collection."

jewels.name: AmericInn by Wyndham International Falls
jewels.booking_route: wyndhamhotels.com (brand booking; linked from the listing, not fetched)
jewels.blurb: 2500 Keenan Drive: "free breakfast and WiFi, an indoor pool, and hot tub"; "dog-friendly, non-smoking"; "three miles from Falls International Airport (INL)" and three miles from the Canadian border crossing to Fort Frances. HotelGuides lists 85 rooms and suites over 4 floors. Its Northern Lights Pub hosts a free soup-and-chili guest reception Sunday-Thursday.

jewels.name: Days Inn by Wyndham International Falls
jewels.blurb: 2331 Highway 53 South, International Falls; 218-283-9441. HotelGuides lists it "1 mile from Falls Airport", 2 floors and 57 rooms with no elevator, exercise room and free continental breakfast.

jewels.name: The Thunderbird
jewels.blurb: Serving guests "since 1937", "just across Highway 11 from the Voyageurs National Park Rainy Lake Visitors Center" - "the closest and most convenient basecamp for all year-round park activities"; 54 acres with 1,200 feet of Rainy Lake shoreline and "15 renovated lodge rooms".

jewels.name: Thunderbird Dining Room & Lounge
jewels.blurb: "Our world-class Dining Room has a renowned reputation and beautiful views of Rainy Lake. Executive Chef John Barnes creates amazing signature dishes and daily specials"; breakfast, lunch, dinner and pizza menus, and a lakeside cocktail lounge with "a full-service copper top bar" and "large stone fireplace".

jewels.name: Cantilever Cocktail Room
jewels.blurb: "Enjoy a cocktail made with our in house craft spirits made from the finest local ingredients. Order a flight of bites"; distillery tours of "Minnesota-distilled bourbon, gin, and vodka" made "using the finest Minnesota grains and water from the Canadian Shield."

jewels.name: The Falls Bistro at the Cobblestone
jewels.blurb: Inside the Cobblestone Hotel & Suites, 1 Memorial Dr, International Falls: "chef-inspired American fare" - poutine, burgers, steak and seafood, bourbon salmon - with handcrafted cocktails; opens at 4 PM. 218-324-4660.

jewels.name: Chocolate Moose Restaurant Co.
jewels.booking_route: walk-in; online ordering on the own website
jewels.blurb: "An icon in the Borderland of International Falls": "hearty portions" for breakfast, lunch and dinner - pancakes, omelets, "our ever-popular Monte Cristo sandwich", burgers, pastas, wraps and specialty dinners.

jewels.name: Sha Sha Resort Bar & Grill
jewels.blurb: "At the end of the road on Rainy Lake, about 10 miles east of International Falls": large lakeside decks, "famous Long Island iced teas and nachos", a gift shop, cabins, and the chipmunk-feeding tradition. 1664 Highway 11 East; 218-286-3241.

jewels.name: Loony's Brew, Ranier
jewels.blurb: "On the shores of Rainy Lake in Ranier", next to Cantilever: craft beer, spirits, wine, lattes, smoothies, non-alcoholic brews and pizzas, with "live music, events, and lake views from the deck". 3481 Main St; 218-540-1001.

jewels.name: Boondock's Bar & Grill + RV Campground, Ray
jewels.blurb: On Highway 53 in Ray: food with patio seating in summer, Bingo Thursdays at 6 pm, Mexican Night Wednesdays at 5 pm, and "An on-site RV campground available"; a stop on the ATV and snowmobile trails. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays. 4660 US-53; (218) 875-2700.

jewels.name: Gateway General Store, Kabetogama
jewels.blurb: "A true Northwoods general store with a little bit of everything - groceries, gifts, bait, licenses, and more"; locally loved ice cream and take-and-bake pizza. 9378 Highway 53; (218) 875-2121.

jewels.name: Island View Lodge & Cabins
jewels.booking_route: email via the listing (booking method not read)
jewels.blurb: On Rainy Lake: "15 cabin rentals and lodge rooms", a meal and cocktail "overlooking Rainy Lake and Voyageurs National Park", and "a full-service marina with floating docks and boat rentals".

jewels.name: Sandberg's Idlewild Resort, Kabetogama
jewels.blurb: "Enjoy the Beauty of Voyageurs National Park in Complete Comfort": cabins with private bathrooms, full kitchens and sun decks, a heated pool and spa, protected boat harbor with full dock service, "Kayaks and Paddle Boards" and boat rentals; family and dog friendly. Now booking summer 2027.

jewels.name: Voyageurs Conservancy
jewels.booking_route: programmes and shop via the own website
jewels.blurb: "Voyageurs Conservancy is the official nonprofit partner of Minnesota's national park"; it funded many of the park's night-sky-friendly lights (NPS Dark Sky page), is listed by the NPS for guided hiking and environmental education, and sells Voyageurs-inspired apparel supporting park projects.

faq.q: Can you camp at Voyageurs National Park?
faq.a: Yes, with a permit. "137 sites are located on the park's large lakes and are directly accessible from any park boat launch"; there are also backcountry sites reached by boat and trail and "Two hike-in campsites along the Kab-Ash Trail that don't require a boat." "All camping types require a reservation/permit" on Recreation.gov.

faq.q: Can you visit Voyageurs National Park without a boat?
faq.a: Partly. "The park's visitor centers and some trails can be reached by car, but much of its beauty is best explored by boat." Without a boat you can take the ranger-led tour boats from the Rainy Lake and Kabetogama/Ash River visitor centers (mid-June to end of September), or use "Local businesses with valid Commercial Use Authorizations" that rent watercraft and run water taxis.

faq.q: Can you rent a houseboat at Voyageurs National Park?
faq.a: Not from the park: "Voyageurs National Park does not have houseboats available for rent but there are several commercial options in the gateway communities" serving the Rainy Lake and Namakan districts, including Crane Lake. Every houseboat needs an NPS overnight permit - "$15 nightly fee in additional to a $10 reservation service fee per transaction".

faq.q: Are there boat tours in Voyageurs National Park?
faq.a: Yes. From the Rainy Lake Visitor Center the Voyageur runs the "Grand Tour (2.5 hrs)", "Life on the Lake Tour (2.5 hrs)" and "Kettle Falls Cruise (6.5 hrs)"; from Kabetogama/Namakan the Ne-Zho-Dain runs a 5.5-hour Kettle Falls Tour, Life on the Lake and Ellsworth Rock Gardens. Season "mid-June through the end of September"; tickets on Recreation.gov from April 15 at 9am, or 1-877-444-6777.

faq.q: Does Voyageurs National Park have an entrance fee?
faq.a: No: "Voyageurs National Park does not have an entrance fee." Fees apply to tent campsites ("a reservation fee and nightly amenity fees"), houseboat permits, ranger-led boat tours, special interpretive programmes, winter equipment rentals and special use permits.

faq.q: Is Voyageurs National Park open?
faq.a: "It is open and free to visit year-round." Visitor center hours vary: Ash River, Kabetogama Lake and Crane Lake closed for the season after September 27, 2026 and reopen May 29, 2027; Rainy Lake Visitor Center is open "October 1-31, 2026: 10 a.m.-4 p.m., 7 days a week".

faq.q: Do you need bear spray in Voyageurs National Park?
faq.a: The NPS does not require it, but says "Bear pepper spray can be used defensively to stop an aggressive bear in Voyageurs" and to choose "an EPA approved product that is specifically designed to stop bears." About 150 black bears live in the park; what is required is food storage - in a bear-proof locker, a certified bear-proof cooler or canister, or hung 14 feet up.

faq.q: Can you fish in Voyageurs National Park?
faq.a: Yes. "Fish abound in the 30 named lakes" and "Fifty-four fish species have been identified", including Walleye, Sauger, Northern Pike and Smallmouth Bass. "Visitors fishing within Voyagers National Park must obtain a State of Minnesota Fishing license", and fishing follows Minnesota law except for the park-specific rules on bait and campsites.

faq.q: Is Voyageurs National Park dog friendly?
faq.a: In set places. Pets are allowed at frontcountry campsites and day-use sites, on lake surfaces where motorboats are allowed, outside visitor centers and on the Rainy Lake Visitor Center Recreation Trail; not on backcountry sites on the Kabetogama Peninsula, at the Kab-Ash primitive sites, on tour boats, inside visitor centers or on other trails. Leash "not exceeding six feet in length".

faq.q: What is the closest airport to Voyageurs National Park?
faq.a: "Falls International Airport is located in International Falls, Minnesota. Taxi service and rental cars are available here. Most flights entering the area will pass through the larger Minneapolis-St. Paul airport located about 5 hours south". "There is no public transportation to Voyageurs National Park."

seo.meta_title: Voyageurs National Park: Houseboats, Boat Tours & Kettle Falls | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: Free entry, 137 boat-in campsites, ranger boat tours to Kettle Falls, houseboat fleets on Rainy and Crane lakes, ice roads, and dark skies for the aurora.

name: Isle Royale National Park
line: Lake Superior wilderness archipelago of wolves and moose

jewels.name: Wolves and moose of Isle Royale
jewels.booking_route: none needed - wildlife seen on the park's trails and shores
jewels.blurb: "The gray wolf (Canis lupus)... has been the prevailing predator of Isle Royale National Park since its arrival to the island in the late 1940s", most likely "by crossing an ice bridge that formed between the island and the Canadian mainland during the winter of 1948"; the population has ranged "from 50 animals in 1980 to a low of two animals between 2016 and 2018". Best chance of a sighting: "along lakeshores, open areas, or hiking trails."

jewels.name: Backcountry campgrounds and permits
jewels.booking_route: free self-issued permit on arrival (small parties); group permits reserved ahead with the park
jewels.blurb: "36 campgrounds located across the island", reached by foot or watercraft, each with tent sites, a water source and outhouses; "Permits are required, regardless of group size or method of travel, for all overnight stays." Parties of six or fewer camp free on a first-come, first-served permit; groups of seven or more reserve ahead at "$25 per permit fee". Fires "only... in designated metal rings or standing grills."

jewels.name: Rock Harbor Lodge
jewels.booking_route: rockharborlodge.com online booking or (877) 841-1064; bookable 366 days ahead
jewels.blurb: "The only full-service lodging facility on the island", on the northeast end: "Sixty rooms are available; each accommodates four persons and offers a private bath. Each room provides a Lake Superior view", plus "Twenty duplex cottages" with kitchenettes. Operated by "a park concessionaire, Isle Royale Resorts"; the lodge site is "© Aramark 2026". 2026 season "June 5, 2026 – September 12, 2026".

jewels.name: 165 miles of island trails
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park entrance fee only
jewels.blurb: "There are 165 miles of trails and 36 campgrounds" on an island "approximately 50 miles long and 9 miles wide", topped by "Mount Desor at 1,394 feet". Day hikes start from both Rock Harbor and Windigo; the NPS warns "Terrain is rough and uneven" and lists day-pack essentials: water, snacks, rain gear, first aid kit, map and compass.

jewels.name: NPS backpacking kit list for Isle Royale
jewels.booking_route: bought before the crossing - REI.com via AvantLink, or gear hire from Arrive Outdoors
jewels.blurb: The NPS's own "Essential Equipment" list: "Well broken-in boots", "Waterproof backpacking tent", "Sleeping bag (rated to 20 degrees F)", "Raingear (breatheable)", "Water filter (0.4 microns or smaller)", "Backpacking stove", "Topographic map", "Sunscreen", "Insect repellant", "Headnet", "Compass". Clothing: wool and quick-drying synthetics "ideal for Isle Royale's changeable climate". Pack weight: "no more than 30% of your body weight".

jewels.name: Water filter and treatment kit
jewels.booking_route: bought before the crossing - REI.com via AvantLink, or Amazon Associates (Outdoors)
jewels.blurb: "All surface lake and stream water should be considered contaminated with pathogens (non-potable)"; "Potable water is only available in Rock Harbor and Windigo." The NPS methods: a virus-rated purifier, or a "Water Filter (0.4 microns or finer) + Chemical Treatment", or boiling "at least one minute (bring plenty of fuel canisters)". UV purifiers "have not been manufacturer-tested for hydatid tapeworm... and cannot be considered effective." Bring "a replacement cartridge".

jewels.name: Animal-resistant hard-sided food container
jewels.booking_route: bought before the crossing - REI.com via AvantLink, or Amazon Associates (Outdoors)
jewels.blurb: "In recent years, a small number of wolves have taken an interest in human food and activities." Backpackers store food, trash and scented items in campground lockers "OR... in approved, animal-resistant hard-sided containers"; "Do not hang food in campgrounds"; kayak hatches "are not animal resistant"; off-trail campers stash containers "200 feet away from campsite". The packing guide lists an "Animal Resistent Container".

jewels.name: Rain gear and warm layers for the crossing
jewels.booking_route: bought before the crossing - Amazon Associates (Apparel) or REI.com via AvantLink
jewels.blurb: The NPS day-trip orientation: "Isle Royale's weather can be unpredictable. Pack your bag with the elements in mind, including rain gear and warm layers for the Lake Superior crossing." Day-trippers should be ready for an unexpected overnight: "bringing essential items: prescriptions, food, and extra clothing for variable weather. Consider bringing a tent, sleeping pads, and sleeping bags; Isle Royale does not provide these items for visitors."

jewels.name: Interior-lake canoe and kayak routes
jewels.booking_route: none needed for the routes - a backcountry permit to overnight; rentals in person at Rock Harbor or Windigo
jewels.blurb: "Lake Superior is well-known for its cold waters, fog, and sudden, wave-generating squalls. Small, open vessels are encouraged to use interior lake waterways instead." Interior routes and portages lie on the northeast half, marked "P" on a post; canoes "at least 15' long"; "Recreational kayaks are not recommended." Boat rentals at Windigo and Rock Harbor; ferries carry canoes and kayaks for a fee.

jewels.name: Isle Royale shipwrecks by dive permit
jewels.booking_route: free dive registration at the Rock Harbor, Windigo or Houghton visitor center
jewels.blurb: "Isle Royale's ten major shipwrecks span seventy years", "from wooden side-paddle steamers to massive steel freighters." Surface water "rarely exceeds 55 degrees Fahrenheit; below 50 feet, 34-37 degrees. Full wetsuit is necessary; a drysuit is recommended." Every diver registers at a visitor center; "There are no facilities for filling dive cylinders at Isle Royale."

jewels.name: MV Sandy sightseeing tours from Rock Harbor
jewels.booking_route: rockharborlodge.com Book Now, reservable in advance
jewels.blurb: "Sightseeing tours are offered six days a week": Passage Island ("a picturesque 1881 lighthouse"), Hidden Lake/Lookout Louise ("where you can see Ontario's Sleeping Giant"), Edisen Fishery/Rock Harbor Lighthouse ("the oldest lighthouse (1855) on Isle Royale") and a Raspberry Island sunset cruise. Adult $60, children 11 and under $30; open to all visitors.

jewels.name: Rock Harbor fishing charters
jewels.blurb: "Half-day fishing charters for up to four guests" aboard "an inspected 24' charter boat operated by a U.S.C.G licensed captain", June 5 - September 11, 2026; a Michigan DNR licence is sold at the Lodge Office. "Catch and Cook": "the Lighthouse Restaurant can cook your catch for you once you return".

jewels.name: Washington Harbor Camper Cabins (Windigo)
jewels.blurb: On the southwest end: "a unique alternative to tent camping"; each cabin has "2 Twin Bunk Beds and 1 Full-size Futon", table and chairs, outdoor grill and private deck; "All cabins do not have indoor plumbing, but guests have access to shared outdoor restroom facilities." The NPS counts "two rustic, one-room camper cabins" with electrical outlets.

jewels.name: Rock Harbor Dockside Store and Windigo store
jewels.blurb: The NPS: the Rock Harbor store "offers groceries, freeze dried foods, daily fishing licenses (cash only), fishing tackle, stove fuel, camping, hiking, and boating accessories, showers, laundry facilities"; the Washington Harbor (Windigo) store sells "camping supplies, stove fuel" and rents motorboats, canoes and kayaks. Fuel cannot fly: Isle Royale Seaplanes says iso-butane and white gas "can be purchased on Isle Royale, at both Windigo and Rock Harbor."

jewels.name: Houghton Visitor Center and RANGER III
jewels.booking_route: RANGER III reservations through the NPS (fares page renders by script; not read)
jewels.blurb: The NPS's own 165-foot, 648-ton passenger vessel: "All service departs from Houghton, Michigan and travels to either Rock Harbor or Windigo"; it "generally travels to Isle Royale Tuesdays and Fridays and returns Wednesdays and Saturdays", about 6 hours, departing 9:00 am ET. The Houghton Visitor Center, 800 E. Lakeshore Drive, is open May 26 - September 20 Monday-Friday 8 am - 5 pm ET and Saturday 10 am - 5 pm ET.

jewels.name: Isle Royale Queen IV (Copper Harbor)
jewels.blurb: From 14 Waterfront Landing, Copper Harbor: "voyage from beautiful Copper Harbor to the wilderness of Isle Royale in only 3 hours". The NPS: departs 8:00 am EDT, leaves Rock Harbor 2:45 pm EDT, same-day return for day-trippers and overnighters, typically early May to end of September; "There is no car ferry service." (906) 289-4437.

jewels.name: Grand Portage Isle Royale Transportation Lines (Voyageur II, Sea Hunter III)
jewels.booking_route: own website Book Now (2027 opens late November, per the operator)
jewels.blurb: From Grand Portage, MN: Sea Hunter III to Windigo, "$110.50 Adult Camper One-way fare", "$120.50 Day trip passenger over and back in the same day"; Voyageur II circles the island to Windigo, McCargoe Cove, Belle Isle and Rock Harbor ($110.50 adult one way from Grand Portage); canoes/kayaks $55.25 one way. Terminal parking "$5" a day, charged by the village of Grand Portage.

jewels.name: Isle Royale Seaplanes (Hubbell)
jewels.blurb: The park's "sole concessionaire offering seaplane transportation", from 26998 W. 16th Street, Hubbell, MI, to Windigo or Rock Harbor: one way "$289/per person", round trip or day trip "$420/per person", "These ticket prices include all taxes and fees"; flight about 45 minutes; parking $10 a day. No stove fuel of any kind on board.

jewels.name: Keweenaw Adventure Company
jewels.blurb: Copper Harbor, "Established in 1994": guided Lake Superior sea kayak day trips and "multi-day Lake Superior kayak tours on Isle Royale National Park", mountain-bike shuttles and repair, "a small retail shop where we supply essential bike parts and kayak accessories", and "Canoe, sit-on-top kayak and SUP rentals".

jewels.name: Portage Paddle Sports
jewels.booking_route: walk-up rentals (no booking method on the page)
jewels.blurb: At 1100 W Lakeshore Dr, Houghton (the City RV Park entrance) and 2000 Jasberg Street, Hancock: "Renting Paddle Boards and Kayaks and serving up hand dipped Ice Cream"; the City of Houghton adds "From Memorial Day to Labor Day they offer bike, kayak, and paddle board rentals". Both sites read "Closed for the season" on 2026-10-03.

jewels.name: Isle Royale and Keweenaw Parks Association store
jewels.blurb: The park's nonprofit partner at 800 E. Lakeshore Dr., Houghton: "Books, Maps, Apparel & Souvenirs" - "your purchases support our parks" - and an annual "Isle Royale Night Sky Photography Workshop" on the island for beginner and intermediate photographers.

jewels.name: Hampton Inn & Suites Houghton
jewels.blurb: Listed by Michigan Technological University among Houghton hotels at "820 Shelden Avenue, Houghton, MI 49931", 906-487-1700 - the same street as the NPS Houghton Visitor Center. Hilton's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express Houghton-Keweenaw
jewels.blurb: Listed by Michigan Technological University among Houghton hotels at "1110 Century Way, Houghton, MI 49931", 906-482-1066. IHG's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: The Vault Hotel
jewels.blurb: 600 Shelden Ave, Houghton: "Housed inside a beautifully restored historic bank" - "Formerly the Houghton National Bank, Built 1887" - with a guest-only cocktail bar, The Counting Room; the hotel cites "Conde Nast Reader's Choice Awards Top 15 Hotels in Midwest 2023 & 2024."

jewels.name: Keweenaw Mountain Lodge
jewels.booking_route: own website or phone; no walk-ins
jewels.blurb: Copper Harbor: "A four-season historic wilderness resort at the top of the Keweenaw, est. in 1934", a WPA-era lodge and "international dark sky park"; "24 cabins, with 27 units" lined along the first hole of the golf course and the forest. "Lodging reservations are done in advance, either online or over the phone — no walk-ins."

jewels.name: Grand Portage Lodge & Casino
jewels.blurb: The Minnesota gateway: renovated rooms with queen or king beds, "access to our indoor heated pool, hot tub, and fitness room", suites with fireplace and whirlpool; free cancellation "until noon the day of check-in". The Grand Portage ferry line names it as a place to stay overnight before the crossing.

jewels.name: City of Houghton RV Park
jewels.blurb: 1100 West Lakeshore Drive on the Portage Waterway: "25 sites" with water, sewer and "20-30-50 amp electric service"; "We do not accept pop-up campers or tents as there are no bathroom/shower facilities". Daily rate $60, one week $55 a night, one month+ $50 a night; next to the Ray Kestner Waterfront Park beach and a four-mile waterfront trail into downtown. Opens "May 1, 2026 (weather dependent)".

jewels.name: Grand Portage Marina RV Park and Campground
jewels.blurb: "Located adjacent to the Marina with 29 sites with full hook ups and a comfort station with restrooms, showers and laundry facilities. There may be a few tent sites available." Season "lasts until October 15th"; 1-218-475-2476. The ferry line names it for "RV sites and tent sites" in Grand Portage.

jewels.name: Fort Wilkins Historic State Park campground
jewels.booking_route: Michigan DNR state park reservations (michigan.gov refused the fetch - HTTP 403)
jewels.blurb: About a mile east of Copper Harbor: "camping, day-use facilities, a restored 1844 military outpost and one of the first lighthouses on Lake Superior", with costumed interpreters and a rentable cabin on Lake Fanny Hooe (Copper Harbor Improvement Association). Hipcamp lists the campground at "160 sites · Tents, RVs" with electrical hookups and toilets.

jewels.name: Keweenaw Waters Resort
jewels.blurb: 17800 Canal Road, Houghton, on the Keweenaw Waterway: a "Single level glamping cabin with 1 bedroom, 1 bath, and 1 queen bed plus a two-twin loft" and water-view patio, Northwoods cabins up to 3,700 sq. ft., and "89 Full-Hookup 20, 30, and 50 amp sites"; "RV Park & Campground Sites Starting at $34/Night", "Cabins Starting at $95/Night"; electric boat rentals on the Portage Canal.

jewels.name: Greenstone Grill (Rock Harbor)
jewels.blurb: "Pizza, burgers, sandwiches, fresh salads, late-night snacks, cappuccino, and a wide selection of regional beer and wine each evening", plus grab-and-go; the deck "is a favorite gathering spot". June 5 - September 12, 2026; breakfast 6:30-11:00 am, lunch/dinner 11:00 am - 8:00 pm.

jewels.name: Lighthouse Restaurant (Rock Harbor)
jewels.booking_route: on the island (no booking method on the page)
jewels.blurb: The lodge dining room, June 5 - September 12, 2026: breakfast 7:00-8:30 am, dinner 5:30-8:00 pm. The NPS: "hearty meals, including fresh lake trout"; through "Catch and Cook" it will cook a charter guest's catch.

jewels.name: Harbor Haus
jewels.blurb: Copper Harbor, "situated right on the shore of Lake Superior": "a vast dining menu featuring fresh local fish, seafood, steaks", with local berries and vegetables in season and "No prefabricated dishes"; ore freighters pass the picture windows. The site notes "the Harbor Haus is for sale". Dinner reservations by phone.

jewels.name: Keweenaw Brewing Company taproom
jewels.blurb: Downtown Houghton on the north side of Shelden Ave. (US-41): "a daily selection of fresh beers brewed right on our premises" with sacks of roasted peanuts; "$4.25 pints"; local restaurants deliver to the door.

jewels.name: The Library Restaurant and Brewpub
jewels.booking_route: walk-in (no booking method on the page)
jewels.blurb: 62 Isle Royale St., Houghton, Monday-Saturday 11 a.m. - 12 a.m., under new owners: beer production is paused while "new federal and state liquor licenses" process, with a Michigan tap takeover meanwhile.

jewels.name: Island View Dining Room (Grand Portage)
jewels.booking_route: walk-in (no booking method on the page)
jewels.blurb: At Grand Portage Lodge: "delicious comfort food with a spectacular view of Lake Superior and Pete's Island", breakfast, lunch and dinner seven days a week; breakfast 7-11 am, dinner to 9 or 10 pm; a Friday steak buffet at $19.99.

jewels.name: Grand Portage National Monument
jewels.booking_route: none needed - visitor site; free backcountry permits online
jewels.blurb: In Grand Portage, MN: "the first National Park Service unit to be co-managed with a Tribal Nation" - a Heritage Center on the fur trade and Anishinaabe culture and a reconstructed fur trade depot; summer hours 5/23 - 10/12, Heritage Center 9 am - 5 pm daily; two backcountry campsites at Fort Charlotte by free permit.

faq.q: Can you drive to Isle Royale National Park?
faq.a: No. "Isle Royale can only be accessed by crossing Lake Superior via a boat or seaplane" and "No Vehicles are Allowed on the Island" - the ferries carry people and select freight only. Your vehicle stays on the mainland in Houghton, Copper Harbor, Hubbell or Grand Portage.

faq.q: How do you get to Isle Royale National Park from Grand Portage?
faq.a: By ferry. The Sea Hunter III runs Grand Portage to Windigo in "1.5 hours", departing "9:30 am eastern time/8:30 am central time"; the Voyageur II reaches Windigo in "2 hours" and continues to Rock Harbor. Both are seasonal.

faq.q: How much is the ferry to Isle Royale National Park?
faq.a: From Grand Portage, Grand Portage Isle Royale Transportation Lines publishes "$110.50 Adult Camper One-way fare" to Windigo on the Sea Hunter III, "$120.50 Day trip passenger over and back in the same day", and $110.50 adult one way on the Voyageur II; canoes and kayaks are $55.25 one way. Other ferries publish their own fares.

faq.q: Can you fly to Isle Royale National Park?
faq.a: Yes, by seaplane. "Isle Royale Seaplanes is the sole concessionaire offering seaplane transportation to Isle Royale National Park", flying from Hubbell, Michigan to Windigo and Rock Harbor, typically "from mid-May through mid-September". The nearest airport, Houghton County Memorial, is 8 miles from Houghton.

faq.q: What are the Isle Royale National Park fees?
faq.a: "Isle Royale National Park charges a $7 per person daily entrance fee to enter or remain within the park per calendar day"; children 15 and under are exempt. An Isle Royale Season Pass costs $60 and covers the holder and up to three adults. The park takes credit cards only for entrance fees.

faq.q: Can you camp at Isle Royale National Park?
faq.a: Yes. There are "36 campgrounds located across the island". "Permits are required, regardless of group size or method of travel, for all overnight stays"; parties of six or fewer get free first-come, first-served permits, and groups of seven or more reserve ahead at $25 per permit.

faq.q: When does Isle Royale National Park close for the season?
faq.a: "Isle Royale National Park is open every year from April 16 through October 31. The island is closed from November 1 through April 15 due to extreme winter weather conditions"; the closure "extends 4.5 miles out into Lake Superior from the island."

faq.q: Is Isle Royale National Park dog friendly?
faq.a: No: "Dogs, cats and other mammals are not allowed on the island." "Service dogs are welcome on Isle Royale. However, a service dog permit must be obtained prior to your trip."

faq.q: What time zone is Isle Royale National Park in?
faq.a: "Isle Royale National Park is on eastern time, since it is part of Keweenaw County, Michigan." The Grand Portage boats run on central time.

faq.q: How big is Isle Royale National Park?
faq.a: "The main island, Isle Royale, is approximately 50 miles long and 9 miles wide." The park is an archipelago of "over 400 islands", with "165 miles of trails and 36 campgrounds"; the high point is Mount Desor at 1,394 feet.

faq.q: Is Illinois Beach State Park free?
faq.a: Entry is free, but the beach carries a small fee. IDNR: "The Illinois Department of Natural Resources does not charge an Entrance Fee to any state owned or operated land with the exception of Wildlife Prairie Park and sites with beaches. Beaches charge a $1 a day per person for beach use only."

faq.q: What is camping like at Illinois Beach State Park?
faq.a: The campground has "220 Class A Premium sites with electricity and access to showers and sanitary facilities" and is "open from April 1 through Nov. 15". "Reservations can be made up to 180 days in advance" through ExploreMoreIL; "Unreserved campsites are available on a first-come, first-serve basis." Sites have no individual water or sewer hookups, but there are water hydrants and a dump station.

faq.q: Does Illinois Beach State Park have showers?
faq.a: Yes, in the campground: its 220 sites have "electricity and access to showers and sanitary facilities", and "Five handicap accessible campsites are present in the campground near the shower buildings."

faq.q: Can you swim at Illinois Beach State Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Swimming is a major summertime attraction along the sandy shorelines, and both units provide ample parking." But "there are no on-duty lifeguards, so please be careful."

faq.q: Can you fish at Illinois Beach State Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Fishing is allowed along the beach area in both units (except in the swimming areas) and there are several small inland fishing ponds, including Sand Pond, where a disabled fishing pier is available."

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Illinois Beach State Park?
faq.a: Yes, but not everywhere: "Dogs are not allowed on the beach or in the nature preserve. Dogs are allowed in the campground, the picnic area, and the remainder of the trails as long as they are on a leash. Pets are not to be left unattended."

faq.q: Can you drink at Illinois Beach State Park?
faq.a: No. "Alcohol is prohibited at Illinois Beach State Park." The camping page adds: "No Possession or Consumption of Alcohol allowed on any site in the Campground."

faq.q: Where is Illinois Beach State Park?
faq.a: In Zion, IL 60099, "stretching 6.5 miles along the sandy shore of Lake Michigan in northern Illinois." From the south: "I-294 north to Rt 173 east (approx. 8 miles) to Sheridan Road. Make a right on Sheridan Road to Wadsworth Road, make a left, and you will be in the park." Park office 847-662-4811.

faq.q: Is there a resort at Illinois Beach State Park?
faq.a: Yes. The Illinois Beach Resort and Conference Center (Illinois Beach Hotel) is "Located directly on the shores of Lake Michigan"; IDNR calls it "the only hotel in the state that is nestled along the sandy beaches of Lake Michigan." It is open year round, with Nolan's Restaurant Wednesday-Sunday 4:00-8:00 pm.

faq.q: What is there to do at Illinois Beach State Park?
faq.a: IDNR lists "swimming, boating, picnicking, hiking, fishing, camping, and simply appreciating nature." The South Unit has "5 miles of trails, including a 2.2-mile loop trail with a graveled surface"; in the north, "Camp Logan Trail is a 1.8-mile multi-use loop"; the Zion Bike Trail links the two units.

faq.q: How much is Indiana Dunes State Park?
faq.a: Per vehicle per day: "$7 - noncommercial vehicles with Indiana license plates" and "$20 - noncommercial vehicles with out-of-state license plates, every day, including holidays." A "$50 Annual Entrance Pass" and a "$120 Non-resident Annual Entrance Pass" are also sold.

faq.q: Can you camp at Indiana Dunes State Park?
faq.a: Yes. The DNR lists "Electric - 140 (all 50 amp service)" campsites and a "Youth Tent Area", with reservations at indianastateparks.reserveamerica.com.

faq.q: Does Indiana Dunes State Park have full hookups?
faq.a: The DNR's park page lists the campground as "Electric - 140 (all 50 amp service)" and does not mention water or sewer hookups at the sites. Check the electric campground map on the DNR page or the reservation listing before booking.

faq.q: Does Indiana Dunes State Park allow dogs?
faq.a: Not on the swimming beach: "Dogs are not allowed on the Indiana Dunes State Park beach." Indiana Dunes Tourism adds that "if they are on a six-foot leash, they can be on the other parts of the beach" outside the swimming beach.

faq.q: Can you swim at Indiana Dunes State Park?
faq.a: Yes - the park lists "Swimming / Beach" on Lake Michigan, and "During the summer, swimming hours may change because of weather and staffing." It is the one Indiana state park beach not under the "Swim at Your Own Risk" policy, and children 12 and younger "must be supervised by someone aged 16 or older."

faq.q: Can you fish at Indiana Dunes State Park?
faq.a: Only for smelt: the DNR lists the activity as "Fishing (Smelt Only)".

faq.q: What time zone is Indiana Dunes State Park in?
faq.a: "Indiana Dunes State Park is in the Central Time Zone, one hour behind Eastern Time."

faq.q: How many acres is Indiana Dunes State Park?
faq.a: "Indiana Dunes consists of 2,182 acres of primitive, beautiful, historic, and unique Hoosier landscape."

faq.q: Where is Indiana Dunes State Park located?
faq.a: At "1600 N. 25 E. Chesterton, IN 46304", on Lake Michigan in northwest Indiana.

faq.q: What is the difference between Indiana Dunes State Park and the national park?
faq.a: Ownership and rules: "The National Park is owned by the United States Government's Department of the Interior. The State Park is owned by the State of Indiana's Department of Natural Resources (DNR)." The state park charges "$7 for in-state vehicles and $20 for out-of-state vehicles", and pets are allowed on national park beaches but not on the state park swimming beach.

name: Starved Rock State Park
line: Eighteen sandstone canyons and rain-fed waterfalls

jewels.name: Starved Rock overlook
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free; "all state parks are free for everyone to enjoy"
jewels.blurb: The "125-foot sandstone butte" the park is named for (the IDNR activity page lists the walk as ".6 miles Roundtrip"); in the winter of 1682-83 "the French constructed Fort St. Louis on top of Starved Rock due to its advantageous position overlooking the Illinois River." One of the best January eagle-viewing points.

jewels.name: Canyon waterfalls and icefalls
jewels.blurb: "There are 8 canyon waterfalls that are accessible to visitors: French, Wildcat, La Salle, Ottawa, Kaskaskia, Illinois, St. Louis, and Aurora." They "occur March through June but, may dry out late June through October"; in January the same canyons hold icefalls. "Wading and swimming or using the canyons as waterslides are prohibited" - fines start at $195.

jewels.name: Starved Rock Lodge
jewels.blurb: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps from 1933 and opened in 1939; "added to the National Register of Historic Places in May of 1985"; its Great Hall fireplace is "the largest in Illinois". 69 guest rooms plus cabins, an indoor pool with two saunas and a hot tub; "the only lodging facility in beautiful Starved Rock State Park." Open year-round; 815-667-4211.

jewels.name: Wildcat Canyon
jewels.blurb: "Wildcat Canyon 2 miles Roundtrip" - one of the IDNR's suggested hikes and one of the eight canyon waterfalls; the Lodge's French Canyon trailhead "leads to the eastern section of the park such as the overlooks, Wildcat Canyon, and La Salle Canyon."

jewels.name: French Canyon
jewels.blurb: "French Canyon .8 miles Roundtrip" - the shortest canyon walk the IDNR suggests, reached from behind the visitor center; in winter it is "not suitable... for those without micro cleats or Yaktrax".

jewels.name: St. Louis and Aurora Canyons
jewels.blurb: "Aurora Canyon and St. Louis Canyon 3 miles Roundtrip"; St. Louis Canyon is spring fed - "The only icefall that formed this year because the canyon is spring fed is St. Louis Canyon." Trailhead from the St. Louis Canyon lot off Route 178.

jewels.name: Winter bald eagle viewing
jewels.blurb: "Bald eagles can be seen throughout the year fishing along the Illinois River"; in January the best viewing is "from the sandstone butte known as Starved Rock, the sea wall along the Illinois River across from the visitor center, or the Illinois Waterway Visitor Center". The visitor center screens "On the Wings of the Wind (bald eagle film) 15 minutes".

jewels.name: Starved Rock State Park Campground
jewels.booking_route: ExploreMoreIL (recreation.exploremoreil.com), online only; accessible and youth-group sites by phone 815-667-4726
jewels.blurb: "133 Class-A Premium campsites. Electric hook-up only" (30 or 50 amp); two shower houses with flush toilets, dump station, playground; maximum "1 family... or 4 adults per site with 2 tents or 1 RV and 1 tent." "RESERVATIONS ARE REQUIRED", 6 months to 4 days ahead, online only; the West Loop is open all year, the East Loop closes from the weekend before Thanksgiving to April 1.

jewels.name: Starved Rock Lodge log cabins
jewels.blurb: "These authentic log cabins were built in the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps": Sunset Cabins (quad cabins, some with a wood-burning fireplace) and three standalone Pioneer Cabins "150 yards from the Lodge" with no TVs, where dogs are allowed with a rabies certificate.

jewels.name: Starved Rock Lodge Historic Trolley Tours
jewels.booking_route: own website ("Online bookings subject to additional fees and taxes") or (815) 220-7386
jewels.blurb: "a 90-minute trolley tour with stops at the Starved Rock State Park Visitors Center, the IL Waterway Visitor Center and through downtown Utica", April-December, Mon/Wed/Fri at 3 PM; Adults $20, Seniors $17, Children 12 and under $15. Seasonal Fall Color, Ghost and Hegeler Carus Mansion trolley tours.

jewels.name: Sainte Genevieve riverboat cruises
jewels.booking_route: own website, (815) 220-7386 or the Lodge front desk
jewels.blurb: Booked through the Lodge: a Starved Rock Trolley to the boat, then a Sunset Cruise on the Illinois River (June-August $50 adults, $40 children; September-October with dinner $75/$65) or "Lock and Lunch" through the Starved Rock Lock ($77/$67; 2027 dates "coming soon").

jewels.name: Starved Rock Lodge guided seasonal hikes
jewels.blurb: "Year-round, Saturday & Sunday at 10am, $25/person", lunch included (a wrap, chips, granola bar, fruit and bottled water); special Mega Hikes "four times a year"; the Lodge has also launched its "first-ever guided hiking tours at Matthiessen State Park".

jewels.name: Starved Rock Visitor Center
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free; PO Box 509, Utica, IL 61373, 815-667-4726
jewels.blurb: "should be the first stop": museum-quality exhibits on history, geology and ecology; open "Daily 9 a.m. to 4 p.m." (closed on listed holidays); films on request including the CCC and the bald eagle; the Le Rocher Gift Shop is run by the Starved Rock Foundation.

jewels.name: Free IDNR naturalist programmes and Junior Ranger
jewels.booking_route: free; some via Starved Rock Eventbrite registration
jewels.blurb: "All IDNR/state park programs and events are free to park visitors" - e.g. 10/17/26 "Leaf Peeping and Tree Seeking" hike and 12/13 nature journaling; Junior Ranger booklets at the visitor center earn "their very own Junior Ranger badge".

jewels.name: Illinois, Ottawa and Kaskaskia Canyons
jewels.blurb: On the park's eastern edge off Route 71: "Illinois, Ottawa, and Kaskaskia Canyons trails do not contain staircases but there are a few creek crossings where feet may get muddy or wet in the winter and spring".

jewels.name: Starved Rock Lodge Restaurant
jewels.booking_route: online reservations on the Lodge site or (815) 220-7321
jewels.blurb: "open daily for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Reservations are recommended"; Sunday brunch buffet 10:30 AM-3 PM; the Back Door Lounge and Veranda; the IDNR describes "a restaurant, bar and grill with outdoor seating, cafe, and concession stand". (815) 220-7321.

jewels.name: Winter traction for icy canyon trails
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI via AvantLink, or Amazon Associates)
jewels.blurb: The IDNR's own kit advice: in winter "Trails will be icy and snow packed. Traction devices such as micro cleats or Yaktrax on hiking boots are highly recommended." French and La Salle canyons are "not suitable in winter for those without micro cleats or Yaktrax".

jewels.name: Waterproof hiking shoes for spring mud

jewels.blurb: The IDNR on spring: "Trails will be very muddy with standing water in a few areas. Waterproof hiking shoes are highly recommended, and a change of dry socks and clean shoes for the ride home. Please do not wash your shoes off in the park's sinks."

jewels.name: Water for hikers and dogs in summer

jewels.blurb: "Visitors are asked to pack plenty of water for themselves and their pets in order to stay hydrated and cool on the trails"; "there are no bathrooms, trash cans, or water fountains located on the trail system", and dogs must not "drink from canyon waterfalls, creeks, or the Illinois River."

jewels.name: Matthiessen State Park

Its Vermilion River Area has the biking trails Starved Rock does not allow, "just 2 miles south of the park" (IDNR Q&A).

Its 1870 Bricks & Stones building hosts weddings and retreats.

faq.q: Is Starved Rock State Park free?
faq.a: Yes. The IDNR answers: "The wonderful thing about Illinois is that all state parks are free for everyone to enjoy." Camping, the Lodge and the Lodge's tours carry their own charges.

faq.q: Can you camp at Starved Rock State Park?
faq.a: Yes, only in the state campground: "Camping is only allowed at designated campsites at the Starved Rock State Park Campground located south of the park off Route 71". It has "133 Class-A Premium campsites. Electric hook-up only", and "RESERVATIONS ARE REQUIRED", made online at recreation.exploremoreil.com 6 months to 4 days ahead.

faq.q: Can you swim at Starved Rock State Park?
faq.a: No: "Swimming, wading, or sliding in any water bodies, including rivers, canyon creeks, and waterfalls, is not allowed." Fines begin at $195.

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Starved Rock State Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Dogs are permitted in the park as long as they are leashed, their owners clean up after them, dispose of waste properly, and ensure they have enough water while hiking." They may not drink from canyon waterfalls, creeks or the river, and "Dogs are not permitted on guided hikes or programs."

faq.q: Can you kayak at Starved Rock State Park?
faq.a: Yes, on the Illinois River. "The optimal location for launching your boat is at the Lone Point Shelter area, situated along Route 71 on the eastern side of the park"; "Kayak and canoe rental is not available at the park." The IDNR's Q&A adds that "Kayak Starved Rock manages all kayak rentals and tours out of Lone Point Shelter".

faq.q: Can you bike at Starved Rock State Park?
faq.a: Not on its trails: "Bikes are not allowed on the trails at Starved Rock due to the fragile sandstone geology, but you can travel just 2 miles south of the park to the Matthiessen Vermillion River Area (NOT allowed at the Dells area of Matthiessen) at Matthiessen State Park where there are biking trails to enjoy!"

faq.q: Can you fly a drone at Starved Rock State Park?
faq.a: No: "Drones are not allowed at Starved Rock State Park due to the number of visitors on the trails, picnic area, and overlooks, and the disturbance to wildlife such as the park's nesting bald eagle population."

faq.q: Why is it called Starved Rock State Park?
faq.a: "The name Starved Rock State Park is derived from a Native American legend": after Chief Pontiac was killed in 1769, a group of Illinois "sought refuge atop a 125-foot sandstone butte, which is now known as Starved Rock" and were encircled by the Ottawa and Potawatomi. The IDNR adds: "This is just a tale though and not supported by any archaeological evidence or historical documentation."

faq.q: What should I wear to Starved Rock State Park?
faq.a: It depends on the season, per the IDNR: in winter "Traction devices such as micro cleats or Yaktrax on hiking boots are highly recommended"; in spring "Waterproof hiking shoes are highly recommended, and a change of dry socks and clean shoes for the ride home"; in summer "pack plenty of water for themselves and their pets".

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Starved Rock State Park?
faq.a: The IDNR gives the seasons by what you want to see: waterfalls "occur March through June but, may dry out late June through October"; "Fall colors typically peak the 2nd to 3rd week of October"; icefalls form "in the month of January", when eagles concentrate below the lock and dam. The busiest time is "Friday through Sunday from 11-3" between mid-March and early November.

name: Warren Dunes State Park
line: Lake Michigan dunes rising 260 feet

jewels.name: The dunes and three miles of Lake Michigan shoreline
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond a Recreation Passport for vehicle entry
jewels.blurb: "Its rugged dune formation, rising 260 feet above the lake, offers spectacular views"; "3 miles of shoreline" and "an extensive network of richly forested dunes, large open dunes and interdunal wetlands."

jewels.name: Buoyed swim beach and day-use area
jewels.booking_route: none needed - Recreation Passport for vehicle entry
jewels.blurb: "A buoyed swim area is located along the day-use area on Lake Michigan"; three accessible bathroom buildings with foot showers and bottle fillers; three 100-foot accessible walkways; two beach/aqua wheelchairs to borrow; "five picnic areas located along the main entrance road". The DNR warns "state parks do not have lifeguards".

jewels.name: Six miles of dune and forest trails
jewels.blurb: DNR: "6 miles of hiking trails". Visit Southwest Michigan: "most are moderately difficult and all offer photo-worthy scenery. You can hike the trails all year, but the best months are March to November"; "Foot trails range from ⅓ mile to one mile long."

jewels.name: Mt. Randall Modern Campground
jewels.blurb: 182 sites in two loops, "shady and sunny, and some are wooded"; tagged electrical service, pull-through sites, some 50-amp, toilet and shower building, playground. 2026 rates table: $60 full hook-up, $50 50-amp, $45 20/30-amp; reservable May 1 - October 21.

jewels.name: Third Coast Paddling, Warren Dunes rentals
jewels.booking_route: own website online booking, walk-ins if available
jewels.blurb: The in-park rental station (the DNR calls it Third Coast Surf) "on the north side of the park, just past the far end of the parking lot, and right next to the dog beach": "Single / DOUBLE KayakS," "Stand-Up Paddleboards," "Loungeboards," and "Sandboards / Sand Sleds"; "10AM - 6PM EST Sat/Sun" from "Memorial Day Weekend through early October"; rentals from "$25 per hour" with life jackets included. (269) 468-9399.

jewels.name: Warren Dunes Rustic Mini Cabins
jewels.blurb: "There are three rustic cabins in Mt. Randall campground. Each cabin sleeps six people and includes two full-size beds and two single bunk beds"; ceramic heater, electricity, deck, fire pit and cook grill - Pine (#5), Oak (#51) and Hemlock (#65). 2026 rates table: $80; reservable May 1 - October 21.

jewels.name: Warren Dunes Hildebrandt Semi-Modern Campground
jewels.blurb: 37 sites, "more rustic and offers a relaxing atmosphere. Most sites are sunny and open, while some are wooded"; "There is no electrical service available"; vault toilets, with Mt. Randall's shower buildings "just a five-minute walk away". 2026 rates table: $40; reservable May 1 - October 21.

jewels.name: The dog beach
jewels.booking_route: none needed - Recreation Passport for vehicle entry
jewels.blurb: "Pets are allowed north of the northernmost swim buoy at the beach, providing 2.5 miles of shoreline open to pets. Pets must always be on a 6-foot leash and under an owner's immediate control."

jewels.name: Hang gliding and sandboarding the dunes
jewels.blurb: DNR: the dune "is excellent for hang gliding (permit is required)". Visit Southwest Michigan: "Hang glide off towering dunes; request a required permit from the park staff" and "Rocket down tall dunes on your sandboard."

jewels.name: Coast Guard-approved life jackets
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI.com via AvantLink)
jewels.blurb: The kit the DNR tells beach visitors to bring: "We also highly recommend bringing U.S. Coast Guard-approved life jackets—especially for children, new swimmers, and anyone less confident in the water", because "state parks do not have lifeguards". Warren Dunes is on the DNR's list of buoyed Great Lakes swim beaches.

jewels.name: Weko Beach Campground
jewels.blurb: Campspot: 3 miles straight-line, Bridgman - "a sandy shoreline on beautiful Lake Michigan! Including 68 campsites, and 11 rustic cabins"; "a seasonal boat launch, kayak rentals, picnic areas, and a playground"; "head over next door and check out Warren Dunes State Park". 4.3 from 194 verified reviews.

jewels.name: Tabor Hill Winery & Restaurant
jewels.blurb: Buchanan: "pairs award-winning Michigan wines with seasonally inspired cuisine"; "Recently recognized by Wine Enthusiast as one of the 57 Best Winery Restaurants in the World"; head chef Justin Carlisle; restaurant Thursday-Saturday 12-9 pm, Sunday 12-6 pm, closed Monday-Wednesday. (269) 422-1161.

jewels.name: Lemon Creek Winery
jewels.blurb: Berrien Springs: "Our 165-year-old historic farm sits on over 300 rolling acres of vineyards and orchards. Open year-round"; "12 flights to choose from in the summer and 8 flights in the winter. Each flight comes with five 2oz. pours"; U-pick fruit and a farm market. Hours Monday-Friday 11am-6pm, Saturday 10am-6pm, Sunday 12pm-6pm.

jewels.name: Warren Woods State Park
jewels.booking_route: none needed - Recreation Passport for vehicle entry
jewels.blurb: "a 311-acre nature preserve and hidden gem just 7 minutes from Warren Dunes State Park" with "a towering beech and majestic maple forest and the meandering Galien River"; "a quiet, 1-mile trail that follows the scenic river"; the Elm Valley Road entrance closes in winter.

jewels.name: Beach food trucks and Big Springs Souvenir Shop
jewels.blurb: "The Big Springs Souvenir Shop – located in the beach building – sells T-shirts, sweatshirts, ice cream, snacks and more." "There are five food trucks (hamburgers, hotdogs, ice cream, tacos, slushies, smoothies and more) located in the beach parking lot May through Labor Day weekend."

jewels.name: Grand Mere State Park
jewels.booking_route: none needed - Recreation Passport for vehicle entry
jewels.blurb: "magnificent sand dunes, deep blowouts and half a mile of Lake Michigan shoreline, accessible by the park's two trails. Two inland lakes lie behind the dunes"; bluegill fishing on South and Middle lakes; a track chair to borrow at no cost. "Hunting activities occur along the Dune Trail during designated seasons."

jewels.name: Hickory Creek Winery
jewels.blurb: 750 Browntown Road, Buchanan: "Traditional guided tasting of 5 wines - $15 per person" or a 5-wine flight board; tasting room and patio; "We do it all by hand, bucket-by-bucket." Open daily (Sat 11am-7pm, Sun-Thu 12-5pm, Fri 12-6pm). (269) 422-1100.

jewels.name: Nature programs and the Explorer program
jewels.booking_route: none needed - check the park's explorer program calendar
jewels.blurb: "Seasonal naturalists offer nature-based programming at the park during the summer and/or fall"; "The park also offers weekly nature programs not listed in the online calendar."

jewels.name: Winter on the dunes
jewels.booking_route: none needed - Recreation Passport for vehicle entry
jewels.blurb: "Sled and snowboard on the dunes." "Cross-country ski on a three-mile loop that takes you through a beautiful, wooded area behind the Great Warren Dunes. Or snowshoe on the dunes and other trails." "Photograph ice formations and snowy vistas."

jewels.name: Warren Dunes Youth Group-Use Campground
jewels.blurb: "This rustic group campground is available for groups up to 100. There are six sites that include picnic table and fire pit. There is a hand pump for water." 2026 rates table: "$20/group of 6", year-round. Reserve by calling the park, 269-426-4013.

jewels.name: Linens and cookware for the mini cabins
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (Sea to Summit via AvantLink)
jewels.blurb: The kit the DNR tells cabin guests to bring: "You must provide your own linens and cookware." The cabin supplies a "waist-high cook grill (only cooking unit provided)".

jewels.name: Shamrock Park RV Park - Berrien Springs
jewels.blurb: Campspot: 14 miles straight-line; "a picturesque retreat nestled along the scenic St. Joseph River" near U-pick fruit farms and the Berrien County Youth Fair; starting at $40.00; 4.8 from 39 verified reviews.

jewels.name: Wandering Soul Cabin, Sawyer
jewels.blurb: Glamping Hub: "located just a short drive away from the shores of Lake Michigan about half a mile from charming downtown" Sawyer; "About five minutes down the road from the property, glampers will find Warren Dunes State Park"; check-in 03:00 PM; "Smoking and pets are not allowed." New listing, no reviews.

jewels.name: Glamping Get Away bell tent, Niles
jewels.blurb: Glamping Hub: "Bell tent in Niles, MI", "4 guests • 1 bedroom • 3 beds • 1 bathroom", "located near the Saint Joseph River"; composting toilet; pets on leash; check-in 02:00-11:00 PM; 4.8 from 3 reviews.

jewels.name: Courtyard by Marriott St. Joseph Benton Harbor
jewels.blurb: 1295 Cinema Way, Benton Harbor, 269-210-3000, as listed by Visit Southwest Michigan: The Bistro, indoor pool and fitness centre; "a short drive to ... Silver Beach, Lake Michigan, and many other great attractions like local wineries, Warren Dunes, and the Kids Museum." Marriott's own page was not fetched (brand sites refuse automated reads).

jewels.name: SpringHill Suites by Marriott St. Joseph Benton Harbor
jewels.blurb: 1255 Cinema Way, Benton Harbor, 269-338-8300, as listed by Visit Southwest Michigan: a "Ninety-two-room all-suite property" off Interstate 94, "6 miles from both downtown St. Joseph and the Amtrak Station. Lake Michigan's Silver Beach is 5.5 miles away"; free hot breakfast, indoor pool. Marriott's own page was not fetched.

jewels.name: Hilton Garden Inn Benton Harbor/St. Joseph
jewels.blurb: 1300 Cinema Way, Benton Harbor, 269-926-5000, as listed by Visit Southwest Michigan: "We're off I-94, near golf courses and local breweries. Silver Beach on Lake Michigan's shoreline is 15 minutes away"; Garden Grille & Bar, indoor pool, pet friendly, "ADA/ Wheelchair Accessible", 106 guest rooms. Hilton's own page was not fetched.

jewels.name: Staybridge Suites Benton Harbor - St. Joseph
jewels.blurb: 1275 Cinema Way, Benton Harbor, 269-371-0000, as listed by Visit Southwest Michigan: "Spacious suites come with fully equipped kitchens"; complimentary breakfast buffet, evening social three days a week, indoor pool, guest laundry. IHG's own page was not fetched.

jewels.name: The Inn at Harbor Shores
jewels.booking_route: own website (link on the Visit Southwest Michigan listing) or phone
jewels.blurb: 800 Whitwam Drive, St. Joseph: "Set along the scenic St. Joseph River and just moments from the beaches of Lake Michigan"; Plank's Tavern, a full-service spa, marina, indoor and outdoor pools, bike rentals, and the "Jack Nicklaus Signature public golf course". 269-983-1111.

jewels.name: Hidden Ponds RV Resort - South Haven
jewels.blurb: Campspot: 37 miles straight-line; "spacious concrete pads with full hookups situated around peaceful, private fishing ponds", a heated pool, wellness trails, pickleball and "a dedicated off-leash dog park"; starting at $79.00; 4.9 from 9 verified reviews.

jewels.name: Riverfront Park Campground, Niles
jewels.blurb: Campspot: 18 miles straight-line; "nestled in the woods along the scenic Dowagiac River" with "extra-large campsites, many with direct river or private pond frontage"; general store, laundry, playground; no ratings yet.

jewels.name: Silver Beach Hotel
jewels.booking_route: own website (link on the Visit Southwest Michigan listing) or phone
jewels.blurb: 100 Main Street, St. Joseph, 269-983-7341, as listed by Visit Southwest Michigan: "90 minutes east of Chicago", boutique streets and Lake Michigan beaches "just a short walk away"; "All rooms have a balcony with a view!"

jewels.name: Staymaker at Journeyman Distillery
jewels.blurb: Journeyman Distillery's on-site restaurant in the Featherbone Factory, 109 Generations Drive, Three Oaks: "Open 362 days a year"; daily reservations or walk-ins; groups larger than 8 by email. (269) 820-2050.

jewels.name: Redamak's
jewels.blurb: New Buffalo: "The hamburger that made New Buffalo, Michigan famous!!"; started by George and Gladys Redamak in 1946, Maroney-owned since July 15, 1975; opens for the season in "Early March" and closes for winter; "No, we also don't allow call ahead seating."

jewels.name: Luisa's Harbert Swedish Bakery & Market
jewels.blurb: 13698 Red Arrow Hwy, Harbert: "The iconic Harbert Swedish Bakery has been providing Harbor Country with the best baked goods and prepared foods for over 100 years"; open 8:00 am - 2:00 pm, Thursday - Sunday. 269.469.9037.

jewels.name: Silver Beach Pizza
jewels.booking_route: own website reservations, carryout or delivery
jewels.blurb: 410 Vine Street, St. Joseph: "award-winning pizza and ice-cold schooners at Saint Joseph's most iconic dining spot" with Lake Michigan views; Mon-Thu 4-9pm, Fri 4-10pm, Sat 12-10pm, Sun 12-9pm. (269) 983-4743.

jewels.name: Lake Michigan Shore Wine Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - a trail of independent wineries
jewels.blurb: "a collaboration of 15 quality focused wineries located in the Lake Michigan Shore AVA"; "Located at the 42nd parallel and the southern end of Lake Michigan, our region contains 90% of Michigan's vineyards."

jewels.name: Sarett Nature Center
jewels.booking_route: own website (link on the Visit Southwest Michigan listing)
jewels.blurb: 2300 N Benton Center Road, Benton Harbor, as listed by Visit Southwest Michigan: "over 1,000 acres of protected land and eight miles of scenic trails"; boardwalks over wetlands and fens; "the tree top walkway"; an electric-powered vehicle or balloon-tired wagon can be reserved for access. 269-927-4832.

faq.q: How much does it cost to get into Warren Dunes State Park?
faq.a: Vehicle entry needs a Michigan Recreation Passport. For non-Michigan-registered vehicles the DNR lists "Annual $42" and "Daily $12 - good for entry and re-entry to any state park for the day." Michigan-registered vehicles pay "$15 when purchased at time of license plate registration renewal"; "A daily pass for residents is not available."

faq.q: Can you camp at Warren Dunes State Park?
faq.a: Yes. The DNR lists the Mt. Randall Modern Campground (182 sites), the Hildebrandt Semi-Modern Campground (37 sites, "no electrical service available"), three Rustic Mini Cabins that each sleep six, and a Youth Group-Use Campground for groups up to 100. Reservations: "800-447-2757 or reserve online".

faq.q: How much is camping at Warren Dunes State Park?
faq.a: The DNR's 2026 rates table lists Mount Randall at $60 (full hook-up), $50 (50-amp) and $45 (20/30-amp); Hildebrandt semi-modern at $40; the Mini Cabins at $80; and the rustic group camp at "$20/group of 6". The Recreation Passport is a separate fee.

faq.q: Does Warren Dunes State Park allow dogs?
faq.a: Yes, on part of the beach: "Pets are allowed north of the northernmost swim buoy at the beach, providing 2.5 miles of shoreline open to pets. Pets must always be on a 6-foot leash and under an owner's immediate control."

faq.q: Can you swim at Warren Dunes State Park?
faq.a: "A buoyed swim area is located along the day-use area on Lake Michigan." The DNR adds that buoys are "typically in place from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day", that "state parks do not have lifeguards", and that under double red flags "you're not allowed to enter the water from the beach."

faq.q: Can you have alcohol at Warren Dunes State Park?
faq.a: Not in season: "You may not possess or consume an alcoholic beverage in the park April 1 through Sept. 30 (unless the park manager has granted written authorization through an event permit)."

faq.q: Does Warren Dunes State Park have showers?
faq.a: The Mt. Randall Modern Campground has a toilet and shower building; Hildebrandt campers use "three modern toilet and shower buildings ... at the Mt. Randall modern campground, just a five-minute walk away." On the beach, "Each bathroom building offers two foot showers and bottle fillers."

faq.q: Can you metal detect at Warren Dunes State Park?
faq.a: "Metal detecting is allowed in certain park areas. Please consult the park map for designated locations and review applicable regulations. Only registered campers can metal detect in campgrounds."

faq.q: How many acres is Warren Dunes State Park?
faq.a: The DNR says the park "provides 1,500 acres of recreational opportunities along the beautiful shore of Lake Michigan", with "3 miles of shoreline" and dunes "rising 260 feet above the lake." Visit Southwest Michigan gives a different figure, "1,952 acres".

faq.q: What time does Warren Dunes State Park open?
faq.a: Visit Southwest Michigan lists the hours as "Year-round, Sunday-Saturday: 8 a.m. to 10 p.m."
