name: Badlands National Park
line: Buttes, fossil beds and bison prairie

jewels.name: Badlands Loop Road (Highway 240)
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park entrance fee only
jewels.blurb: a two-lane paved road through the North Unit, "1-2 Hours", with a dozen stops including Big Badlands, Yellow Mounds and Pinnacles overlooks; open year-round, 24/7; NPS: "Do not stop in the road" and "the Loop Road does close due to weather conditions occasionally in the winter"

jewels.name: Notch Trail
jewels.blurb: 1.25 miles round trip, moderate to strenuous, 1.5-2 hours, through a canyon and up a ladder to a ledge view of the White River Valley; NPS: "NOT recommended for anyone with a fear of heights. The trail can be treacherous during and after rains."

jewels.name: Fossil Preparation Lab
jewels.blurb: "The ONLY National Park where you can interact with paleontologists and interns" as they prepare specimens; at Ben Reifel Visitor Center, 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM, May 23 - October 31, 2026, 20-60 minutes

jewels.name: Sage Creek Rim Road and Roberts Prairie Dog Town
jewels.blurb: a 1-2 hour dirt/gravel drive (SD 590) where "Bison, bighorn, prairie dogs and a wide variety of birds are frequently seen", with four overlooks including Roberts Prairie Dog Town; "may be temporarily closed during or after heavy rain or snow"; NPS: keep "a minimum of a 100-foot distance from any wildlife"

jewels.name: Door Trail
jewels.blurb: 0.26 miles round trip, easy, about 20 minutes: an accessible boardwalk through "the Door", a break in the Badlands Wall, with marked posts continuing into the formations; site of the summer 8:30 am ranger Geology Walk

jewels.name: Window Trail
jewels.blurb: 0.26 miles round trip, easy, about 20 minutes: a short accessible boardwalk to a natural window in the Badlands Wall looking into an eroded canyon

jewels.name: Ben Reifel Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: the main visitor centre at Cedar Pass: museum exhibits "from ancient mosasaurs to Lakota history", the 25-minute film The Land of Stone and Light, a Badlands Natural History Association bookstore and Junior Ranger booklets; hours 7am-7pm summer, 8am-5pm spring and fall, 8am-4pm winter

jewels.name: Cedar Pass Lodge cabins
jewels.blurb: in-park cabins (King, King Duplex, Double Queen, Double Queen & Futon, Double Queen Cottage, with ADA options), "April 15th - October 15th"; run by Explor Badlands LLC, "a Concessioner under Contract with the U.S. Government"; the lodge was founded by Ben Millard in 1926 as a dance hall, "the first establishment in what would later become Badlands National Park"

jewels.name: Night Sky Program
jewels.blurb: "Park astronomers will guide you through the night sky" at the Cedar Pass Campground Amphitheater, June - September (9:30 PM June-July, 9:00 PM August, 8:30 PM September), with telescopes; the NPS says "visitors will be exposed to more than 7,500 stars" on any given night

jewels.name: Castle Trail
jewels.blurb: the park's longest established trail, 10.2 miles round trip, moderate, about 5 hours, from the Door and Window parking area to the Fossil Exhibit Trail; can be split into shorter segments

jewels.name: Cedar Pass Campground
jewels.blurb: 96 sites in the Agate, Butte and Group loops near Ben Reifel Visitor Center and Cedar Pass Lodge, some with electric hookups; "Quiet hours are from 10:00 pm - 6:00 am"; campfires prohibited, portable propane grills permitted; phone (605) 433-5460

jewels.name: Wall Drug Store, Wall
jewels.blurb: "Since 1931, Wall Drug has evolved into a 76,000-square-foot wonderland of free attractions, including the Western Art Gallery Restaurant"; Travel South Dakota names the cafe's "legendary hot beef sandwiches with mashed potatoes and gravy, buffalo burgers"

jewels.name: Minuteman Missile National Historic Site
jewels.booking_route: advance reservation required for Delta-01 tours (route not confirmed - reservation page returned 404)
jewels.blurb: three Cold War sites along 15 miles of I-90: the visitor center "immediately north of I-90, exit 131" (the park's Interior exit), Launch Control Facility Delta-01 at Exit 127 and the Delta-09 silo at Exit 116; a 30-minute film; "Advanced reservations are required for all guided-tours" of Delta-01; phone 605-433-5552

jewels.name: Fossil Exhibit Trail
jewels.blurb: 0.34 miles round trip, easy: a "Fully accessible boardwalk loop trail" with "fossil replicas and exhibits of now extinct creatures"; ranger Fossil Talks at 10:30 am and 2:00 pm, May 17 - September 26, 2026

jewels.name: Water: one gallon per person per day (NPS kit)
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates)
jewels.blurb: The NPS safety page advises "drinking 1 gallon of water per day" and warns "Summer in the badlands is hot and dry with temperatures often exceeding 100° Fahrenheit"; for backcountry trips: "Always carry at least one gallon of water per person per day". The kit this asks for is water bottles or a hydration reservoir sized to a gallon a person.

jewels.name: Sun and heat cover: SPF 15+, long sleeves, wide-brimmed hat (NPS kit)
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates apparel)
jewels.blurb: The NPS advises "wearing sunscreen with an SPF of 15 or higher, and covering up with long sleeves, pants, and a wide-brimmed hat" and to "dress in layers"; summer heat "often exceeding 100° Fahrenheit".

jewels.name: Closed-toed boots for badlands terrain (NPS kit)
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates shoes)
jewels.blurb: The NPS: "closed-toed shoes or boots are essential for hiking and exploring the badlands environment"; "Badlands terrain is unstable", and prairie rattlesnakes "seek shade under boardwalks, stairs, and tall grasses" - "Do not place your hands and feet in areas you cannot see".

jewels.name: Sage Creek Campground
jewels.blurb: a free, first-come first-served campground of 22 sites off Sage Creek Rim Road; accessible vault toilets, rough terrain

jewels.name: Backcountry camping and open hiking (Sage Creek Wilderness, Deer Haven)
jewels.blurb: "an open hike park, meaning that you are free to hike and camp off-trail"; no permit currently required but you must register at one of five points; camp "at least 0.5 miles from a road or trail"; "Campfires are not allowed under any circumstances"; "Always carry at least one gallon of water per person per day"; backcountry camping is currently prohibited in the South Unit

jewels.name: Badlands-White River KOA, Interior
jewels.blurb: 80 sites at 20720 SD Highway 44, Interior: Deluxe Cabins, Camping Cabins, tepees, tent sites and full-hookup RV sites (30/50 amp, water, sewer; max length "60ft"), with a pool, mini golf, playground, laundry and dump stations; season "April - Oct."; (605) 433-5337. koa.com returned 403, so this rests on Campendium.

jewels.name: Waysides restaurant, Cedar Pass
jewels.blurb: "The only location to purchase food in Badlands National Park" (NPS); Great Plains specialties with bison, blue corn, wild rice, chokecherries; 7:00 am - 8:00 pm, no reservations required; Travel South Dakota lists the Cedar Pass restaurant's "Sioux Indian Taco"

jewels.name: Sheep Mountain Table
jewels.blurb: a 5-mile dirt road to an overlook on the North/South Unit border, plus 2.5 miles more for high-clearance vehicles only; four-wheel drive recommended; NPS: "should not be driven during or after storms"; call (605) 433-5361 for status

jewels.name: White River Visitor Center (South Unit)
jewels.blurb: museum exhibits on the Badlands and Lakota heritage; the NPS "comanages the South Unit of the Badlands with the Oglala Lakota Tribe"; "typically May through October", 8am-5pm; Porch Talks at 10:30 AM and 2:30 PM, May 17 - September 7, 2026

jewels.name: Stronghold District and Stronghold Table
jewels.blurb: Pine Ridge Indian Reservation lands "owned by the Oglala Sioux Tribe and managed by the National Park Service"; Stronghold Table "is thought to be the site of the last Ghost Dance of the 19th century"; "you must obtain permission from private landowners" to cross to NPS land, and "off-road travel is prohibited"; a former WWII aerial gunnery range

jewels.name: Cliff Shelf Nature Trail
jewels.blurb: 0.86 miles round trip, moderate, about 30 minutes: a boardwalk-and-stair loop climbing 200 feet through juniper, a "popular birdwatching area"

jewels.name: Saddle Pass Trail
jewels.blurb: 0.68 miles round trip, strenuous, about 40 minutes: a steep climb up the Badlands Wall to a view over the White River Valley; NPS: "Treacherous during and after rains and can be dangerous during extreme heat."

jewels.name: Medicine Root Loop Trail
jewels.blurb: 4.18 miles round trip, moderate, about 2 hours, through mixed-grass prairie with distant Badlands views; reached from the Old Northeast Road pulloff or the Castle and Saddle Pass trails

jewels.name: Badlands Astronomy Festival
jewels.booking_route: none needed - schedule at Ben Reifel Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: a three-day festival (July 17-19, 2026) with a scale-model solar system walk, solar observing, speakers on topics including Lakota astronomy, and evening telescopes; "events do not require advance registration or tickets"; Minuteman Missile NHS runs paper rocket-building

jewels.name: Summer ranger programmes
jewels.blurb: Geology Walk on the Door Trail (8:30 AM), Prairie Walk from Ben Reifel (5:30-6:30 PM, "easy to moderate prairie hike" off-trail) and the Evening Program at the Cedar Pass Amphitheater on topics including "bison, bighorn sheep, fossils"; May 17 - September 26, 2026

jewels.name: Junior Ranger and I Walked the Badlands
jewels.blurb: "Pick up a Junior Ranger Booklet at the visitor center and turn it in to earn a Junior Ranger badge"; a GPS Adventure earns an "I Walked the Badlands" patch; an online Pick Your Park Adventure earns a patch by mail

jewels.name: Badlands Hotel & Campground, Interior
jewels.booking_route: own website booking; 605-433-5335; also listed on Hipcamp
jewels.blurb: rooms, a 2-bedroom apartment, 30/50-amp RV sites including pull-throughs, standard and group tent sites (up to 30), fire pits, laundry and two bathhouses at 900 SD Hwy 377; "Located just a mile from the iconic Badlands National Park"

jewels.name: Circle View Guest Ranch, Interior
jewels.blurb: a working cattle ranch on 2,800 acres with "badlands formations, a river valley", seven guestrooms with private baths and a full ranch breakfast at 7:30am in the Kruse family kitchen; open year-round; 20055 E. Highway 44

jewels.name: Badlands Frontier Cabins, Wall
jewels.blurb: "Thirty-Three (33) authentic custom built log cabins with modern amenities", private baths and daily housekeeping at 1101 Glenn Street, "just six miles from the entrance to Badlands National Park"

jewels.name: Fly Badlands scenic flights, Wall
jewels.blurb: narrated 40- and 60-minute scenic flights from Wall Municipal Airport with Golden Hour and GoPro add-ons; "a truly memorable way to experience one of America's most dramatic landscapes"; walk-ins welcome

jewels.name: Hotel Alex Johnson Rapid City, Curio Collection by Hilton
jewels.blurb: Travel South Dakota: "Located in downtown Rapid City in the Black Hills of South Dakota, this 1928 hotel is a member of the coveted Curio Collection by Hilton"; "Germanic Tudor-inspired architecture"; Juniper at Vertex Sky Bar and Paddy O'Neill's Irish Pub & Grill on site. Hilton's own page was not fetched.

jewels.name: Hilton Garden Inn Rapid City
jewels.blurb: Travel South Dakota: "Our Hilton Garden Inn Rapid City hotel is nestled in the beautiful Black Hills. Located just off of Interstate 90"; free Wi-Fi, airport shuttle and an on-site restaurant.

jewels.name: Fairfield Inn by Marriott, Rapid City
jewels.blurb: Travel South Dakota: "After a long day of splashing at WaTiki ® Indoor Waterpark Resort, slide into a lavish pillow-top bed and rest the night away" - the Fairfield is attached to the WaTiki waterpark on Rapid City's east side.

jewels.name: Sleepy Hollow Campground, Wall
jewels.booking_route: reservations available; phone (605) 279-2100 (own site not reached)
jewels.blurb: 54 RV pull-through sites and 40 tent spaces one block from Wall Drug at 118 W 4th Ave, with a heated pool, dog park, playground and laundry; open seasonally; (605) 279-2100

jewels.name: Black Hills & Badlands Sunrise & Set (Hipcamp)
jewels.blurb: a 40-acre working farm with an ARTAX tent campsite and the BADLANDS BUNKHOUSE cabin, billed as a "peaceful prairie retreat"

jewels.name: SCHEELS Camp & Hike Shop, Rapid City
jewels.blurb: "Whether you're prepping for your first overnight trek or upgrading your ultralight kit, our Camp and Hike Experts are ready to gear you up"; stocks "Osprey, Big Agnes, Nemo, and MSR". The last full gear shop on the I-90 approach from the west; Rapid City is 75 miles from the park (NPS directions page).

jewels.name: Badlands and Wall Drug day tour from Rapid City (North America Travel Service)
jewels.booking_route: inquiry form or phone 0800 820 3380 for schedule and pricing
jewels.blurb: a 7-8 hour narrated tour with pickup from downtown Rapid City hotels, stopping at Ben Reifel Visitor Center, the Loop Road and Wall Drug; the listing still names the Prairie Homestead, which its own website says is "permanently closed"

jewels.name: Days Inn by Wyndham Wall

jewels.name: Salty Steer, Wall

jewels.name: Badlands Saloon & Grille, Wall
jewels.blurb: per Travel South Dakota, "hearty burgers, steaks and pizza" with a focus on "fresh ingredients and family recipes"

jewels.name: Cowboy Corner, Interior
jewels.blurb: per Travel South Dakota, a "convenience store with a café that serves lunch and occasionally dinner on weekends"

jewels.name: Wagon Wheel Bar & Grill, Interior
jewels.blurb: per Travel South Dakota, a bar "serving some food, including pizza and burgers" with "a full bar with whiskey, beer, and pop"

jewels.name: Wakin' Bacon food truck, Wall

jewels.name: National Grasslands Visitor Center, Wall

jewels.name: Bigfoot Pass picnic area

jewels.name: Dahl's Chainsaw Art, Wall area

faq.q: What is the Badlands National Park entrance fee?
faq.a: The NPS lists $30 for a private vehicle, $25 for a motorcycle and $15 for an individual on foot or bicycle, each valid for 7 days, and $55 for a Badlands annual pass. "Entrance fees are collected year round."

faq.q: Is Badlands National Park open 24 hours?
faq.a: Yes. The NPS states "Badlands National Park is open 24 hours a day, seven days a week", though winter weather may temporarily close roads.

faq.q: Can you camp in Badlands National Park?
faq.a: Yes. The NPS lists Cedar Pass Campground (96 sites, some with electric hookups, reserved on recreation.gov) and Sage Creek Campground, "free, first-come first-serve, 22 sites".

faq.q: Do you need a permit for Badlands National Park?
faq.a: Not for backcountry camping at present. The NPS says "No permits are currently required for overnight stays", but you must register at one of five locations, camp "at least 0.5 miles from a road or trail", and "Campfires are not allowed under any circumstances". Backcountry camping is currently prohibited in the South Unit.

faq.q: Where can you see wildlife in Badlands National Park?
faq.a: The NPS says "Bison, bighorn, prairie dogs and a wide variety of birds are frequently seen from Sage Creek Rim Road", a gravel road that may close after heavy rain or snow. Keep "a minimum of a 100-foot distance from any wildlife".

faq.q: What can you do at Badlands National Park with kids?
faq.a: The Fossil Preparation Lab at Ben Reifel Visitor Center is open 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM, May 23 - October 31, 2026; the NPS calls Badlands "The ONLY National Park where you can interact with paleontologists and interns". Summer ranger programmes include Fossil Talks and an evening Night Sky Program.

faq.q: Where can you eat in Badlands National Park?
faq.a: The NPS says the only place to buy food in the park is Cedar Pass Lodge, near Ben Reifel Visitor Center; its restaurant is Waysides.

faq.q: How far is Badlands National Park from Rapid City?
faq.a: "Badlands National Park is located 75 miles east of Rapid City, South Dakota", with entrances from I-90 at Exit 131 (Interior) and Exit 110 (Wall).

faq.q: What should you wear to Badlands National Park?
faq.a: The NPS advises "wearing sunscreen with an SPF of 15 or higher, and covering up with long sleeves, pants, and a wide-brimmed hat", to "dress in layers", and says "closed-toed shoes or boots are essential for hiking and exploring the badlands environment". It also advises "drinking 1 gallon of water per day".

faq.q: What is the weather like in Badlands National Park in October?
faq.a: The NPS gives "October Averages: High 68°F, Low 39°F, Precipitation 0.90 inches" and says in fall "Weather becomes more stable".

name: Theodore Roosevelt National Park
line: Badlands bison, wild horses and Roosevelt's cabin

jewels.name: South Unit Scenic Loop Drive
jewels.blurb: the NPS's "36-mile Scenic Loop Drive" from Medora with "outstanding views of the badlands, prairie dog towns, and abundant wildlife watching"; "Travel time around the loop is about 90 minutes"; the full loop reopened on November 25, 2025 after a roughly $51 million repair of the section closed since 2019

jewels.name: Bison in both units
jewels.blurb: bison "roam throughout the North and South units of the park, and most visitors see them as they drive the park roads"; NPS: "They generally appear tranquil, but may attack without warning if they are disturbed"

jewels.name: Wild horses of the South Unit
jewels.blurb: about 198 horses in the South Unit, often seen near the Talkington trailhead (I-94 Exit 36), Painted Canyon, Buck Hill and Wind Canyon; they "are often visible from the Scenic Loop Drive and from I-94"

jewels.name: North Unit Scenic Drive and River Bend Overlook
jewels.blurb: a "14-mile scenic drive" off US 85 that "rolls across the badlands and then climbs up to the historic River Bend Overlook" and on to Oxbow Overlook; out and back "generally takes just over one hour"; River Bend has an accessible viewing deck

jewels.name: Painted Canyon Overlook and Trail
jewels.blurb: a 0.9-mile, 45-minute trail that "Descends into canyon revealing rock layers and junipers"; the NPS warns "every step down means a step back up on the return"; Painted Canyon has its own visitor centre and park store

jewels.name: Maltese Cross Cabin
jewels.booking_route: none needed; tour times not stated on the page
jewels.blurb: Roosevelt's 1883 ponderosa pine cabin, which he called "a temporary home", behind the South Unit Visitor Center; shown at the 1904 St. Louis World's Fair and holding a trunk marked "T.R."; wheelchair accessible per the NPS

jewels.name: Wind Canyon Trail
jewels.blurb: 0.4 miles, 20 minutes, in the South Unit: "Canyon-side hiking with river views" and a named sunset spot; also one of the NPS's wild-horse viewing locations

jewels.name: Medora Musical, Burning Hills Amphitheatre
jewels.blurb: "the ultimate Country Western Music Revue" in an outdoor amphitheatre of over 2,800 seats, with wheelchair and mobility seating on the mezzanine; 2026 season June 3 to September 12; adults $62.95-$85.95, students $25.95-$45.95, age 6 and under free; 15% senior discount on Tuesdays

jewels.name: Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library, Medora
jewels.booking_route: timed tickets at trlibrary.com/tickets; engine not named
jewels.blurb: "open now" in Medora, with museum, retail store and restaurant; fall hours September 14 to November 30 Tue-Fri 9-4, Sat-Sun 9-6; "Last timed entry" 90 minutes before closing; the outdoor boardwalk is "Accessible outside of Library hours"

jewels.name: Prairie dog towns and the Buckhorn Trail
jewels.blurb: "The park road passes through three large prairie dog towns in the South Unit"; in the North Unit, Prairie Dog Town via Buckhorn is 1.5 miles and the full Buckhorn 11.4 miles; NPS: "Rattlesnakes and black widow spiders often live in prairie dog burrows"

jewels.name: Pitchfork Steak Fondue
jewels.blurb: "we take 12 oz steaks, cooked to medium-well perfection, and give them a western-style fondue twist!" - New York strips on pitchforks dunked in barrels of oil, with a buffet and live music; 2026 season June 3 to September 12; $54.55 full, $29.35 buffet only, kids' hotdog meal free for 12 and under

jewels.name: Oxbow Overlook
jewels.blurb: at the end of the North Unit Scenic Drive, "a spectacular scenic vista" over the meandering Little Missouri, with an accessible sidewalk, interpretive waysides, restrooms and RV parking

jewels.name: Maah Daah Hey Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed; shuttles via Dakota Cycling Adventures
jewels.blurb: per Medora, "This 144-mile trail traverses the Badlands, Little Missouri National Grasslands, private land, and the North and South Units" for hiking, biking and horses, managed by the USFS Dakota Prairie Grasslands; the NPS hiking page calls it a "96-mile trail connecting all three units"

jewels.name: Elkhorn Ranch Unit
jewels.booking_route: none needed; ask at a visitor centre about road conditions
jewels.blurb: Roosevelt's second ranch, "thirty-five miles north of Medora"; "While the Elkhorn Cabin no longer stands, foundation stones indicate where the structure... was once located"; NPS: "The last three miles of the route sometimes require 4-wheel drive and/or a high-clearance vehicle"

jewels.name: Petrified Forest Loop
jewels.blurb: "Theodore Roosevelt National Park is home to the third highest concentration of petrified wood in the United States"; 3 miles out and back to either section or 10.4 miles for the loop; NPS: "Directions to the Petrified Forest trailhead have changed. Please use the approved legal route from I-94, Exit 10"

jewels.name: Caprock Coulee Trail
jewels.blurb: North Unit: the 1.5-mile nature trail through "Badlands terrain; diverse habitats and dry washes", or the full 4.3-mile loop climbing to a butte ridge, 2-3 hours

jewels.name: Cottonwood Campground
jewels.blurb: 76 sites including one group site in the South Unit, pull-throughs up to 85 ft; "Beginning May 1, 2026 all sites are by reservation at recreation.gov"; primitive, no hookups or showers

jewels.name: Juniper Campground
jewels.blurb: the North Unit campground; "Many sites are quite large (over 50 ft)" and walk-to sites "can only accomodate passenger vehicles"; two accessible sites; primitive, no hookups or showers

jewels.name: Medora Campground, cabins and Conestoga wagons
jewels.blurb: 226 tent and RV sites from tent-only to 50-amp full hookups, cabins for 7-8 including the new Rivers Edge Cabins, and Conestoga wagons that sleep 4 with a king bed and air conditioning "along the Little Missouri River"; season May 12 to October 4

jewels.name: Rough Riders Hotel, Medora
jewels.blurb: a former boarding house with "a grand hearth, tin-tiled ceiling, and one of the largest private libraries of books by and about Theodore Roosevelt"; historic wing by stairs only, ADA rooms in the standard wing; year-round

jewels.name: Hotel 1883, Medora
jewels.blurb: "Nestled along the west bank of the Little Missouri River", over 100 rooms in 15 layouts, with an indoor pool and hot tub and continental breakfast; named for the year Medora was founded

jewels.name: Buck Hill
jewels.blurb: 0.2 miles, "Short but steep", to the highest accessible point in the park; the NPS names the Buck Hill area for elk "feeding in early morning or evening"

jewels.name: Boicourt Overlook and Skyline Vista
jewels.blurb: two of the park's shortest walks: Skyline Vista, 0.1 miles, "Flat, paved"; Boicourt Overlook, 0.2 miles, "ranger-recommended for sunsets"; both named by the NPS as hard-surfaced

jewels.name: Achenbach Trail and Sperati Point
jewels.booking_route: free backcountry permit at the North or South Unit Visitor Center for overnight
jewels.blurb: North Unit, 18 miles, 10-12 hours, with "Steep climbs and descents and two river crossings"; the shorter Sperati Point via Achenbach is 1.5 miles from Oxbow Overlook to a river overlook

jewels.name: Little Missouri River float, Medora to Long X Bridge
jewels.booking_route: free backcountry permit for overnight camping; no outfitter named by the NPS
jewels.blurb: 107.5 miles, about five days; "May and June usually being the best months"; "A river depth of at least 2.5 feet (699 cfs) at Medora is required for fair boating"; storms can make it "a raging torrent carrying large logs and debris"

jewels.name: Medora Trail Rides (Medora Riding Stables)
jewels.blurb: guided rides run by the Theodore Roosevelt Medora Foundation: 30 minutes $47.95, 1 hour $56.95, 2 hours $113.95; minimum age 7, 250 lb limit; fall season September 28 to October 11, Friday-Sunday only; the NPS says "Guided trail rides are no longer offered within the park"

jewels.name: Dakota Cycling Adventures, Medora
jewels.blurb: at 365 Main St, "the only full service bike shop in the heart of the Badlands": rentals, Maah Daah Hey shuttles and guided tours; named by Medora as the trail's outfitter (as Dakota Cyclery)

jewels.name: Water kit for badlands hiking
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail link (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates)
jewels.blurb: the NPS: "The most important thing to have with you on a hike in the North Dakota badlands is water" - "we recommend around 1 liter of water per person per hour", and "Backcountry hikers should plan to carry all the water they will need for their entire itinerary"; the park has no services inside it

jewels.name: Boots, map and first-aid kit for the trails
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail link (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates); maps at the park visitor centers
jewels.blurb: the NPS: "Always wear proper footwear and carry a map and first aid kit" - "you shouldn't just throw on flip-flops and head out on the trail"; "Detailed maps are available for sale at the park visitor centers"; it also warns of "ticks in late spring and early summer" and that rattlesnakes "do not always give a warning before striking"

jewels.name: Bully Pulpit Golf Course
jewels.blurb: 18 holes "carved into North Dakota's Badlands" along the Little Missouri, billed as "Voted USA Today's #1 Best Golf Course in 2025"; April-October, weather dependent; summer from $147, spring and fall from $107, juniors free with a paying adult; shuttle from select Medora lodging

jewels.name: Chateau de Mores State Historic Site, Medora
jewels.blurb: "This 26-room, two-story frame building was built in 1883 as the summer residence of the Marquis's family"; the chateau is closed October 1-April 30, the interpretive centre open Tue-Sat 9-5 in that period; adult $10, child 6-17 $5; "Allow one hour for visit"

jewels.name: North Dakota Cowboy Hall of Fame, Medora
jewels.blurb: "the interpretive center for the history of the northern plains and North Dakota's western lifestyle", with galleries on Native Americans, homesteaders, ranchers and rodeo cowboys; children free; year-round with adjusted winter hours

jewels.name: Theodore's Dining Room and TR's Tavern
jewels.blurb: "upscale Western cuisine" in the Rough Riders Hotel; TR's Tavern pours "Classic Cocktails with a TR Twist" with Maple Bourbon Brussel Sprouts, Shrimp and Grits and Bourbon Steak Tips, Wednesday-Sunday 4-8:30 pm, year-round

jewels.name: Medora Gospel Brunch
jewels.blurb: the 2026 show "Hope Rising" with a band and gospel quartet and "endless helpings of egg bakes, breakfast meats, and more" at the Town Square Showhall; June 12 to September 13, 2026, Tue, Wed, Fri and Sun at 9 am MDT; adults $59.95-$65.95 with brunch

jewels.name: Rough Rider State Park (formerly Sully Creek), near Medora
jewels.blurb: "just minutes away from the historic town of Medora": modern sites $25-30, primitive $15, equestrian camping, a Maah Daah Hey trailhead "just northwest of the park entrance", and spring canoeing on the Little Missouri; book up to 95 days ahead

jewels.name: Red Trail Campground, Medora
jewels.blurb: "family owned and operated campground, providing campers with a second home for over 47 years"; Good Sam and FMCA discounts; season May 15 to September 30

jewels.name: Boots Campground, Medora
jewels.blurb: "3576 East River Road South, Medora", "one mile outside of Historic Medora": 16 RV sites with "full electrical and water hookups" plus sewer, 30/50-amp, rigs to 50 ft, 3 cabins, Wi-Fi and the on-site Boots Bar & Grill; no bathrooms or showers on site; from $45 a night (Campspot listing)

jewels.name: The Crossings Campground, Belfield
jewels.blurb: "301 Highway 10 West, Belfield": 31 full-hookup RV sites (30/50-amp, sewer, water, Wi-Fi) in "a clean, no-frills atmosphere"; "9.5 miles from Painted Canyon Overlook & Visitor Center", "15 miles east of TRNP South Unit & Historic Medora", "30 miles south of" the North Unit; "we do not have an office or bathroom facilities on site"

jewels.name: TownePlace Suites by Marriott Dickinson
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "240 29th Street West, Dickinson, ND 58601" among Dickinson, ND hotels; the NPS puts Dickinson 35 miles from the South Unit. The brand's own page (marriott.com) was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Hampton Inn Dickinson
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "100 14th Street West, Dickinson, ND 58601" among Dickinson, ND hotels; the NPS puts Dickinson 35 miles from the South Unit. The brand's own page (hilton.com) was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Dickinson
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "103 14th Street West, Dickinson, ND 58601" among Dickinson, ND hotels; the NPS puts Dickinson 35 miles from the South Unit. The brand's own page (ihg.com) was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Candlewood Suites Dickinson
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "1430 Sims Street, Dickinson, ND 58601" among Dickinson, ND hotels; the NPS puts Dickinson 35 miles from the South Unit. The brand's own page (ihg.com) was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Little Mo Nature Trail
jewels.blurb: North Unit river-bottom loop, 0.7 miles paved or 1.1 miles unpaved, 30-45 minutes; one of the NPS's hard-surfaced accessible trails

jewels.name: Lone Tree Loop and the creek loops
jewels.blurb: South Unit day-long loops: Lone Tree, 9.6 miles with "Difficult stream crossings"; Jones/Lower Talkington/Lower Paddock, 11.4 miles; Upper Paddock/Talkington, 15.4-19.4 miles with Painted Canyon access

jewels.name: Ridgeline and Coal Vein trails
jewels.blurb: South Unit short hikes: Ridgeline, 0.6 miles with stairs and a badlands focus; Coal Vein, 0.6-0.8 miles, a geology trail "featuring historic coal vein"

jewels.name: North Unit longhorn demonstration herd
jewels.blurb: "A small demonstration herd is kept in the North Unit as a cultural resource. They may be spotted around mile marker two of the scenic drive"

jewels.name: Dakota Nights Astronomy Festival
jewels.blurb: 2026 dates were August 14-15 at the South Unit Visitor Center lawn and Peaceful Valley Ranch: solar scopes, stomp rockets, a Night Explorer Junior Ranger and telescope stargazing 8:45-11:30 pm

jewels.name: Point to Point Park, Medora
jewels.blurb: "mini golf, perception illusion house, zipline adventures and a lazy river pool modeled after the Little Missouri"; paid attractions weekends 11 am-7 pm; packages $27.95-$58.95; trails, pickleball and the wooden children's park free

jewels.name: Medora fall shows and Medora Musical Christmas
jewels.blurb: The Everly Brothers Experience (October 7-18) and Figuring It Out (October 21-November 1, 2026) at the Old Town Hall Theater; Beer and Bacon Festival October 3; Medora Musical Christmas at Burning Hills, December 3-20

jewels.name: Salt + Scoria Restaurant, TR Presidential Library
jewels.blurb: the library's restaurant, "offering full and lite service menus depending on season"

jewels.name: Badlands Pizza, Medora
jewels.blurb: "The perfect grub spot for families!" - specialty pizzas such as the Cowboy Combo, "Vegan & gluten-free options", draft beer and live music Thursday-Saturday; seasonal, June 3 to September 19 in 2026, so closed on this build date

jewels.name: Medora Fudge & Ice Cream Depot
jewels.blurb: "homemade fudge and ice cream" with a shaded patio; open May 30 to September 12 and "Closed Sept 13 - May 29"

jewels.name: Wannagan Creek Cabins, north of Medora
jewels.blurb: four cabins - "stay right next to Theodore Roosevelt National Park" - "just minutes off Interstate 94" with a "two night minimum"; bath linens supplied, bring your own bedding; no pets

jewels.name: Watford City hotels for the North Unit
jewels.blurb: the Watford City visitor site lists The Watford, Little Missouri Inn & Suites, Roosevelt Inn & Suites, Teddy's Residential Suites and Comfort Inn & Suites; the NPS puts Watford City 15 miles from the North Unit

jewels.name: Watford City Basin RV Resort
jewels.blurb: "304 16th Ave SW, Watford City", the North Unit's gateway town: a 57-acre park billing itself "the largest full-service RV destination in western North Dakota" with "784 full hook-up sites with 50/30/20-amp service" (the booking panel shows 341 RV sites and 64 cabins), clubhouse, showers and laundry

jewels.name: Stonehome Brewing Company, Watford City
jewels.booking_route: walk-in; events and catering via its site
jewels.blurb: "Real. AuthenTic. Craft." - brewery with food at 313 Fox Hills Parkway, Watford City, the North Unit's gateway town; open daily from 9 or 11 am

jewels.name: Dickinson museum campus
jewels.blurb: per the Dickinson visitor bureau, the Badlands Dinosaur Museum "Houses thousands of rock, mineral and fossil specimens including a complete real Triceratops skeleton", beside the Joachim Regional Museum and the Pioneer Machinery Hall

jewels.name: Theodore Roosevelt Center, Dickinson State University
jewels.blurb: "a rotating exhibit gallery, research library, reading room, and workspaces" on the DSU hilltop campus, "open to the public free of charge year-round (with seasonal hours)"; home of the TR Digital Library

jewels.name: Dickinson dining: BrickHouse Grille, JD's BBQ, Phat Fish Brewing
jewels.blurb: the three restaurants the Dickinson visitor bureau names in its one-day itinerary (their own sites returned 403 this session)

faq.q: How much is Theodore Roosevelt National Park?
faq.a: The NPS lists $30 for a private vehicle, $25 for a motorcycle and $15 per person on foot or bicycle (16 and over), each valid for 7 days. A Theodore Roosevelt annual pass is $55, and America the Beautiful passes are accepted.

faq.q: Is Theodore Roosevelt National Park open?
faq.a: The NPS says the park is "open 24 hours a day, year-round", and the full South Unit Scenic Loop Drive reopened on November 25, 2025, after a section had been closed since 2019. "Portions of the South Unit Scenic Loop Drive and North Unit Scenic Road may be closed in winter due to snow and ice."

faq.q: What time zone is Theodore Roosevelt National Park in?
faq.a: Two: "The North Unit operates on Central time, while the South Unit operates on Mountain time."

faq.q: Can you stay in Theodore Roosevelt National Park?
faq.a: Only by camping. The NPS states: "No lodging is available inside Theodore Roosevelt National Park." South Unit lodging is in Medora and in Beach (25 miles), Belfield (15 miles) and Dickinson (35 miles); North Unit lodging is in Watford City (15 miles), Alexander (35 miles) and Killdeer (45 miles).

faq.q: Can you camp in Theodore Roosevelt National Park?
faq.a: Yes. Cottonwood (South Unit) and Juniper (North Unit) are primitive campgrounds with "no hookups or showers", plus Roundup Group Horse Camp, all reserved on recreation.gov. Backcountry camping needs "a free Backcountry Permit in the North or South Unit Visitor Centers".

faq.q: Do you need reservations for Theodore Roosevelt National Park?
faq.a: Not to enter - one of the entrance passes is required. For Cottonwood Campground the NPS states: "Beginning May 1, 2026 all sites are by reservation at recreation.gov".

faq.q: Where can you see bison in Theodore Roosevelt National Park?
faq.a: Bison "roam throughout the North and South units of the park, and most visitors see them as they drive the park roads." The NPS warns: "They generally appear tranquil, but may attack without warning if they are disturbed."

faq.q: Where can you see horses in Theodore Roosevelt National Park?
faq.a: The NPS says the horses live in the South Unit only and "are often visible from the Scenic Loop Drive and from I-94"; it names the Talkington trailhead area off Exit 36, Painted Canyon, Buck Hill and Wind Canyon.

faq.q: Is the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library open?
faq.a: The library in Medora is "open now", with a museum, store and the Salt + Scoria restaurant; fall hours run September 14 to November 30, Tuesday-Friday 9-4 and Saturday-Sunday 9-6, with "Last timed entry" 90 minutes before closing.

name: Wind Cave National Park
line: Boxwork cave beneath a bison prairie

jewels.name: Natural Entrance Tour
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov (120 days to 2 days ahead) or same-day tickets at the visitor center; "Roughly half of all tour tickets are held in reserve for same-day sales"
jewels.blurb: 1 hour 15 minutes, 2/3 mile, 300 stairs, MODERATE: "This tour includes a visit to the natural entrance of Wind Cave where visitors can see the largest opening to the cave and learn how we get our name"; "Wind Cave's famous boxwork is abundant throughout this trip"; exits by elevator. "This is a great tour for families." Adults $16, ages 62+ and 6-15 $8, 5 and under free.

jewels.name: Wind Cave boxwork
jewels.booking_route: seen only on a ranger-guided cave tour ("All access is by a ranger guided tour")
jewels.blurb: "Boxwork is found in small amounts in other caves, but perhaps in no other cave in the world is boxwork so well-formed and abundant as in Wind Cave. Boxwork is made of thin blades of calcite that project from cave walls and ceilings, forming a honeycomb pattern." The park calls Wind Cave "one of the longest and most complex caves in the world."

jewels.name: Garden of Eden Tour
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov (120 days to 2 days ahead) or same-day at the visitor center
jewels.blurb: 1 hour, 1/4 mile, 150 stairs: "This one-hour tour is our least strenuous tour. It is a wonderful sample of Wind Cave. Small amounts of all of the beautiful cave formations - boxwork, cave popcorn, and flowstone - are seen"; enters and leaves by elevator. Adults $14, ages 62+ and 6-15 $7. Runs year-round (10:00 am and 3:00 pm, November 1, 2026 to April 24, 2027).

jewels.name: Bison herd on the Wind Cave prairie
jewels.blurb: "There are 400-450 bison in Wind Cave National Park"; good places to see them are "along U.S. 385, S.D. 87, and primitive roads N.P.S. 5 & 6." The herd descends from 14 bison sent by the American Bison Society from the New York Zoological Gardens in 1913 and six from Yellowstone in 1916. Visitors must stay at least 25 yards away; "Bison are more aggressive during the calving and mating season from May through August."

jewels.name: Fairgrounds Tour
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov (120 days to 2 days ahead) or same-day at the visitor center
jewels.blurb: 1 hour 30 minutes, 2/3 mile, 450 stairs, STRENUOUS: "explores both the upper and middle levels of Wind Cave" - boxwork in the middle level, popcorn and frostwork in the upper; "This is our most strenuous walking tour", with "one flight of 89 steps going up." Adults $16, ages 62+ and 6-15 $8.

jewels.name: Wild Cave Tour
jewels.booking_route: phone only, 605-745-4600, up to one month ahead during visitor center hours
jewels.blurb: Summer only, up to 4 hours, VERY STRENUOUS: "an introduction to safe caving in an undeveloped part of the cave"; "Most of the tour is spent crawling on your hands and knees"; visitors "will need to fit through a space that is 10 inches tall and 3 feet wide". Limited to 6 people, minimum age 16; $45. The park provides helmets, lights, gloves, elbowpads and kneepads.

jewels.name: Candlelight Tour
jewels.booking_route: phone only, 605-745-4600, up to one month ahead during visitor center hours
jewels.blurb: Summer only, 2 hours, 2/3 mile, 424 stairs, STRENUOUS: "Experience the cave by candlelight the way the earliest explorers of Wind Cave saw it!" in "a less developed, unlit section of the cave"; each participant carries a candle bucket. Limited to 10 people, minimum age 8; $16.

jewels.name: Wind Cave Visitor Center
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free; 26611 US Highway 385, Hot Springs, SD 57747; 605 745-4600
jewels.blurb: "opened daily all year except Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's Day", 8:00 am - 4:30 pm with expanded summer hours; "All cave tours leave from the visitor center." Exhibit rooms on bison and the cave, the park film One Park, Two Worlds, and a park store run by the Black Hills Parks and Forests Association. "Do not use your GPS to find the visitor center - you will get lost."

jewels.name: Elk Mountain Campground
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov (reservations late May-September; first-come, first-served through Recreation.gov otherwise)
jewels.blurb: "straddles the edge of a ponderosa pine forest and open prairie"; 75 sites, "but rarely fills to capacity"; maximum site length 36 feet. "$24.00 per site per night regularly, and $12.00 per site per night when the water is turned off (generally October through May)"; Senior and Access Pass holders pay half. Open year-round; reservable late May through September. Accessible sites B2 and D3.

jewels.name: Natural Entrance of Wind Cave
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free walk from the visitor center
jewels.blurb: The cave's natural opening, "a deeply spiritual place to many people"; in Lakota oral tradition Wind Cave (Oniya Oshoka) is where "not only were the first humans born from the cave, but the first bison came from the cave as well." Wheelchair users can reach it "via a ramp and sidewalk from the visitor center".

jewels.name: Accessibility Tour
jewels.booking_route: phone 605-745-4600 the day of or up to three days ahead, or ask at the information desk
jewels.blurb: 30 minutes, 100 feet, 0 stairs, EASY: "Limited areas of the cave are accessible to wheelchairs and those with limited mobility"; rides the elevator in and out, from a building "about 200 yards south of the visitor center" with accessible parking. Adults $6, 62+ and 6-15 $3. Sign-language interpreters with two weeks' notice.

jewels.name: Kit for the cave tour
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates) - nothing is sold by the park
jewels.blurb: The park's own list: "Long sleeves or jackets. The cave temperature is a constant 54°F (12°C)." "Comfortable shoes with non-slip soles. Sandals are not recommended"; the Candlelight and Wild Cave tours require "Sturdy, lace-up hiking boots or shoes (designed for trail) with aggressive tread". Bags, food, water and walking sticks are not allowed in the cave.

jewels.name: Kit for the prairie trails
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates) - topographic maps are sold at the visitor center bookstore
jewels.blurb: "Carry and drink plenty of water. There are few water sources and all water in the backcountry must be boiled, filtered, or treated." "Wear fully enclosed footwear and long pants as poison ivy and ticks may be encountered anywhere in the park. It's also recommended to bring a wide brimmed hat, sunscreen, and bug spray." "Bring a park map" and extra layers - summer storms bring "large hail".

jewels.name: Rankin Ridge Nature Trail
jewels.blurb: 1 mile round trip, EASY loop: "Gain spectacular views from the highest point in the park"; the fire tower is closed, but "on a clear day, you may be able to see as far as the Badlands from the trail's eastern edge." RVs and trailers are not permitted at the trailhead.

jewels.name: Prairie Vista Trail
jewels.blurb: About 1 mile round trip, EASY: "Stroll the prairie grasslands from the visitor center. Waysides provide information along the way." One of the park's two pet-friendly trails.

jewels.name: Elk Mountain Trail and elk bugling
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free trail and free ranger program
jewels.blurb: 1 mile round trip, EASY, around the campground: "During September and October, elk may be heard bugling at dawn and dusk." A free ranger Elk Bugling Program runs "from mid- to late-September" from the campground amphitheater, then caravans to listen for elk.

jewels.name: Prairie dog town on Bison Flats
jewels.blurb: "The prairie dog town nearest the visitor center is on Bison Flats, at the south junction of the visitor center road and U.S. 385, about ½ mile (0.8 km) south of the visitor center." An interpretive exhibit sits at the junction of U.S. 385 and S.D. 87. "Do not feed prairie dogs or other wildlife."

jewels.name: Wind Cave Canyon Trail
jewels.blurb: 1.8 miles one way, EASY: "This former road follows Wind Cave Canyon to the park boundary. Limestone cliffs provide nesting areas for cliff swallows, canyon wrens, and great horned owls." Look for Red-headed and Lewis' woodpeckers.

jewels.name: Centennial Trail (Wind Cave section)
jewels.blurb: 6 miles one way, STRENUOUS: "the southernmost part of a 111-mile trail through the Black Hills, ending at Bear Butte State Park"; it crosses prairies and ponderosa forest along Beaver Creek. "Shuttles are available in the Black Hills for through-hikers"; overnight parking needs a camping permit.

jewels.name: Highland Creek Trail
jewels.blurb: 8.6 miles one way, STRENUOUS: "the longest and most diverse trail in the park, crossing mixed-grass prairies, ponderosa pine forests, and riparian habitats of Highland Creek, Beaver Creek, and Wind Cave Canyon."

jewels.name: Boland Ridge Trail
jewels.blurb: 2.6 miles one way, STRENUOUS: "A series of climbs offer panoramic views of the Black Hills, Red Valley, and the plains beyond. Elk are often seen from this trail in the morning and evening." Trailhead on NPS 6.

jewels.name: Cold Brook Canyon Trail
jewels.blurb: 1.4 miles, MODERATE: "a ponderosa forest gives way to the open prairie and crosses a prairie dog town, a good place to see prairie falcons and other raptors." Trailhead about 1 mile south of the visitor center on US 385.

jewels.name: Backcountry camping and the open-hike policy
jewels.booking_route: free permit at the visitor center information desk
jewels.blurb: "Backcountry camping is allowed in the northern part of the park. A free permit is required", obtained at the visitor center information desk. "Wind Cave National Park is an open hike park meaning visitors are welcome to hike off designated trails" - bring plenty of water and a map; "cell service within the park is very limited."

jewels.name: Horseback riding by permit
jewels.booking_route: free day-use permit at the visitor center (bring your own horse)
jewels.blurb: "Horses are permitted throughout Wind Cave National park" with a day-use permit from the visitor center; riding is prohibited "near water sources, directly on any maintained hiking trail, on park roadways, and in the campground and picnic areas", and hay must be certified weed free.

jewels.name: Custer State Park
jewels.blurb: Borders Wind Cave to the north: "Encompassing 71,000 acres in the Black Hills, Custer State Park is home to abundant wildlife and adventure"; "9 campgrounds including camper cabins, tent campsites, RV campsites with electricity, and horse camp" (Blue Bell, Center Lake, Game Lodge, Grace Coolidge, Legion Lake, Stockade Lake North and South, Sylvan Lake among them). Entrance $25 per vehicle for 1-7 days. Stay at least 100 yards from bison.

jewels.name: Wildlife Loop State Scenic Byway
jewels.booking_route: self-drive with a state park entrance license
jewels.blurb: "Travel through 18 miles of open grasslands and pine-speckled hills that much of Custer State Park's wildlife calls home" - bison, pronghorn, deer, elk, coyotes, burros and prairie dogs; allow "between 1.5 and 2 hours to complete the loop". Open year-round with a South Dakota State Park Entrance License.

jewels.name: Buffalo Safari Jeep Tour
jewels.booking_route: own website booking (Custer State Park Resort)
jewels.blurb: Open-air Jeeps "off-road to the private, interior dirt roads of the Park" in search of "pronghorns, elk, and the noble buffalo"; 1 1/2 to 2 hours, "Daily departures from 6am to 6pm during Prime Season", limited winter departures November through April; departs Creekside Lodge at the State Game Lodge. "Steps required, assistance available."

jewels.name: Buffalo Roundup
jewels.booking_route: none needed - public viewing areas on the Wildlife Loop (park entrance license applies)
jewels.blurb: "As the hooves of more than 1,300 American buffalo thunder through the valley" riders drive the herd into corrals for sorting; the event "attracts more than14,000 people each year." 2026 edition: roundup Friday September 25, 2026, from 9:30 a.m. MT (lots open 6:15 a.m.); Arts Festival September 24-26, 2026 at the State Game Lodge.

jewels.name: State Game Lodge
jewels.booking_route: own website booking engine (custerresorts.com) or reservations office
jewels.blurb: One of four historic lodges of Custer State Park Resort: "Welcome to the regal State Game Lodge, home to historic lodge rooms"; its rooms "have seen a full interior renovation for 2025". The dining room serves breakfast, lunch and dinner, "Open seasonally from the end of April through mid-October"; reservations 605-255-4541. The resort has "228 fully-modernized sleeping accommodations" and is "operated by South Dakota based concessionaire The Ramkota Companies since the contract was awarded in 2007."

jewels.name: Under Canvas Mount Rushmore
jewels.booking_route: own website booking (undercanvas.com) - book direct, not via Hyatt (ledger note)
jewels.blurb: "tucked among ponderosa pines and juniper on an original gold mining settlement less than four miles from Mount Rushmore National Monument"; Deluxe, Stargazer ("viewing window above the king-size bed"), Suite, Safari and family tents with wood-burning stoves; dogs welcome for a nightly fee. 2027 dates: April 29 - September 27. The NPS puts Mount Rushmore 41 miles from the Wind Cave visitor center.

jewels.name: Allen Ranch
jewels.booking_route: phone 605-745-1890 (no online booking route on the listing read)
jewels.blurb: Hot Springs: "RV sites with electricity, water and a dump station nearby, scenic tent sites next to the river. Tipi and Glamping packages with a full Cowboy Breakfast options are available"; modern shower building; glamping and tipi check-in 3:00 pm. 13065 Fall River Rd; 605-745-1890.

jewels.name: Hot Springs SD / Black Hills KOA Holiday
jewels.blurb: Off SD Hwy 79 near Hot Springs: "Pull-thru RV sites (up to 80 feet)" with full hookups and a KOA Patio, Deluxe Cabins with full baths, camping cabins and tent sites, a heated pool (Memorial Day - Labor Day) and a fenced dog park. Season April 1 - October 31, 2026; hosts Thad and Nicole Weiss.

jewels.name: Fall River Ranch RV Resort
jewels.blurb: Hot Springs: opened July 1, 2021 with 31 sites; "The finished sites have full hook-ups available (sewer, water, electric, picnic tables, fire rings)"; 30 and 50 amp, "Big Rig Friendly"; "Your Black Hills RV Base Camp!" (605) 745-3080.

jewels.name: Sunrise Ridge Campground
jewels.blurb: 27288 Wind Cave Rd., Hot Springs: "Located just north of Hot Springs, we are minutes from Wind Cave National Park and The Mammoth Site"; 70 acres; "Whether you have a 45 foot motorhome, tent or anything in between, our newly renovated sites". 605-745-4397.

jewels.name: Hidden Lake Campground and Resort
jewels.blurb: 27291 Evans Street, Hot Springs: "23 campsites, 20 cabins, a shower house with laundry facility, store and a private lake for swimming, canoeing, kayaking, fishing". 605-745-4042.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn & Suites, Custer
jewels.blurb: Listed by Visit Custer (the Custer tourism improvement district) at "433 West Mt Rushmore Rd, Custer, SD 57730". The NPS puts Custer 20 miles north of the Wind Cave visitor center on U.S. 385. IHG's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Alex Johnson Hotel, Curio Collection by Hilton
jewels.blurb: 523 Sixth St., Rapid City: "Since opening its doors on July 1, 1928, the hotel has played host to several presidents, countless celebrities, and a few spirits of its own"; Juniper at Vertex Sky Bar on the roof. 605-342-1210. At the ring's edge: the NPS gives 56 miles (about 65 minutes) as the fastest drive from the visitor center to Rapid City.

jewels.name: South Dakota Outdoor Shop
jewels.blurb: Custer: "a laid-back, community-minded gear shop" that "began in 2019 as a small bike and climbing store" and "has grown into a full-service outdoor and lifestyle shop stocked with high-quality gear, apparel, footwear, and accessories for hiking, climbing, camping, and everyday life"; visitors' reviews on its own site mention e-bike rentals for the Mickelson Trail. (605) 673-2240.

jewels.name: Black Hills Power Bikes
jewels.blurb: Custer, "located right off the Mickelson Trail": Vtuvia electric power bikes and Trek Verve 1 pedal bikes, "3 hour rentals, and all day rental options". The trail runs 109 miles from Edgemont to Deadwood on the old Burlington Northern line, with 15 trailheads.

jewels.name: The Mammoth Site
jewels.booking_route: admission at the site (ticketing not read)
jewels.blurb: Hot Springs: "The Mammoth Site boasts the largest concentration of Columbian mammoths in the world. Tour this ancient sinkhole and stand on the edge of discovery" - an indoor active dig with Ice Age exhibits, "universally accessible walkways", and one of four accredited museums in South Dakota. (605) 745-6017.

jewels.name: Evans Plunge Mineral Springs
jewels.booking_route: admission and punch cards at the door
jewels.blurb: "Established in 1890, evans plunge is the oldest tourist attraction in the Black Hills"; "Natural spring-fed waters maintain an average POOL TEMPERATURE of 87 degrees fahrenheit" with "5,000 gallons of water per minute" from a thermal spring. Owned by the City of Hot Springs; 1145 North River Street; 605-745-5165.

jewels.name: Hot Springs
jewels.blurb: The gateway town 11 miles south of the visitor center (NPS): "Called Minnekahta (warm waters) by the original white settlers in 1879, the town's name was changed to Hot Springs in 1886. Earlier, the Lakota and the Cheyenne Indian tribes fought for control of the natural warm waters." Chamber at 801 S. 6th Street, 605-745-4140.

jewels.name: Custer
jewels.blurb: The northern gateway, 20 miles from the visitor center (NPS): "Stay in Custer to savor every minute on your Black Hills vacation. Here, you're closer to South Dakota's biggest attractions - Mount Rushmore National Memorial, Custer State Park and Wind Cave National Park." Chamber at 615 Washington Street, 605-673-2244.

jewels.name: Skogen Kitchen
jewels.blurb: Custer: "a chef driven concept, offering innovative dinner options. Owners Joseph Raney (Chef) and Eliza Raney (GM) moved to South Dakota from Southern California" to "bring flavors from around the world to Custer". Dinner Tuesday - Saturday.

jewels.name: Whiskey River - Cuisine, Cocktails & Tap Room
jewels.blurb: Hot Springs: "a unique taproom experience" with "local craft beer and wine selections from South Dakota breweries and wineries" and "Audubon Certified Pastures by Evergreen Ranch meats"; breakfast, lunch and dinner. (605) 745-2739.

jewels.name: The Kitchen Ink
jewels.blurb: 741 Jennings Ave, Hot Springs: "Handcrafted dining, specialty drinks, and scratch desserts"; "Seasonally fresh, locally sourced food alchemy. Family Oriented down home dining!" Mon-Sat 7:30am - 7:30pm, Sun 9:00am - 3pm. (605) 515-1440.

jewels.name: The 309 General Bar & Restaurant
jewels.blurb: 309 N River St, Hot Springs: "rustic Wild West atmosphere" with "handmade burgers and unique specialties like chislics and onion rings", gluten-free options and live music; summer hours Wed - Sat 12:00pm - 12:00am. (605) 891-4787.

jewels.name: Two Cows Creamery & Bistro
jewels.blurb: Hot Springs: "Every ice cream flavor we sell is hand-crafted and made in-house with milk and cream from our very own dairy cows"; "28 flavors", handmade waffle cones and a build-your-own burger with hand-cut fries. (605) 745-3838.

jewels.name: Southern Hills Diner & Bakery
jewels.blurb: 12572 Sheps Canyon Road, "6 miles south of Hot Springs on the way to Cascade Falls. Farm to table experience"; a full-service diner and bakery with a pastry chef; Thurs - Mon 8:00am - 2:00pm. 605-745-7203.

jewels.name: Ruby House Restaurant
jewels.blurb: 124 Winter St, Keystone: "Step back in time & relax in our 1900's style dining room" - prime rib, steaks, seafood, buffalo steaks and ribs, full bar; open April - October. 605-666-4404.

jewels.name: State Game Lodge dining room
jewels.blurb: Custer State Park: "casual yet elegant breakfast and lunch dining with a more formal ambiance for dinner", open from the end of April through mid-October; reservations 605-255-4541. The resort runs four restaurants plus the Chuckwagon Cookout; Coolidge General Store is "a leisurely 1/2 mile walk" from the lodge.

faq.q: Is Wind Cave National Park free?
faq.a: Yes for the surface: "An entrance pass is not required to access Wind Cave National Park." "There are no fees to drive through or hike in the park. Fees are only charged for cave tours" - from $6 (Accessibility Tour) to $45 (Wild Cave Tour) for adults.

faq.q: Do you need reservations for Wind Cave National Park?
faq.a: Not to enter, but for cave tours they are "highly recommended as tours often sell out March through October and on holiday weekends throughout winter." Garden of Eden, Natural Entrance and Fairgrounds tickets are on Recreation.gov "from 120 days until two days in advance"; the Candlelight and Wild Cave tours are reserved by phone. "Roughly half of all tour tickets are held in reserve for same-day sales."

faq.q: Can you camp at Wind Cave National Park?
faq.a: Yes. "The Elk Mountain Campground is open year-round and is the only campground in the park. Sites can be reserved at www.recreation.gov late May through September, and are first-come, first-served through www.recreation.gov at all other times." The fee is $24 a night, $12 when the water is turned off. Backcountry camping needs a free permit from the visitor center.

faq.q: Where can you see bison in Wind Cave National Park?
faq.a: "There are 400-450 bison in Wind Cave National Park. They are grazers and usually found on the grasslands. There are several good places to see bison along U.S. 385, S.D. 87, and primitive roads N.P.S. 5 & 6." The NPS adds: "Bison are large, fast, nimble, and very dangerous... Please observe them from a safe distance."

faq.q: How far is Wind Cave National Park from Mount Rushmore?
faq.a: "The most direct route to Mount Rushmore National Memorial via U.S. Highway 385 and S.D. Highway 244... is 41 miles (66 km) and driving time is approximately one hour." The scenic route through Custer State Park and the Iron Mountain Road is "almost 50 miles (80 km) and takes 1.5 to 2 hours".

faq.q: How far is Wind Cave National Park from Rapid City?
faq.a: The fastest route, via the gravel 7-11 Road and S.D. 79, is "56 miles (90 km) and takes about 65 minutes to drive." Avoiding the gravel road through Hot Springs is 68 miles, about 1 hour 15 minutes; the Black Hills route through Custer and Hill City is 59 miles, about 90 minutes.

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Wind Cave National Park?
faq.a: Yes, within limits: on a leash no longer than six feet, in "Grassy areas near the visitor center", "The Elk Mountain Campground" and "Both the Prairie Vista Trail and Elk Mountain Campground Trail." Pets are not allowed on cave tours, ranger programs, in public buildings, "The backcountry or any trails except those listed above."

faq.q: Is Wind Cave National Park wheelchair accessible?
faq.a: Partly. "Limited areas of the cave are accessible to wheelchairs and those with limited mobility" on the half-hour Accessibility Tour, which uses the elevator. "The visitor center is accessible to wheelchairs", campsites B2 and D3 are accessible, and the natural entrance is reachable "via a ramp and sidewalk from the visitor center".

faq.q: What is the closest airport to Wind Cave National Park?
faq.a: "Nearest commercial airport is in Rapid City, SD." The NPS adds that "No public transportation serves the park."

faq.q: Is Wind Cave National Park open year round?
faq.a: Yes: "The park's surface is open all day, every day for you to explore. However, snow and severe weather can limit access to some remote parts of the park, especially in winter." The visitor center is open daily all year except Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day, and cave tours run through the winter.

seo.meta_title: Wind Cave National Park: Cave Tours, Bison & Camping | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: Free entry, six ranger-led cave tours through rare boxwork, 400-450 bison on the prairie, Elk Mountain Campground, and stays around Hot Springs and Custer.

hero.query: Wind Cave National Park bison prairie

name: Hot Springs National Park
line: A national park you walk into from a city street, where the thermal water still runs into two working bathhouses and free jug fountains

jewels.name: Fordyce Bathhouse Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: the park visitor center at 369 Central Avenue: free self-guided tours over four floors - marble bath halls, a music room, a gymnasium with wooden equipment, the historic Fordyce Spring in the basement; in its working years (1915-1962) "the only bathhouse to have a bowling alley"

jewels.name: Bathhouse Row and the Grand Promenade
jewels.blurb: the row of historic bathhouses on Central Avenue, ringed by a paved four-to-five-foot walkway loop with benches; the Grand Promenade above it is fully paved with multiple access points

jewels.name: Buckstaff Bathhouse
jewels.booking_route: walk-in - the site states no reservations are required for baths or massages; phone 501-623-2308
jewels.blurb: open since 1912 at 509 Central Avenue and "the only facility on the Row that has never fully closed"; the traditional sequence of whirlpool mineral bath, steam cabinet, sitz bath, hot towel packs and Swedish massage

jewels.name: Quapaw Baths & Spa
jewels.booking_route: online through its own website or by phone (booking engine not named on the page as fetched)
jewels.blurb: 413 Central Avenue: public thermal pools ("four large thermal pools ranging in temperature from 95-104 degrees" per the city's listing), private baths, a steam cave, massages and the Quapaw Cafe; packages from $150; no services for children under 14; open Wednesday-Monday 10am-6pm

jewels.name: Superior Bathhouse Brewery
jewels.blurb: a bathhouse turned brewery at 329 Central Avenue, billed as "the only brewery located in a National Park" and brewing with thermal spring water; closed Tuesdays

jewels.name: Hotel Hale
jewels.booking_route: online reservation system on its own site (engine not named as fetched); phone 501-760-9010
jewels.blurb: nine suites in the 1892 Hale Bathhouse at 341 Central Avenue, each with "a large soaking tub that has hot spring mineral water pumped directly into every room", and the Eden restaurant

jewels.name: Hot Springs Mountain Tower (park concession)
jewels.booking_route: on-site ticket sales stated (final tickets 30 minutes before closing); no online engine observed
jewels.blurb: 216 feet tall at 1,256 feet elevation, overlooking "140 square miles of surrounding countryside"; open 9am-6pm daily, adults $13, seniors 55+ $12, National Park Pass holders $11, children 5-11 $6.50

jewels.name: Hot Springs Mountain Drive, the Pagoda and Goat Rock Overlook
jewels.blurb: an 1880s carriage road from Fountain Street to the 1911 Pagoda lookout and the tower, continuing to North Mountain's Goat Rock Overlook facing the Zigzag Mountains - the "recharge zone for the thermal springs"

jewels.name: West Mountain Drive and trails
jewels.blurb: a two-way road to a summit loop with three overlooks, the 1924 picnic shelter and views to Lake Hamilton; the NPS: "The West Mountain trails are less traveled, providing greater opportunities for wildlife sightings"

jewels.name: Sunset Trail
jewels.blurb: the park's longest trail, about 10 miles one way or a 15-17 mile loop, in three sections - West Mountain (2.8 mi), Sugarloaf Mountain (2.6 mi, with Balanced Rock Overlook) and Stonebridge Road (3.8 mi)

jewels.name: Hot Water Cascade, Display Spring and the jug fountains
jewels.blurb: the springs emerge at 143°F; the Cascade on Arlington Lawn is the largest visible spring, the Display Spring sits behind the Maurice Bathhouse, and "Drinking the hot springs water is perfectly normal, even encouraged" at free jug fountains

jewels.name: Ranger programs and Junior Ranger
jewels.blurb: outdoor walks, Fordyce tours and pop-up programs year-round on a seasonal timetable, Junior Ranger programs on summer Saturdays at 2 pm; no reservations

jewels.name: In the Trees Luxury Treehouses & Cabins
jewels.booking_route: Mews (app.mews.com distributor link on its site)
jewels.blurb: treehouses and cabins with private jacuzzis on a 550-acre property in the Ouachitas at 121 Blowout Mountain Rd; add-on massages, private chef and e-bike rentals near the Northwoods and Cedar Glades trails

jewels.name: Starlight Haven Hot Springs
jewels.blurb: 27 acres with geodesic domes, handcrafted treehouses with fireplaces, and luxury safari tents (ADA accessible), every unit with a private hot tub

jewels.name: Fern Dell: Secluded Woodland Glamp
jewels.blurb: a "secluded and private glam-camp for two on 16 wooded acres" - bell tents with queen beds and an outdoor kitchen

jewels.name: DeGray Lake Resort State Park Rent-A-Yurts
jewels.booking_route: Arkansas State Parks reservation system (reserve.arkansasstateparks.com) or phone
jewels.blurb: three Rent-A-Yurts beside a 90-room lodge, 18-hole championship golf course and full-service marina at Bismarck; free entry to the state park

jewels.name: Lake Catherine State Park Rent-A-Yurt and cabins
jewels.blurb: one Rent-A-Yurt and 20 cabins (one with a private fishing pier) on 1,900-acre Lake Catherine, with the Falls Branch waterfall trail and seasonal horseback rides ($60-$62 per rider)

jewels.name: Ouachita River Haven, Pencil Bluff
jewels.blurb: riverside camp with tipi rentals and a bunkhouse plus tent and RV sites, "1000 ft of river access, with canoe & kayak docks, swimming hole"; a Hipcamp 2024 Best in Arkansas finalist

jewels.name: Ouachita Campground at Edendell, Oden
jewels.blurb: 28 acres off Highway 88 between Mena and Hot Springs with one furnished canvas glamping deck, RV and tent sites, half a mile from the Ouachita River

jewels.name: Gulpha Gorge Campground (NPS)
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov - all 40 sites require prior reservation, up to 6 months ahead
jewels.blurb: the park's own campground: 40 tent-and-RV sites, all with full hookups (30/50 amp, water, sewer), not pull-through; $34/night; 14 consecutive days and 30 days a year maximum

jewels.name: Lake Ouachita State Park
jewels.blurb: on Arkansas' largest lake (40,000 acres): 93 campsites, 8 cabins, 4 camper cabins, a seasonal marina renting barges, canoes and kayaks, and the Three Sisters' Springs historic site; free entry

jewels.name: DeGray Lake Resort State Park campground
jewels.booking_route: Arkansas State Parks reservation system or phone
jewels.blurb: 113 campsites from basic tent spots to Class AAA full hookups, two swim beaches, five hiking trails and disc golf

jewels.name: Lake Catherine State Park campground
jewels.blurb: 70 campsites (47 Class AAA full hookup, 23 Class B) and 6 primitive tent sites, a free swimming beach (no lifeguard) and year-round interpretive programs

jewels.name: Hot Springs National Park KOA Holiday
jewels.blurb: RV sites up to 70 feet, tent sites, camping cabins and deluxe cabins at 838 McClendon Road; the city listing notes a complimentary shuttle to Oaklawn during live racing and to Magic Springs

jewels.name: Lake Hamilton Escape RV & Cabin Campground
jewels.blurb: lakefront RV sites with private layout decks, big-rig hilltop sites and furnished waterfront cabins from $125/night at 200 River Oaks Drive

jewels.name: Finish Line RV Park
jewels.blurb: renovated, gated RV park at 263 Golf Links Rd with paved sites, full hookups and a dog park, from $40/night, near Oaklawn and the Creek Greenway Trail to Bathhouse Row

jewels.name: FHU Resort in Hot Springs Nat Park
jewels.blurb: eight full-hookup RV sites listed on Hipcamp beside the Oaklawn district

jewels.name: Charlton Recreation Area (Ouachita National Forest)
jewels.booking_route: not observed (the Forest Service page returned 403)
jewels.blurb: a 1935 Civilian Conservation Corps stone dam forming a swimming area on Walnut Creek, 48 camping units with full or partial hookups, and the Lake Ouachita Vista Trail

jewels.name: Fancy Hill Cabins and RV Park, Caddo Gap
jewels.blurb: 12 acres on the South Fork of the Caddo River in the Ouachita National Forest: five RV and tent sites and two handmade cabins, one couples-only with a creekside hot tub

jewels.name: The Arlington Resort Hotel & Spa
jewels.blurb: the 1920s twin-towered hotel at 239 Central Avenue with Mineral Water Rooms piped with hot springs water, a historic thermal bathhouse, and rooms from $129

jewels.name: Garvan Woodland Gardens
jewels.blurb: the University of Arkansas botanical garden on 4½ miles of wooded shoreline at 550 Arkridge Road; adults $22, children 4-12 $10, cart tours $20; seasonal Holiday Lights (2026 dates not confirmed)

jewels.name: Oaklawn Racing Casino Resort
jewels.blurb: thoroughbred racing since 1904 at 2705 Central Avenue, with a 24/7 smoke-free casino, trackside suites and the Astral Spa; racing-season dates not confirmed this build

jewels.name: Magic Springs Theme and Water Park
jewels.booking_route: own online ticket store and group tickets (10+); engine not named as fetched
jewels.blurb: theme park and water park just outside downtown; Magic Screams runs "9/26-11/1" with trick-or-treating by day and scare zones by night

jewels.name: National Park Duck Tours
jewels.blurb: a 75-minute land-and-water tour in a WWII-era DUKW from 418 Central Avenue past Bathhouse Row and onto Lake Hamilton; daily 9:30am-6pm, private charters for groups

jewels.name: Fun Day Boat Rentals, Lake Hamilton
jewels.blurb: family-owned pontoon rentals "delivered right to your vacation property" on Lake Hamilton

jewels.name: Mountain Harbor Resort & Spa, Lake Ouachita
jewels.blurb: family-owned for over 70 years at Mt Ida: lodging, full-service marina, the Turtle Cove Spa, scuba diving, fishing and hiking

jewels.name: Northwoods Trails
jewels.blurb: 31.5+ miles of green, blue and black singletrack, flow trails and the Lucky 13 expert section, with a skills park at Cedar Glades; the Pullman trailhead links to downtown through the park

jewels.name: Greenway Outfitters
jewels.booking_route: Booqable on its own site, or phone 501-463-2453
jewels.blurb: Pedego e-bike and Giant/Liv rentals, repairs and craft coffee at 300 Valley Street beside the Hot Springs Greenway; delivery $45 in town, $60 surrounding

jewels.name: Parkside Cycle
jewels.blurb: a 30-year Hot Springs bike shop at 719 Whittington Ave with rentals for individuals and groups

jewels.name: Ron Coleman Mining, Jessieville
jewels.blurb: public quartz crystal digging, night digs, a zip line over the mine, military-vehicle mine tours, horseback rides and the Crystal Ridge Campground

jewels.name: Mid-America Science Museum
jewels.booking_route: own online shop (shop.midamericamuseum.org); engine not named
jewels.blurb: hands-on science museum at 500 Mid America Blvd; adults $15, children and seniors $13; closed Mondays

jewels.name: Gangster Museum of America
jewels.blurb: seven galleries and an antique casino on the 1920s-1940s gangster era of Hot Springs, at 510 Central Avenue

jewels.name: Hot Springs Documentary Film Festival, October 9-17, 2026
jewels.blurb: the 35th edition of "the longest running, all-documentary film festival in North America", opening with a gala at Oaklawn

jewels.name: Central Avenue galleries and studios
jewels.blurb: Visit Hot Springs lists Justus Fine Art Gallery (827 A Central), Artists Workshop Gallery (610A Central), American Art Gallery (724 Central), Emergent Arts and Dryden Pottery (Whittington Ave) and Fox Pass Pottery

jewels.name: Crater of Diamonds State Park, Murfreesboro
jewels.blurb: "One of the only places in the world where the public can search for real diamonds in their original volcanic source"

jewels.name: McClard's Bar-B-Q
jewels.blurb: founded 1928 by Alex and Alice McClard at a tourist court, where a guest paid for lodging with a recipe for "the world's greatest hot sauce"; still family-run, now in its fourth generation

jewels.name: The Ohio Club
jewels.blurb: "Arkansas' Oldest Operating Bar", serving since 1905 at 336 Central Ave, a Prohibition haunt of Al Capone, Bugsy Siegel and Babe Ruth, with live music Thursday to Sunday; closed Wednesdays

jewels.name: Crystal Ridge Distillery
jewels.blurb: "Seven generations of Bradley family craft" at 455 Broadway St, distilling moonshine and Arkansas vodka; tastings and tours by appointment

jewels.name: Mountain Valley Spring Water Visitor Center
jewels.booking_route: not observed (hours not posted; call ahead)
jewels.blurb: the Ouachita spring water bottled in glass since 1871 keeps a public visitor center at 150 Central Ave, on Bathhouse Row's doorstep

faq.q: Does Hot Springs National Park charge an entrance fee?
faq.a: No. The NPS states "No entrance pass required." Camping at Gulpha Gorge carries a fee ($34 per night).

faq.q: Can I soak in the hot springs?
faq.a: Not outdoors. The NPS says there are no outdoor soaking opportunities; Buckstaff Bathhouse (509 Central Avenue) and Quapaw Bathhouse (413 Central Avenue) offer full immersion in the thermal water.

faq.q: Can I drink the thermal spring water?
faq.a: Yes. The NPS states "Drinking the hot springs water is perfectly normal, even encouraged," and provides it free at jug fountains around the park. The springs emerge at 143°F.

faq.q: How do I book Gulpha Gorge Campground?
faq.a: On Recreation.gov. All 40 sites require prior reservation; each has full hookups and costs $34 per night. Accessible sites open one week in advance.

faq.q: Do I need a reservation at Buckstaff Bathhouse?
faq.a: No. Buckstaff states that no reservations are required; baths and massages are walk-in.

faq.q: Can children use Quapaw Baths & Spa?
faq.a: Not under 14. Quapaw states "WE DO NOT OFFER ANY SERVICES FOR CHILDREN UNDER THE AGE OF 14."

name: Gateway Arch National Park
line: A five-person pod up the inside of a 1965 steel arch, a free museum underneath it, and a whole city of free museums, blues rooms and toasted ravioli around it

jewels.name: Tram Ride to the Top
jewels.booking_route: operator's own ticketing at tickets.gatewayarch.com (Bi-State Development), plus phone (877) 982-1410 and the Visitor Center desk

jewels.name: Museum at the Gateway Arch

faq.q: Do I need a ticket to visit Gateway Arch National Park?
faq.a: Not for the museum, gift store or cafe, which the NPS says are always free. You need a ticket for the Tram Ride to the Top, the documentary film, the VR theater and the riverboats.

faq.q: How much does the tram to the top of the Gateway Arch cost?
faq.a: The NPS lists adults (16+) starting at $15 and children (3-15) starting at $11, with infants free and prices varying by date. $3 of the adult ticket is the NPS entrance fee. Tickets are sold at gatewayarch.com, by phone at (877) 982-1410 and at the park entrance.

faq.q: Can I ride the Arch tram in a wheelchair?
faq.a: No. The operator states no wheelchairs, walkers, scooters or strollers are permitted in the trams or on the Observation Deck, and visitors must walk at least 96 steps. The museum has free wheelchairs and a replica arch section with livestream video.

faq.q: How long does the Tram Ride to the Top take?
faq.a: About 45-60 minutes in all, including pre-boarding exhibits, the ride up and down, and a maximum of 10 minutes at the top.

faq.q: When do the Gateway Arch riverboats run?
faq.a: Daily sightseeing cruises run March to November from the cobblestone levee; in December the boats run holiday-themed cruises.

faq.q: Is the Old Courthouse open?
faq.a: Yes. It reopened in May 2025 after renovation and is open daily 9am to 5pm, free, closed on Christmas, Thanksgiving and New Year's Day, with ranger tours daily at 2:15 pm.
