name: Garner State Park
line: Frio River swimming and summer jukebox dances

jewels.name: Frio River swimming and tubing
jewels.booking_route: park entry only - day pass $8 ages 13+, reserve on ReserveAmerica or (512) 389-8900
jewels.blurb: "With 2.9 miles of Frio River winding through 1,774 acres of scenic Hill Country terrain"; "Swim in the Frio River or float its waters on an inner tube, operate a paddle boat". TPWD's current alert: "Swimming is permitted on the river at your own risk. No lifeguards are on duty."

jewels.name: The summer jukebox dance
jewels.booking_route: no booking - park entry; schedule on garnerstatepark.com/the-dance
jewels.blurb: "Since the 1940s, young folks (and the young at heart) have been gathering at the park's concession building on summer evenings for a jukebox dance. They still do so today." The concession lists Summer Dances "May 24-Aug 10", "8:30-11pm", on the "Pavilion Dance Floor". TPWD: "Arrive early, as parking lots get full and gates can close as early as 8:30 p.m."

jewels.name: Old Baldy Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park trail, within entry
jewels.blurb: "Old Baldy Trail", 0.5 mi., rated "Challenging"; the Bridges Trail delivers "a great view of Old Baldy at Painted Rock Overlook and the shade of the giant Ashe juniper tree" - "Use caution on the loose rocks and steep terrain."

jewels.name: Garner historic cabins
jewels.blurb: 17 kitchen cabins in the Old Garner area - 13 "Cabins with Fireplace" at $150 nightly and 4 without at $130 (one ADA), each with "Kitchen sink, Microwave, Refrigerator, Stove without oven", a bathroom with shower and two double beds; "No linens, blankets or towels provided"; "A 2-night minimum reservation is required on all cabins"; "No pets". The CCC built "a lodge and cabins" here between 1935 and 1941.

jewels.name: Garner State Park campsites
jewels.blurb: Some 347 sites across Old and New Garner: 12 pull-through full-hookup sites in Shady Meadows ($35; "No tents are allowed, and there is no shade or tree cover"), 137 water-and-50-amp sites in Rio Frio and Live Oak ($26), 39 electric sites in Oakmont ($26), 35 30-amp sites ($22), and 124 water-only sites ($15-$20; RVs "20 feet or less"), all plus entry. "Live Oak Camping Area is closed January and February."

jewels.name: Garner screened shelters
jewels.blurb: 21 shelters in Pecan Grove (Old Garner, $35) and 16 in River Crossing (New Garner, $30), plus entry: "Electricity", "Light and outlet inside", "Picnic table inside", fire ring with grill and water spigot outside; up to 8 people; "No RVs are allowed at the shelters"; "No pets".

jewels.name: CCC combination building and dance pavilion
jewels.blurb: "CCC Company 879 developed Garner between 1935 and 1941"; "The CCC utilized native limestone and hewn bald cypress to construct this building and dance pavilion. The building overlooks the river, and is the centerpiece of the park." The park "opened June 1, 1941, and was named for John Nance 'Cactus Jack' Garner".

jewels.name: Crystal Cave Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park trail, within entry
jewels.blurb: "Crystal Cave Trail" (0.6 mi.), "Challenging in several places, the trail provides access to one of the park's natural wonders": "Don't forget a flashlight as you enter this 30-foot deep cave. Enjoy the slightly cooler temperatures, and help us protect the cave's namesake."

jewels.name: Frio Canyon Trail and the park trail network
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park trails, within entry
jewels.blurb: "Explore 16 miles of trails, some leading to bird's-eye views": the Frio Canyon Trail (2.9 mi.) - "Experience the vastness of the Frio Canyon while hiking or biking this relatively flat trail" - the Ashe Juniper Trail (2.5 mi.), Foshee (1.7 mi.) and the Old Entrance Road (0.8 mi.), "built in the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps as part of the original park entrance."

jewels.name: Garner Boat House rentals
jewels.booking_route: walk-up, cash only, at the Boat House
jewels.blurb: The park concession rents a "1 Person Kayak" ($15 per hour), "2 Person Kayak" ($20), "Paddle Boat" ($20), "Stand Up Paddle Board (SUP)" ($20) and "iFloat" ($10); "Must be 18 years old to rent, bring a valid ID", "Cash Only", "No Refunds"; open "7 Days a Week" in summer, closed December-January. TPWD adds that the park loans "fishing gear for use in the park."

jewels.name: Fishing the Frio without a license
jewels.booking_route: none needed - within park entry; loaner gear from the park
jewels.blurb: "Try your luck fishing the Frio - no license needed to fish from shore!" and "We also loan fishing gear for use in the park." The Park Store stocks "fishing supplies".

jewels.name: The Garner Grill
jewels.blurb: The concession grill: "Everything is made fresh when you order it-no warmers or stale food here"; burgers of "1/3lb meat on a sourdough bun from a Houston bakery", including an Axis deer burger; summer "11am-4pm", "Open Daily" from Memorial Weekend; cash only.

jewels.name: Garner ice cream and gelato shop
jewels.blurb: "Hand dipped Gelato in a variety of delicious flavors. Gelato shakes and sundaes also available", plus "Fresh Fudge Made fresh in house", "Candied Pecans made fresh throughout the day" and popcorn; "Summer Hours-Open Daily 11am-11pm".

jewels.name: Garner Park Store
jewels.blurb: "Groceries, grillin' meats, snacks, coffee, cleaning supplies, RV, toiletries, swim gear, fishing supplies, drinks" plus Lodge Cookware and Case Knives; summer "8am-10pm DAILY", "usually open daily through December, weather and visitation permitting."

jewels.name: Stinkin' Sweet Candy Golf
jewels.blurb: The park's mini golf, "Newly renovated for 2023! Rental fee includes one round of 18 holes": first round $7 per person (4 and up), second round $4, ages 3 and under $2; a candy shop of "old school, crazy, gross and funny treats" alongside.

jewels.name: Trail water, a quart an hour
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI via AvantLink, or Amazon Associates)
jewels.blurb: TPWD's own kit advice for Garner's trails: "Drink plenty of water. Your body quickly loses fluids when you're on the trail. Bring a quart (32 oz.) of water per hour of activity." July's average high is 97 degrees.

jewels.name: Sun, insect and footwear kit
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI via AvantLink, or Amazon Associates)
jewels.blurb: TPWD on Garner's trails: "Know your limits. Prepare for sun and heat. Wear sunscreen, insect repellent and appropriate clothing/hiking shoes." Most trails are "rugged, rocky and cover a wide variety of terrain and elevations."

jewels.name: Flashlight for Crystal Cave
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI via AvantLink, or Amazon Associates)
jewels.blurb: TPWD: "Don't forget a flashlight as you enter this 30-foot deep cave."

jewels.name: Lost Maples State Natural Area
jewels.booking_route: day pass via ReserveAmerica (Texas State Parks) or (512) 389-8900
jewels.blurb: Vanderpool: "Lost Maples protects a special stand of Uvalde bigtooth maples"; "The show varies, depending on weather conditions. Check our Fall Foliage report (starting mid-October)." "October and November are our busiest times. We reach capacity daily." Named by TPWD on the Garner page among "Other TPWD parks nearby".

jewels.name: Briscoe-Garner Museum
jewels.blurb: Uvalde: "dedicated to sharing the remarkable lives and legacies of two of the most influential 20th century political leaders from the Lone Star State: Vice President 'Cactus' Jack Garner and Governor Dolph Briscoe" - the namesake of the park. Run by the Briscoe Center (UT Austin); hours and street address not on the page read.

jewels.name: Neal's Lodges
jewels.booking_route: own website BOOK NOW, reserve@nealslodges.com or (830) 232-6118
jewels.blurb: Concan: "founded in 1926 and is a family-owned and operated vacation hideaway on the beautiful spring-fed Frio River" - "81 cabins, 10 lodges, 17 condos, 45 RV hook-ups, and 16 tent sites", "River access exclusively for Neal's guests", a country store and Neal's Dining Room; "CLOSED THE MONTH OF JANUARY". 20970 Hwy 127, (830) 232-6118.

jewels.name: Happy Hollow Frio River Outfitters
jewels.booking_route: phone (830) 232-5266 / text (830) 279-5990; lodging via own online reservation link
jewels.blurb: 32580 US-83, Concan: rents tubes and kayaks with a river shuttle - Fri-Sun 10 AM-5 PM ("shuttle until 3 PM"), Thursday 11 AM-2 PM, Mon-Wed "By Appointment" - and lets River Houses and Riverfront Bungalows. (830) 232-5266.

jewels.name: Camp Riverview
jewels.booking_route: Campspot reservation system from the own site
jewels.blurb: 1636 County Road 350, Concan: "Full Hook Up, 30/50 amp" RV sites, tent sites and "Efficiency, one and two bedroom cabins that sleep up to six comfortably", with Frio River floating, a playground, laser tag and a camp store; reservations run on Campspot. (830) 232-5412.

jewels.name: Pitmaster RV Park
jewels.blurb: Listed on Campspot in Concan ("4 miles" on its near-Concan page): "featuring 50 spacious full-hookup sites, tent camping, and unique lodging options such as a covered wagon and a Native American teepee."

jewels.name: Stars Over Texas RV Park-Frio
jewels.blurb: Listed on Campspot in Concan ("6 miles" on its near-Concan page): "Nestled in the scenic Frio River Canyon...51 RV Sites- that are surrounded by the Biggest Shadiest Oak Trees & all sites are less than 100 yards from the SOT Country Club." Cabins and RV sites.

jewels.name: Riverbend on the Frio
jewels.booking_route: RMS Cloud booking engine (bookings.rmscloud.com) from the own site
jewels.blurb: 32710 N US Hwy 83, Concan: "Standalone Cabins," "Small Motels," "Deluxe Motels," "RV Slots," and "RV Rentals"; "Extended monthly stays" are offered "October 15 through March 1" for Winter Texans. (830) 232-6616.

jewels.name: Seven Bluff Cabins & RV Park
jewels.blurb: 4251 County Road 348, Concan, on the Frio River at Seven Bluff Crossing: "20 cabins and 17 RV sites to choose from"; listed by the Frio Canyon Chamber under tube and kayak rentals. +1 (830) 232-5260.

jewels.name: Frio Pecan Farm
jewels.blurb: 144 Ranch Rd 337 East, Leakey: "17 log cabins" that "Sleep up to 6" and "17 Vacation Homes" that "Sleep 8 to 24", with the Frio River running through the property; "Reservations cannot be made online. Please Call the Office at 830-232-5294 to book".

jewels.name: Frio Rentals
jewels.blurb: Cabins, lodges and bungalows "deep in the heart of the Frio Canyon" near Leakey - one property "A 5 minute drive from Garner State Park" - with hot tubs, pools and river access; "Four separate bungalows containing seven private rooms". (830) 232-4781.

jewels.name: Speakeasy Resorts - The Highball and The Moonshine
jewels.blurb: "FRIO RIVER • CONCAN, TX" "Luxury Home Rentals" "close to Garner state park": The Highball "Sleeps up to 25" (5 bedrooms, 3,800 sq ft, "Heated Pool & Spa", arcade games); The Moonshine "Sleeps up to 24" (4,300 sq ft on over 2 acres). 210-313-4972.

jewels.name: Seco Ridge Campgrounds
jewels.blurb: Utopia, on Hipcamp: "Private, family-friendly campgrounds in the Texas Hill Country. Great views, and just minutes from Garner State Park and Lost Maples State Natural Area" - primitive tent sites and a Bunkhaus.

jewels.name: Hampton Inn Uvalde
jewels.blurb: Listed by Visit Uvalde (the city's visitor bureau) at "2714 E Main St, Uvalde, TX 78801 • (830) 278-1300". Uvalde is the gateway town TPWD points visitors to ("Visit the Uvalde Visitors Center"). Hilton's own page was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Uvalde
jewels.blurb: Listed by Visit Uvalde at "2801 E Main St, Uvalde, TX 78801 • (877) 666-3243". IHG's own page was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: House Pasture Cattle Company
jewels.blurb: "Restaurant, Full Bar, Live Music", "Located in the heart of Concan, Texas" at "3064 CR 348 ( River Road )"; seasonal - the page notes it is "closed for the off-season" and reopens Memorial Day weekend. (830) 232-6580.

jewels.name: Neal's Dining Room
jewels.blurb: 20720 TX-127, Concan: the dining room of Neal's Lodges (founded 1926), "within walking distance from most cabins" per the Lodges' site; menu, specialties and desserts on its own site.

jewels.name: Bent Rim Grill
jewels.booking_route: walk-in; groups and catering by phone
jewels.blurb: 657 West Ranch Road 337, "½ mile west of Highway 83, Leakey": "Ride to Eat, Eat to Ride" - 100% Angus burgers grilled to order, weekend breakfasts, a bar, and live music Saturdays 7-11pm. 830-232-6649.

jewels.name: Gypsy Sally's
jewels.blurb: "Burg · Margs · TXMX" at "373 Market Street Leakey, Texas 78873", with catering. 830-260-1001.

jewels.name: Hippie Chick's River Shack
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Frio Canyon Chamber of Commerce under Restaurants & Cafes in Concan (facebook.com/hippiechicsconcan). No own website; nothing else stated.

jewels.name: Magers Family Farm & Bakery
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Frio Canyon Chamber of Commerce under Bakeries. The Magers name is the park's own origin story: TPWD records that "The Magers family, German immigrants who settled in this area, opened part of their land for camping in the 1920s."

jewels.name: Leakey
jewels.blurb: The Real County seat on the Frio, home of the Frio Canyon Chamber of Commerce ("Daily 8am-5pm", (830) 834-5020, P.O. Box 743 Leakey), whose directory lists 15 restaurants and cafes, 17 RV parks and campgrounds and 30 cabin and resort properties across the canyon. TPWD sends Garner visitors to the Chamber "for more information."

faq.q: How much does it cost to get into Garner State Park?
faq.a: TPWD lists "Ages 13+: $8 daily"; children 12 and under are free. A "Texas State Parks Pass" at "$70 Per Year" gives "unlimited visits to more than 80 state parks without paying entrance fees."

faq.q: Do you need reservations for Garner State Park?
faq.a: Strongly advised: "We often reach capacity and highly recommend reservations for both camping and day use. To guarantee entry, reserve passes online or by calling the customer service center before you visit" - (512) 389-8900.

faq.q: Do you need a fishing license at Garner State Park?
faq.a: Not from the bank: "Try your luck fishing the Frio - no license needed to fish from shore!" TPWD adds, "We also loan fishing gear for use in the park."

faq.q: Can you kayak at Garner State Park?
faq.a: Yes. The park concession's Boat House rents a "1 Person Kayak" at "$15 per hour" and a "2 Person Kayak" at "$20 per hour", plus paddle boats, SUPs and floats; "Must be 18 years old to rent, bring a valid ID" and it is "Cash Only". It opens "7 Days a Week" in summer and is closed in December and January.

faq.q: What time is the Garner State Park dance?
faq.a: The concession lists the dance at "8:30-11pm", "7 days a week starting Memorial Weekend", with "Summer Dances May 24-Aug 10" and "Spring Break Dances MARCH 8-15". TPWD advises: "Arrive early, as parking lots get full and gates can close as early as 8:30 p.m."

faq.q: Can you take alcohol to Garner State Park?
faq.a: Not in public view. The Texas State Parks rules: "Public display or consumption of alcohol is prohibited. All outdoor areas within the park are public."

faq.q: Are dogs allowed at Garner State Park?
faq.a: On a leash: "keeping pets on leashes, no longer than 6 feet, at all times. Please note: Pets are not permitted in any buildings at Texas State Parks." Garner's cabins and screened shelters are both listed as "No pets".

faq.q: What should I take to Garner State Park?
faq.a: TPWD's trail advice: "Prepare for sun and heat. Wear sunscreen, insect repellent and appropriate clothing/hiking shoes"; "Bring a quart (32 oz.) of water per hour of activity"; and for Crystal Cave, "Don't forget a flashlight". Cabins come with "No utensils or dishes" and "No linens, blankets or towels provided".

faq.q: When was Garner State Park established?
faq.a: "The park opened June 1, 1941, and was named for John Nance 'Cactus Jack' Garner", a Uvalde native and US vice president from 1933 to 1941. "CCC Company 879 developed Garner between 1935 and 1941."

faq.q: What are the cabins like at Garner State Park?
faq.a: 17 cabins in Old Garner - 13 with fireplace at $150 a night and 4 without at $130, plus entry - each with "Kitchen sink, Microwave, Refrigerator, Stove without oven", a bathroom with shower, two double beds and central air and heat. "A 2-night minimum reservation is required on all cabins"; "No pets".

seo.meta_title: Garner State Park: Frio River, Old Baldy & the Dance | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: 2.9 miles of Frio River, 16 miles of trails, the summer jukebox dance, cabins and campsites that fill early, and where to camp and stay in Concan and Uvalde.

name: Palo Duro Canyon State Park
line: The country's second largest canyon, in the Panhandle

jewels.name: Palo Duro Canyon
jewels.booking_route: day pass via the Texas State Parks reservation system (ReserveAmerica) or at the gate
jewels.blurb: "The second largest canyon in the country lies in the heart of the Texas Panhandle"; elevation 2,759 to 3,463 feet, "over 30 miles of trails", hiking, biking, horseback riding, geocaching and bird watching. Adults $8 a day, children 12 and under free.

jewels.name: Lighthouse Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park trail, covered by the entrance fee
jewels.blurb: "2.8 mi. (one-way)", "2 hrs.", "Moderate" - the park's signature hike to the Lighthouse formation. TPWD warns that "most heat-related injuries and deaths for people and pets occur on this trail" and to "take plenty of water."

jewels.name: TEXAS Outdoor Musical
jewels.blurb: Presented "at the Pioneer Amphitheater in Palo Duro Canyon", 11450 State Park Hwy Rd 5; "Show Runs Tuesday - Sunday" in season. TPWD lists "summer performances of the TEXAS Outdoor Musical". Tickets and dinner details by phone 806.651.2181 or info@texas-show.com.

jewels.name: Palo Duro Canyon rim cabins
jewels.booking_route: Texas State Parks reservation system (ReserveAmerica) or (512) 389-8900
jewels.blurb: Three CCC-built cabins on the rim, sleeping 4 each: Lighthouse and Goodnight ("Located on the canyon rim with a beautiful view", fireplace, queen bed, full futon, shower) at $125 a night, and Sorenson with two fireplaces at $150, plus entrance fee; $50 deposit at check-in; no pets.

jewels.name: Palo Duro Glamping
jewels.booking_route: own website "BOOK NOW" (booking engine not named)
jewels.blurb: "Luxury camping" inside the park: "Each Glaming cabin is fully furnished" with "air conditioning, a fridge, a coffee maker, a gas grill and fire pit (propane included), games, linens, a covered porch, hammocks, s'mores kits". TPWD: "you cannot reserve this site through our system." 806.488.2821.

jewels.name: Old West Stables
jewels.blurb: Inside the park: "Our most popular 1-hour ride is perfect for first time riders. You'll see the beauty and ruggedness of Palo Duro Canyon State Park close up"; groups "never exceeding 5 riders"; riders 6 and up, adults under 225 lbs; "No riding experience needed!" (806) 488-2180.

jewels.name: Palo Duro Canyon electric campsites
jewels.booking_route: Texas State Parks reservation system (ReserveAmerica, parkId 1200105)
jewels.blurb: Juniper (18 sites, 30/50 amp, three ADA sites), Mesquite and Sagebrush (47 sites) and Hackberry (32 sites) - water and electric hookups, restrooms with showers, Mesquite/Sagebrush and Hackberry taking "up to 60-foot RVs"; $26 a night plus entrance fee.

jewels.name: Fortress Cliff and hike-in primitive camping
jewels.blurb: 18 tent-only drive-up sites in the Fortress Cliff area ("Picnic table, Fire ring, Water nearby, Shade shelter", no RVs) at $16, and hike-in primitive camping for 40 at $12 - "Minimum 1/2 mile hike; bring your own water", containerized fuel stoves only, no open fires.

jewels.name: Cow Camp cabins
jewels.booking_route: Texas State Parks reservation system (ReserveAmerica) or (512) 389-8900
jewels.blurb: Four basic cabins on the canyon floor: electricity, microwave, refrigerator, A/C and heat, full bed and twin bunk; "Restrooms with showers are nearby"; cabin #2 sleeps 2 with ADA features; $60 a night; "No linens provided".

jewels.name: Givens, Spicer, Lowry and CCC trails
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park trails, covered by the entrance fee
jewels.blurb: TPWD rates both "Difficult": the Givens, Spicer, Lowry trail at 3.1 mi and the CCC trail at 1.4 mi.

jewels.name: Pioneer Nature Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park trail, covered by the entrance fee
jewels.blurb: The park's short walk: "Pioneer Nature: 0.4 mi.", rated "Easy".

jewels.name: Palo Duro Canyon Visitor Center and park store
jewels.booking_route: none needed - covered by the entrance fee
jewels.blurb: The Visitor Center sits on the canyon rim; the park store sells "books, pottery, jewelry".

jewels.name: The Trading Post
jewels.blurb: On the canyon floor: "souvenirs, snacks, meals" (TPWD); Palo Duro Glamping sells burger kits at the Trading Post for "$7.99".

jewels.name: Water for every mile of trail
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI via AvantLink, or Amazon Associates)
jewels.blurb: TPWD's own kit rule: "Bring at least one quart of water per person per mile", with extra for pets; on the Lighthouse Trail "take plenty of water"; hike-in campers "bring your own water".

jewels.name: Sun and heat protection for the canyon
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI via AvantLink, or Amazon Associates)
jewels.blurb: TPWD: "Prepare for sun and heat" and "Wear sunscreen, insect repellent and appropriate clothing/hiking shoes" - the canyon floor is where "most heat-related injuries and deaths for people and pets occur" on the Lighthouse Trail.

jewels.name: Doves Rest Cabins
jewels.blurb: "The #1 And Only Private Vacation Homes Overlooking Palo Duro Canyon State Park": 20 cabins in four groups (Longhorn Ranch, North Rim, West Rim incl. SkyHouse and Lighthouse, Wildlife) with electric fireplaces, hot tubs, propane grills, full kitchens and Wi-Fi, some with EV chargers; "a few minutes from the main entrance", 16 miles from Canyon.

jewels.name: Canyon Rim RV
jewels.booking_route: Hipcamp listing (own site canyonrimrv.com redirects to an unrelated domain)
jewels.blurb: "uniquely situated on the rim of the breathtaking Palo Duro Canyon" with full hookups (Hipcamp listing). Its own domain now redirects elsewhere, so nothing more is stated here.

jewels.name: Amarillo By Morning RV Park
jewels.blurb: 900 S Lakeside Dr, Amarillo: "just off I-40 & Lakeside, nestled under mature trees for a peaceful, shaded stay"; big-rig friendly full hookups, Deluxe or Premium sites, daily $75, and a free shuttle to the Big Texan RV Ranch's heated indoor pool. (806) 373-1431.

jewels.name: Big Texan RV Ranch
jewels.blurb: 1414 Sunrise, Amarillo: full hookups at all sites, "Heated indoor pool", sauna, "3 Fenced dog parks", "Free coffee and bagels in the morning", and cabins with an "authentic old west experience with modern comforts"; daily RV rate $85. (806) 373-4962.

jewels.name: Amarillo RV Resort
jewels.blurb: "spacious RV accommodations and well-appointed cottages for vacationers and travellers" (Hipcamp listing); The Dyrt lists it as a full-service resort with RVs, cabins and glamping.

jewels.name: Amarillo KOA
jewels.blurb: Listed by The Dyrt as offering "RVs and glamping accommodations", 5 miles from Amarillo. koa.com refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else is stated here.

jewels.name: Hampton Inn & Suites Canyon
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "3101 4th Avenue, Canyon, TX 79015", "14 miles" from Palo Duro Canyon State Park. Hilton's own page was not fetched (brand sites return 403), so nothing else is stated here.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Canyon
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "2901 4th Avenue, Canyon, TX 79015" (I-27, Exit 106), "14 miles" from Palo Duro Canyon State Park. IHG's own page was not fetched, so nothing else is stated here.

jewels.name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott Amarillo
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "1740 Airport Blvd, Amarillo, TX 79118" (I-40, Exit 76), "18 miles" from Palo Duro Canyon State Park. Marriott's own pages return HTTP 403, so nothing else is stated here.

jewels.name: Four Points by Sheraton Downtown Amarillo
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "1911 I-40 East, Amarillo, TX 79102" (I-40, Exit 71), "20 miles" from Palo Duro Canyon State Park. Marriott's own pages return HTTP 403, so nothing else is stated here.

jewels.name: Home2 Suites by Hilton East Amarillo
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "7775 I-40 East, Amarillo, TX 79118" (I-40, Exit 75), "18 miles" from Palo Duro Canyon State Park. Hilton's own page was not fetched, so nothing else is stated here.

jewels.name: Panhandle-Plains Historical Museum
jewels.blurb: 2503 4th Avenue, Canyon, Texas 79015 - collections spanning art, archaeology, geology, paleontology, textiles, transportation and regional history. 806-651-2244. Hours and admission were not on the page read.

jewels.name: Cadillac Ranch
jewels.blurb: "Now located along I-40 in Amarillo, Cadillac Ranch and the Big Texan Steak Ranch and Microbrewery are two famous Route 66 attractions"; Visit Amarillo invites visitors to "spray your mark on Cadillac Ranch".

jewels.name: Amarillo Route 66 Historic District
jewels.booking_route: none needed - a public street district
jewels.blurb: "The official Route 66 Historic District in Amarillo is located on 6th Ave. between Georgia & Western Streets"; "Route 66 is turning 100, and there's no better place to celebrate than Amarillo."

jewels.name: The Big Texan Steak Ranch
jewels.blurb: "Feeding folks since 1960", family-owned: "The Big Texan's legendary 72-ounce steak challenge is not for the faint of heart" - finish it within one hour and it is free; attempts are live-streamed. Visit Amarillo calls it a Route 66 attraction now on I-40.

jewels.name: GoldenLight Cafe and Cantina
jewels.blurb: 2906 SW 6th Ave, Amarillo, in the Route 66 district: a restaurant and music venue hosting "local and touring bands"; Visit Amarillo calls it "Amarillo's oldest restaurant, offering up live music and great burgers".

jewels.name: Tyler's Barbeque
jewels.blurb: 3301 Olsen Boulevard, Amarillo: "Real Texas barbeque. Oak-smoked daily. Served until it's gone." Tuesday-Friday 11 AM-7 PM, Saturday 11 AM-6 PM, closed Sunday and Monday.

jewels.name: OHMS Cafe & Bar
jewels.blurb: 619 S. Tyler St., Amarillo: "Amarillo's Upscale American Bistro" - "Nestled in the historic downtown of Amarillo, OHMS Cafe & Bar fuses the soul of Santa Fe with the heart of the panhandle." Lunch Tue-Fri, dinner Tue-Sat.

jewels.name: Bracero's Mexican Bar & Grill
jewels.blurb: Visit Amarillo: located in what was once a Route 66 gas station in the Historic District.

jewels.name: Rain Premier Sushi Bar and Lounge
jewels.blurb: Visit Amarillo: "A popular downtown Amarillo restaurant" with a cosmopolitan feel.

jewels.name: Public House
jewels.blurb: Visit Amarillo: elevates comfort food to a new level.

jewels.name: Palo Duro Canyon group camps and Mack Dick Pavilion
jewels.booking_route: Texas State Parks Customer Service Center by phone, (512) 389-8920
jewels.blurb: TPWD's group sites inside the park: "Group Camp (Wolfberry)" - nine campsites for up to 72 people with "30/50-amp electric and water hookups", $225 nightly; a youth "Group Camp" for 32 people, $50 nightly; the Tasajillo Pavilion for 54, $300 daily; and the "Group Hall with Kitchen (Mack Dick Pavilion)" for 169, air-conditioned and wheelchair accessible, $1000 daily or "$2000 total" Friday-Sunday - all plus entrance fees. "Call (512) 389-8920 for reservations".

faq.q: How much is it to get into Palo Duro Canyon State Park?
faq.a: TPWD lists "Adult (13+ years): $8" daily and "Child (12 years and under): Free". The $70 Texas State Parks Pass gives "unlimited visits to more than 80 state parks without paying entrance fees".

faq.q: Do you need reservations for Palo Duro Canyon State Park?
faq.a: TPWD recommends you "Check day pass availability and make reservations online"; the park "often reaches capacity". "Day pass entrance permits may be reserved up to one month before your visit", and "Day passes are especially important for weekends and holidays and at our busiest parks."

faq.q: Can you camp at Palo Duro Canyon State Park?
faq.a: Yes: water-and-electric sites at $26 (Juniper, Mesquite/Sagebrush, Hackberry, up to 60-foot RVs on two loops), tent-only drive-up sites at $16, and hike-in primitive camping at $12 ("Minimum 1/2 mile hike; bring your own water"), all plus entrance fee, booked online through ReserveAmerica.

faq.q: Does Palo Duro Canyon State Park have cabins?
faq.a: Yes: three CCC-built rim cabins - Lighthouse and Goodnight at $125 a night and Sorenson at $150, each sleeping 4 - and four Cow Camp cabins on the canyon floor at $60, where "Restrooms with showers are nearby" and "No linens provided". Glamping is booked separately: "you cannot reserve this site through our system."

faq.q: Does Palo Duro Canyon State Park allow dogs?
faq.a: Yes, on a leash: "Keep pets on leashes for their safety, and to protect wildlife." Bring extra water for them - TPWD notes that on the Lighthouse Trail "most heat-related injuries and deaths for people and pets occur". Pets are not allowed in the cabins.

faq.q: What time does Palo Duro Canyon State Park close?
faq.a: TPWD gives gate hours of "7:30 a.m. - 10 p.m." and office hours of "7:30 a.m. - 5:30 p.m.", open daily.

faq.q: Where is Palo Duro Canyon State Park?
faq.a: "The second largest canyon in the country lies in the heart of the Texas Panhandle." The park address is 11450 Park Road 5, Canyon, TX 79015; (806) 488-2227.

faq.q: What is there to do in Palo Duro Canyon State Park?
faq.a: TPWD lists hiking, biking, horseback riding, camping, geocaching, bird watching and "summer performances of the TEXAS Outdoor Musical", across "over 30 miles of trails" and 1,500 acres for riding.

faq.q: Where should I stay near Palo Duro Canyon State Park?
faq.a: HotelGuides lists the nearest hotels in Canyon, 14 miles away - Hampton Inn & Suites Canyon and Holiday Inn Express & Suites Canyon at I-27 Exit 106 - with more on I-40 in Amarillo at 18-20 miles. Inside the park there are cabins, campsites and Palo Duro Glamping.

name: Grand Canyon National Park
line: A mile-deep canyon seen from a paved rim, a train from Williams, a river run of up to 18 days, a ring of tented camps, and a park mid-recovery from the August 2026 flood

jewels.name: The Rim Trail, Mather Point to Yavapai Point
jewels.blurb: the most-used 0.7-mile stretch of the South Rim, 15-30 minutes one way with constant canyon views, ending at the 1928 Yavapai Geology Museum on the rim edge

jewels.name: Hermit Road (Red Route)
jewels.blurb: a 7-mile rim road of overlooks, closed to private vehicles 1 March - 30 November 2026 and served by a shuttle every 12 minutes until an hour after sunset

jewels.name: Desert View Watchtower
jewels.blurb: Mary Colter's tower modelled on ancestral Puebloan architecture, 23 miles east of Grand Canyon Village at the end of Desert View Drive

jewels.name: Bright Angel Trail day hikes
jewels.blurb: graded turnaround points at Mile-and-a-Half and Three-Mile resthouses; as of 28 September 2026 the trail is open to River Resthouse but resthouse water is turned off

jewels.name: South Rim mule rides
jewels.blurb: Xanterra-run rides, currently on a limited schedule: the Canyon Vista Mule Ride (8:00 and 12:00) and the Havasupai Garden Mule Ride (7:00)

jewels.name: Colorado River raft trips
jewels.blurb: professionally guided trips of 3 to 18 days, often reserved a year or two ahead, run by 15 NPS-authorised concessioners; longer private trips go through a weighted lottery

jewels.name: Grand Canyon Star Party
jewels.blurb: a free week of telescopes on the South Rim each June (6-13 June 2026), with nightly talks at 8 pm and constellation tours from 9 pm

jewels.name: The North Rim
jewels.blurb: open through 30 November 2026 or first major snow, with campground, general store and scenic drives; no overnight lodging since the Dragon Bravo Fire destroyed Grand Canyon Lodge

jewels.name: El Tovar and the Historic District lodges
jewels.blurb: El Tovar Hotel, Bright Angel, Kachina, Thunderbird and Maswik lodges, run by Xanterra on the rim; closed to overnight guests through 31 October 2026

jewels.name: Under Canvas Grand Canyon
jewels.blurb: Grand Canyon Junction (Valle): safari-style tents with ensuite baths and wood stoves, including glass-roofed Stargazer tents, on a DarkSky-certified 160-acre site about 25 minutes from the South Rim entrance; open 15 April - 26 October 2026

jewels.name: Clear Sky Resorts: Grand Canyon
jewels.blurb: Valle: transparent sky domes for 2 to 7 guests, from standard to themed domes, with stargazing tours, yoga and Native American flute-making; closes for the 2026 season on 17 October

jewels.name: Wander Camp Grand Canyon
jewels.blurb: Valle area, about 25 minutes from the South Rim: off-grid canvas bell tents of 200+ sq ft with shared bathrooms, solar lighting, communal fire pits and an on-site food truck

jewels.name: WYLDSTAY Grand Canyon
jewels.blurb: 40 private acres about 25 minutes outside the South Rim: an off-grid tented 'luxury dark sky resort' with a holistic spa, yoga, sound baths and a labyrinth

jewels.name: Highland Grand Canyon
jewels.blurb: Rowe Well Road, about 4 miles from the South Rim: five boutique off-grid tents on 10 acres in the Kaibab National Forest, locally owned, with an outdoor kitchen, fire pit and telescope

jewels.name: Backland Luxury Nature Resort
jewels.blurb: a luxury glamping resort listed about 90 minutes from the South Rim; unit types and amenities were not verified in this build

jewels.name: Grand Canyon Glamping Resort (Grand Canyon West)
jewels.blurb: glamping wagons, tipis, tents and Stargazer Domes plus dry camping sites, a 1-mile drive from the Grand Canyon West Skywalk entrance

jewels.name: Shash Diné Eco-Retreat
jewels.blurb: 12 miles south of Page: a year-round glamping stay on a working ranch raising Navajo Churro sheep, built around a Navajo cultural experience

jewels.name: Village Camp Flagstaff
jewels.blurb: Flagstaff: an outdoor cabin and RV resort with rental cabins, clubhouse bar and bistro, seasonal pool and year-round hot tub

jewels.name: Mather Campground
jewels.blurb: the NPS campground in Grand Canyon Village, open all year, no hookups, with laundry and showers; reservations up to 6 months ahead via recreation.gov; currently dry camping under Stage 4 water restrictions

jewels.name: Desert View Campground
jewels.blurb: NPS campground 23 miles east of the Village, open 11 April - 18 October 2026, no hookups, bookable up to six months ahead on recreation.gov

jewels.name: North Rim Campground
jewels.blurb: the NPS campground on the North Rim, open 1 June - 15 October 2026; water and RV hookups not available; reservations via recreation.gov

jewels.name: Tusayan - Montane Campground (formerly Ten-X)
jewels.blurb: Kaibab National Forest campground 9 miles south of the Village, open 15 May - 10 October 2026, no hookups

jewels.name: Grand Canyon Camper Village
jewels.blurb: private campground in Tusayan, 7 miles south of Grand Canyon Village, open seasonally, with hookups and coin-operated showers

jewels.name: DeMotte Campground
jewels.blurb: National Forest campground 7 miles north of the North Rim park boundary, no hookups; its status after the 2025 Dragon Bravo Fire was not established

jewels.name: Kaibab Camper Village
jewels.blurb: Jacob Lake, about 40 miles from the North Rim: 60 gravel sites, open May - October, listed as the only campground near the North Rim with RV hookups

jewels.name: Grand Canyon KOA (Highway 64)
jewels.blurb: 5333 State Highway 64, described as the closest RV park in Williams to the Grand Canyon, with 50-amp sites, a pool and fire-pit rentals; open year-round

jewels.name: Williams / Circle Pines KOA
jewels.blurb: 4 miles west of downtown Williams: sites to 90 feet, 50-amp, pool, spa, mini golf and bike rentals; open 15 March - 1 November

jewels.name: Grand Canyon Railway RV Park
jewels.blurb: beside the Williams train depot, the only all-paved RV park in Williams, with pull-through, buddy and back-in spaces, pool, hot tub and a pet resort

jewels.name: Canyon Motel & RV Park
jewels.blurb: Williams, beside the Kaibab National Forest: historic motel rooms, caboose suites and railway-car suites alongside large-rig RV sites

jewels.name: Tusayan
jewels.blurb: the closest town to the South Rim, about a mile from the park gate, with hotels, tours and the Grand Canyon National Park Airport for scenic flights; its lodging is unaffected by the in-park closure

jewels.name: Grand Canyon Railway from Williams
jewels.blurb: a heritage train running since 1901 from the Williams depot to the South Rim, about two and a half hours each way, with dining and observation cars; reported operating in late September 2026

jewels.name: Bearizona Wildlife Park
jewels.blurb: Williams: a drive-through of more than three miles of ponderosa forest past bears, wolves, bison and elk, plus the walk-through Fort Bearizona; open daily 9 am - 4 pm

jewels.name: Grand Canyon Brewing + Distillery
jewels.blurb: a Williams brewery and distillery with a taproom at 301 North 7th Street, making beer, spirits and ready-to-drink cocktails

jewels.name: Flagstaff and Lowell Observatory
jewels.blurb: the world's first International Dark Sky City (24 October 2001), home of the observatory known for the discovery of Pluto

jewels.name: Grand Canyon West Skywalk
jewels.blurb: a glass walkway 70 feet out over the rim at Eagle Point on the Hualapai Reservation, about 4,000 feet above the canyon floor; ticketed and not affiliated with the national park

jewels.name: Grand Canyon Trail Rides
jewels.blurb: formerly Apache Stables, just outside the South Entrance near Tusayan: one- and two-hour Kaibab National Forest rides plus twilight campfire and wagon rides

jewels.name: Canyon Adventures Bike Tours and Café
jewels.blurb: beside the Grand Canyon Visitor Center: bike rentals and guided rides (mid-March to 31 October) on about 13 miles of rim roads and Greenway trails, including a 6.5-mile paved run to Tusayan

jewels.name: South Rim coach tours (Xanterra)
jewels.blurb: daily in-park coach tours to Hermits Rest and/or Desert View, plus sunrise and sunset tours

jewels.name: Grand Canyon Conservancy Field Institute
jewels.blurb: the park partner's guided programme, from a family day hike to a backpacking trip or an outdoor photography class

jewels.name: Papillon helicopter tours
jewels.blurb: helicopter flights from the South Rim, including the 25-30 minute North Canyon Tour and the 40-50 minute Grand Kingdom; air tours operate outside park boundaries

jewels.name: El Tovar Dining Room, South Rim
jewels.booking_route: Tock (exploretock.com), parties of 1-10 up to 60 days ahead; dinner reservations required
jewels.blurb: Native stone and Oregon pine dining room in the historic El Tovar Hotel with murals of Hopi, Apache, Mojave and Navajo customs; Prime Rib Hash and Salmon Tostada served for decades. The concessioner page currently lists all services as closed.

jewels.name: Rod's Steak House, Williams
jewels.blurb: Family-owned Route 66 steakhouse operating since 1946, keeping a 1940s steak grill and its neon cow awning, at 301 E Historic Route 66; per the Williams visitor bureau listing.

jewels.name: Pine Country Restaurant, Williams
jewels.booking_route: walk-in; online ordering for takeout; phone 928-635-9718
jewels.blurb: Gateway diner known for pies made daily in more than 50 flavours, from Lemon Meringue to Chocolate Covered Cherry Cream; open 7 am-9 pm.

jewels.name: Cruiser's Cafe 66, Williams
jewels.blurb: Route 66 cafe at 233 W Route 66 with restored gas pumps and road signs, a patio on the Mother Road, summer live music, and locally crafted beers and spirits; per the Williams visitor bureau listing.

jewels.name: Flagstaff Brewery Trail
jewels.booking_route: own form (LoyalBrew digital passport registration) or printed passport
jewels.blurb: Free passport across Flagstaff's breweries (digital via LoyalBrew or printed); collect every sticker, with no time limit, for a commemorative pint glass at the Flagstaff Visitor Center.

jewels.name: Beaver Street Brewery, Flagstaff
jewels.blurb: Flagstaff's first brewpub, opened March 1994, still brewing in its original brewhouse with wood-fired pizzas and the 21+ Brews & Cues billiards bar; per the Flagstaff visitor bureau listing.

jewels.name: Historic Barrel House, downtown Flagstaff
jewels.blurb: Historic Brewing Company's microbrewery and gastropub at 110 S. San Francisco Street, a stop on the Brewery Trail; per the Flagstaff visitor bureau listing.

jewels.name: Dark Sky Brewing Taproom & Pizzicletta, Flagstaff
jewels.blurb: Microbrewery and pizzeria pairing at 117 N Beaver Street in downtown Flagstaff, a stop on the Brewery Trail; per the Flagstaff visitor bureau listing.

jewels.name: Drinking Horn Meadery Mead Hall, Flagstaff
jewels.blurb: Honey-mead producer ('Live Simply. Drink Simply.') with a Mead Hall tasting room at 108 E Route 66.

jewels.name: Brandy's Proper Cafe, Flagstaff
jewels.blurb: Route 66 cafe joining Brandy's Restaurant & Bakery (50-year history) with Proper Meats + Provisions' James Beard-nominated butcher-driven sandwiches; per the Flagstaff visitor bureau listing.

jewels.name: Atria, Flagstaff
jewels.blurb: Chef Rochelle Daniel's seasonal modern American restaurant at 103 N. Leroux St using locally grown ingredients; she is a James Beard Award semifinalist and 2017 Arizona Culinary Hall of Fame inductee; per the Flagstaff visitor bureau listing.

faq.q: Can you stay overnight inside Grand Canyon National Park right now?
faq.a: Not in park lodging until November. After the 29 August 2026 flash flood damaged the park's water line, all in-park hotels closed to overnight guests from 31 August, and the closure has been extended through 31 October 2026. Reservations arriving 1 November and later are proceeding as planned, pending water restoration. Hotels in Tusayan, outside the park, are unaffected.

faq.q: Where can you go glamping near the Grand Canyon?
faq.a: Most of the camps sit in the Valle / Grand Canyon Junction corridor south of the South Rim. Under Canvas Grand Canyon is about 25 minutes from the South Rim entrance and runs 15 April - 26 October 2026; Clear Sky Resorts, Wander Camp and WYLDSTAY are in the same area, and Highland Grand Canyon is about 4 miles from the rim.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to hike in the Grand Canyon?
faq.a: Not for a day hike. The NPS says a backcountry permit is required for overnight camping outside Mather, Desert View and North Rim campgrounds, and that day hikes, including nighttime day hikes, need none. Organised non-commercial groups of 12-30 doing rim-to-rim need a Special Use Permit.

faq.q: How do you reserve a campsite at the Grand Canyon?
faq.a: NPS campground reservations can be made up to six months ahead through recreation.gov or by phone at (877) 444-6777. NPS campgrounds in the park have no RV hookups, and Trailer Village, the full-hookup RV park, is currently closed due to water shortage.

faq.q: How much does it cost to enter Grand Canyon National Park?
faq.a: $35 per private vehicle, $30 per motorcycle, or $20 per person on foot or bicycle, valid for 7 days. Non-US residents aged 16 and over pay an extra $100 each unless they hold an Annual or America the Beautiful pass.

faq.q: Is the North Rim open in 2026?
faq.a: Yes, through 30 November 2026 or the first major snowstorm, with the campground, general store and select scenic drives and viewpoints open. There is no overnight lodging on the North Rim since the Dragon Bravo Fire destroyed Grand Canyon Lodge, and the North Kaibab Trail is closed.

name: Saguaro National Park
line: Two saguaro forests on either side of Tucson - the paved Cactus Forest Loop in the Rincon Mountain District, the gravel Bajada Loop and Signal Hill petroglyphs in the Tucson Mountain District - ringed by the Desert Museum, Mission San Xavier del Bac, Sabino Canyon, Mount Lemmon and the first UNESCO City of Gastronomy in the United States

jewels.name: Cactus Forest Loop Drive (Rincon Mountain District, east)
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park entrance fee only
jewels.blurb: an 8-mile paved scenic loop with "several trailheads, scenic vistas and pullouts"; open to bicycles but "narrow with multiple tight turns and steep hills"; highlighted by the NPS for sunset; no vehicles over 102 inches wide or 40 feet combined length

jewels.name: Bajada Loop Drive (Tucson Mountain District, west)
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park entrance fee only
jewels.blurb: a 6-mile unpaved, graded dirt loop with scenic pullouts, picnic areas and trailheads; bikes on the road only - "Riding on trails around this loop is not permitted"

jewels.name: Signal Hill petroglyphs
jewels.blurb: on the Bajada Loop Drive, "the best place to see petroglyphs within the park", with a spiral petroglyph atop the Signal Hill Trail and a picnic area with shelters and grills; "The trails from this area (including the short walk up to the petroglyphs) are not ADA accessible"

jewels.name: Valley View Overlook Nature Trail
jewels.blurb: an easy 0.8 mile (1.3 km) round trip off the Bajada Loop, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s, ending on a ridge with benches looking over Avra Valley, Signal Hill and "the jagged ridge of Picacho Peak to the north"

jewels.name: Desert Discovery Trail (west)
jewels.blurb: a 1/2-mile "paved trail with exhibit signs" with "Pavement texturing and shade ramadas with resting benches"; trail guides available in braille

jewels.name: Desert Ecology Trail and Mica View Trail (east)
jewels.blurb: two short accessible walks in the Rincon Mountain District: the 1/4-mile Desert Ecology Trail, "paved trail has exhibits along the way" with benches, and the 0.7-mile Mica View Trail on a "hard-packed surface conducive to wheelchairs, walkers" to the Broadway Trailhead

jewels.name: Rincon Mountain and Red Hills visitor centers and cactus gardens
jewels.blurb: one visitor center in each district, each with "restrooms, water fountains, maps, hiking trails, a driving loop, programs, and staff"; "Water fountains are found at both visitor centers and only there"; both have "paved cactus garden paths"; summer 8 am-4 pm, winter 9 am-5 pm

jewels.name: Freeman Homestead Trail (east)
jewels.blurb: an easy 1-mile walk past a historic homestead site, a saguaro grove and a desert wash

jewels.name: Loma Verde Loop (east)
jewels.blurb: an easy 3.8-mile loop with 60 ft of elevation change, mesquite trees and overlook views

jewels.name: Hope Camp and Ridgeview Trail (east)
jewels.blurb: a moderate 2-mile walk with 400 ft of gain, panoramic views and seasonal wildflowers; the Hope Camp Trail also runs 2.8 miles from the Loma Alta trailhead, open to bikes, and "connects the Arizona Trail"

jewels.name: Garwood Dam and Wildhorse Tank (east)
jewels.blurb: a moderate 6.4-mile hike to a perennial water source with Santa Catalina views

jewels.name: Tanque Verde Ridge Trail (east)
jewels.booking_route: none needed for day use; camping by permit on Recreation.gov
jewels.blurb: the east district's strenuous ridge climb - up to 8.7 miles and 4,000 ft of elevation, past a crested saguaro; the NPS names it for sunset, and it leads to Juniper Basin campground (6,000 ft, 6.9 mi)

jewels.name: Wild Dog Trail and Signal Hill add-on (west)
jewels.blurb: an easy 1.8-mile trail with an optional 0.5-mile Signal Hill add-on

jewels.name: King Canyon and Gould Mine Loop (west)
jewels.blurb: an easy-to-moderate 2.4-mile loop with 380 ft of gain through a sandy wash and rocky sections; the NPS notes "bees may be present due to moisture"

jewels.name: Sendero Esperanza to the Ridge and Wasson Peak (west)
jewels.blurb: moderate to strenuous, 3.4 to 8 miles and 220 to 1,600 ft of gain, to the Tucson Mountain District's highest point at 4,687 ft

jewels.name: Saguaro Wilderness backcountry campgrounds (Manning Camp and five others)
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov permit (up to 2 months in advance, per the NPS outdoor activities page)
jewels.blurb: the park's only camping: 6 hike-in designated campgrounds - Manning Camp (6 sites, 7,920 ft, 7.5 mi from Turkey Creek), Spud Rock Spring, Happy Valley Saddle, Juniper Basin, Grass Shack (10 mi) and Douglas Spring; $8 per campsite per night, max 6 per site; "There are no accommodations for any vehicle camping (including RV)"

jewels.name: Ranger-led programmes (year-round, busiest January-April)
jewels.booking_route: none observed - see the park calendar
jewels.blurb: guided programmes in both districts, "from ranger talks around our gardens to night hikes"; the widest choice January through April; summer limited by "extreme temperatures during the daytime"; schedules on the park calendar

jewels.name: Golden Gate multi-use trail and park cycling
jewels.blurb: a "wide gravel path" reached from the Bajada Loop or Picture Rocks Road on the former Golden Gate Road, now "permanently closed to vehicle traffic"; e-bikes allowed "only where traditional bicycles are allowed"; "Drinking water is NOT available on the Cactus Forest Drive, Bajada Loop Drive or at any picnic area"

jewels.name: Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum
jewels.booking_route: not observed (desertmuseum.org returned 403 on three URLs)
jewels.blurb: founded in 1952 just west of Tucson: a zoo, aquarium, botanical garden, natural history museum, art gallery and publisher on 98 acres, with "two miles (3.2 km) of walking paths traversing 21 acres", over 230 animal species and 1,200 plant varieties, nearly 400,000 visitors a year; Visit Tucson calls it "a zoo, garden and museum"

jewels.name: Old Tucson
jewels.blurb: built in 1939 for the movie Arizona (1940) beside the Tucson Mountains near the park's western section; now "The Adventure Park" with studio tours and stunt shows, Nightfall and Ghost Tours in October 2026 and Yuletide November 24 - December 24; online tickets "Save $5 per Ticket Compared to Walk-Up Pricing"; lease ends April 2027 and Pima County is seeking an operator

jewels.name: Mission San Xavier del Bac
jewels.booking_route: none needed; 1950 W San Xavier Rd, (520) 294-2624 (sanxaviermission.org)
jewels.blurb: founded in 1692 by Father Eusebio Francisco Kino on the Tohono O'odham Nation's San Xavier reservation; the church was built 1783-1797 and is "the oldest European structure in Arizona", a National Historic Landmark since 1960 and still an active parish serving the village of Wa:k

jewels.name: Mission Garden
jewels.blurb: "a living agricultural museum of Sonoran Desert-adapted heritage fruit trees, traditional local heirloom crops and edible native plants" at the foot of Sentinel Peak, representing about 4,100 years of continuous cultivation; open Wednesday-Sunday, 8am-2pm October-March

jewels.name: Tohono Chul Sonoran Botanic Garden
jewels.blurb: "49 acres of serene beauty", an accredited botanical garden and Level II arboretum at 7366 North Paseo del Norte, with the Garden Bistro (daily 9am-4pm); grounds 8am-5pm daily; $20 general, $15 seniors 62+

jewels.name: Sabino Canyon Crawler
jewels.booking_route: own online reservation system on sabinocanyoncrawler.com
jewels.blurb: the electric shuttle in the Sabino Canyon Recreation Area: a Sabino Canyon route with hourly departures 9 AM-4 PM ($15 adults, $8 children) and a Bear Canyon route, plus seasonal Saturday Night Tours of "approximately 90 minutes"; a separate $8 amenity fee per vehicle

jewels.name: Sky Island Scenic Byway (Catalina Highway) to Mount Lemmon
jewels.blurb: a 27-mile byway climbing "to shady conifer forests at nearly 9,000 feet", with "biological diversity equivalent to a drive from Mexico to Canada", starting among saguaros in the Sonoran Desert

jewels.name: Mount Lemmon Ski Valley and the Sky Ride
jewels.blurb: in the Coronado National Forest at 10300 Ski Run Rd: winter skiing, the Sky Ride scenic chairlift year-round, a restaurant, gift shop and fudge store; Thursday-Monday, "closed Tuesday and Wednesday"

jewels.name: Pima Air & Space Museum
jewels.blurb: "one of the largest non-government funded aviation & space museums in the world" with "about 400 historic aircraft" on "80 acres" and six indoor hangars; adults $22.50 for one day; summer hours 9 AM-3 PM

jewels.name: Tanque Verde Ranch
jewels.blurb: "one of America's old-time cattle and guest ranches", established in 1868, an all-inclusive dude ranch on 640 acres "nestled among Rincon mountains and adjacent to Saguaro National Park and Coronado National Forest"; packages include lodging, three meals, horseback riding and most activities

jewels.name: White Stallion Ranch
jewels.blurb: "a historic, traditional, yet upscale family-owned and operated dude ranch" run by the True family since 1965 on 3,000 acres, with 43 rooms and 170 horses; riding, archery, rock climbing, jeep tours and a spa

jewels.name: Hacienda Del Sol Guest Ranch Resort
jewels.blurb: a Catalina Foothills resort operating "since 1929", with The Grill, the Terraza Garden Patio & Lounge, a spa, complimentary Sunday yoga, and billed as "Tucson's Premier Place for Weekly Live Music"; the base for Backroads' family trip

jewels.name: Loews Ventana Canyon Resort
jewels.blurb: "A Sonoran Escape for all the Senses" in the Catalina foothills: 398 rooms including 27 suites, two Tom Fazio-designed golf courses, the Lakeside Spa, two heated pools, and the Flying V restaurant; AAA Four Diamond

jewels.name: Camp Saguaro (Hipcamp), Tucson
jewels.blurb: a Hipcamp property listed for tents, RVs and lodging, rated 100% across 889 reviews on Hipcamp's Saguaro National Park glamping page

jewels.name: Diamond J RV Park, Tucson Mountain Park edge
jewels.blurb: an adults-only (18+) RV park at 3451 S. San Joaquin Rd with 128 "40' ultra-wide sites", full hookups, and reviewer-reported "trails that go straight to Tucson Mountain Park and Saguaro National Park"

jewels.name: Tucson E-Bike Adventures - Saguaro National Park East E-Bike Tour
jewels.booking_route: AAA Travel / Viator platform (also listed on Expedia and Pelago)
jewels.blurb: a 2 hour 30 minute guided e-bike tour of the east district, including "E-Bike, Battery, Helmet, Guide"; minimum age 16, riders "110-260 lbs." and 5'1" to 6'5"; from $168.70 per person on AAA's listing

jewels.name: Backroads - Arizona's Saguaro & Tucson Family Multi-Adventure Tour
jewels.blurb: a 4-day, 3-night family trip for ages 7-17 (minimum 4) that will "hike and bike through diverse Saguaro National Park", visit the Desert Museum, hike Sabino Canyon and ride in the Tucson Mountains foothills, staying at Hacienda Del Sol; from $3,199 per person; 2027 departures in February, March and November

jewels.name: Saguaro Corners Restaurant & Bar
jewels.blurb: "just outside Saguaro National Park East since 1956, on the corner of Escalante and Old Spanish Trail": a scratch kitchen with 18 craft taps and a "shaded and misted patio with Rincon Mountain views" and "wildlife and desert beauty right out our windows"; closed Mondays

jewels.name: El Güero Canelo - the Sonoran hot dog
jewels.blurb: a "James Beard Award-winning" Tucson institution serving Sonoran hot dogs inspired by Hermosillo recipes (AFAR)

jewels.name: Ruiz Hot Dogs
jewels.blurb: a small cart on 22nd Street serving Sonoran hot dogs (AFAR)

jewels.name: Tacos Apson
jewels.blurb: mesquite-grilled costillas de res (beef ribs) (AFAR)

jewels.name: Caruso's, Fourth Avenue
jewels.blurb: "has been going strong since 1938" on Fourth Avenue and "still uses the same copper pot" for its signature red sauce (AFAR)

jewels.name: Cup Café at Hotel Congress
jewels.blurb: in Hotel Congress, known for "legendary baked eggs" (AFAR)

jewels.name: Downtown Kitchen + Cocktails
jewels.blurb: "highlighting indigenous ingredients for years", including "Dr. Pepper pork belly biscuits" made with local mesquite bean flour (AFAR)

jewels.name: Heirloom Farmers' Market at Rillito Park
jewels.blurb: a Sunday market with "space for more than 80 small businesses", including Country Harvest Pantry's "heirloom beans that have been a staple of Arizona cuisine for thousands of years" (AFAR)

jewels.name: Pueblo Vida Brewing and Crooked Tooth Brewing
jewels.blurb: Pueblo Vida, with "some of the best" hazy IPAs in the state, and Crooked Tooth, with "Sonoran sours in flavors like Key lime pie and hibiscus" (AFAR)

jewels.name: Tucson City of Gastronomy
jewels.booking_route: none - a designation and certification body, not a bookable product
jewels.blurb: "On 15 December 2015, Tucson, Arizona, became the first UNESCO City of Gastronomy designated in the United States"; the organisation "Certifies and endorses restaurants, food artisans, culinary events, and experiences"

faq.q: Is there a campground at Saguaro National Park?
faq.a: Not a drive-in one. The NPS states there are no accommodations for any vehicle camping, including RV. Camping is at six designated hike-in campgrounds in the Saguaro Wilderness, $8 per campsite per night, with permits on Recreation.gov.

faq.q: How much does it cost to enter Saguaro National Park?
faq.a: $25 per private vehicle, $20 per motorcycle and $15 per person on foot or bicycle; a Saguaro annual pass is $45. The NPS states that only debit and credit cards are accepted, no cash.

faq.q: Which district of Saguaro should I visit, east or west?
faq.a: Both have a visitor center, a loop drive and short trails. The Rincon Mountain District (east) has the 8-mile paved Cactus Forest Loop Drive and the backcountry campgrounds; the Tucson Mountain District (west) has the 6-mile graded dirt Bajada Loop Drive and the Signal Hill petroglyphs.

faq.q: How much water should I carry hiking in Saguaro?
faq.a: The NPS says that on hot summer days you should be drinking 1 quart of water per hour of hiking, and to avoid 10 am - 4 pm in the summer months; in winter, take at least 2 quarts per day. Water fountains are found only at the two visitor centers.

faq.q: Where can I see petroglyphs in Saguaro National Park?
faq.a: At Signal Hill on the Bajada Loop Drive in the west district, which the NPS calls the best place to see petroglyphs within the park. The short walk up to the petroglyphs is not ADA accessible.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Saguaro National Park?
faq.a: The NPS describes winter as mildly warm, with days averaging 65 degrees and nights averaging 40, and ranger programmes are busiest January through April. Summer daytime temperatures regularly reach well over 100 degrees, and the monsoon runs June 15 to September 30.

name: White Sands National Park
line: World's largest gypsum dunefield

jewels.name: Dunes Drive
jewels.booking_route: pay at the White Sands Entrance Station - $25 per private vehicle, cash or credit/debit
jewels.blurb: "an eight-mile (13 km) scenic drive"; "the first five miles of Dunes Drive are paved and the last three miles are a hard-packed gypsum sand road"; "The 16-mile (26km) round-trip drive takes approximately 45 minutes", with "outdoor exhibits, hiking trails, picnic areas, vault toilets, and parking areas" along it. The park itself: "Great wave-like dunes of gypsum sand have engulfed 275 square miles of desert, creating the world's largest gypsum dunefield."

jewels.name: Sledding the gypsum dunes
jewels.booking_route: none needed - bring a sled or rent/buy one at the White Sands Trading Post
jewels.blurb: "Waxed plastic snow saucers work best and can be rented or purchased at the park's gift shop"; sledding is "Allowed in the loop portion of Dunes Drive". "Choose a dune with a gently sloping face and a level run-off at the end";"Sit or lay on the sled, with your feet pointing downhill"; "Do not stand up while sledding."

jewels.name: Sunset Stroll
jewels.blurb: "A leisurely, ranger-guided stroll through the gypsum sand dunes" timed to conclude at sunset; "Sunset strolls are offered three days a week on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday"; "45 minutes to one hour". "Program is free. Park entrance fees apply." "Reservations are not required or permitted." Meets at the "Sunset Stroll Meets Here" parking area, 8 miles from the fee station.

jewels.name: Moonlight Hike
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov or 1-877-444-6777, from one month ahead at 8:00 am MT
jewels.blurb: "Hike the dunes under the magical glow of the moon"; "March through November, on nights surrounding the full moon"; "1.5 - 2 hours". "$8 per person ages 16 and older and $4 per child ages 15 and younger" plus entrance fees. "Tickets are available one month before the day of the tour at 8:00 am Mountain Time" and "often sell out in a matter of minutes." "Flashlights, headlamps, and flash photography are not allowed."

jewels.name: Full Moon Night
jewels.blurb: "Enjoy the radiance of the dunes beneath a full moon with live music, ranger programs, and special guest presenters and artists"; May through October; "The park hours are generally extended two hours from the park's normal closing time on all Full Moon Nights." 2026: May 1, May 31, June 29, July 29, August 27, September 26, October 25. "Program is free. Park entrance fees apply." "Reservations or tickets are not required."

jewels.name: Lake Lucero Tour
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov or 1-877-444-6777, from one month before the tour
jewels.blurb: "Take a tour to Lake Lucero with a ranger and learn about the formation of the sands", with "thousands of exposed selenite crystals"; "November through March"; "Three hours"; "$8 per person ages 16 and older and $4 per child ages 15 and younger". Meets at the "Small Missile Range Gate, located on Hwy 70 West between mile markers 174 and 175"; the drive is "17.5 miles (27.36 km) one-way".

jewels.name: Alkali Flat Trail
jewels.blurb: "5 miles (8 km), out-and-back", "Strenuous", about "3 hours": "This trail takes you through the heart of the sands, up and over steep dunes, to the edges of the Alkali Flat", the bed of an ice-age lake - "this trail is not flat". "Take a minimum of two 32-ounce (1 L) bottles of water per person"; "If you cannot see the next trail marker because of blowing sand or because the trail marker is knocked down, do not proceed—return to your car."

jewels.name: White Sands Visitor Center
jewels.booking_route: none needed - 19955 Highway 70 West, Alamogordo, NM 88310
jewels.blurb: Built 1936-1940 as a WPA project; "In 1990, the visitor center and adjacent seven buildings...were officially designated as the White Sands National Park Historic District", with "decoratively carved corbels" and "individually crafted tin lighting fixtures." Museum exhibits and a 17-minute film every 30 minutes (Spanish and audio-description versions). "The visitor center and gift shop are open 363 days a year, closing on Thanksgiving and Christmas Day." 575-479-6124.

jewels.name: White Sands Trading Post (park gift shop)
jewels.blurb: Operated by Western National Parks Association, the gift shop "sells sleds for sledding, pre-packaged food, bottled water, and souvenirs" - "convenient, ready-to-eat food options including packaged sandwiches, bottled drinks, salty snacks, and sweet treats" - the only food in the park. It stays open during missile-test closures.

jewels.name: Fossilized footprints exhibit
jewels.booking_route: none needed - in the visitor center
jewels.blurb: "the largest collection of fossilized human footprints", showing humans in the Tularosa Basin "at least 23,000 years ago" - "probably the most important resources in the Americas to understand the interaction of humans and extinct animals from the ice age." "Currently the footprints at White Sands are inaccessible", but an exhibit of "casted human footprints" opened at the visitor center in January 2024.

jewels.name: Yucca, Roadrunner and Primrose picnic areas
jewels.booking_route: first-come, first-served; Group Use Area by reservation with the park
jewels.blurb: "There are a total of 62 shaded tables in the three designated public picnic areas", with elevated grills, "located off Dunes Drive about six to seven miles (9.65 –11.26 km) from the fee station"; Roadrunner has two pavilions for up to 20 people; the Group Use Area pavilion needs a reservation ("Reservations are required to use this area").

jewels.name: Backcountry camping (closed)
jewels.booking_route: none - closed, no reopening date published
jewels.blurb: Normally "ten primitive backcountry camping sites available on a first-come, first-served basis" (things-to-do page). Today: "Backcountry camping is currently closed while park staff assess environmental conditions and other key factors"; no reopening date; "Currently, overnight stays are not permitted within White Sands National Park."

jewels.name: Kit for sun and heat in the dunes
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates) - water and snacks also sold at the park gift shop
jewels.blurb: The park's list: "One gallon (4 liters) of water per person per day is recommended", with salty snacks; "A hat, sunscreen, and long sleeves are all recommended to protect yourself from sunburn in the dunes" - even in winter; "Adequate clothing (rain jacket and warm layers)"; "Closed toed shoes are suggested. Venomous creatures can be found throughout the dunefield." Also a first aid kit and flashlight.

jewels.name: Kit for dune hiking and navigation
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates)
jewels.blurb: "Wear a wide-brimmed hat, sunscreen with an SPF of 15 or higher, sunglasses" and lightweight long sleeves and long pants; carry "the park map, compass, flashlight with extra batteries, whistle, signal mirror, and first-aid kit" - GPS can be unreliable here, and the safety page warns "Do not rely on your phone⁠— cell service is spotty in the park." "Have at least one gallon (4L) of water per person, per day."

jewels.name: Kit for sledding the dunes
jewels.booking_route: park gift shop (rent or buy), or affiliate retail referral (Amazon Associates; REI.com via AvantLink) for a saucer brought from home
jewels.blurb: "Waxed plastic snow saucers work best and can be rented or purchased at the park's gift shop"; "You may also bring your own sleds." The NPS warns to watch for "the hard ground at the dune's base where injuries commonly occur" and to never sled "into a parking area or roadway."

jewels.name: Kit for the night hike and Lake Lucero
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates)
jewels.blurb: Moonlight Hike: bring "Hat, jacket, and gloves," "closed-toe shoes," and "two liters of water per person" - "Flashlights, headlamps, and flash photography are not allowed." (moonlight-hike page) Lake Lucero: closed-toe hiking shoes, sunscreen, hats, sunglasses, snacks and "a minimum of one gallon of water per person"; long sleeves and pants recommended (https://www.nps.gov/whsa/planyourvisit/lake-lucero-tour.htm, read 2026-10-03).

jewels.name: Oliver Lee Memorial State Park
jewels.booking_route: ReserveAmerica (newmexicostateparks.reserveamerica.com), up to six months ahead
jewels.blurb: "Set against the dramatic Sacramento Mountains, this park features a historic ranch house, quiet camping in the Chihuahuan Desert, and pools of water under the cottonwood trees of Dog Canyon." 15 water/electric sites (30 amp), 1 ADA site (50 amp), 24 developed dry sites with 8 tent pads; "Guided Tours of the Historic Oliver Lee Ranch House -Contact Park for current schedule". 8 miles south of Alamogordo via US 54, then 4 miles east on Dog Canyon Road; (575) 437-8284. The NPS lists it 24 miles from White Sands.

jewels.name: Aguirre Spring Campground
jewels.booking_route: first-come, first-served; group shelters by phone 575-525-4300, 48 hours ahead
jewels.blurb: BLM: "The high wall, needle-like spires of the Organ Mountains curve dramatically around a semicircle of Chihuahuan Desert habitat"; "a total of 55 individual campsites that are available on a first-come first-served basis"; $7 per vehicle per campsite overnight, $5 day use; "The recommended max length for RVs is 23 feet". Baylor Pass Trail (six miles one way) and Pine Tree Trail (four-mile loop). The NPS lists it 39 miles from White Sands.

jewels.name: Hacienda RV Resort
jewels.blurb: 740 Stern Drive, Las Cruces: "113 meticulously maintained RV sites" with "30/50 amp electrical hookups," "full water and sewer hookups," and "free high-speed WiFi"; hot tub, fitness center, dog park and clubhouse; Pull Thru XL sites 69'-110'; 1.5 miles from Old Mesilla. (575) 528-5800. Las Cruces sits at the ring's edge: the NPS puts the park entrance 52 miles east of Las Cruces.

jewels.name: KOA of Las Cruces
jewels.blurb: Listed by Visit Las Cruces: "conveniently located one mile from Interstate 10, overlooking Las Cruces and the scenic Mesilla Valley". koa.com refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so site types and rates are not stated here.

jewels.name: TownePlace Suites, Las Cruces
jewels.blurb: Marriott's extended-stay brand, listed by Visit Las Cruces under "Nationally Known Brands" at 2143 Telshor Ct., Las Cruces, as pet friendly. marriott.com refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Hilton Garden Inn, Las Cruces
jewels.blurb: Listed by Visit Las Cruces under "Nationally Known Brands" at 2550 Don Roser Dr., Las Cruces, as pet friendly. hilton.com refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Home2 Suites by Hilton, Las Cruces
jewels.blurb: Listed by Visit Las Cruces under "Nationally Known Brands" at 1120 N. Telshor Blvd., Las Cruces, as pet friendly. hilton.com refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Staybridge Suites, Las Cruces
jewels.blurb: IHG's extended-stay brand, listed by Visit Las Cruces under "Nationally Known Brands" at 2651 E. Northrise Dr., Las Cruces, as pet friendly. ihg.com refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: The Lodge at Cloudcroft
jewels.blurb: Established 1899 in the Sacramento Mountains at "9,000 feet above sea level"; its golf course is "one of the highest courses in New Mexico"; dining at "1899", and "Rebecca" is "our resident ghost." Part of the independent 223 Collection.

jewels.name: Hotel Encanto de Las Cruces
jewels.blurb: Visit Las Cruces: "A unique New Mexico hotel with an ambiance reflective of Spanish and Mexican Colonial history and tradition"; 705 S. Telshor Blvd.; offers a "pet-friendly package" with room, doggie toy and blankets.

jewels.name: New Mexico Museum of Space History
jewels.booking_route: admission at the museum (prices page not read)
jewels.blurb: "Did you know that New Mexico's Tularosa Basin was the cradle of America's space program?" Moon rocks, satellite replicas and the International Space Hall of Fame (est. 1976); the New Horizons Dome Theater & Planetarium. 1301 North White Sands Blvd., Alamogordo; (575) 437-2840; open Monday and Wednesday-Saturday 10-5, Sunday 12-5, closed Tuesday. The museum notes its Fifth Floor is temporarily closed for renovation (nmspacemuseum.org, read 2026-10-03).

jewels.name: Heart of the Desert Pistachios & Wine
jewels.blurb: "New Mexico's first and largest producing pistachio grove", founded 1974 with over 13,000 pistachio trees; wine tasting room, gift shop and free farm tours of the groves, roasting facility and vineyard. On Highway 54/70, Alamogordo; 800.432.0999; Mon-Sat 8AM-6PM, Sun 9AM-6PM.

jewels.name: Organ Mountains-Desert Peaks National Monument
jewels.blurb: BLM: "The Organ Mountains are a steep, angular mountain range with rocky spires that jut majestically above the Chihuahuan Desert floor to an elevation of 9,000 feet." 496,330 acres, established May 21, 2014; hiking, horseback riding, mountain biking, camping and wildlife viewing, including Aguirre Spring and the Sierra Vista Trail.

jewels.name: Ski Cloudcroft
jewels.blurb: "The Southern Most Ski Area in New Mexico, where families come to ski, snowboard, tube and, most importantly, have fun!" Top elevation 9,100 feet, base 8,400; winter and summer tubing. The 2025-26 season closed March 7, 2026 "due to warm weather and insufficient snow". 1920 1/2 U.S Highway 82, Cloudcroft; (575) 682-2333.

jewels.name: Alameda Park Zoo
jewels.blurb: Alamogordo: "Home to nearly 300 animals representing 90 species, the 12-acre Alameda Park Zoo"; daily 9am-5pm except Christmas and New Year's; (575) 439-4290.

jewels.name: Alamogordo
jewels.blurb: The gateway town: the visitor center is "about 15 miles (24 km) west of Alamogordo", about 15 minutes' drive, and "The nearest gas station is located in Alamogordo". Visit Alamogordo's visitor center: 1301 North White Sands Blvd., 575-439-4100.

jewels.name: Cloudcroft
jewels.blurb: "Perched nearly 9,000 feet above sea level in the Sacramento Mountains, Cloudcroft was once accessible only by train", with "boutique shopping and cozy cafés to hiking, mountain biking, and winter skiing" (Visit Alamogordo day trips). The NPS names the Lincoln National Forest campgrounds around it (Pines, Silver, Skyline) at about 35-69 miles from the park.

jewels.name: Las Cruces and Old Mesilla
jewels.blurb: The western gateway: the park entrance is "about 52 miles (84 km) east of Las Cruces", about an hour on US-70 (NPS). Visit Las Cruces counts "nearly 60 different hotels" and names Mesilla's "classic New Mexican restaurants" with "inviting patios". Visitors bureau: 336 S. Main St., (575) 541-2444.

jewels.name: La Posta de Mesilla
jewels.blurb: "The year was 1939": a "historic adobe hacienda" on the old Butterfield Stagecoach route serving "Mexican Food & Steaks", known for fajitas, chile rellenos and margaritas. 2410 Calle De San Albino, Mesilla; (575) 524-3524.

jewels.name: Double Eagle (Mesilla)
jewels.blurb: Named by Visit Las Cruces with La Posta among Mesilla's "classic New Mexican restaurants" with "inviting patios". Its own site was not fetched, so nothing else is stated here.

jewels.name: Oppenheimer Gasthaus
jewels.blurb: Listed by Visit Alamogordo: 902 N New York Ave, Alamogordo, NM 88310; 575-348-2853.

jewels.name: 575 Brewing Company
jewels.blurb: Listed by Visit Alamogordo: 234 West 8th St., Alamogordo.

jewels.name: D.H. Lescombes (Alamogordo)
jewels.blurb: Listed by Visit Alamogordo: 261 Panorama Blvd., Alamogordo; 575-616-5595.

jewels.name: Pizza Patio
jewels.blurb: Listed by Visit Alamogordo: 2203 E. 1st. St., Alamogordo; 575-434-9633.

jewels.name: Rustic Café
jewels.blurb: Listed by Visit Alamogordo: 3500 N. White Sands Blvd., Alamogordo; 575-437-2770.

jewels.name: Hi-D-Ho Drive-In
jewels.blurb: Listed by Visit Alamogordo: 414 S. White Sands Blvd., Alamogordo; 575-437-6400.

faq.q: Is White Sands National Park free?
faq.a: No. The NPS entrance fee is $25.00 per private vehicle, $20.00 per motorcycle and $15.00 per person on foot or bicycle (16 and older); a White Sands annual pass is $45.00. "Children ages 15 and younger enter for free" (basicinfo page). Payment is "Cash or Credit/Debit" at the entrance station.

faq.q: Can you camp at White Sands National Park?
faq.a: Not at present: "Backcountry camping is currently closed while park staff assess environmental conditions and other key factors", and "Currently, overnight stays are not permitted within White Sands National Park." No reopening date has been set. The NPS points campers to Oliver Lee Memorial State Park (24 miles) and Aguirre Springs (39 miles).

faq.q: Can you rent sleds at White Sands National Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Waxed plastic snow saucers work best and can be rented or purchased at the park's gift shop." You may also bring your own. Sledding is allowed in the loop portion of Dunes Drive; "Sit or lay on the sled, with your feet pointing downhill" and "Do not stand up while sledding."

faq.q: Can you take dogs to White Sands National Park?
faq.a: Yes, on a leash: "The leash can be no longer than six feet (2 m)." "Do not bring pets inside the visitor center", pick up after your pet, and never leave a pet in a vehicle - "Within just ten minutes, the inside vehicle temperature will become 25 degrees warmer than the outside temperature."

faq.q: When is White Sands National Park closed?
faq.a: The park closes on Thanksgiving and Christmas Day. Separately, "White Sands Missile Range regularly conducts military tests. For visitor safety, the only road into the dunefield, Dunes Drive, may be closed for periods of up to three hours during military tests"; one is listed for October 15, 2026, 7:00 to 9:00 am. "The park visitor center and gift shop remain open during military test closures."

faq.q: How far is White Sands National Park from Las Cruces?
faq.a: "Drive time: About 1 hour" east on US-70; the entrance is "about 52 miles (84 km) east of Las Cruces on the north side (left-hand side) of the road." From Alamogordo it is about 15 miles and 15 minutes; from El Paso, about 1.5 hours.

faq.q: What is the closest airport to White Sands National Park?
faq.a: The NPS names "El Paso, TX, about 85 miles (136.79 km) from the park". "No public transportation serves the park", and rideshare services typically won't provide return pickups.

faq.q: What should you wear at White Sands National Park?
faq.a: "A hat, sunscreen, and long sleeves are all recommended to protect yourself from sunburn in the dunes" - even in winter; "Adequate clothing (rain jacket and warm layers)" because weather shifts fast; and "Closed toed shoes are suggested. Venomous creatures can be found throughout the dunefield." Carry "One gallon (4 liters) of water per person per day".

faq.q: Do you need reservations for White Sands National Park?
faq.a: Not to enter - the fee is paid at the entrance station. The ticketed ranger program is the Moonlight Hike: book on Recreation.gov or at 1-877-444-6777; "Tickets are available one month before the day of the tour at 8:00 am Mountain Time" and "often sell out in a matter of minutes." The Lake Lucero tour (November-March) books the same way.

faq.q: What are the White Sands fossil footprints?
faq.a: Ice-age trackways of people and megafauna on Lake Otero - "the largest collection of fossilized human footprints", showing humans here "at least 23,000 years ago". "Currently the footprints at White Sands are inaccessible", but an exhibit of "casted human footprints" opened at the visitor center in January 2024.
