name: Carlsbad Caverns National Park
line: The Big Room and the evening bat flight

jewels.name: Big Room Trail
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov timed entry (recreation.gov/ticket/facility/234637) or 877-444-6777; $15 entrance paid at the visitor center
jewels.blurb: "the largest single cave chamber by volume in North America"; a "relatively flat" 1.25-mile (2 km) trail of "about 1.5 hours", or a 0.6-mile, 45-minute shortcut; "cave formations of all shapes and sizes, and a rope ladder used by explorers in 1924"; reached by elevator.

jewels.name: Bat Flight Program
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free, first come first served
jewels.blurb: "Enjoy a ranger program and watch thousands of bats emerge from Carlsbad Cavern": Brazilian free-tailed bats, every evening April through October, at the amphitheater "about a five minute walk from the visitor center"; "The program is free and you do not need reservations"; no electronic devices of any kind.

jewels.name: Natural Entrance Trail
jewels.blurb: 1.25 miles (2 km), about one hour, "extremely steep" - about "750 feet (229 m)—equivalent to walking up or down a 75-story building"; past "Devil's Spring, the Whale's Mouth, and Iceberg Rock"; "not recommended for visitors with heart or respiratory conditions"; last hike-in 2:30 pm.

jewels.name: Dawn bat return
jewels.blurb: Early risers (around 4-6 a.m.) watch bats "re-enter the cavern with spectacular dives from heights of hundreds of feet. Individual bats may reach speeds of 25 mph (40 km/h) or more."

jewels.name: King's Palace ranger-guided tour
jewels.blurb: Listed on Recreation.gov at "$10:00" adult and "$5:00" for ages 6-15, "available through the park website"; ⚠️ the NPS fees page reads "All tours are temporarily suspended until further notice."

jewels.name: Ranger star viewing and night hikes
jewels.booking_route: none needed - register at the visitor center desk on the day for night hikes
jewels.blurb: "Come explore the night sky through the eye of a powerful telescope. Park rangers will point out space objects near and far"; free. Night hikes: 1.5 miles round trip after the Bat Flight, age 8+, maximum 12, long pants and red-light headlamps required; "More dates to be announced".

jewels.name: Surface desert trails
jewels.blurb: Eleven named routes from the Walnut Canyon Overlook and Chihuahuan Desert Nature Trail to Old Guano Trail, Slaughter Canyon, Yucca Canyon and the Guadalupe Ridge Trail; ⚠️ Guadalupe Ridge (visitor center to Slaughter Canyon Trail), Rattlesnake Canyon and Juniper Ridge are closed by flood damage.

jewels.name: Rattlesnake Springs
jewels.blurb: "Enjoy an oasis of plants and wildlife in a serene setting. You can hear an see a variety of birds that make Rattlesnake Springs their home"; picnic tables under large cottonwoods, accessible restrooms; open from half an hour before sunrise to half an hour after sunset; about 15 miles (24 km) from the visitor center.

jewels.name: Walnut Canyon Desert Drive
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free park road (currently closed)
jewels.blurb: "Explore the stories of ancient life, people of the past, and desert survival on a one hour scenic drive": 9.5 miles one-way, unpaved, closed to RVs, buses and trailers; ⚠️ closed - "Recent flooding has caused major damage to the road. It is unknown when repairs will begin".

jewels.name: Backcountry camping by free permit
jewels.booking_route: free permit at the visitor center on the day; not reservable
jewels.blurb: "Only backcountry camping is permitted in the park. Overnight RV parking or car camping is not allowed"; a "free backcountry use permit at the visitor center on the day of arrival (no advanced reservations issued)"; groups up to 10, maximum seven consecutive nights; "no reliable water source in the park's backcountry".

jewels.name: Carlsbad Caverns Trading Company restaurant
jewels.blurb: In the visitor center past the gift shop: "limited food options and bottled, fountain, and hot drinks", "open until 3 pm"; the same concessioner runs the $15-a-day kennel (575-785-2281). No food in the cave: "Any consumption of food and drink, except plain, unflavored water, is prohibited in any cave."

jewels.name: Cavern kit: lug-sole shoes and a light jacket
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI.com via AvantLink)
jewels.blurb: The NPS list: "Closed-toe shoes with good traction (e.g. lug soles) are recommended"; "bring a light jacket or sweater as the year-round temperature in the cavern is about 56ºF (13ºC)"; plain water only - "No flavored water or drinks"; strollers not permitted, "baby backpacks are suggested".

jewels.name: Desert hike kit: water and sun protection
jewels.blurb: For the surface trails the NPS says bring "Water (2 quarts (1.9 L) per two hiking hours)" and "Sun protection (for eyes and skin)"; "there is no reliable water source in the park's backcountry. Pack plenty of water—at least one gallon (3.8 L) per person per day."

jewels.name: Night-hike kit: red-light headlamp and long pants
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI.com via AvantLink)
jewels.blurb: For ranger night hikes on "unimproved, dimly-lit trails" with thorny vegetation: "Long pants mandatory; no open-toed shoes; bring water and red light headlamps"; star viewers are asked to "use red lens flashlights to preserve night vision."

jewels.name: Whites City
jewels.blurb: The park turn-off: "Turn north from US Hwy 62/180 at White's City"; the NPS notes "A campground and amenities are available seven miles (11 km) from the visitor center in White's City, New Mexico."

jewels.name: Whites City RV Park
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce at "19 Carlsbad Caverns Hwy", (575) 361-3665 - the campground the NPS places in Whites City, seven miles from the visitor center. Its own site was not reached (whitescity.com is a parked domain), so nothing else is stated here.

jewels.name: Whites City Cavern Inn
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce under Whites City at "17 Carlsbad Cavern Hwy", (855) 516-1090 - the closest listed rooms to the park gate.

jewels.name: Cactus Cafe
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce among locally owned restaurants at "26 Carlsbad Caverns Hwy, Whites City NM" - the eat stop at the park turn-off.

jewels.name: Carlsbad
jewels.blurb: The gateway city "about 20 miles (32 km) south" of which the park turn-off lies; the NPS sends visitors to "the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce at 575-887-6516" for lodging and dining; local airport with rental cars and taxi service; Greyhound and TNM&O bus lines.

jewels.name: Trinity Hotel
jewels.blurb: "built in 1892 as the First National Bank", later "the historic headquarters of the Carlsbad Irrigation District"; "nine luxurious hotel suites"; afternoon wine tasting "featuring our own Spirit of Seven Rivers varieties made right here along the Pecos Valley"; 201 South Canal St, 575-234-9891.

jewels.name: The Trinity restaurant
jewels.blurb: In the 1892 bank building: "breakfast, lunch and dinner Tuesday-Sunday", "classic dishes and our amazing green chile cheeseburger" and "traditional American Italian dishes like lasagna, chicken parmigiana"; daily wine tasting.

jewels.name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott Carlsbad
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce at "2525 S. Canal St", (575) 887-8000. Marriott's own page was not fetched (brand pages return 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: TownePlace Suites Carlsbad
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce at "311 Pompa St", (575) 689-8850. Marriott's own page was not fetched (brand pages return 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Hampton Inn & Suites by Hilton Carlsbad
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce at "120 Esperanza Circle", (575) 725-5700. Hilton's own page was not fetched (brand pages return 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express Carlsbad
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce at "2210 W Pierce St", (575) 234-1252. IHG's own page was not fetched (brand pages return 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Candlewood Suites Carlsbad
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce at "3711 San Jose Blvd", (575) 941-3711. IHG's own page was not fetched (brand pages return 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Brantley Lake State Park
jewels.blurb: "Located fifteen miles North of Carlsbad", "the southernmost lake in New Mexico": 51 developed campsites - 38 water and electric (30 amp), 10 water and electric (50 amp), 3 full hookup (50 amp) - plus shoreline and boat-in primitive camping; boating, kayaking, fishing and "exceptional bird watching".

jewels.name: Bud's Place RV Park
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce under RV Parks/Campgrounds at "900 Standpipe Rd", (888) 204-4470. Its own site was not fetched, so nothing else is stated here.

jewels.name: Ellipse Global Lodge & RV Park
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce under RV Parks/Campgrounds at "26 Quahada Rd.", (575) 649-3883. Its own site refused the connection, so nothing else is stated here.

jewels.name: Living Desert Zoo and Gardens State Park
jewels.blurb: "This native wildlife zoo exhibits more than 40 species of animals and hundreds of species of plants native to the Chihuahuan Desert" - bald eagles, mountain lions, wolves and black bears; 1504 Skyline Dr., Carlsbad; 9 am-5 pm, last entry 3:30 pm; adults $10, children 7-12 $5, 6 and under free.

jewels.name: Guadalupe Mountains National Park
jewels.booking_route: none needed to visit; campgrounds per the NPS
jewels.blurb: "the world's most extensive Permian fossil reef, the four highest peaks in Texas"; Carlsbad's visitor site places it "55 miles away across the Texas border" with "two campgrounds" offering individual and group sites.

jewels.name: Guadalupe Mountain Brewing Co.
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce among member restaurants at "3324 National Parks Hwy" - on the highway toward the park. Its own site timed out (HTTP 522), so nothing else is stated here.

jewels.name: Blue House Bakery & Cafe
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce among member restaurants at "609 N Canyon St.", Carlsbad.

jewels.name: Red Chimney BBQ
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce among member restaurants at "817 N. Canal St.", Carlsbad.

jewels.name: Lucky Bull Grill
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce among member restaurants at "220 W. Fox St.", Carlsbad.

jewels.name: Flume at Stevens Inn
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce among member restaurants at "1829 S. Canal St.", the address of the Stevens Inn on the same Chamber's lodging list.

jewels.name: Lucy's Mexicali
jewels.blurb: Listed by the Carlsbad Chamber of Commerce among member restaurants at "710 S. Canal St.", Carlsbad.

faq.q: Do you need reservations for Carlsbad Caverns National Park?
faq.a: Yes, for the cavern: "A timed entry reservation must be purchased to access Carlsbad Cavern" ($1.00, required year-round). Recreation.gov releases tickets "30 days in advance at 8 AM MT" and "The park does not offer stand-by or wait list tickets."

faq.q: How much does it cost to go to Carlsbad Caverns National Park?
faq.a: "Adults 16 years and older are $15, children 15 and younger are free. There are additional fees for guided tours." The timed-entry reservation adds $1.00.

faq.q: Can you camp at Carlsbad Caverns National Park?
faq.a: Only in the backcountry: "Carlsbad Caverns National Park offers no overnight lodging or campgrounds." "Primitive camping is allowed in the backcountry only, and requires a free permit which is issued at the park's visitor center when you arrive (not reservable in advance)." A campground is available in White's City, seven miles from the visitor center.

faq.q: How long does it take to tour Carlsbad Caverns?
faq.a: The Big Room Trail is 1.25 miles and takes "about 1.5 hours (on average)", or 45 minutes on the 0.6-mile shortcut; the Natural Entrance Trail is 1.25 miles and "about one hour". With limited time, the NPS suggests: "Enter and exit the cavern by elevator and walk the Big Room Trail."

faq.q: What should I wear to Carlsbad Caverns?
faq.a: "Closed-toe shoes with good traction (e.g. lug soles) are recommended", and "You may want to bring a light jacket or sweater as the year-round temperature in the cavern is about 56ºF (13ºC)."

faq.q: Is Carlsbad Caverns National Park dog friendly?
faq.a: Only in a limited way: "Pets are not allowed in the cavern, on unpaved park trails on the surface, off road, during the Bat Flight Program, or in the visitor center." A concession kennel charges "$15/day", 9:00 am-3:30 pm.

faq.q: What is the closest airport to Carlsbad Caverns National Park?
faq.a: Carlsbad has a local airport with rental cars and taxi service. The NPS lists Roswell at 103 miles, El Paso at 151 miles, Midland at 194 miles and Albuquerque at 304 miles.

faq.q: Can you take pictures in Carlsbad Caverns?
faq.a: "Yes, and you may use a flash. Tripods, bipods, and monopods are prohibited." At the Bat Flight Program, though, "Electronic devices are not allowed", including "cameras of any kind".

faq.q: Is Carlsbad Caverns National Park open on Thanksgiving?
faq.a: No: "The park is open every day, except Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's days, weather and road conditions permitting."

faq.q: What are Carlsbad Caverns National Park's hours?
faq.a: Visitor center "9 am–5 pm". The last cavern entrance ticket is sold at 2:15 pm and the last cavern entrance is 2:30 pm; the elevator runs in 9:30 am-2:30 pm, and the "Last Elevator OUT of the Cavern" is 4:45 pm.

name: Petrified Forest National Park
line: Painted Desert, petrified logs and Route 66

jewels.name: Painted Desert overlooks
jewels.booking_route: none needed - roadside overlooks inside the park (park entrance fee applies)
jewels.blurb: "Enjoy spectacular views of the Painted Desert from several overlooks in this area"; Kachina Point at the Painted Desert Inn overlooks the red Painted Desert. Westbound I-40 drivers "take Exit 311, drive the 28 miles through the park and connect with Highway 180 at the south end".

jewels.name: Blue Mesa
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park trail and loop road
jewels.blurb: "Walk the 1 mi (1.6 km) trail and/or drive the 3.5 mi (5.6 km) loop road to explore colorful geology."

jewels.name: Crystal Forest
jewels.blurb: "Many petrified logs glimmer with quartz crystals along a paved 0.75 mi (1.2 km) loop trail." Taking wood is prohibited: "Although it seems as if there is an endless supply of petrified wood here, it is limited."

jewels.name: Historic Route 66 alignment
jewels.booking_route: none needed - roadside pull-out on the park road
jewels.blurb: "A 1932 Studebaker sits where famed Route 66 once cut through the park." "Petrified Forest National Park is the only park in the National Park System containing a section of Historic Route 66"; "A line of telephone poles still marks the road bed of Historic Route 66 within the park."

jewels.name: Painted Desert Inn National Historic Landmark
jewels.booking_route: none needed - museum inside the park (park entrance fee applies)
jewels.blurb: "This trading post turned inn turned museum offers exhibits on the park's recent human history." Built of petrified wood and native stone by Herbert David Lore (registered 1924), rebuilt by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s, reopened "in the late 1940s under the renowned Fred Harvey Company" with interiors by Mary Colter and dining-room murals by "renowned Hopi artist" Fred Kabotie; a National Historic Landmark since 1987. Open 9am to 4pm.

jewels.name: Newspaper Rock
jewels.booking_route: none needed - overlook on the park road
jewels.blurb: "Look down from an overlook to see over 650 petroglyphs, some as old as 2000 years."

jewels.name: Puerco Pueblo
jewels.blurb: "View ancestral Puebloan homes and petroglyphs along a 0.3 mi (0.5 km) loop trail." Accessible restroom on site.

jewels.name: Agate Bridge
jewels.blurb: "See a 110 ft (34 m) petrified log spanning a gully."

jewels.name: Rainbow Forest Museum and Giant Logs Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - museum and trail at the south entrance
jewels.blurb: "Study paleontological exhibits in the museum and walk a 0.4 mi (0.6 km) loop trail." The demonstration lab, where paleontologists prepare fossils, is "Open Thursday, Friday, and Saturday 9 am-12 pm and 1 pm-4 pm"; touch tables and open-captioned films.

jewels.name: Long Logs and Agate House
jewels.blurb: "A 2.6 mi (4.2 km) trail showcases some of the longest, most colorful petrified logs in the park and a partially reconstructed pueblo originally built of petrified wood."

jewels.name: Jasper Forest
jewels.booking_route: none needed - overlook on the park road
jewels.blurb: "Enjoy a panoramic view of an area with a high concentration of petrified wood."

jewels.name: Wilderness backpacking by free permit
jewels.booking_route: free same-day permit in person at a visitor center
jewels.blurb: "The backpacking wilderness permit is free. You may obtain it in person from either visitor centers, Painted Desert Inn or Rainbow Forest Museum, on the day that you want to backpack." "The permits are available until 4:30 pm." "Group camping is limited to 8"; camp "at least a half mile from your vehicle"; "No wood or charcoal fires are allowed. Please use fuel stoves."

jewels.name: Painted Desert Visitor Center
jewels.booking_route: none needed - north entrance off I-40 Exit 311
jewels.blurb: "Stop for historic architecture, information, bookstore, gift shop, food, and gas." Open 8am to 5pm; open-captioned park film; BARK Ranger certificates for dogs.

jewels.name: Painted Desert Diner
jewels.booking_route: walk-in at the Painted Desert Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: "The Painted Desert Diner and a convenience store for snacks are located next to the Painted Desert Visitor Center." "Limited snacks are also available for purchase at the curio shop in Rainbow Forest." Accessible restroom at the diner.

jewels.name: Kit for the desert drive and trails
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates) - nothing is sold by the park
jewels.blurb: The park's own list: "Take all the water you will need when traveling through the park and when hiking... One gallon per person per day is recommended during summer months when hiking." "Wear sunscreen to protect yourself from the Arizona sun. The sun's rays are stronger due to the high elevations." "Be prepared! There is no water and little shade in the backcountry."

jewels.name: Kit for a wilderness overnight
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates) - nothing is sold by the park
jewels.blurb: The backpacking rules set the kit: water at "One gallon per person per day is recommended during summer months"; "No wood or charcoal fires are allowed. Please use fuel stoves"; camp "at least a half mile from your vehicle". "Temperatures vary greatly from extreme heat to bitter cold. Be prepared for rapidly changing conditions."

jewels.name: Wigwam Motel
jewels.booking_route: own website booking (Book Now) or reservations@sleepinawigwam.com; "24 hour cancellation policy"
jewels.blurb: 811 W Hopi Dr, Holbrook: "Fifteen white concrete teepees built in 1950", "one of only a handful of wigwam villages left on Route 66"; "Built By Chester Evert Lewis" and "Currently Operated By His Family" as Wigwam Village #6. Queen Bed Wigwam $105 a night plus tax, Double Full Wigwam $115. Discover Holbrook: "Reserve as early as you can." (928) 524-3048.

jewels.name: La Posada Hotel
jewels.blurb: 303 East 2nd Street, Route 66, Winslow: "In 1930, La Posada (The Resting Place) opened to great acclaim as the crown jewel of the Fred Harvey series of luxury railroad hotels"; architect Mary E.J. Colter "considered it to be her finest work." 1-928-289-4366.

jewels.name: The Turquoise Room
jewels.blurb: La Posada's restaurant "serves regional contemporary Southwestern cuisine and is considered by many to be the finest restaurant in the Four Corners region."

jewels.name: Holbrook - Petrified Forest KOA Journey
jewels.booking_route: koa.com online reservations (not fetched - HTTP 403) or (928) 524-6689
jewels.blurb: 102 Hermosa Dr., Holbrook: 119 sites; "30 Amp," "50 Amp," and "Full Hookups"; pull-throughs to "100 feet", maximum vehicle 85 feet; pool, dog park, playground, laundry, showers, store. "Easy access to I-40 gets you to the Painted Desert and Petrified Forest National Park (20 minutes)." (928) 524-6689. koa.com refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so this is sourced to Campendium.

jewels.name: OK RV Park
jewels.blurb: 1576 Roadrunner Rd., Holbrook: "30 Amp, 50 Amp, Full Hookups, Water, Sewer"; "Picnic tables, Pull thru, Big rigs", recreation hall, laundry, showers, dog walk and free wifi; 80 campsites, rigs to 45 feet; accepts "AAA, Good Sam, FMCA, AARP, Military Discounts". Local First Arizona: "well-equipped haven for RV enthusiasts passing through Holbrook. Pets welcome!" (928) 524-3226.

jewels.name: Gateway to the Petrified Forest RV Resort
jewels.blurb: 7551 Ramada Rd., Holbrook: 31 full-hookup pull-through RV sites and 7 tent sites, 30 and 50 amp, rigs to 45 feet, general store and community fire pit; "22 miles from Petrified Forest National Park"; open year-round. (928) 524-2002.

jewels.name: Homolovi State Park
jewels.booking_route: Arizona State Parks reservations (azstateparks.com/reserve) or same day by phone 928-289-4106
jewels.blurb: I-40 Exit 257, 1.5 mi. N on Hwy 87: "'Homolovi' is Hopi for 'Place of the Little Hills' - the traditional name for Winslow, Arizona"; a research center for late Hopi migration (1200s to late 1300s) with a campground. "Homolovi State Park no longer accepts self-pay registrations for camping. Same-day reservations can be made by coming to the visitor center in person or by calling the park office at 928-289-4106 by 4:45 p.m." Entry $10 per vehicle (1 person), $20 (2-4 people).

jewels.name: Holbrook
jewels.blurb: "Holbrook is a small Route 66 town in northeastern Arizona and the county seat of Navajo County, sitting right off Interstate 40." "The Painted Desert entrance is about 26 miles from town off I-40 and the Rainbow Forest entrance is about 20 miles south on Highway 180." The NPS route from eastbound I-40: "take Exit 285 into Holbrook then travel 19 miles on Highway 180 South to the park's south entrance".

jewels.name: Navajo County Historic Courthouse Museum
jewels.blurb: Holbrook: "Built in 1898 of rough native stone".

jewels.name: Jim Gray's Petrified Wood Co.
jewels.blurb: Holbrook, "on Highway 180 just south of downtown" - the legal way to take petrified wood home: the NPS says "Souvenirs are available at local gift shops", since collecting in the park is prohibited.

jewels.name: Big Fella's BBQ
jewels.blurb: Holbrook: "real-deal, slow-smoked Texas brisket right on Route 66".

jewels.name: Colonel Mustard Hot Dogs
jewels.blurb: Holbrook: "proper Chicago-style dogs out of a beautifully restored 1958 Richfield station".

jewels.name: Mesa Italiana
jewels.blurb: Holbrook: "hand-tossed pizza and hearty Italian classics".

jewels.name: Wayside Soda Shop
jewels.blurb: Holbrook: an "old-fashioned soda fountain open only on Wednesdays".

jewels.name: Studio 66 Cafe
jewels.blurb: Holbrook: a "family-run coffee bar with a drive-through and a bakery case".

jewels.name: Route Sixty Sips
jewels.blurb: Holbrook: a coffee shop pouring Route 66-themed drinks.

jewels.name: Arizona Sake
jewels.blurb: Holbrook: a "tiny one-man brewery" offering private tastings.

faq.q: How much is it to get into Petrified Forest National Park?
faq.a: A private vehicle is "$25.00" and admits "one private, non-commercial vehicle (15-passenger capacity or less) and all occupants. Valid for 7 days." A motorcycle is $20 and a person on foot or bicycle $15, with "Youth 15 and under" free. "This park does not accept cash."

faq.q: Can you drive through Petrified Forest National Park?
faq.a: Yes: "The drive through the park is 28 miles. Driving the road at the posted speed limit without stopping takes about an hour." The main road takes larger vehicles and trailers, though some pull-outs are small.

faq.q: How long does it take to visit Petrified Forest National Park?
faq.a: "Most visitors spend 2 to 3 hours enjoying the park, while others sometime return over multiple days."

faq.q: Can you camp in Petrified Forest National Park?
faq.a: Only by backpacking. "There is no RV, car, or front country camping in the park. There is no boondocking, dispersed or 'primitive' camping." Backpackers hike into the Petrified Forest National Wilderness Area on a permit that "is free" and is issued until 4:30 pm.

faq.q: What time can you enter Petrified Forest National Park?
faq.a: "Park hours are 8am to 5pm." "The park is open year round except Thanksgiving and Christmas."

faq.q: What time zone is Petrified Forest National Park in?
faq.a: "Times are Mountain Standard year round. Most of Arizona does not observe Daylight Saving."

faq.q: Is Petrified Forest National Park dog friendly?
faq.a: Yes: "Pets are allowed everywhere in the park except inside buildings. Pets must be on a leash, no longer than six feet, and the owner must clean up after their pet." Visitor centers offer BARK Ranger certificates.

faq.q: How far is Petrified Forest National Park from Phoenix?
faq.a: The NPS gives "259 miles" from Phoenix by Interstates 17 North and 40 East through Flagstaff, or "215 miles" from the east side of Phoenix by Highways 87, 260, 377 and 180.

faq.q: What is the closest major airport to Petrified Forest National Park?
faq.a: The NPS lists major airports in Phoenix, Arizona and Albuquerque, New Mexico; smaller airports in Flagstaff and Show Low, Arizona and Gallup, New Mexico; and a small airport in Holbrook. "There is no public transportation to or within the park."

faq.q: Can you hike in Petrified Forest National Park?
faq.a: Yes - short loops such as Blue Mesa (1 mile), Crystal Forest (0.75 mile, paved) and Giant Logs (0.4 mile), the 2.6-mile Long Logs and Agate House trail, and for a full day "Choose an Off the Beaten Path hike" or go "backpacking in the park Wilderness Area."

faq.q: Do I need a reservation to enter Zion National Park?
faq.a: No. The NPS states you do not need a permit or reservation to enter the park or ride the shuttles. Permits are required for specific activities such as Angels Landing past Scout Lookout and wilderness trips.

faq.q: How do I get an Angels Landing permit?
faq.a: Through a seasonal lottery (four windows a year; for December 1 to February 28 it opens October 1 and closes October 20) or a day-before lottery open 12:01 am to 3 pm MT daily. The application is $6 for up to 6 people, plus $3 per person if selected.

faq.q: Can I drive my own car through Zion Canyon?
faq.a: Not while the shuttles run. Personal vehicles are prohibited on the Zion Canyon Scenic Drive during shuttle season; only Zion Lodge guests with reservations get access codes to drive to the lodge.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to hike the Narrows?
faq.a: Not for the bottom-up hike from the Temple of Sinawava. The 16-mile top-down hike from Chamberlain's Ranch needs a wilderness permit. The Narrows closes to all travel above 150 CFS and during flash flood warnings.

faq.q: How much does it cost to enter Zion?
faq.a: $35 per private vehicle for 1-7 days, $20 per person on foot or bike (15 and under free), or $70 for a Zion Annual Pass. Non-US residents 16 and older pay an additional $100 from January 1, 2026.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Zion?
faq.a: The NPS describes fall as offering the same scenery at a slightly calmer pace, with visitation dropping more dramatically in November. Summer is the busiest season with temperatures regularly over 100°F.

faq.q: Do you need a reservation to enter Bryce Canyon National Park?
faq.a: No. The NPS says you don't need a reservation to enter the park. Campsites are different: there are no first-come, first-served sites, and reservations must be made on recreation.gov.

faq.q: How much does it cost to visit Bryce Canyon?
faq.a: $35 per private vehicle, $30 per motorcycle, or $20 per person on foot or bicycle. Non-US residents aged 16 and over pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless admitted with an annual or America the Beautiful pass. The park does not accept cash.

faq.q: When does the Bryce Canyon shuttle run?
faq.a: In 2026, from 3 April to 18 October. It is free with park admission, serves about 15 stops through the amphitheater area, and buses typically arrive every 15 minutes.

faq.q: What is the best hike at Bryce Canyon for a first visit?
faq.a: The NPS names the Queen's Garden and Navajo Combination Loop as the most popular hike and recommends it for first-time visitors: 2.9 miles, 2 to 3 hours, 625 feet of elevation gain, rated moderate.

faq.q: When is the Bryce Canyon Astronomy Festival?
faq.a: 11 to 13 June 2026, with an astrophotography workshop starting the evening of 10 June. Attending is free with park admission; some events require advance sign-up.

faq.q: Is Bryce Canyon open in winter?
faq.a: Yes. The park is open 24 hours a day all year. North Campground stays open, Sunset Campground closes from November into April, and the Lodge closes in winter though lodging often remains available at the Sunset Lodge Unit.

faq.q: Do I need a timed-entry reservation for Arches in 2026?
faq.a: No. The NPS states that in 2026 advanced timed-entry reservations will not be required and visitors may enter at any time during operating hours. Vehicles may be diverted when areas become too congested, and reservations are still required for Devils Garden Campground and for self-guided and ranger-led Fiery Furnace hikes.

faq.q: How do I get into the Fiery Furnace?
faq.a: Two ways, both reserved in advance: a ranger-led hike ($16 per person, April 12 through early fall, tickets on Recreation.gov) or a self-guided permit ($10 per person, limited numbers each day). Children under 5 are not permitted.

faq.q: Can I camp inside Arches?
faq.a: Yes, at Devils Garden Campground. Sites are reservable for nights between March 1 and October 31 and are first-come, first-served in November and February; $25 a night for 1-10 campers. The NPS says that without a reservation you will probably have to look outside the park.

faq.q: How long is the Delicate Arch hike?
faq.a: The NPS gives 3 miles (4.8 km) round trip with a 480-foot (146 m) climb, steadily uphill, and advises considering summer heat or winter ice and your own fitness before starting.

faq.q: When is Arches least crowded?
faq.a: The NPS says peak congestion runs spring through fall from 8 am to 3 pm, that late afternoon and evening offer sunsets and reduced crowding, and that in summer many trailhead lots fill by 7:30 am.

faq.q: Is Arches a dark sky park?
faq.a: Yes. The NPS states Arches was certified as an International Dark Sky Park in 2019, and names Balanced Rock Picnic Area, the Windows Section, Garden of Eden Viewpoint and Panorama Point for stargazing.

faq.q: How much is the entrance fee at Capitol Reef?
faq.a: The NPS lists $20 for a private vehicle, $15 for a motorcycle and $10 per person on foot or bicycle (under 16 free), valid seven days, or $35 for a Capitol Reef annual pass.

faq.q: Can I get a site at Fruita Campground without a reservation?
faq.a: The NPS states the campground has a 100% reservation system, that reservations open 6 months ahead, and that sites are full several months in advance. Cancelled reservations can be booked, even the same day, on Recreation.gov.

faq.q: Can I pick fruit in the Fruita orchards?
faq.a: Yes, in season, in orchards posted with U-Pick Fruit signs; fruit taken must be paid for at the self-pay station. The NPS gives approximate harvests of apricots late June to mid-July, peaches late July to early September, pears early August to early September and apples mid-August to mid-October.

faq.q: Is the Capitol Gorge road open?
faq.a: Not on the date of this build: the NPS road table updated 9/30/2026 lists Capitol Gorge as Closed. The Scenic Drive and Grand Wash are listed 2WD.

faq.q: Do I need a 4x4 for Cathedral Valley?
faq.a: The NPS says high-clearance vehicles can usually manage the roads, but the loop requires fording the Fremont River and conditions vary with weather. On 10/1/2026 it listed Cathedral Valley as HC4WD to Gypsum Sinkhole and Hartnet Road as likely impassable.

faq.q: When can I buy pie at the Gifford House?
faq.a: The NPS says the Gifford House store and museum is open March 14 (Pi Day) through late November, daily 9 am to 4:30 pm, and sells locally baked fruit pies and homemade ice cream.

jewels.booking_route: none needed - park trail (park entrance fee applies)
jewels.blurb: Island in the Sky, EASY, 0.6 miles round trip, about 30 minutes: "A short hike leads to a cliff-edge arch. Mesa Arch is a classic sunrise spot and is popular among photographers."

jewels.booking_route: none needed - park trail (park entrance fee applies)
jewels.blurb: Island in the Sky, EASY, 1.8 miles round trip, about 1.5 hours: "A stunning out-and-back trail, this walk showcases spectacular panoramic views as it follows the canyon edge." Ranger programs are offered at Grand View Point.

jewels.booking_route: entrance fee at the gate ($30 per vehicle, card only)
jewels.blurb: "The Island in the Sky mesa rests on sheer sandstone cliffs over 1,000 feet (304 m) above the surrounding terrain." About 40 minutes' drive from Moab by US 191 and UT 313; the visitor center "is open year-round, seven days a week, with some closed days in winter."

jewels.name: White Rim Road
jewels.booking_route: permit on Recreation.gov (overnight: $36 reservation fee plus $5 per person per night)
jewels.blurb: "The 100-mile White Rim Road loops around and below the Island in the Sky mesa top" and needs "high-clearance, four-wheel-drive vehicles"; "All vehicles, motorbikes, and bicyclists must have a day-use permit for single day trips on the White Rim." Overnight trips use "20 individual campsites arranged in 10 camping areas". The Shafer Trail and Mineral Bottom switchbacks "require extreme caution."

jewels.booking_route: entrance fee at the gate ($30 per vehicle, card only)
jewels.blurb: "named for the colorful spires of Cedar Mesa Sandstone"; trails and roads "lead to such features as Tower Ruin, Confluence Overlook, Elephant Hill, the Joint Trail, and Chesler Park." Reached by UT 211, 14 miles north of Monticello on US 191 then about 35 miles west; the visitor center "is open daily, spring through fall."

jewels.name: Chesler Park Viewpoint
jewels.blurb: The Needles, STRENUOUS, 5.8 miles round trip, 3-4 hours: "This popular trail leads to a pass overlooking a scenic expanse of desert grasses and shrubs surrounded by sandstone spires."

jewels.name: Druid Arch
jewels.blurb: The Needles, STRENUOUS, 10.8 miles round trip, 5-7 hours: "This trail offers one of the most spectacular views in The Needles", following Elephant Canyon "through deep sand and loose rock."

jewels.name: Cave Spring Trail
jewels.blurb: The Needles, EASY/MODERATE, 0.6-mile loop, about 45 minutes: "This short loop leads to a historic cowboy camp and prehistoric rock paintings and peckings. You will climb two ladders to complete the route."

jewels.name: Upheaval Dome
jewels.blurb: Island in the Sky, MODERATE, 0.6 miles to the first overlook, about 30 minutes: "A short but steep trail leads to a clear view into Upheaval Dome. Exhibits at the end of the trail discuss this unique geologic feature."

jewels.name: Aztec Butte
jewels.blurb: Island in the Sky, MODERATE, 1.4 miles round trip, about 1.5 hours, 225 feet of elevation change; the trail forks to "spectacular views" and to "ancestral Puebloan structures."

jewels.name: Whale Rock
jewels.blurb: Island in the Sky, MODERATE, 0.8 miles round trip, about 1 hour: "This trail leads up the side of a sandstone dome, ending with broad views."

jewels.name: The Maze and Hans Flat Ranger Station
jewels.blurb: "The Maze is the least accessible district of Canyonlands"; "Rarely do visitors spend less than three days in the Maze". Hans Flat Ranger Station, 2.5 hours from Green River, "is open to the public 8 am to 4 pm daily"; from there the canyons are "another 3 to 6 hours by high-clearance, four-wheel-drive vehicle." "There are no services, food, gas, or potable water sources in The Maze."

jewels.name: Horseshoe Canyon guided hikes
jewels.booking_route: ranger-led; no booking route on the page read
jewels.blurb: Part of The Maze district: "The Maze offers guided hikes in Horseshoe Canyon most weekends during spring and fall."

jewels.name: Cataract Canyon
jewels.booking_route: guided trip with a licensed outfitter, or a private river permit on Recreation.gov
jewels.blurb: "Cataract Canyon contains 14 miles of rapids that range in difficulty up to Class V" - a "fourteen-mile stretch of Class III to V whitewater" where the combined flow of the Green and Colorado "spills down ... with remarkable speed and power." "Some companies offer guided whitewater river trips that vary in length from one to many days."

jewels.name: Flatwater on the Green and Colorado
jewels.booking_route: river permit on Recreation.gov; canoe shuttles from Moab outfitters
jewels.blurb: "Flatwater trips may float down either the Colorado or Green rivers as far as Spanish Bottom", with "miles and miles of flatwater perfect for canoes, sea kayaks and other shallow-water boats." Permits are required for all day-use and overnight river trips.

jewels.name: Island in the Sky Campground (Willow Flat)
jewels.blurb: "Island in the Sky Campground (Willow Flat) has 12 sites, first-come, first-served." "Nightly camping fee is $15 per site." "Sites fill quickly spring through fall." "There is no water at the campground"; vehicles up to 28 feet. Open year-round.

jewels.name: The Needles Campground
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov for reservable sites; first-come for the rest
jewels.blurb: "The Needles Campground has 26 sites with fire rings, picnic tables, bathrooms, and running water." "You can reserve some individual sites and all group sites at The Needles." $20 a night; group sites $70 to $225. No RV hookups; RVs up to about 28 feet.

jewels.name: Overnight backcountry permits
jewels.blurb: Backpacking, four-wheel-drive and mountain-bike permits on Recreation.gov, opening four months before each season at 8 am MT; "a non-refundable $36 reservation fee for each permit" plus "$5 per person, per night". "Overnight permits are very competitive for White Rim trips in spring and fall and Needles backpacking trips in spring."

jewels.name: Kit for desert heat and water
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates) - nothing is sold by the park
jewels.blurb: The park's own guidance: carry "at least 2-3 liters per person for front country hikes, and 4 liters or more for backcountry"; "Plan your activities during the cooler parts of the day (early morning or late evening)". The hiking page adds: "Avoid hiking during peak heat on summer days" and "Carry a flashlight, map, and basic first aid equipment."

jewels.name: Kit for navigation, layers and footing
jewels.booking_route: affiliate retail referral (REI.com via AvantLink; Amazon Associates) - park maps are sold in the visitor center bookstores
jewels.blurb: "Download park maps for offline use" and "bring a physical park map and compass as a backup"; "Bring or dress in layers to adapt to changing conditions, especially if camping in fall, winter, or spring"; "Footwear with good tread that can keep traction on uneven terrain." In The Maze, visitors need "the proper equipment or gear for self-rescue."

jewels.name: Dead Horse Point State Park
jewels.booking_route: Utah State Parks online reservations (link on the park page)
jewels.blurb: Utah state park on the road to Island in the Sky: "An immense desert landscape of canyons, high desert woodland, and miles of trails", known for sunrises, sunsets and dark skies. Camping and two sets of yurts - "Pets are not allowed in the Wingate Yurts" but "Moenkopi Yurts are pet friendly"; day passes sold online.

jewels.name: Under Canvas Moab
jewels.blurb: "just seven miles north of Moab, near Utah's famed Canyonlands and Arches national parks" - about 25 minutes from the Island in the Sky entrance; Deluxe, Stargazer, Suite and Safari tents and kids' tents; pet-friendly for a small nightly fee; an International DarkSky-certified resort. 2026 season March 5 - November 1; 2027 March 4 - October 31.

jewels.name: Needles Outpost
jewels.blurb: "Rustic camping a stone's throw from Needles District", 1.5 miles from the Needles visitor center - "the closest camping to the park": dry tent and RV sites, "The Mo'Rockin Bell Tent" with a queen bed, and a group site for up to 15. "Camping is open 1 March to 20 November. Spring and fall weekends book up early." Store open March 15 - November 15.

jewels.name: Moab RV and Glamping Resort
jewels.blurb: Moab: 43 RV sites with full hookups, 28-foot to 65-foot pull-through and back-in, "30/50 Amp"; 25 cabins, glamping tents and tipis with "heat, AC, tvs, and more"; "Pet-friendly for a fee". About 60 minutes from Island in the Sky per the listing.

jewels.name: BLM campgrounds around Moab
jewels.booking_route: first-come cash at the campground; Ken's Lake on Recreation.gov
jewels.blurb: The BLM "maintains 26 campgrounds in the Moab area"; most are "first-come/first-served basis and no reservations are accepted", except Ken's Lake (10 miles south of Moab) and some group sites on Recreation.gov. "All individual sites are $20/night. Pay at the campground with exact cash"; "drinking water is NOT available"; stays limited to 14 days in 30.

jewels.name: Hyatt Place Moab
jewels.blurb: The hotel's own domain hyattplacemoab.com redirects (HTTP 301) to Hyatt's property page "hyatt.com/en-US/hotel/utah/hyatt-place-moab/slczm", which refused the fetch (HTTP 403) - so the Hyatt Place brand affiliation is confirmed and nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites, Moab
jewels.blurb: Listed by Wikivoyage's Moab guide at "1515 Hwy 191 North", +1 435 259-1150, with ichotelsgroup.com as its website. The IHG brand page was not fetched (IHG pages return 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Sorrel River Ranch Resort & Spa
jewels.blurb: Mile 17, UT-128 on the Colorado River: "A luxury Moab resort" of custom-built cabins across 240 acres; Condé Nast Johansens Award Winner 2024 and listed with Forbes Travel Guide; horseback riding, mountain biking, hiking and spa. 435.259.4642.

jewels.name: Sheri Griffith Expeditions
jewels.blurb: Moab river outfitter: Cataract Canyon trips "ranging from 4 to 11 days", including the 11-day "John Wesley Powell Expedition" on the Green and Colorado through Canyonlands, by oarboat, motorized J-rig or paddle boat; one-day trips too. (435) 259-8229.

jewels.name: Navtec Expeditions
jewels.blurb: Moab, operating "since 1896" and "an authorized concessioner of Canyonlands and Arches National Park": rafting, 4x4 backcountry tours, canyoneering and park tours. 1-800-833-1278; 435-259-7983.

jewels.name: Canyonlands by Night & Day
jewels.blurb: "family-owned tour company on the banks of the Colorado River near Moab", running trips "since 1963": Sound and Light Show jet boat tours, a sunset jet boat with dinner, canoe shuttles for the Green and Colorado, 4x4 and helicopter tours. (800) 394-9978.

jewels.name: Rim Tours
jewels.blurb: "Moab's Original Mountain Bike Tour Guides", since 1985: the White Rim as a 4-day camping trip and a full-day Canyonlands tour, small groups, plus "Bike & Gear Rentals". (435) 259-5223.

jewels.name: Moab Cyclery
jewels.blurb: 391 S. Main St., Moab, "Open Daily 7:00 AM - 6:00 PM": "Moab bike rentals, shuttles, repairs, gear, and local trail advice" - mountain bikes and e-bikes "set up for desert riding", trail shuttles, and "water bottles, and all your trail essentials".

jewels.name: Moab
jewels.blurb: The gateway to Island in the Sky, about 40 minutes from its visitor center (NPS): "A small town with a big spirit on the banks of the Colorado River, surrounded by two national parks and the red-rock horizons of the American West." Moab Office of Tourism, 25 E Center St.

jewels.name: Monticello
jewels.blurb: The southern gateway, 14 miles south of the UT 211 turn to The Needles (NPS): "Elevation: 7,069 feet (2,155 meters)", "Sheltered by the Abajo Mountains", with "Full services" and day tours to Canyonlands, the Needles and Canyon Rims Recreation Area.

jewels.name: Moab Brewery
jewels.blurb: 686 S. Main St.: "Our inspiration for our products comes from the beautiful and unique landscape in and around Moab, UT" - beer, spirits and scratch-cooked food; "Open Daily at 11:00am". (435) 259-6333.

jewels.name: Desert Bistro
jewels.blurb: 36 S 100 W: "Internationally inspired fine cuisine with a southwestern flair"; "Open Nightly 5pm to Close". 435-259-0756.

jewels.name: Sabaku Sushi
jewels.blurb: 90 E. Center Street, "open tue - sat 5pm - 9pm"; "We only reserve half the tables in the restaurant, the other half is left available for walk in service." 435-259-4455.

jewels.name: 98 Center
jewels.blurb: 98 East Center Street: "Asian and Local fusion restaurant in Moab, UTAH" - pho, bánh mì and salads made from scratch; "Wednesday - Sunday 11:30 AM - 9:00 PM". 435-355-0098.

jewels.name: Pasta Jay's
jewels.blurb: 4 S Main Street: "Where Red Rocks Meet Italian Flavor"; "Open Daily 11am – 11pm". (435) 259-2900.

jewels.name: River Grill at Sorrel River Ranch
jewels.blurb: Mile 17, UT-128: "Unforgettable dining along the Colorado River, where Moab's red rock cliffs" frame indoor and outdoor starlit meals. 435.259.4642.

faq.q: How much does it cost to get into Canyonlands National Park?
faq.a: "$30.00" per private vehicle ("Admits one private, non-commercial vehicle (15 passenger capacity or less) and all its occupants"), "$25.00" per motorcycle and "$15.00" per person on foot or bicycle; "Youth 15 and under are admitted free." Entrance stations take "Credit/Debit Only".

faq.q: Do you need timed entry for Canyonlands National Park?
faq.a: No: "Timed entry reservations are not required to enter the park."

faq.q: Do you need a permit for Canyonlands National Park?
faq.a: Not to visit, but "You need a backcountry permit for: vehicle, motorbike, and bicycle day-use trips on White Rim, Elephant Hill, Lavender Canyon, and Peekaboo/Horse Canyon roads; all overnight trips; all day-use and overnight river trips."

faq.q: How far is Canyonlands National Park from Moab?
faq.a: To Island in the Sky, "drive 10 miles (16 km) north of Moab" on US 191, then UT 313 "southwest 22 miles (35 km). Driving time to the visitor center from Moab is about 40 minutes." The Needles is reached "40 miles (60 km) south of Moab" on US 191, then about 35 miles west on UT 211.

faq.q: Can you drive through Canyonlands National Park?
faq.a: Not from one district to another: "No bridges or roads connect the districts within the park." UT 313 leads to Island in the Sky, UT 211 to The Needles, and "Only unpaved roads reach The Maze (graded dirt or high-clearance, four-wheel-drive)."

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Canyonlands National Park?
faq.a: "The temperate—and most popular—seasons are spring (April through May) and fall (mid-September through October)", with highs averaging 60º to 80ºF. In summer "temperatures often exceed 100ºF (37ºC)" and late-summer monsoon storms "often cause flash floods."

faq.q: Is Canyonlands National Park open year round?
faq.a: Yes: "Canyonlands National Park is normally open year-round, 24 hours a day." Each district's visitor center "has its own visitor center with operating hours that change with the seasons. Some facilities close in winter."

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Canyonlands National Park?
faq.a: Only in limited places: leashed pets may go "Along established front-country roads or in parking areas" and "In established front-country campgrounds and picnic areas" - not "on any hiking trails, or anywhere off-trail, even while in a carrier", "at any overlooks", in buildings, or in the backcountry, including river trips.

faq.q: Can you fly drones in Canyonlands National Park?
faq.a: No. "Launching, landing, or operating unmanned aircraft (such as drones, quadcopters, or model airplanes) is prohibited."

faq.q: What is the closest airport to Canyonlands National Park?
faq.a: Canyonlands Field (CNY), "16 miles from Moab"; Grand Junction Regional (GJT) is "113 miles from Moab" and Salt Lake City International (SLC) "237 miles from Moab". "There is no public transportation to Canyonlands."

seo.meta_title: Canyonlands National Park: Mesa Arch, White Rim & Camping | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: Island in the Sky, The Needles and The Maze: Mesa Arch, the 100-mile White Rim Road, Cataract Canyon, two park campgrounds and stays around Moab.

name: Sand Hollow State Park
line: Blue reservoir and red Sand Mountain dunes

jewels.name: Sand Hollow Reservoir
jewels.booking_route: day-use fee at the park ($25 Utah resident vehicle, $35 non-resident vehicle, $5 walk-in)
jewels.blurb: "warm, blue waters and red sandstone landscape"; 1,322 surface acres, "nearly twice as large as the nearby Quail Creek Reservoir"; beach access, boating, swimming, kayaking, waterskiing and fishing, with a boat ramp and floating docks. "There is no spearfishing on Sand Hollow Reservoir."

jewels.name: Sand Mountain OHV Area
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond the park day-use fee
jewels.blurb: "Sand Mountain OHV Acreage: 15,000" of a 20,000-acre park; visitors "explore and ride the dunes of Sand Mountain on an off-highway vehicle", and the park points riders to the Utah OHV Program.

jewels.name: Westside Campground
jewels.blurb: "50 sites (2 ADA-accessible sites)" with "Full hookups (Water, 30/50 Amp Electric, and Sewer connections at every site)" and "Modern restrooms with flush toilets and hot showers"; "$50.00 / night".

jewels.name: Sand Hollow Cottages
jewels.blurb: Two beachside cottages, "Sleeps up to 6", with kitchenette, heating/AC and full bathroom; "Full RV hook-up site included"; "Two night minimum"; pets allowed in Cottage 1 only. Fee page: "Sand Hollow Cottages: Per night (Amenities: AC, heat, kitchenette) $200".

jewels.name: Lakeview Campground
jewels.blurb: "30 sites (3 ADA-accessible sites)": 8 full-hookup and 22 partial-hookup sites, "Modern restrooms with flush toilets and hot showers"; "$45.00 / night" partial, "$50.00 / night" full hookup.

jewels.name: Sand Pit Campground
jewels.blurb: "22 sites total" - dry, partial-hookup and group sites, "Modern restrooms and hot showers nearby"; "$28.00 - $35.00 / night" dry, "$35.00 - $45.00 / night" partial, "$75.00 - $125.00 / night" groups.

jewels.name: Primitive Beach Camping
jewels.blurb: "Dispersed shoreline zones (40+ vehicle capacity depending on water levels)", no hookups or facilities, "$30.00 / night per vehicle"; fires here are restricted to propane fires and grills, and "Wood and charcoal are never allowed in this campground."

jewels.name: Beachside Campground
jewels.blurb: "4 (Back in only)" sites with "30/50 Amp Electric hookups" and "No restroom facilities"; "$55.00 / night per vehicle".

jewels.name: Sand Hollow Rentals
jewels.blurb: The park's named concession: "ATV's, UTV's, kayaks, paddle boards and more". Its own site rents "Sea Doo's, Pontoon Boats, Ski Boats" and "Wakeboards, Kayaks, SUPs, Trampolines, Canoes", and runs Sand Mountain OHV tours from "TWO HOUR" ($389) to "four HOUR" ($489); "You must be 18 years or older to rent." 3351 Sand Hollow Rd., Hurricane; 435-383-1200.

jewels.name: Dixie Divers and the Sand Hollow Dive Shack
jewels.blurb: "For your convenience we operate the Dive Shack at Sandhollow State Park during the summer!" - "We have everything you need for a dive at the lake." The St. George shop (558 E. Riverside Dr. #108, (435) 627-2173) teaches "Discover Scuba and Open Water to Master Diver"; the park lists it as a "full-service Dive Center offering classes, gear, rentals and Dive travel", May through October.

jewels.name: Life jackets for the reservoir
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI via AvantLink, or Amazon Associates)
jewels.blurb: The park's own kit rule: "All vessels must be equipped with a properly fitted life jacket for every passenger on board"; "Children under the age of 13 are required to wear a lifejacket at all times while the vessel is underway." Non-motorized craft and non-Utah residents must also complete the Mussel Awareness Course before launching.

jewels.name: Dune whip flag and OHV helmet
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI via AvantLink, or Amazon Associates); or the park gift shop
jewels.blurb: Utah's OHV course on dune riding: "a red or orange whip flag must be attached to the vehicle. The flag must be at least 6" x 12" in size and must be at least eight feet off the ground"; "All OHV operators and passengers under 18 years of age must wear a helmet that is properly fitted and fastened." The park's visitor-center gift shop stocks "OHV safety equipment".

jewels.name: Sand Hollow Visitor Center and Gift Shop
jewels.blurb: Open 7 a.m. - 9 p.m.; the gift shop offers "quality souvenirs including apparel, magnets and stickers, OHV safety equipment, water toys" plus limited snacks and drinks; fishing proclamations are available here. 435-680-0715.

jewels.name: Zion National Park
jewels.booking_route: national park entry; campground via Recreation.gov
jewels.blurb: "Gaze up at massive sandstone cliffs of cream, pink, and red that soar into a brilliant blue sky." Springdale, UT 84767; 435-772-3256. Its Watchman Campground: "Standard sites can be reserved up to 6 months in advance."

jewels.name: Snow Canyon State Park
jewels.blurb: "a 7,400-acre scenic park quietly tucked amid lava flows and soaring sandstone cliffs", with "more than 38 miles of hiking trails, a three-mile paved walking/biking trail and over 15 miles of equestrian trails"; open "6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Daily".

jewels.name: Snow Canyon State Park Campground
jewels.blurb: "Camping is available year-round at the 38-unit campground; reservations are recommended during peak seasons"; reserved "48 hours to 4 months in advance online". "Backcountry camping is not permitted in Snow Canyon."

jewels.name: Quail Creek State Park
jewels.booking_route: day-use at the park; campsites by phone 1-800-322-3770
jewels.blurb: "Quail Creek reservoir was completed in 1985 to provide irrigation and culinary water to the St. George area"; "some of the warmest waters in the state and a mild winter climate", 600 surface acres, up to 120 feet deep; rainbow trout, bullhead catfish and crappie below, largemouth bass and bluegill above. Campsites: "To reserve all campsites call 1-800-322-3770."

jewels.name: Sand Hollow Resort Championship Course
jewels.blurb: 5662 W Clubhouse Dr., Hurricane: a "Championship Course" "Consistently ranked #1 in Utah", a Golfweek "Top 100 Resort Course", with "three of Golf Digest's top 100 golf holes in the country"; "surrounded by the captivating beauty of Sand Hollow Reservoir". (435) 656-4653.

jewels.name: Vacation Villas at Sand Hollow Resort
jewels.blurb: "vacation rentals to suit every need" - "homes, condos, and suites in the Vacation Villas at Sand Hollow Resort" beside the golf course, with Horizon Kitchen + Spirits on site.

jewels.name: Hurricane Valley
jewels.blurb: The gateway towns of Hurricane, La Verkin, Toquerville, Leeds and Apple Valley, with "mountain bike trails, OHV destinations, camping, and water sports at two state parks, set among red rock mesas" (Greater Zion tourism board).

jewels.name: St. George / Hurricane KOA
jewels.blurb: 5800 Old Hwy 91, Hurricane: "114 RV, 15 Tent, 11 Cabins" in the Hurricane Valley (Greater Zion listing; koa.com refused the fetch, HTTP 403). (800) 562-8607.

jewels.name: Under Canvas Zion
jewels.booking_route: own website; travel advisors via undercanvas.com/travel-advisor/
jewels.blurb: Safari-tent camp in Virgin, Utah: Deluxe, Stargazer, Suite and "Angels Landing Suite (sleeps up to 6)" tents with private ensuite bathrooms, wood-burning stoves, on-site dining, nightly campfires and s'mores; dogs welcome for a nightly fee. Season 2026 "March 12th - November 8th".

jewels.name: Cliffrose Springdale, Curio Collection by Hilton
jewels.booking_route: Hilton's reservation system via the own website, or Reservations@cliffroselodge.com
jewels.blurb: 281 Zion Park Blvd, Springdale - "only steps from the entrance of Zion National Park" on the Virgin River: 12 room categories from Riverside rooms to a Grand View Villa, the Anthera restaurant, the Five Petals spa, "24-hour concierge and room service". (435) 772-3234.

jewels.name: The Red Cliffs Lodge Zion, a Tribute Portfolio Hotel
jewels.blurb: 792 Zion Park Boulevard, Springdale: 132 rooms, listed by Greater Zion as "a tribute portfolio hotel" under Marriott, including king suites with sofa beds. (435) 627-5280. Marriott's own page was not fetched.

jewels.name: TownePlace Suites St. George
jewels.blurb: 251 S 1470 E, St. George: an 85-room Marriott hotel in the St. George Area, "book at marriott.com" or (435) 986-9955 (Greater Zion listing; Marriott's own page was not fetched).

jewels.name: Best Western Plus Zion West
jewels.blurb: 44 W 500 N, La Verkin: 69 rooms, "20 miles away before the world famous Zion National Park", with complimentary breakfast, a seasonal outdoor pool, hot tub, EV charging, and pets for an additional fee. (435) 635-0277.

jewels.name: Horizon Kitchen + Spirits
jewels.blurb: At Sand Hollow Resort, Hurricane: "casual dining with a panoramic view", plus in-room dining for resort guests.

jewels.name: Zion Canyon Brew Pub
jewels.blurb: 95 Zion Park Blvd, Springdale: Zion Canyon Brewery's brewpub near the park entrance, small-batch ales with "made-from-scratch pub fare" and live music; its Station II Bar taproom is at 142 N Main St, St. George. 435-522-1360.

jewels.name: Bit and Spur Restaurant and Saloon
jewels.booking_route: Toast online reservations from the own site
jewels.blurb: 1212 Zion Park Boulevard, Springdale: open "7 days a week. 5:00 - 9:30PM" with a late-night menu, a wine list, a kids' menu and a taco truck; online reservations via Toast. (435) 772-3498.

jewels.name: Oscar's Cafe
jewels.blurb: 948 Zion Park Blvd, Springdale, "at the mouth of Zion National Park": breakfasts (pancakes, omelets, breakfast burritos) and lunch and dinner, best known for its hamburgers.

jewels.name: The Painted Pony
jewels.blurb: 2 W St. George Blvd, Ancestor Square, St. George: "Contemporary Seasonal Cuisine" - duck ravioli, bison tenderloin, seared scallops, wagyu - with an extensive wine list and craft cocktails. (435) 634-1700.

jewels.name: George's Corner Restaurant & Pub
jewels.blurb: Ancestor Square, St. George: breakfast, lunch and dinner with live music; "OPEN 8 am - 10pm Sun - Thurs | 8 am - midnight Fri - Sat"; first-come, first-served seating. (435) 216-7311.

faq.q: How much does it cost to get into Sand Hollow State Park?
faq.a: Utah State Parks lists "Day-Use - UT Residents: Per vehicle (Proof of Utah residency required) $25", "Non-Resident Day Use: Per vehicle (no senior discount) $35", "Senior Day-Use - UT Residents: Seniors 65+ ... $10" and "Walk In Fee: Per person $5".

faq.q: Can you camp at Sand Hollow State Park?
faq.a: Yes. The park has Westside ("50 sites", full hookups, $50), Lakeview ("30 sites", $45-$50), Sand Pit ("22 sites total"), Beachside (4 back-in electric sites, $55) and Primitive Beach Camping ("$30.00 / night per vehicle"), plus two cottages that sleep up to 6, booked through ReserveAmerica.

faq.q: Can you swim at Sand Hollow State Park?
faq.a: Yes - the park lists "Beach access, boating, camping, diving ... swimming, waterskiing" among its activities. Before swimming, the park points visitors to its harmful-algae monitoring page for current "Algae Conditions" at the reservoir.

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Sand Hollow State Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Pets must be leashed at all times" and may not be left in vehicles. Pets are allowed in Cottage 1 but not Cottage 2.

faq.q: Can you rent kayaks at Sand Hollow State Park?
faq.a: Yes, through the park's concessionaire Sand Hollow Rentals: "ATV's, UTV's, kayaks, paddle boards and more for those of all ages, shapes and sizes!" (sandhollowrentals.com). Its own site adds "You must be 18 years or older to rent."

faq.q: What time does Sand Hollow State Park open?
faq.a: "Daylight Saving Time: 6 a.m. - 10 p.m."; "Standard Time: 7 a.m. - 9 p.m." The visitor center is open 7 a.m. - 9 p.m.

faq.q: How big is Sand Hollow State Park?
faq.a: "Park Acreage: 20,000", of which "Sand Mountain OHV Acreage: 15,000"; the reservoir covers 1,322 surface acres.

faq.q: When did Sand Hollow State Park open?
faq.a: "Opened to the public as a state park in 2003."

faq.q: Does Sand Hollow State Park have showers?
faq.a: Yes. Westside and Lakeview campgrounds have "Modern restrooms with flush toilets and hot showers", and Sand Pit has "Modern restrooms and hot showers nearby". Beachside has "No restroom facilities" and primitive beach camping has none.

faq.q: How does Sand Hollow State Park compare with Quail Creek State Park?
faq.a: Sand Hollow's reservoir covers 1,322 surface acres, "nearly twice as large as the nearby Quail Creek Reservoir", and the park adds 15,000 acres of OHV dunes. Quail Creek's reservoir "was completed in 1985", covers 600 surface acres, reaches 120 feet deep and has "some of the warmest waters in the state".

seo.meta_title: Sand Hollow State Park: Reservoir, Dunes & Camping | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: Utah's most popular state park: a 1,322-acre reservoir, 15,000 acres of Sand Mountain dunes, five campgrounds and cottages, and Zion within the ring.

name: Rocky Mountain National Park
line: The highest continuous paved road in the US, an elk rut in the meadows, and a timed-entry permit for the busy hours

jewels.name: Trail Ridge Road
jewels.blurb: "the highest continuous paved road in the United States" - 48 miles one-way across the park, climbing to 12,183 feet; open to through travel on 2026-10-02, timed entry required 9 am to 2 pm; status line 970-586-1222

jewels.name: Old Fall River Road
jewels.blurb: a 9.4-mile unpaved, one-way uphill road from Endovalley Picnic Area to 11,796 feet, open to vehicles early July to early October; closing for seasonal maintenance from October 6, 2026; vehicles over 25 feet and trailers prohibited

jewels.name: Timed Entry and Timed Entry+ Bear Lake Road (2026)
jewels.blurb: two reservation types on Recreation.gov with 2-hour entry windows; general 9 am-2 pm May 22-Oct 12, Bear Lake corridor 5 am-6 pm May 22-Oct 18; next-day releases at 7 pm MDT; a non-refundable $2 processing fee

jewels.name: Bear Lake Road and the Bear Lake Shuttle
jewels.blurb: a 9.2-mile paved road climbing from 8,200 to 9,475 feet, open year-round; free Bear Lake shuttle May 22-October 18, 6:30 am to 7:30 pm, every 10-15 minutes, stopping at Park & Ride, Bierstadt Lake, Glacier Gorge and Bear Lake

jewels.name: Hiker Shuttle from Estes Park
jewels.blurb: from the Estes Park Visitor Center to the Park & Ride, daily May 22-September 7 and weekends only September 12-October 18; $2 per reservation (up to 4 tickets) on Recreation.gov, plus a park entrance pass

jewels.name: Bear Lake to Nymph, Dream and Emerald Lakes
jewels.blurb: the chain of lakes above Bear Lake; NPS report of August 21, 2026: dry to Nymph Lake, with "areas that are wet and muddy near Dream Lake"

jewels.name: Bear Lake Nature Trail
jewels.blurb: the loop at the end of Bear Lake Road; NPS report of August 21, 2026: "mostly dry. There could be areas with puddles or that are muddy"

jewels.name: Glacier Gorge: Alberta Falls, Mills Lake, The Loch, Black Lake
jewels.blurb: the Glacier Gorge trail system; the Glacier Gorge Trailhead and parking close September 28-October 1 and October 5-8, 2026 for erosion repair (open October 2-4); use Bear Lake Trailhead, 0.4 miles from Glacier Gorge Junction

jewels.name: Longs Peak and Chasm Lake
jewels.blurb: the park's mountaineering objective via the Keyhole Route; NPS, September 23, 2026: "Fall has arrived on Longs Peak and the environment is transitioning to winter conditions" and the route is "a true mountaineering route and a serious undertaking this time of year"

jewels.name: Sprague Lake Trail
jewels.blurb: 0.8 mile of packed gravel, wood bridge and dirt with benches, a fishing pier and "Stunning views of the Continental Divide"; electric mobility devices permitted

jewels.name: Coyote Valley Trail, Kawuneeche Valley
jewels.blurb: a west-side nature trail permitting electric mobility devices; NPS report: "Enjoy views of the Colorado River and the Kawuneeche Valley"

jewels.name: Lily Lake Trail
jewels.blurb: one of three trails the NPS names as permitting electric OPDMDs used as assistive devices

jewels.name: Cub Lake and Gem Lake trails
jewels.blurb: two named lower-elevation hikes; NPS reports of August 19-20, 2026 describe Cub Lake as "clear and dry" and Gem Lake as "mostly dry" with wet, muddy places

jewels.name: Alpine Ridge Trail and the Alpine Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: a tundra trail at the high point of the Trail Ridge drive; the NPS asks visitors to "Stay on the designated trail and do not cross any ropes to help protect fragile alpine plants"

jewels.name: Elk rut in the meadows (September-October)
jewels.blurb: peak elk viewing during the mating season; meadow closures September 1-October 31 in Horseshoe Park, Moraine Park, Upper Beaver Meadows, Harbison and Holzwarth meadows, 5 pm to 10 am; NPS minimum distance 75 feet for elk

jewels.name: Sheep Lakes and Horseshoe Park bighorn sheep
jewels.blurb: bighorn "commonly seen near Sheep Lakes and Horseshoe Park from May through mid-August"; 66 mammal and 280 bird species parkwide; 120 feet minimum from moose and bears

jewels.name: Wilderness overnight backpacking
jewels.blurb: summer permits reserved on Recreation.gov (opened March 1, 2026), winter permits first-come, first-served; $10 per permit; "All wilderness permits & dashtags MUST be picked up in person" in Estes Park or Grand Lake

jewels.name: Glacier Creek Stables (in park)
jewels.blurb: "One stable is located within the park: Glacier Creek Stables", typically open May through October

jewels.name: Snow Mountain Ranch Yurt Village, Granby (YMCA of the Rockies)
jewels.blurb: hilltop yurts for up to 6 plus 2 on an outside tent pad, with microwave, mini-fridge, linens, Wi-Fi and electricity, open May through late September; plus a full-hookup RV and tent campground; 1101 Co Rd 53, Granby

jewels.name: Winding River Resort, Grand Lake
jewels.blurb: covered wagons, camper cabins, rustic cabins, lodge rooms, RV and tent sites and guest horse camping at 1447 County Road 491, beside the park's west entrance near the Kawuneeche Visitor Center; family-operated since 1972

jewels.name: Jellystone Park of Estes
jewels.blurb: cabins and cottages, 30 hookup RV sites and 40 tent sites at 5495 Hwy 36, Estes Park, May through October, with pool and playground; Visit Estes Park calls it "the closest thing Estes Park has to" glamping

jewels.name: Sun Outdoors Rocky Mountains, Grand Lake area (listing only)
jewels.blurb: listed by the Grand Lake chamber as a campground with RV sites, cabins and glamping options; the operator's own site returned 403 and the chamber listing's address and phone appear to be the visitor center's

jewels.name: People of the Honey, Ward (Hipcamp listing)
jewels.blurb: an off-grid 5-acre sanctuary at 9,000 feet with a 24-foot ceremonial tipi sleeping 6, an off-grid cabin and tent sites; listed as about 35 miles from Estes Park and RMNP

jewels.name: Creekside Paradise, near Boulder (Hipcamp listing)
jewels.blurb: a 42-acre creekside property with a Mongolian yurt, a bell tent and primitive tent sites; listed as about 45 minutes to the park's main entrance; no potable water, power or cell service

jewels.name: Moraine Park Campground (NPS)
jewels.blurb: Recreation.gov, up to 6 months ahead (some sites short-term release); summer season May 21-October 19, 2026; the only in-park campground open in winter, first come, first served; 14 accessible sites

jewels.name: Glacier Basin Campground (NPS)
jewels.blurb: Recreation.gov, up to 6 months ahead; on the Moraine Park shuttle line; the NPS page lists it as "closed for the 2026/2027 Winter Season"

jewels.name: Aspenglen Campground (NPS)
jewels.blurb: Recreation.gov, up to 6 months ahead; 2026 summer season May 21 to September 28

jewels.name: Timber Creek Campground (NPS, west side)
jewels.blurb: Recreation.gov, up to 6 months ahead; 2026 summer season May 21 to October 5

jewels.name: Longs Peak Campground (NPS)
jewels.blurb: first-come, first-served and tents only; "typically opens in early July and closes in early September"

jewels.name: Estes Park / Rocky Mountain National Park KOA Holiday (listing only)
jewels.blurb: named on KOA's Colorado list; koa.com's campground page returned 403, so accommodations, season and address were not confirmed

jewels.name: Grand Lake / Rocky Mountain National Park KOA Journey
jewels.blurb: RV sites and cabins at 143 County Road 48, Grand Lake (the former Elk Creek Campground & RV Park), with camp store, rec room, laundry and dump station

jewels.name: Kirks Flyshop, Estes Park
jewels.blurb: since 2002 at 230 E. Elkhorn Ave: guided fly fishing, RMNP hiking, backpacking, llama trekking and Longs Peak climbs, gear rentals and Lake Estes charters

jewels.name: Estes Park Mountain Shop
jewels.blurb: since 1986: 18,000 sq ft of gear, summer, camping, winter and adaptive equipment rentals, guided climbing, snowshoeing and hiking, and an indoor climbing gym; open 8 am-8 pm daily

jewels.name: National Park Gateway Stables, Fall River Entrance
jewels.blurb: at the edge of the park by the Fall River Visitor Center; "All rides venture into Rocky Mountain National Park", from pony rides to full-day rides; weight limits apply

jewels.name: Sombrero Stables, Estes Park
jewels.blurb: "Riding for the Brand Since 1958" at 1895 Big Thompson Ave: 30-minute to 2-hour rides, a Cowboy Experience and private rides

jewels.name: Rapid Transit Rafting, Estes Park
jewels.blurb: half-day Cache la Poudre and full-day Colorado River trips (Class II-III, ages 7+), May 20 to early September, with round-trip transport from 161 Virginia Dr

jewels.name: Green Jeep Tours, Estes Park
jewels.blurb: open-jeep scenic and wildlife tours of Rocky Mountain National Park and the Estes Park region from 157 Moraine Ave

jewels.name: Wildside 4x4 Tours, Estes Park
jewels.blurb: year-round National Park tours and May 15-December 1 off-road tours in Roosevelt National Forest under a Forest Service special use permit

jewels.name: Estes Park Trolleys
jewels.blurb: about 3-hour trolley tours through RMNP with walking and photo stops, plus Stanley Hotel tours, in 1920s-style enclosed trolleys

jewels.name: Rocky Mountain Conservancy Field Institute
jewels.blurb: the park's nonprofit partner, running expert-led classes, fall elk ecology tours, custom tours and bus tours in the park

jewels.name: Never Summer Mountain Products, Grand Lake
jewels.blurb: independent and family-owned since 1982 at 919 Grand Ave: summer kayak, SUP and bear-canister rentals; winter backcountry ski and snowshoe rentals

jewels.name: Rocky Mountain Stables, Snow Mountain Ranch
jewels.blurb: one- and two-hour guided rides with Continental Divide and park views, plus winter rides and sleigh rides, at Snow Mountain Ranch near Granby; ages 8+, 250 lb limit

jewels.name: Estes Park Aerial Tramway
jewels.blurb: a 2,630-foot ride to the 8,708-foot summit of Prospect Mountain with views of the park, Longs Peak and the Continental Divide; open daily 9 am-7 pm through November 1, 2026

jewels.name: The Stanley Hotel, Estes Park
jewels.blurb: the 1909 landmark at 333 E Wonderview Ave whose Stephen King connection made it famous; historic hotel tours

jewels.name: Grand Lake and Grand Lake Lodge
jewels.blurb: Colorado's largest natural lake, more than 500 acres, "formed by glaciers"; the historic Grand Lake Lodge sits beside the park at 15500 US-34

jewels.name: Rocky Mountain Repertory Theatre, Grand Lake
jewels.blurb: professional musical theatre at 800 Grand Avenue; 2026 season includes a 70s Beehive musical from September 4 and Boulder Ballet on October 10

jewels.name: Estes Park fall festivals: Elk Fest and Autumn Gold
jewels.blurb: Elk Fest brings "vendors, live music, food trucks, and bugling contests in downtown Estes Park"; Autumn Gold celebrates "beer, brats, and music"; 2026 dates not shown on the page fetched

jewels.name: Bird & Jim, Estes Park
jewels.blurb: Seasonal American restaurant at 915 Moraine Ave since 2016, menus built on local ingredients, with a sommelier-curated wine list holding the Wine Spectator Award of Excellence every year since 2020.

jewels.name: Snowy Peaks Winery, Estes Park
jewels.blurb: Winery at 292 Moraine Ave fermenting Colorado-grown grapes (Merlot, Syrah, Viognier, Riesling) with tasting flights and Colorado artisan cheeses, chocolates and charcuterie; daily 11:30 am-7:30 pm.

jewels.name: The Whiskey Vault and MacGregor Chophouse at the Stanley Hotel, Estes Park
jewels.blurb: The Stanley's five dining venues include the Whiskey Vault, billed as Colorado's largest selection of whiskeys and single malt scotches, and the MacGregor Chophouse steakhouse, plus Post Beer & Chicken and the 217 Wine Bar.

jewels.name: Elkins Tasting Room and Mercantile, Estes Park
jewels.blurb: Distillery tasting room at 137 E. Elkhorn Ave whose original Elkins Colorado Whiskey took silver at the 2016 Denver International Spirits Competition; per the Visit Estes Park bureau article.

jewels.name: Hogback Distillery Store & Tasting Room, Estes Park
jewels.blurb: Boulder-based microdistillery pouring Scotch-style whisky in several expressions at 857 Moraine Ave; per the Visit Estes Park bureau article.

jewels.name: Avant Garde Aleworks, Estes Park
jewels.booking_route: walk-in only; rental packages for large groups
jewels.blurb: Family-founded brewery at 920 Dunraven St pouring European-inspired beers and house seltzers, with rotating food trucks, live music and vinyl nights; dog- and family-friendly.

jewels.name: Rock Cut Brewing Company, Estes Park
jewels.blurb: Downtown brewery at 390 W Riverside Drive at the base of Prospect Mountain, with patio, food, crowlers to go and Tuesday trivia; daily 11 am-10 pm.

jewels.name: Lumpy Ridge Brewing Co., Estes Park
jewels.blurb: Handcrafted beers from traditional to adventurous, brewed in a former gas station at 531 S. Saint Vrain Ave; per the Visit Estes Park bureau article.

jewels.name: The Barrel, Estes Park
jewels.blurb: Open-air craft beer, wine and spirits garden at 116 E. Elkhorn Ave with more than 60 rotating taps; per the Visit Estes Park bureau article.

jewels.name: Spirit Hound Distillers, Lyons
jewels.booking_route: not observed for tours (private party reservations offered); phone (303) 823-5696
jewels.blurb: Distillery at 4196 Ute Hwy making American Single Malt Whisky from locally harvested and malted barley; London International Spirits Competition 'Whisky of the Year' 2022 and 2024; tours, cocktail classes and food trucks.

jewels.name: Marigold Lyons
jewels.blurb: Family-owned bistro at 405 Main St cooking Northern Italian and Southern French cuisine, a James Beard Best Chef Mountain semifinalist and on Wine Enthusiast's best wine restaurants list; Wednesday to Sunday dinners.

jewels.name: Oskar Blues original location, Lyons
jewels.blurb: The original Oskar Blues location at 303 Main St for a meal and hand-crafted beers; per the Lyons town visitor listing.

jewels.name: The Historic Rapids Restaurant, Grand Lake
jewels.blurb: Gourmet dining with 'elegant dishes' at the Rapids Lodge in Grand Lake; per the Grand Lake visitor bureau dining page.

jewels.name: Mountain Market, Grand Lake
jewels.blurb: Market for assembling picnic provisions or buying prepared food; per the Grand Lake visitor bureau dining page.

faq.q: Do I need a reservation to enter Rocky Mountain National Park in 2026?
faq.a: From May 22, a timed entry reservation is required between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m. through October 12, 2026, and for the Bear Lake Road Corridor between 5 a.m. and 6 p.m. through October 18, 2026. Entry outside those hours, on foot or bicycle, or with a campground or wilderness reservation is exempt.

faq.q: How do I get a timed entry reservation?
faq.a: On Recreation.gov. Blocks were released on May 1 at 8 a.m. MDT and then on the first of each month; additional reservations are released at 7 p.m. MDT the night before the arrival date. The only cost is a non-refundable $2 processing fee.

faq.q: Is Trail Ridge Road open?
faq.a: On October 2, 2026 the NPS stated that Trail Ridge Road is open to through travel. It is a seasonal road; the recorded status line is 970-586-1222.

faq.q: How much does it cost to enter Rocky Mountain National Park?
faq.a: $30 per private vehicle for one day or $35 for seven days; $15 or $20 per person on foot or bicycle (16+); $70 for the park's annual pass. Non-US residents 16 and older pay an additional $100 unless admitted with an annual or America the Beautiful pass.

faq.q: When is the elk rut, and are any areas closed?
faq.a: The NPS names September-October as peak elk viewing during the mating season. From September 1 to October 31, off-trail foot travel is prohibited 5 p.m. to 10 a.m. in Horseshoe Park, Moraine Park, Upper Beaver Meadows, Harbison Meadow and Holzwarth Meadow.

faq.q: How do I reserve a campsite in the park?
faq.a: Moraine Park, Glacier Basin, Aspenglen and Timber Creek are reserved on Recreation.gov up to six months ahead, with some short-term releases. Longs Peak Campground is first-come, first-served and tents only. In winter, Moraine Park is the only campground open, first come, first served.

faq.q: Is there a shuttle to Bear Lake?
faq.a: Yes. The free Bear Lake shuttle runs May 22 to October 18, 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m., every 10-15 minutes from the Park & Ride. A Hiker Shuttle from the Estes Park Visitor Center needs a $2 Recreation.gov reservation and runs weekends only from September 12 to October 18.
