name: Mesa Verde National Park
line: Ancestral Pueblo cliff dwellings on the mesa

jewels.name: Cliff Palace Tour
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov only - opens 14 days ahead at 8:00 am MDT
jewels.blurb: Chapin Mesa: a "45-minute ranger-led tour"; visitors "descend uneven stone steps and climb four ladders, with an elevation change of 100 ft"; "Total walking distance is 1/4 mile". Season "May 4 - October 21" 2026.

jewels.name: Balcony House Tour
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov only - opens 14 days ahead at 8:00 am MDT
jewels.blurb: A "one-hour tour", "one of the most adventurous in the park": "climb a 32 ft ladder, crawl through an 18 in wide by 27 in tall tunnel extending 12 ft long, and climb up a 65 ft open cliff face".

jewels.name: Long House Tour
jewels.blurb: Wetherill Mesa: a "90-minute, ranger-guided tour", "2.25 miles round-trip" plus a "0.75 mile walk from the Wetherill Mesa parking lot", "climbing two 15 ft ladders"; "Allow 115 minutes to 135 minutes for the entire Long House experience". Season "May 22 - October 21" 2026.

jewels.name: Square Tower House Tour
jewels.blurb: Backcountry: a "120-minute tour", "1-mile in and out", with "two 16 ft ladders" and a "34 ft long narrow cliff ledge"; strenuous; "Bring a minimum of 1/2 gallon (2 liters) of water per person".

jewels.name: Mug House Tour
jewels.blurb: Backcountry: a "120-minute tour", "2.25 mile round-trip"; visitors "descend/ascend a 6 ft ladder unassisted"; strenuous.

jewels.name: Step House
jewels.booking_route: none needed - covered by the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: Wetherill Mesa: no reservation required, a "self-guided site when a ranger is present"; "1 mile round-trip" with a "165 ft" elevation change.

jewels.name: Mesa Top Loop Road
jewels.booking_route: none needed - covered by the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: "This 6-mile drive features eleven stops with paved trails and views of cliff dwellings like Cliff Palace"; open daily 8 a.m. to sunset in winter, and year-round for self-guided exploration.

jewels.name: Spruce Tree House overlook
jewels.blurb: "Spruce Tree House is the best preserved and third-largest cliff dwelling", seen from a covered porch and accessible overlook near the museum; a daily ranger talk runs here.

jewels.name: Mesa Verde Museum
jewels.blurb: 2026 hours: "May 4 - October 21: 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, DAILY", "October 22 - December 31: 10:00 am to 3:00 pm, DAILY"; closed for renovations until late April. Wheelchairs to borrow.

jewels.name: Petroglyph Point Trail
jewels.blurb: 2.4 miles roundtrip, 227 ft: "Very Challenging—unmaintained with a narrow passage, stone stairs, steep edges, loose rock, scrambling required." Counterclockwise recommended.

jewels.name: Soda Canyon Overlook Trail
jewels.blurb: "Easy", 1.2 miles roundtrip, 70 ft: a level out-and-back through pinyon-juniper forest.

jewels.name: Point Lookout Trail
jewels.blurb: "Moderate", 2.2 miles roundtrip, 400 ft, with "Steep switchbacks" to the park's landmark formation.

jewels.name: Prater Ridge Trail
jewels.blurb: "Strenuous", 7.8 miles roundtrip, 675 ft, with north and south loop options - the park's longest listed hike.

jewels.name: Park Point
jewels.blurb: The park's highest point at 8,572 feet, reached by "a very steep hike on pavement"; leashed pets allowed on its paved areas.

jewels.name: Night skies at an International Dark Sky Park
jewels.booking_route: none needed - check the park calendar
jewels.blurb: The NPS lists "Stargaze" among things to do: Mesa Verde is a certified International Dark Sky Park; summer evening programmes run at the Morefield Campground Amphitheater.

jewels.name: Far View Lodge
jewels.booking_route: own website booking (visitmesaverde.com) or 970-529-4465 per NPS
jewels.blurb: "the only lodging located within Mesa Verde National Park", 15 miles beyond the entrance: 150 Kiva and Kiva Deluxe View rooms; "no in-room televisions or cell service—just quiet moments, star-filled skies"; listed season "April 17 - October 18"; pet-friendly; operated by Aramark.

jewels.name: Morefield Campground
jewels.blurb: Four miles from the entrance: "nearly 267" campsites including "15 full hook-up RV sites" and "17 group sites"; "Showers & Laundry Adjacent to Campground Store", Knife Edge Café breakfast, "well-stocked grocery and camp store"; listed season "April 24 - October 18".

jewels.name: 700 Years Tour
jewels.booking_route: FareHarbor (visitmesaverde-aramark) or in person at Far View Lodge, Far View Terrace or Morefield
jewels.blurb: Aramark's 4-hour coach tour with an "NAI-certified guide", short hikes to mesa-top sites and guaranteed Cliff Palace access; adults $129, children (5-11) $99; departs 8:00 am or 1:00 pm from Far View Lodge, May 4 - October 18.

jewels.name: Metate Room Restaurant
jewels.blurb: At Far View Lodge: "colorful Native American art and sweeping views"; the "contemporary menu draws inspiration from traditional regional ingredients and flavors"; dinner 5:00-9:00 pm Apr 17 - Oct 18.

jewels.name: Far View Terrace
jewels.blurb: Park dining at "Navajo Hill @ Mile 15, inside Mesa Verde National Park"; (970) 565-3738; a 700 Years Tour sales point.

jewels.name: Spruce Tree Terrace
jewels.blurb: Near the Mesa Verde Museum at Mile 21; in winter "The only available food service is on the mesa top at Spruce Tree Terrace Café" (NPS).

jewels.name: Hydration kit: a gallon of water a day
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI.com via AvantLink)
jewels.blurb: The NPS: "Carry water with you everywhere, and drink it"; "we recommend that individuals carry and drink at least a gallon of water each day"; backcountry tours: "Bring a minimum of 1/2 gallon (2 liters) of water per person".

jewels.name: Hands-free daypack for the ladder tours
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI.com via AvantLink)
jewels.blurb: Tours involve "rough trails with steep dropoffs, uneven steps, and climbing ladders" and visitors need both hands free - Balcony House alone has a 32 ft ladder and a 65 ft open cliff face.

jewels.name: Warm layers for 7,000-8,400 feet
jewels.blurb: "Elevations range between 7,000 and 8,400 feet"; "Be prepared with water, snacks, and layers of warm clothing"; "Afternoon thunderstorms are common in the summer months and can approach quickly."

jewels.name: Winter traction devices
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to a gear retailer (REI.com via AvantLink)
jewels.blurb: For winter hiking, "traction devices are recommended whenever snow or icy conditions exist"; the main road's "shady curves" are "often icy night and day".

jewels.name: Ute Mountain Tribal Park
jewels.blurb: Towaoc, at the junction of Highways 160 and 491: full-day (9am-4pm) and half-day (9am-12pm) tours of archaeological sites on tribal land - "YOU MUST HAVE A UTE GUIDE TO ENTER THE UTE MOUNTAIN UTE TRIBAL LAND"; "No dogs are allowed"; cabins and camping; (970) 565-9653.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express - Mesa Verde
jewels.blurb: Listed by Mesa Verde Country at "2121 East Main Street, Cortez, CO 81321", (970) 565-6000. IHG's own page was not fetched (brand pages return 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Hampton Inn Cortez
jewels.blurb: Listed by Mesa Verde Country at "2244 East Hawkins Street, Cortez, CO 81321", (970) 564-5924. Hilton's own page was not fetched (brand pages return 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Best Western Turquoise Inn & Suites
jewels.blurb: Listed by Mesa Verde Country at "535 East Main Street, Cortez, CO, 81321", "(970) 565-3778". Nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Ancient Echoes at Kelly Place
jewels.blurb: McElmo Canyon, 10.2 miles outside Cortez on the Trail of the Ancients byway: a lodge, adobe casitas and camping on a 38-acre archaeological and horticultural preserve with "immediate access to ancient dwellings"; Mesa Verde (8 miles); 970.565.3125.

jewels.name: Mesa Verde RV Resort
jewels.blurb: 35303 Hwy 160, Mancos: "The Premier RV Resort in the Four Corners"; RV and tent sites and cabins, two hot tubs, a heated pool (Memorial Day-Labor Day), 24/7 laundry, dog-walking area; "Now open year round with limited spaces in Winter"; (970) 533-7421.

jewels.name: Ancient Cedars/Mesa Verde RV Park
jewels.blurb: Listed by Mesa Verde Country at "928 E Main Street", Cortez, CO 81321, "(970) 565-4048".

jewels.name: Cortez RV Resort
jewels.blurb: Montezuma County, 14 mi from Mancos on Hipcamp: a "35-site resort with diverse lodging near Mesa Verde National Park and regional attractions".

jewels.name: Mancos State Park
jewels.blurb: Colorado Parks and Wildlife: "an ideal destination for outdoor enthusiasts and travelers year-round"; 32 campsites; open daily 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.; reservations at cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613.

jewels.name: Bright Star Campground
jewels.blurb: Montezuma County, 11 mi from Mancos: a "Community-driven campground with tipis, camping cabins, tent/RV sites, and a Navajo Hogan"; "complimentary WiFi, drinking water, ice, hot showers."

jewels.name: The Dome at Mesa Verde
jewels.blurb: Montezuma County, 9.5 mi from Mancos: a "Luxury custom geodesic dome on 250 acres with sauna, firepit" and "on-site Concierge" services (Hipcamp listing summary; the listing page itself did not render).

jewels.name: Southwest Luxury Glamping
jewels.blurb: Montezuma County, 1.8 mi from Mancos: "Three glamping sites minutes from downtown Mancos with proximity to Mesa Verde."

jewels.name: Canyon Trails Ranch
jewels.blurb: Montezuma County, 27 mi from Mancos: a "Family-run ranch offering 17 shepherd wagon sites and camping, established 1965."

jewels.name: Kokopelli Bike and Board
jewels.booking_route: own website rental booking or walk-in
jewels.blurb: 130 W Main St, Cortez ((970) 565-4408) and 315 Central Ave, Dolores ((970) 676-0060): "Shop Local!" - bikes and gear for sale, with rentals at both locations, and access to Phil's World, Sand Canyon and High Country trails.

jewels.name: WildEdge Brewing Collective
jewels.blurb: 111 North Market, Cortez: "opened on April 11th, 2017 in downtown Cortez after a 7 month renovation of a vacant warehouse"; Tue-Sat 3-9 pm, Sun 3-7 pm, closed Mondays.

jewels.name: Mancos Brewing Company
jewels.blurb: 484 Hwy 160 E Frontage Rd, Mancos: "a true public house"; "We offer wood fired pizza, fresh salads, sandwiched, home style casserole dishes and appetizers"; closed Tuesdays.

jewels.name: Dolores River Brewery
jewels.blurb: 100 S 4th St, Dolores: "SW Colorado's premium beer garden and music space", "SINCE 2002"; wood-fired pizza Friday-Sunday and rotating food partners; open Tue-Sun from 4 pm; 970-882-4677.

jewels.name: The Pie Maker Bakery
jewels.blurb: Listed by Mesa Verde Country at "17 North Harrison Street, Cortez, CO 81321", "(970) 560-6039"; its own site redirects to a Square store that did not render.

jewels.name: The Depot
jewels.blurb: Listed by Mesa Verde Country under Specialty & Farm-to-Table at "520 Railroad Ave., Dolores, CO, 81323", (970) 882-7500.

jewels.name: Cortez
jewels.blurb: The western gateway: Mesa Verde Country lists its Holiday Inn Express, Hampton Inn and Best Western, RV parks on East Main Street, WildEdge Brewing and The Pie Maker Bakery; the park is a "one-hour drive from Cortez" (NPS).

jewels.name: Mancos
jewels.blurb: The eastern gateway on Highway 160: Mesa Verde RV Resort, Mancos Brewing Company, Mancos State Park and the glamping listings Hipcamp measures from it; NPS names Mancos as a pet-boarding community.

jewels.name: Dolores
jewels.blurb: Mesa Verde Country's third community, north of Cortez: Dolores River Brewery, The Depot on Railroad Ave, a Kokopelli Bike and Board shop and the Dolores River RV Resort.

faq.q: Do you need reservations for Mesa Verde National Park?
faq.a: Not to enter: "Mesa Verde National Park is Open Daily, Year-Round" with no reservations required. The ranger-led cliff dwelling tours do need tickets: "Reservations open 14 days in advance, beginning at 8:00 am MDT and fill up early." Step House needs no reservation.

faq.q: What tours are there at Mesa Verde National Park?
faq.a: Ranger-led tours of Cliff Palace ("45-minute", four ladders), Balcony House ("one-hour", a 32 ft ladder and a tunnel), Long House ("90-minute", 2.25 miles), and the backcountry Square Tower House, Mug House and Oak Tree House tours ("120-minute"). Step House is self-guided.

faq.q: Is Mesa Verde National Park free?
faq.a: No. A private vehicle is $30.00 from May 1 to Oct 22, "Valid for 7 days", and $20.00 from Oct 23 to Apr 30; per person $15.00. "This park does not accept cash" - "Entrance fees are credit/debit only."

faq.q: Is Mesa Verde National Park open year round?
faq.a: Yes: "Mesa Verde National Park is Open Daily, Year-Round." In winter Far View Lodge, Morefield Campground and most dining close, while the Mesa Top Loop Road stays open; cliff dwelling tours "Begin in early May" and end mid-to-late October.

faq.q: How long do you need at Mesa Verde National Park?
faq.a: The NPS says to plan "at least two hours just to drive into and out of the park" - the first cliff dwelling viewpoint is 21 miles, about 45 minutes, up the park road. A Long House visit alone takes "115 minutes to 135 minutes".

faq.q: Can you camp in Mesa Verde National Park?
faq.a: Yes, at Morefield Campground, "located four miles from the park entrance. It has spaces for tents, trailers, and RVs, including 15 full-hookup RV sites (reservations recommended)." It is operated by Aramark.

faq.q: Where can you stay in Mesa Verde National Park?
faq.a: "Far View Lodge is the only lodging located within Mesa Verde National Park", 15 miles beyond the entrance, with 150 Kiva and Kiva Deluxe View rooms and "no in-room televisions or cell service".

faq.q: Can you take dogs to Mesa Verde National Park?
faq.a: Only in limited places: "Leashed pets are allowed on roads, parking lots, and paved areas on Mesa Top Loop and Park Point", but "not on trails, in ancestral sites or buildings". "A kennel is available in the Morefield Campground" (970-565-2133).

faq.q: What is the closest airport to Mesa Verde National Park?
faq.a: The NPS lists airports at Cortez, Colorado; Durango, Colorado; and Farmington, New Mexico. The park is a "one-hour drive from Cortez" and a "1.5 hour drive from Durango".

faq.q: When was Mesa Verde National Park established?
faq.a: "President Theodore Roosevelt established Mesa Verde National Park on June 29, 1906", "the first national park of its kind", to preserve "nearly 5,000 ancestral sites".

seo.meta_title: Mesa Verde National Park: Cliff Dwelling Tours, Far View Lodge & Where to Stay | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: Ranger-led Cliff Palace and Balcony House tours, booked 14 days ahead, Far View Lodge, Morefield Campground and stays in Cortez and Mancos.

name: Great Sand Dunes National Park
line: Tallest dunes in North America

jewels.name: High Dune on First Ridge
jewels.booking_route: none needed - covered by the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: "the most common destination in the dunefield, providing a great view of the entire dunefield. It is about 688 feet (209 m) from base to top." "Average round trip hiking time for High Dune is 2 hours over 2.5 miles (4 km)" - but "Plan to take as much as 4 hours to hike roundtrip, if not acclimated to the higher elevation". There are no trails in the dunefield.

jewels.name: Sandboarding and sand sledding on the dunefield
jewels.booking_route: none needed in the park - boards are rented from San Luis Valley shops before arrival
jewels.blurb: "Sandboarding, sledding, and skiing are permitted anywhere on the dunefield away from vegetated areas." From the main Dunes Parking Area "it's a minimum 0.7 mile (1km) hike to get to the small or medium-sized slopes; the top of the first high ridge is 1.25 miles." "The National Park Service does not rent sand sleds or sandboards. Plan to rent gear before arriving at the park."

jewels.name: Medano Creek and its surge flow
jewels.booking_route: none needed - covered by the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: "When there's water in Medano Creek at the base of the dunes, adults and kids alike love to splash in the stream. Watch for waves in the water, a phenomenon called 'surge flow.'" Peak flow "in an average year occurs in late May or early June". ⚠️ 2026: "Snow pack in the Medano Creek watershed in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains is at near record low for this year."

jewels.name: Hidden Dune
jewels.booking_route: none needed - covered by the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: "Hidden Dune is the tallest dune in North America at 741 feet (225 m)." "Plan on 7 miles (11 km) round trip over 6 hours, starting from the main Dunes Parking Lot"; "A false summit... hides the actual summit for much of the hike".

jewels.name: Star Dune
jewels.booking_route: none needed - covered by the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: "currently the second tallest dune in North America. It is a majestic dune now measuring 736 feet (224 m) from base to summit." "From the Dunes Parking Lot, hike about 2 miles (3.2 km) south down the Medano Creek bed until the massive pyramid-shaped Star Dune comes into view. Follow a ridge to its summit."

jewels.name: Pinon Flats Campground
jewels.blurb: "located one mile north of the Visitor Center, open April through October. All sites are by reservation"; individual sites "$20/night", "88 sites, tents and/or RVs up to 25 feet (no hook-ups available)"; a few driveways fit RVs to 35 feet; restrooms with flush toilets and potable water in all three loops, no showers; "Each site has a bear locker". Group sites A and B (20-40 people, $80) and C (15-30 people, $65), tents only.

jewels.name: Dunes Backcountry and Sand Ramp Trail backpacking
jewels.blurb: "Great Sand Dunes National Park offers two different backpacking experiences - seven designated sites along the Sand Ramp Trail and 20 non-designated sites in the Dunes Backcountry." Permits "are only available through the Recreation.gov online permit system for a non-refundable fee of $6.00"; "No Permits are required for backpacking in the Great Sand Dunes National Preserve." Buck Creek, 1.0 mile from the Amphitheater lot, is "ideal for families with children who want a short backpacking hike".

jewels.name: Medano Pass Primitive Road
jewels.booking_route: none needed - own high-clearance 4WD, or a 4WD tour/rental from the operators the NPS lists
jewels.blurb: "4-Wheel Drive (4WD) high-clearance vehicles with a 4L transfer case setting ARE REQUIRED on this road. All-Wheel-Drive (AWD) vehicles, mini-SUVs, wagons, and similar vehicles with lower clearance are not permitted"; "there is no cellular signal along the Medano Pass Primitive Road". Conditions as of October 2nd, 2026: OPEN, with "difficult and deep water conditions at the 3rd, 4th, and 5th Creek Crossings." Camping "in one of 21 sites" first-come, first-served when open.

jewels.name: International Dark Sky Park nights
jewels.booking_route: none needed - the park is open 24 hours
jewels.blurb: "Half the park is after dark! With a combination of dry air, little light pollution, and high elevation, Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve is certified as an International Dark Sky Park by Dark Sky International"; view "at least 1 1/2 hours after sunset, or 1 1/2 hours before sunrise"; "August and September provide some of the best night skies of the year".

jewels.name: Great Sand Dunes Junior Ranger programme
jewels.booking_route: none needed - pick up the booklet at the Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: "plan on a total visit of at least 2 hours to complete the Junior Ranger Booklet, available at the visitor center. There are three different age groups in the booklet: 3-6, 7-9, 10-12, and 13 and up." Completers "earn a Great Sand Dunes Junior Ranger Badge"; the booklet can be downloaded before the visit.

jewels.name: Free dunes sand wheelchairs
jewels.booking_route: phone reservation with the Visitor Center, 719-378-6395 (free loan)
jewels.blurb: "Visitors can reserve the free use of special balloon-tire wheelchairs to access the dunes. You'll need a strong helper to push the chair through sand." A 4-wheel or 3-wheel chair; leave an ID at the Visitor Center; "Reserve a wheelchair in advance by calling the visitor center at 719-378-6395." One chair "has been provided by Friends of the Dunes."

jewels.name: Great Sand Dunes Visitor Center
jewels.booking_route: none needed - 11999 State Highway 150, Mosca, CO 81146; (719) 378-6395
jewels.blurb: "Rangers are present to assist you with trip planning, Junior Ranger books and badges, directions, and other questions"; exhibits include "a large diorama depicting park and preserve ecosystems, a night sky video" and "a 3D model of the valley"; a 20-minute park video. Open daily 9:00 am - 4:30 pm "except Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's Day" (2025 hours as posted).

jewels.name: Horseback riding in the park and preserve
jewels.booking_route: none needed for day rides; backcountry stock camping by permit
jewels.blurb: "Most of the national park and the entire national preserve are open to horse use"; trailers park at "the horse trailer parking area at the beginning of the Medano Pass Primitive Road"; horses may camp at the Little Medano, Aspen, Cold Creek and Sand Creek backcountry sites with a permit. Pinon Flats, the Dunes Parking Lot area to High Dune and the Wellington Ditch Trail are closed to horses.

jewels.name: Closed-toe boots for 150-degree sand
jewels.blurb: NPS: "High-top boots with long pants work best to keep sand out of your shoes. Do not wear sandals, which will just chafe your feet. If you must hike on a summer afternoon, bring closed-toe boots or shoes to prevent burning your feet." And: "Keep your close-toed shoes/boots with you while riding boards so that you can walk on hot sand before and after riding."

jewels.name: Sun hat, sunscreen, layers and wind goggles
jewels.blurb: NPS ranger tips: "Protect yourself from the cold and sun with sunscreen, sunglasses, and DRINK plenty of water. The air is usually very dry in this high elevation semi-desert environment." "Wear Layered Clothing - Be prepared for chilly nights and sunny cool to warm days, windy conditions"; "Goggles can be a handy item during higher wind days."

jewels.name: Dunes backpacking kit: sand stakes and a gallon of water a night
jewels.blurb: The park's Recreation.gov permit page: "Backpackers must carry 1 gallon of water/person/night as there is no creek to filter"; "Secure tents with sand stakes or sandbags. Strong winds may occur any time of year." "Sand temperatures may reach 150° F on summer afternoons. Wear closed-toe shoes".

jewels.name: Great Dunes Oasis Board Shop
jewels.booking_route: walk-in only - "No apps, no online booking"; 719-378-2222
jewels.blurb: Named by the NPS as "located 4 miles from the Great Sand Dunes Visitor Center near the park entrance". Its own page: "Sand Board : $20 / day (+ tax) Sand Sled: $20 / day (+ tax)"; "No reservations needed. Just stop by the board shop during open hours"; "Daily Rentals are due back by 3:30 pm". Board Shop 9a-4p.

jewels.name: Great Sand Dunes Oasis campground and motel
jewels.booking_route: phone only - 719-378-2222 ("No apps, no online booking")
jewels.blurb: "The last stop before the tallest sand dunes in North America. Store, restaurant, R.V. spaces, rooms, cabins, tent sites, and board rentals; just minutes away from the park entrance." Wilderness tent sites $33 (first-come, first-served), 20 full-hookup pull-thru RV sites at $55, rustic cabins $88, motel $219 (open 5/1 to 9/30), four group tent sites for 10-75 people. "Just our family serving yours since 1985."

jewels.name: Rustic Rook Resort
jewels.blurb: "Choose from Fully Furnished Glamping Tents, Grain Bin Villas, Camper Cabins and BYO Tent Sites"; "located just 19 miles from the Great Sand Dunes National Park entrance"; "enjoy a complimentary hot breakfast each morning and S'mores by the campfire at night"; sled rental and an International Dark Skies page. "Grain Bins open year around | All other sites open May 18th 2026 - Oct 3rd".

jewels.name: Zapata Falls Campground and Recreation Area
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov (the NPS: "Zapata Falls Campground is now by reservation on recreation.gov")
jewels.blurb: BLM / Colorado State Land Board area "approximately 5 miles south of Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve", campground "3.5 miles (5.8km) up an unpaved road. Elevation 9,088ft." "23 Individual sites (11 Tent, 12 RV, 1 Group Tent...)", vault toilets, "No public drinking water system", "no hookup services". The trail to the falls is "rocky and steep" - wading the creek "is the only way to reach the falls."

jewels.name: Base Camp Family Campground and RV Park
jewels.blurb: "Voted #1 Campground in Alamosa Colorado": "Largest Pull Through Sites In The Area-100' x 40'", "Big-Rig-Friendly", full hookups, huge tent sites with a 10x10 shelter, dry cabins ("Electric Only - Bring Your Own Bedding"), large private showers, laundry, and "Sand Board & Sand Sled Rentals (Site Delivery Available)".

jewels.name: Cool Sunshine RV Park
jewels.blurb: "a pet-friendly RV park with 41 camp sites (full hookup back-in sites and pull through sites) and 6 tent sites", "just a block from downtown" Alamosa, with a clubhouse and a covered patio with putting green; "over 30 restaurants within a 15 minute walk".

jewels.name: Alamosa / Great Sand Dunes KOA Journey
jewels.blurb: A KOA Journey campground: "Pull-through RV Sites with 50-amp service", "Premium Tent Sites" and lodging; "Panoramic Mountain Views". The NPS lists it "31 miles southwest of Great Sand Dunes Visitor Center, 4 miles east of Alamosa. RVs, hookups, tents, cabins. Open warmer months only."

jewels.name: Hampton Inn Alamosa
jewels.blurb: Listed by Visit Alamosa: "Hampton Inn Alamosa combines modern comforts with small-town hospitality, offering a convenient home base near downtown Alamosa, Great Sand Dunes National Park, and the best of the San Luis Valley." The brand page was not fetched (hilton.com routinely refuses), so nothing else is stated here.

jewels.name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Alamosa
jewels.blurb: Listed by Visit Alamosa: "Located on the west side of Alamosa near shopping, entertainment, and local attractions, Fairfield Inn & Suites offers a comfortable stay with modern amenities and easy access to Great Sand Dunes National Park and Adams State University." The brand page was not fetched (marriott.com routinely refuses).

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Alamosa
jewels.blurb: Listed by American Southwest at "3418 Mariposa Street, Alamosa, CO 81101": "74 rooms and suites", "an indoor pool, (small) fitness center, whirlpool and free breakfast bar"; "the Great Sand Dunes, is 33 miles away." The guide carries affiliate links (its own disclosure); the IHG page was not fetched.

jewels.name: Kristi Mountain Sports
jewels.blurb: "Since 1969, Kristi Mountain Sports has been the San Luis Valley's premier location for all your biking, hiking, camping, climbing, skiing, snowboarding, and sandboarding needs"; "Sandboard & Sled Rentals $20/day"; "Walk-in's welcome!" The NPS: rents "year round. Call (719) 589-9759 the day before to reserve a board... Closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays."

jewels.name: Spindrift Sandboards
jewels.blurb: "Located just 25 miles from Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve, Spindrift Sandboards offers the premier sandboarding and sandsledding experience in Blanca, Colorado"; "Rentals start at $20 per board or sled per day, plus tax"; "Instruction available for new riders"; "After-hours drop-off available upon request".

jewels.name: Dunes 4x4 Ltd
jewels.blurb: Half-day 4x4 adventure tours: "travel along the Medano Pass 4x4 road, winding along the edge of the dune field and up into the Sangre de Cristo mountains"; "We provide beverages and snacks along the way, stretch our legs and hike in the creek, into the dunes, and there is opportunity for sand boarding too." Listed by the NPS for 4WD tours, 303-564-7705.

jewels.name: Kaiyote Tours
jewels.blurb: Its own site lists "Sand Dunes N.P." tours in "Birding", "Hiking" and "Overnight Backpacking", alongside Rocky Mountain N.P. "Family and Group Tours". The NPS: "This company offers guided birding, hiking, or overnight backpacking tours of Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve. 970-556-6103."

jewels.name: Great Sand Dunes Oasis Restaurant
jewels.blurb: "Hot meals, cold drinks, and a view of the dunes. Breakfast, lunch, and dinner" - breakfast burritos "smothered with your choice of secret family recipe red or green chili", huevos rancheros, a kids' menu; "Groups of 6 or more add 18% gratuity". ⚠️ The home page on 2026-10-03 read "Restaurant: Closed for the Season".

jewels.name: Dune Valley Distillery
jewels.booking_route: own website - board rental appointments and event tickets; email for private tastings
jewels.blurb: "Producing unique Colorado vodkas made from local Potato and Quinoa"; "BOARDS BOTTLES & BEBIDAS and small bites", sandboard rentals, an event and music venue; "We are about 15 miles north of Alamosa and a stones throw away from the Great Sand Dunes". September 2026 hours Thursday-Saturday 11am-8pm, Tuesday & Wednesday 11am-5pm.

jewels.name: San Luis Valley Brewing Company
jewels.blurb: 631 Main Street, Alamosa: "OPEN 7 DAYS A WEEK!", 11am-10pm daily; year-round beers include Alamosa Amber, Ol' 169 Oatmeal Stout and the chili beer Valle Caliente; "we seek out the highest quality ingredients to ensure our beer has the full flavor and excellence that define a great small-batch craft brewery."

jewels.name: Calvillo's Mexican Restaurant
jewels.blurb: Visit Alamosa: "dedicated to serving authentic Mexican cuisine, offering a diverse menu that highlights the rich culinary traditions and regional dishes from various states across Mexico"; "an all-day buffet", a full bar and "a banquet room, making it suitable for both casual dining and hosting larger group events". 400 Main Street, (719) 587-5500.

jewels.name: Milagros Coffeehouse
jewels.blurb: Visit Alamosa: "a 501(c)3 nonprofit and a social enterprise of La Puente" serving "simple, healthy, delicious food and beverages"; "All proceeds go to support the social services of La Puente." 529 Main Street, 719-589-9299.

jewels.name: Sand Dunes Recreation hot springs pool
jewels.blurb: "Natural Hot artesian Oasis" north of Hooper, with "Cabins, RV & Tent Sites", The Greenhouse, the Mile Deep Grille "located near main pool" and the Pivot Public House; "ENTIRE FACILITY IS CLOSED EVERY THURSDAY FOR CLEANING". The NPS lists it as "privately owned facility located 32 miles west" with a "geothermal swimming pool", open year round, and it rents sandsleds and sandboards.

jewels.name: Mile Deep Grille at Sand Dunes Recreation
jewels.blurb: The hot-springs facility's restaurant, "located near main pool", with a small-plates menu in The Greenhouse; the facility is closed every Thursday. Menu and hours were not published on the page read.

jewels.name: Colorado Gators Reptile Rescue
jewels.blurb: "See hundreds of rescued reptiles including alligators, crocodiles, caiman, tortoises, and turtles"; "All visitors to Colorado Gators have the opportunity to pet, hold, and take pictures with a small alligator!" 2026: open daily 9am-5pm February 27 - November 01. Admission: 5 and under free, 6-15 $15, 16-64 $30, "Ages 65-79 $15", 80 and over free. 9162 Lane 9 N, Mosca.

faq.q: Is Great Sand Dunes National Park free?
faq.a: No. The NPS lists "Private Vehicle: $25.00", "Motorcycle: $20.00" and "Per Person: $15.00" for visitors 16 or older (children under 16 enter free), or "Annual Entrance - Park: $45.00".

faq.q: Do you need reservations for Great Sand Dunes National Park?
faq.a: Not to enter: "There are no advance reservations, timed entries, or visitor limits at Great Sand Dunes. It is optional to purchase your entrance pass in advance." Camping at Pinon Flats is by reservation only on Recreation.gov.

faq.q: Can you camp at Great Sand Dunes National Park?
faq.a: Yes. Pinon Flats Campground is "open April through October. All sites are by reservation on recreation.gov or call 1-877-444-6777. Individual and group sites can be reserved up to 3 months in advance." Backpackers camp in the Dunes Backcountry or at Sand Ramp Trail sites with a $6.00 Recreation.gov permit.

faq.q: Can you sandboard at Great Sand Dunes National Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Sandboarding, sledding, and skiing are permitted anywhere on the dunefield away from vegetated areas." But "The National Park Service does not rent sand sleds or sandboards. Plan to rent gear before arriving at the park." The nearest listed rental is the Great Dunes Oasis Store, 4 miles from the Visitor Center.

faq.q: Do you need 4WD for Great Sand Dunes National Park?
faq.a: Not for the main park area - Highway 150 and County Road 6 "are paved highways". Only the Medano Pass Primitive Road needs it: "4-Wheel Drive (4WD) high-clearance vehicles with a 4L transfer case setting ARE REQUIRED on this road."

faq.q: Can you ride ATVs at Great Sand Dunes National Park?
faq.a: No: "Mechanized or motorized vehicles are not permitted on the dunefield, and ATVs are not permitted in the park and preserve." The dunes "were made a wilderness by Congress in 1976".

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Great Sand Dunes National Park?
faq.a: Yes, on a leash of 6 feet or less, in the main use areas: "Pets are permitted in the Preserve (including Mosca Pass Trail) and main use areas of the Park (including Pinon Flats Campground, Dunes Overlook Trail, and along the Medano Pass Primitive Road)." They are not permitted "In the backcountry of the dunefield, beyond the first high ridge of dunes". The NPS warns of sand "up to 150 degrees F" and suggests pet booties.

faq.q: What is the closest airport to Great Sand Dunes National Park?
faq.a: "Commercial air service is available to a small airport at Alamosa, Colorado, 38 miles from Great Sand Dunes. Colorado Springs, Denver, and Albuquerque are served by many commercial airlines. Rental cars are available at all these airports."

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Great Sand Dunes National Park?
faq.a: It depends on what you come for. "September has some of the best weather of the year, with an average high of 71 F and a low of 42 F." For the creek, "Late May and early June are the best opportunity to experience 'surge flow'" - but those weekends "are extremely crowded". In summer, "always plan your dunes time for early morning or evening".

faq.q: When is Great Sand Dunes National Park open?
faq.a: "Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, year round." The Visitor Center was posted as open "daily 9:00 am - 4:30 pm throughout the year, except Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's Day" (2025 hours); Pinon Flats Campground is open April through October.

seo.meta_title: Great Sand Dunes National Park: Dunes, Sandboarding & Camping | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: North America's tallest dunes: High Dune and Star Dune hikes, sandboard rentals nearby, Pinon Flats camping booked 3 months out, and dark-sky nights.

name: Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park
line: Sheer black walls above the Gunnison River

jewels.name: South Rim Drive and its 12 overlooks
jewels.booking_route: none needed - included in the park entrance pass ($30 private vehicle, 7 days)
jewels.blurb: "The South Rim Drive is a scenic paved road that follows the canyon rim for 7 miles from Tomichi Point to High Point and features 12 overlooks." "Allow 2 to 3 hours to view all 12 overlooks." Season spring to fall; it "generally opens to vehicular access in mid- to late April". "The South Rim Drive is an accessible way to take in the scenic views along the canyon rim."

jewels.name: The Painted Wall
jewels.booking_route: none needed - seen from the rim overlooks
jewels.blurb: "The Painted Wall is the tallest vertical wall in Colorado, with a height of 2,250 ft (686 m)". From the North Rim, the Chasm View Nature Trail "breaks out of the pinyon/juniper forest at the North Chasm View to provide excellent views of Painted Wall and Serpent Point."

jewels.name: Warner Point Trail
jewels.blurb: "At its deepest, the canyon is 2,722 ft (830 m) deep at Warner Point." The trail starts at High Point at the end of the South Rim Drive; 0.8 mi one way, "Moderate strenuous": "Looking south, you can see the San Juan Mountain Range, Uncompahgre Valley, and Bostwick Park. Looking north, enjoy views of the West Elk Mountains." Pets not allowed; "steep in places and not wheelchair accessible."

jewels.name: South Rim Visitor Center
jewels.booking_route: none needed - no separate fee beyond park entrance; 9800 Hwy 347, Montrose
jewels.blurb: "a great first-stop": "get recommendations from park rangers, tour the interactive exhibits, watch the park movie, shop the park bookstore"; "Maps, newspapers, junior ranger books, and wilderness permits are available here." Open all year except Christmas Day and New Year's Day; "In the summer, the parking lot often fills." A 3D tactile map and rock samples for blind and low-vision visitors.

jewels.name: North Rim Road
jewels.booking_route: none needed - included in the park entrance pass
jewels.blurb: "The North Rim Road is unpaved and provides access to 6 overlooks"; "Allow 2-3 hours for a leisurely tour"; "The canyon walls on the North Rim are almost vertical, offering impressive views." Season summer and fall - "The North Rim is closed to vehicles in the winter and early spring." "There are no accessible or paved overlooks."

jewels.name: East Portal Road to the Gunnison River
jewels.booking_route: none needed - reached only from inside the park
jewels.blurb: "Continue down the East Portal Road for 5.2 miles (8.4 km). The road will become steep and windy. In a few places, the road is a 16% grade"; "Vehicles over 22 feet are prohibited on the East Portal Road." At the bottom: East Portal Campground, river access and the Gunnison Tunnel and Diversion Dam exhibits. "The road is closed in winter, typically from November to April."

jewels.name: International Dark Sky Park stargazing
jewels.booking_route: none needed - programmes listed on the park calendar
jewels.blurb: "Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park was certified as an International Dark Sky Park in September 2015", with "stargazing programs scheduled throughout the summer months." "The park does not close and allows for night sky viewing at all hours." Named viewing spots: Chasm View, Dragon Point and Sunset View overlooks (South Rim); Chasm View Nature Trail and Kneeling Camel Overlook (North Rim).

jewels.name: Junior Ranger and Night Explorer booklets
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free at the South Rim Visitor Center or downloadable
jewels.blurb: "Pick up a Junior Ranger Activity Booklet at the Black Canyon of the Gunnison South Rim Visitor Center"; requirements include "writing your observations, drawing pictures, completing field activities, and attending a ranger-led program." The free Junior Ranger Night Explorer booklet teaches how to "find the North Star, track the phases of the moon, use a planisphere".

jewels.name: Ranger programmes on the South Rim
jewels.booking_route: none needed - "Reservations are not required for all programs"
jewels.blurb: Duration 20-60 minutes: "Ranger programs are offered as either short talks, guided walks, or illustrated evening programs at the campground." Season year round; "Geology programs are offered at accessible overlooks. Campground evening programs can be accessed by a ramp; wheelchairs require assistance due to steepness."

jewels.name: Chasm View Nature Trail (North Rim)
jewels.blurb: 0.3 mi, Easy, from the North Rim Campground: "This short loop trail breaks out of the pinyon/juniper forest at the North Chasm View to provide excellent views of Painted Wall and Serpent Point." One of the two trails where leashed dogs are allowed. Season spring to fall.

jewels.name: Rim Rock Trail
jewels.blurb: 1 mile, Moderate: "Rim Rock Trail is a popular trail connecting the South Rim Campground and South Rim Visitor Center. It is rocky, contains stairs, and passes by steep drop-offs with views into Black Canyon." Leashed dogs allowed. Condition on the day read: "Trail passes through heavily burned area; beware of uneven surfaces and blowing ash."

jewels.name: Oak Flat Loop Trail
jewels.blurb: 1.6 mi round trip, Strenuous, from the South Rim Visitor Center: "This 1.6 mi (2.6 km) trail offers variety to the hiker who would like to explore below the rim without going all the way to the river. The trail is narrow in places and traverses some steep slopes." Pets not allowed.

jewels.name: Cedar Point Nature Trail
jewels.blurb: "This short, moderately sloped trail offers visitors a chance to brush up on local flora with guideposts describing the various plants along the way." Leashed pets allowed.

jewels.name: Deadhorse Trail (North Rim)
jewels.blurb: 2.6 mi one way, or 6.6 mi round trip with the loop, Moderate, from Kneeling Camel Overlook: "Deadhorse Trail takes hikers into the Black Canyon of the Gunnison Wilderness Area. It offers good views of Deadhorse Gulch and East Portal on the Gunnison River, as well as good birding." Pets not allowed.

jewels.name: North Vista Trail to Exclamation Point
jewels.blurb: 1.6 mi to Exclamation Point or 3.6 mi to Green Mountain, Moderate, from the North Rim Ranger Station: "Constructed by the Volunteers for Outdoor Colorado, the North Vista Trail offers some of the best scenic views and birding in the park. Difficulty varies from moderate to strenuous based on distance."

jewels.name: Uplands Trail
jewels.blurb: 0.9 mi, Moderate: "This .9-mile (1.4 km) trail links the Rim Rock Trail (near the campground) to the upper Oak Flat Loop Trail near the South Rim Visitor Center." Pets not allowed; on the day read it "passes through heavily burned area".

jewels.name: South Rim Campground
jewels.blurb: "A limited number of sites (25, all non-electric) have reopened for camping" after the 2025 fire; fees "$34 (electric) $20 (non-electric)"; open year-round, "Sites available by reservation only, year-round. Reserve sites online at Recreation.gov". Recreation.gov notes no water hookups or dump station, "GENERATOR USE IS NOT PERMITTED", and "Bears frequent the area; all food must be kept in approved containers". Accessible sites A21 and B1.

jewels.name: North Rim Campground
jewels.booking_route: first-come first-served; pay by Recreation.gov Scan & Pay
jewels.blurb: 13 sites at $20; "All sites are first-come first-served, but payment MUST be submitted online using the Scan & Pay feature on Recreation.gov's mobile app"; water seasonal. The campground road is gravel and "all sites are unpaved and unimproved."

jewels.name: East Portal Campground
jewels.booking_route: first-come first-served; pay by Recreation.gov Scan & Pay
jewels.blurb: 15 sites at $20 (upper sites only open on the day read), first-come first-served with Scan & Pay, beside the Gunnison River at the foot of the East Portal Road; "All campsites are unimproved, and some require walking down steps from the parking area".

jewels.name: Inner Canyon wilderness routes
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov permit (South Rim, May 1-Oct 31); free day-of permit on the North Rim and in winter
jewels.blurb: "Permits are required for all inner canyon wilderness use - both day and overnight trips." South Rim routes: Gunnison (15-person limit), Tomichi (9), Warner (23); North Rim: Pinyon Draw, Long Draw, Slide Draw. "Wilderness routes are not trails; they are unmarked, physically demanding, very steep scrambles with loose rock." North Rim permits are free, first-come first-served on the day.

jewels.name: Rock climbing the Chasm Walls
jewels.booking_route: wilderness use permit (see Inner Canyon routes)
jewels.blurb: "Black Canyon is a full-on adventure climbing area"; of "the 145 climbing routes", 117 rate between 5.10 and 5.13 "and many require aid." "The majority of the climbing activity takes place around North and South Chasm Walls, where the canyon is 1,820 ft (555 m) deep." A wilderness use permit applies; raptor closures March 15 to July 15. "Rock climbing at Black Canyon is not recommended for beginners."

jewels.name: Winter snowshoeing and cross-country skiing
jewels.booking_route: none needed - check the park calendar for ranger snowshoe walks
jewels.blurb: Open in winter: Tomichi and Gunnison Point overlooks, the South Rim Visitor Center and the trails; closed: East Portal Road, North Rim Road and the South Rim Road beyond the visitor center. Snowshoe on the "South Rim Ski and Snowshoe Trail (beginner level)" or the upper Oak Flat Loop (intermediate); rangers may lead guided snowshoe walks "January to mid-March".

jewels.name: Inner-canyon kit: four quarts of water a day
jewels.blurb: NPS kit for wilderness routes: "4 quarts of water per person per day, or a water filter if filling up at the river", high-energy food, waste bags, rain gear, sturdy boots, map/compass, first aid kit, sun protection, and headlamp with batteries. On the rim: "Remember that if you're thirsty, you're already dehydrated. Drink water often."

jewels.name: Layers and rain or snow gear for 8,000 feet
jewels.blurb: NPS: conditions "vary greatly between the canyon rim (approximately 8,000 feet) and canyon floor (approximately 6,000 feet)... Layered clothing appropriate for each season is recommended." "Be prepared for all conditions by dressing in layers, bringing rain or snow gear, and proper footwear."

jewels.name: Red-light headlamp for the Dark Sky Park
jewels.blurb: NPS: "For all nighttime activities in the park, red light-equipped headlamps or flashlights are best to help preserve night vision and reduce light pollution." In winter the park suggests "cross-country skiing by moonlight or headlamp."

jewels.name: Binoculars for wildlife watching
jewels.blurb: NPS "Know Before You Go": "Bring binoculars or a camera lens with zoom capabilities"; "Wear clothing that blends in with environment". For bears: "Do not run. Back away slowly. Break eye contact."

jewels.name: Bear-resistant food storage at the campground
jewels.blurb: Recreation.gov notice for South Rim Campground: "Bears frequent the area; all food must be kept in approved containers". On the trails the NPS adds: "Keep your backpack within arms reach at all times."

jewels.name: Montrose
jewels.booking_route: none needed - a gateway town; Office of Business and Tourism, 107 South Cascade Avenue, 970-497-8558
jewels.blurb: The South Rim Visitor Center sits "14 miles (22.5 km) northeast of Montrose, Colorado"; "The nearest restaurants and hotels are in Montrose, CO" (NPS). The city's tourism office: "You can find everything from charming bed and breakfasts to well-known and conveniently located major hotel brands" - 14 hotels listed on the day read.

jewels.name: Montrose Black Canyon KOA
jewels.blurb: 200 N Cedar Ave, Montrose: "Open all year... All sites have 30/50-amp pull-throughs - some are 75 feet long!"; heated pool, hot tub, laundry, gift shop, playground and "large open-air pavilion with free gas grills"; free Wi-Fi at each site. (970) 249-9177. KOA's own page returned 403 when fetched.

jewels.name: Riverbend RV Park and Cabins
jewels.blurb: 65120 Old Chipeta Trail, Montrose: "Montrose's only boutique RV park offering wide and level FHU RV sites, clean and well-stocked riverfront and rustic cabins, and tent camping on the river" - "74 FHU RV sites", a fenced dog park, river access, cruiser bikes and free coffee. Listed as handicap accessible. (970) 249-8235. Own site returned 403.

jewels.name: Cedar Creek RV Park and Lodging
jewels.blurb: 126 Rose Ln, Montrose: RV stays, tent sites, tiny homes and extended stays; pull-through full-hookup 50-amp sites published at "Nightly Week Day: $55 Nightly Weekend $60" in summer, with weekly and seasonal monthly rates. Its own seasonal note: "Fall (Sep-Nov): Mild to crisp... Fall foliage drives/hiking (peak Sep-mid-Oct aspens)".

jewels.name: The Hop Yard Hideaway bell tents
jewels.blurb: Billy Goat Hop Farm, Montrose: 15 sites on 35 acres, "Within a 60-minute drive from the South Rim Entrance Station". Four lodging sites are 16-foot bell tents, "fully outfitted tents with one queen bed, two twin beds, bedding, pillows, and towels" with lights and electric; 11 RV/tent sites (vehicles under 35 ft). "Fridays on the Farm" (May 22 to October 2) bring a beer barn, food truck and live music. 98% from 137 reviews.

jewels.name: Crawford State Park
jewels.blurb: Colorado Parks and Wildlife: "The park has 337 acres of land and a 400-acre reservoir. The park's 6,600-foot elevation means the climate is mild at any season"; 66 campsites, 220 species of birds, 3.2 miles of trails; one mile south of Crawford, the North Rim's gateway town. Daily vehicle pass $15-$17 for out-of-state plates. Boat ramps closed for the rest of 2026; hand-launched craft allowed.

jewels.name: Ridgway State Park
jewels.blurb: CPW: "nearly 300 campsites across three campgrounds (Elk Ridge, Dakota Terraces, and Pa-Co-Chu-Puk), accommodating tents, trailers, and RVs", "three year-round yurts" and "15.6 miles of diverse trails"; "accessible restrooms, showers, campsites, fishing piers, beach access, and trails". CPW names Black Canyon of the Gunnison among the places to explore from it.

jewels.name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Montrose
jewels.blurb: Listed by the City of Montrose at "25 Tributary Street, Montrose, CO 81401", (970) 230-3777, linking to Marriott's property page. Marriott's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Hampton Inn Montrose
jewels.blurb: 1980 N. Townsend Ave, Montrose, (970) 252-3300: "Offering a complimentary airport shuttle"; free hot breakfast and "Hampton On the Run® Breakfast Bags"; indoor pool and whirlpool; "meeting space for up to 64 guests"; pet-friendly. Hilton's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403).

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Montrose
jewels.blurb: 1391 S. Townsend Ave, Montrose, (970) 240-1800: "122 large rooms and suites", indoor pool and spa, outdoor spa, complimentary full breakfast, "pet-friendly, 100% non-smoking and free airport shuttle service is available upon request"; listed as handicap accessible. IHG's own page refused the fetch (HTTP 403).

jewels.name: Elk Mountain Resort
jewels.blurb: 97 Elk Walk Road, Montrose: "Located just 20 miles southwest of downtown Montrose at an elevation of 9,000 feet", with a private heliport, health club, tennis, shooting range and a "Wine Mine"; pet-friendly. On the day read: "Starting Sept 8th, 2026 Resort is open Thursday/Friday/Saturday From 4pm - 8pm". 970.901.5370.

jewels.name: Gunnison River Expeditions
jewels.blurb: Hotchkiss: "guided float fishing and white water rafting trips through the Black Canyon of the Gunnison Gorge. This stretch of Gold Medal water is famous for world class rainbow and brown trout fishing"; "Established in 1985", it calls itself "the largest, most experienced fly fishing outfitter on the Gunnison River" - wilderness float fishing, walk/wade trips, "Class III-IV white water rafting", equipment rentals and lodging. "Booking Now for Summer and Fall 2026".

jewels.name: Ed's Fly Shop
jewels.blurb: 432 E Main St, Montrose: "Fly Fishing Guides and Gear, Gunnison River" - rods, reels, waders, sun protection, camping kit (Helinox, Sea to Summit, Goal Zero) and a guide service for the Gunnison Gorge, Uncompahgre and San Miguel rivers. 970-964-9991.

jewels.name: Camp Robber
jewels.blurb: 1515 Ogden Rd, Montrose: opened by Bill and Kim Volk "in 1994 in downtown Montrose"; salads, pastas, steaks, seafood and New Mexican food - "what we are best known for - Green Chile Pistachio Pork Medallions and Green Chile Chicken Potato Soup"; the Robbers Roost Bar. (970) 240-1590.

jewels.name: Horsefly Brewing Company
jewels.blurb: 846 East Main Street, Montrose: "No Crap on Tap"; house beers, handcrafted cocktails and pub food including "award winning burgers"; "Our family friendly establishment has plenty of room including dining on our spacious outdoor patio" with frequent live music. Open every day at 11am; (970) 249-6889.

jewels.name: Colorado Boy Pizzeria & Brewery
jewels.blurb: 320 E. Main St., Montrose: "An Authentic Pizzeria & Brewery In Downtown Montrose, Colorado"; open 4:00-9:00 p.m. on the day read; (970) 240-2790.

jewels.name: Storm King Distilling Co.
jewels.booking_route: walk-in tasting room; tours on request; (970) 765-5606
jewels.blurb: 41 W. Main St., Montrose: named for Storm King peak above the Uncompahgre Valley; craft spirits from raw materials "locally sourced whenever possible"; a tasting room and patio with an evolving cocktail programme - "Make sure to ask about a tour when you come in". (970) 765-5606.

jewels.name: Bluecorn Cafe & Mercantile
jewels.blurb: 1842 S Townsend, Montrose: "award-winning coffee, fresh goodies baked from scratch and healthy breakfast, brunch & lunch starring local ingredients", plus the handcrafted beeswax candle mercantile and ticketed live events at the candle factory.

jewels.name: LaNoue DuBois Winery
jewels.blurb: 67289 Trout Rd, Montrose: estate-grown, high-elevation wines with "amazing views of the San Juans"; "LaNoue DuBois Winery earned the 2025 Colorado Wine of the Year award"; tasting room and wine club. Neighbour to the Hop Yard Hideaway. (970) 964-5112.

faq.q: Do you need reservations for Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park?
faq.a: No. The NPS states: "No reservations are required to enter Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park." An entrance pass is still required - "Although an entrance pass is required... vehicle reservations are not needed." South Rim campsites are by reservation only on Recreation.gov.

faq.q: How much are tickets for Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park?
faq.a: The NPS lists "Private Vehicle $30.00 7-Day Vehicle Pass", "Motorcycle $25.00 Valid for 7 days" and "Per Person $15.00 7-Day Individual Pass (pedestrian or bicycle)"; "An annual pass to Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park is available for $55.00."

faq.q: Can you camp in Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park?
faq.a: Yes, at three campgrounds. South Rim Campground is "by reservation only, year-round" on Recreation.gov, with "25, all non-electric" sites reopened after the 2025 fire; North Rim (13 sites) and East Portal (15 sites) are "first-come first-served, but payment MUST be submitted online using the Scan & Pay feature on Recreation.gov's mobile app". Inner-canyon camping needs a Wilderness Use Permit.

faq.q: Can you drive through Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park?
faq.a: Not from rim to rim: "There is no bridge or road through the park or connecting the rims. Both rim drives have one access point from the highway, and dead-end within the park. Driving from one rim to the other involves driving along non-park roads and can take 2+ hours."

faq.q: What is the difference between the North Rim and South Rim of Black Canyon of the Gunnison?
faq.a: The NPS: "South Rim is the busier, more developed side of the park. It is closer to Montrose, CO and U.S. Highway 50" - with the South Rim Drive, visitor center and campground. "The north rim of Black Canyon is rugged and primitive with limited services", reached by car seasonally.

faq.q: How long do you need in Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park?
faq.a: For the South Rim Drive, the NPS says "Allow 2 to 3 hours to view all 12 overlooks"; for the North Rim Road, "Allow 2-3 hours for a leisurely tour"; and "Allow 2 to 3 hours to drive from one rim to the other."

faq.q: How far is Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park from Denver?
faq.a: Measured from the South Rim Visitor Center, the NPS gives "264 miles (425 km) southwest of Denver, Colorado"; Montrose is 14 miles away and Grand Junction 75 miles.

faq.q: Can dogs go to Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park?
faq.a: On a leash, in limited places: "Leashed pets are permitted in picnic areas, campgrounds, and parking lots, on paths to overlooks, and along roads currently open to vehicles. Leashed pets are only permitted on the Rim Rock Trail and on the North Rim Chasm View Nature Trail." Leashes must be no longer than six feet.

faq.q: When was Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park established?
faq.a: "It was established as a national monument on March 2, 1933 and redesignated as a national park on October 21, 1999."

faq.q: What is the elevation of Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park?
faq.a: "Due to its steepness and elevation change, conditions can vary greatly between the canyon rim (approximately 8,000 feet) and canyon floor (approximately 6,000 feet)." The NPS advises: "Take precautions, drink plenty of water, and slow down."

name: Yellowstone National Park
line: Geysers on a timetable, a canyon with a 308-foot waterfall, and a valley where the NPS says bison and elk draw wolves and grizzlies

jewels.name: Old Faithful and the Upper Geyser Basin
jewels.blurb: about 150 geysers in one square mile; as of January 2025 the median interval between Old Faithful eruptions is "102 minutes ± 10 minutes", and rangers predict it and five other geysers; predictions posted at the Old Faithful Visitor Education Center

jewels.name: Grand Prismatic Spring, Midway Geyser Basin
jewels.blurb: "Perhaps the most photographed hot spring", beside Excelsior Geyser, which in the late 1800s erupted over 300 feet; the NPS warns of crowded parking in summer and suggests off-hours

jewels.name: Fairy Falls Trail and the Grand Prismatic Overlook
jewels.blurb: a 5.4-mile hike from the southern trailhead to the 200-foot Fairy Falls, with a side trail to the overlook above Grand Prismatic Spring; the overlook has grades up to 19% and is not currently accessible

jewels.name: Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone, Artist Point and the Brink of the Lower Falls
jewels.blurb: roughly 20 miles long and more than 1,000 feet deep; the Lower Falls drops 308 feet and the Upper Falls 109 feet; Artist Point on the South Rim, and Lookout, Inspiration and Grand View points plus the Brink of the Lower Falls on North Rim Drive

jewels.name: Lamar Valley and the northern range
jewels.blurb: "one of the major summer grounds for bison and elk, which attracts predators like wolves and grizzly bears"; the NPS says road pullouts are the places to watch from, and to keep at least 100 yards from bears and wolves and 25 yards from all other animals

jewels.name: The 2026 road and entrance season
jewels.blurb: entrances are not gated at night when open; roads opened in stages April 17 to May 22, 2026; most close October 31, 2026 and the Dunraven, Beartooth and Chief Joseph passes October 12; the North Entrance-to-Cooke City road is the one generally open year-round

jewels.name: Winter oversnow season and the Non-Commercially Guided Snowmobile Access Program
jewels.blurb: roads open to oversnow travel "usually by mid-December"; Old Faithful reachable only by guided snowmobile or snowcoach or under the program - up to four non-commercial groups a day by lottery, $40/day plus $6 application, five snowmobiles per permit

jewels.name: Old Faithful Snow Lodge, winter 2026-27
jewels.blurb: open December 16, 2026 to March 7, 2027 and reached only by commercial over-snow transportation; Mammoth Hot Springs Hotel is "the only hotel accessible by personal vehicle during the winter months"

jewels.name: In-park lodges: Old Faithful Inn and eight more
jewels.blurb: nine lodging options run by Yellowstone National Park Lodges, the authorized concessioner - Old Faithful Inn (May to mid-October), Lake Yellowstone Hotel, Canyon Lodge, Mammoth Hot Springs Hotel, Roosevelt Lodge Cabins and others; the NPS says lodging "fills quickly"

jewels.name: Roosevelt Old West Dinner Cookout, horseback and stagecoach rides
jewels.blurb: from Roosevelt Corral: 1- or 2-hour horseback rides (age 8 and up), a replica Tally-Ho stagecoach, and a cookout at Yancy's Hole reached by horse, stagecoach or covered wagon; 2027 bookings open November 5, 2026

jewels.name: Yellowstone Tribal Heritage Center, Old Faithful
jewels.blurb: Indigenous artists and scholars from 27 Tribes offering photography, beadwork, moccasin making, dancing, storytelling and flintknapping; 2026 season May 25 to October 3

jewels.name: Yellowstone Expeditions Yurt Camp (winter)
jewels.blurb: a backcountry yurt camp "only one half mile from the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone", reached by tracked snow-vans from West Yellowstone; multi-day ski tours include guides, meals, lodging and rentals; taking 2026-2027 reservations

jewels.name: Under Canvas West Yellowstone
jewels.blurb: safari tents with ensuite bathrooms on the Bar N Ranch, about 10 minutes from the West Entrance; Stargazer tents, shared-bath Safari tents and a Madison River Suite for seven; restaurant, nightly campfires; 2027 season May 19 to September 7

jewels.name: Under Canvas North Yellowstone - Paradise Valley
jewels.blurb: tents with ensuite bathrooms and wood stoves between the Absaroka and Gallatin ranges, with over a mile of Yellowstone River frontage for fly fishing and Embers Cafe; 2027 season May 6 to September 30

jewels.name: Yellowstone Tipis, Gardiner
jewels.blurb: tipis with private spa bathrooms, breakfast and a gas fire pit at 50 Jardine Road, "minutes away from Yellowstone's North Entrance", plus the Hawkeye Suite house for up to 10; named Best Glamping in Distinctly Montana's 2023 rankings by its own account

jewels.name: Yellowstone Dreamin' Retreat, Paradise Valley
jewels.blurb: 12 canvas suites of 500 sq ft for four or six, with heated mattress pads, private fire pits and continental breakfast; shared restroom trailers; 27 miles from the park entrance by its own account; open summer only per the Gardiner chamber

jewels.name: Sun Outdoors Yellowstone North, Gardiner (glamping pods and RV)
jewels.blurb: pet-friendly glamping pods with private bathroom and kitchenette, standard and deluxe RV sites and a riverfront cabin for 10 at 14 Jardine Road, where the Yellowstone and Gardner rivers meet; open summer (chamber listing - own site returned 403)

jewels.name: Chico Hot Springs Resort, Pray (Conestoga wagons)
jewels.blurb: a historic Paradise Valley resort of more than 100 years with two geothermal pools, lodge rooms, cabins, chalets and glamping-style Conestoga Wagons, about 30 miles from the North Entrance; open year-round

jewels.name: Fireside Resort, Wilson (Jackson Hole)
jewels.blurb: LEED-certified cabins with private campfires, billed as "a hybrid between camping, a luxury hotel suite, and a private vacation rental cabin", at 2780 N Moose Wilson Road; RV sites run separately as Jackson Hole Campground; distance to Yellowstone not stated

jewels.name: Madison Campground (in park)
jewels.blurb: 276 sites, May 1 to October 17, 2026, reserved through Yellowstone National Park Lodges (yellowstonenationalparklodges.com)

jewels.name: Canyon Campground (in park)
jewels.blurb: 272 sites, May 29 to September 19, 2026, reserved through Yellowstone National Park Lodges

jewels.name: Fishing Bridge RV Park (in park)
jewels.blurb: 310 sites, May 8 to October 17, 2026, reserved through Yellowstone National Park Lodges

jewels.name: Mammoth Campground (NPS)
jewels.blurb: 82 sites, open year-round; recreation.gov in season and "first-come, first-served sites from October 15 - April 1" - the one exception to the rule that all campsites must be reserved in advance

jewels.name: Slough Creek Campground (NPS)
jewels.blurb: 16 sites in the northeast near the Lamar Valley, June 15 to October 12, 2026, reserved on recreation.gov

jewels.name: Yellowstone Grizzly RV Park & Cabins, West Yellowstone
jewels.blurb: full-hookup pull-through sites, luxury cabins and camping cabins with bath at 210 S Electric St, "just three blocks from the west entrance"; open year-round, booked through Campspot

jewels.name: Yellowstone Park / West Gate KOA Holiday
jewels.blurb: RV sites, cabins and tent sites about 6 miles from the West Entrance, with indoor heated pool, bike rentals and cafe; May through October (chamber listing - koa.com returned 403)

jewels.name: Yellowstone Park / Mountainside KOA Holiday
jewels.blurb: long pull-through RV sites, cabins by Denny Creek and tent sites 7.5 miles from the West Entrance, with trail access into the Gallatin National Forest; May through October (chamber listing)

jewels.name: Yellowstone RV Park & Campground, Gardiner
jewels.blurb: 46 full-hookup RV sites and river-view tent sites on the Yellowstone River at 121 Hwy 89 South, 1 mile from the North Entrance; 2027 reservations opened October 1, 2026

jewels.name: Yellowstone Hot Springs RV Park, Campground & Suites
jewels.blurb: three mineral pools (103-105°F, 98-100°F and a 60-65°F cold plunge) eight miles north of the North Entrance, with RV sites, tent camping, cabins and suites; day pass $10 per person

jewels.name: Island Park KOA Holiday, Idaho
jewels.blurb: formerly Valley View RV Park: full-hookup RV sites and deluxe cabins at 5152 N Hwy 20, about 10 miles from West Yellowstone (Island Park chamber listing)

jewels.name: RedRock RV Park, Island Park
jewels.blurb: RV sites at 3707 Redrock Road, away from highway traffic near Red Rock National Wildlife Refuge, 22 miles from the West Entrance (Island Park chamber listing)

jewels.name: Yellowstone Raft Company, Gardiner
jewels.blurb: Gardiner's first raft company (1978), on the Yellowstone River in the Yankee Jim Canyon area; holds NPS and Forest Service permits by its own account; published prices: 8 Mile Whitewater $76 (ages 5+), 18 Mile Whitewater $159, Scenic Float $79, 1-hour horseback $150

jewels.name: Wild West Rafting, Gardiner
jewels.blurb: half-day 8-mile and full-day 18-mile Yellowstone River trips, scenic floats, horseback, fly fishing and an overnight trip with riverside tipi camping and a cowboy dinner, at 129 US Hwy 89 S

jewels.name: Montana Whitewater, Gardiner
jewels.blurb: Yellowstone River rafting from 603 Scott St, Gardiner - "a fun, wide, high volume river" for families with children 6+ - plus zipline and fly fishing; states all activities close mid-September

jewels.name: Parks' Fly Shop, Gardiner
jewels.blurb: established 1953 at 202 2nd St S: walk-and-wade trips on park waters, Yellowstone River floats, private waters, beginner trips, casting lessons and winter guided trips

jewels.name: Blue Ribbon Flies, West Yellowstone
jewels.blurb: fly shop and guide service running float, Hebgen Lake, walk/wade and road trips, with waters including the Gibbon River and Soda Butte Creek

jewels.name: Yellowstone Wolf Tracker, Gardiner
jewels.blurb: private 6-8 hour day tours and a 6-day all-inclusive program focused on wolves, bears, bison, elk and bighorn sheep in the Lamar Valley area

jewels.name: Yellowstone Safari Company, Bozeman
jewels.blurb: family-owned wildlife safaris including Lamar Valley trips, winter wildlife tours (November-April) and 2-5 day adventures, with locations in Gardiner, West Yellowstone, Big Sky and Cody; describes itself as an "Authorized Permittee of the National Park Service"

jewels.name: Jackson Hole Wildlife Safaris
jewels.blurb: full-day Yellowstone tours and 2-3 day bear and wolf safaris in summer, Yellowstone snowmobile and snowcoach tours in winter, with lodging pickup in Jackson Hole; named on the NPS guided-tours list

jewels.name: Yellowstone Vacations Snowcoach Tours
jewels.blurb: full-day heated snowcoach tours to Old Faithful and Canyon; from West Yellowstone December 15 to March 15 (Canyon to March 9), from Gardiner December 15 to March 7; operator listed by the NPS as DNC Parks & Resorts Yellowstone Adventures dba Yellowstone Vacations

jewels.name: Yellowstone Forever Institute

jewels.name: Grizzly & Wolf Discovery Center, West Yellowstone

jewels.name: Voices of Yellowstone: First Peoples Celebration, Gardiner

jewels.name: Yellowstone Film Festival, Cody

jewels.name: The Irma Hotel restaurant, Cody

jewels.name: Cody Cattle Company, Cody

jewels.name: 2 Mules Chuckwagon, Cody
jewels.blurb: Summer-season Western dinner beside the Buffalo Bill Center, per the Cody Yellowstone visitor bureau listing.

jewels.name: Pahaska Tepee, near the East Entrance
jewels.blurb: Buffalo Bill's original hunting lodge near Yellowstone's East Gate, listed under chuckwagon and ranch dining, per the Cody Yellowstone visitor bureau listing.

jewels.name: Sitti's Table, Cody

jewels.name: Pat O'Hara Brewing Co., Cody
jewels.blurb: Brewpub opened in 2013 with 15 craft beers on tap and Irish pub fare such as shepherd's pie and fish and chips; closed Tuesdays.

jewels.name: Katabatic Brewing Co., Livingston

jewels.name: Livingston Farmers Market

jewels.name: Sage Lodge dining, Pray (Paradise Valley)
jewels.blurb: The Grill and the Fireside Room serve locally sourced Montana fare, including weekend brunch and a Breakfast & Bubbly package.

jewels.name: The Old Saloon, Emigrant (Paradise Valley)
jewels.blurb: Saloon operating since 1902 serving Montana-style portions, with breakfast, lunch and dinner Thursday to Sunday and live music.

jewels.name: Wonderland Cafe & Lodge, Gardiner
jewels.booking_route: walk-in; reservations only for groups of six or more and lodge guests
jewels.blurb: Green Certified farm-to-table cafe serving locally sourced, seasonal baked goods, lunch and dinner, open year-round at the North Entrance.

jewels.name: Cafe Madriz, West Yellowstone

jewels.name: Wild West Pizzeria & Saloon, West Yellowstone
jewels.blurb: Pizzeria with a family dining room (11am-10pm daily) and a saloon open until 2am; closed seasonally March 18 to April 9.

jewels.name: TroutHunter bar & grill, Island Park, Idaho
jewels.blurb: Riverfront lodge, fly shop and bar & grill on the Henry's Fork since 1999, with live music nights.

faq.q: Do I need a reservation to enter Yellowstone?
faq.a: No. The NPS states that visiting Yellowstone does not require a reservation to enter, but lodging and campground reservations often fill months in advance.

faq.q: When do Yellowstone's roads close for the season in 2026?
faq.a: Most park roads close October 31, 2026. Dunraven Pass, the Beartooth Highway and the Chief Joseph Scenic Byway close October 12, 2026. The road from the North Entrance at Gardiner to Cooke City is the only one generally open year-round to regular vehicles.

faq.q: How do I get to Old Faithful in winter?
faq.a: Only by guided snowmobile or snowcoach, or through the Non-Commercially Guided Snowmobile Access Program. Roads open to oversnow travel usually by mid-December.

faq.q: How do I reserve a campsite in Yellowstone?
faq.a: Bridge Bay, Canyon, Fishing Bridge RV Park, Grant Village and Madison are reserved through Yellowstone National Park Lodges; Indian Creek, Lewis Lake, Mammoth, Slough Creek and Tower Fall through recreation.gov. All sites must be reserved in advance except Mammoth's first-come sites from October 15 to April 1.

faq.q: How much does it cost to enter Yellowstone?
faq.a: $35 per private vehicle, $30 per motorcycle, $20 per person on foot, bicycle or ski, or $70 for a Yellowstone Annual Pass. Non-US residents aged 16 and older pay an additional $100 unless admitted with an Annual or America the Beautiful Pass.

faq.q: How close can I get to bison and bears in Yellowstone?
faq.a: The NPS says to stay at least 100 yards (91 m) from bears, wolves and cougars, and at least 25 yards (23 m) from all other animals, including bison and elk.

faq.q: How often does Old Faithful erupt?
faq.a: The NPS states the median interval changes; as of January 2025 it is 102 minutes plus or minus 10 minutes, with intervals ranging from 54 to 118 minutes. Rangers post predictions.

name: Grand Teton National Park
line: A boat across Jenny Lake, bison on Mormon Row, and a mountain range you can climb with the oldest guide service in the country

jewels.name: Jenny Lake shuttle boat
jewels.blurb: the boat from the South Jenny Lake dock across the lake toward the popular trailheads; no reservation required, ADA-accessible boats; 2026 season May 15 to September 30 (now ended)

jewels.name: Jenny Lake shore trail
jewels.blurb: one of four trails the NPS names as accessible, with asphalt surfaces and appropriate grades; Jenny Lake Visitor Center open May 15 - October 12, 2026

jewels.name: Cascade Canyon
jewels.blurb: the canyon west of Jenny Lake, which the NPS lists for mule deer, moose, ground squirrels, pikas and marmots among the boulder fields

jewels.name: Teton Park Road and its season
jewels.blurb: the inner park road under the range, closed to vehicles November 1 to April 30 between Taggart Lake Trailhead and Signal Mountain Lodge, then open to bikes and walkers until snow and groomed for skiing mid-December to mid-March

jewels.name: Mormon Row Historic District
jewels.blurb: 27 homesteads settled 1896-1937 east of Blacktail Butte, off Antelope Flats Road; the John and T.A. Moulton barns are the most photographed buildings; on the National Register since 1997

jewels.name: Oxbow Bend
jewels.blurb: slow water 1 mile east of Jackson Lake Junction where the NPS lists river otters, bald eagles, beavers, moose and elk

jewels.name: Snake River corridor, Jackson Lake Dam to Moose
jewels.blurb: "Elk and bison graze in grassy meadows" with bald eagles, beavers and moose in the willows; Blacktail Pond and Timbered Island nearby for elk, moose and pronghorn; NPS rule: 100 yards from bears and wolves, 25 yards from all other wildlife

jewels.name: Jackson Lake and the Elk Island cruises
jewels.blurb: scenic, breakfast, lunch and dinner cruises from Colter Bay Marina, 1.5-2.5 hours, $39-$95; GTLC states 2026 cruises ended in mid-July and the NPS lists Colter Bay and Signal Mountain marinas closed

jewels.name: Laurance S. Rockefeller Preserve
jewels.blurb: a preserve with its own center (open June 1 - September 20, 2026) and drop-in ranger programs including "Bear Necessities"; the Moose-Wilson Road from the Preserve to Moose is currently listed "Closed to all use"

jewels.name: Climbing the Grand Teton
jewels.blurb: no climbing permit for day climbs, but overnight trips need a backcountry permit; the NPS: "A fall on steep snow and failure to self-arrest with an ice axe is the number one cause of injury and death"

jewels.name: Backcountry camping permits
jewels.blurb: required for all overnight backcountry stays; about one third reservable from early January on recreation.gov, two thirds walk-up; $20 permit plus $7 per person per night

jewels.name: Grand Teton Pathway

jewels.name: Jenny Lake Lodge
jewels.blurb: GTLC's cabin lodge, June to early October, whose Signature Stay package includes breakfast, a nightly five-course dinner, cruiser bicycles and horseback riding (availability extremely limited); booking 2027

jewels.name: Jackson Lake Lodge

jewels.name: Signal Mountain Lodge

jewels.name: Triangle X Ranch

jewels.name: Colter Bay Tent Village (canvas tent cabins)

jewels.name: Jenny Lake Campground (NPS)

jewels.name: Million Dollar Cowboy Bar and Steakhouse, Jackson
jewels.booking_route: not observed (steakhouse has its own site); phone (307) 733-2207

jewels.name: Grand Teton Distillery, Driggs, Idaho
jewels.booking_route: not observed (tours section on site); phone (208) 354-7263

faq.q: Do I need a reservation to enter Grand Teton National Park?
faq.a: No. The NPS states that Grand Teton does not offer entrance reservations or timed entry. All park lodging and campgrounds are reservable, though, and the NPS says to book well ahead.

faq.q: How do I reserve a campsite in Grand Teton?
faq.a: All park campground sites are by advance reservation only, on Recreation.gov, up to six months ahead. NPS-run campgrounds are Gros Ventre, Jenny Lake, Signal Mountain, Colter Bay and Lizard Creek; Colter Bay RV Park, Colter Bay Tent Village and Headwaters are run by the concessioner.

faq.q: When is the Teton Park Road closed?
faq.a: The Teton Park Road is closed to vehicles November 1 to April 30 between Taggart Lake Trailhead and Signal Mountain Lodge. It is open to biking and walking in the shoulder seasons until snow covers it, and groomed for skiing and snowshoeing from mid-December to mid-March.

faq.q: How much does it cost to enter Grand Teton?
faq.a: $35 per private vehicle, $30 per motorcycle or $20 per person on foot or bike, each valid 7 days, or $70 for a Grand Teton Annual Pass. Non-US residents aged 16 and older pay an additional $100 unless admitted with an Annual or America the Beautiful Pass.

faq.q: Do I need to book the Jenny Lake shuttle boat?
faq.a: No. Jenny Lake Boating states reservations are not required; the boat leaves from the South Jenny Lake dock. Its 2026 season ran May 15 to September 30.

faq.q: How close can I get to wildlife in Grand Teton?
faq.a: The NPS requires a distance of at least 100 yards from bears and wolves and 25 yards from all other wildlife, and states it is illegal to feed wildlife.

faq.q: Where are the best places to see wildlife in Grand Teton?
faq.a: The NPS names Oxbow Bend (otters, bald eagles, beavers, moose, elk), Mormon Row (bison and pronghorn in spring, summer and fall), the Snake River from Jackson Lake Dam to Moose, Cascade Canyon, Blacktail Pond and Timbered Island.
