name: Glacier National Park
line: A 50-mile road over the Continental Divide, railway-era lodges, and a summer that runs from early July to the third Monday of October

jewels.name: Going-to-the-Sun Road
jewels.blurb: 50 miles across the park, about 2 hours without stopping, topping out at Logan Pass at 6,646 feet; typically fully open from early July to the third Monday of October

jewels.name: Logan Pass - three-hour parking (2026 rule)
jewels.blurb: no vehicle reservation in 2026; instead every private-vehicle space at Logan Pass was limited to three hours with a free timestamped kiosk permit, 1 July to 7 September 2026, enforced 24 hours a day

jewels.name: Logan Pass Shuttle (ticketed, 2026 pilot)
jewels.blurb: ticketed-only shuttle with early-morning express routes to Logan Pass, 1 July to Labor Day 2026; $1 ticket on Recreation.gov, released 60 days ahead and the night before

jewels.name: Highline Trail and Hidden Lake Overlook
jewels.blurb: the two Logan Pass hikes the NPS names: Hidden Lake Overlook fits inside three hours of parking, the Highline to Granite Park Chalet needs a shuttle ticket

jewels.name: Many Glacier Hotel
jewels.blurb: Great Northern Railway hotel of 1914-15 on Swiftcurrent Lake, five storeys and 214 rooms and suites; open 5 June to 21 September 2026

jewels.name: Grinnell Glacier hike
jewels.blurb: 10.6 miles round trip with 1,600 feet of gain from Many Glacier, cut to about 7 miles by taking the two-lake boat across Swiftcurrent Lake and Lake Josephine

jewels.name: Red Bus Tours
jewels.blurb: a fleet of 33 vintage 1930s buses, described by the operator as the oldest touring fleet anywhere; 16 passengers each, departing from lodges on both sides of the park, bookable for 2026

jewels.name: Glacier Park Boat Co. lake tours
jewels.blurb: the boat tours on Many Glacier, Two Medicine, Rising Sun (St. Mary Lake) and Lake McDonald, plus small-boat rentals at Apgar, Lake McDonald, Two Medicine and Many Glacier

jewels.name: Under Canvas Glacier, Coram
jewels.blurb: safari-style tents with wood-burning stoves about 7 miles from the west entrance; ensuite Deluxe and Suite tents and family kids-tent options; open 29 May to 14 September 2026

jewels.name: West Glacier and the Belton Chalet
jewels.blurb: the west-entrance village with the Amtrak Belton station and the historic Belton Chalet across the street; Belton Chalet open 8 May to 11 October 2026

jewels.name: East Glacier and Glacier Park Lodge
jewels.blurb: the Great Northern's first big lodge (1912-13), across from the 1913 East Glacier Amtrak station; open 29 May to 27 September 2026

jewels.name: St. Mary Village
jewels.blurb: east-entrance base at the foot of Going-to-the-Sun Road, open 29 May to 5 October 2026; St. Mary Visitor Center is an east-side departure point for the Logan Pass shuttle

jewels.name: Whitefish
jewels.blurb: the resort town "at the edge of Glacier National Park", 12 miles from Glacier Park International Airport and an Empire Builder stop

jewels.name: Whitefish Winter Carnival LXVIII
jewels.blurb: Whitefish's winter carnival, dated 5-7 February 2027

jewels.name: North American Indian Days, Browning
jewels.blurb: one of the largest gatherings of US and Canadian tribes, held the second week of July at Stampede Park on the Blackfeet Reservation just east of the park

jewels.name: Granite Park Chalet
jewels.blurb: Great Northern backcountry chalet of 1914-15 on the Highline Trail; one of the two chalets the NPS says still function, and its guests are exempt from the Logan Pass overnight-parking ban

jewels.name: BaseGlamp, north of Whitefish
jewels.blurb: year-round site of 12 geodesic domes on 20 acres about 15 minutes north of Whitefish, with ensuite bathrooms, wood-burning stoves and outdoor cedar hot tubs (listing seen in search results)

jewels.name: ROAM Beyond Glacier, Columbia Falls
jewels.blurb: "an immersive outdoor lodging experience" of tiny Roaming Cabins on wheels at 2347 Middle Rd, Columbia Falls

jewels.name: Columbia Falls RV Park glamping tents
jewels.blurb: canvas wall tents with queen or king beds, air conditioning and heating, "just 15 minutes from the west entrance"; seasonal

jewels.name: North Forty Resort, Columbia Falls
jewels.blurb: family-owned log-cabin retreat on 40 acres with twenty-three cabins and a summer glamping tent sleeping up to 4 (seen in search results)

jewels.name: North American RV Park & Yurt Village, Coram
jewels.blurb: family-run RV park with yurts and camping cabins about 5.5 miles from the west entrance, open April through October (listing seen in search results)

jewels.name: Lodgepole Gallery and Tipi Village, Blackfeet Reservation
jewels.blurb: 11 tipis sleeping four each, with fire rings, bison dinners and cultural programmes of Native drumming and singing, east of the park

jewels.name: Glacier Grizzly Resort (tipis), near the east side
jewels.blurb: listed with around 50 tipis on 250 acres about 11 miles from the St. Mary entrance; one listing reports it closed permanently, so its current status is NOT CONFIRMED (seen in search results)

jewels.name: NPS reservation campgrounds (8)
jewels.blurb: Apgar, Avalanche, Fish Creek, Many Glacier, Rising Sun, St. Mary, Sprague Creek and Two Medicine are reservation-only on Recreation.gov; the NPS says "a majority of Glacier's campgrounds require a reservation"

jewels.name: NPS first-come, first-served campgrounds
jewels.blurb: Bowman Lake, Cut Bank, Kintla Lake, Logging Creek and Quartz Creek; vehicle combinations over 21 feet are not allowed at Cut Bank, Kintla Lake, Logging Creek and Quartz Creek, and Cut Bank uses Recreation.gov Scan & Pay (seen in search results)

jewels.name: West Glacier KOA Resort
jewels.blurb: KOA resort outside West Glacier with Deluxe Studio Cabins and Sky Deck cabins sleeping up to four, pools and staff-led activities (KOA page seen in search results; direct fetch refused)

jewels.name: St. Mary / East Glacier KOA Holiday
jewels.blurb: KOA at the base of the park's east side with upgraded RV sites and Deluxe Cabins with full baths (KOA page seen in search results; direct fetch refused)

jewels.name: Johnson's of St. Mary
jewels.blurb: campground, cabins and RV park a quarter-mile from the St. Mary entrance, 82 RV and 75 tent sites, with a family-style cafe; open mid-May to mid-September (listing seen in search results)

jewels.name: San-Suz-Ed RV Park, West Glacier
jewels.blurb: RV park, campground and bed and breakfast at 11505 Highway 2 East, West Glacier, with full hookups and pull-through sites (listing seen in search results)

jewels.name: Glacier Peaks RV Park & Cabins, Columbia Falls
jewels.blurb: 60 RV spaces and cabins 3 miles west of Columbia Falls, about 30 minutes from the park (listing seen in search results)

jewels.name: Swan Mountain Outfitters horseback rides
jewels.blurb: the NPS-named horseback concessioner, riding from corrals at Many Glacier, Lake McDonald and Apgar; no rides in winter

jewels.name: Flathead River rafting, West Glacier
jewels.blurb: four companies the NPS lists - Glacier Guides and Montana Raft, Glacier Raft Company, Great Northern Resort and Wild River Adventures - run the Middle and North Forks of the Flathead under US Forest Service permits

jewels.name: Sun Tours, East Glacier Park
jewels.blurb: Blackfeet interpretive tours over Going-to-the-Sun Road, guided by residents of the Blackfeet Reservation, with pickups in East Glacier Park, Browning and the St. Mary valley (listing seen in search results)

jewels.name: Bike and e-bike rental, Apgar and West Glacier
jewels.blurb: Flathead Outdoors rents hybrid bikes and e-bikes at West Glacier and in Apgar Village; Going-to-the-Sun Road opens to cyclists for a spring window before cars (seen in search results)

jewels.name: Polebridge Mercantile, North Fork
jewels.blurb: 1914 off-grid general store and bakery near the park's north-west corner, known for its huckleberry bear claws (seen in search results)

jewels.name: Glacier Distilling Company, Coram
jewels.blurb: craft distillery tasting room about 10 minutes from the west entrance, maker of Bearproof huckleberry whiskey and Logan Pass single malt (seen in search results)

jewels.name: Whitefish Mountain Resort, summer
jewels.blurb: scenic lift or gondola to a summit with views of Glacier's peaks, alpine slides and an aerial adventure park; summer 2026 daily operations ran 13 June to 7 September (seen in search results)

jewels.name: The Huckleberry Patch, Hungry Horse
jewels.blurb: Huckleberry specialist at the only stoplight in Hungry Horse with its own cannery, bakery, sweetshop and pantry (plus Flathead cherry goods) and a lunch and dinner menu; summer hours 9am-9pm.

jewels.name: Park Cafe and Grocery, St. Mary
jewels.blurb: Cafe at the park's east entrance, established in the early 20th century and known for its pies (apple, huckleberry, pecan, rhubarb); cafe 8am-9pm daily.

jewels.name: Serrano's Mexican Restaurant, East Glacier
jewels.booking_route: Toast (online takeout ordering); dine-in reservations not observed
jewels.blurb: Historic cantina serving traditional and contemporary Mexican dishes, fajitas and margaritas, with outdoor seating and mountain views; 5-9pm.

jewels.name: Backslope Brewing, Columbia Falls
jewels.booking_route: walk-in, no reservations; Toast for online food orders
jewels.blurb: Family-friendly brewery and kitchen 'in the shadow of Glacier National Park', open Tuesday to Saturday 11am-8pm.

jewels.name: Spotted Bear Spirits, Whitefish
jewels.blurb: Downtown craft distillery and cocktail lounge across from Depot Park making Montana whiskey, huckleberry vodka and gin; $2 per bottle of Midnight Forest goes to Backcountry Hunters and Anglers.

jewels.name: Tupelo Grille, Whitefish
jewels.blurb: Downtown Southern-cuisine restaurant established in 1995, with an award-winning wine list and Sunday brunch.

jewels.name: Latitude 48, Whitefish
jewels.blurb: Central Avenue bistro of locally sourced shareable plates, wood-fired pizzas, steaks and oysters, with a Red Room happy hour.

jewels.name: Loula's Cafe, Whitefish
jewels.blurb: Family-owned scratch kitchen in the lower level of the historic Masonic temple, using Montana beef and local produce, known for homemade pies including huckleberry/cherry.

jewels.name: Cafe Kandahar, Kandahar Lodge, Whitefish Mountain Resort
jewels.booking_route: phone 406-862-6098 or email (no online route observed)
jewels.blurb: Fine-dining chop-house kitchen at Kandahar Lodge on the mountain (the site also brands it Buchanan's at Kandahar), with a limited menu in the lodge bar.

jewels.name: Whitefish Farmers Market
jewels.blurb: Tuesday evening market (5-7:30pm) at Depot Park on Central Avenue, June 2 to September 29, 2026, running since 2003 with farmers, food trucks and artisans.

jewels.name: Kalispell Farmers Market
jewels.blurb: Saturday market (9am-12:30pm) at Flathead Valley Community College, running more than 50 years; 2026 season May 2 to October 17, plus a Harvest Holiday Market on October 17.

jewels.name: SunRift Beer Company, Kalispell
jewels.blurb: Downtown Kalispell taproom brewing beer 'inspired by the life we all crave here in the Flathead Valley', with food menus.

faq.q: Do you need a vehicle reservation for Glacier National Park?
faq.a: Not in 2026. The NPS states vehicle reservations were not required in 2026, including in Many Glacier, Two Medicine and the North Fork. Instead, from 1 July to 7 September 2026, Logan Pass parking was limited to three hours and the Logan Pass shuttle required a ticket. Rules for 2027 were not established in this build.

faq.q: When is Going-to-the-Sun Road open?
faq.a: The NPS says the road has been fully open by early July and is typically fully open until the third Monday of October, with exact dates depending on snow and weather. The section from West Glacier to Lake McDonald Lodge is plowed year-round, weather permitting.

faq.q: How much does it cost to enter Glacier National Park?
faq.a: In 2026 a 7-day private vehicle pass is $35 ($25 in winter), a 7-day per-person pass is $20, and the Glacier annual pass is $70. International visitors aged 16 and over pay an extra $100 per person unless they hold an annual or America the Beautiful pass.

faq.q: What is the closest airport to Glacier National Park?
faq.a: Glacier Park International Airport (FCA) in Kalispell, 30 miles from the West Entrance and 12 miles from Whitefish. Amtrak's Empire Builder also stops at East Glacier, West Glacier and Whitefish.

faq.q: Are there bears in Glacier National Park?
faq.a: Yes. The NPS states researchers estimate Glacier provides habitat for nearly one thousand bears, that bear spray has been shown to be the most effective deterrent, and that approaching within 100 yards of bears or wolves is prohibited.

faq.q: When is Under Canvas Glacier open?
faq.a: 29 May to 14 September in 2026 and 28 May to 13 September in 2027. The camp is in Coram, about 7 miles from the park's west entrance.

hero.query: Glacier National Park, Montana

name: Death Valley National Park
line: The lowest point in North America, a Gold Tier dark-sky park, and a ring of ghost towns, hot springs and date farms across the California-Nevada line

jewels.name: Badwater Basin
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park entrance fee only
jewels.blurb: "The lowest point in North America is a surreal landscape of vast salt flats" - 282 feet below sea level, nearly 200 square miles of salt; an ADA accessible ramp leads to a wooden boardwalk; 1 mile round trip to the salt flat edge; 30 minutes south of Furnace Creek; NPS: summer hiking discouraged after 10 AM

jewels.name: Artists Drive and Artists Palette
jewels.blurb: a one-way scenic loop of about 30 minutes off Badwater Road, starting 8.5 miles south of the Highway 190 junction; "a length restriction of 25 ft. (7.6 m) due to sharp bends and large dips"

jewels.name: Dantes View
jewels.blurb: a viewpoint 5,575 feet above Badwater Basin on the Black Mountains ridge, "an unparalleled view of the swirling white salt flats", 45 minutes from Furnace Creek, popular at sunrise and sunset, with an 8-mile round-trip ridge trail toward Mt. Perry

jewels.name: Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes
jewels.blurb: a dune field just east of Stovepipe Wells Village off CA-190, 2 miles round trip to the tallest dune (185 feet gain), "dramatic shadows at sunrise and sunset"; no official trails; pets prohibited; NPS: "HIKING NOT ADVISED AFTER 10 AM IN THE SUMMER"

jewels.name: Ubehebe Crater
jewels.blurb: a maar volcano about half a mile across and 500-777 feet deep, about 2,100 years old; 1.5-mile, 1-hour moderate rim hike with 500 feet of gain; paved overlook lot for buses and large RVs; about an hour from Furnace Creek

jewels.name: Golden Canyon
jewels.blurb: a 3-mile moderate-to-strenuous canyon hike rated by the NPS, and in winter a ranger-led Golden Canyon Hike of about three-quarters of a mile; NPS: "Summer temperatures can be dangerous in the park's lower elevations"

jewels.name: Harmony Borax Works and Salt Creek Interpretive Trail
jewels.blurb: two easy short walks - Harmony Borax Works 0.4 mile on a paved path through mining history (a ranger walk in winter, and an NPS night-sky pick) and the 0.5-mile Salt Creek Interpretive Trail

jewels.name: Mosaic Canyon and Natural Bridge
jewels.blurb: Mosaic Canyon, 4 miles, moderate to difficult, and Natural Bridge, an easy 1 mile - two of the NPS's named canyon walks

jewels.name: Telescope Peak
jewels.blurb: the park's hardest named day hike, 12.2 miles, rated difficult, to the 11,049-foot summit that rises above Badwater; Wildrose Peak (7.9 miles) is the shorter difficult alternative

jewels.name: Backcountry roads: the Racetrack and Titus Canyon
jewels.booking_route: none needed; jeep hire via Farabee's
jewels.blurb: "Death Valley has more miles of roads than any other national park" - nearly 1,000 miles across 3.4 million acres; high-clearance or 4WD required on rough routes, NPS asks for "2 full size spare tires" and warns "rescue is likely to be extremely delayed"; Titus Canyon closed in sections from October 2, 2026

jewels.name: Ranger programs (mid-November to mid-April)
jewels.booking_route: none needed; Paleontology Hikes via recreation.gov when offered
jewels.blurb: free, no-reservation talks and walks from December to March - Badwater, Harmony Borax Works, Golden Canyon, Sand Dunes, a Night Sky Talk at Furnace Creek and family programmes; "No outdoor formal programs are scheduled during summer due to extreme heat"; ticketed Paleontology Hikes not offered in 2026

jewels.name: Gold Tier dark skies
jewels.blurb: Gold Tier, the highest classification from the International Dark-Sky Association; rangers name Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes, Harmony Borax Works, Badwater Basin and Ubehebe Crater as top spots; an annual spring Dark Sky Festival with NASA speakers

jewels.name: The Inn at Death Valley, Furnace Creek
jewels.blurb: "An elegant hideaway since 1927", a AAA four-diamond resort for more than 37 years, with natural springs, palms, new casitas, a spring-fed pool and fine dining; the Oasis also lists horseback riding and a spa

jewels.name: The Ranch at Death Valley, Furnace Creek
jewels.blurb: the family-friendly half of the Oasis, next to the NPS visitor centre on Highway 190, after a $200 million renovation: rooms with private patios, a spring-fed pool, a date-palm town square and several places to eat

jewels.name: Stardust Astrotours at the Oasis
jewels.booking_route: not observed (price and engine not shown on the Oasis or stardustastrotours.com pages; Oasis 800-236-7916)
jewels.blurb: guided small-group night sky tours with astronomers, departing from the Oasis resort: laser-guided constellations, high-powered telescopes, all equipment provided; the Oasis cites Bortle Class 2 darkness and the Leonids (November 16-18, 2026) and Geminids (December 13, 2026)

jewels.name: Furnace Creek Golf Course
jewels.blurb: billed as "the lowest elevation course in the world", at 214 feet below sea level, shared by guests of the Inn and the Ranch

jewels.name: Stovepipe Wells Village
jewels.booking_route: StayNTouch (stovepipewellsvillagehotel.ibe.stayntouch.com); RV sites via its website
jewels.blurb: the in-park concession at 51880 Highway 190, run by POWDR: air-conditioned rooms including accessible rooms, full-hookup RV sites, tent sites, a pool, a restaurant and saloon, and a 24-hour gas station

jewels.name: Panamint Springs Resort
jewels.booking_route: not observed (panamintsprings.com showed a bot check)
jewels.blurb: named by the NPS as an in-park private operation with "resort accommodations, camping, a restaurant and gas station" on the park's west side; 775-482-7680

jewels.name: Furnace Creek Campground
jewels.blurb: the NPS campground open year-round that "takes reservations for October 15th - April 15th season" on recreation.gov up to 6 months ahead; NPS: Furnace Creek and Texas Springs "are typically full on weekends and holidays"

jewels.name: Sunset, Texas Springs and the first-come campgrounds
jewels.blurb: every NPS campground except Furnace Creek is first-come, first-served - Sunset, Texas Springs, Stovepipe Wells, Mesquite Spring, Wildrose, Mahogany Flat, Thorndike (Emigrant closed indefinitely); "The park's largest campground, Sunset, almost always has sites available, even in peak season"

jewels.name: Farabee Jeep Rentals & Tours, Furnace Creek
jewels.blurb: named by the NPS as the Furnace Creek jeep outfitter; daily guided tours to the Racetrack, Echo, Cottonwood/Marble and Hole in the Wall with snacks and water, and self-drive rentals on Echo, Hole in the Wall, Cottonwood/Marble and Goler

jewels.name: Rhyolite ghost town, Beatty, Nevada
jewels.blurb: a BLM-managed former gold-mining boomtown on NV 374 with the Cook Bank Building, "one of the most photographed buildings in the West", and "Nevada's best preserved 'bottle house'"; day use only; listed by the NPS among nearby attractions

jewels.name: Goldwell Open Air Museum, Rhyolite
jewels.booking_route: none needed; donations on its website
jewels.blurb: seven monumental outdoor sculptures by Belgian artists led by the late Albert Szukalski, including "Last Supper" and "Lady Desert", at 1 Golden St; grounds open 24 hours, visitor centre about Monday-Saturday 10-4

jewels.name: Marta Becket's Amargosa Opera House and Hotel, Death Valley Junction
jewels.blurb: a historic desert opera house and hotel at Highway 127 and State Line Road, with daily guided tours at 9 am and 6 pm ($20 adults, $10 children), a separate cafe, and occasional shows

jewels.name: China Ranch Date Farm, Tecopa
jewels.blurb: a date farm at #8 China Ranch Rd selling several California date varieties and its own hybrids, date nut bread, muffins and cookies from its bakery, with trails to abandoned mines, the Old Spanish Trail and the Tonopah & Tidewater railroad bed

jewels.name: Tecopa Hot Springs & Campground
jewels.blurb: an Inyo County park run by concessionaire Flippin-Hamrick: 30 partial-hookup RV sites and over 200 dry sites, tent camping, and two bathhouses with separate men's and women's hot mineral pools at about 102°F; nude bathing "per local code"

jewels.name: Shoshone Village
jewels.blurb: the Shoshone Inn, RV park, campground and vacation rentals around a warm springs swimming pool, with the Crowbar Cafe & Saloon and the Shoshone Museum, an interpretive centre for the Amargosa and Death Valley region; one ADA-accessible bungalow

jewels.name: Tarantula Ranch, Beatty
jewels.blurb: an 8-acre Mojave Desert vineyard property with three teardrop-trailer glamping units, five RV/tent sites named for grape varietals, a shared bathhouse, outdoor kitchen and a "Wine Hall"; Star Host, 98% recommended

jewels.name: Falcon Cottage (Death Valley Desert Cottage), Pahrump
jewels.blurb: a cabin for up to six with a private unheated pool (comfortable May-October), stone fire pit, grills, fibre WiFi, and crib and high chair on request

jewels.name: Miss Kathy's Short Branch, Crystal, Nevada
jewels.blurb: a western-decor motel-room cabin for two with private shower, air conditioning, StarLink WiFi and pets on leash, twenty minutes from Ash Meadows and Devil's Hole and about twenty minutes from Pahrump

jewels.name: Alabama Hills, Lone Pine
jewels.booking_route: none needed; free BLM camping permit
jewels.blurb: "golden granite boulders rising up from the desert floor" and rock arches about 3 miles west of Lone Pine where Movie Road meets Whitney Portal Road, with Mobius Arch and over 400 films shot since the 1920s; BLM camping needs a free permit

jewels.name: Museum of Western Film History, Lone Pine
jewels.blurb: "America's only Western Film Museum" at 701 S. Main Street, open daily 9-5 for an $8 suggested donation, covering over 400 films shot in the Eastern Sierra; hosts the Lone Pine Film Festival each October

faq.q: Do I need a reservation to enter Death Valley National Park?
faq.a: No. The NPS states that no reservation is required to enter the park. A private vehicle pays $30 for 7 days.

faq.q: Can I reserve a campsite in Death Valley?
faq.a: Only at Furnace Creek, which takes reservations on recreation.gov for the October 15 to April 15 season, up to 6 months ahead. All other NPS campgrounds are first-come, first-served; the NPS says Sunset, the largest, almost always has sites available, even in peak season.

faq.q: Is Scotty's Castle open?
faq.a: No. As of the NPS update of September 28, 2026, Bonnie Clare Road and Scotty's Castle are closed due to flood recovery work, with no access permitted, including pedestrians.

faq.q: Is Titus Canyon Road open?
faq.a: Not in full. The NPS lists the one-way section closed from October 2, 2026 to May 2027 and the two-way section closed from October 27 to December 2026.

faq.q: When do ranger programs run?
faq.a: From mid-November to mid-April, with daily talks and walks December to March. The NPS says no outdoor formal programs are scheduled during summer due to extreme heat.

faq.q: Is Death Valley good for stargazing?
faq.a: The NPS states the park holds Gold Tier, the highest classification from the International Dark-Sky Association, and names Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes, Harmony Borax Works, Badwater Basin and Ubehebe Crater as top spots.

seo.meta_title: Death Valley National Park: Badwater, Dunes, Dark Skies & Where to Stay | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: Badwater, the dunes, Gold Tier dark skies, current road closures, NPS campgrounds and where to stay from Furnace Creek to Tecopa hot springs and Beatty glamping.

hero.query: Death Valley National Park, California

name: Great Basin National Park
line: Lehman Caves, bristlecone pines and Gold Tier dark skies

jewels.name: Lehman Caves
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov (Lehman Caves Tours ticket facility 251853) or limited walk-up tickets at the Lehman Caves Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: "Passageways in the marble rock are filled with beautiful speleothems including stalactites, stalagmites, popcorn, and cave bacon." Ranger tours only: Lodge Room (60 min, 0.4 mi, Easy) $12 adult / $6 youth; Grand Palace (90 min, 0.6 mi, Moderate, 69 stairs) $15 / $8; "Cave tours are limited to 20 visitors each"; "The cave naturally remains around 52ºF (11ºC)"; "White Nose Syndrome Screening is mandatory".

jewels.name: Wheeler Peak Bristlecone Grove (Bristlecone Trail)
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free park trail; no entrance fee
jewels.blurb: 2.8 miles, 600 ft gain from 9,890 ft, Moderate, 1.5-3 hours from the Bristlecone Trailhead at the end of the Scenic Drive, to "the oldest living organisms in the world"; the grove once held "the Prometheus Tree, the oldest non-clonal organism on earth", removed in 1964. The Glacier Trail continues beyond the grove.

jewels.name: Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive
jewels.blurb: A 12-mile "out and back road" gaining "over 4,000 feet in elevation" to "an elevation exceeding 10,000 feet above sea level", with pullouts on Mount Moriah, Lehman Creek, Wheeler Peak, Doso Doyabi Peak and the Snake Valley - the "equivalent of driving from Baker, Nevada, to the frozen Yukon". Usually open by Memorial Day weekend; no vehicles or trailers over 24 feet beyond mile marker 3.

jewels.name: Ranger astronomy programmes at the Astronomy Amphitheater
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free, first come at the amphitheater by the Lehman Caves Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: "roughly between Memorial Day and Labor Day, Great Basin Astronomy Rangers lead programs at the Astronomy Amphitheater every Thursday through Sunday": a thirty-minute talk then an hour and a half at the telescopes; "Programs are free and require no reservation, though there is a maximum capacity." "The Great Basin Observatory is the only research grade observatory in a national park."

jewels.name: Stargazing on your own in a Dark Sky Park
jewels.blurb: "some of the darkest skies in the lower 48 states"; the NPS names the Astronomy Amphitheater, Mather Overlook on the Scenic Drive, the Baker Archaeological Site and the Ranching Exhibit on Highway 488 - "none of the locations above allow overnight camping." Allow "up to thirty minutes for the human eye to adjust to the darkness".

jewels.name: Alpine Lakes Loop
jewels.blurb: 2.7 miles, 440 ft gain from 9,890 ft, rated Easy, 1.5-3 hours: "this loop hike passes by two alpine lakes" - Teresa and Stella - "all while going through alpine meadows and coniferous forests." Links with the Bristlecone Trail for 4.1 miles. "Potable water is not available along the Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive."

jewels.name: Accessible Gothic Palace Tour
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov (cave tour 195) or walk-up at the Lehman Caves Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: 30 minutes, 0.3 miles, no stairs, "intended for persons with limited mobility"; $8 adult, $4 youth (5-15), under 5 free. "Access Pass and Senior Pass holders are entitled to a 50% discount on cave tour tickets for the cardholder only."

jewels.name: Introduction to Wild Caving Tour
jewels.blurb: 180 minutes, 1.5 miles, "Strenuous" with scrambling and belly crawling; adults only, $40. Separately, seven wild caves are open by permit and "Permits must be submitted at least two weeks before the intended caving trip" (nps.gov/grba permits page).

jewels.name: Junior Ranger and Night Explorer booklets
jewels.blurb: "Learn about the Great Basin using this booklet. Explore the life of a bristlecone, deep caves, and other fun subjects with the help of Baby Raven." The Junior Ranger Night Explorer booklet earns a Dark-Sky patch with "star trails and a bristlecone"; booklets download from the park site, and "rangers are not able to mail any junior ranger materials".

jewels.name: Evening ranger programmes
jewels.booking_route: none needed - times posted at the Lehman Caves Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: "Rangers provide evening programs in the park between Memorial Day and Labor Day on a number of topics"; "During the summer months, rangers present programs for all ages at the Lehman Caves Visitor Center almost daily."

jewels.name: Wheeler Peak Campground
jewels.blurb: At nearly 10,000 feet beneath Wheeler Peak and Doso Doyabi, with "paved parking spurs, picnic tables, campfire rings and grills along with vault toilets"; reservable "from late June through Labor Day weekend"; "Neither vehicles over 24 feet in length nor towed units over 24 feet in length are permitted"; $20 a night, 50% off with Senior or Access passes.

jewels.name: Upper Lehman Creek Campground
jewels.blurb: At 7,500 feet among ponderosa pine and white fir beside "a clear mountain stream"; paved parking spurs; "The nightly rate is $20." "There is no potable water available at Upper Lehman Creek Campground."

jewels.name: Lower Lehman Creek Campground
jewels.blurb: "perfect for RVs, with large, paved, pull-through parking at six of the nine camping sites" at 7,300 feet; unstaffed, no potable water. The NPS: "Winter camping is available in the Lower Lehman Creek Campground" (visiting-in-winter page). $10 dump fee at the Visitor Center (fees page).

jewels.name: Grey Cliffs group campsites
jewels.blurb: "The campground is tucked beside limestone cliffs and set amongst pinyon pines"; "Groups utilizing a group campsite must include a minimum of 9 persons and cannot exceed a maximum group size of 16 persons per site"; group sites $30 a night (individual sites $20); "The campground cannot accommodate RVs or trailers"; reservations "from Memorial Day through September."

jewels.name: Baker Creek Campground
jewels.blurb: "one of five developed campgrounds at Great Basin National Park", in pinyon-juniper with "shade, close to the Lehman Caves Visitor Center" and backcountry trail access; $20 a night; "This campground has a short reservation window to accommodate those last second travel plans."

jewels.name: Baker-Johnson Lakes backcountry loop
jewels.booking_route: free backcountry permit from the park (no quota, per the permits page)
jewels.blurb: "Backcountry permits are required for any backcountry camping on the Baker-Johnson Lakes Loop"; both lakes sit above 10,000 feet where campfires are prohibited and portable stoves must be used; "Group size in the backcountry is limited to 12 persons and/or 6 pack animals."

jewels.name: Lexington Arch
jewels.blurb: "Hypothesized to be left over from an ancient cave system, Lexington Arch is one of the most incredible features of Great Basin, replicated nowhere else in the park." The road is "almost entirely gravel and dirt"; "4WD is recommended on this road, and high clearance is absolutely necessary." Leashed pets are allowed on this trail (nps.gov/grba pets page).

jewels.name: Winter ski touring and snowshoeing on the Scenic Drive
jewels.blurb: "The Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive closes to vehicle traffic, but remains open to skiers and snowshoers"; "Novice skiers can find gentle slopes for touring or experienced ski mountaineers can challenge their skills on steep and deep backcountry runs." Free camping in the closed Wheeler Peak Campground in winter.

jewels.name: Great Basin Cafe and Gift Shop
jewels.blurb: "located at the Lehman Caves Visitor Center", "open for the summer season, April through October"; "The Cafe is the only restaurant within the boundaries of Great Basin National Park". (775) 234-7200.

jewels.name: Water and a filter for the high desert
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Carry plenty of water and drink it!" "All surface water should be chemically treated, boiled, or passed through a filter capable of eliminating harmful microbes and parasites, such as giardia, before drinking." On the Scenic Drive, "Potable water is not available" - the NPS suggests "about one gallon per person per day" (Alpine Lakes Loop page).

jewels.name: Hat and sunscreen above 10,000 feet
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Sunburn is a common problem when hiking at high elevations" because the thin atmosphere filters less; "Wear a hat and sunscreen."

jewels.name: Layered non-cotton clothing
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Avoid hypothermia by wearing appropriate, layered clothing. Do not wear cotton clothing, which becomes very cold when wet." "It can snow any time of the year at high elevations" (weather page), and the cave holds "around 52ºF" (cave tours page).

jewels.name: Red headlamp for the dark sky
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to Black Diamond Equipment (AvantLink)
jewels.blurb: NPS stargazing kit: a red flashlight or headlamp to "preserve your night vision", binoculars or a telescope, and a star chart or app; allow "up to thirty minutes for the human eye to adjust to the darkness".

jewels.name: Satellite communicator where phones fail
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Cell phone reception is not reliable in the park and surrounding areas. Do not rely on them!" and on the directions page, "Do not rely on navigation apps to guide to correct locations."

jewels.name: Winter backcountry kit (shovel, beacon, probe)
jewels.blurb: NPS winter list: a "properly fitted backpack", food, water, "extra clothing (especially extra socks and gloves)", and in avalanche terrain a "snow shovel," "avalanche beacon," and "avalanche probe."

jewels.name: Stargazer Inn

faq.q: Is Great Basin National Park free?
faq.a: Entry is: "An entrance pass is not required to access Great Basin National Park." Cave tours ($5-$40 for adults) and developed campgrounds ($20 a night) carry their own fees.

faq.q: Can you camp in Great Basin National Park?
faq.a: Yes. "Great Basin has five campgrounds available for visitors. Some campgrounds are closed seasonally due to weather." There are group sites at Grey Cliffs, free primitive campsites ("free but do not have water") and backcountry camping; "There are many options to camp outside Great Basin National Park when the campgrounds fill."

faq.q: Where can you see bristlecone pines in Great Basin National Park?
faq.a: On the Bristlecone Trail from the Bristlecone Trailhead at the end of the Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive: 2.8 miles round trip, 600 feet of gain from 9,890 feet, rated Moderate, to the Wheeler Peak Bristlecone Grove, home to "the oldest living organisms in the world."

faq.q: What is the closest airport to Great Basin National Park?
faq.a: The NPS lists Cedar City Regional Airport at 142 miles, St. George Regional Airport at 207 miles, Salt Lake City at 234 miles and Las Vegas at 286 miles; the full-service airports with "rental cars, international flights" are Salt Lake City and Las Vegas.

faq.q: How far is Great Basin National Park from Las Vegas?
faq.a: The NPS gives 286 miles from the Las Vegas airport. From southern Nevada: "Take U.S. Highway 93 north to the junction with Highways 6 & 50", then south on Nevada 487 five miles to Baker and west on Highway 488 five miles to the park.

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Great Basin National Park?
faq.a: Only in limited places: "Leashed pets can only be exercised in the campgrounds, in front of the visitor centers, and along roads." "Pets are not permitted on trails or in the backcountry of the park, except leashed pets on the Lexington Arch Trail or the trail between Baker and the Great Basin Visitor Center", and "Pets are not permitted in Lehman Caves or at evening programs".

faq.q: Is Great Basin National Park open in winter?
faq.a: Yes. "Lehman Caves Tours are also offered year round" and "Lower Lehman Creek Campground remains open through winter." "The Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive closes to vehicle traffic, but remains open to skiers and snowshoers", and "no food service exists in the park during the winter."

faq.q: Is there cell service in Great Basin National Park?
faq.a: Not reliably: "Cell phone reception is not reliable in the park and surrounding areas. Do not rely on them!"

faq.q: When was Great Basin National Park established?
faq.a: "Great Basin National Park - October 27, 1986; Lehman Caves National Monument - January 24, 1922".

faq.q: What time zone is Great Basin National Park in?
faq.a: Pacific. Driving in from southern Utah, "you will be crossing into the Pacific Time zone when you cross the Nevada border."

faq.q: Is there lodging or food inside Joshua Tree National Park?
faq.a: No. The NPS states there is no lodging in the park, and no gas stations, restaurants or grocery stores. There is no water in the interior of the park, so visitors bring their own food, water and supplies.

faq.q: How do I book a campsite in Joshua Tree?
faq.a: Black Rock, Cottonwood, Indian Cove, Jumbo Rocks, Ryan and Sheep Pass Group take reservations on recreation.gov the same day or up to 6 months ahead. Belle, Hidden Valley and White Tank are first-come, first-served: occupy a site, then register and pay at an entrance station within one hour.

faq.q: How much does it cost to enter Joshua Tree?
faq.a: $30 per private vehicle for 7 days, $25 per motorcycle, $15 per person on foot or bicycle (under 16 free), or $55 for a Joshua Tree Annual Pass.

faq.q: Do non-US residents pay the $100 nonresident fee at Joshua Tree?
faq.a: The NPS list of parks charging a $100 nonresident fee to non-US residents 16 and over names eleven parks, and Joshua Tree is not on it.

faq.q: When is Joshua Tree busiest?
faq.a: October through May, with the busiest times on weekends, holidays and spring break (March to mid-April). The NPS suggests arriving before 8 am and using the North or South Entrance; the West Entrance is the busiest.

faq.q: Where is the best stargazing in Joshua Tree?
faq.a: The park is an International Dark Sky Park with designated stargazing areas at Quail Springs, Hidden Valley, Cap Rock and Ryan Mountain parking lots; for darker skies the NPS names Cottonwood Campground and Pinto Basin Road between Cholla Cactus Garden and Cottonwood.

Crossing times: "Anacapa & Santa Cruz: About 1 hour / Santa Rosa & Santa Barbara: About 2.5-3.5 hours / San Miguel: About 3-4.5 hours". (805) 642-1393.

jewels.booking_route: none needed - free park trail; reached by Island Packers boat
jewels.blurb: 2 miles round trip, MODERATE, from Scorpion Beach: "Not to be missed. Magnificent coastal vistas and seasonal whale viewing. To avoid a steep climb, hike clockwise, beginning from campground (near site #22) and looping back to Scorpion Anchorage."

jewels.name: Painted Cave, Santa Cruz Island
jewels.booking_route: none needed - seen from the water; no landing
jewels.blurb: NPS: "one of the largest and deepest sea caves in the world", on the northwest coastline of Santa Cruz.

"The park visitor center has a tower with telescopes, which can be used for whale watching."

Closed Thanksgiving and December 25.

jewels.name: Channel Islands Junior Ranger badge

"Bring your completed booklet to the visitor center in Ventura Harbor or park staff on the islands to get your badge. jewels.blurb: "25 sites plus 6 group sites", half a mile from the pier, vault toilets, drinking water available; the NPS calls it "the most convenient park campground and provides the most recreational opportunities." "Reservations are required for all park campgrounds" and "can be made up to six months in advance on recreation.gov."

jewels.name: The island campgrounds of Anacapa, Santa Rosa, San Miguel and Santa Barbara
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov, up to six months ahead
jewels.blurb: Anacapa: 7 sites, half a mile from the pier "(includes 157 stairs)", no drinking water; Santa Rosa's Water Canyon: 15 sites, flush toilets, drinking water; San Miguel: 9 sites, "1 mile on steep/narrow trail"; Santa Barbara: 10 sites; Prisoners Harbor on Santa Cruz: 6 sites. "Campfires are not allowed."

jewels.name: Water, food and layers for a day on the islands
jewels.blurb: NPS: "There are no supplies on the islands. Take water, food, and other necessities." "Weather conditions change rapidly; dress in layers." Island Packers adds a jacket, closed-toe shoes, sunscreen and a hat to the list.

jewels.name: Wind-proof tent and stove for island camping
jewels.blurb: NPS camping rules: sturdy, low-profile tents with stakes for the wind, "especially outer islands"; "Campfires are not allowed. Use only chemical-fuel stoves for cooking"; "Campers must store all food and trash in animal-proof containers. Food storage boxes are provided at campsites"; "Campers must pack out their own trash."

jewels.name: Sea kayak safety kit: lifejacket, helmet, wetsuit
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to rei.com (AvantLink); boats and wetsuits are included on the concessioner's guided tours
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Lifejackets-all paddlers must have lifejackets"; visitors must "wear a helmet at all times when exploring sea caves"; "Wetsuits are highly recommended. Water temperatures remain cold throughout the year." Paddlers also carry a VHF radio, tow line, compass, throw bag, first aid kit and signalling device.

jewels.name: Channel Islands Adventure Company
jewels.booking_route: ZAUI online booking (sbadventureco.zaui.net) from the own website
jewels.blurb: "Authorized Concessioner in Channel Islands National Park" since 1999: "Channel Islands Sea Cave Kayak Tours" and guided snorkelling; "Ocean kayaks, paddle jackets, helmets, wet suits, and basic kayaking instruction are included." Snorkel tour "Ages 10+" and guests "must know how to swim". Has "led hundreds of schools groups on outdoor education trips since 1999." The NPS names it as the guided kayak concessioner at Scorpion Anchorage, with "snorkel equipment rentals". (805) 884-9283.

jewels.name: Channel Islands Kayak Center
jewels.booking_route: own website tours page or phone
jewels.blurb: "local kayak and stand up paddleboard rentals, our family friendly History and Wildlife kayak adventure tour, as well servicing rentals and guided kayak tours to the world famous Channel Islands"; sells the Hobie kayak line with "free demo's daily". Channel Islands Harbor (3600 S. Harbor Blvd.) and Ventura (1691 Spinnaker Drive). Island Packers: "Rentals are available through Channel Islands Kayak Center." (805) 984-5995.

jewels.name: Ventura Dive & Sport
jewels.booking_route: charter portal from the own website; phone
jewels.blurb: 1559 Spinnaker Dr, Suite 108, Ventura: a 5-Star PADI Instructor Development Center with "Rental Equipment", PADI courses including SCUBA Camp (ages 10-15), and the dive boat Raptor ("Fast, comfortable and spacious") running trips to Anacapa and Santa Cruz. 1-805-650-6500.

jewels.name: Ventura Beach RV Resort
jewels.blurb: 800 West Main Street, Ventura, on 14 acres: RV sites, tent camping and rentals; "Swimming pool and hot tub, restrooms and showers, laundry facilities, free Wi-Fi, a recreation room, playground, general store"; "Just a short 7-minute walk from the beach and minutes from Ventura Pier and Downtown Ventura." "NO ONLINE RESERVATIONS! PLEASE CALL 805-643-9137".

jewels.name: Rincon RV Parkway
jewels.booking_route: none - first come, first served (Ventura County Parks)
jewels.blurb: Pacific Coast Highway, 6 miles north of Ventura: "Close to 130 sites" for self-contained RVs only; "No hook-ups. First come, first served only. 5 day stay limit April 1- October 31; 14 day limit November 1 - March 31."

jewels.name: Faria County Campground
jewels.blurb: 4350 West Pacific Coast Highway, 5 miles north of Ventura: "42 sites for tents and RVs. Full hook-ups, showers, fire rings, playground, horseshoe pits." Booked through Ventura County Parks (ventura.org/parks-department or 805-654-5000).

"There are 90 campsites" for self-contained vehicles only, "Tents are not permitted"; the Ventura River Group Camp has "four developed group campsites, each with a capacity of 30 people" plus a primitive RV area "for groups up to 50 people". California State Parks notes North Beach "closed through at least June 2026 due to construction projects".

Outdoor heated pool, bicycle rentals, Alexander's Restaurant; the listing notes proximity to Channel Islands National Park. (805) 658-1212.

jewels.name: Residence Inn by Marriott Ventura Beach

faq.q: Can you drive to Channel Islands National Park?
faq.a: Not to the islands. The NPS says "you can't drive to the islands. A short but exciting ocean voyage or a commercial flight in a small airplane is required." You can drive to the mainland visitor center in Ventura Harbor, "the only location visitable in under half a day without island travel."

faq.q: How do I get to Channel Islands National Park from Ventura?
faq.a: By boat. "Islands can only be reached by boat. Advanced planning is highly recommended." Island Packers, "1691 Spinnaker Dr. Ventura, CA 93001", (805) 642-1393, runs the public boat service from Ventura Harbor and Channel Islands Harbor.

faq.q: How long is the ferry ride to Channel Islands National Park?
faq.a: Island Packers: "Travel times vary by island, route, weather, and wildlife sightings: Anacapa & Santa Cruz: About 1 hour / Santa Rosa & Santa Barbara: About 2.5-3.5 hours / San Miguel: About 3-4.5 hours".

faq.q: Can you camp at Channel Islands National Park?
faq.a: Yes, on all five islands. "Reservations are required for all park campgrounds" and "can be made up to six months in advance on recreation.gov." Scorpion Canyon on Santa Cruz has "25 sites plus 6 group sites" and drinking water; on most islands "Drinking water...must be brought with you". "Campfires are not allowed."

faq.q: How much does Channel Islands National Park cost?
faq.a: Entry is free: "An entrance pass is not required to access Channel Islands National Park." Camping and the boat crossing are paid separately; those fares were not on the pages read.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Channel Islands National Park?
faq.a: The NPS says "The best chance for warm weather, calm winds, and seas continues" through the fall, particularly October. "Dense fog is common during the late spring and early summer months", and "most rain falling between December and March." Gray whales pass "from mid- to late-December through mid-March".

faq.q: Is Channel Islands National Park dog friendly?
faq.a: No. "No pets. Pets are not allowed on the islands. Pets can carry diseases that could harm the island fox or other animals that are unique to the islands. Service animals require a permit from the park superintendent."

faq.q: Can you snorkel at Channel Islands National Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Cool off after a hike with a snorkel, dive, or kayak in the Landing Cove on Anacapa Island or at Scorpion Anchorage on Santa Cruz Island." The park's kayak concessioner, Channel Islands Adventure Company, offers "snorkel equipment rentals, and guided snorkel tours"; "Wetsuits are highly recommended. Water temperatures remain cold throughout the year."

faq.q: Does Channel Islands National Park have a visitor center?
faq.a: Yes, on the mainland at 1901 Spinnaker Drive, Ventura: "The fully accessible visitor center is open 8:30 am until 5 pm daily", with free ranger programmes "On weekends and holidays at 11 am and 3 pm". A second contact station, Outdoors Santa Barbara, is at 113 Harbor Way, Santa Barbara.

faq.q: Is Channel Islands National Park good for kids?
faq.a: The park runs a Junior Ranger programme: "Complete a Channel Islands Junior Ranger Booklet and earn a free badge." "Booklets are also available at the visitor center, on the islands from park staff, and at Island Packers."

faq.q: Do I need a reservation to drive into Yosemite in 2026?
faq.a: No. The NPS announced it will no longer use a timed reservation system in 2026, and is managing access through real-time traffic monitoring, parking management and extra staffing at peak periods. It recommends planning ahead for weekends and holidays and considering weekday visits.

faq.q: How do I get a permit to hike Half Dome?
faq.a: Permits are required seven days a week while the cables are up, with a maximum of 300 hikers a day. The preseason lottery runs March 1 through March 31 with results in mid-April; it costs a $10 non-refundable application fee plus $10 per person if a permit is awarded.

faq.q: How do I book a campsite inside Yosemite?
faq.a: All thirteen NPS campgrounds list reservations as required in season. Most Yosemite Valley, Wawona and Hodgdon Meadow sites are released 5 months ahead on the 15th, Camp 4 one week ahead, and the Tioga Road campgrounds two weeks ahead. For 2026 the park said all front-country campgrounds are reservable on Recreation.gov.

faq.q: Where can I go glamping near Yosemite?
faq.a: Mariposa County's tourism site lists AutoCamp (Airstreams and tents, Midpines), Wildhaven (tents and cabins, Mariposa), Indian Flat's Jupe tents (El Portal), Yosemite Bug tent cabins (Midpines), Tenaya's Explorer Cabins (Fish Camp) and in-park Curry Village and High Sierra Camps. On Highway 120, Under Canvas Yosemite sits 10 minutes from the Big Oak Flat entrance.

faq.q: How much does it cost to enter Yosemite?
faq.a: $35 per private vehicle for seven days, $30 per motorcycle, $20 per person on foot or bicycle, or $70 for an annual pass. Non-US residents aged 16 and over pay an extra $100 each unless they hold an annual or America the Beautiful pass. Cash is not accepted.

faq.q: Can I get to Yosemite without a car?
faq.a: Yes. YARTS runs buses to Yosemite Valley from Merced and Mariposa on Highway 140, Tuolumne County on Highway 120, Mono County on Highway 395/120E, and Fresno and Madera County on Highway 41.

jewels.blurb: a 2.7-mile loop from the Sherman Tree parking lot or shuttle stop through the Giant Forest sequoias, the largest unlogged grove; listed among NPS ranger recommendations

jewels.name: Big Trees Trail
jewels.blurb: a 1.1-mile loop from the Giant Forest Museum parking lot, one of the NPS's ranger-recommended Giant Forest walks

jewels.name: Moro Rock
jewels.blurb: a granite dome in Giant Forest whose stairway is on the National Register of Historic Places; 0.4 mile from the trailhead (plus a 3.2-mile road walk from Giant Forest Museum when the road is closed); NPS: "Avoid climbing if snow or ice are present. Stay away from Moro Rock during thunderstorms or if there's static in the air."

jewels.name: Tunnel Log
jewels.blurb: a fallen giant sequoia carved through so cars could pass, driven through "Since 1935", 0.5 mile past Moro Rock; "Vehicles taller than 8 feet (2.4 m) can use a bypass"; the road "generally opens by the Wednesday before Memorial Day"

jewels.name: Crystal Cave
jewels.booking_route: online only via Sequoia Parks Conservancy (sequoiaparksconservancy.org), at least 36 hours ahead
jewels.blurb: a marble cave seen only on a guided tour of about 50 minutes on a half-mile loop; "Bring jackets; the temperature inside is 50 degrees F (10 degrees C)"; "Tickets are not available at the cave"; vehicles over 22 feet cumulative length not allowed on Cave Road; tours ended for 2026, expected back late spring 2027

jewels.name: Crescent Meadow and Tharp's Log
jewels.blurb: a meadow loop of "about 1.8 miles round trip" at the end of Moro Rock / Crescent Meadow Road, to Tharp's Log, "a cabin built onto a hollowed-out sequoia in 1858"; on weekends "shuttles are the only way to reach Moro Rock and Crescent Meadow"; "partially paved and may be accessible, depending on abilities"; NPS: "Bears are common to see in meadows, especially in the spring and early summer"

jewels.name: Mineral King
jewels.booking_route: none needed; local wilderness permits at the Mineral King Ranger Station
jewels.blurb: a subalpine valley open "seasonally from late May through October"; "Mineral King Road is extremely narrow, steep, winding, and unpaved in some areas" and "RVs and trailers are not advised"; "Trails here are solitary, remote, and strenuous"; marmots "have been known to dine on radiator hoses and car wiring"; nearest gas in Three Rivers about 30 miles and 1.5 hours away; road delays and closures for the rest of the 2026 season

jewels.name: Lodgepole Campground
jewels.blurb: the central Sequoia campground at 6,700 feet with showers and laundry nearby, beside the Lodgepole Market, open seasonally May to October; "Site reservations are available online at recreation.gov or by phone at 877-444-6777"

jewels.name: Tokopah Falls Trail, Lodgepole
jewels.blurb: a 3.8-mile round trip from the trailhead across the road bridge from the Lodgepole Campground parking lot, on the NPS ranger recommendations list

jewels.name: Marble Falls Trail, Foothills
jewels.blurb: a 6.2-mile round trip from Potwisha Campground near site #14, in the low Foothills; NPS: "Drowning is the primary cause of death in the parks. Rocks near rivers are slippery."

jewels.name: Hospital Rock Picnic Area
jewels.blurb: a Foothills picnic area by the Middle Fork of the Kaweah, "usually warm and dry throughout the year", with outdoor exhibits on Native American history - the place called Pah-din - plus accessible restrooms, grills, water and RV parking; the Paradise Creek Trail starts nearby

jewels.name: Giant Forest Museum and Foothills Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: the two Sequoia visitor centres open 9 am to 4:30 pm in the NPS spring schedule, each with a Sequoia Parks Conservancy park store; Foothills has free public Wi-Fi; Giant Forest Museum issues self-serve wilderness permits and lends wheelchairs

jewels.name: Potwisha Campground
jewels.blurb: the Foothills campground listed as "Open year-round", the only campground with a dump station; NPS campsites are $32 a night for up to six people, reserved on recreation.gov; "Roadside camping is not permitted in the parks"

jewels.name: Wilderness permits and backpacking
jewels.blurb: "Wilderness permits cost $15 each trip plus $5 per person within the quota season" (May 22 to September 26, 2026), reservable on recreation.gov up to six months ahead, released daily at 7:00 AM Pacific; walk-ups from 1:00 pm the day before; "bear canisters ... are still required in most of the park"

jewels.name: Montecito Sequoia Lodge and Stony Creek Lodge
jewels.booking_route: phone (operator sites not checked this build)
jewels.blurb: two lodges named in the NPS trip planner on the Sequoia National Forest stretch of Generals Highway: Montecito Sequoia, "cabins, a restaurant, a hotel, and Wi-Fi" ((559) 565-3388); Stony Creek, "room rentals, a market, and a gas station" ((559) 565-3909); both seasonal

jewels.name: Wuksachi Lodge
jewels.blurb: the in-park lodge, open year-round and operated by Delaware North: "102 spacious guest rooms" in Standard, Deluxe and Superior categories, a "90-seat full-service restaurant and lounge" with an "oversized stone fireplace"; ADA-compliant rooms in all categories; no central air conditioning at this elevation, fans provided

jewels.name: The Peaks Restaurant and Pizza Deck, Wuksachi
jewels.blurb: the concessioner's "upscale dining at Wuksachi" serving Sierra alpine cuisine with forest views, plus the Wuksachi Pizza Deck and the Lodgepole Grill, Market and Snack Bar; the Lodgepole Market rents tents, sleeping bags, stoves and trekking poles

jewels.name: Sequoia Adventure Tour (Sequoia Parks Conservancy)
jewels.blurb: "A customized adventure with your own knowledgeable guide" through Giant Forest from the park's nonprofit partner: 2 to 6 hours, up to 8 people, $150 per hour with a 2-hour minimum

jewels.name: Pear Lake Winter Hut
jewels.booking_route: FareHarbor, reservations open December 9 at 9:00 AM
jewels.blurb: a ten-bunk backcountry hut 6 miles from Wolverton (7,200 ft) to Pear Lake (9,200 ft), $75 per person per night, February 6 to April 5 in 2026; "for experienced backcountry skiers and snowshoers only"; "avalanche conditions exist at all times on the trail"; "There are NO REFUNDS or date changes"

jewels.name: Sequoia Parks Conservancy Field Institute
jewels.blurb: naturalist-led adventures and events such as the Sequoia Foothills River Walk, Stargazing at Lake Kaweah and the Christmas Bird Count, run by the park's partner organisation

jewels.name: All-Outdoors Kaweah River Rafting, Three Rivers
jewels.blurb: a one-day trip on "Class IV+ | Fast-Paced Intricate Whitewater" from Three Rivers Hideaway Camp, mid-April through June (snowmelt dependent), minimum age 15, $244 per person; one of five outfitters listed as permitted on the Kaweah

jewels.name: Three Rivers Hideaway
jewels.blurb: "a full service RV Park, with cabins & campground" on the Kaweah River, open year-round, "3.5 miles from the Foothills Entrance (Hwy. 198) to Sequoia National Park and 5 miles from Lake Kaweah"; the rafting meet point for All-Outdoors

jewels.name: Gateway Restaurant & Lodge, Three Rivers
jewels.booking_route: own restaurant reservation system and lodging booking platform; (559) 561-4133
jewels.blurb: "a cozy seven-room lodge with a restaurant that serves breakfast, lunch and dinner options in both casual and fine-dining settings" on the Kaweah River at 45978 Sierra Drive, bar open until midnight, with banquet and reception services

jewels.name: Sequoia Guides
jewels.booking_route: email or call/text (559) 556-4936, then PayPal invoice
jewels.blurb: private guiding by lead guide Krista Simonic under NPS Commercial Use Permit #SEKI-FC-2026-01: day hiking from $400 a group, stargazing from $175, snowshoeing December-March from $350, step-on tours for motor coaches, and wheelchair accessible tours; "Every private tour plants a tree"

jewels.name: Sequoia Sightseeing Tours, Three Rivers
jewels.blurb: "Small-group experiences using comfortable air-conditioned 10-passenger vans": Sequoia Majesty from Three Rivers year-round, Sequoia Splendor from Wuksachi Lodge (April 26-October 30), and private full-day and winter tours

jewels.name: Keifers Giant Sequoia Tours
jewels.blurb: private tours into Sequoia and Kings Canyon "using luxurious SUVs with experienced former park rangers": a full-day Sequoia tour, a half-day Giant Sequoia tour and a half-day Winter Wonderland tour; Visit Visalia lists year-round tours for groups of 1-6

jewels.name: Big Trees Tours
jewels.booking_route: FareHarbor; telescope experience via Airbnb only
jewels.blurb: guided experiences led by a local wildlife biologist: the 3-hour easy Heart of the Giant Forest Hike from the Sherman Tree parking area, and one-hour group stargazing near Potwisha Campground

jewels.name: AutoCamp Sequoia, Three Rivers
jewels.booking_route: own website (engine not identified on the page read)
jewels.blurb: glamping at 40457 Sierra Drive on a river bend: Airstreams, cabins, BaseCamps that pair an Airstream suite with a canvas tent, and bunk rooms; pool and river access, a clubhouse, bike rentals, EV charging, a Kitchen and General Store, complimentary granola and coffee, and arranged park tours and onsite yoga

jewels.name: Sequoia RV Ranch, Three Rivers
jewels.blurb: a riverside RV park "only 8 miles from the entrance of Sequoia National Park" with Deluxe River Sites, Premium Pull Thrus, water and electric sites and dry camping for RVs and tents, a spring-fed swimming hole and fishing hole, laundry and a dog park

jewels.name: Lemon Cove Village RV Park, Lemon Cove
jewels.blurb: a year-round Good Sam park with full hookups, level pull-through sites, a swimming pool, gemstone mining and fossil dig; "Walk-ins welcome. Reservations encouraged, but not necessary"; about 19 miles east of Visalia

jewels.name: Kaweah Oaks Preserve, near Visalia
jewels.blurb: 344 acres protecting "one of the last remaining valley oak riparian forests in the San Joaquin Valley", seven miles east of downtown Visalia off Highway 198; free, open "Sunrise to Sunset 365 Days a Year"; "over 300 plant and animal species including bobcats, great horned owls"; no bicycles or horses; run by Sequoia Riverlands Trust

jewels.name: Riata Ranch International, Three Rivers
jewels.booking_route: contact page or (559) 303-0729; no online booking or rates seen
jewels.blurb: listed by Visit Visalia for "Trail rides in Sierra Nevada foothills along the North Fork of the Kaweah River"; the ranch at 42390 North Kaweah River Road offers "Horseback riding, training, and adventure"

jewels.name: Kaweah Marina, Lake Kaweah, Lemon Cove
jewels.blurb: "patio boats, aqua cycles, kayaks and paddle boards available for rent" on Lake Kaweah off Highway 198; winter hours mid-September to March 9am-4pm, closed Mondays and Tuesdays

jewels.name: The Vintage Press, Visalia
jewels.blurb: farm-to-fork restaurant open since 1966 at 216 N Willis Street, with over 900 wines and what Wine Spectator calls "one of the best wine lists in the world"

jewels.name: Visalia Craft Beer Trail
jewels.blurb: a downtown brewery district trail with BarrelHouse Brewing Co. and Brewbakers Brewing Co., and "Visalia's newest tap rooms" Salty Walrus and Long Shot; wine rooms include Blend Wine Room and Wine Buff Tasting Room

jewels.name: We Three Bakery, Three Rivers
jewels.blurb: a local bakery at 43370 Sierra Drive with "coffee and baked goods for early risers" that packs lunches for the river or the park; patio dining; closed Tuesdays

jewels.name: Sequoia Cider Mill Restaurant, Three Rivers
jewels.blurb: a family restaurant at 40311 Sierra Drive serving breakfast, lunch and dinner daily; "Specialize in grilled meats and Mexican food"

jewels.name: Serrano's Mexican Restaurant, Three Rivers
jewels.blurb: daily breakfast, lunch and dinner at 40869 Sierra Drive, from "burritos and tacos to full seafood dinners", with patio dining

faq.q: Do I need a reservation to enter Sequoia National Park?
faq.a: No. The NPS states that reservations are not accepted or required. A private vehicle pays $35 for 1-7 days.

faq.q: Is there an extra fee for international visitors?
faq.a: Yes. The NPS states that each non-US resident aged 16 and older must pay a $100 nonresident fee in addition to the standard entrance fee, unless admitted with an Annual or America the Beautiful Pass. The Non-Resident America the Beautiful Annual Pass is $250.

faq.q: Is Crystal Cave open?
faq.a: Not now. The NPS states that guided tours of Crystal Cave have ended for the 2026 season and are expected to begin again in late spring of 2027. Tickets are sold online only through the Sequoia Parks Conservancy and are not available at the cave.

faq.q: Can I drive an RV to Moro Rock or Crystal Cave?
faq.a: Not a long one. The NPS lists a 22-foot restriction on Moro Rock / Crescent Meadow Road, with longer vehicles not allowed, and vehicles over 22 feet cumulative length are not allowed on Crystal Cave Road. It recommends 22 feet on Generals Highway from Potwisha Campground to Giant Forest.

faq.q: How far is the General Sherman Tree from the parking lot?
faq.a: The NPS says it is about a half mile from the main parking lot, with an uphill return; an accessible paved path of about 500 feet, gently sloped, leads from the accessible parking on Generals Highway.

faq.q: Which campground is open all year?
faq.a: The NPS lists Potwisha Campground in the Foothills as open year-round. Standard sites are $32 a night and reservations are made on recreation.gov.
