hero.query: Sequoia National Park, California

name: Kings Canyon National Park
line: General Grant Tree and the glaciated Cedar Grove canyon

jewels.name: General Grant Tree Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park trail; park entrance fee applies
jewels.blurb: A "1/3 mile (0.5 km)" "paved trail": "One of the world's largest living trees. President Coolidge proclaimed it the Nation's Christmas tree in 1926." The NPS calls the tree "the world's second largest tree by volume". Joint SEKI page; the tree is in Kings Canyon's Grant Grove.

jewels.name: Zumwalt Meadow Trail
jewels.blurb: "0.8 mile (1.3 km)" that "passes high granite walls, lush meadows, and the Kings River"; "relatively level and may be suitable for some wheelchair users." Cedar Grove, Kings Canyon side (joint SEKI page).

jewels.name: Mist Falls Trail
jewels.blurb: An "8-mile round trip" from Cedar Grove: a "sandy trail follows the glaciated South Fork Canyon through forest and chaparral", gaining "600'" "during the last mile."

jewels.name: Roaring River Falls
jewels.blurb: "A very short, shady walk to a powerful waterfall rushing through a granite chute"; "Paved, relatively accessible." The planner lists it at 0.4 miles from a trailhead on Highway 180.

jewels.name: Panoramic Point
jewels.blurb: "offering great views of the Kings Canyon, Hume Lake, and the mountains beyond"; the trail is 0.5 miles from the Panoramic Point parking lot (spring planner). "Motor homes and trailers prohibited" on the road, which the planner lists among spring closures.

jewels.name: Big Stump Loop Trail
jewels.blurb: A "2-mile loop" "through an old-growth giant sequoia grove that was logged in the late nineteenth century", with "large sequoia stumps" (the spring planner gives 1.6 miles from the Big Stump Picnic Area). Big Stump is "The first resting spot after the park entrance station on Highway 180".

jewels.name: North Grove Loop
jewels.blurb: "1.5 mile (2.4 km)", "lightly traveled", with "a close look at the big trees" through "meadows and creeks, through mixed conifer and sequoia forest".

jewels.name: Big Baldy Ridge and Buena Vista Peak
jewels.blurb: Big Baldy Ridge: "roundtrip 4.4 miles (7.1 km)", "600 feet (183 m)", "great views out and down into Redwood Canyon" to "the summit at 8209 feet". Buena Vista Peak: "2 mile (3.2 km) round-trip" to a "360-degree view".

jewels.name: Knapp's Cabin and Sheep Creek Cascade
jewels.blurb: Knapp's Cabin: "A short walk" to a historic fishing cabin from the 1920s. Sheep Creek Cascade: a "two-mile round trip" that "gains 600' in elevation" on a "moderately strenuous hike up the forested Don Cecil Trail".

jewels.name: Kings Canyon Visitor Center
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free visitor center inside the fee area
jewels.blurb: Grant Grove: open "9 am to 4:30 pm" (spring 2026 planner); Park Store (Sequoia Parks Conservancy), "Free public Wi-Fi", "Self-issue wilderness permits"; manual wheelchairs to borrow; "assistive listening devices and audio description are available for the park film."

jewels.name: Wilderness permits from Roads End
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov (Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks Wilderness Permits) or self-issue station
jewels.blurb: "Reservations can be made up to six months in advance of your trip, and are released daily at 7:00 AM Pacific Standard Time"; 2026 quota season "May 22, 2026 - September 26, 2026"; "$15 each trip plus $5 per person within the quota season"; the Road's End Permit Station in Cedar Grove opens "7:00am - 3:30pm" in quota season. The parks are "97% designated Wilderness" (spring planner).

jewels.name: Azalea Campground, Grant Grove
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov or (877) 444-6777; off-season scan-and-pay in the Recreation.gov app
jewels.blurb: Recreation.gov: "110 sites" at 6,500 feet, each with "a picnic table, a fire ring, and a food storage box", flush toilets and potable water, near Grant Grove Village; "Late spring, summer and early fall the campground is on reservations. When it is not on reservations sites are first come first served". Planner: "$32 per night".

jewels.name: Sheep Creek Campground, Cedar Grove
jewels.blurb: "nestled in the stunning Kings Canyon, one of the deepest canyons in the United States" and "a wonderful place for families to spend time in the great outdoors"; paved roads "making it easier for both RVs and smaller cars"; five comfort stations with flush toilets; the Cedar Grove Visitor Center is ".25 miles" away.

jewels.name: Moraine and Sentinel Campgrounds, Cedar Grove
jewels.blurb: Moraine: each site has "a fire ring, picnic table and large bear-proof food storage box", paved roads for RVs and cars, "five comfort stations"; Cedar Grove Visitor Center ".75 miles" away. Sentinel: "Each campsite has a large food storage locker (47"W x 33"D x 28"H)" (nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/sentinel.htm).

jewels.name: Canyon View Group Sites, Cedar Grove
jewels.blurb: "four large group sites and 12 mid-sized group sites for a total of 16 sites"; "This is a TENT ONLY Group Campground. No RV's or Trailers allowed." Flush toilets and drinking water; "Nearby the Kings River offers excellent trout fishing."

jewels.name: Sunset Campground group sites, Grant Grove
jewels.blurb: At 6,500 feet; "Group sites A & B are for tents only"; "Each group site can accommodate 15-30 people"; "located across the street from Grant Grove Village"; trails within walking distance include "the one mile trail to the General Grant Tree".

jewels.name: Grant Grove Stables
jewels.booking_route: call the stable for reservations (number not on the NPS page); visitsequoia.com lists (866) 807-3598
jewels.blurb: "1-2 hour guided trips. Routes include the General Grant Tree, North Grove, Lion Meadow, and Dead Giant Loop." "Currently rides are offered to single family groups of up to 6 people." "Open typically June through mid-October, weather permitting". A concession permit holder.

jewels.name: Cedar Grove Pack Station
jewels.booking_route: call the pack station; walk-in may be available for day rides
jewels.blurb: "Rides range from one hour to all day, and there are options for all experience levels. Day trips offer rides along the Kings Canyon River." Single family groups of up to 6; "Walk-in reservations may be available for day rides." June to mid-October.

jewels.name: John Muir Lodge, Grant Grove
jewels.blurb: "The pinnacle of Kings Canyon lodging", 36 rooms, "Built in 1998" with "open-beam ceilings, a stone fireplace, and a historic redwood mantel"; 86728 Highway 180; dogs at "$25 per night". Operated by DNC Parks & Resorts at SEKI, Inc. (Delaware North), the joint Sequoia and Kings Canyon concessioner.

jewels.name: Grant Grove Cabins
jewels.blurb: "both timber and tent cabin styles": Duplex Cabin with Bath, Camp Cabin, Tent Cabin ("Tent cabins do not have heat or electricity") and the Honeymoon Cabin #9, "Built in 1910"; all "within walking distance of Grant Grove and the world-famous General Grant Tree." Check-in at John Muir Lodge (Delaware North).

jewels.name: Cedar Grove Lodge
jewels.blurb: "Nestled in a glaciated canyon, Cedar Grove Lodge is located in the heart of Kings Canyon National Park at Cedar Grove"; "Open May through mid-October"; 21 rooms, Patio Rooms with a kitchenette; "The front office at Cedar Grove Lodge closes daily at 9 p.m." (Delaware North).

jewels.name: Grant Grove Restaurant
jewels.booking_route: walk-in (no reservation method on the page)
jewels.blurb: "locally sourced, sustainable, and organic ingredients, surrounded by majestic giant sequoia trees overlooking Bradley Meadow"; breakfast 7-10 a.m., lunch/dinner 11:30 a.m.-8 p.m.; a courtyard with seasonal walk-up pizza, sandwiches, coffee and ice cream; kids menu. 83923 CA-180.

jewels.name: Cedar Grove Grill
jewels.blurb: "light meals and snacks" with "outdoor al fresco dining on our balcony overlooking the Kings River"; "counter service"; breakfast 7-10 AM, lunch 11:30 AM-2:30 PM, dinner 4-8 PM.

jewels.name: Grant Grove Market
jewels.blurb: "Next to John Muir Lodge three miles from the Kings Canyon, Big Stump entrance", "a buzzing retail hub where visitors can resupply, reenergize and regroup on arrival": groceries, beer, wine and camping supplies; in winter it stocks tire chains, hats and gloves, with snowshoes for rent. 9 AM-5 PM.

jewels.name: Cedar Grove Market
jewels.blurb: "near Roads End, right on Highway 180, for a fantastic park essentials pit stop"; stocks camping gear, "bear-proof food containers", picnic supplies and souvenirs; 7 AM-9 PM. The NPS notes canister rental is available at visitor centers "except for Cedar Grove", so this is Cedar Grove's canister source.

jewels.name: Bear canister for the Rae Lakes Loop and Kings Canyon wilderness
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to bearvault.com (AvantLink); or rent at a park visitor center
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Containers are required in the Dusy Basin, Rae Lakes Loop, North Dome, Rock Creek and Pear and Emerald Lakes areas from May 1 through October 31"; rentals "are available for rent at visitor centers, except for Cedar Grove". The permit page adds that canisters "are still required in most of the park, but may not be available for rental."

jewels.name: Water filter for park streams
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Park waterways may contain bacteria, including Giardia. Properly filter or treat water before drinking." And on altitude: "Plan for a slow ascent and drink lots of water."

jewels.name: Footwear traction and warm layers for snow season
jewels.blurb: The planner's map legend: "Traction device on footwear strongly recommended" on winter routes; "Hypothermia can occur year-round. Stay warm and eat snacks." Grant Grove Market stocks hats and gloves and rents snowshoes in winter (visitsequoia.com/shop).

jewels.name: Boyden Cavern
jewels.booking_route: FareHarbor (own website); walk-up tickets typically available in the mornings
jewels.blurb: "a fantastic marble cavern" with "stalactites, stalagmites, flowstone, pendants, and shields" in Sequoia National Forest, "19 miles east of Grant Grove on Highway 180"; walking tour 45-60 minutes, flashlight tours 65-75 minutes (minimum 4 guests); 2026 season "7 days a week through Nov 8, 2026"; "a small family run business" under a Forest Service permit.

jewels.name: Kings River Expeditions
jewels.blurb: "one and two-day whitewater rafting trips" on "the Class 3 Kings River", "just 90 minutes East of Fresno in the Sierra and Sequoia National Forests and near Kings Canyon and Yosemite National Parks"; trips "begin and end at Twin Pines Camp"; group trips offered; next rafting season begins "in April, 2027."

jewels.name: Kings Canyon Scenic Byway (Highway 180)
jewels.booking_route: none needed - public highway; park entrance fee applies inside the park
jewels.blurb: "50 spectacular miles leading to Roads End, all along Highway 180"; it "begins in the foothills outside of Fresno", "enters the Grant Grove area of Kings Canyon National Park", "descends through Sequoia National Forest" and "ends at the Cedar Grove area".

jewels.name: Hume Christian Camps, Hume Lake
jewels.blurb: "Hume Christian Camps & Retreats" at "64144 Hume Lake Rd, Hume, CA 93628": youth camps, adult retreats, school ministries and "Guest group rentals"; registration at register.hume.org. The NPS planner lists Hume Lake as the place to call for gas in Sequoia National Forest: "Hume Lake (559) 305-7770".

jewels.name: Mike And Di's Retreat, Dunlap
jewels.blurb: Three "Sky Pod" tree-tent units on a 40-acre property near 5,000 feet, each sleeping 2, with "Private flushing toilet and outdoor shower at each unit", a shared outdoor kitchen and private decks; about 10-15 minutes from the Grant Grove Visitor Center (host).

jewels.name: Delilah Ridge Winery vintage glamping, Squaw Valley
jewels.blurb: "46 acres" with "a small boutique winery", wine tastings on site, and six vintage trailers and bell tents - "Fiona (1967), Mai Tai (1954), Lola (1970 Airstream)" - with electricity; a seasonal pool; "only 20 minutes from the gates of Kings Canyon/Sequoia National Parks" (host). Own site tagline: "Your Kings Canyon & Sequoia Winery/Vintage Glamping Destination!"

jewels.name: Dunlap Canyon Retreat
jewels.blurb: "22 acres of camp sites" in Dunlap: 30 sites (1 tent-only group site, 25 RV/tent sites, 4 lodging yurts); sites #3-#5 with water and sewer hookups; "restrooms with showers" in a geodesic dome, laundry, a seasonal pond; "about 25mi from sequoia and Kings Canyon right off the Highway 180" (host).

jewels.name: Camp Hye Sierra, Dunlap
jewels.blurb: A 160-acre retreat "about 35 miles east of Fresno", "perfect for reflection and fellowship": 4 RV/tent sites ("no electrical hookup"), four cabin units ("MATTRESSES ONLY. YOU NEED TO BRING YOUR OWN SLEEPING BAGS AND PILLOWS"), two stocked lakes, canoes and paddle boats; "within a 30-minute drive from the Grant Grove Visitor Center" (host).

jewels.name: Bella Brooke Cafe and Gena's Sierra Inn, Dunlap
jewels.booking_route: walk-in ("No Reservations Needed"); motel booking via the own website
jewels.blurb: "37692 E Kings Canyon Road, Dunlap CA 93621": "aged steaks, country sized burgers, hearty pastas, strong coffee, and local micro brew beer"; "7am - 10pm Everyday. No Reservations Needed. Open To Everyone." Motel cabins and chalets; about 20 minutes from the Big Stump Entrance and "less than 5 minutes from the last gas and groceries before entering the National Parks."

jewels.name: Clingan's Junction cabins and coffee, Squaw Valley
jewels.blurb: "Cozy cabins + coffee, conveniently located 19 miles from Sequoia and King's Canyon National Park": four remodeled cabins (Mimi's Cottage, Sweet Mountain Cabin, Cozy Mountain Cabin, Clingan's Junction Cottage) and an on-site coffee shop; 559-790-6432. The site also says "just 16.2 miles from the entrance".

jewels.name: Marriott Hotel Visalia
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "300 South Court, Visalia, CA 93291", "46 miles from Kings Canyon Park North Entrance", described as "Upper-upscale, smoke-free, full-service, downtown hotel". Marriott's own page was not fetched (brand sites return 403), so nothing else is stated here. Visalia is the Sequoia-side gateway; the 46 miles is HotelGuides' figure.

jewels.name: Hampton Inn Visalia
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "4747 West Noble Avenue, Visalia, CA 93277", 49 miles from Kings Canyon Park North Entrance. Hilton's own page was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express Visalia
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "5625 West Cypress Avenue, Visalia, CA 93277", 49 miles from Kings Canyon Park North Entrance. IHG's own page was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

faq.q: Do you have to pay to enter Kings Canyon National Park?
faq.a: Yes. "Pay your entrance fee at park entrance stations." A 7-day pass for US residents is "$35" per single vehicle, "$30" per motorcycle and "$20" per individual; non-residents pay "$35 +$100/non-resident" per vehicle, the per-person fee charged "for each non-resident visitor 16 years or older". Annual and lifetime passes cover the fee.

faq.q: Can you camp in Kings Canyon National Park?
faq.a: Yes, in designated campgrounds: Azalea, Sunset and Crystal Springs at Grant Grove and Sentinel, Sheep Creek, Moraine and Canyon View group at Cedar Grove. "Reservations are required except for Azalea Campground"; sites hold up to six people at "$32 per night", and "Roadside camping is not permitted in the parks."

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Kings Canyon National Park?
faq.a: Only in developed areas, not on trails: "Pets are not permitted on any trails in the parks. Pets in designated areas must be kept on a maximum 6-foot (1.8 m) leash at all times." John Muir Lodge offers "Dog-friendly accommodations" at a "$25 per night pet fee" (visitsequoia.com).

faq.q: Do you need a permit for Kings Canyon National Park?
faq.a: For overnight wilderness trips, yes. "Reservations can be made up to six months in advance of your trip, and are released daily at 7:00 AM Pacific Standard Time"; in the 2026 quota season ("May 22, 2026 - September 26, 2026") the fee is "$15 each trip plus $5 per person". Day visitors pay the entrance fee.

faq.q: Where can you stay in Kings Canyon National Park?
faq.a: Three lodges run by the park concessioner: John Muir Lodge ("36 rooms in Kings Canyon National Park"), Grant Grove Cabins ("both timber and tent cabin styles") and Cedar Grove Lodge ("21 guest rooms", May through mid-October), booked at visitsequoia.com or (866) 807-3598 - plus the seven NPS campgrounds.

faq.q: Where can you eat in Kings Canyon National Park?
faq.a: Grant Grove Restaurant serves breakfast 7-10 a.m. and lunch/dinner 11:30 a.m.-8 p.m. "overlooking Bradley Meadow", with a seasonal walk-up courtyard; in Cedar Grove the Grill offers "light meals and snacks" on a balcony "overlooking the Kings River". The Grant Grove and Cedar Grove markets sell groceries and picnic supplies.

faq.q: Can you swim in Kings Canyon National Park?
faq.a: The NPS warns: "Drowning is the primary cause of death in the parks. Rocks near rivers are slippery. Most drowning victims did not intend to swim. Currents are strong, fast, and very cold. Do not leave children unattended anywhere near a river edge." For Cedar Grove it flags "Severe drowning danger", particularly spring through early summer (nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/cedar-grove.htm).

faq.q: Can you hunt in Kings Canyon National Park?
faq.a: No: "Hunting and trapping are illegal in the parks." In the neighbouring Sequoia National Forest hunting is allowed "Only seasonally with a license" (California Department of Fish and Wildlife, 559-243-4005).

faq.q: Is Kings Canyon a national park?
faq.a: Yes. "The Grant Grove area was originally General Grant National Park, created in 1890 to protect giant sequoias from logging." Today, per the NPS planner, "This is not one, but two national parks—Sequoia and Kings Canyon—managed by the National Park Service as one unit."

faq.q: Is Kings Canyon National Park open in winter?
faq.a: Grant Grove stays reachable, with "deep snow and cold temperatures in winter"; Cedar Grove "typically operates from May through early to mid-November" (nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/cedar-grove.htm). The spring 2026 planner listed "Highway 180 to Cedar Grove (opens late April)" and "Panoramic Point Road" as closed, and chains or traction devices can be required. Road conditions: (559) 565-3341.

seo.meta_title: Kings Canyon National Park: General Grant Tree & Cedar Grove | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: The General Grant Tree, Zumwalt Meadow and Mist Falls, seven campgrounds, three lodges, 2026 entrance fees, and glamping and RV stays on Highway 180.

name: Pinnacles National Park
line: Talus caves, volcanic spires and California condors

jewels.name: High Peaks to Bear Gulch Loop
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park trail; park entrance fee applies
jewels.blurb: "6.7 miles round trip, 4 to 5 hours", elevation "1,425 feet", rated "Strenuous": "ascending through wildflower-filled meadows in spring, then descending through shady woodlands".

jewels.name: Bear Gulch Cave
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park trail; check cave status before going
jewels.blurb: A talus cave sheltering "Townsend's big-eared bats", whose maternity colony is "the largest one between San Francisco and Mexico"; "Mid-May - Mid-July: The entire cave is closed to protect the bats during the pupping season". The Lower Cave can be explored "without needing to turn back, even when the upper section is closed." Lower and Upper Cave both "OPEN" on the day read.

jewels.name: California condors of the High Peaks
jewels.blurb: "In 2003, Pinnacles became a release site for the California Condor." The NPS birding page: "Arrive early to spot California Condors roosting before they take flight"; condors carry "vinyl ID tags" with colors indicating age, and sightings can be reported to the Pinnacles Condor Program at 831-389-4486, extension 4276.

jewels.name: Balconies Cave from Old Pinnacles Trailhead
jewels.blurb: "5.3 miles round trip, 3 to 5 hours", no elevation gain, rated "Moderate"; Balconies Cave "OPEN" on the day read. The NPS advises: "pack a flashlight or headlamp. Cave sections can be dark".

jewels.name: Moses Spring to Rim Trail Loop
jewels.blurb: "2.2 miles round trip, 1 to 1-1/2 hours", elevation "500 feet", rated "Moderate"; the NPS names Moses Spring Trail among its kid-friendly trails.

jewels.name: Condor Gulch to High Peaks Loop
jewels.blurb: "5.3 miles round trip, 3 to 5 hours", elevation "1,300 feet", rated "Strenuous".

jewels.name: Pinnacles Campground
jewels.blurb: East side, open year-round: "family and group tent sites, as well as RV sites with electric hookups" (120v/30-amp); "Each tent and group site is equipped with a picnic table and fire ring"; "Coin-operated showers, a dump station"; "The pool is typically open from mid-April through the end of September". The concessioner counts "134 campsites". "Generators are not allowed at any time in any site"; "First come, first served sites are NOT available at this location".

jewels.name: Pinnacles Campground tent cabins
jewels.blurb: "canvas-sided tent cabins that provide a rustic lodging experience", sleeping up to four, "open year-round"; the only roofed stay in the park - "There is no lodging available within Pinnacles National Park". Tent cabin check-in 3pm, checkout 11am (Recreation.gov).

jewels.name: Prewett Point Trail
jewels.blurb: "0.9 miles round trip, 1/2 to 1 hour", elevation "70 feet", rated "Easy" (nps.gov/pinn trails page); "This newly constructed accessible trail is less than a mile long and offers panoramic views."

jewels.name: Bench Trail accessible section
jewels.blurb: "A recently hardened and graded section of the Bench Trail is now accessible for visitors using wheelchairs."

jewels.name: Rock climbing on volcanic breccia
jewels.booking_route: none needed - self-guided; no permit is mentioned on the climbing FAQ
jewels.blurb: "The rock formations here are composed of volcanic breccia, which can be loose in places, increasing the potential for rockfall." Topropes "are perfect for beginners"; multi-pitch climbs on Machete Ridge for the experienced; "During the nesting season from January through July, certain climbing areas may be temporarily closed". The NPS names no commercial guide and points climbers to Friends of Pinnacles.

jewels.name: Chalone Peak Trail
jewels.blurb: "9 miles round trip, 3 to 5 hours", elevation "2,040 feet", rated "Strenuous".

jewels.name: Juniper Canyon Loop
jewels.blurb: "4.3 miles round trip, 2 to 3 hours", elevation "1,215 feet", rated "Strenuous".

jewels.name: Junior Ranger Program and ranger nature walks
jewels.blurb: "The Junior Ranger Program at Pinnacles National Park is a fun and educational way for kids to explore and learn about the park's unique ecosystems, wildlife, and geological features." "Join a park ranger for a fun nature walk!" "Older kids and school groups can participate in service learning projects throughout the year."

jewels.name: Group campsites at Pinnacles Campground
jewels.blurb: "Group sites: 20 people, five vehicles max" (concessioner); "Group sites can be reserved up to 12 months in advance" (NPS). Non-commercial groups of 16+ passengers pay "$15.00" per person entrance, children 15 and under exempt.

jewels.name: Birding the 181 documented species
jewels.blurb: "181 documented species"; the spires host "Turkey Vultures, Peregrine Falcons, and Prairie Falcons" plus migrants like "Blue-Gray Gnatcatchers and various warbler species"; "The rocky spires and monoliths provide ideal vantage points for bird watching."

jewels.name: Pinnacles Campground Store
jewels.blurb: Run by Pinnacles Recreation Company, "a small, family-owned business" and the park's concessioner: "A general store with basic foods and camping supplies is located on-site" (Recreation.gov); open "9:30am-5pm daily". "There are no restaurants or grocery stores within Pinnacles National Park."

jewels.name: East side weekend shuttle
jewels.booking_route: none stated - boards at the campground
jewels.blurb: Runs "seasonally in late winter and spring from 8 am to 5:30 pm Friday through Sunday" from the campground; it had concluded for the season on the day read. Pets are not allowed on shuttle buses.

jewels.name: Mission Nuestra Señora de la Soledad
jewels.booking_route: none needed - walk-in during open hours
jewels.blurb: "Founded in 1791 by Father Fermin Lasuen", "the thirteenth mission to be founded in California"; 36641 Fort Romie Road, Soledad; open "10AM-4PM Tuesday-Sunday. Closed on Mondays"; self-guided tours through the volunteer-staffed shop.

jewels.name: Paicines Ranch
jewels.blurb: "Nestled in the heart of San Benito County": a working ranch of about 7,000 acres of rangeland, 550 acres of row crops and 25 acres of vineyard, all certified organic; rooms and cottages to book, birding under dark skies, "Weddings, Retreats & Gatherings". 831-628-0288.

jewels.name: Calera Wine Company
jewels.blurb: 11300 Cienega Road, Hollister: Robert Parker Wine Advocate calls it "one of the most compelling Pinot Noir specialists of not only the New World, but of Planet Earth"; founder Josh Jensen planted on remote limestone slopes atop Mount Harlan. Tastings booked through its tours and tastings page; (831) 637-9170.

jewels.name: Eden Rift Vineyards
jewels.blurb: 10034 Cienega Road, Hollister: tastings "Thursday-Sunday from 12pm to 5pm" on the Dickinson House lawn, ATV vineyard tours, and helicopter tours through Specialized Aviation; (831) 636-1991.

jewels.name: DeRose Winery
jewels.blurb: 9970 Cienega Road, Hollister: "a land rich in winemaking history" with dry-farmed vineyards; tasting "Monday-Friday, 11:00 am - 5:00 pm Saturday and Sunday, 11:00 am - 4:00 pm"; 831-636-9143.

jewels.name: Léal Vineyards
jewels.blurb: 300 Maranatha Drive, Hollister: in operation "since 1998", calls itself "one of the most sought-after wineries in California" and runs all-inclusive event services; 1.831.636.1023.

jewels.name: Jardines de San Juan
jewels.blurb: 115 3rd St, San Juan Bautista: established in 1977 by Alicia and Manuel Santana and still family-owned; open 7 days, Sunday-Thursday 11 am - 8 pm, Friday and Saturday 11 am - 9 pm; (831) 623-4466.

jewels.name: Food & Wine at The Overlook, Paicines Ranch
jewels.blurb: Farm-to-table dinners "featuring ingredients from local farmers and the ranch's own livestock"; Thursday lunches 11:30 AM-1:30 PM; seasonal dinners and concerts on the ranch calendar.

jewels.name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Hollister
jewels.blurb: Listed by American Southwest at "390 Gateway Drive, Hollister, CA 95023" with "77 guest rooms & suites", "a fitness center, and indoor pool"; "Pinnacles National Park, is 30 miles south." Marriott's own page was not fetched (brand sites return 403 to this agent), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Hollister
jewels.blurb: Listed by American Southwest at "391 Gateway Drive, Hollister, CA 95023": "93 room/suite", "24 hour fitness & business centers, an indoor pool", opened in late 2022. IHG's own page was not fetched (brand sites return 403 to this agent).

jewels.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Hollister
jewels.blurb: Listed by American Southwest at "660 San Felipe Road, Hollister, CA 95023": "42 room, exterior corridor", at the junction of highways 25 and 156.

jewels.name: Pinnacles View - 2 mi from Park
jewels.blurb: Soledad: "Park your fully self-contained camping vehicle beside our organic vineyard, just 2 miles from the Westside entrance of Pinnacles National Park." 4 RV-only sites for self-contained rigs under 30 feet; "No tent or car camping is allowed"; "we do NOT have services on site"; no campfires, no pets.

jewels.name: Song of the Ancients: Dark Sky Camping
jewels.blurb: Paicines, Diablo Range: 4 RV/tent sites on 40 acres, "dark skies, ancient blue oaks, forest bathing"; fire pits with grills, flush toilets, outdoor hot shower, potable water; sites take 12 to 20 people; no hookups and "no stores nearby". Hipcamp lists it 14 miles from the park.

jewels.name: Camp Carmel Valley - Glamping
jewels.blurb: "Located on 115 acres historic boys and girls summer camp complete with pool, tennis, and hiking in Carmel Valley, CA": Sunset and Solstice/Sunrise cabins, safari tents at Rustic Grove Camp and a bunk room; breakfast included with all glamping stays; weekend campfires, yoga and archery. Hipcamp lists it 28 miles from the park.

jewels.name: Hollister Hills State Vehicular Recreation Area
jewels.booking_route: first-come, first-serve at the kiosk; a few sites online
jewels.blurb: 7800 Cienega Road, about 5 miles south of Hollister in the Gabilan Mountains: "Camping $10 per vehicle per night"; Lower Ranch and Upper Ranch campsites "remain first-come, first-serve"; only two remote Hudner Ranch sites and the Lower Ranch ADA sites reserve online. An off-highway-vehicle park.

jewels.name: Pinnacles National Park Foundation
jewels.booking_route: none needed - volunteering and donations via the website
jewels.blurb: A "501(c)(3) non-profit organization dedicated to supporting Pinnacles National Park", funding "high-priority programs and projects unfunded by park budgets" - habitat restoration, wildlife conservation, cultural resources, volunteering. PO Box 2080, Hollister; 831.320.1570.

jewels.name: Water for the trail - one liter per hour
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Water is not available on the trails, so bring enough for your entire trip"; "carry and drink at least one liter of water per person per hour" of hiking.

jewels.name: Flashlight or headlamp for the talus caves
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Bring a Flashlight: Navigating these caves in the dark without proper lighting can be dangerous." The trails page: "pack a flashlight or headlamp. Cave sections can be dark".

jewels.name: Sun protection - hat, sunscreen, light clothing
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Wear light-colored clothing, a hat, and sunscreen to shield yourself from direct sunlight." "Staying hydrated and protecting yourself from the sun is critical."

jewels.name: Sturdy boots with ankle support
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Sturdy shoes or boots with ankle support and good tread are essential."

jewels.name: Binoculars for condor watching
jewels.blurb: NPS birding page: "Binoculars: A pair in the 7-10 power range is ideal."

jewels.name: Climbing helmet for loose breccia
jewels.blurb: NPS climbing FAQ: "wear a helmet, especially on the West Side where loose rocks are common"; use "brown or gray webbing" for anchors and "Chalk balls" instead of loose chalk.

faq.q: Is Pinnacles National Park free?
faq.a: No. The NPS lists a private-vehicle fee of "$30.00", valid 1-7 days for up to 15 passengers; "$15.00" per person on foot or bicycle (under 16 free); motorcycles "$25.00". America the Beautiful passes, including the "$20.00" Senior Annual, are accepted. The park does not accept cash.

faq.q: Can you camp at Pinnacles National Park?
faq.a: Yes, at Pinnacles Campground on the east side, which has "Tent, group, and RV sites" plus tent cabins. "Tent and RV sites can be reserved up to 6 months in advance. Group sites can be reserved up to 12 months in advance", through recreation.gov or (877) 444-6777.

faq.q: Can you drive through Pinnacles National Park?
faq.a: No: "There is no road connecting the East and West entrances of the park." The shortest drive between them goes through King City on Highway 101.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Pinnacles National Park?
faq.a: The NPS: "Spring and fall are typically the most pleasant weather for hiking and visiting the park." In July and August "Daytime temperatures... frequently exceed 100°F (38°C)".

faq.q: Can you bring dogs to Pinnacles National Park?
faq.a: Only to some areas. Pets are allowed in "Picnic areas, Campground, Parking lots, Paved roads" on a six-foot leash, and are not allowed on "All park trails, Shuttle buses, Park buildings."

faq.q: When did Pinnacles become a national park?
faq.a: "On January 10, 2013 President Barack Obama signed legislation passed by Congress that redesignated the monument as a National Park." It had been a national monument since 1908.

faq.q: Where can you see condors in Pinnacles National Park?
faq.a: The NPS points to the High Peaks - "Arrive early to spot California Condors roosting before they take flight" - and says the Balconies Trail may also offer sightings. It recommends binoculars "in the 7-10 power range".

faq.q: Where can you stay in Pinnacles National Park?
faq.a: "There is no lodging available within Pinnacles National Park" apart from the campground, which offers tent sites, RV sites and "canvas-sided tent cabins" sleeping up to four, "open year-round". The NPS points to chambers of commerce in San Benito County, King City, Soledad and the Salinas Valley for town lodging.

faq.q: Which is better, the east or west entrance of Pinnacles National Park?
faq.a: They serve different visits. The east side has the Pinnacles Visitor Center, the campground and "24-hour access to trails"; the west side has the Pinnacles Visitor Contact Station and a day-use gate "open from 7:30 am to 8:00 pm". No road connects the two.

faq.q: What should you wear to Pinnacles National Park?
faq.a: The NPS: "Wear light-colored clothing, a hat, and sunscreen to shield yourself from direct sunlight"; "Sturdy shoes or boots with ankle support and good tread are essential"; and bring a flashlight for the caves.

seo.meta_title: Pinnacles National Park: High Peaks, Talus Caves & Condors | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: Strenuous High Peaks loops, Bear Gulch and Balconies talus caves, California condors since 2003, east-side camping with tent cabins, and where to stay nearby.

name: Point Lobos State Natural Reserve
line: Cypress headlands and kelp-forest coves

jewels.name: Cypress Grove Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond the reserve entry fee ($10.00 per vehicle)
jewels.blurb: Leaves from the Information Station; California State Parks rates it "accessible for 0.25 mile" with excellent views of the cove, with accessible parking in the Cypress Grove area and an accessible restroom at Cypress Grove.

jewels.name: Diving and snorkelling at Whalers and Bluefish Coves
jewels.booking_route: state dive reservation online from the Point Lobos SCUBA Diving page, or (831) 624-8413
jewels.blurb: "Diving is permitted only at Whalers and Bluefish Coves" in the Point Lobos State Marine Reserve: "70 foot-high kelp forests" with "lingcod, rockfish, harbor seals, sea otters, sea stars, and more"; ten teams of two a day; proof of certification and a reservation required; weekend/holiday $30 and weekday $20 per pair plus processing fee; "Snorkeling is NOT permitted at China Cove or Gibson Beach."

jewels.name: Sand Hill Trail (Sea Lion Point)
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond the reserve entry fee
jewels.blurb: A "paved accessible loop trail about 0.4 mile long" leading to views of the cove "and perhaps the occasional otter and/or sea lion", with accessible parking at the Sea Lion Point lot.

jewels.name: Bird Island Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond the reserve entry fee
jewels.blurb: From the Bird Island trailhead, "0.52 miles" on an "aggregate, rock, & wood" surface; the Bird Island picnic area has "four accessible tables including accessible parking and restroom". Gibson Beach, the South Shore Trail and the South Plateau Trail leave from the same trailhead.

jewels.name: Point Lobos docent-guided walks
jewels.booking_route: listed on the docents' public walks page; booking terms not stated
jewels.blurb: Public walks by the reserve's docents, mostly 10:00-10:30am with some at 1:00pm, from the Information Station or Whalers Cabin: the "Cypress Grove Treasures Walk" on "cultural history and the natural wonders", an "Easy-Access Adventure Walk" for "visitors of all abilities" on the Sea Lion Point trail, a General Walk, and "The Women Who Shaped and Saved Point Lobos Walk". No cost or booking terms were stated on the page.

jewels.name: Whalers Cabin Museum
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond the reserve entry fee
jewels.blurb: Open "9:00am to 5:00pm (As staffing permits)" at Whalers Cove; the state describes the reserve as "once the site of countless industrial activities, from whaling operations and gravel quarries to the largest abalone cannery on the West Coast."

jewels.name: Point Lobos Summer Adventures
jewels.booking_route: registration with the Program Director, ashley.wemp@parks.ca.gov, (831) 884-2957
jewels.blurb: "an outdoor day camp for kids and teenagers", based at Point Lobos with visits to other local parks: hiking, nature art, habitat restoration, and "whale watching, kayaking and on other cool field trips". 2026 sessions June 15-26 ($600), July 6-17 ($600), July 20-29 ($450); registration first-come, first-served.

jewels.name: Kayak and stand-up paddleboard launch at Whalers Cove
jewels.booking_route: state reservation from the Point Lobos SCUBA Diving page, or (831) 624-8413
jewels.blurb: "Kayaks and Stand-Up Paddleboards are $10 to launch"; "There is a limit of four Kayak/ SUPs per day", entering only at the Whalers Cove dive ramp; reserved "in the same way as dive reservations"; "CA State Parks does not rent any kayaks, stand up paddleboards, or dive equipment to park visitors."

jewels.name: Carmelo Meadow and Granite Point Trails
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond the reserve entry fee
jewels.blurb: Carmelo Meadow runs "0.25 miles each way" from the entry station and links to the Granite Point Trail, "0.36 miles each way", both compacted soil "generally flat at less than 5% slopes"; the route "winds through native Monterey Pine forest and terminates at Whalers Cove."

jewels.name: Lace Lichen Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond the reserve entry fee
jewels.blurb: "0.75 miles each way" through native forest on compacted soil, rated accessible by California State Parks; one of the three trails the state lists from the reserve entrance, with the Carmelo Meadow and South Shore trails.

jewels.name: Point Lobos trail network
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond the reserve entry fee
jewels.blurb: The state's Point Lobos Hiking Trails page names the Perimeter Trail and the trails from five trailheads: the Reserve Entrance (Carmelo Meadow, South Shore, Lace Lichen), the Information Station (Cypress Grove, North Shore, Sea Lion Point / Sand Hill, South Shore), Bird Island (Bird Island, Gibson Beach, South Shore, South Plateau), Whalers Cove (Granite Point, North Shore, Cabin) and Piney Woods (Pine Ridge, South Shore).

jewels.name: Picnic areas at Whalers Cove, Piney Woods and Bird Island
jewels.booking_route: none needed beyond the reserve entry fee
jewels.blurb: Three picnic areas: Whalers Cove "one accessible table on firm surface", Piney Woods an accessible table on dirt, and Bird Island "four accessible tables including accessible parking and restroom". Reserve rules: "Smoking and fires of all types are prohibited; this includes small cookstoves" and "Alcohol consumption is not allowed anywhere within the reserve."

jewels.name: Group, tour-bus and school-field-trip entry
jewels.booking_route: special event permit via the reserve's Special Events Coordinator, 831-624-3407; school groups via the School Group Coordinator, 831-625-1470
jewels.blurb: "ALL tours and buses MUST have a special event permit to enter the reserve. ALL school groups MUST have a reservation to enter the reserve." Bus (10-24 passengers) $50.00 and Bus (25+ passengers) $100.00, "PERMIT REQUIRED"; vehicles over 21 ft are not allowed, except "school field trip buses with a permit for drop off and pick up of students." Special Events Coordinator (tours, beach weddings, films) 831-624-3407.

jewels.name: Layers for the coastal fog: what the state says to expect
jewels.booking_route: affiliate link to the retailer (AvantLink); bought before the trip
jewels.blurb: Under "Seasons/Climate/Recommended Clothing" the state writes: "Fair sunny days, occasional winter rains, and dry summers, moderated by fog from July through September characterize the central California coastal climate." Rain shell, warm layer and walking shoes for a fog-and-sun day, bought before the trip.

jewels.name: Snorkel and dive kit for Whalers Cove: bring your own
jewels.booking_route: affiliate link to the retailer (AvantLink); bought before the trip - or hired from a Monterey dive shop
jewels.blurb: "CA State Parks does not rent any kayaks, stand up paddleboards, or dive equipment to park visitors. There are a variety of shops that rent gear to the public in Monterey." "All SCUBA divers must have a device capable of maintaining positive buoyancy"; "All snorkelers need a buddy in order to enter the water."

jewels.name: Binoculars for watching marine mammals at a distance
jewels.booking_route: affiliate link to the retailer (AvantLink); bought before the trip
jewels.blurb: The state quotes NOAA Fisheries: "recommended distances of at least 100 YARDS (300 feet) for whales, and 50 YARDS (150 feet) for dolphins, seals, sea lions, and turtles"; and "If you approach seals, otters, whales, or seabirds and notice they are alerting to your presence then you are too close."

jewels.name: 8-Day Yosemite, Sequoia & California Coast Adventure (Southwest Adventure Tours, on TourRadar)
jewels.blurb: A multi-day guided group tour, San Francisco round trip, 8 days, 4-14 participants, ages 8+, from EUR 4,707 per person; Day 6 "Cambria to Monterey" includes a "Scenic drive along Pacific Coast Highway (Highway 1)" and "Visit Point Lobos State Natural Reserve". TourRadar's listing: "Ancient Sequoia groves give way to coastal paths at Point Lobos State Park and along Moonstone Beach in Cambria".

jewels.name: Carmel-by-the-Sea
jewels.blurb: The gateway village three miles north of the reserve: "this one-square mile, fairytale village full of inspired restaurants, wine tasting, boutique shops, art galleries, a white-sand beach, and stunning scenery—all within walking distance from your hotel or inn."

jewels.name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
jewels.blurb: 886 Cannery Row, Monterey; a nonprofit whose mission is "to inspire conservation of the ocean". Adult $65 (ages 18-69), Youth $50 (5-17), Senior $50 (70+), free for ages 4 and under; "Purchase your tickets in advance for a smooth entry process."

jewels.name: Carmel Mission Basilica
jewels.booking_route: visit details on the mission's Plan Your Visit pages (admission terms not read); 831.624.1271
jewels.blurb: 3080 Rio Road, Carmel: "A PLACE OF WORSHIP, EDUCATION, HISTORY, AND ART" with museums and "the extraordinary collection art and religious artifacts"; "Two centuries ago, the Carmel Mission was in ruins." Sunday Masses 9:00 and 11:00 a.m. in the Basilica.

jewels.name: Aquarius Dive Shop, Monterey
jewels.blurb: 2040 Del Monte Ave., Monterey: "Established in 1970, Aquarius Dive Shop is Monterey Bay's premier PADI 5-Star Instructor Development Center", with a heated training pool, "a full service rental department", and guided shore dives - "We offer shore dives every day." Mon-Thu 9am-6pm, Fri-Sun 7am-7pm. The reserve itself rents no dive equipment.

jewels.name: Monterey Bay Kayaks
jewels.blurb: Kayak and stand-up paddleboard rentals, guided tours and classes "in the Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary, exciting harbor and Cannery Row shoreline with sea otters, seals, sealions, kelp beds and more", plus Elkhorn Slough; stores selling "Kayaks - new and used, Gear, Clothing & More"; open daily 9-5, (831) 373-5357.

jewels.name: Carmel by the River RV Resort
jewels.blurb: 27680 Schulte Rd., Carmel: 35 back-in sites, all with water, sewer, 30 or 50 amp electric, WiFi and cable TV; pet-friendly; propane fire-pit rentals; "8.6 miles to Point Lobos State Natural Reserve". No tent camping.

jewels.name: Ventana Campground, Big Sur
jewels.booking_route: hyatt.com booking link from the campground site, or 855-391-8683
jewels.blurb: 48123 Highway 1, Big Sur, "30 miles south of Carmel": a tent-only campground on 40 acres in a redwood canyon with glamping tents ("A More Refined Way to Connect with Nature"), two modern bath houses, picnic table and fire ring per site; "We cannot accommodate RVs"; up to 2 dogs per site on leash; a three-night minimum in the busy summer season. Bookings run through Hyatt.

jewels.name: Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park campground
jewels.blurb: "Big Sur's largest campground", 26 miles south of Carmel: tent, en route, group and hike-and-bike sites; RVs to 32 ft and trailers to 27 ft, with a dump station; Big Sur Lodge has "61 guest rooms". ⚠️ The state lists the park as closed due to the Timber Fire as of September 15, 2026.

jewels.name: Alila Ventana Big Sur
jewels.blurb: 48123 Highway One, Big Sur, an Alila resort in the Hyatt family: "Ventana's 54 rooms and suites are arranged around our 160-acre property in secluded groupings"; stays include dining, non-alcoholic drinks, wellness programming and valet; restaurants The Sur House, The Glass House and SurStream; glamping on the same estate.

jewels.name: Carmel Valley Ranch
jewels.blurb: One Old Ranch Road, Carmel, in The Unbound Collection by Hyatt: "LUXURY CALIFORNIA RESORT ON 500 ACRES" with all-suite accommodation, pools, Spa Aiyana, its own vineyard and "The only Pete Dye-designed bentgrass golf course" (page text truncated there); "Romantics and families alike find action and fun".

jewels.name: La Playa Hotel, Carmel-by-the-Sea
jewels.booking_route: direct booking per the Carmel tourism listing; (831) 293-6100
jewels.blurb: Listed by Carmel's official tourism site among Carmel hotels and inns, (831) 293-6100, "Book Direct", with a listed "$1,149.00 Average Nightly Rate". The hotel's own page was not read.

jewels.name: Hog's Breath Inn
jewels.blurb: 547 San Carlos St., Carmel-by-the-Sea: "Founded in 1970 by Clint Eastwood", USDA Prime steak and sustainable seafood "beside the warmth of our famous fireplaces and heated outdoor patio"; the patio is dog-friendly; lunch daily from 11:00 a.m.

jewels.name: Rio Grill
jewels.blurb: 101 Crossroads Blvd, Carmel, at "The Crossroads at Highway 1 and Rio Road — the gateway to Big Sur": California Fusion since 1983, "Originally opened in 1983 as a coastal sister to Mustard's Grill"; Mon-Thu 11:30 AM-8:00 PM, Fri-Sat to 9:00 PM.

jewels.name: Little Napoli
jewels.blurb: Corner of Dolores St. & 7th St. in the 1928 El Paseo Building, Carmel-by-the-Sea: "Opened in 1990", Chef Pèpe's southern Italian; "Best Italian Restaurant – 2025 Golden Pine Cones"; dinner nightly 4pm-9:00pm; "Reservations are recommended but not required"; cashless; pet-friendly courtyard.

jewels.name: Vesuvio
jewels.blurb: 543 6th Ave, Carmel-by-the-Sea, across from Devendorf Park: "Wood-fired pizza. Two bars, one on the roof. Open nightly at four." "Walk-ins welcome. The rooftop, the full Downstairs Bar and a few dining tables are always held for you."

jewels.name: Cultura Comida y Bebida
jewels.blurb: Dolores Street between 5th & 6th Avenue, in the Su Vecino Courtyard, Carmel-by-the-Sea: "Celebrating The Culture of Oaxaca, Mexico"; menu "all made from scratch" from fresh local ingredients; a mezcal library; (831) 250-7005.

jewels.name: Carmel Belle
jewels.booking_route: walk-in; online ordering on own website
jewels.blurb: Dowd Building #110, Ocean Avenue & San Carlos, Carmel-by-the-Sea: breakfast, lunch and dinner from "the freshest local ingredients from Monterey County"; open daily 8:00am-5:30pm; 831-624-1600.

faq.q: Do you need tickets for Point Lobos State Natural Reserve?
faq.a: There is no timed ticket for a car; entry is paid per vehicle: "Vehicle $10.00 Senior $9.00 Disabled (with Discount Pass) $5.00". Buses pay $50.00 or $100.00 with a permit, and "ALL tours and buses MUST have a special event permit to enter the reserve. ALL school groups MUST have a reservation to enter the reserve." Divers and snorkellers need a separate reservation.

faq.q: Is Point Lobos State Natural Reserve free?
faq.a: No. California State Parks lists "Vehicle Day Use: $10.00", with a $9.00 senior rate and $5.00 with the Disabled Discount Pass, and notes that "Special rates may apply for peak season, high demand holiday periods, and during weekends." The reserve accepts state passes including the California Explorer and Golden Poppy annual passes.

faq.q: What are the hours at Point Lobos State Natural Reserve?
faq.a: "RESERVE HOURS 8 am - 7 pm No Vehicles or Pedestrians may enter the Reserve after 6:30 pm." The Information Station and the Whalers Cabin Museum open "9:00am to 5:00pm (As staffing permits)".

faq.q: Can you camp at Point Lobos State Natural Reserve?
faq.a: No. "No Camping. The reserve is strictly a Day Use facility and all visitors must exit by closing time." Smoking and fires "of all types are prohibited; this includes small cookstoves."

faq.q: Does Point Lobos State Natural Reserve allow dogs?
faq.a: No. "Dogs are not allowed anywhere within the reserve and cannot be left inside parked vehicles."

faq.q: Can you swim at Point Lobos State Natural Reserve?
faq.a: The state's page covers diving and snorkelling, not swimming: "The diving area is limited to Whalers and Bluefish Coves. All other areas of the Reserve are closed to diving and aquatic activity. Snorkeling is NOT permitted at China Cove or Gibson Beach." Diving and snorkelling need a reservation, and "All snorkelers need a buddy in order to enter the water."

faq.q: Where is Point Lobos State Natural Reserve?
faq.a: "The reserve is located on the central coast of California in Monterey County. The entrance is located three miles south of Carmel on Highway 1." Mailing address: Route 1 Box 62, Carmel, CA 93923.

faq.q: What are the trails at Point Lobos State Natural Reserve?
faq.a: California State Parks groups them by trailhead: from the Reserve Entrance, Carmelo Meadow, South Shore and Lace Lichen; from the Information Station, Cypress Grove, North Shore, Sea Lion Point / Sand Hill and South Shore; from Bird Island, Bird Island, Gibson Beach, South Shore and South Plateau; from Whalers Cove, Granite Point, North Shore and Cabin; from Piney Woods, Pine Ridge and South Shore; plus the Perimeter Trail.

faq.q: Is Point Lobos State Natural Reserve good with kids?
faq.a: The reserve runs Point Lobos Summer Adventures, "an outdoor day camp for kids and teenagers" with hiking, nature art, habitat restoration and "whale watching, kayaking and on other cool field trips"; 2026 sessions were June 15-26 and July 6-17 at $600 and July 20-29 at $450, registration first-come, first-served.

faq.q: Where do you park at Point Lobos State Natural Reserve?
faq.a: Inside the reserve, at a $10.00 vehicle fee; "any vehicle (commercial, motorhome, live-in van, etc.) over 21 ft long is not allowed to drive or park within Point Lobos State Natural Reserve." Accessible parking is at the entrance, the Sea Lion Point lot, the Cypress Grove area and each trailhead (California State Parks accessible features page).

seo.meta_title: Point Lobos State Natural Reserve, CA: Trails, Diving & Carmel | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: Day-use reserve 3 miles south of Carmel: cypress trails, sea lions, kelp-forest diving at Whalers Cove by reservation, $10 per car, no dogs, no camping.

name: Redwood National Park
line: The tallest trees on earth, a free-entry national park run with three California state parks, Roosevelt elk on the meadows and a ring of lagoon kayaking, oyster boats and bluff-top inns from Crescent City to Eureka

jewels.name: Tall Trees Grove
jewels.booking_route: free NPS Tall Trees Trailhead permit, online only (nps.gov/redw/planyourvisit/permits.htm)
jewels.blurb: a 4.5-mile round-trip trail, rated moderate-strenuous with an 800-foot elevation gain, off Bald Hills Road; "Plan 4 hours including 2 hiking hours"; a free Tall Trees Trailhead permit is "required year-round" and can be made up to 24 hours in advance; vehicles must be 21 feet or less and trailers are not allowed

jewels.name: Fern Canyon Loop
jewels.booking_route: free Gold Bluffs Beach day-use permit May 15 to September 15 (nps.gov/redw/planyourvisit/permits.htm); state park vehicle day-use fee applies
jewels.blurb: a 0.7-mile loop off Davison Road, "slippery, wet year-round", with "30-foot fern-covered walls"; "Some of the exquisite ferns...are ancient species whose ancestry can be traced back 325 million years"; seasonal bridges summer only; free Gold Bluffs Beach day-use permits "are required May 15th to September 15th"

jewels.name: Lady Bird Johnson Grove
jewels.blurb: a 1-mile loop, easy and level, off Bald Hills Road about 2 miles from Highway 101, through old-growth redwood forest with rhododendrons and azaleas in spring; "No parking for RVs and trailers"

jewels.name: Trillium Falls Trail
jewels.blurb: a 2.5-mile loop, moderate with some steep grades, from the Elk Meadow Day Use Area on Davison Road 3 miles north of Orick; "The trail leads you through the misty hallways of an ancient redwood home" to a 10-foot cascade

jewels.name: James Irvine Trail
jewels.blurb: "The quintessential redwood trail", 4.2 miles, moderate, from the Prairie Creek Visitor Center through to Fern Canyon; the NPS says to plan "4-5 hours traveling through the enormous old-growth trees"

jewels.name: Elk Prairie Trail
jewels.blurb: a 2.8-mile moderate trail from Elk Prairie Campground that will "Meander through one of the most heavily populated Roosevelt elk areas in the parks"

jewels.name: Stout Memorial Grove
jewels.blurb: a 0.5-mile loop at the east end of Howland Hill Road in Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park, a "Majestic example of an ancient coast redwood forest" on the Smith River floodplain; "After the initial descent from the parking lot, the trail is easy and flat"; summer access also from Jedediah Smith Campground; no motor homes or trailers on Howland Hill Road

jewels.name: Grove of Titans
jewels.blurb: a 1.7-mile out-and-back from the east end of Howland Hill Road, 1 to 1.5 hours with 137 feet of elevation, through old-growth redwoods; NPS Visitor Guide 2026: "Limited parking, no motor homes or trailers on Howland Hill Road"

jewels.name: Boy Scout Tree Trail
jewels.blurb: 5.5 miles out and back from the west end of Howland Hill Road, 3-4 hours with 900 feet of elevation, to Fern Falls and the Boy Scout Tree; "Moderate, some steep grades and switchbacks"; the NPS warns of "Many vehicle break-ins at this trailhead"

jewels.name: Simpson-Reed Trail
jewels.blurb: a 1-mile loop off Walker Road from US 199 in Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park, "Easy, level (Rated: barrier free)" through old-growth redwoods with waysides; the 2026 Visitor Guide gives 0.8 mile and 50 feet of elevation; no motor homes or trailers on Walker Road

jewels.name: Damnation Creek Trail
jewels.blurb: 2.2 miles one-way from milepost 16.0 on Highway 101 in Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park down to the ocean; "Strenuous, numerous steep grades and switchbacks. Trail drops 1,000 feet (16 percent grade)"; NPS: "Many vehicle break-ins at this trailhead"

jewels.name: Yurok Loop Trail and Lagoon Creek
jewels.blurb: a 1-mile loop (1.25 miles in the 2026 Visitor Guide) from the Lagoon Creek picnic area on US 101, beach flowers and Lagoon Creek; the guide adds: "From the loop, head south on the Coastal Trail 4 mi to reach the Klamath River Overlook"

jewels.name: Big Tree Wayside and Circle Trail
jewels.blurb: a 0.5-mile loop, 15 to 40 minutes with 22 feet of elevation, off the Newton B. Drury Parkway to the Big Tree; "Connect with either the Cathedral Trees Trail or the Foothill Trail for a longer hike"

jewels.name: Revelation Trail, Prairie Creek Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: a 0.3-mile loop, 15 to 45 minutes with 9 feet of elevation, through old-growth redwoods, "Developed specifically for the visually impaired"; the visitor centre sits 6 miles north of Orick on the Newton B. Drury Scenic Parkway

jewels.name: Howland Hill Road
jewels.blurb: a scenic drive of 10 miles one-way, about 45 minutes, that will "Follow a winding dirt road through old-growth redwoods in Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park"; mostly unpaved, two-way and narrow; motor homes, RVs and trailers not advised; it reaches Stout Grove, Grove of Titans and Boy Scout Tree

jewels.name: Newton B. Drury Scenic Parkway
jewels.blurb: "A not-to-be-missed alternative to US 101" that "passes through the heart of the old-growth redwood forest in Prairie Creek Redwoods State Park": paved, two-way, 10 miles one-way, about 30 minutes, no commercial vehicles; home to the Prairie Creek Visitor Center and Big Tree Wayside

jewels.name: Coastal Drive Loop and High Bluff Overlook
jewels.blurb: a 9-mile loop, about 45 minutes, mostly paved with a one-way northbound section; "This narrow road with steep grade and sharp curves offers panoramic views of the Pacific Ocean and Klamath River Estuary", passing High Bluff Overlook and a World War II radar station; motor homes, RVs and trailers prohibited

jewels.name: Klamath River Overlook
jewels.blurb: an overlook at the end of Requa Road above the mouth of the Klamath River, reached also by the Coastal Trail 4 miles south of the Yurok Loop; the Visitor Guide notes "Requa Road motor homes and trailers not advised" and that lands within one mile of each side of the Klamath River for 43 miles upstream compose the Yurok Reservation

jewels.name: Jedediah Smith Campground
jewels.booking_route: ReserveCalifornia.com or 1-800-444-7275, at least 48 hours and up to 6 months ahead
jewels.blurb: a year-round state park campground on US 199, 9 miles northeast of Crescent City, beside the Hiouchi Visitor Center and a summer-only campground store; RVs to 25 feet, trailers to 21 feet; one of two campgrounds with four ADA-accessible cabins that sleep six with "electricity; heaters and lights" but no kitchen or bathroom; $35 a night for developed sites

jewels.name: Mill Creek Campground
jewels.booking_route: ReserveCalifornia.com or 1-800-444-7275, at least 48 hours and up to 6 months ahead
jewels.blurb: the spring-to-fall campground in Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park, RVs to 28 feet and trailers to 24 feet, $35 a night for developed sites

jewels.name: Elk Prairie Campground
jewels.booking_route: ReserveCalifornia.com or 1-800-444-7275, at least 48 hours and up to 6 months ahead
jewels.blurb: a year-round campground in Prairie Creek Redwoods State Park, RVs to 27 feet and trailers to 24 feet, with four ADA-accessible bunk cabins and park wifi at the campground kiosk; the Elk Prairie Trail starts here through "one of the most heavily populated Roosevelt elk areas in the parks"

jewels.name: Gold Bluffs Beach Campground
jewels.booking_route: ReserveCalifornia.com or 1-800-444-7275; summer day-use reservation also required for Gold Bluffs Beach
jewels.blurb: a year-round beachfront campground off Davison Road in Prairie Creek Redwoods State Park, RVs to 24 feet and trailers prohibited, with a hiker/biker-only backcountry site inside it ("$5 per person, per night"); Roosevelt elk are frequently seen at Gold Bluffs Beach; NPS: "Sneaker waves are difficult to spot, and within 30-seconds they will run hundreds of feet up the beach slope"

jewels.name: Redwood Creek Trail and the backcountry camps
jewels.booking_route: free backcountry permit online, at least 48 hours ahead; "No phone reservations are made for backcountry permits" (nps.gov/redw/planyourvisit/permits.htm)
jewels.blurb: 8 miles to Tall Trees Grove, moderate to strenuous, from off Bald Hills Road; "Redwood Creek runs high and fast during the winter. Foot bridges across the creek have been removed until the summer season"; designated backcountry camps include DeMartin (10 sites), Flint Ridge (8), Little Bald Hills (5), 44 Camp (4), Elam Camp (3) and dispersed Redwood Creek gravel bars; free online permits only

jewels.name: Enderts Beach and Crescent Beach Overlook
jewels.blurb: the Last Chance section of the Coastal Trail, 0.6 mile one-way and "Moderate, some steep grades", from the end of Enderts Beach Road south of Crescent City; the Visitor Guide lists Roosevelt elk on Enderts Beach Road and warns "powerful 'sneaker' waves can occur at any time"

jewels.name: Roosevelt elk viewing
jewels.blurb: elk "are frequently seen by adoring visitors near Elk Prairie, Elk Meadow, Gold Bluffs Beach, Bald Hills Road, and Enderts Beach Road"; the NPS: "elk can be agressive, especially the males during the fall elk rut and the females during spring calving season. Stay back at least 75 ft (25 m)"

jewels.name: Visitor centres, Junior Ranger and ranger programmes
jewels.blurb: five visitor and information centres - Crescent City Bookstore (1111 Second Street), Hiouchi, Prairie Creek, Kuchel (2 miles south of Orick on US 101) and Chah-pekw O' Ket'-toh "Stone Lagoon" - with maps, Junior Ranger books, passport stamps, and a Bark Ranger programme for pets; ranger programme calendar by QR code or at a visitor centre; park stores run by the Redwood Parks Conservancy

jewels.name: Trees of Mystery, Klamath
jewels.booking_route: phone/email (1-800-638-3389, tofm@treesofmystery.net); no online engine seen on the homepage
jewels.blurb: a roadside attraction at 15500 US-101, Klamath, operating since 1946: the SkyTrail, where you "Glide through the forest in enclosed gondolas", the Redwood Canopy Trail, old-growth trails, the Paul Bunyan and Babe statues, and the End of the Trail Museum, "One of the largest private collections of artifacts"; Blue Ox Cafe and Motel Trees on site

jewels.name: Historic Requa Inn, Klamath River mouth
jewels.blurb: "Built in 1914, the plain, almost utilitarian arts and crafts Inn" where "the river meets the ocean" at Requa; every room different, many with river views, some with claw-foot tubs; seasonal breakfast; the inn states the four redwood parks "are all within a 40-minute radius of the Inn"

jewels.name: Kayak Trinidad
jewels.booking_route: phone/email ((707) 329-0085, reservations@kayaktrinidad.com); no engine seen on the homepage
jewels.blurb: "Coastal Northern California's Premiere Paddlesports Outfitters", over 25 years, at Scenic Drive and Main Street in Trinidad, running a Trinidad Bay "Whales & Wildlife" kayak tour, a Big Lagoon Wildlife Tour and Sunday Social Paddles, "for all levels of paddler"

jewels.name: Elk Meadow Cabins, Orick
jewels.booking_route: own site elkmeadowcabins.com or (707) 302-8393 (homepage did not load this session)
jewels.blurb: vacation rental cabins on a 27-acre meadow at 7 Valley Green Camp Rd, about 2 miles north of Orick off Highway 101, where Roosevelt elk graze on the property; each with a "fully stocked kitchen with cooking & eating utensils", dishwasher, laundry and satellite TV; weddings take a minimum of 6 cabins for 2+ nights

jewels.name: SeaQuake Brewing, Crescent City
jewels.blurb: a brewery and restaurant at 400 Front St, Crescent City, pouring year-round and seasonal craft beers and kombucha alongside "brick oven pizzas, local grass-fed burgers, locally caught fish dishes, our famous cheese curds"

jewels.name: Mystic Forest Campground, Klamath
jewels.blurb: a small family-run campground on 50 acres of forest "sprinkled with redwood trees" between Klamath and Crescent City, with 15 tent-only sites among 23 on Hipcamp, plus "restrooms, showers, a game room, a mini golf course, horseshoes, and a half-mile trail"; 98% recommended across 875 reviews

jewels.name: The Fairy Forest, Trinidad
jewels.blurb: a single 12x14 ft canvas glamping tent for up to four on 4 acres of old-growth and roughly 120-year-old redwoods a mile from Trinidad, with a queen bed, heating, an outdoor heated shower, fire pit and greenhouse seating; no potable water; camped on since the 1950s; 95% recommended across 278 reviews

jewels.name: Ravens Roost, Crescent City
jewels.blurb: a bell-tent glamping site for up to three with a "Vintage horse trailer that has been converted into a charming bathhouse", fire pit, hammock and swinging sofa, heater, mini fridge, Keurig and WiFi; Star Host, 100% recommended (13 reviews)

jewels.name: Redwood Cathedral Treehouse (Redwood Retreat), Crescent City
jewels.blurb: a two-story treehouse platform 22 feet above the forest floor inside a "cathedral tree", with an 8-foot geodesic dome, composting toilet and a dumbwaiter for gear; bring your own water, flashlights and bedding; 97% recommended across 318 reviews

jewels.name: Redwood Creek Buckarettes horseback rides, Orick
jewels.blurb: guided rides into Redwood National Park from the Orick Rodeo Grounds, daily May through November: the 1.5-hour Goose Pen Ride ("get your picture taken on your horse inside one of these giant wonders"), the 2-hour Majestic Ride to "a majestic grove of untouched old growth redwoods", and a 4-hour Picnic Ride with lunch

jewels.name: Turtle Rocks Oceanfront Inn, Trinidad
jewels.booking_route: own site turtlerocksinn.com or (707) 677-3707 (engine not checked)
jewels.blurb: an inn on three oceanfront acres in a wind-protected cove south of Sue-Meg State Park, rooms averaging 500 square feet, each with a "private glass-paneled deck overlooking the Pacific Ocean" and the offshore Turtle Rocks sea stacks; daily gourmet breakfast buffet 8:30-10:00

jewels.name: Lost Whale Bed & Breakfast Inn, Trinidad
jewels.booking_route: own site lostwhaleinn.com or (707) 677-3425 (engine not checked)
jewels.blurb: a bluff-top inn above Abalone Cove that Sunset Magazine called "one of the ten most romantic inns in the country", with a private trail to two miles of secluded beaches, tidepools, sea otters and a sea lion colony, a 24-hour ocean-view hot tub, in-room spa services, and breakfasts and afternoon wine receptions using the inn's own produce; children welcome; two-night minimum June 15 to September 15

jewels.name: Sunset Restaurant, Trinidad
jewels.blurb: a restaurant at Cher-Ae Heights Casino, 27 Scenic Drive, perched above Trinidad Bay with "brilliant views of the Pacific shoreline"; seafood-led with whole steamed ruby red trout, spicy prawn and sausage penne and smokehouse ribs, and a bar for craft cocktails and house-infused spirits

jewels.name: Samoa Cookhouse, Samoa (Eureka)
jewels.blurb: "the last surviving cookhouse of the West", serving lumber-camp meals "since 1890": "Your food is brought to the table in large bowls and platters, allowing you to help yourself and pass it around", with a complimentary museum of logging relics and private rooms for groups up to 160; 5 minutes from Eureka over the Samoa Bridge. STATUS TO CONFIRM: the Visit Redwoods listing carries a note "Temporarily closed for renovations as of August 2023", while a search result from samoacookhouse.net showed Wednesday-Sunday hours

jewels.name: Humboldt Bay Oyster Tours and Humboldt Bay Provisions, Eureka
jewels.blurb: a "4 Hour Boat Tour and Tasting" for up to six, departing 11 AM from Humboldt Bay Provisions at 205 G St in Old Town Eureka, touring the bay's oyster aquaculture by motorboat, with "12 oysters prepared for them at Humboldt Bay Provisions" per guest; the tasting room and oyster bar was "established in 2012"

jewels.name: Chart Room Restaurant, Crescent City Harbor
jewels.blurb: named by the Crescent City Harbor District as "a beloved waterfront seafood spot known for its hearty clam chowder", at 130 Anchor Way on the harbor, where the district lists sea lion and seal viewing, sport fishing and whale watching

jewels.name: Schmidt's House of Jambalaya, Crescent City Harbor
jewels.blurb: a "New Orleans-style bistro that offers a delightful mix of Cajun and Creole classics" at 110 Anchor Way on Crescent City Harbor (Harbor District listing)

jewels.name: Redwood Harbor Village RV and Bayside RV, Crescent City Harbor
jewels.blurb: the two RV parks the Crescent City Harbor District lists at the harbor, beside the California Coastal Trail for walking and biking and the harbor's free Wi-Fi

faq.q: Does Redwood National Park charge an entrance fee?
faq.a: No. The NPS states the park is free to visit and has no entrance stations. California State Parks charge day-use fees, cash only, at Jedediah Smith Day-Use Area, Gold Bluffs Beach/Fern Canyon and Elk Prairie Picnic Area; federal and California State Park pass holders do not pay them.

faq.q: Do I need a permit for Fern Canyon?
faq.a: From May 15 to September 15, yes. The NPS requires a free Gold Bluffs Beach day-use permit, which also covers Fern Canyon trailhead parking, booked online only.

faq.q: How do I visit Tall Trees Grove?
faq.a: With a free Tall Trees Trailhead permit, required year-round and booked online. The trail is 4.5 miles round trip with an 800-foot elevation gain, off Bald Hills Road; the NPS says to plan 4 hours.

faq.q: Where can I see Roosevelt elk?
faq.a: The NPS names Elk Prairie, Elk Meadow, Gold Bluffs Beach, Bald Hills Road and Enderts Beach Road, and asks visitors to stay back at least 75 feet, more in the fall rut and spring calving season.

faq.q: Are there cabins in the park?
faq.a: Yes, eight ADA-accessible cabins, four at Elk Prairie and four at Jedediah Smith campgrounds. Each sleeps six with electricity, heat and lights but no kitchen or bathroom; bring your own bedding. Book on ReserveCalifornia.

faq.q: What is the weather like?
faq.a: The NPS gives coastal temperatures of mid-40s to low-60s F year-round, with most of the 60-80 inches of annual rain falling October to April and summer fog along the coast.

seo.meta_title: Redwood National Park: Tall Trees, Fern Canyon, Elk & Where to Stay | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: Tall Trees and Fern Canyon permits, Roosevelt elk, free entry, park campgrounds and cabins, and where to stay and eat from Crescent City to Trinidad and Eureka.
