name: Lassen Volcanic National Park
line: Boiling mud, Lassen Peak and Cinder Cone

jewels.name: Bumpass Hell Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park trail, covered by the entrance fee
jewels.blurb: "Bumpass Hell Trail provides access to the largest hydrothermal area in the park." 3 miles round trip, about 2 hours; "the trail drops 300 feet into the basin where a boardwalk provides an up-close view of the hydrothermal features." Season "Approximately late July through October". "Stay on established trails and boardwalks in/around the basin."

jewels.name: Lassen Peak Trail
jewels.blurb: "Round-Trip Distance: 5 miles (8 km)", start 8,500 ft, gain 1,957 ft, 4-5 hours, summer and fall; the route "climbs through twisted mountain hemlock and whitebark pine trees on sand-like cinders" then "steepens into series of switchbacks along a rocky ridge to the summit."

jewels.name: Sulphur Works
jewels.booking_route: none needed - roadside stop on the park highway
jewels.blurb: "Sulphur Works is the easiest of the park's hydrothermal areas to access. This hydrothermal area is an otherworldly place of vibrant colors, pungent scents, and shifting ground." "The sidewalk to Sulphur Works is paved and accessible to wheelchairs." Reached by vehicle in summer and fall only.

jewels.name: Cinder Cone Trail
jewels.blurb: "Hike to the base or summit of the dramatic Cinder Cone volcano via this popular trail in the Butte Lake Area": 2.4 miles to the base, 4 miles round trip to the summit, 846 ft of gain from 6,061 to 6,907 ft, past "the Fantastic Lava Beds and the colorful Painted Dunes"; open "Approximately June through November".

jewels.name: Lassen Park Highway scenic drive
jewels.booking_route: none needed - private vehicle entrance fee at the gate
jewels.blurb: "Take the one-hour drive along the 30-mile park highway." The NPS notes many sights "can be seen from the main park road (Highway 89)." Closed to through traffic by snow approximately November through April.

jewels.name: Manzanita Lake Loop
jewels.blurb: "Enjoy scenic views and wildlife watching on this 1.7-mile loop." Manzanita Lake Campground beside it is "within walking distance of the scenic Manzanita Lake, a popular fishing and family destination" with "impressive views of Lassen Peak".

jewels.name: Junior Ranger programme
jewels.booking_route: none needed - booklet at the visitor centers
jewels.blurb: "The activities in the Junior Ranger booklet are best-suited to kids age 5 to 12." "Kids pick up a Junior Ranger Activity Booklet at the Loomis Museum (summer only) or Kohm Yah-mah-nee Visitor Center" and "receive a Lassen Volcanic National Park Junior Ranger badge" once a ranger reviews it.

jewels.name: Kohm Yah-mah-nee Visitor Center
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free with park entry
jewels.blurb: "Open 7 days/week", "9:30 am - 4:30 pm", year-round; "The visitor center is fully accessible with tactile exhibits including a relief map of the park".

jewels.name: Loomis Museum
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free with park entry
jewels.blurb: "2026 season - May 21 - November 2 Thursdays - Mondays (closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays)", "9:30 am - 4:30 pm"; one of the two places to pick up the Junior Ranger booklet in summer.

jewels.name: Devastated Area Interpretive Trail
jewels.blurb: "Discover the history of the Devastated Area on this short walk with trailside signs." "Accessible parking spaces and vault toilets are available at the trailhead."

jewels.name: Lily Pond Trail
jewels.blurb: "This half-mile, self-led interpretive walk explores the rich diversity of plant and animal life in this unique volcanic landscape."

jewels.name: Juniper Lake
jewels.blurb: The NPS calls it the "largest lake in the park" with "crystal clear snow-fed waters"; its 18-site campground is listed as closed for maintenance.

jewels.name: Fishing in Lassen's lakes and streams
jewels.booking_route: none needed in the park (licence rules not read in this build)
jewels.blurb: "Numerous lakes and streams provide plentiful opportunities for fishing."

jewels.name: Winter snowshoeing and skiing
jewels.booking_route: none needed - winter entrance fee only; backcountry camping needs a wilderness permit
jewels.blurb: When Highway 89 closes "when snow settles in", the park offers "snowshoeing and cross-country skiing and areas for sledding and snowplay" and, for the experienced, "backcountry ski and snowboard". "Self-contained vehicle camping is allowed" at the Southwest Parking Area.

jewels.name: Ranger-led programmes
jewels.booking_route: none needed - programme calendar on nps.gov (not read)
jewels.blurb: "Learn about Lassen with a ranger. A variety of programs are typically offered late-May through September." Summer adds "field seminars".

jewels.name: Manzanita Lake Campground
jewels.blurb: "Manzanita Lake Campground (elevation 5,900 ft.) is the largest campground in Lassen Volcanic National Park" - 179 sites, $26 full service / $15 dry camping; every site has "one bear-resistant storage locker". Stay limit "14 nights". Reservations via recreation.gov or (877) 444-6777.

jewels.name: Manzanita Lake Group Campground
jewels.blurb: "located at the west end of Loop B in Manzanita Lake Campground, the largest campground in Lassen Volcanic National Park"; "Campsite capacity is 15 persons per site and a maximum of 4 vehicles."

jewels.name: Summit Lake, Butte Lake and Warner Valley campgrounds
jewels.blurb: Summit Lake North 46 sites ($24), Summit Lake South 48 sites ($22 / $15 dry), Butte Lake 101 sites ($22 / $15 dry), Warner Valley 17 sites ($21), Southwest Walk-In 21 sites ($16). "Reservations are required for all campgrounds except Juniper Lake and Southwest Walk-in."

jewels.name: Manzanita Lake Camping Cabins
jewels.blurb: "Situated near the northwest entrance to the park, the rustic Manzanita Lake Camping Cabins" come as "a one-room cabin that sleeps three", "a two-room cabin that sleeps six" and "a one-room bunkhouse that sleeps up to eight people"; no electricity, running water or linens; open mid-May through mid-October.

jewels.name: Drakesbad Guest Ranch
jewels.blurb: "a secluded getaway lodge at the southeast end of Lassen Volcanic National Park, featuring 19 traditional lodge and bungalow units"; season "June 12th - October 12th"; two-night minimum; "All meals are included"; guests go "hiking, horseback riding, swimming, fishing" with rides to Terminal Geyser, Devils Kitchen and Boiling Springs Lake. Operated by Snow Mountain LLC, an NPS-authorized concessioner.

jewels.name: Backcountry camping by wilderness permit
jewels.blurb: "Wilderness permits for backcountry camping must be obtained prior to your visit to the park" through Recreation.gov; "Permits can be reserved a maximum of 90 days prior to the start date"; "$6 per permit non-refundable Recreation.gov administration fee" plus "$5 per-trip, per-person fee (16 years and older)".

jewels.name: Bear canister for the backcountry
jewels.blurb: NPS: "All food, trash, toiletries, and other scented items" must be stored in approved bear-resistant containers; "Hanging food is not permitted." Canisters are mandatory "from April 16 - November 30" and go "100 feet (or 70 big steps) from both your tent and cooking area."

jewels.name: Water, sun cover and layers for Lassen Peak
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Carry plenty of water, take breaks often" and "Carry extra layers for warmth"; "Sun Exposure is considerable on Lassen Peak Trail. Tree shade may be found in the first mile after which limited shade is available." For winter: "layers, waterproof gear and outerwear, and sun protection".

jewels.name: Footwear and trekking poles for Bumpass Hell
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Hikers are encouraged to wear or bring a hat and carry water" and wear "proper footwear (good tread, ankle support, closed toe)", "using trekking poles to help maintain balance"; on Lassen Peak, "Wear proper footwear and consider using trekking poles" for snow.

jewels.name: Wildland Trekking - Best of Lassen Volcanic Basecamp
jewels.blurb: A guided "5 days, 4 nights" basecamp trip from Sacramento for "2-7 Guests", "12 and older": "Summit Lassen Peak", Bumpass Hell, Brokeoff Mountain, Cinder Cone and the Fantastic Lava Beds; "All meals are included from breakfast on Day 1 through lunch on the last day"; tent, pad, sleeping bag, day pack and trekking poles supplied. Wildland is part of the Intrepid Group.

jewels.name: Outdoor Adventure Club - Lassen backcountry ski guiding
jewels.blurb: "we've been permitted and insured to guide backcountry skiing, splitboarding, and AIARE avalanche classes in Lassen for over 20 years"; Group Weekends staying at their Mineral cabin (Intro and Intermediate) and private guiding "starting at $550/day for 1-2 skiers".

jewels.name: Outdoor Adventure Club - ski, splitboard and avalanche gear rental
jewels.blurb: Rents "backcountry ski, splitboard and avalanche gear" including "beacons, shovels, and probes" from "our cabin in the town of Mineral", for guests registered on a trip or staying at the Mineral house; "advance planning is suggested" as "supplies are limited".

jewels.name: Manzanita Lake Camper Store
jewels.blurb: Near the northwest entrance: "beverages, snacks, organic salads, and deli sandwiches"; season "May 21-October 12, daily 8 am-8 pm". The NPS lists "Food and beverages, camping supplies, and gifts" plus watercraft rentals, gasoline, showers and laundry.

jewels.name: Lassen Cafe & Gift
jewels.blurb: In the Kohm Yah-mah-nee Visitor Center at the southwest entrance: "salads, fresh fruits, hot or cold sandwiches, as well as a variety of beverages (including espresso drinks) and soft-serve ice cream"; patio with mountain views and a fireplace inside; group lunches on request at (530) 595-3555.

jewels.name: Highlands Ranch Resort
jewels.blurb: Mill Creek, on Hwy 36E in Lassen National Forest, "approximately 10 minutes east of the park": 7 newly built cottages and an American Bistro with full bar and a large wood-burning fireplace; summer (May 20-Nov 1) daily 8 AM-9 PM, winter Thursday-Sunday. 530-595-3388.

jewels.name: Mill Creek Resort
jewels.blurb: "the off-the-beaten-path mountain resort" in a historic 1930s lodge at 40271 Highway 172, Mill Creek: cabins with full kitchens, glamping tents, RV sites and vintage RV rentals; open year-round, pet-friendly, no Wi-Fi or cell service. Hipcamp lists it with "Cabins, Glamping Tents, RV Spots".

jewels.name: Lassen Glampsite (No Electricity)
jewels.blurb: Listed by Hipcamp among glamping near Bumpass Hell as a "Glampsite Cabin" in Lassen National Forest, 13 mi away.

jewels.name: Cedar Lodge Motel & RV Park
jewels.blurb: 1487 County Road 324, Chester: "just outside Lassen National Park" and "less than a mile from the pristine waters of Lake Almanor"; 17 RV sites with water, sewer and 30/50-amp electric (11 full hook-up, 3 pull-through, an oversized family site for up to 4 RVs, 2 boondocking sites) plus 9 cabin and lodging units.

jewels.name: Sacramento River RV Park
jewels.blurb: Redding, listed by Campspot near Lassen with waterfront, pool, fishing, dog park, playground, showers, laundry and dump station.

jewels.name: North Shore Campground, Lake Almanor
jewels.blurb: 541 Catfish Beach Road, Chester: "With over a mile of Lake Almanor shoreline, you'll enjoy immaculate views, a peaceful environment, and many fun activities"; 63 RV sites (30-amp, water), 30 tent sites and 5 cabins; boat launch, kayaking, playground, store, showers and laundry.

jewels.name: McArthur-Burney Falls Memorial State Park
jewels.blurb: A "129-foot white-water falls on Burney Creek", "northeast of Redding, 6 miles north of Highway 299 on Highway 89 near Burney"; tent, hike-and-bike and remote campsites and cabins ("The cabins are closed during winter"), camping $35 a night, day use "$10.00" per vehicle, "8:00 a.m. to sunset".

jewels.name: Hilton Garden Inn Redding
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "5050 Bechelli Lane, I-5, Exit 675, Redding, CA 96002", "44 miles from Lassen Volcanic National Park". The brand page was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Hampton Inn & Suites Redding
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "2160 Larkspur Lane, I-5, Exit 677, Redding, CA 96001", "45 miles from Lassen Volcanic National Park". The brand page was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: TownePlace Suites by Marriott Redding
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "2180 Larkspur Lane, I-5, Exit 677, Redding, CA 96002", "45 miles from Lassen Volcanic National Park". The Marriott page was not fetched (the Sheraton Redding domain failed its certificate check), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Red Bluff
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "2810 Main Street, I-5, Exit 650, Red Bluff, CA 96080", "44 miles from Lassen Volcanic National Park". The IHG page was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Red Onion Grill
jewels.blurb: 303 Peninsula Drive, Lake Almanor: "craft-cocktails, farm-to-table eats"; Wednesday-Sunday 5PM-8:30PM, closed Monday and Tuesday; (530) 596-1800; large groups via info@redoniongrill.com.

jewels.name: Timber House Restaurant, Brewery & Lodge
jewels.blurb: 501 Main Street, Chester: established in 1962, closed for years and reopened by Toni and Robert Vanella and Carol and Berton Bertagna - "popular pub fare", an on-site brewery with seasonal craft beers and a restored nine-room lodge; restaurant Friday-Monday, 11 a.m.-2 p.m. and 5-9 p.m.

jewels.name: Kopper Kettle
jewels.blurb: 243 Main Street, Chester; 530-258-2698; "Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner" (Lake Almanor Area Chamber listing).

jewels.name: St. Bernard Lodge
jewels.blurb: 44801 Hwy 36 East; 530-258-3382; stbernardlodge.com; "Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Cocktails" (Lake Almanor Area Chamber listing).

jewels.name: Tantardino's Pizzeria & Pasta
jewels.blurb: 441 Ponderosa Drive, Lake Almanor Peninsula; 530-596-3902; "Lunch, Dinner, Cocktails" (Lake Almanor Area Chamber listing).

jewels.name: Waganupa Brewing
jewels.blurb: 401 Peninsula Dr #9, Lake Almanor Peninsula; listed for "Beer" (Lake Almanor Area Chamber listing).

faq.q: How much is Lassen Volcanic National Park?
faq.a: The NPS lists "Private Vehicle (Apr 16-Nov 30) $30.00" and "Private Vehicle (Dec 1-Apr 15) $10.00"; motorcycles $25.00 / $10.00; per person $15.00 / $10.00; and "Annual Entrance - Park $55.00".

faq.q: Can you camp in Lassen Volcanic National Park?
faq.a: Yes. Seven campgrounds are listed, from Manzanita Lake (179 sites) to Warner Valley (17 sites), at $15 to $26 a night; "Reservations are required for all campgrounds except Juniper Lake and Southwest Walk-in", via recreation.gov or (877) 444-6777. Backcountry camping needs a Recreation.gov wilderness permit.

faq.q: Is Lassen Volcanic National Park dog friendly?
faq.a: Only where a car can go: "A pet may go anywhere a car may go: roads and road shoulders (not snow-covered), campgrounds, picnic areas, and parking lots." "Pets are not permitted on any hiking trail, in the park backcountry... in any body of water, or inside visitor centers or other park facilities." Leashes must be under six feet.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Lassen Volcanic National Park?
faq.a: Summer is "The most popular season in the park" with "the widest selection of activities and services"; "Wildflowers peak in high elevation areas between July and September." Snow lingers: "Bumpass Hell Trail remains closed due to snow coverage into July".

faq.q: When does Lassen Volcanic National Park close?
faq.a: The park itself does not close: "Lassen Volcanic National Park is open 24 hours per day, 365 days per year." The park highway does - Highway 89 typically "closes in mid- to late November" for snow and has closed as early as October 18.

faq.q: Can you drive through Lassen Volcanic National Park?
faq.a: In summer and fall, yes: "Take the one-hour drive along the 30-mile park highway." The highway "is closed to through traffic due to snow approximately November through April."

faq.q: Does Lassen Volcanic National Park have hot springs?
faq.a: It has hydrothermal areas, not bathing springs: "Bumpass Hell Trail provides access to the largest hydrothermal area in the park." The NPS warns: "Water and mud in hydrothermal areas is acidic. Do not put water or mud from park hydrothermal areas on your skin."

faq.q: What are things to do in Lassen Volcanic National Park with kids?
faq.a: The Junior Ranger programme: "The activities in the Junior Ranger booklet are best-suited to kids age 5 to 12", picked up "at the Loomis Museum (summer only) or Kohm Yah-mah-nee Visitor Center", with a badge on completion.

faq.q: Do you need a permit for Lassen Volcanic National Park?
faq.a: For backcountry camping, yes: "Wilderness permits for backcountry camping must be obtained prior to your visit to the park" through Recreation.gov, and "Permits can be reserved a maximum of 90 days prior to the start date."

faq.q: Can you fish in Lassen Volcanic National Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Numerous lakes and streams provide plentiful opportunities for fishing."

name: Olympic National Park
line: A mountain ridge, a moss-hung rain forest and a wilderness coast, joined by one highway that loops the whole peninsula

jewels.name: Hurricane Ridge (road open; Day Lodge destroyed, rebuild no earlier than 2028)
jewels.blurb: "the most easily accessed mountain area within Olympic National Park", 17 miles south of Port Angeles; the conditions page shows the road open to the ridge with Obstruction Point and Hurricane Hill roads open; winter road scheduled Friday-Sunday and holiday Mondays with chains required; the 1952 Day Lodge burned in May 2023

jewels.name: Hurricane Hill Trail
jewels.blurb: 1.6 miles one way from the end of the Hurricane Ridge Road, about 700 feet of gain, to panoramic views

jewels.name: Hurricane Ridge astronomy programs and winter snowshoe walks
jewels.blurb: free ranger-led telescope evenings at the Ridge in summer, weather permitting, and ranger-guided snowshoe walks in winter

jewels.name: Hall of Mosses and Spruce Nature Trail, Hoh Rain Forest
jewels.blurb: two loops from the Hoh visitor center - the 0.8-mile Hall of Mosses through maples "draped with abundant club moss" and the 1.2-mile Spruce Nature Trail by creek and river; the Hoh River Trail runs on, 18.5 miles out-and-back; visitor center closed January to early March

jewels.name: Marymere Falls and Mount Storm King, Lake Crescent
jewels.blurb: 0.9 miles one way to Marymere Falls from Storm King Ranger Station (first half-mile wheelchair accessible); the Mount Storm King spur is 2.1 miles one way and "climbs 2,100 feet!"

jewels.name: Spruce Railroad Trail and the Olympic Discovery Trail
jewels.blurb: 4 miles one way along Lake Crescent's north shore, paved, pets and bikes allowed, with a 6.5-mile paved extension west; part of the Olympic Discovery Trail that runs from Port Townsend to La Push

jewels.name: Sol Duc Falls
jewels.blurb: 0.8 miles one way through old-growth forest from the end of the Sol Duc Road to the falls overlook

jewels.name: Salmon Cascades Overlook, Sol Duc Valley
jewels.blurb: where "visitors come to watch the determined coho salmon leap over the falls"; the NPS gives late September to early October as the best viewing

jewels.name: High Divide Loop and Seven Lakes Basin
jewels.blurb: "a popular 2-3 day hike" from the Sol Duc; Sol Duc/Seven Lakes Basin is a wilderness quota area booked on Recreation.gov, with bear canisters required in all wilderness camp areas

jewels.name: Rialto Beach and Hole-in-the-Wall
jewels.blurb: drift logs, pounding surf and sea stacks; Hole-in-the-Wall is a sea-carved arch about 1.5 miles north; the NPS: "Always check the tides! It's possible to get stranded when certain areas of the coast become impassable when high tide rolls in."

jewels.name: Second Beach, La Push
jewels.blurb: a 0.7-mile hike from La Push Road to tide pools and sea stacks on the Olympic Wilderness Coast

jewels.name: Ruby Beach
jewels.blurb: a 0.2-mile walk from Highway 101 down to the coast and its sea stacks

jewels.name: Kalaloch Beach 4 tide pools
jewels.blurb: the NPS: "Beach 4 is an excellent location to tidepool looking for seastars, and anemones of various colors can be seen at low tides"; "Certain areas may become impassable during high tides and overland trails must be used."

jewels.name: Ozette boardwalks to the coast
jewels.blurb: "Two three-mile boardwalk trails lead to the coast where seals and gray whales can be spotted during migratory months"; a 15-site lakeside campground; wilderness permits and bear canisters are not available at Ozette Ranger Station

jewels.name: Elwha Valley: Madison Falls and the Olympic Hot Springs Road
jewels.blurb: site of "one of the largest ecosystem restoration projects in National Park Service history"; closed to vehicles beyond the Madison Falls parking lot due to flood damage, open beyond it to bikes, walkers, stock and leashed pets

jewels.name: Lake Crescent Lodge
jewels.blurb: in-park cottages, cabins and lodge rooms on the glacially carved lake, season April 17, 2026 to January 1, 2027; rowboats for rent at the lodge

jewels.name: Log Cabin Resort, Lake Crescent
jewels.blurb: camping, chalets, cabins and lodge rooms on the north shore, season May 15 to September 29, 2026 (closed now for the year); kayak and canoe rentals in season

jewels.name: Sol Duc Hot Springs Resort
jewels.blurb: rustic cabins (standard and kitchenette), naturally heated mineral pools and a freshwater pool, the Springs Restaurant; open March to November; Aramark concession

jewels.name: Kalaloch Lodge
jewels.blurb: "the only oceanfront lodge in Olympic National Park" - main lodge rooms, bluff cabins and the Seacrest House, Creekside Restaurant; run by Delaware North as an authorized NPS concessioner

jewels.name: Lake Quinault Lodge (Olympic National Forest)
jewels.blurb: built 1926 and marking 100 years in 2026; lakeside lodge rooms, indoor pool and sauna, Roosevelt Dining Room, kayak rentals; Aramark under a US Forest Service permit

jewels.name: Sol Duc Rainforest Retreat, near Lake Crescent (listing)
jewels.blurb: 14 sites on 9 acres beside the Olympic Discovery Trail, about 1-1.5 miles from Lake Crescent, including canvas tents and yurts with tent decks, hot showers and covered outdoor kitchens - per its Hipcamp listing

jewels.name: Whiskey Creek Beach, near Port Angeles
jewels.blurb: beachfront cabins, glamping/tent sites and RV hookups on the Strait of Juan de Fuca, booked direct on its own site

jewels.name: Mike's Beach Resort Glamping Village, Lilliwaup (Hood Canal, Staircase side)
jewels.blurb: fully furnished camping tents with beds, heating, bedding, towels, outlets and wifi, plus a private BBQ and firepit at each site, alongside Hood Canal waterfront cabins at 38470 N US Hwy 101

jewels.name: Kalaloch Campground (NPS)
jewels.blurb: 175 sites on the coast, open year-round; reservations on recreation.gov May 15 to September 20, 2026, first-come outside that window

jewels.name: Mora Campground (NPS)
jewels.blurb: 94 sites about 3 miles from Rialto Beach, open year-round; reservations on recreation.gov May 15 to September 20, 2026, first-come otherwise

jewels.name: Hoh Rain Forest Campground (NPS)
jewels.blurb: year-round; reservations on recreation.gov June 12 to September 6, 2026, first-come outside that window

jewels.name: Sol Duc Hot Springs RV and Campground
jewels.blurb: 82 sites in old-growth forest along the river; reservations on recreation.gov March 20 to November 1, 2026

jewels.name: Heart O' the Hills Campground (NPS)
jewels.blurb: 105 sites in old-growth forest 5 miles south of Port Angeles on the Hurricane Ridge road; first-come, first-served, year-round, walk-in only in heavy snow

jewels.name: First-come NPS campgrounds: Deer Park, Graves Creek, North Fork, Ozette, Queets, South Beach (and Staircase)
jewels.blurb: no reservations at Deer Park (self-register, June to mid-October), Graves Creek, North Fork, Ozette, Queets and South Beach (May 19 to October 10, 2026); Staircase takes recreation.gov reservations July 8 to September 29 and is first-come otherwise

jewels.name: Crescent Beach & RV Park, Port Angeles
jewels.blurb: 67 RV, tent and cabin sites on 18 acres behind a half-mile sandy beach at 2860 Crescent Beach Rd (address per the Port Angeles visitor bureau), open year-round, near the Tongue Point Marine Life Sanctuary tide pools

jewels.name: Elwha Dam RV Park, Port Angeles
jewels.blurb: big-rig pull-throughs, tent sites, guest houses and e-bike rentals at 47 Lower Dam Rd, year-round, billed as an "Olympic Basecamp"

jewels.name: John Wayne's Waterfront Resort, Sequim
jewels.blurb: 89 RV and tent sites and 9 fully equipped bay-view cabins on 20 acres by Sequim Bay, on the Olympic Discovery Trail near John Wayne Marina - per its Hipcamp listing

jewels.name: Quileute Oceanside Resort, La Push
jewels.blurb: owned and operated by the Quileute Tribe: oceanfront luxury and rustic cabins, apartments, ocean and riverview RV spots and tent sites at 330 Ocean Drive, "no TVs or Wi-Fi"

jewels.name: Rain Forest Resort Village, Lake Quinault
jewels.blurb: Parkside Suites, Fireplace Cabins, the Village Inn and an RV campground on the lake shore, home of the "World's Largest Spruce Tree" by its own account

jewels.name: Hoh River Rafters, Forks
jewels.blurb: half-day Class II float trips on the Hoh at 9am or 2pm, March 1 to September 15, no experience needed; published at $150 per person

jewels.name: Olympic Hiking Co., Port Angeles
jewels.blurb: "a commercially authorized tour company in Olympic National Park" since 2016 - small-group and private guided hikes, guided backpacking, and coast trailhead shuttles such as Rialto to Ozette and Third Beach to Oil City

jewels.name: Experience Olympic, Port Angeles
jewels.blurb: a "Permittee of Olympic National Park" since 2013, woman-owned: private guided nature days for birding, tidepooling (April-August low tides), the Elwha restoration, Hurricane Ridge, the Hoh and the coast

jewels.name: Elevate Outdoors, Port Angeles
jewels.blurb: kayak tours on Lake Crescent and Freshwater Bay, Olympic Discovery Trail bike tours and combination days, May to October; bike rentals by reservation year-round, at 220 E 1st Street

jewels.name: Puget Sound Express whale watching, Port Townsend
jewels.blurb: 4-hour half-day whale watching April-November and a full-day San Juan Islands trip April-September from 227 Jackson Street; whale sightings on 99% of trips by its own account, with a free return trip if none

jewels.name: Quinault Rainforest Tour (Lake Quinault Lodge)
jewels.blurb: a 3-hour guided shuttle tour 33 miles into the Quinault valley and the Valley of the Giants, year-round, 9:30 am departures, minimum 4 passengers; $55 plus tax

jewels.name: M.V. Coho ferry, Port Angeles to Victoria BC
jewels.blurb: Black Ball Ferry Line's daily, year-round 90-minute crossing of the Strait of Juan de Fuca, 22.59 nautical miles

jewels.name: Hurricane Ridge Ski & Snowboard Area
jewels.blurb: a non-profit, locals-run lift area inside the park; 2026-27 season tentatively Saturdays, Sundays and Monday holidays, 10 am-4 pm, snow permitting, with ski school, tubing and snowshoeing

jewels.name: Purple Haze Lavender, Sequim
jewels.blurb: farm store at 180 Bell Bottom Rd, Wednesday-Sunday 10am-5pm; fields bloom from late June through July, some into September

jewels.name: Sequim Lavender Festival
jewels.blurb: the Sequim Lavender Growers Association's festival of farm visits, u-pick, live music and 200+ artisan vendors; 2026 dates were July 17-19

jewels.name: Dungeness Crab Festival, October 9-11, 2026
jewels.blurb: a free three-day festival on the Port Angeles Waterfront City Pier - crab dinners from 14,000+ crabs, 75+ vendor booths, live music and Coast Guard boat tours

jewels.name: Finnriver Farm & Cidery, Chimacum
jewels.booking_route: walk-in Cider Garden; events and groups by phone 360-339-8478 or email
jewels.blurb: Certified Organic, Salmon Safe B Corp farm, orchard and cidery along a salmon stream; year-round Cider Garden (Wed-Sun 12-8pm) with draft ciders, Finnriver Kitchen, seasonal tours and weekend live music.

jewels.name: Hama Hama Oyster Saloon and Farm Store, Lilliwaup (Hood Canal, Staircase side)
jewels.booking_route: reservations recommended but not required; phone (360) 877-5811 or email
jewels.blurb: Sixth-generation family shellfish farm whose farm store has sold fresh shellfish since the 1970s; outdoor Oyster Saloon open weekends year round, oyster classes in winter.

jewels.name: Finistere, Port Townsend
jewels.blurb: Farm-to-table restaurant ('End of the Land') on Lawrence Street, dinner Wednesday to Saturday 5-8pm with a 3-5pm happy hour.

jewels.name: Alder Wood Bistro, Sequim
jewels.blurb: Wood-fired pizza and contemporary dining, Wednesday to Saturday 4-8pm, with seasonal garden dining Memorial Day weekend through late September.

jewels.name: Next Door Gastropub, Port Angeles
jewels.booking_route: no reservations; phone (360) 504-2613 to join a text waitlist
jewels.blurb: Elevated pub fare from fresh local ingredients with ten rotating taps of local, regional and artisan beer, plus a full cocktail bar.

jewels.name: Pane d'Amore, Port Townsend and Sequim
jewels.blurb: Artisan bakery dating to 2004 with shops in Port Townsend (Tue-Sat 7-6, Sun 7-3) and Sequim (Tue-Sat 8-2).

jewels.name: Dungeness Valley Creamery, Sequim
jewels.blurb: Family-owned raw A2 Jersey dairy whose farm store at 1915 Towne Road sells raw milk and cream, eggs, cheeses, raw honey and Lopez Island ice cream.

jewels.name: Chimacum Corner Farmstand, Chimacum
jewels.blurb: Rural natural grocery and nursery open daily 8am-7pm, stocking hyper-local produce, cheeses, sustainably caught seafood and dishes made daily in the Corner Kitchen.

jewels.name: Jefferson County Farmers Markets (Port Townsend and Chimacum)

jewels.name: Port Angeles Farmers Market

jewels.name: Harbinger Winery, Port Angeles

jewels.name: FairWinds Winery, Port Townsend
jewels.blurb: Winery making Washington wines including Aligote and Lemberger plus Port O'Call fortified wines, with walk-in tastings Friday to Sunday 12-5pm and barrel tastings.

jewels.name: Propolis Brewing, Port Townsend

jewels.blurb: Port Townsend distiller of premium whisky and fruit brandy.

faq.q: Is Highway 101 open around Olympic National Park?
faq.a: Not continuously in October 2026. The NPS states US 101 at the Hoh River Bridge, south of Forks, is closed 5 a.m. Thursday, Oct. 1 to noon Tuesday, Oct. 6 and 5 a.m. Thursday Oct. 8 to noon Tuesday, Oct. 13, with no detour across the Hoh River. The Hoh Rain Forest stays reachable from Forks.

faq.q: Is the Hurricane Ridge Day Lodge open?
faq.a: No. The NPS states the 1952 Day Lodge was destroyed by fire in May 2023. A design contract was awarded in September 2025 and construction may start in 2028 at the earliest. The road to the ridge is open; in winter it is scheduled Friday through Sunday and holiday Mondays, weather permitting, with tire chains required.

faq.q: How do I reserve a campsite in Olympic National Park?
faq.a: Kalaloch, Mora, Hoh, Fairholme, Sol Duc and Staircase take recreation.gov reservations in set summer windows and are first-come outside them. Deer Park, Graves Creek, Heart O' the Hills, North Fork, Ozette, Queets and South Beach are always first-come, first-served.

faq.q: How much does it cost to enter Olympic National Park?
faq.a: $30 per private vehicle for 7 days, $25 per motorcycle, $15 per person on foot or bike (under 16 free), or $55 for an Olympic Annual Pass. The park does not accept cash.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to backpack in Olympic?
faq.a: Yes. Wilderness permits are created through Recreation.gov; quota areas include the Ozette Coast, Seven Lakes Basin and Royal Basin. Summer-season permits (May 15 to October 15) are released April 15 at 7:00 am Pacific. Bear canisters are required in all wilderness camp areas.

faq.q: What does the park say about tides on the coast?
faq.a: The NPS states that "Several points along the coast are only passable at lower tides" and advises carrying a tide chart, available at visitor centers and coastal ranger stations.

name: Mount Rainier National Park
line: A glaciated volcano with wildflower meadows at Paradise and Sunrise, a year-round historic inn at Longmire, guided summit climbs from Ashford, and treehouses, yurts and Airstreams at the gates

jewels.name: Paradise and the Henry M. Jackson Memorial Visitor Center
jewels.booking_route: none needed - entrance fee only; no timed entry in 2026
jewels.blurb: the park's high meadow hub at 5,400 feet, 19 miles from the Nisqually Entrance, with exhibits, film, ranger programmes and cafeteria; visitor centre usually daily May to early October, weekends and holidays mid-October through April; average 640 inches of snow a year

jewels.name: Skyline Trail, Paradise
jewels.blurb: a 5.5-mile loop through subalpine meadows with views of Mount Rainier, glaciers and the Tatoosh Range; NPS: "Snow can linger on trails well into June or even July"

jewels.name: Wildflower season at Paradise and Sunrise

jewels.name: Sunrise, Burroughs Mountain and Mount Fremont Lookout

jewels.name: Longmire Historic District

jewels.name: Carbon River temperate rainforest
jewels.booking_route: none needed for day use; Ipsut Creek requires a wilderness permit
jewels.blurb: a corner of the park whose rainfall makes it "resemble that of a temperate rainforest"; the road "was washed out by the 2006 Flood and is closed to vehicles past to the park boundary"; Ipsut Creek Campground 5 miles in, open year-round; Chenuis Falls 7.4 miles round trip

jewels.name: Mowich Lake

jewels.name: Ohanapecosh old-growth forest and Silver Falls

jewels.name: Timed entry: none in 2026
jewels.booking_route: none needed - pay at entrance; digital America the Beautiful pass via Recreation.gov

jewels.name: Summit climbing permits

jewels.name: Wilderness permits and the Wonderland Trail

faq.q: Do I need a timed entry reservation for Mount Rainier in 2026?
faq.a: No. The NPS states that timed entry reservations are currently not required anywhere in the park and that the park will not implement a timed entry reservation for any portion of the park in 2026.

faq.q: Can I drive to Sunrise right now?
faq.a: No. As of the NPS update of September 24, 2026, Sunrise and Sunrise Road remain open to pedestrians and bicyclists and closed to private vehicles for the remainder of the 2026 season.

faq.q: When are the wildflowers best?
faq.a: The NPS says that in most years many flowers are blooming by mid-July and by the first of August the meadows should be very impressive.

faq.q: What does it cost to climb Mount Rainier?
faq.a: The NPS climbing fee is $82 per person, plus $12 per person per night for a wilderness permit in summer. Guided climbs are offered by three authorized services; RMI posts its Four Day Climb at $2,595-$2,995.

faq.q: Is there lodging inside the park?
faq.a: Yes. The National Park Inn at Longmire is open year-round and the 1916 Paradise Inn is generally open mid-May through early October, both run by Rainier Guest Services.

faq.q: Which park campgrounds take reservations?
faq.a: Cougar Rock is reservable on Recreation.gov with some first-come sites; White River is first-come only; Ohanapecosh is closed for 2026; Mowich Lake walk-in sites need a wilderness permit.

name: Crater Lake National Park
line: Caldera rim of America's deepest lake

jewels.name: Scenic Rim Drive
jewels.booking_route: none needed - included in the park entrance fee
jewels.blurb: "33 miles (53 km) of lake views, panoramic vistas, forests and meadows" with "30 overlooks with ample car parking" and "access to five picnic areas, hikes of various difficulty, geologic formations and several waterfalls"; "Allow a minimum of two hours (including sight-seeing stops) to circumnavigate the lake". West and East Rim Drives close around November 1 and "reopen in stages beginning in May (depending on snowfall)".

jewels.name: Sinnott Memorial Overlook
jewels.booking_route: none needed - included in the park entrance fee
jewels.blurb: At Rim Village: "The oldest and most popular viewpoint in the park built specifically to offer a united view of the beauty the geologic story." Summer ranger programmes include "Short talks on a variety of subjects at the Sinnott Memorial Overlook in Rim Village".

jewels.name: Crater Lake Lodge
jewels.blurb: "Opened in 1915", "71 hotel rooms and the Crater Lake Dining Room" at Rim Village; 2026 season "May 15th, 2026 - October 13th, 2026"; "ADA Bed Options" in Standard Lodge Rooms. Run by the park concessioner, Explor Crater Lake; late-afternoon ranger talks are given "on the patio with lake views or indoors near the fireplace" (NPS ranger programmes page).

jewels.name: Garfield Peak Trail
jewels.blurb: 3.6 miles, 1,010 feet of gain: "Trail begins in the trees but quickly opens to a meadow. Switchbacks weave views of the lake and valleys, craggy peaks and scree slopes." Most high trails are "snow and ice covered December into June."

jewels.name: Watchman Peak Trail
jewels.blurb: 1.6 miles, 420 feet of gain, Moderate: "An extremely crowded trail especially at sunset. Moderate ascent to a fire lookout."

jewels.name: Mount Scott Trail
jewels.blurb: 4.4 miles, 1,250 feet of gain to "The park's highest peak at 8,929 ft (2,721 m) and the oldest at 425,000 years old."

jewels.name: Crater Lake Trolley
jewels.booking_route: Peek ("book your tour with Peek") or 541-882-1896; day-of tickets at Rim Village (NPS)
jewels.blurb: A park concessioner running "daily trolley tours" of the "historic 33-mile Rim Drive", "typically begin in July and run through mid-September", "five to seven stops at significant overlooks" (NPS). Its own site: tours "LAST 2 HOURS" and "START AT THE RIM VILLAGE NEAR THE CRATERLAKE LODGE"; Adults $44.00, Seniors (65+) and Military $42.00, Children 6-13 $25.00, under 6 free; one wheelchair per trolley with a day's notice.

jewels.name: Mazama Campground
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov (reservations July 1 - October 1, 2026); first come first serve late May - June 30, 2026
jewels.blurb: "The 214 campsites each feature a picnic table, fire ring with a grill and a bear-resistant food locker"; Tent $35.00, RV no hookups $35.00, electricity $48.00, full hookups $57.00; restrooms, gas station, potable water, dump station and "showers that are available in Loop F"; the Mazama Camper Store stocks "groceries, propane, firewood, and gasoline." Operated by Explor Crater Lake.

jewels.name: The Cabins at Mazama Village
jewels.blurb: 2026 season "May 8th, 2026 - October 4th, 2026"; Standard cabins with "2 Queen Beds" and a "private bath that feature a shower", ADA cabins with "1 Queen Bed"; "no phone, TV, and air conditioning." Beside Annie Creek Restaurant and the Mazama Village Store.

jewels.name: Junior Ranger programme
jewels.booking_route: none needed - ask at a visitor center
jewels.blurb: "Stop by a visitor center and ask for a Junior Ranger Book"; children complete the required pages, return to the visitor center and "receive a badge". The NPS things-to-do page: "Each day during summer, four times a day, kids get to discover Crater Lake National Park with a ranger."

jewels.name: Ranger-guided snowshoe walks
jewels.booking_route: none sold - contact the park, 541-594-3000, for schedules
jewels.blurb: "Ranger-guided snowshoe walks are offered most years from late November through the end of April"; "No previous snowshoeing experience is necessary"; "Aside from the park entry fee, there is no cost for the snowshoe walk and snowshoes are provided free".

jewels.name: Godfrey Glen Trail
jewels.blurb: 1.1 miles, 50 feet of gain: "An old trail with a new accessibility surface", "Recommended for all terrain wheelchairs with assistance"; the accessibility page calls it "the park's fully accessible trail". One of the few trails where leashed pets are allowed.

jewels.name: Plaikni Falls Trail
jewels.blurb: 2.0 miles, 100 feet of gain: "An easy stroll through a forest to a waterfall fed by snowmelt"; "Accessible to all-terrain wheelchairs except for the last 1/4".

jewels.name: The Pinnacles
jewels.blurb: 0.8 miles, 10 feet of gain: "Easy forest walk above a canyon filled with volcanic spires (pinnacles)"; "Accessible to all-terrain wheelchairs".

jewels.name: Castle Crest Wildflower Trail
jewels.blurb: 0.5 miles, 100 feet of gain: "The trail loops around a spring-fed meadow which hosts over 200 wildflower species."

jewels.name: Cleetwood Cove Trail (closed 2026-2028)
jewels.blurb: "a steep and strenuous hike. In 1.1 miles (1.7 km) the trail drops 700 feet (213 meters)" - the only route to the shore, where "Swimming, wading and fishing are permitted in the lake" and boat tours leave. 🔴 "This trail will be closed for a major rehabilitation project for the 2026, 2027, and 2028 seasons."

jewels.name: Backcountry camping and the Pacific Crest Trail
jewels.booking_route: free permit in person at the Ranger Station, no more than 1 day ahead
jewels.blurb: "A backcountry camping permit is required year-round for all overnight trips in the park." "Permits are issued free of charge" and "must be obtained in person. They are not available over the phone, or more than 1 day in advance. The Ranger Station is located 100 yards southwest of the Steel Visitor Center." The Pacific Crest Trail crosses the park and is one of the few trails open to leashed pets.

jewels.name: Crater Lake Lodge Dining Room
jewels.blurb: Breakfast 7:00-10:00 am, lunch 11:00 am-2:00 pm, dinner 4:00-9:00 pm, "May 15th, 2026 - October 13th, 2026"; dinner reservations recommended up to a week ahead; parties of 12 or more are group reservations; small plates in the Great Hall and on the Terrace between meals; a certified green restaurant.

jewels.name: Annie Creek Restaurant
jewels.booking_route: walk-in (no reservation method on the page)
jewels.blurb: Mazama Village: "Specialty sandwiches, pizza and, soups are some of the featured menu items"; breakfast 7:00-10:30 am, lunch and dinner 11:00 am-9:00 pm, "May 22nd, 2026 - October 1st, 2026"; with the Annie Creek Scoop Shop, 11:00 am-7:00 pm.

jewels.name: Rim Village Cafe
jewels.blurb: "grab-and-go food like sandwiches, salads and snacks"; 10:00 am-5:00 pm until May 15, then 9:00 am-8:00 pm from May 15, 2026; "Closed for Christmas Day".

jewels.name: Cosmos - Exploring the Pacific Northwest (9 days)
jewels.blurb: An escorted "Exploring the Pacific Northwest" by Cosmos, 9 days "From Seattle to Portland", "All Ages Welcome", from $2,389 (double occupancy); Day 5 "Bend to Medford" includes "Crater Lake National Park visit" and "Crater Lake viewing."

jewels.name: Crater Lake Resort, Fort Klamath
jewels.blurb: "50711 OR-62, Fort Klamath, Oregon", "7 miles from the south gate of Crater Lake National Park"; "13 Cabins" with "full kitchens, decks, BBQs", RV and tent sites, glamping tents, and "Free canoes on Fort Creek" with "paddles and life jackets included"; "Open year-round".

jewels.name: Crater Lake Resort glamping bell tents
jewels.blurb: "4 Glamping Sites" of "Brand-new canvas bell tents": "1 queen bed + 2 twin beds", "Real linens. Real pillows. Lanterns inside."; "No electricity, no water in-tent"; "Open May 15 - October 15"; deposit of the first night, full refund if cancelled 30+ days before arrival.

jewels.name: Crater Lake Resort RV Park
jewels.blurb: "Full: water, 30/50-amp power, sewer. Partial: water + power." "Most sites accommodate rigs up to 35 feet. All sites are back-in only"; bathhouse with hot showers, "On-site laundry", Tesla Supercharger, general store; "Open year-round"; "From $57/night" partial, "From $73.67/night" full hookup.

jewels.name: Diamond Lake RV Park
jewels.blurb: "We have 110 full hookup sites with either 30 or 50 amp service"; laundry, restrooms and showers; "At just seven miles from Crater Lake National Park and three miles from The Lodge"; "All vehicles must be parked before dark." 541-793-3318.

jewels.name: Diamond Lake Resort
jewels.blurb: Cabins ("rustic to luxury") and motel & studios on Diamond Lake, "located only seven miles" from Crater Lake National Park; summer boat, bike, kayak and paddleboard rentals; winter cross-country skiing, cat skiing on Mt. Bailey, snow tubing, ice fishing and snowmobile rentals. 350 Resort Drive, Diamond Lake; (541) 793-3333.

jewels.name: Diamond Lake Resort bike and boat rentals
jewels.booking_route: phone 541-793-3333 ext. 5 or in person at the Marina Store
jewels.blurb: "Our fleet of 'Diamond Back' mountain bikes are a great way to venture around the lake" on a "12 mile paved loop around Diamond Lake"; "1/2 Day (4 Hours): $30 plus $5/additional hour" or "$22/hour"; the Marina Store also rents boats, paddle boats, patio boats, kayaks and paddleboards. Reserve at 541-793-3333 ext. 5.

jewels.name: Diamond Lake Campground (Umpqua National Forest)
jewels.blurb: "Meandering along most of the east shore of the mile-high Diamond Lake, this large campground boasts spectacular views of both Mount Bailey and Mount Thielsen"; "238 sites, including double and standard sites"; accessible flush toilets and showers, amphitheater, boat ramp, dump station; 14-night maximum stay.

jewels.name: Union Creek Campground (Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest)
jewels.blurb: "constructed in 1934 by the Civilian Conservation Corp. The campground is located 18 miles west of Crater Lake National Park and in the midst of an old growth forest." "There are 73 campsites", "not recommended for trailers over 28 feet long"; first-come sites available; Rogue Gorge and Natural Bridge interpretive trails nearby.

jewels.name: Rogue Gorge and Natural Bridge
jewels.blurb: Two Forest Service interpretive trails beside Union Creek Campground: "Rogue Gorge" and "Natural Bridge" both have trails "with views of the Upper Rogue River" (Recreation.gov, Union Creek Campground).

jewels.name: Union Creek Resort
jewels.blurb: Has "welcomed guests and travelers since 1922" at 56484 Highway 62, Prospect - a "Basecamp to Crater Lake"; renovated Union Creek Lodge rooms (2014), "17 authentic log cabins" and larger vacation-rental cabins for groups; cash-free. Winter snowshoeing, skiing and snowmobiling listed.

jewels.name: Beckie's Cafe
jewels.blurb: "Serving since in 1926, Beckie's Café is famous for good reason: delicious, home-style food, great service, an awesome location just minutes from Crater Lake National Park, and our celebrated Beckie's pies, made fresh daily." "Daily 8:00 AM to 7:00 PM"; the cafe and resort are "listed on the National Register of Historic Places."

jewels.name: The Lodge at Diamond Lake - Cafe and Mt. Bailey Room
jewels.blurb: "The Café and Mt. Bailey Room" in the Lodge at Diamond Lake Resort: breakfast, lunch and dinner, summer "7 days a week | 7am - 9pm", winter weekdays 8am-8pm and weekends 8am-9pm.

jewels.name: South Shore Pizza
jewels.blurb: Diamond Lake Resort's second restaurant, about a mile from the lodge: "fresh, hand-made pizzas, brews, sandwiches, ice cream and more".

jewels.name: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott Klamath Falls
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "460 Timbermill Drive, Klamath Falls, OR 97601", "51 miles from Crater Lake National Park" - at the edge of the ~50-mile ring. Marriott's own page was not fetched (marriott.com blocks this route), so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Klamath Falls
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "2430 South 6th Street, Klamath Falls, OR 97601", "53 miles from Crater Lake National Park" - just beyond the ~50-mile ring. IHG's own page was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Hilton Garden Inn Medford
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "1000 Welcome Way, I-5, Exit 27, Medford, OR 97504", "54 miles from Crater Lake National Park" - in Medford, whose airport the NPS names as "The closest airport with commercial flights". Hilton's own page was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Water and layers for the high rim
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Carry with you more water than you normally drink." "Dress in layers and keep dry, warm clothes nearby"; "Wear appropriate clothing outdoors, including hats, mittens, coats and footwear." "Arrange activities to minimize your exposure to lightning danger. This often means hiking early in the day."

jewels.name: Sun clothing for the summer trails
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Wear lightweight, loose-fitting and light-colored clothing if you'll be out in the heat"; at altitude, "Upon arrival, take time to acclimate to avoid, headaches, dizziness, and fainting." "All trails begin above 4,000 feet in elevation" (hiking page).

jewels.name: Tire chains for the winter road
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Use tire chains or traction tires when posted as being required (during snowy or icy periods)." The park averages "41 ft (12.5 m) of snow at park headquarters" a year (weather page); the South and West entrances on Highway 62 stay open year-round.

jewels.name: Food storage for camp and backcountry
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Keep all food securely stored and out of reach from wildlife." Mazama Campground sites carry "a bear-resistant food locker" (Explor Crater Lake); in the backcountry the camper carries the storage. Bears: "there are only five months when bears are active but even then, seeing one is not likely" (NPS FAQ).

faq.q: What is the entrance fee for Crater Lake National Park?
faq.a: A private vehicle is "$30.00" from May 22 to October 31 and "$20.00" from November 1 to May 21; a motorcycle $25.00 / $15.00; "Per Person $15.00" for a hiker, cyclist or pedestrian. The park's annual pass "costs $55."

faq.q: Do you need reservations for Crater Lake National Park?
faq.a: Not to enter: "Although an entrance fee or NPS pass is required to enter Crater Lake National Park, vehicle reservations are not needed." Lodging is another matter - the concessioner says "Accommodations in Crater Lake are at capacity the entire season. Book as soon as possible in order to secure reservations."

faq.q: Can you swim in Crater Lake?
faq.a: Normally yes, from the shore at Cleetwood Cove: "Swimming, wading and fishing are permitted in the lake." But the Cleetwood Cove Trail - the only route to the water - "will be closed for a major rehabilitation project for the 2026, 2027, and 2028 seasons."

faq.q: Are there boat tours on Crater Lake?
faq.a: Not at present: "Due to major rehabilitation work on the Cleetwood Trail and lakeshore facilities, boat tours will not be available in 2026 or 2027." The alternative the NPS names is the Crater Lake Trolley's two-hour Rim Drive tour, which "typically begin in July and run through mid-September".

faq.q: How deep is Crater Lake?
faq.a: "Crater Lake is 1,943 feet deep. It's the deepest lake in the United States and the deepest volcanic lake in the world."

faq.q: Is Crater Lake National Park open year-round?
faq.a: "The park is open year-round, 24 hours a day." Roads close "with the first big snowstorm, or on November 1, whichever comes first"; "Typically, plowing begins on West Rim Drive in mid-April and all roads are ready to open by mid-July."

faq.q: What is the closest airport to Crater Lake National Park?
faq.a: "The closest airport with commercial flights is in Medford, Oregon (75 miles from Park Headquarters)." From Medford, "Follow Highway 62 to the park's West Entrance. Open year-round." "There is no public transportation in the vicinity of the park."

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Crater Lake National Park?
faq.a: "Summers at Crater Lake are short but sunny. July, August, and September are your best bets for warm, dry weather." "In May, June, and October, sunny days alternate with periods of rain and snow."

faq.q: Can you take dogs to Crater Lake National Park?
faq.a: In limited places: Mazama Campground and all picnic areas, along roads within 50 feet of pavement, parking areas and paved walkways, and only these trails - Lady of the Woods, Godfrey Glen, Annie Spur, Grayback Drive and the Pacific Crest Trail. "All leashes must be a maximum of six feet", and pets "are not permitted on the Cleetwood Cove Trail."

faq.q: Can you camp in Crater Lake National Park?
faq.a: Yes. Mazama Campground has 214 sites with "a picnic table, fire ring with a grill and a bear-resistant food locker", first come first serve from late May to June 30, 2026 and on reservation from July 1 to October 1, 2026, "booked through our Recreation.gov website link". Backcountry camping needs a free permit obtained in person.

seo.meta_title: Crater Lake National Park: Rim Drive, Lodge & Where to Stay | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: America's deepest lake at 1,943 ft: the 33-mile Rim Drive, Crater Lake Lodge, Mazama camping, and the 2026-2028 Cleetwood Cove closure. Book early.

hero.query: Crater Lake National Park Wizard Island from the rim

name: North Cascades National Park
line: Glacier peaks, Diablo Lake and roadless Stehekin

jewels.name: North Cascades Highway (State Route 20)
jewels.booking_route: none needed - a public state highway; no entrance fee
jewels.blurb: "Drive approximately 30 miles across the park on the North Cascades Highway (State Route 20), and experience the old growth forests, cascading waterfalls, and mountain scenery of North Cascades. Allow at least an hour to drive this beautiful, winding road." Highlights by milepost: North Cascades Visitor Center (119.9), Newhalem (120.5), Gorge Creek Falls (123.4), Diablo Lake Overlook (131.7), Happy Creek Forest Walk (134.3), Ross Lake Overlooks (136).

jewels.name: Diablo Lake Overlook
jewels.booking_route: none needed - a free roadside overlook
jewels.blurb: At mile 131.7 of State Route 20: "Enjoy stunning views of the lake and surrounding mountain peaks." The NPS names it the best roadside sunrise and sunset spot: "The most easily accessible area along State Route 20 with the best views for sunset and sunrise is Diablo Lake Overlook."

jewels.name: Cascade Pass Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed for a day hike; overnight needs a backcountry permit via Recreation.gov
jewels.blurb: At the end of the Cascade River Road: "7.4 miles (12 km) roundtrip / 1,700 ft (518 m) elevation gain" - "A popular day hike with spectacular views of peaks and glaciers." The NPS adds that the trailhead "is typically open mid-July, road dependent" and backcountry permits for the Cascade Pass area "are very competitive, especially for Sahale Glacier camp."

jewels.name: Stehekin and Lake Chelan National Recreation Area
jewels.booking_route: none needed to visit; reached by Lady of the Lake ferry, float plane or on foot
jewels.blurb: "Nestled at the headwaters of Lake Chelan, the third deepest lake in the United States"; "There are no roads that lead into Stehekin. Connected to the outside world only by foot, boat, or plane." A hub for "the 61,949-acre Lake Chelan National Recreation Area". For 2026: "The North Cascades Lodge at Stehekin is closed for the 2026 summer season"; no cell reception, no ATM.

jewels.name: Thunder Knob Trail
jewels.blurb: Mile Post 130: "3.7 miles (6 km) roundtrip / 680 ft (207 m) elevation gain" - "A popular trail to a view of Diablo Lake."

jewels.name: Happy Creek Forest Walk
jewels.blurb: Mile Post 134: ".03 mile (.05 km) loop / 42 ft (13 m) elevation gain" - "Stroll through the forest along a cascading creek", with an optional 2.6-mile round-trip spur to a waterfall. The NPS lists it as a "fully accessible boardwalk" path: "a 1/3 mile (1/2 kilometer) loop through ancient forest."

jewels.name: North Cascades Visitor Center and Sterling Munro Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free; group presentations by prior arrangement
jewels.blurb: Near milepost 120 by Newhalem: "Relief map of the park and surrounding area, exhibit room featuring multimedia exhibits on the park's natural and cultural history"; a theater, "Several short, accessible interpretive trails", and "Special presentations available for school and other groups by prior arrangement." From the Sterling Munro Boardwalk, "View the Picket Range". (360) 854-7200.

jewels.name: Backcountry permits for the Stephen Mather Wilderness
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov reservation, or walk-up permit at the Wilderness Information Center, 7280 Ranger Station Rd., Marblemount
jewels.blurb: "Backcountry permits are required year-round in North Cascades National Park for all overnight trips." About 60% of backcountry sites are reservable on Recreation.gov (2026: early-access lottery March 2-13, general on-sale April 29 at 7 am Pacific); the rest are walk-up permits from the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount. Recreation fee "Adults (16 and older) - $10 per person", youth free, plus a "$6 non-refundable" reservation fee.

jewels.name: Junior Ranger Program
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free, at park visitor centers
jewels.blurb: "A dynamic new Junior Ranger Program is now available for kids and families visiting their national park. Four age-appropriate booklets introduce the unique natural and cultural history of the North Cascades through a series of fun activities." Booklets and badges are picked up at park visitor and information centers.

jewels.name: Colonial Creek North and South Campgrounds
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov or 1-877-444-6777 in season; first-come, first-served outside it
jewels.blurb: "Colonial Creek Campground is a remote, yet bustling campground nestled in old growth forest with trail and lake access" on Diablo Lake; "Colonial Creek - $24 per night". Ten walk-in, tent-only sites (#64-#73) at Colonial Creek South stay open year-round, first-come, first-served, "with no fee, no water, and no trash services". RV dump station at Colonial Creek South in season.

jewels.name: Ross Dam Trail
jewels.blurb: Mile Post 134: "2.5 miles (3.9 km) roundtrip / 532 ft (162 m) elevation gain" - "Hike this moderate trail to walk across the historic Ross Dam. Option for a longer hike or backpack along Ross Lake."

jewels.name: Sourdough Mountain Trail
jewels.blurb: Mile Post 126: "10.4 miles roundtrip (16.7 km) / 4,870 ft (1,484 m) elevation gain" - "A difficult trail with spectacular views of peaks and lakes."

jewels.name: Hidden Lake Trail
jewels.blurb: Off the Cascade River Road: "9 miles (14.5 km) roundtrip / 2,900 ft (884 m) elevation gain" - "A steep hike to a small mountain lake and historic fire lookout."

jewels.name: Newhalem Creek Campground
jewels.blurb: "Newhalem Campground is a comfortable facility close to town, the Visitor Center, and the Skagit River." The NPS says it "has the most sites for larger RVs" (sites that allow RVs "can generally accommodate a total combined length of 20-50 feet"); RV dump station near the exit in season; "none of the campsites within the park have RV hookups" and no park campground has showers.

jewels.name: Goodell Creek Campground
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov or 1-877-444-6777 in season; first-come, first-served outside it
jewels.blurb: "Goodell Creek Campground is situated in lush, old growth forest on the banks of the Skagit River"; "Goodell Creek - $20 per night". One of the campgrounds that "remain open year-round for first-come, first-served camping outside the operational season with no fee, no water, and no trash services: Goodell Creek (19 sites)".

jewels.name: Lower Goodell Creek Group Campground
jewels.blurb: "Lower Goodell Creek Group campsite is a convenient campground on the banks of Goodell Creek that accommodates large groups." Group campsites can be reserved "one year in advance" on Recreation.gov, against six months for individual sites.

jewels.name: Hozomeen
jewels.blurb: "Visit remote Hozomeen at the north end of Ross Lake"; "Hozomeen campground - Free." Reached only by "The Silver-Skagit Road to Hozomeen", which "provides the only road access to the Ross Lake shoreline. This 37 mile (60 km) gravel road connects with B.C. Highway 1 (Exit 168) near Hope, British Columbia."

jewels.name: Fishing in the Skagit and the park lakes
jewels.booking_route: none needed in the park - a Washington State fishing licence is required (WDFW)
jewels.blurb: "The Skagit River, one of Washington's major watersheds, is home to seven species of anadromous fish (five salmon species, steelhead, and cutthroat trout) and freshwater trout and char." A Washington State licence is required and "Fishing licenses are not sold at any visitor or information station in the park complex, and you must obtain a license before visiting."

jewels.name: Ross Lake Resort
jewels.booking_route: own website accommodation lottery list, plus a last-minute availability table
jewels.blurb: "In existence since 1952, Ross Lake Resort is nestled in the heart of the North Cascade Mountains and is comprised of fifteen floating cabins and a marina"; "There is no road access to Ross Lake Resort." 2026 season June 11 - October 31. It "operates under a concession contract within North Cascades National Park"; cabins are filled by an annual lottery list. The NPS names it as overnight lodging in the park, 206-486-3751.

jewels.name: Ross Lake Resort Equipment Rentals
jewels.booking_route: first-come, first-served reservations with the resort
jewels.blurb: "We rent motorboats, canoes, kayaks, paddle boards, and fishing rods to all visitors to Ross Lake"; "All equipment rentals include life jackets/PFDs." Daily rates read: motor boat $190.00 + tax (fuel included), canoe $80.00 + tax, single kayak $90.00 + tax, double kayak $119.00 + tax. "No day-use motor boat or canoe rentals Friday-Sunday or on holidays"; no canoe or kayak rentals to parties with children under three.

jewels.name: Skagit Tours - Diablo Lake boat tours
jewels.blurb: "North Cascades Institute, in partnership with Seattle City Light, offers visitors fun, interactive tours of the Upper Skagit Valley and North Cascades National Park." The Diablo Lake & Lunch Tour aboard the Alice Ross IV lasts 2.5-3 hours and ran "Wednesday - Sunday, July 3 - September 7" in 2026; afternoon and fall morning cruises last about 2 hours. "Diablo Lake Boat Tours are wheelchair accessible!" (360) 854-2599.

jewels.name: Wildland Trekking - Ross Lake Traverse in the North Cascades
jewels.booking_route: Wildland sells direct - own website or 800-715-4453
jewels.blurb: A guided backpacking trip of "5 Days, 4 Nights", "from $2835": "This multi-day hiking trip in North Cascades National Park begins with a pickup at your hotel in Seattle", along Ruby Arm and over Hidden Hand Pass to Hozomeen Lake. "Group Size 1-5 Guests"; "Trip Begins Seattle, WA"; "Permit applications open on February 1 each year." Wildland also lists a 4-day "Wonders of the North Cascades" and a 3-day "Cascade Pass and Sahale Glacier" trip. Wildland has been owned by Intrepid Travel since 26 January 2022 (handoff/US-PARKS-TOUR-OPERATORS-2026-10-03.json, via Skift).

jewels.name: North Cascades Environmental Learning Center
jewels.booking_route: own website (Base Camp lodging, Conferences & Retreats request form) or (360) 854-2599
jewels.blurb: "A field campus in North Cascades National Park" on the north shore of Diablo Lake, "Operated by North Cascades Institute in partnership with the National Park Service and the City of Seattle": 16 buildings, "Overnight lodging for up to 92 participants", "A lakeside dining hall", "A dock on Diablo Lake for paddling adventures" and "ADA-accessible facilities and pathways"; programmes include "family camps, boat tours, photography and art retreats, conferences and group retreats."

jewels.name: Lady of the Lake (Lake Chelan Boat Company)
jewels.booking_route: own website ticketing (RESERVE YOUR TICKETS NOW)
jewels.blurb: "Year Round Ferry Service To Stehekin, Holden Village, & Upper Lake Chelan": same-day round trips, overnight and one-way tickets, Stehekin activity packages, and private charters "for all occasions: weddings, receptions, birthdays, reunions". The NPS lists the Lake Chelan Boat Company among companies permitted in the park complex, 509-682-4584, and names passenger ferry service "from Chelan on U.S. Route 97".

jewels.name: North Cascades River Expeditions
jewels.blurb: "Family Friendly Whitewater: Upper Skagit", plus Sauk, Methow and Tieton trips; "We thank Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Wenatchee National Forest, and North Cascades National Park for allowing us to operate on their lands." Arlington, WA; 1-800-634-8433. The NPS lists it under "Raft, Float, and Fishing Trips".

jewels.name: North Cascades Mountain Guides
jewels.blurb: Climbing and skiing trips listed under "North Cascades National Park", "Washington Pass", "Mount Shuksan" and "Mazama Rock Climbing", plus AIARE avalanche courses and "Crevasse Rescue and Glacier Travel". The NPS lists it among permitted guides, 509-996-3194.

jewels.name: Winthrop / N. Cascades National Park KOA Holiday
jewels.blurb: "Located at the base of the North Cascades National Park, Winthrop KOA is your basecamp"; "1 mile east of Winthrop on SR 20/Cascade Loop Scenic Hwy", 1114 State Route 20. "Open May 15 to October 25"; "RV Sites with a KOA Patio", "Deluxe Cabins with full baths", "Premium Tent Sites", "Group meeting facilities"; check-in 3:00 pm, check-out 11:00 am. Reserve: 1-509-996-2258.

jewels.name: Pearrygin Lake State Park
jewels.booking_route: Washington State Parks reservations online or (888) 226-7688
jewels.blurb: 625 Bear Creek Rd, Winthrop: "a perfect escape to enjoy camping, hiking, swimming, or even snowshoeing and Nordic skiing. With 1,186 acres to enjoy"; amenities include accessible campsites, showers, a trailer dump, boat ramp and dock; cabins and a vacation house to rent. Discover Pass one-day $10, annual $45. (509) 996-2370.

jewels.name: Bell tent glamping at Pearrygin Lake (Glamping Hub)
jewels.blurb: A Winthrop bell-tent rental "Located directly on the shores of Pearrygin Lake State Park and 1 hour from North Cascades NP"; the site has "three fishing docks, a swimming beach, a kids' playground" and rents kayaks and paddleboards; check-in 2:00-10:00 PM, check-out 11:00 AM. Listed as new with no reviews.

jewels.name: Sun Mountain Lodge
jewels.blurb: Winthrop: "With more than 1,500 acres of magnificent wilderness as your playground and Patterson Lake adjacent to thousands of acres of national forest and the North Cascades National Park, Sun Mountain Lodge offers outdoor adventures year-round"; the Main Lodge, Mt. Gardner and Mt. Robinson buildings and cabins at Patterson Lake; "a spa, multiple dining options, and outdoor adventures including, hiking, skiing, and horseback riding"; meetings and weddings.

jewels.name: Freestone Inn & Cabins
jewels.blurb: "The Freestone Inn is located just 15 miles west of Winthrop in Mazama, Washington"; lodge rooms with gas fireplaces and private decks, and pet-friendly cabins with "apartment-sized kitchens". "Freestone Inn Restaurants are closed indefinitely."

jewels.name: Hampton Inn Chilliwack
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "8050 Lickman Road, Chilliwack, BC V2R 3Z9", "45 miles from North Cascades National Park" - on the British Columbia side, where the NPS says the gravel Silver-Skagit Road to Hozomeen "connects with B.C. Highway 1 (Exit 168) near Hope". Hilton's own page was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Chilliwack
jewels.blurb: Listed by HotelGuides at "8114 Young Road, Chilliwack, BC V2P 0C4", "43 miles from North Cascades National Park" - the British Columbia approach to Hozomeen and Ross Lake. IHG's own page was not fetched, so nothing else about the property is stated here.

jewels.name: Upriver Grill & Taproom
jewels.blurb: 60084 State Rte 20, Marblemount: "we believe that great food starts with fresh, locally sourced ingredients. Our menu features a delightful fusion of classic American dishes and innovative recipes"; open "Monday - Sunday 11 am to 8 pm"; 360.873.4221. The Concrete chamber places it "along Hwy 20 at the western gateway to North Cascades National Park" and notes it is open seasonally.

jewels.name: Mondo Restaurant
jewels.blurb: 60102 State Rte 20, Marblemount: "a cozy, casual eatery... serving a flavorful fusion of American and Korean-inspired cuisine" - "burgers, kimchi-influenced dishes, teriyaki plates, bibimbap, gyoza and more"; listed hours 11:00 AM-8:30 PM Mon-Thu, 8:00 AM-9:00 PM Fri-Sun, "hours may fluctuate seasonally". (Concrete chamber listing; own site not fetched.)

jewels.name: Karina's Deja Brew
jewels.blurb: 60103 State Rte 20, Marblemount: "a charming, locally loved coffee shop and café nestled right on State Route 20" with "freshly brewed espresso drinks, specialty lattes... pastries, light bites, outdoor seating, and casual walk-up or drive-thru service"; (360) 301-6950. (Concrete chamber listing.)

jewels.name: Stehekin Pastry Company
jewels.blurb: "The Pastry Company is where the Valley Gathers. Every delicious item is made by hand"; "If you have been to Stehekin then most likely, you have been to the Pastry Company"; it also rents the Stehekin Log Cabins and does event catering. Reached only by boat, plane or trail, like all of Stehekin.

jewels.name: Old Schoolhouse Brewery
jewels.blurb: Pub at 155 Riverside Avenue, Winthrop - "Come Enjoy Winthrop's Only Riverside Seating" on the Chewuch River - with locations in Twisp and the Mazama Public House "At the Trailhead in Mazama"; open 7 days a week. Brewery 509-996-3183.

jewels.name: Rocking Horse Bakery
jewels.blurb: 265 Riverside Avenue, Winthrop: "Delectable handmade pastries, beautiful, smooth espresso drinks, signature breads, made-from-scratch sandwiches, and salads"; "Whenever possible, we use locally grown or produced ingredients." Current hours read: "open from 7AM to 2PM Thursday through Monday." (509) 996-4241.

jewels.name: Three Fingered Jack's Saloon
jewels.blurb: "For decades, Three Fingered Jack's has been serving locals and visitors in the heart of downtown Winthrop. What started as a historic saloon remains a gathering place"; breakfast Friday-Sunday 7:00-10:30 AM, prime rib every Friday, full bar.

jewels.name: The Mazama Store
jewels.blurb: "A little bit of everything good": 50 Lost River Road, Mazama, open "EVERYDAY 7am-6pm", with an outdoor bakery and espresso area, a weekly bread schedule, and "24 Hour Gas | Diesel | Non-ethanol" - the last fuel before the park's eastern side, where the NPS warns there are no gas stations along State Route 20 within the park. 509-996-2855.

jewels.name: Winthrop
jewels.blurb: The Methow Valley gateway on State Route 20: "The Wild West's last frontier, where every season brings a new adventure"; spring "Vibrant wildflowers offer the perfect backdrop for outdoor enthusiasts to explore our scenic trails"; summer hiking and river rafting.

jewels.name: Bear canister for the canister-only camps
jewels.blurb: The NPS backcountry camp table marks Fisher and Thunder Basin "No Campfires, Bear Canister Required" and Desolation "No Campfires, Bear Canisters Required"; Junction and Heaton Stock list "Hang/Canister". "Backcountry permits are required year-round in North Cascades National Park for all overnight trips."

jewels.name: Warm, waterproof clothing and a tent
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Storms are common: always be prepared for a few days of rain and wind. Warm, waterproof clothing and a tent are necessary for spring, fall and winter trips into the backcountry."

jewels.name: Satellite communicator where cell service fails
jewels.blurb: NPS: "There is limited cell phone reception in the park and cell service should never be relied on." It advises downloading "the official National Park Service app to access the free offline maps" before entering. In Stehekin: "There is no cell phone reception."

jewels.name: Ice axe for Copper Ridge and the high camps
jewels.booking_route: affiliate referral to Black Diamond Equipment (AvantLink)
jewels.blurb: NPS on Copper Ridge: camps "remain snow covered into July"; "Attempting to access the ridge before the snow melts is dangerous. Visitors must be proficient with an ice axe for steep snow fields and be prepared for high creek crossings." At Cascade Pass, hazards include "steep, icy slopes, uncertain river crossings, and flooded or snow-covered camps."

faq.q: Is North Cascades National Park free?
faq.a: Yes. The NPS states: "There is no fee to enter North Cascades National Park Service Complex. There are no trailhead or parking fees for trails that begin on National Park Service lands." Adjacent U.S. Forest Service trailheads can require a Northwest Forest Pass, and campgrounds and backcountry permits carry their own fees.

faq.q: Do you need reservations for North Cascades National Park?
faq.a: Not to enter: "No, there is no reservation system to enter the park. You are welcome to enter and exit the park at any time." Campsites do need one in season: "Camping reservations are required during the operational season (mid-May to early September) and are only available online at recreation.gov or by calling 1-877-444-6777."

faq.q: What is the best time to visit North Cascades National Park?
faq.a: "The best weather for visiting the North Cascades generally occurs between mid-June and late-September. Snow is off all but the highest trails by July." Spring and autumn are "becoming more popular" for car tours "enticing for color and wildlife during the less busy 'shoulder seasons'."

faq.q: Can you camp in North Cascades National Park?
faq.a: Yes. "All drive-in campgrounds along State Route 20 are on a reservation system through recreation.gov" during the season (mid-May to early September); Goodell Creek, Gorge Lake and ten walk-in sites at Colonial Creek South stay open year-round first-come, first-served. "There is no dispersed camping in the park complex", and occupancy is limited to "eight people, three tents, and two vehicles per site."

faq.q: Do you need a permit to backpack in North Cascades National Park?
faq.a: Yes: "Backcountry permits are required year-round in North Cascades National Park for all overnight trips." Reserve on Recreation.gov and pick the permit up the day before the trip, or get a walk-up permit at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.

faq.q: Where can you stay in North Cascades National Park?
faq.a: "Overnight lodging within the park can be found at Ross Lake Resort and the North Cascades Lodge at Stehekin. Other lodging accommodations can be found in the Stehekin and Chelan areas as well as along State Route 20 in the Skagit River Valley west of the park and the Methow River Valley to the east." For 2026 the NPS adds that the North Cascades Lodge at Stehekin "is closed for the 2026 summer season."

faq.q: Can you drive through North Cascades National Park?
faq.a: Yes, in season: "Drive approximately 30 miles across the park on the North Cascades Highway (State Route 20)... Allow at least an hour to drive this beautiful, winding road, and add more time for stops along the way." The NPS says to check road conditions for seasonal closures before arriving.

faq.q: Is North Cascades National Park dog friendly?
faq.a: Only in parts: "Pets are not allowed within the national park except leashed on the Pacific Crest Trail." Leashed pets are allowed within the Ross Lake and Lake Chelan National Recreation Areas, and "pets are welcome in drive in campgrounds and picnic areas". Leashes must be no longer than 6 feet.

faq.q: Where can you shower in North Cascades National Park?
faq.a: Not in the park campgrounds: "No, none of the park campgrounds have showers. However, campers can pay to shower in the local communities. Some private campgrounds outside of the park have shower options for their campers or may have showers available for purchase for non-campers."

faq.q: Can you fish in North Cascades National Park?
faq.a: Yes, under Washington State rules: "Visitors fishing within North Cascades National Park Service Complex must follow the fishing license requirements in accordance with the laws and regulations of the State of Washington." Licences "are not sold at any visitor or information station in the park complex, and you must obtain a license before visiting."

seo.meta_title: North Cascades National Park: Diablo Lake, SR 20 & Stehekin | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: Free entry, the 30-mile North Cascades Highway, Diablo Lake, Cascade Pass, Ross Lake's floating cabins, roadless Stehekin, and where to camp and stay nearby.
