name: Virgin Islands National Park
line: Coral reefs, sugar ruins and Cinnamon Bay

jewels.name: Trunk Bay Underwater Snorkel Trail
jewels.booking_route: pay the Trunk Bay amenity fee on site; facilities open 8 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
jewels.blurb: "the Underwater Snorkel Trial, a great place for beginners and anyone who wants to learn about marine life" - about 300 feet along the west side of Trunk Bay Cay with underwater plaques. Trunk Bay carries the park's only expanded amenity fee: "Individual Day Pass (16 years and older): $5.00", "Interagency Senior Pass: $2.50 for holder". Beach wheelchairs and accessible paths to the water.

jewels.name: Reef Bay Trail
jewels.blurb: "From the trailhead to the beach is about three miles one way"; "a steep strenuous hike" with a 900-foot climb back, past "ancient rock carvings left behind by the pre-Colombian Taino", "Danish sugar plantation ruins" and "stone walls from cattle grazing"; "During rainy season the waterfall can be spectacular."

jewels.name: Annaberg Sugar Plantation
jewels.blurb: On St. John's north shore, remains of an 18th-19th century Danish colonial sugar plantation where over 600 enslaved Africans laboured; the NPS allows "1-2 Hours" and calls it "the park's most accessible historic plantation site." "The trail from the parking lot to the historic district is fairly steep and rocky."

jewels.name: Waterlemon Cay and Leinster Bay
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free; reached on foot
jewels.blurb: Reached by the Leinster Bay Trail, about a 10-minute walk from the Annaberg parking lot: shallow coral heads on a sandy bottom plus deeper drop-offs with blue chromis and sea turtles. The NPS warns snorkellers off the cay's north side for strong currents and to "stand only in sand".

jewels.name: Cinnamon Bay Nature Loop and Accessible Trail
jewels.blurb: "30-60 Minutes": a self-guided walk through a historic sugar plantation site with signs on plantation-era life, bay rum and tyre palm trees; "The first .09 miles of the Cinnamon Nature loop is accessible via the boardwalk... wheelchair and stroller friendly."

jewels.name: Reef Bay Guided Hike
jewels.booking_route: FareHarbor link on the NPS ranger-programmes page
jewels.blurb: A ranger-led "interpretive guided hike that will explore the history and culture of St. John", "just under 3 miles one way", a "STRENUOUS hike" past the petroglyph site and sugar ruins, returning by a "40-minute boat cruise" to Cruz Bay; check-in 7:45 AM at the Visitor Center; bring sturdy shoes, 2-3 liters of water, lunch and sunscreen.

jewels.name: Francis Bay Boardwalk and beach
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free boardwalk and beach
jewels.blurb: "a wheelchair accessible boardwalk to a beautiful salt pond, perfect for bird viewing"; the NPS rates Francis Bay ideal for beginner snorkellers in calm water. Friends of Virgin Islands National Park leads a Francis Bay Bird Walk on Fridays at 7:30am from October 9, 2026 (friendsvinp.org).

jewels.name: Maho Bay sea turtles
jewels.blurb: Named by the NPS for sea turtle sightings in its seagrass beds; Salomon and Honeymoon bays, also on the NPS list, add white-sand beaches and fringing reefs.

jewels.name: Ram Head Guided Hike
jewels.booking_route: seasonal dates on the park's calendar of events; booking method not stated on the page read
jewels.blurb: A ranger-led "intermediate hike just under 2 and a half miles" from the Salt Pond Bay parking lot, "rocky and steep in some areas", telling the story of the "1733 African Revolution"; run on "seasonal dates on the calendar of events". The NPS: "In the early morning of November 23, 1733, a small group of enslaved people entered the Danish West India Company's fort in Coral Bay" (the-1733-akwamu-insurrection.htm).

jewels.name: Night Sky in the Park
jewels.booking_route: none stated - meet at Cinnamon Bay on the published evenings
jewels.blurb: A ranger programme at Cinnamon Bay Beach and Campground "every other Wednesday at 8:15pm, November through May"; the NPS recommends a flashlight, long pants and insect repellent.

jewels.name: Cruz Bay Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: "1300 Cruz Bay Creek, St. John, VI 00830", 340-776-6201; "Monday-Thursday 8:15 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Friday 8:15 a.m. to 1:30 p.m."; exhibits include coral displays and "a raised-relief map of St. John"; "wheelchair-accessible entrance, parking, and restrooms". The Friends of the park run the retail store here.

jewels.name: Junior Ranger programme
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free at the Visitor Center
jewels.blurb: Ask a ranger at the Cruz Bay Visitor Center desk for the workbook: "When you bring your Junior Ranger workbook back to the visitor center, you'll get your Junior Ranger badge and be awarded the Junior Ranger program certificate." Fourth graders collect their Every Kid in a Park pass at the same desk.

jewels.name: Hawksnest Beach
jewels.blurb: "wheelchair-accessible parking, restrooms, changing rooms, and accessible paths to water"; the NPS advises "It is not advisable to snorkel directly over the reef" here - keep to the reef perimeters.

jewels.name: Overnight moorings in the park
jewels.booking_route: Recreation.gov mobile app at park pay stations
jewels.blurb: "Regular overnight fee: $26.00/night"; "Senior/Access Pass: $13.00/night". The NPS: "Visitors are encouraged to use the recreation.gov mobile app to pay overnight mooring fees" by QR code at pay stations; boat exclusion areas are set in the Superintendent's Compendium.

jewels.name: Trunk Bay Cafe and Bar
jewels.blurb: One of the two cafes inside the park: "Trunk Bay Café and Bar at Trunk Bay". The Snack Shack and Bar operate "10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m." (NPS hours page).

jewels.name: Reef-safe sunscreen for the reefs
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Please Use Reef Safe Sunscreen!" The park tells snorkellers to check the ingredient list for chemicals such as oxybenzone and octocrylene that cause coral bleaching, because a "reef safe" label alone is no guarantee; the hiking page asks for reef-safe sunscreen too.

jewels.name: Water for the trail - half a gallon per four hours
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Bring plenty of water and snacks, ½ gal of water for each four hours of hiking is minimum recommendation." Wear "cool, loose clothing and comfortable sturdy walking or hiking shoes"; "Many trails have limited (or no) cell phone access!"

jewels.name: Closed-toe shoes and repellent for Reef Bay
jewels.blurb: NPS kit for the Reef Bay Trail: "Sturdy, closed-toe shoes", "plenty of water, some snacks and a lunch, and a hat", "Mosquito repellent" and "a swimsuit if you'd like to take a dip"; the surface "can be slippery even when dry."

jewels.name: Cinnamon Bay Beach & Campground - bare and group sites
jewels.booking_route: own website booking (bookings10.rmscloud.com) or 340-714-7144; groups by email
jewels.blurb: "the only designated campground on St. John" (USVI tourism board), inside the park on the North Shore. Bare sites "Include a wood platform with rain cover, picnic table and charcoal grill", "2 adults and 2 kids max"; bare sites with a 4-person tent and comfort kit; group tents where "Each tent has two twin bunks and can sleep 4 people", reserved through groups@cinnamonbayvi.com. Two-night minimum on pre-reserved stays; closed Sept. 1 - Oct. 31.

jewels.name: Cinnamon Bay eco-tents and cottages
jewels.blurb: Eco-tents: "Each rental has a fan, light, electric outlet, queen size bed, linens, bath towels, cooking kit, picnic table, chairs on the porch and can comfortably sleep 2 people"; family eco-tents add twin bunks and "can sleep 4 people". Concrete cottages for 4 with "ceiling fans/lights, electric outlet, a queen bed, day bed/sofa (w/trundle)... mini fridge, grill". Direct access to Cinnamon Bay Beach.

jewels.name: Rain Tree Cafe and the Cinnamon Bay food truck
jewels.blurb: At Cinnamon Bay Beach & Campground: the Rain Tree Cafe serves breakfast and dinner daily and a food truck serves lunch, drinks and ice cream. The NPS: "meals are served in an open-air dining hall and grab and go food and beverage items are also available in the Cinnamon Bay food truck near the beach."

jewels.name: Cinnamon Bay watersports rentals
jewels.booking_route: on site at Cinnamon Bay; info@cinnamonbayvi.com
jewels.blurb: "Cinnamon Bay Beach & Campground offers on-site kayak, paddleboard, snorkel gear and chair rentals" (USVI tourism board); the campground's own site lists kayaks, paddleboards, snorkel gear and beach chairs. Bare-site campers can reserve limited rental items in advance.

jewels.name: Caribbean Dreams: Exploring the U.S. & British Virgin Islands in 10 Days
jewels.blurb: A 10-day small-group tour by Across Caribbean Excursions sold on TourRadar, group size 2-8, "All Ages Welcome": it starts in Charlotte Amalie, ferries to St. John, and day 3 includes "Hike Reef Bay Trail or explore sugar plantation ruins" and "Snorkeling at Trunk Bay and Cinnamon Bay" in Virgin Islands National Park, then on by boat to Tortola. Accommodation, guide, select meals and transport included; flights and insurance not.

jewels.name: Virgin Islands Ecotours
jewels.blurb: Guided kayak, hike and snorkel trips on three islands, including "Sea Turtle Kayak & Snorkel - North Shore St. John" (3 hours, from $119), "The Best of St. John: Kayak, Snorkel & Beach Picnic" (5 hours, from $159) and "Coral Bay Kayak, Turtles & Tacos" (3 hours, from $89); kayak, SUP and snorkel-gear rentals. St. John base: 520 Mongoose Jct, Cruz Bay; (340) 779-2155.

jewels.name: Cruz Bay Watersports
jewels.blurb: "Snorkel, Sail, Jet Ski and Day Trip to the British Virgin Islands from St. Thomas and St." John; departures from The Ritz-Carlton St. Thomas and Westin Frenchman's Reef/St. John; private yacht and catamaran charters; over 30 years in the islands. (340) 244-1493. The USVI tourism board: its catamarans let you "slip into the water at an unspoiled cay, diverse reef or off-the-beaten-path snorkeling spot".

jewels.name: VI SNUBA Excursions
jewels.blurb: USVI tourism board: "exciting tours that are a cross between snorkeling and scuba diving around the reefs of Trunk Bay" (visnuba.com). Own page not fetched in this build.

jewels.name: Ocean Surfari
jewels.blurb: USVI tourism board: "Join an Ocean Surfari snorkeling excursion aboard the 47-foot Reef Surfari that takes guests for outings throughout Virgin Islands National Park". Own page not fetched in this build.

jewels.name: Red Hook - Cruz Bay passenger ferry
jewels.blurb: Run by "Transportation Services & Varlack Ventures" ((340) 776-6282 and (340) 776-6412): "Non-Resident One-way $8.15", "Child (2-11) One-way $1"; weekday departures from Red Hook from 5:30 am to 11:30 pm. A Charlotte Amalie - Cruz Bay service leaves Charlotte Amalie at "10:00 am, 3:00 pm, 5:30 pm" (subject to seasonal change).

jewels.name: Red Hook - Cruz Bay car barges
jewels.booking_route: operator online tickets or at the barge
jewels.blurb: Operators named by the Virgin Islands Port Authority: Big Red Barge, Global Marine LLC (Tug Life) and Love City Car Ferries; non-resident one-way "$50", round trip to "$65"; "Purchasing your ticket online does not guarantee a spot on any barge at a specific time."

jewels.name: Mongoose Junction, Cruz Bay
jewels.blurb: USVI tourism board: a "mosaic of stone walls and shaded courtyards" in Cruz Bay, with Made in St. John ("sells clothing designed and screen-printed on the island") and the St. John Experience Gallery; Wharfside Village on the waterfront has shops "specializing in handmade jewelry and gifts".

jewels.name: St. John Brewers Tap Room
jewels.blurb: "Local craft beers, sodas and our Green Flash energy drink" made on St. John; the Tap Room is on the "2nd Floor Mongoose Junction, Cruz Bay", "Open Daily 12 PM TO 9 PM", "Serving Food 12 PM TO 8 PM"; +1 340-715-7775.

jewels.name: Lime Out
jewels.booking_route: first-come for dining; shuttles booked through the own website
jewels.blurb: "A floating taco and cocktail bar anchored in the bay" in Coral Bay, boat access only, with floating lily pads and a swim-up bar; 10:30 AM to 4:30 PM, Sunday through Friday (closed Saturdays until mid-December). From St. John the Salt + Lime Express shuttle leaves Coral Bay's dinghy dock ($30/person); from St. Thomas the Taco Taxi from Emerald Beach. No dining reservations. (340) 643-5333.

jewels.name: The Lime Inn
jewels.booking_route: walk-in (no reservation method on the page)
jewels.blurb: "Tasty tacos & handcrafted tacos in the heart of Cruz Bay" - the land-based sister of Lime Out; "OPEN SUNDAY THRU FRIDAY / 3:00 PM - 9:00 PM [CLOSED SATURDAYS]", happy hour 3:00-5:00 PM; info@limeinn.com.

jewels.name: Ocean 362 at Gallows Point Resort
jewels.blurb: "modern Caribbean cuisine with fresh, local ingredients, complemented by stunning sunset views over the ocean", on the Gallows Point peninsula in Cruz Bay; seasonal, with limited September availability. The USVI tourism board: "an airy terrace just above Cruz Bay".

jewels.name: Gallows Point Resort
jewels.blurb: "The only resort in Cruz Bay, St. John offering oceanfront accommodations": 5 acres on a peninsula a 5-minute walk from town; one-bedroom suites facing Pillsbury Sound or Cruz Bay Harbor, each with king bed and full kitchen; complimentary ferry shuttle, 24/7 reception.

jewels.name: The Westin St. John Resort Villas
jewels.blurb: USVI tourism board: "Roomy villas and townhouses are perched up in the hills, but convenient shuttles make them easy to access"; placed "near Cruz Bay" in the board's St. John itinerary.

jewels.name: Lovango Resort & Beach Club
jewels.blurb: USVI tourism board: "Book a villa, cottage or air-conditioned treehouse with spectacular views high above the island." Own page not fetched in this build.

jewels.name: The Ritz-Carlton, St. Thomas
jewels.blurb: USVI tourism board: "The ultimate luxury destination, with its immaculate beach, tropical landscaping and stunning views across Great Bay to St. John"; a "five-star hotel's private white-sand beach along Great Bay". Cruz Bay Watersports departs from the resort. Marriott's own page was not fetched (brand pages refuse automated reads), so nothing else is stated.

jewels.name: The Westin Beach Resort & Spa at Frenchman's Reef
jewels.blurb: USVI tourism board: "A modern, airy take on classic island living", with views of "bright-blue Morningstar Bay" on St. Thomas. Cruz Bay Watersports departs from Westin Frenchman's Reef. Marriott's own page was not fetched, so nothing else is stated.

jewels.name: Morningstar Buoy Haus Beach Resort at Frenchman's Reef, Autograph Collection
jewels.blurb: USVI tourism board: a "private beach hugging the coastline of Morningstar Bay just steps from your villa-style guest room" on St. Thomas. A Marriott Autograph Collection property by its own name; Marriott's page was not fetched, so nothing else is stated.

jewels.name: Marriott's Frenchman's Cove
jewels.blurb: USVI tourism board: "Two- and three-bedroom villas are comfortable and family friendly, with kitchens and dining rooms"; a "multicolored, multistory" resort that "commands unmatched views of Pacquereau Bay from its hillside perch" on St. Thomas.

jewels.name: Bolongo Bay Beach Resort
jewels.blurb: USVI tourism board: "This all-inclusive boutique resort on the southern coast of St. Thomas offers comfortable rooms with either beach access or stunning views." Own page not fetched in this build.

jewels.name: Friends of Virgin Islands National Park
jewels.booking_route: via friendsvinp.org (booking procedure not stated on the page read)
jewels.blurb: A 501(c)(3) founded in 1988 that runs the Reef Bay hike, a Francis Bay Bird Walk (Fridays 7:30am from October 9, 2026), seminars, demonstrations and boat trips October-June, youth programmes (Learn to Swim, Learn to Fish, summer camps), a snorkelling app, and the retail store at the Visitor Center. (340) 779-4940.

faq.q: How do I get to Virgin Islands National Park?
faq.a: The NPS: "You will need to fly to St. Thomas and take a ferry over. There is a ferry for pedestrians and a car barge as well."

faq.q: Is there a ferry from St. Thomas to Virgin Islands National Park?
faq.a: Yes. The Virgin Islands Port Authority lists the Red Hook - Cruz Bay passenger ferry run by "Transportation Services & Varlack Ventures", "Non-Resident One-way $8.15", with weekday departures from Red Hook from 5:30 am to 11:30 pm, and a Charlotte Amalie - Cruz Bay service leaving Charlotte Amalie at "10:00 am, 3:00 pm, 5:30 pm" (subject to seasonal change). Car barges also run Red Hook - Cruz Bay.

faq.q: Can you camp in Virgin Islands National Park?
faq.a: Yes, at Cinnamon Bay. The NPS: "The campground is open seasonally. Make reservations by visiting Cinnamon Bay Resort & Campground's official website." Its sites range from bare platforms to eco-tents and cottages.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Virgin Islands National Park?
faq.a: The NPS states: "The park is busiest from November to April in a typical year." For the hurricane window, NOAA: "The Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 to November 30" (nhc.noaa.gov/climo).

faq.q: How many acres is Virgin Islands National Park?
faq.a: "Virgin Islands National Park is comprised of 7,259 acres of terrestrial habitat, which is about 60%, of the island's land mass. The park also includes 5,650 acres of adjacent submerged lands."

faq.q: Is Virgin Islands National Park open?
faq.a: The park is "Open year-round 24 hours a day." The Visitor Center is open "Monday-Thursday 8:15 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Friday 8:15 a.m. to 1:30 p.m." and closed Thanksgiving Day, December 25 and July 4; Trunk Bay facilities open "8 a.m. to 4:00 p.m."

faq.q: Where is the Virgin Islands National Park visitor center?
faq.a: At "1300 Cruz Bay Creek, St. John, VI 00830", phone 340-776-6201.

faq.q: What is there for kids in Virgin Islands National Park?
faq.a: The Junior Ranger programme: ask a ranger at the Cruz Bay Visitor Center for the workbook, and "When you bring your Junior Ranger workbook back to the visitor center, you'll get your Junior Ranger badge and be awarded the Junior Ranger program certificate." Fourth graders collect their Every Kid in a Park pass at the same desk.

faq.q: Does the Virgin Islands have all-inclusive resorts?
faq.a: The USVI tourism board lists Bolongo Bay Beach Resort: "This all-inclusive boutique resort on the southern coast of St. Thomas offers comfortable rooms with either beach access or stunning views."

seo.meta_title: Virgin Islands National Park: Trunk Bay, Reef Bay & Cinnamon Bay | TravelWell
seo.meta_description: No entrance fee, Trunk Bay's underwater snorkel trail, the Reef Bay petroglyph hike, Cinnamon Bay camping, and the ferry from St. Thomas to St. John.

name: American Samoa National Park
line: Paleotropical rainforest, Ofu lagoon and Mount 'Alava

jewels.name: Mount 'Alava Trail
jewels.blurb: "Enjoy hiking through a tropical Samoan rainforest with fruit bats and many types of birds. Along the trail you'll see the park's efforts to remove invasive trees and plant native species. About halfway up the trail is a banana and coconut plantation." "Distance: 7 mi / 11.3 km roundtrip"; "The trailhead is located at Fagasā Pass, 1.2 miles from Route 001 in Pago Pago."

jewels.name: Ofu lagoon and Ofu Beach
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free; reached by Samoa Airways flight or boat to Manu'a
jewels.blurb: "The Ofu island unit has a shallow protected reef with a great diversity of coral cover and fish. This is a feast for the eyes in the morning light. Keep an eye out for octopus and sea turtles." "Ofu island's south beach is consistently featured in travel publications as the quintessential tropical paradise." The NPS adds: "Be aware of the location of rip currents (avas) wherever you swim."

jewels.name: Mount 'Alava Adventure Trail
jewels.blurb: "This challenging loop trail takes you along ridgelines with views of the north and central parts of the national park and island. Hike up and down 'ladders' or steps with ropes for balance. There are a total of 56 ladders and 783 steps!" It reaches the summit and descends to Vatia Village. "Distance: 5.6 mi / 9 km roundtrip".

jewels.name: Lower Sauma Ridge Trail and overlook
jewels.blurb: "This interpretive trail takes you to Samoan archeological sites. Along the trail are exhibits and spectacular views of the northeast coastline of the island and the Vai'ava Strait National Natural Landmark. Visible looking north is the tall and skinny Pola Island, a nesting area for seabirds." "Distance: 0.4 mi / 0.6 km roundtrip". Its overlook is the one the NPS calls "accessible with assistance".

jewels.name: Pola Island Trail, Vatia
jewels.blurb: "This short, fairly flat trail leads to a rough and rocky beach with views of the coastline and Pola Island." "Distance: 0.1 mi / 0.2 km roundtrip". "Due to unfriendly dogs, please drive past the last house at the end of the paved road in Vatia Village. This rough section of road will lead you to three exhibits and the trailhead."

jewels.name: Tuafanua Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free park trail; closed Sundays
jewels.blurb: "Hike up switchbacks from Vatia Village through lush tropical rainforest to a hidden coastline. At the ridge-top, enjoy ocean views before a steep descent on several ladders with ropes to a quiet, rocky beach and view of Pola Island." "This trail is closed on Sundays." "Distance: 2.2 mi / 3.5 km roundtrip". "WARNING: Do not to enter the ocean at the beach due to dangerous waves and currents."

jewels.name: Lata Mountain, Ta'u
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park land; the NPS says local park guides are often available for Manu'a trails
jewels.blurb: "The highest point in American Samoa (3,170 feet/966 meters), lies near the center of Ta'ū island where it is almost always draped with a cloud. The mossy cloud forest environment supports a large community of ground and tree ferns."

jewels.name: Laufuti Falls and the Ta'u sea cliffs
jewels.booking_route: none needed - park land; contact the park about Manu'a guides
jewels.blurb: "The south side of Ta'ū is a volcanic caldera. Steep walls formed when it collapsed. Laufuti Stream flows along an intermediate bench between walls before its route takes it off the cliffs at the coast. This waterfall is dramatic after heavy rain, but much of the time is just a trickle." The Laufuti Falls trail is among those the NPS calls "minimally maintained and challenging".

jewels.name: Si'u Point Trail and the Sau'a site
jewels.blurb: "This trail follows an old road in the coastal forest past the culturally important Saua site to the southeast tip of Ta'ū island." "Distance: 5.7 mi / 9.2 km roundtrip". The NPS: "The Sau'a Site on Ta'ū island is one important area that is associated with the legends of the origins of Polynesian culture."

jewels.name: Oge Beach Trail, Olosega
jewels.blurb: "This trail traverses the shoulder between Mata'ala Ridge and Maga Point, where boobies and frigate birds are often seen. Follow the trail down slope past Maga Point to emerge at Oge, a remote coral rubble beach that faces Ta'ū." "This trail is maintained in partnership with the village of Olosega." "Distance: 2.7 mi / 4.3 km roundtrip".

jewels.name: World War II Heritage Trail
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free trail; Tour American Samoa also lists a guided "WWII Heritage Tour"
jewels.blurb: "Hike past multiple World War II installations that helped protect American Samoa from a Japanese invasion. Also, enjoy the tropical rainforest and listen to native bird songs. Along the last section of the trail, experience many steep 'ladders' or steps with ropes that end where a tramway used to transport visitors to the summit of Mount 'Alava." "Distance: 1.7 mi / 2.7 km roundtrip".

jewels.name: Fruit bats and native birds of the rainforest
jewels.blurb: "Bats are the only native mammals found in American Samoa. The two species of fruit bat and one insect-eating bat species are harmless to people. They have a wingspan close to three feet." On Manu'a: "Manu'a is home to several birds not found on Tutuila—the Blue-crowned Lory, Friendly ground dove, and the elusive Spotless crake."

jewels.name: Humpback whales off Manu'a
jewels.booking_route: none needed - seen from shore; Pago Pago Marine Charters sells whale watching
jewels.blurb: "Southern humpback whales are a frequent sight from August through November. During this season, mother-calf pairs can be seen playing just beyond the surf break."

jewels.name: National Park visitor center and park store, Pago Pago
jewels.blurb: "open on weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m." and "closed on weekends and federal holidays" (park web page). The Visitor Guide places it "in Pago Pago, across from the Pago Way Service Station" with "Exhibits", "Cultural Videos", "Restrooms", "Park Store", "First Aid" and "Information"; "Park rangers are available throughout the day to help you plan a safe and memorable visit". Visitor center and restrooms are accessible.

jewels.name: Junior Ranger programme
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free at the visitor center or by mail
jewels.blurb: "The free Junior Ranger Activity Book is a great way to have fun and learn about the National Park of American Samoa and the National Park Service. When you finish, see a park ranger at the visitor center or mail your activity book to the national park. We'll check it and send your book back to you along with your certificate and badge."

jewels.name: Stargazing in Manu'a
jewels.blurb: "Away from major light pollution, enjoy the constellations of the Southern Hemisphere and clear views of the Milky Way."

jewels.name: Water for the trail - two to three liters
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Never hike without water; carry two to three liters per person." "Ask the visitor center about trail conditions."

jewels.name: Sun protection - sunglasses, sunscreen, hat
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Solar radiation is intense! Wear sunglasses, sunscreen, a hat, and protective clothing."

jewels.name: Insect repellent and snorkel-partner kit
jewels.blurb: NPS: "Carry insect repellent." "Always snorkel with a partner." "Coral rubble beaches are difficult to walk on—watch your step. Rocky areas can be slippery." "Don't touch the coral! Cuts from coral take a long time to heal."

jewels.name: Ofu Ranger Station
jewels.blurb: "The Ofu Ranger Station is also open to the public by advanced appointment only." The NPS Visitor Guide notes that "The Ofu lagoons and the National Park Service Research Lab are a hot spot for scientific research on the effects of climate change on coral reefs."

jewels.name: Tradewinds Hotel
jewels.blurb: "A tropical haven where you find the peace and relaxation that you deserve, all in style and comfort with superior service reflecting the spirit of American Samoa." Ottoville Road, minutes from Pago Pago Airport with complimentary airport transfers; outdoor pool, spa, gym and conference facilities; the Equator Bar & Restaurant. Independent - no chain affiliation on the page read. 1.684.699.1000.

jewels.name: Sadie's by the Sea, Utulei
jewels.blurb: "Beach-front property featuring private beach, snorkeling, kayak rentals, full-service casual dining, swimming pool and meeting rooms", centrally located near the dock and government offices. The tourism board: "Charming beachfront hotel in Utulei, perfect for swimming, snorkeling, and kayaking".

jewels.name: Sadie Thompson Inn, Fagatogo
jewels.blurb: On Pago Pago Harbor, "home to Sadie's Restaurant, American Samoa's finest restaurant" (own claim); a historic building from the early 20th century with standard rooms and apartments with full kitchens. The tourism board: "Historic charm in Fagatogo with cozy rooms, a restaurant, and a welcoming atmosphere".

jewels.name: Tisa's beach fales, Alega
jewels.blurb: The American Samoa Visitors Bureau: "Authentic experience with beachfront fales, traditional feasts, and eco-friendly stays" in Alega Village. Tisa's own site: "World Famous Tisa's Barefoot World in American Samoa. Located at her pristine, exclusive beach and Marine Sanctuary in Alega Village." tisa@tisasbarefootbar.com, +1.684.622.7447. Fale details and prices are not on the pages read.

jewels.name: Moana O Sina, Tafuna
jewels.blurb: The American Samoa Visitors Bureau: "Upscale coastal B&B in Tafuna with elegant ensuite rooms, Polynesian charm, tropical gardens, oceanfront pool". Tel +1-684-699-8517, reservations@moanaosina.com. Own page not fetched in this build.

jewels.name: Le Falepule
jewels.blurb: The American Samoa Visitors Bureau: "Boutique stay with terrace views, ensuite Samoan-style rooms, tropical breakfast, peaceful escape". Tel +1-684-733-7042, proprietor.mos@gmail.com. Location not stated on the page read; own page not fetched.

jewels.name: Pago Airport Inn
jewels.blurb: The American Samoa Visitors Bureau: "Conveniently located near the airport, offering clean, comfortable rooms surrounded by lush trees". Listed with a Facebook page only; own page not fetched.

jewels.name: Gods of Sand, Aunu'u
jewels.blurb: The Visitors Bureau: "Surf and island tours with lodging, gear, transport, and authentic Aunu'u experiences." Own booking page: a "studio apartment with two doubles or 1 king, a shared bathroom, and sink area" on Aunu'u; surf sessions with "Transport to and from is included, 1.5 hours minimum per session"; island tours, car rentals, snorkelling, diving, fishing and cliff jumping also listed. No prices on the page.

jewels.name: Pago Pago Marine Charters
jewels.blurb: "Game Fishing, Scuba Diving, Whale Watching or site seeing tours" plus "snorkeling, island coastal excursions, trips to neighbor islands and scientific excursions" aboard the 50ft catamaran Double Hooked and the 39ft Double Barrel; "The boats of Pago Pago Marine Charters are the only privately owned commercial vessels capable of making the long trips to Swains and Rose." Certified instructors with full equipment rentals and a hyperbaric chamber.

jewels.name: Tour American Samoa - National Park + Tisa's Barefoot Bar
jewels.blurb: "5.5 hours", "$235 per person", "maximum is 8 people": Vatia village and the Pola Island views, beach access, lunch and snorkel time. Same operator (Best Tours, "Customizable, cruise-friendly American Samoa adventures" per the Visitors Bureau) runs the 3.5-hour "Aiga Bus Scenic Tour" ("USD $75 per person") via Afono Pass and Vatia, plus "National Park Plus Tour", "Mt. Alava Plus Adventure" and "WWII Heritage Tour" for non-cruise guests.

jewels.name: Aunu'u Island Cultural Excursion
jewels.blurb: Tour American Samoa: "4-5 Hours", "USD $195 per person", "Authentic Samoan lunch and activities", by ferry to Aunu'u; the "minimum is 20 passengers"; "not available on Sundays or religious holidays". The NPS on Aunu'u: "The one mile trip to the island costs one dollar per person. The ferry may stop running mid-day, so make sure you know when your captain will return."

jewels.name: North Shore Tours
jewels.blurb: The American Samoa Visitors Bureau: "Wilderness and coastal excursions across American Samoa, destination hikes, remote beaches, wildlife, and tides." Facebook page only; not fetched.

jewels.name: Alofas Tours
jewels.blurb: The American Samoa Visitors Bureau: "Family-run tours showcasing American Samoa's culture, traditions, villages, and scenic landscapes." Facebook page only; not fetched.

jewels.name: America Samoa Tours & Travel
jewels.blurb: The American Samoa Visitors Bureau: "Trusted Pago Pago guides delivering scenic, cultural, and heritage-rich day excursions." Phone (684) 256-9383.

jewels.name: Equator Bar & Restaurant, Tradewinds Hotel
jewels.blurb: At the Tradewinds Hotel: American and Samoan cuisine, "including traditional UMU-cooked dishes and raw tuna preparations (Samoan OKA)".

jewels.name: Sadie's Restaurant, Sadie Thompson Inn
jewels.blurb: At the Sadie Thompson Inn on Pago Pago Harbor, which calls it "American Samoa's finest restaurant" (the operator's own claim).

jewels.name: Goat Island Cafe, Sadie's by the Sea
jewels.booking_route: walk-in at Sadie's by the Sea
jewels.blurb: One of the restaurants Sadie's Hotels names on its own site (Sadie's Restaurant, Goat Island Cafe, Rubble's 2.0 "coming soon"); Sadie's by the Sea offers "full-service casual dining" on its beachfront. Menu and hours not on the page read.

jewels.name: Tisa's Barefoot Bar
jewels.blurb: "put up your aching feet and indulge in Tisa's famous homemade Pina Kolada, and allow the spirit of nature to restore your inner peace." A "Samoan Feast" is listed among its special events (no day or time on the page). Alega Village, 14.2710 S, 170.1322 W.

jewels.name: Fagatogo Marketplace
jewels.blurb: The American Samoa Visitors Bureau: "Savor traditional Samoan dishes like palusami and taro" at the Fagatogo Marketplace. The NPS: aiga buses "originate and terminate at the market in Fagatogo, the village next to Pago Pago."

jewels.name: National Marine Sanctuary of American Samoa and Fagatele Bay
jewels.booking_route: none needed - ask the landowning family for trail access
jewels.blurb: NOAA: the sanctuary "comprises six protected areas covering 13,581 square miles of nearshore coral reef and open ocean across the Samoan archipelago"; Fagatele Bay was designated in April 1986. The NPS Fagatele Bay Trail is "located outside of the national park, on private land" - "Turtles, whales, sharks, and giant clams all find refuge in this protected area" - and "The family might charge a fee."

jewels.name: Tauese P.F. Sunia Ocean Center
jewels.blurb: The American Samoa Visitors Bureau: "marine exhibits and interactive learning". The NPS Visitor Guide map places the Ocean Center and the National Marine Sanctuary of American Samoa in Utulei on Pago Pago Harbor. Hours not on the pages read.

jewels.name: Jean P. Haydon Museum, Fagatogo
jewels.blurb: The American Samoa Visitors Bureau: in Fagatogo, with "moon rocks and Apollo mission exhibits". Hours not on the page read.

jewels.name: Aunu'u Island
jewels.blurb: The American Samoa Visitors Bureau: reached by "local alia boat 1.2 miles from Tutuila". The NPS lists 'Aunu'u Island among the seven National Natural Landmarks designated in 1972: "Drive the coast east to the village of 'Au'asi and take the 'Aunu'u island ferry. The one mile trip to the island costs one dollar per person."

jewels.name: Pago Pago Harbor and Rainmaker Mountain
jewels.blurb: The Visitors Bureau names Pago Pago Harbor a scenic viewpoint featuring "Rainmaker Mountain". The NPS: Matafao Peak and Rainmaker Mountain, National Natural Landmarks on opposite sides of the harbor, "are two of five great masses of volcanic rocks extruded as molten magma during major episodes of volcanism which created Tutuila Island." "Rainmaker Mountain is easily viewed from the west side of Pago Pago Harbor. For a closer view, drive to Āfono Pass".

jewels.name: Blunts Point gun batteries
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free trail outside the park
jewels.blurb: "These trails are located outside of the national park. Located at the top of these points are gun batteries that protected Pago Pago Harbor after the bombing of Pearl Harbor in 1941." Blunts Point Trail: "Distance: 0.6 mi / 1 km roundtrip", between Faga'alu and Utulei; "Look for the sign next to the IBM Laundromat". Breakers Point "is closed on Sundays".

jewels.name: Cape Taputapu
jewels.blurb: A National Natural Landmark: "Cape Taputapu offers the best illustration in American Samoa of wave action on older massive volcanic activity which created Tutuila Island." "Drive the coast road west to the village of 'Āmanave... The cape is about a mile walk along the shoreline. Only hike at low tide."

jewels.name: Fogama'a Crater - TEMPORARILY CLOSED
jewels.booking_route: none - temporarily closed per the NPS
jewels.blurb: 🔴 CLOSED as the NPS states it: "Note: Temporarily closed. Contact the national park at 684-633-7082 for more information." A National Natural Landmark: "Fogama'a Crater is one of the very few illustrations of the most recent volcanism in American Samoa". Listed so Atlas can say it is closed; never offered as a stop.

jewels.name: Hawaiian Airlines, Honolulu - Pago Pago
jewels.blurb: The American Samoa Visitors Bureau: "Flights from Honolulu to Pago Pago operate twice weekly year-round, with additional flights during North American summer, Christmas, and New Year", on a 294-seat A330-200. The NPS: the park is "accessible via flights into Pago Pago International Airport on the island of Tutuila."

jewels.name: Samoa Airways and Talofa Airways - Apia and Manu'a flights
jewels.blurb: The Visitors Bureau: Samoa Airways flies "direct from Fagalii, Samoa, to Pago Pago, American Samoa, daily (9-12 flights)" plus inter-island service to Manu'a "four times weekly using 19-seat Twin Otter aircraft"; Talofa Airways offers "six daily flights" from Samoa and "two weekly flights from Nuku'alofa, Tonga." The bureau also names the "Manu'atele Ferry" between Tutuila and Manu'a. ⚠️ The undated NPS Visitor Guide names Polynesian Airlines as Manu'a's only carrier - the bureau's current page is used.

faq.q: How do I get to American Samoa National Park?
faq.a: The NPS: "Located some 2,600 miles southwest of Hawai'i," the park is "accessible via flights into Pago Pago International Airport on the island of Tutuila." Smaller regional flights connect to Ta'u and Ofu.

faq.q: What airlines fly to American Samoa?
faq.a: The American Samoa Visitors Bureau names Hawaiian Airlines ("Flights from Honolulu to Pago Pago operate twice weekly year-round, with additional flights during North American summer, Christmas, and New Year"), Samoa Airways ("direct from Fagalii, Samoa, to Pago Pago, American Samoa, daily (9-12 flights)", and to Manu'a four times weekly) and Talofa Airways ("six daily flights" from Samoa and "two weekly flights from Nuku'alofa, Tonga").

faq.q: What island is American Samoa National Park on?
faq.a: Three. The NPS: "The national park includes sections of three islands—Tutuila, Ta'ū, and Ofu." "About 4,000 acres of the national park is underwater, offshore from all three islands."

faq.q: When is the best time to visit American Samoa National Park?
faq.a: The NPS describes two seasons: "The long, wet summer season (October to May) brings frequent rain showers and the potential for tropical storms, while the cooler, drier season (June to September) offers more temperate weather." Its Visitor Guide adds that southern humpback whales "are a frequent sight from August through November."

faq.q: Can you camp in American Samoa National Park?
faq.a: Only with a permit. The park compendium: "Camping is only allowed by permit with prior permission of the Superintendent."

faq.q: Where can I stay near American Samoa National Park?
faq.a: There is no lodge in the park. The American Samoa Visitors Bureau lists, on Tutuila: Tradewinds Hotel near the airport, Sadie's by the Sea in Utulei, Sadie Thompson Inn in Fagatogo, Pago Airport Inn, Tisa's beachfront fales in Alega, Moana O Sina in Tafuna, Le Falepule, and Airbnb stays.

faq.q: When was American Samoa National Park established?
faq.a: The park's laws-and-policies page cites "Public Law 100-571 – October 31, 1988" as establishing the park and "Public Law 107-336 – December 16, 2002" as expanding it. The NPS management page adds that the park was "officially created in 1993 through a special agreement" and that the land "belongs to the local villages...and is leased to the National Park Service for 50 years."

faq.q: Is the American Samoa National Park visitor center open on weekends?
faq.a: No. The NPS: the visitor center in Pago Pago is "open on weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m." and "closed on weekends and federal holidays."

faq.q: What is American Samoa National Park known for?
faq.a: Its rainforest and reefs. The NPS: "This is the only rainforest of its kind in a United States national park. About 9,500 acres of tropical rainforest are protected here." On the reefs, "over 950 species of fish and over 250 species of coral have been documented."

faq.q: Are there tours of American Samoa National Park?
faq.a: Yes, local day tours. Tour American Samoa lists a 5.5-hour "National Park + Tisa's Barefoot Bar" tour ("$235 per person", "maximum is 8 people") visiting Vatia village and the Pola Island views, a 3.5-hour "Aiga Bus Scenic Tour" ("USD $75 per person"), and "National Park Plus Tour" and "Mt. Alava Plus Adventure" for non-cruise guests, booked by email.
